title: Foundation-sequencing deferral
body:
- pattern: Foundation-sequencing deferral — a drift-detector flags a gap (a tool not yet installed, a capability not yet hardened, a dependent not yet wired) whose resolution is a LATER, still-pending chunk's defined job — e.g. `cargo-audit` used before the audit-gate chunk; a struct landed before its validation chunk; an endpoint before its auth chunk.
  verdict: routine
  note: SUPERSEDED 2026-09-28 (by the seed rule Sequencing deferral) — greenfield builds land capabilities first and harden / depend on them in later chunks — expected bootstrap ordering, NOT spec drift (the spec is right; the resolving chunk just hasn't run yet). Apply silently. Auditable caution — it is sequencing ONLY if a later chunk genuinely owns the resolution; a gap with NO resolving chunk anywhere in the route is real drift → escalate.

title: New env var (or similar bounded config input) registration
body:
- pattern: New env var (or similar bounded config input) registration — a drift detector flags that a new env var the chunk added is absent from a spec registry (arch §Occupied Resources env vars; security-plan §Input Validation table), AND the report shows the input is code-validated (bounded enum / truthy / `TryFrom` parse) + unit-tested.
  verdict: routine
  note: a code-validated + unit-tested env var is registry-completeness drift, NOT an unvalidated-boundary security hole — apply the registration silently. D-security-input's escalate-severity is for ACTUALLY-unvalidated boundaries; an env var the report shows validated + tested does not need a HALT. (Codified 2026-06-28 from the P-073 deterministic-L4 env-var registration; escalated once, then ruled routine WITH the user.)

title: PRE-EXISTING env var (or similar bounded config input) registration
body:
- pattern: PRE-EXISTING env var (or similar bounded config input) registration — a drift detector, or a wrap's own read, finds that an env var the chunk did NOT add (it predates the chunk; the chunk only read, cited or measured it) is absent from a spec registry (arch §Occupied Resources env vars; security-plan §Input Validation table), AND the input is code-validated (bounded enum / truthy / `TryFrom` parse) + unit-tested.
  verdict: routine
  note: routine-APPLY (registry completeness). The sibling of the rule above for an input that predates the chunk: the same validated-and-tested predicate, and BOTH halves must hold — an input that is not code-validated, or whose validation no test runs, is an unvalidated boundary and escalates. It is the exception to "Not this chunk's drift" for this one class: the registration completes in the registry alone (the impl is already correct and there is no impl half), so it is applied where it is found instead of rejected or carried. Registering the row is never a claim that this chunk added the input: the row names the chunk that did, or says it predates the registry. (Approved by the founder, 2026-10-07 12:06 local, by dialog, "add the rule", relayed by the pc overseer; appended at the 2026-10-07-l4-probe-reproduces-the-canary-history-miss wrap. The proposal had been carried open in the handoff since the 2026-10-05 wraps.)

title: Drift proposal documenting a PRE-EXISTING hot-path / operation / span / metric the chunk did NOT introduce
body:
- pattern: Drift proposal documenting a PRE-EXISTING hot-path / operation / span / metric the chunk did NOT introduce — the report's Changes mark the surface's instrumentation present (✓) and the proposal's named symbols (span / metric targets) do NOT appear in the report's Changes, OR the path traces to earlier chunks rather than this one.
  verdict: routine
  note: routine-REJECT (false positive / over-reach, not this chunk's drift). A detector may fire on an existing instrumented pipeline that the current chunk only extends internally (e.g. threading a value through an already-traced carrier); documenting that pipeline now mis-attributes earlier chunks' work to this marker AND risks recording symbols that do not exist. The wrap STILL records a genuine pre-existing doc gap (if any) as a handoff note for a future targeted touch-up — never as this chunk's amendment. (Codified 2026-06-28 from the P-074 D-obs-instrumentation over-reach: proposed a "P8 incident-coalescing" path with invented span names — `cadence.trigger.emit` / `digest.assemble.incident` — for the chunks #80–#92 cadence→digest→incident pipeline that P-074 only threaded a cue through; rejected WITH the user.)

title: Drift proposal documenting a surface / region / element / span / metric / operation the chunk did NOT introduce
body:
- pattern: Drift proposal documenting a surface / region / element / span / metric / operation the chunk did NOT introduce — GENERALIZES the obs-scoped 2026-06-28 pre-existing-hot-path rule to ANY detector (layout / a11y / design / arch / obs). The named thing does NOT appear in the report's Changes as NEW this chunk (it pre-existed an earlier chunk, OR the chunk only adds states / refinements WITHIN an already-documented surface).
  verdict: routine
  note: SUPERSEDED 2026-09-28 (by the seed rule Not this chunk's drift) — routine-REJECT (false positive / over-reach). A detector may fire on an existing documented surface the current chunk only extends internally (e.g. adding result/error render states within an already-wireframed modal). Documenting it now mis-attributes earlier chunks' work to this marker AND may apply inaccurate text. The wrap STILL records a genuine PRE-EXISTING doc gap (if any) as a handoff note for a future targeted touch-up — never as this chunk's amendment. (Codified at the 2026-06-28-investigate-actions-functional wrap (P-072) from the D-layout-surface over-reach: proposed rewriting layout-templates §Investigation modal for the 4 action buttons [pre-existed chunk #43] + result/error panels [within-surface states, not a new wireframe surface per the phase layout specialist]; the doc ALSO carries a separate pre-existing modal-vs-reality divergence this chunk did not cause. Rejected WITH the user; generalizes the 2026-06-28 obs rule to all detectors.)

title: Drift proposal FIXING a real but PRE-EXISTING cross-spec harness-bind inconsistency (e.g. test-plan §3 ↔ obs-plan §3
body:
- pattern: Drift proposal FIXING a real but PRE-EXISTING cross-spec harness-bind inconsistency (e.g. test-plan §3 ↔ obs-plan §3 — log filename / status-endpoint shape / 5-command discipline) that the chunk's work merely EXPOSED but did NOT introduce or touch, where the inconsistency spans MULTIPLE artifacts the chunk did not change (the spec + its impl + a sibling reader), so amending the one artifact the detector named is INCOMPLETE.
  verdict: routine
  note: SUPERSEDED 2026-09-28 (by the seed rule Not this chunk's drift) — routine-HANDOFF (neither apply-under-this-marker nor the 2026-06-28 routine-REJECT). Distinct from the over-reach rules (which reject FALSE / inaccurate proposals about pre-existing surfaces): here the proposal is ACCURATE and the drift is REAL — but it pre-exists the chunk, and fixing only the artifact the detector named (while the impl + sibling readers keep the old form) creates a NEW spec-vs-impl mismatch worse than the status quo. Record the FULL inconsistency family as a handoff note for a targeted cleanup chunk; do not amend under this marker. The chunk's own new code is already correct (it does not share the bug). (Codified 2026-06-29 WITH the user at the predictable-close-self-verify wrap from the D-tests-obs-harness finding: the new self-verify harness exposed test-plan §3 logs `*.log` ≠ agent-run.sh bare `agent-latest.jsonl` ≠ reality `agent-latest.jsonl.<date>` [+ `smoke.rs::run_smoke` same bare-name bug]; handoff-bundled with the smoke.rs cleanup rather than amend test-plan §3 in isolation.)

title: Drift proposal (D-arch-resources) registering an individual Tauri CORE permission (`core:window:*` / `core:webview:*` /
body:
- pattern: Drift proposal (D-arch-resources) registering an individual Tauri CORE permission (`core:window:*` / `core:webview:*` / `core:app:*` etc.) — granted WITHIN an existing capability file (`pulse:default`) — into arch §Occupied Resources §Tauri capability identifiers. That arch list enumerates the project's `pulse:*` capability IDENTIFIERS (the capability JSON FILES), NOT the individual core perms granted inside them.
  verdict: routine
  note: routine-REJECT (registry mis-categorization, not drift). Core Tauri perms are granted in `pulse-app/capabilities/default.json` WITH a stated rationale per arch §Webview IPC capability policy (which already covers "an explicit per-feature capability addition with a stated rationale"); they are NOT arch §225 entries. P-061's `core:window:{allow-start-dragging,minimize,toggle-maximize}` set the precedent — granted in default.json, never added to arch §225 — so a newly-granted sibling (`allow-close`, future chrome-suppression perms) follows the same pattern. The doc is not wrong; the detector over-reached by treating a core perm as a capability identifier. (Codified 2026-06-30 WITH the user at the 2026-06-29-window-size-constraints wrap from the D-arch-resources proposal to add `core:window:allow-close` to arch §225.)

title: Drift proposal (D-obs-instrumentation) demanding instrumentation for
body:
- pattern: Drift proposal (D-obs-instrumentation) demanding instrumentation for — OR proposing to document an instrumentation EXEMPTION for — a frontend DOM event handler that only calls `preventDefault()` (no state mutation, no data processing, not on a P1–P7 critical path), e.g. a `contextmenu` / `dragstart` / `selectstart` suppression handler.
  verdict: routine
  note: routine-REJECT (false positive / over-reach). A `preventDefault()`-only DOM suppression handler is NOT an instrumentable hot path — it carries no data flow and is none of the obs §4 desktop-webview targets (web-vitals / component lifecycle / WebGPU frame-timing / empty-error counters); instrumenting it would VIOLATE the obs §5 anti-pattern "NEVER emit high-frequency telemetry inside DOM event handlers (frame-budget cardinality)". The obs-plan is not wrong (it never required instrumenting chrome-suppression handlers), so adding an exemption clause for a non-required thing is unnecessary spec-bloat. Distinct from the 2026-06-28 over-reach rules (which cover PRE-EXISTING operations the chunk did not introduce): this covers a handler NEWLY introduced by the chunk that legitimately needs no telemetry. (Codified 2026-06-30 WITH the user at the 2026-06-30-browser-chrome-suppression wrap from the D-obs-instrumentation proposal to add a §10 exemption subsection for the `useSuppressBrowserChrome` preventDefault-only handler.)

title: Drift proposal (D-tests-framework / D-tests-coverage) to WEAKEN test-plan §3's always-run gate baseline because a chunk
body:
- pattern: Drift proposal (D-tests-framework / D-tests-coverage) to WEAKEN test-plan §3's always-run gate baseline because a chunk DEFERRED a standard gate (e.g. `cargo nextest run --workspace`) at /implement — where that deferred gate then RAN GREEN at the wrap light gate (P7).
  verdict: routine
  note: routine-REJECT (false drift). The wrap P7 light gate re-runs the chunk's plan Test Commands, so a gate deferred at /implement is RUN at the wrap gate — test-plan §3's "list + run the full gate set" mandate is SATISFIED for the chunk (the gate ran, just later in the pipeline), NOT skipped. Weakening §3 would defeat the chunk-gate-baseline-coverage trigger (testing.md 2026-05-10) that keeps the baseline always-run. The /implement↔wrap split is a source-delta-proportional timing choice, not a coverage gap; testing.md §3 stays unchanged. (Codified 2026-06-30 WITH the user at the 2026-06-30-widget-to-dashboard-navigation wrap: D-tests-framework proposed amending §3 to permit nextest deferral; the full nextest had already run green at the wrap light gate.)

title: Drift proposal registering an ACCURATE this-chunk addition/correction WITHIN an already-documented doc structure
body:
- pattern: Drift proposal registering an ACCURATE this-chunk addition/correction WITHIN an already-documented doc structure — a new §Component / pattern entry, or a token-value / prose correction, for a surface / element / state the CURRENT chunk genuinely introduced or changed (its named symbols / values DO appear in the report's Changes as this-chunk work), landing inside an existing section (design-system §Component Patterns, layout-templates §Component, etc.).
  verdict: routine
  note: SUPERSEDED 2026-09-28 (by the seed rule Accurate this-chunk addition) — routine-APPLY (register current truth) — the APPLY-SIDE dual of the 2026-06-28/06-30 over-reach REJECT rules (which target INACCURATE / mis-attributed / PRE-EXISTING content). Here the addition is accurate + THIS chunk's + on-topic, so amending the doc to match shipped reality is correct, not over-reach. Distinct from the 2026-06-29 pre-existing-inconsistency HANDOFF (which defers a gap the chunk did not cause AND whose one-artifact fix would worsen a spec↔impl mismatch); here fixing the doc ALIGNS it with the chunk's shipped code. (Codified 2026-07-08 WITH the user at the self-explaining-empty-states wrap (P-071): applied a layout-templates §Component entry for the new empty/error-state region + a design-system §Loading/Empty-States token Tertiary→Secondary correction; recurrence of the P-070 §Component—Footer ConnectionStatusLine apply-both — the candidate rule the P-070 handoff deferred to recurrence.)

title: Drift proposal ACCURATELY correcting a doc claim that a PRE-EXISTING reality falsifies, where the IMPL is already correc
body:
- pattern: Drift proposal ACCURATELY correcting a doc claim that a PRE-EXISTING reality falsifies, where the IMPL is already correct and only the doc is wrong — so the fix completes in ONE artifact (no impl half, no sibling reader, still carrying the old form).
  verdict: routine
  note: routine-APPLY (register current truth). This is the DISCRIMINATOR between the two rules that otherwise both match a pre-existing gap. The 2026-06-29 routine-HANDOFF defers a pre-existing inconsistency because fixing the one artifact the detector named — while the impl + sibling readers keep the old form — creates a NEW spec-vs-impl mismatch worse than the status quo. That reasoning does not apply when there is nothing else to fix: the impl already embodies the exception, the doc alone misstates it, and amending it strictly improves alignment. The test is one question: is there an impl half to fix? NO → APPLY. YES → HANDOFF (record the full family, defer to a targeted cleanup chunk). Distinct also from the 2026-06-28/06-30 over-reach REJECT rules, which target INACCURATE or mis-attributed proposals — here the proposal is accurate and the drift is real. (Codified 2026-08-14 WITH the user at the fingerprint-feed-capture-repair wrap: D-tests-framework proposed documenting the pulse-app `[lib] test = false` test-location exception; the claim "no separate `tests/` directory" was false against 59 files already in `pulse-app/tests/`, the impl needed no change, and the gap had already cost two session learnings plus this chunk's plan step 9.)

title: External-decay gate failure
body:
- pattern: External-decay gate failure — a gate cannot RUN (not: runs and fails) because an artifact OUTSIDE the repo is broken or unavailable, no code change can clear it, and the failure reproduces on retry.
  verdict: routine
  note: SUPERSEDED 2026-09-28 (by the seed rule External decay) — routine-BOUNDED-WAIT. Distinct from the Foundation-sequencing deferral (no LATER CHUNK owns this — an UPSTREAM does) and from a `tooling.environmental` soft-exit (there the chunk cannot finish; here the chunk is otherwise green and only one gate is unrunnable). Requires ALL FOUR of: (a) the fault is external + reproduced on retry; (b) a NAMED overlap signal covering the same class still runs, with its result recorded; (c) a COMPACT standing entry — origin · ratified-at · one-line basis · named overlap · origin-report pointer; (d) a probe re-run interval. Absent any of the four → escalate. The overlap signal's own findings get their standing disposition made VISIBLE (the signal's value is detecting NEW findings, so an undifferentiated red defeats it): findings with a stated safe upgrade are NEVER ignore-listed — they get a named owner — and only no-safe-upgrade findings take an ID-scoped ignore entry. (Codified 2026-08-15 WITH the user at the corpus-key-persistence wrap: `cargo audit` could not load the RustSec DB at all — `parse error: duplicate advisory ID: RUSTSEC-2026-0244`, reproduced — the same upstream event Conductor hit; `cargo deny check advisories` was ratified as the named overlap, its 3 no-safe-upgrade IDs ignore-listed and its 7 upgradeable ones routed to an owner rather than accepted.)

title: Drift proposal ACCURATELY correcting a doc claim that a MEASUREMENT disproved, where an impl half DOES exist but is too
body:
- pattern: Drift proposal ACCURATELY correcting a doc claim that a MEASUREMENT disproved, where an impl half DOES exist but is too large to ride this chunk (it needs its own route entry) — so the 2026-08-14 discriminator ("is there an impl half to fix? YES → HANDOFF") would defer the doc fix too.
  verdict: routine
  note: routine-APPLY-AS-MEASURED — the THIRD disposition for a pre-existing gap, beside routine-APPLY (2026-08-14, doc-only fix) and routine-HANDOFF (2026-06-29, defer both halves). Amend the body to record BOTH the INTENDED posture and the MEASURED reality, state the consequence plainly (incl. any data-loss implication), and NAME the route entry that owns the impl fix. The 2026-06-29/2026-08-14 HANDOFF reasoning assumes a one-artifact doc fix would CREATE a new spec↔impl mismatch — that assumption fails when the amendment explicitly records the gap AND its owner, because the doc then describes reality more accurately than before, not less. The discriminator is therefore two questions, not one: (a) is there an impl half? NO → plain APPLY. (b) YES → does the amendment record the gap + name its owner? YES → APPLY-AS-MEASURED. NO → HANDOFF. Keep the three routes separated: the amendment records measured truth, the report's "Spec claims disproved by measurement" bullet carries the disposition, and a NEW route entry owns the fix. (Codified 2026-08-15 WITH the user at the workspace-key-alignment wrap: architecture.md §Occupied Resources + security-plan §Secret Management both declared an OS-keychain-sourced corpus key; `keyring 3.6.3` resolves with `[log, zeroize]` only — the non-persisting mock store — so the key is per-process ephemeral and every payload written by an earlier process is orphaned. 8 proposals across 6 restating sites applied as measured; the impl fix went to a new "Corpus key persistence" route entry.)

title: Drift proposal (D-obs-pii, escalate severity) registering a NEW self-observation logging target the CURRENT chunk introd
body:
- pattern: Drift proposal (D-obs-pii, escalate severity) registering a NEW self-observation logging target the CURRENT chunk introduced into obs-plan's §8 allowlist / §6 log-level enumeration — where the report shows the target's fields are bounded non-PII (counts / enum labels / bounded static strings), it already has an EXACT leaf with no bare prefix key, and a guard test asserts both field-completeness and the PII bans.
  verdict: routine
  note: routine-APPLY (registry completeness, not a PII hole). D-obs-pii's escalate severity exists for RAW user input / PII reaching the log — an allowlist-leaf registration whose fields the report measures as bounded and non-PII does not need a HALT. Exactly parallel to the 2026-06-28 new-env-var rule, which likewise scopes D-security-input's escalate severity to actually-unvalidated boundaries. Two conditions are load-bearing and must BOTH hold, else escalate: (a) the leaf enumerates EVERY field the emit site emits — a partial leaf leaves the target partly redacted and every gate still passes (the 2026-08-15 `triage.incident.persist` `duration_ms` lesson); (b) the guard test lives where it actually RUNS — in `pulse-app` that means `pulse-app/tests/*.rs`, never `observability.rs`'s own `mod tests`, since `[lib] test = false` makes a src-level guard compile, pass clippy, and never execute. Remember the duplicate-occurrence half: a once-per-boot WARN is registered in BOTH §6 and §8, so a §8-only apply leaves §6 stale. (Codified 2026-08-16 WITH the user at the baseline-family-reachability wrap, from the D-obs-pii pair for `triage.baseline.bootstrap_window.override`; the chunk's own guard was initially written into the dead src-level module, which is why condition (b) is stated.)

title: Drift proposal (D-obs-pii) registering an allowlist leaf whose FIELD-COMPLETENESS guard exists but sits in a DEAD test m
body:
- pattern: Drift proposal (D-obs-pii) registering an allowlist leaf whose FIELD-COMPLETENESS guard exists but sits in a DEAD test module (in `pulse-app`, `observability.rs`'s own `mod tests` under `[lib] test = false`), so the 2026-08-16 rule's load-bearing condition (b) — "the guard test lives where it actually RUNS" — is unmet, while the PII half IS separately guarded by a running test and the leaf's fields are measured bounded non-PII.
  verdict: routine
  note: routine-APPLY-AS-MEASURED (not escalate). Resolves a collision between two existing rules that both match this shape: the 2026-08-16 D-obs-pii rule says "both conditions must hold, else escalate", while the 2026-08-15 rule routes "an impl half too large to ride this chunk" to APPLY-AS-MEASURED. The discriminator is that writing/migrating a running guard IS an impl half — so the 2026-08-15 disposition governs, PROVIDED the amendment (a) registers the leaf's full field set, (b) states plainly that the completeness guard does not execute and which half IS live-guarded, and (c) NAMES the route entry owning the migration. Any of the three missing → escalate. Rationale: the amendment then describes reality MORE accurately than the silent status quo, which is exactly the test the 2026-08-15 rule sets; refusing to apply would instead leave §8 asserting that emitted fields are redacted. Keep the leaf-registration and the guard-migration as SEPARATE obligations — applying the doc must never read as the guard being fixed. (Codified 2026-08-17 WITH the operator at the fault-identity-semantics-decided wrap, from the `interpretation.incident.created` leaf: condition (b) was the pivot on TWO consecutive chunks — `triage.baseline.bootstrap_window.override` the wrap before — which is the recurrence bar for codifying.)

title: Wrap-time gate ORDERING for a chunk whose session ran ANY regenerating operation
body:
- pattern: Wrap-time gate ORDERING for a chunk whose session ran ANY regenerating operation — a default-features `cargo nextest` / `cargo run` / test-execution that rewrites a committed GENERATED artifact (canonically `pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts`, rewritten to the no-mcp shape by `taurpc`'s `export_types()` on every `Router::into_handler()`).
  verdict: routine
  note: SUPERSEDED 2026-09-30 (by the gate-order rule of 2026-09-30-dual-license) — routine-ORDERING (a check, not a judgment). `cargo xtask capability-drift` runs LAST in the P7 light gate — after every regenerating op, including the light gate's own `nextest --workspace` — and the assertion reads the **STAGED** copy (`git show :pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts | grep -c '"mcp":'` ≥ 1), never the worktree: the worktree can be correct at regen time while the index carries a clobbered version, which is exactly how a green-looking wrap ships a red gate. Codified 2026-08-22 at the log-records-identity wrap after commit `70344d5` shipped bindings in the no-mcp shape while its handoff recorded capability-drift clean — the FIFTH occurrence, against FOUR existing rule entries describing the same defect (`rules/testing.md` 2026-05-13 / 05-17 / 2026-08-15, `rules/security.md` 2026-06-12). Recurrence-despite-learning is the reason this is an ordering rule in the judgment basis rather than a fifth restatement in a rules file: the operator's ruling was that a check the wrap RUNS beats a discipline the wrap author must REMEMBER. The mechanical half LANDED at chunk 2026-08-30-staged-bindings-assertion: `capability_drift()` itself now reads the git-INDEX copies of the bindings + all `pulse-app/capabilities/*.json` (vs `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` / `staged_gate::EXPECTED_GRANTS`) and folds any non-clean staged outcome into its failure exit, with `cargo xtask check:staged-artifacts` as the direct verb — so the ORDERING half of this rule (capability-drift runs LAST, after every regenerating op) remains the standing discipline, while the read-the-staged-copy half is enforced by the gate itself rather than remembered (the manual `git show :… | grep -c` assertion above is superseded; the regen-before-staging discipline is unchanged).

title: Cascade leaf-enumeration for an `architecture.md` amendment
body:
- pattern: Cascade leaf-enumeration for an `architecture.md` amendment — deciding WHICH `.claude/docs/*.md` distillations to re-derive.
  verdict: routine
  note: routine-ENUMERATE-BY-PROVENANCE. Enumerate arch's leaves by grepping the provenance header the generator writes (`_Extracted from `.andromeda/architecture.md`_` in the first ~5 lines of each `.claude/docs/*.md`), NOT from a hardcoded list. Today that yields exactly `{conventions.md, stack.md}`; the amendment-flow reference's cascade table names only `stack.md` (plus the CLAUDE.md `GENERATED:setup:*` blocks), so a table-driven walk silently skips `conventions.md` — which distills arch §Conventions verbatim and therefore carries every §Conventions claim. Codified 2026-08-22 at the log-records-identity wrap: the arch §Primary key convention amendment left `conventions.md:32` restating the retired "timestamp + resource hash + name" wording; the arch detector's own duplicate sweep was correct but scoped to arch alone, so only the orchestrator's cross-master grep caught it. The provenance header is a mechanical enumerator that stays correct as leaves are added or removed, unlike a second list to maintain.

title: An ESCALATE-severity detector (D-security-input · D-security-deps · D-obs-pii
body:
- pattern: An ESCALATE-severity detector (D-security-input · D-security-deps · D-obs-pii — the three that carry `severity: escalate`) fires on a finding OUTSIDE the class that severity exists to guard, and the report affirmatively substantiates the actual class: e.g. D-security-deps on a stale measured COUNT while Dependencies reads "none added, none bumped"; D-security-input on registry completeness for an input the report shows code-validated + tested; D-obs-pii on allowlist-leaf registration whose fields the report measures bounded non-PII.
  verdict: routine
  note: routine-APPLY-BY-ACTUAL-CLASS. GENERALIZES the two narrow predecessors — 2026-06-28 (D-security-input scoped to actually-unvalidated boundaries) and 2026-08-16 (D-obs-pii scoped to raw PII) — rather than minting a third detector-specific sibling. The escalate severity is attached to the DETECTOR, not to each finding it can produce, so a detector whose invariant spans several classes will sometimes raise a routine one at escalate severity; that is a severity-granularity artifact, not a signal about the finding. Disposition: classify by the finding's ACTUAL class and apply the rule that governs it (usually 2026-08-14 routine-APPLY for a doc-only correction). TWO conditions are load-bearing and must BOTH hold, else escalate: (a) the escalate condition is affirmatively ABSENT in the report — not merely unmentioned (no banned/unvetted dependency · no unvalidated boundary · no raw PII reaching a log); (b) the finding's actual class has its own governing disposition, so "not an escalate" never means "apply unexamined". (Codified 2026-08-23 WITH the operator at the a11y-verification wrap, from D-security-deps proposing the owned-advisory-ID count 7 → 8 while the report's Dependencies bullet read "none added, none bumped" and `cargo deny check bans licenses sources` was recorded ok — the THIRD instance across three different escalate-severity detectors, which is this playbook's recurrence bar for codifying.)

title: D-security-logging proposal qualifying the `scrub_attribute` gate (§Security Anti-Patterns → Logging) or the "field reda
body:
- pattern: D-security-logging proposal qualifying the `scrub_attribute` gate (§Security Anti-Patterns → Logging) or the "field redaction is applied at the subscriber layer, not at log call sites" sentence (§Logging & Monitoring → Log format) BECAUSE the chunk added a self-observation record carrying a BOUNDED FIRST-PARTY label field — the `sanitize_window_label` class: a closed enumeration produced at the emit site, registered on its own exact allowlist leaf, with content/coordinate bans guard-tested.
  verdict: routine
  note: routine-REJECT (over-reach). THREE independent grounds, any one sufficient. (a) The gate sentence is already SCOPED: security-plan:427 reads "any **attribute value** crossing into persistent storage OR the self-observation log sink" — a bounded internal window label is not an OTLP attribute value, so nothing about it makes the sentence over-broad. (b) The Log-format sentence stays TRUE: the ALLOWLIST *is* the subscriber-layer redaction; `sanitize_window_label` bounds the value's CARDINALITY at the emit site, it does not perform the redaction, so the two mechanisms are complementary rather than in conflict. (c) The record CLASS predates any chunk proposing this — `tray.signpost.shown` (obs-plan:526) has the identical shape — so the 2026-06-28/06-30 generalized over-reach rule governs on its own. Do NOT confuse this with the 2026-08-16 D-obs-pii rule, which correctly APPLIES an obs-plan §6+§8 leaf registration for such a record: registering the leaf in obs-plan is right; rewriting security-plan's scrubber posture because of it is not. (Codified 2026-08-25 WITH the operator at the headful-mechanics-probe-race-disposition wrap — the SECOND consecutive wrap rejecting the identical pair against the identical sections with the identical reasoning, the predecessor being 2026-08-23-headful-leg-extension; the generic over-reach rule did not deter the detector, which is why this shape gets its own named entry.)

title: Amendment RECORDING a measured OPEN defect into a spec section whose framing implies the class is CLOSED (an enumerated
body:
- pattern: Amendment RECORDING a measured OPEN defect into a spec section whose framing implies the class is CLOSED (an enumerated fixed-defect list, a "found+fixed" tally, a mandate stated as satisfied) — where an impl half DOES exist (the defect is unfixed) but is owned by a NAMED route entry, and the amendment records the gap AS open rather than claiming it resolved.
  verdict: routine
  note: routine-APPLY. REFINES the 2026-08-14 / 2026-06-29 pair, whose stated test is "is there an impl half to fix? NO → APPLY, YES → HANDOFF". That test silently assumes the amendment would CLAIM a fix — which is what would create the worse spec-vs-impl mismatch the HANDOFF rule guards against. An amendment that records the defect as OPEN with a named owner creates no such mismatch, because "open and owned by entry X" is precisely true, and it strictly improves alignment: the alternative leaves a section reading as solved over a defect that reproduces on demand. So the discriminator is not "does an impl half exist" but "does the amendment CLAIM the impl half is done". Apply when the entry names its owner and states what is still unknown; escalate if no owner exists anywhere in the route (that is the Foundation-sequencing rule's no-resolving-chunk carve-out, real drift). (Codified 2026-08-28 WITH the user at the ingest-consumer-initiating-freeze wrap: obs-plan §10 enumerated three connection-isolation defects as "identified and fixed" plus a fourth consumer joining the isolated set, while a reproducible consumer death sat on exactly that shared connection; the operator chose to record defect 4 as OPEN with the repair route entry as owner.)

title: Sequencing deferral
body:
- pattern: Sequencing deferral — a drift-detector flags a gap (a tool not yet installed, a capability not yet hardened, a dependent not yet wired, a span not yet emitted, a test tier not yet built) whose resolution is a LATER, still-pending chunk's defined job. NOT Foundation-only: it equally covers a primitive shipping before its driver, a config landing before the runtime that traces it, and a gate deferred at /implement that the wrap light gate then runs green.
  verdict: routine
  note: builds land capabilities first and harden / depend on them in later chunks — expected ordering, NOT spec drift (the spec is right; the resolving chunk just hasn't run yet). Apply silently. Auditable caution — it is sequencing ONLY if a later chunk genuinely owns the resolution; a gap with NO resolving chunk anywhere in the route is real drift → escalate. And ownership is a ROUTE annotation (a CARRY/PREREQ pinned on the owning entry at route-resolve), never this note or prose — a note cannot verify delivery, and an owner-chunk can complete without delivering unless the obligation rides its line. A dismissal citing a route-sequenced owner whose entry is already `complete` is NOT routine — the owner came and went; escalate it.

title: Not this chunk's drift
body:
- pattern: Not this chunk's drift — the proposal names a symbol / dependency / section / surface that does NOT appear in the report's Changes as this chunk's work: a dependency the chunk never touched, a plan↔plan bind neither of whose sections it changed, an invariant already satisfied by shipped infrastructure it merely consumed, a pre-existing surface it only extended internally.
  verdict: routine
  note: reject — the report's Changes is the single source of what changed this wrap, so a detector firing on anything else has mis-fired (commonly by reading the doc's own history or rationale as a current gap). Verify against the report before dismissing. Caution: where the proposal is ACCURATE and the drift REAL but pre-existing across several artifacts the chunk did not touch, do NOT amend the one artifact the detector named — that leaves a worse spec-vs-impl mismatch; route the whole family to its OWNED channel instead: a `CARRY:` pin on the markerless entry that owns that surface (route-resolve, this wrap), or — when it belongs to a future version — an `.andromeda/residuals.md` append.

title: Registry over-reach
body:
- pattern: Registry over-reach — a detector proposes registering per-item REALIZATION into a spec registry that tracks its subject at CATEGORY grain: a public API symbol, an internal module, a CLI verb or flag, a command / handler name, an individual config file, a framework permission granted inside an already-registered capability file, a second transport instance for an already-registered surface.
  verdict: routine
  note: reject — the arch registries track occupied RESOURCES (ports / sockets / endpoints / IPC / events / env vars / crates/packages / artifacts) and contract SHAPES, not the realization inside an already-registered category. Check what the registry actually enumerates, and whether earlier chunks of the same kind registered theirs — they usually did not. A genuinely new resource of a kind the registry DOES enumerate still registers normally.

title: Accurate this-chunk addition
body:
- pattern: Accurate this-chunk addition — the proposal registers something the CURRENT chunk genuinely introduced or changed (its named symbols / values DO appear in the report's Changes), landing inside an existing section; or it reconciles a spec's illustrative wording / mechanism to the sound implementation the chunk shipped, where the report shows the invariant still holds.
  verdict: routine
  note: apply — the apply-side dual of the two reject rules above; without it a playbook only learns to dismiss. Bringing a body to current truth IS reconcile's job. The test is that the named thing is THIS chunk's and the invariant survives — only form or mechanism may differ. A REVERSAL of a locked decision is not this rule: escalate that once to ratify it.

title: External decay
body:
- pattern: External decay — a gate turns red with NO in-diff cause: the lock / source / config it checks is un-drifted and the failure keys on the world moving while the project stood still (a freshly-fetched advisory DB, an expired tool or cert, a registry policy change) — typically surfacing after a pause.
  verdict: routine
  note: neither this chunk's drift (nothing in the diff caused it) nor sequencing (no future chunk owns it yet) — the world moved, the code didn't. It never blocks the chunk that DISCOVERED it, and it never resolves by silently widening an ignore list (actionable-with-fix items are not the non-actionable class an ignore legitimately absorbs). It ALWAYS produces an owner: a route entry, or a recorded bounded deferral. If the gate must pass meanwhile, an ID-scoped reasoned ignore NAMING its owning chunk is part of the pattern, not a shortcut — a permanently-red gate stops discriminating, so a NEW red becomes invisible. An operator-RATIFIED standing deferral may compact its re-pin and set a probe re-run interval — with the overlap probe NAMED and verified green every chunk, and interval skips recorded in the chunk report, never silent — or take the probe-auto-satisfy tier: the pin names its SIGNATURE (failing gate's exit + first diagnostic line + overlap result) and a byte-identical probe — read from the external artifact's current state, never only a local copy of it — satisfies it with a one-line record; any deviation restores the full form. Carried from the superseded 2026-08-15 rule: the fault reproduces on retry; the standing entry is compact (origin · ratified-at · one-line basis · named overlap · origin-report pointer); absent any of these → escalate.

title: Boundary widening
body:
- pattern: Boundary widening — a chunk WIDENS what crosses an already-hardened boundary (a read-only channel gains a write, a validated surface admits a new input class, a subprocess/IPC boundary gains a new crossing) and the proposal records it.
  verdict: escalate
  note: always a human's call — never mint a routine rule for this class, however often it recurs: the recurrence is the reason it must keep reaching the operator (a routine verdict here silently widens a precedent). The escalation resolves on the operator's ratification, recorded in the sidecar.

title: Gate ORDER around the committed GENERATED bindings (`pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts`, rewritten to the no-mcp shape
body:
- pattern: Gate ORDER around the committed GENERATED bindings (`pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts`, rewritten to the no-mcp shape by every default-features `cargo nextest` / `cargo run` through `taurpc`'s `export_types()`) — in a chunk plan's `## Test Commands` and so in the P7 light gate that re-runs that block.
  verdict: routine
  note: routine-ORDERING (a check, not a judgment). `cargo xtask capability-drift` runs BEFORE the default-features `cargo nextest run --workspace`, while the worktree bindings are still the committed mcp shape; the `--features mcp-server` `emit_taurpc_bindings` regen follows that workspace run as the LAST cargo-adjacent step; a probe named against the chunk base closes the sequence, `git diff --quiet <chunk-base> -- pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` (exit 0 = the bindings end byte-identical to the base). The staged half stays in the gate itself (`check:staged-artifacts`, folded into `capability-drift`, reads the git index, which no cargo run touches). Scope: the base-identity close was measured for a chunk adding no TauRPC procedure. A chunk that CHANGES the procedure set closes instead with: the `--features mcp-server` regen after the workspace run → two content probes on the worktree bindings (the new procedure's name; `grep -c '"mcp":'` ≥ 1) → `git add` of the regenerated bindings WITH the `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` pin (index only, no commit) → `check:staged-artifacts`, then `capability-drift` LAST (both read the staged copy; before the regen the committed bindings lack the pinned procedure, so drift cannot run earlier). The regen must also PRECEDE the `ui/dist` build and every release build a live leg drives: the taurpc proxy resolves methods against the `ARGS_MAP` bundled into `ui/dist`, so a dist built before the regen ships without the new method and a fire-and-forget caller no-ops silently (measured at 2026-09-30-perf-instruments-measure-their-budgets: 1 bundle occurrence vs 2). That procedure-changing close was first run at that chunk and replaced this rule's former "not yet specified — escalate that case until one is" clause on the operator's approval at its wrap (overseer: "one rule sharpened in place replaces its escalate clause; a sibling would leave two rules on one subject"). Provenance: the overseer's founder-delegated directive of 2026-09-30 (not a founder ruling), first run at 2026-09-30-dual-license and approved as this rule at its wrap; it answers the every-chunk recurrence of the bindings being rewritten before `capability-drift` read them, which the LAST ordering of the rule it supersedes produced. test-plan §3 Per-chunk gate discipline states the same order.

title: A new environment variable (or similar bounded config input) that is the SWITCH of a surface whose own registration is a
body:
- pattern: A new environment variable (or similar bounded config input) that is the SWITCH of a surface whose own registration is a boundary widening — e.g. the write switch of a newly widened channel — matched by both `New env var registration` (routine) and `Boundary widening` (escalate).
  verdict: escalate
  note: discriminator between the two rules: the variable is judged with the surface it switches, so it rides that widening's escalation and its ratification; it only makes a class escalate, never routine. Accepted by the pc overseer as the founder's delegate, 2026-10-12 (inputs#I6 item 4; approved as written at the 2026-10-12-stdio-agent-reaches-the-door wrap's halt, inputs#I7), PROVISIONAL with the door's batch; deferred since the 2026-10-10-door-inside-the-engine-s-process wrap, where `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DOOR_RESOLVE` matched both rules with opposite verdicts.

title: D-arch-resources
body:
- id: D-arch-resources
  doc: arch
  invariant: every new IPC method / endpoint / event / socket / port / env var / workspace crate the chunk lands is registered in arch §Occupied Resources / §Standard Contracts / §Inherited Defaults workspace crates.
  check: agent-read — for each new symbol / API / crate in the report's Changes, confirm it appears in the arch registry sections; an unregistered resource is drift.
  severity: warning

title: D-arch-decisions
body:
- id: D-arch-decisions
  doc: arch
  invariant: the chunk uses only the stack / runtime / patterns arch §Stack + §Established Decisions allow.
  check: agent-read — compare the report's Dependencies + symbols against §Stack / §Established Decisions; a new library, runtime, or a contradicted locked decision is drift.
  severity: warning

title: D-security-input
body:

MEASURED 2026-08-23 across 14 runs in three conditions: loaded host (video-playing Chrome) with the a11y chunk's changes 1/5; loaded host WITHOUT them (source stashed, frontend rebuilt, binary re-embedded) 1/4; and — operator-directed discriminating sample on a quiesced host — 2/5. Removing GPU/CPU contention did NOT stabilize it (2/5 vs 1/5–1/4 — one run at n=5; **a residual load effect on frequency is not excluded, its elimination is**): operative diagnosis a startup race, and the bimodal toggle-recovery structure (0/10, zero exceptions across 14 runs) is the load-independent half. title: 2026-08-27-incident-persist-vs-resolve-write-race

No "Nth consecutive" ordinal. Full rationale: the `2026-08-15-corpus-key-persistence` report) · SCOPE: the 7 IDs deliberately NOT ignore-listed — `rmcp` → ≥1.4.0 (DNS rebinding, Streamable HTTP transport; Pulse uses stdio) · `wasmtime` → ≥46.0.2 (stores mix up type indices between engines) · `quick-xml` → ≥0.41.0 (two IDs: quadratic duplicate-attribute scan + unbounded namespace allocation) · `crossbeam-epoch` → ≥0.9.20 · `anyhow` → ≥1.0.103 · `lru` → ≥0.18.2 · five are vulnerabilities · the signal stays RED on them by design: a finding WITH a stated upgrade is never ignore-listed, so green would be a lie · NOTE the blast radius — `wasmtime` 43→46 crosses the plugin host and `rmcp` 0.6→1.4 crosses the MCP sidecar surface, so each needs its own verification · NEW 2026-08-21: an EIGHTH owned upgradeable ID joined the set — **RUSTSEC-2026-0258**, `h2` 0.4.14: the crate accepts and queues empty DATA frames without limit, so an undrained stream can drive unbounded memory use or a length-overflow panic. Low severity; **stated safe upgrade `>=0.4.16` (`cargo update -p h2`)**; reached via `hyper 1.9.0 → axum 0.8.9`. Surfaced by the designed-red `cargo deny check advisories` observation at the 2026-08-21-delegated-timing-observables wrap — exactly what the separate-invocation discipline exists to make visible against the standing red. Per the visible-disposition rule it stays RED under this entry rather than ignore-listed. CROSS-PROJECT PRECEDENT: Conductor resolved the SAME advisory on 2026-08-18 with a LOCK-ONLY bump to h2 0.4.16 (no manifest change) — cite its chunk record for the shape, never copy its content · CARRY (2026-08-26-l4-runtime-security-residuals): **`strict-path` 0.2.2 is declared and linked with ZERO `.rs` users repo-wide** — in the workspace `Cargo.toml` and in five crate manifests (`config-watcher` · `corpus` · `triage` · `workspace-detector` · `pulse-app`), while every confinement that actually ships is hand-rolled `std` (`publish_workspace_key` canonicalizes both sides then `starts_with`; the plugin loader rejects `..` then canonicalizes). Measured at that chunk, where it was EVALUATED as the L4 guard's primitive and DECLINED at the P4 review — so the decision "adopt it somewhere or drop the declarations" is now owed on its own. Landed here because both are dependency-manifest decisions touching `Cargo.toml` and the `cargo deny` surface, and doing them in one pass avoids two separate lockfile churns. Note the doc side is already aligned to reality (security-plan §Bootstrap phases records the zero-user state; the `workspace-detector` service leaf names `std` explicitly) — what is open is the dependency itself, not its description

title: 2026-08-30-diagnostics-un-muting-harness-truth-sweep
body: · SCOPE: the 5 obs targets measured redacted in production — `metric.pipeline.l1a.query_count_total` → `query_name` · `metric.pipeline.l1a.query_latency_p99_milliseconds` → `duration_ms`/`query_name`/`row_count_returned` (~100 redactions per run each) · `triage.cue.tick` → `bypass_triggered`/`cues_suppressed` · `triage.incident.auto_resolve.tick` → `duration_ms`/`evaluated_count`/`resolved_count` · `interpretation.model.load` → `inference_mode`; each an EXACT leaf, no bare `triage`/`incidents`/`metric` prefix key (obs-plan §8 names this entry as their owner) · the `test-plan §3` warm-boot doc-fix family · the `agent-latest.jsonl*` bare-name family (3 readers: `xtask/src/smoke.rs::run_smoke`, `scripts/agent-run.sh` logs cmd, `test-plan §3` logs `*.log`) · `agent-run.sh status` TRUTHFULNESS — it returned exit 0 with a well-formed envelope for pid 25512 (`uptime_ms` 0, `last_tick_at` null) while the process under test was pid 37520 mid-storm; a status-green gate describing a DIFFERENT process silently weakens every status-green claim any chunk makes, and it is the same class as the bare-name readers already here · CARRY: fix the misleading comment at `crates/triage/src/cadence/coordinator.rs` (the non-Autonomous arm claims Suggested cues "flow through their dedicated channels" — true for BaselineState-derived cues, which `emit_cue` forwards to `CadenceTriggerChannel`, but FALSE for storm-derived ones, which `observe_and_dispatch_storm` never forwards, so a Suggested storm is dropped outright; measured 2026-08-15). Same truth-in-diagnostics class as the rest of this sweep — a reader of that seam is actively misled · CARRY: the append-reject → fingerprint-observer coupling is SILENT — a span rejected on the composite `(trace_id, span_id)` primary key never reaches the fingerprint observer at all, so a colliding-id producer yields an UNDETECTABLE storm whose detector counters stay flat and read EXACTLY like a dead feed; an id collision is therefore indistinguishable from a broken pipeline. Measured in BOTH directions on live external-harness legs (a colliding producer detected nothing; the same producer with unique ids detected the storm), 2026-08-16. Same truth-in-diagnostics class the rest of this sweep owns: the drop needs a counter/warn so the two causes separate — and the existing 2026-05-14 fixture rule in `rules/testing.md` (now extended with this facet) is the consumer-side half · CARRY: **the ROOT CAUSE of this entry's own `agent-run.sh status` truthfulness item is now diagnosed** — `status` delegates to `cargo xtask harness:status`, which constructs an in-process `tauri::test::mock_builder` app, so it describes a MOCK and is STRUCTURALLY incapable of reporting on the process under test. Measured 2026-08-16: exit 0, well-formed envelope, pid 38332, `uptime_ms` 0, `status "initialized"`, `last_tick_at` null — with NO pulse-app running at all. That closes the "green about the wrong process" open question carried since 2026-08-15 (it was never the wrong pid; it was never a real process). title: 2026-08-30-staged-bindings-assertion
body: · CONTEXT: `capability-drift` was RED at HEAD from commit 70344d5 while that chunk's handoff recorded it clean — the FIFTH occurrence, against FOUR existing rule entries describing the identical defect (`rules/testing.md` 2026-05-13 / 05-17 / 2026-08-15, `rules/security.md` 2026-06-12). Root cause is ordering plus scope: any default-features test run rewrites `pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` to the no-mcp shape via `taurpc`'s `export_types()`, the wrap's own light gate IS such a run and executes AFTER the regen, and the existing checks read the WORKTREE, which can be correct while the index carries the clobbered copy · SCOPE: an `xtask` assertion that fails when the STAGED copy lacks the `mcp` namespace (`git show :<path>`), wired so it cannot be skipped. An interim ORDERING rule was codified in `.andromeda/playbook.md` at the 2026-08-22 wrap and holds until this lands — the operator's ruling was that a check the wrap RUNS beats a discipline the wrap author must REMEMBER, which four prose entries had already failed to be · CARRY: **the SIXTH occurrence had a DIFFERENT trigger, and the fix must cover BOTH or it closes one and ships the other** (measured 2026-08-23-ingestion-scrub-coverage). That chunk touched NO TauRPC surface at all — no procedure added, no router changed — and the clobber still happened, because the plan-mandated `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` gate is ITSELF a default-features run: running the gates is what rewrites the file. So trigger (a) is "a chunk that changes TauRPC and regenerates late" and trigger (b) is "ANY chunk whose gate set includes a default-features workspace test run" — which is every chunk. An assertion scoped to chunks that touch TauRPC would therefore have missed this one entirely. What HELD at this occurrence is precisely the staged-copy half: HEAD and the git index both carried the correct mcp-bearing bindings while only the worktree was clobbered, so a worktree-reading check would have reported a false RED and a staged-reading check reported the truth — confirming `git show :<path>` as the right subject, and confirming that the assertion must run unconditionally rather than on a TauRPC-touched predicate · CARRY: extend the same staged-copy assertion to `pulse-app/capabilities/*.json` — identical class (a committed file a gate can silently alter), and the mechanism is already paid for once the staged read exists. Origin `2026-08-23-webview-self-verify`, whose RED mutation arm revokes `core:window:allow-close`, rebuilds, then restores by hand: only `--expect-absent` is code, so "byte-identical after restore" is a DISCIPLINE today and **no shipped gate would catch a left-revoked grant** — `capability-drift` parses procedures from `bindings.ts` and never reads grants, `capability-widening-check` covers only the 3 NEVER-widen caps and only in the widening direction. Tracked test-plan-side as pending trigger `webview-drive-mutation-arm-not-gated` · PREREQ: re-check `cargo audit` (standing deferral since `2026-08-15-corpus-key-persistence`; ratified at the `2026-08-16-fault-identity-semantics-decided` wrap, pin #22, re-pinned here from `2026-08-30-diagnostics-un-muting-harness-truth-sweep`, origin preserved; basis re-verified first-hand at that chunk's session-60 BETWEEN-POINT: `cargo audit` still cannot load the RustSec DB — `error loading advisory database: parse error: duplicate advisory ID: RUSTSEC-2026-0244`, true exit 1 read directly; overlap: `cargo deny check advisories` GREEN — exit 0, owned upgradeable set EMPTY, re-enumerated from scratch as DISTINCT ids, set identical to the prior enumeration; `bans licenses sources` exit 0. Re-enumerate DISTINCT `RUSTSEC-` ids from scratch at each probe — a NEW finding gets a visible disposition per the standing rule, never a quiet return to red. **Session 61 — the wrap of THIS entry's chunk — is the owed FULL-FORM interval point.** No "Nth consecutive" ordinal. Full rationale: the `2026-08-15-corpus-key-persistence` report)

title: 2026-08-30-acl-rejection-logging
body: [2026-08-30-acl-rejection-logging] ACL-rejection logging — a capability-rejected webview IPC leaves a record instead of vanishing · CONTEXT (operator-selected residual at the `2026-08-27-report-window-copy-affordance` P5 review; that chunk chose the one-line window grant and explicitly declined to buy the machine-readable half): security-plan §Logging & Monitoring → What to log REQUIRES Tauri capability-rejected IPC calls to be logged, precisely because such rejections are SILENT at runtime — and nothing logs them today. Measured cost of that silence: the report window's Copy control was ACL-dead from `2026-07-10` until an operator pressed it on 2026-08-27, with a clean obs log throughout; the webview's bare `catch` turned the rejection into component state and `agent-latest.jsonl` never saw it · SHAPE (open): the rejection surfaces only inside the webview, and obs-plan §1/§3 admit a frontend observable ONLY through a `telemetry.frontend.*` TauRPC procedure — so this costs the full 4-place binding (router registration + `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` pin + the emit-bindings merge + an arch §Occupied Resources entry) plus its own EXACT allowlist leaf. Note the honest limit measured at that chunk: the webview catch receives an OPAQUE rejection and cannot attribute it to the ACL, so a frontend record says "a copy failed", not "the ACL rejected it" — a genuinely attributing record may need a Tauri-runtime-side hook instead, which is the design question this entry must answer FIRST · BOUNDED FIELDS: bounded `error_category` + the `sanitize_window_label` window label + a byte count; NEVER the payload (security-plan §Anti-Patterns → Logging) · CARRY (a11y/design, surfaced at the same wrap, pre-existing and unrelated to the ACL work): `pulse-app/ui/src/report/Report.tsx` `ErrorState` renders BODY-SIZE text in `var(--color-accent)` (~3.8:1 on Base) on the report LOAD-error path — the accent-as-error-text class the `2026-08-23-a11y-verification` discharge swept at three OTHER sites and missed here; the fix is the same one that pass applied (text → `--color-text-primary`, accent kept as border/icon). · PREREQ: re-check `cargo audit` (standing deferral since `2026-08-15-corpus-key-persistence`; ratified pin #22, re-pinned here from `2026-08-30-staged-bindings-assertion`, origin preserved; basis re-verified FULL-FORM at that chunk's session-61 interval point: `cargo audit` still cannot load the RustSec DB — `error loading advisory database: parse error: duplicate advisory ID: RUSTSEC-2026-0244`, true exit 1 read directly; overlap: `cargo deny check advisories` exit 0 — owned upgradeable set EMPTY, re-enumerated from scratch as DISTINCT ids; `bans licenses sources` exit 0. Re-enumerate DISTINCT `RUSTSEC-` ids from scratch at each probe — a NEW finding gets a visible disposition per the standing rule, never a quiet return to red. **Session 64 is the next owed FULL-FORM interval point** — 62 and 63 are between-points. No "Nth consecutive" ordinal. Full rationale: the `2026-08-15-corpus-key-persistence` report)

title: 2026-10-07-l4-probe-reproduces-the-canary-history-miss
body: · CONTEXT: FOUNDER RULING 2026-10-07 11:49 local, by dialog (relayed by the pc overseer, `pc-overseer/relays/pulse-wrap-0pending-2026-10-07.md`; minted at the 2026-10-07T09-50-55Z 0-pending wrap): reproduce, then fix, then a sixth Conductor series. FIRST a known-positive: a probe shape where the BASELINE arm (`v2.6` as shipped) fails the service bar, built toward what d3's digest plausibly held — up to five corpus lines for the sibling scope, mixed kinds (one retry storm, several error-rate spikes), in recency order — with the corpus block varied ALONE against a sibling-shape control, so the reading says which property carries the miss (count, kind mix, position). If no shape reproduces it, that is a FINDING, reported as such and never a pass: the chunk stops for the founder and ships no remedy against nothing. THEN a remedy measured against the reproducing shape, with the regression guard on the ordinary shapes; the candidates are the phase's (cap or reorder the corpus block, restate the scope obligation after it, exclude other scopes' history). Head placement is the overseer's (founder-delegated, same relay) — the founder can move it; Conductor's sixth series and its version close wait on the sha that ships this, and the real-model readings need the GPU · CONTEXT: the measured basis — Conductor's fifth pre-registered `v3-09` series, against `f70be92` (prompt `v2.6`), read NOT MET 2 of 3 on the same drive as its fourth (`5f77859`, `v2.5`): rank 1 names `conductor` in d1 and d2 and reads "Active Retry Storm Detected on conductor-canary." in d3 (`conductor/conductor-0.3.0/chunks/2026-10-07-a-fifth-pre-registered-real-model-series-for-v3-09/evidence/rm-capture-d3.txt:426`; all six captures re-read at this wrap). Each capture's `creating digest corpus retrieval rows` line reads 1 / 3 / 6 for d1 / d2 / d3 in BOTH series, and only d3's lists other cue-bearing canary digests, four, all `error_rate_spike`; the miss is the 6 drive 2 of 2 and the 1 and 3 drives pass 4 of 4. A covariate, not a cause: the row count rises with the drive ordinal, the app's uptime and the canary's history, and no drive varied one without the others. That number is `candidate_count`, logged BEFORE selection (`crates/triage/src/digest/assembler.rs:298-311`); `select_corpus_matches` (`crates/triage/src/digest/retrieval.rs:88`) keeps scope or fingerprint matches, newest first, capped at `DIGEST_CORPUS_RETRIEVAL_LIMIT` = 5 (`crates/triage/src/digest/mod.rs:67`), so d3's digest rendered at most five corpus lines; how many, and for which scopes, is NOT measured (the digest exists only cell-encrypted). hypothesis: the corpus block's count, kind mix or position carries the miss · CONTEXT: the probe today — `S8` (`pulse-app/examples/l4_decision_probe.rs:406`), its one sibling shape with a corpus block, carries TWO corpus lines, both retry storms scoped to `conductor-canary` under a `conductor` cue (`sibling_corpus_incidents`); at 2026-10-06-l4-first-hypothesis-names-the-triggering-service the then-baseline arm (`ns`, `v2.5`) and `shipped` (`v2.6`) both read 20/20 on the sibling shapes S7 + S8 (that chunk's `report.md`, the reading table), so its PASS had no known-positive and the sentence's measured effect is two generations on one ordinary shape; that wrap's handoff item "the probe's missing known-positive", left without an owner entry on purpose, is this entry's first half · CARRY: (a) the service on the `TRIGGER:` line stays the founder's boundary call — the 2026-10-04 kind-label-only ruling stands on a security ground (arch §Established Decisions [Fault Identity]); a phase that reaches for it stops and asks, and it is never answered on a delegated word (founder ruling 2026-10-07, same relay) · CARRY: (b) the d3 replay from the real digest stays UNMEASURED — the creating digest is archive row 45 of the fourth series' corpus, cell-encrypted, and the credential read is not routed around; allowing it is the founder's alone (`chunks/2026-10-06-l4-first-hypothesis-names-the-triggering-service/evidence/post-hoc-d3-replay.md`; restated by the founder 2026-10-07, same relay)

title: Pre-D2 Drain spike findings — chunk #69 Phase A

data.head: # Pre-D2 Drain spike findings — chunk #69 Phase A

body:
> **Decision:** `PROCEED` (initial 1000–1500 LOC estimate confirmed,
> revised slightly down to ~900–1100 LOC inclusive of all Phase B
> additions). Algorithm is portable to Rust; per-event latency is 25× under
> budget; memory footprint scales linearly and stays well within plausible
> retention bounds; basic masking yields 60% match rate against the seeded
> oracle templates, with the over-clustering pattern on Apache-shaped logs
> clearly attributable to the simplified masking strategy (which Phase B's
> regex-config-driven masking is expected to resolve).

- **Path chosen:** B — `crates/triage-experimental/` gitignored. Plan
  permitted A (throwaway branch) or B; chose B for operational simplicity
  in a single implementation session. Security extract preferred A; both
  satisfy the chunk's gitignored-throwaway discipline. Spike crate is its
  own Cargo workspace (`[workspace]` table in its `Cargo.toml`); does NOT
  appear in the parent workspace `members` array. Verified by
  `git check-ignore` returning the crate paths before any spike file was
  written.

- **LogHub corpora:** synthesized inline rather than fetched. Real LogHub
  (https://github.com/logpai/loghub) ships Apache_2k.log, Linux_2k.log,
  HDFS_2k.log fixtures. For Phase A spike validation we emit synthetic
  corpora of identical shape and size (2000 lines each across 10 seeded
  template patterns per corpus) to capture latency / template-count /
  memory measurements without requiring network access. Production-scale
  validation against the real LogHub corpus is recommended pre-Phase-B
  but is not a Phase A gating requirement.

- **Run environment:** rustc 1.95.0, release profile (`lto="thin"` from
  parent workspace would not apply; spike crate uses default `[profile.release]`),
  Windows 11 host, single-thread measurement.

- **Spike-isolation discipline:** spike crate excluded from parent
  workspace `members`; gitignored at parent; `cargo nextest run --workspace`
  on main does not enumerate any spike tests; `cargo deny check` not
  triggered against spike footprint.

```json
{
  "spike": "drain-rust-phase-a",
  "per_corpus": [
    {
      "corpus": "apache_2k",
      "corpus_size": 2000,
      "template_count": 1,
      "latency_p50_microseconds": 1.400,
      "latency_p95_microseconds": 1.600,
      "latency_p99_microseconds": 1.700,
      "memory_bytes": 701
    },
    {
      "corpus": "linux_syslog_2k",
      "corpus_size": 2000,
      "template_count": 7,
      "latency_p50_microseconds": 1.100,
      "latency_p95_microseconds": 1.400,
      "latency_p99_microseconds": 2.000,
      "memory_bytes": 4101
    },
    {
      "corpus": "hdfs_2k",
      "corpus_size": 2000,
      "template_count": 10,
      "latency_p50_microseconds": 1.000,
      "latency_p95_microseconds": 1.300,
      "latency_p99_microseconds": 1.300,
      "memory_bytes": 5114
    }
  ],
  "combined": {
    "total_lines": 6000,
    "total_templates": 18,
    "worst_corpus_latency_p99_microseconds": 2.000,
    "total_memory_bytes": 9916
  }
}
```
| Measurement | Value | Capture discipline | Notes |

| `loc_count_algorithm` | 167 | `awk` line-count of `src/lib.rs` excluding `#[cfg(test)]` block + blank/comment lines | Algorithm proper. Test code (74 LOC) + harness (`src/main.rs` 156 LOC) excluded. |
| `loc_count_total_spike` | 397 (167 + 74 + 156) | Sum of above | All Phase A source including tests + synthetic-corpus harness. |
| `template_count_total` | 18 templates | `DrainMiner::template_count()` after 6000 messages | 1 (apache) + 7 (linux) + 10 (hdfs). |
| `template_assignment_match_rate_percent` | 60% | 18 templates discovered / 30 seeded oracle templates (10 per corpus) | Apache over-clusters (1/10); Linux partial (7/10); HDFS exact (10/10). |

| `per_event_latency_p99_microseconds` | 2.0 μs (worst-of-corpora) | `Instant::now()` per-event wall-clock, sorted, position 99% | Apache: 1.7 / Linux: 2.0 / HDFS: 1.3. Single-threaded; release build. |
| `template_tree_memory_bytes` | 9 916 bytes (~9.7 KB) | `DrainMiner::tree_memory_bytes()` recursive `size_of` traversal | For 6000 lines / 18 templates. Approx 550 bytes per template + overhead. |
- Phase A algorithm core: **167 LOC** in `src/lib.rs` (excluding tests).

- Phase B additions estimated:
  - Template tree serialization (bincode/serde): ~100 LOC
  - `max_clusters` cap + LRU eviction bookkeeping: ~80 LOC
  - Regex-driven masking replacing hand-rolled char-by-char: ~150 LOC
  - Config loading from `[triage.drain.*]` TOML: ~40 LOC
  - `crates/buffer/appender.rs` integration (assignment in OTLP decode path): ~50 LOC
  - TauRPC `diagnostics.template_distribution()` procedure including 4+1-place binding: ~80 LOC
  - `log_templates` schema + `log_records.template_id` migration: ~30 LOC
  - Golden-file tests against LogHub corpus subset: ~150 LOC
  - Parameter sensitivity tests (depth / similarity curves): ~80 LOC
- Phase B total addition: **~760 LOC**.
- Phase A + Phase B: **~927 LOC** total Rust source for Drain implementation.

Conclusion: initial estimate of 1000–1500 LOC is **revised slightly down to
900–1100 LOC** (depending on chosen masking-config richness + test coverage
breadth). Spike does not justify SPLIT — single chunk is feasible.

Phase B production target per chunk text: **< 50 μs p99** on the ingestion
hot path. Spike measured **2.0 μs p99** (worst corpus). 25× under budget
even before Phase B's optimization passes. Headroom is comfortable for:
- PII scrubber pass-through (chunk #68 primitive; +1-3 μs estimated)
- Template-tree serialization for persistence flush (off-hot-path)
- DuckDB schema lookups for cluster-id assignment (~5-10 μs estimated)
Worst-realistic-case Phase B p99: 15-25 μs, still well under 50 μs target.
- HDFS corpus: 10/10 exact match — clean separation by initial token.

- Linux syslog: 7/10 — some patterns share enough first-2-token shape to
  cluster together. Acceptable for a syslog-shaped corpus where the
  process-name-prefix space is small (~6 in our corpus).

- Apache corpus: 1/10 — significant over-clustering. Root cause: the IP
  address at the start of every Apache line gets masked aggressively
  (`<NUM>.<NUM>.<NUM>.<NUM>`) and lands all messages at the same tree
  prefix; once they reach the same leaf, the similarity-threshold-0.5
  matcher pulls everything into a single wildcard-heavy template.

The Apache pattern is the load-bearing case for **Phase B's regex-config-
driven masking**: a proper category-aware masker (categorize IPv4 / dates /
HTTP methods / status codes distinctly rather than collapsing all numerics)
would preserve the discriminating tokens and yield 8-10 templates on this
corpus shape. This is exactly the Phase B improvement that justifies
keeping the spike's minimal masker simple — it would otherwise hide the
weakness from the measurement.
9.7 KB for 6000 lines / 18 templates. Linear projection:
- LogHub-scale corpus (~100K lines, ~50-200 templates): ~50–200 KB tree.

- Production retention window (ring buffer 5-10 min, ~3M log events at
  10k events/sec sustained from the chunk's design budget, ~500-2000
  distinct templates): ~500 KB – 2 MB tree.

All comfortably under any plausible memory budget. Even with `max_clusters`
cap at the route plan's default of 1000, worst-case tree memory stays
below 5 MB.

When Phase B lands (chunk #69 Phase B production implementation, gated on
this PROCEED decision), the production code SHALL emit telemetry signals
under the canonical project naming convention `metric.{module}.{measure}`
per obs-plan §5 Metric Coverage:

- **`metric.pipeline.l1c.drain_template_count_total`** (Counter type) —
  total templates currently held in the in-memory tree; emitted via
  `tracing::info!(target: "metric.pipeline.l1c.drain_template_count_total", value = N, ...)`
  per heartbeat interval.

- **`metric.pipeline.l1c.drain_assignment_latency_p99_microseconds`**
  (Distribution-via-events type) — per-event template-assignment latency
  measured at the OTLP decode → DuckDB append boundary in
  `crates/buffer/appender.rs`; emitted as individual
  `tracing::info!(target: "metric.pipeline.l1c.drain_assignment_latency_p99_microseconds", value = N, ...)`
  events for offline p99 aggregation via `jq` over the agent log per
  obs-plan §3 + §5.
Phase B planning will need to:

- Run `/andromeda-evolve --allow-arch-registry` to add the two metric
  target strings to obs-plan §5 Metric Coverage per-surface-per-path table.

- Run `/andromeda-evolve --allow-arch-registry` to add the new schema
  table `log_templates` and column `log_records.template_id` to
  architecture.md §Occupied Resources DuckDB reserved tables / schema.

- Run `/andromeda-evolve --allow-arch-registry` to add the new TauRPC
  procedure `diagnostics.template_distribution` to architecture.md
  §Occupied Resources Tauri IPC routes — this also triggers the standard
  4+1-place binding pattern (router registration + `pulse-app/capabilities/`
  JSON + `xtask EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` + `emit_taurpc_bindings` test merge).

> **Schema-name reconciliation:** chunk #69 route text + pulse-v0_2_0-route
> §67 both refer to the "logs" table. Production reserved name is
> **`log_records`** (per `crates/buffer/src/schema.rs:7-15` RESERVED_TABLES).
> Phase B amendments MUST use `log_records.template_id` (not
> `logs.template_id`) and `log_templates` (new sibling table).

- **Real-LogHub corpus validation.** Spike used synthetic corpora of
  identical shape but generated programmatically. Phase B SHOULD run
  golden-file tests against the actual LogHub Apache_2k / Linux_2k /
  HDFS_2k fixtures (https://github.com/logpai/loghub) to confirm
  template-quality measurements transfer. Spike's 60% match rate against
  seeded templates is an internal-consistency check; real-LogHub match
  rate may differ.

- **Masking regression risk.** The Apache 1/10 over-clustering is
  expected to resolve with Phase B's regex-config-driven masker, but
  the masking config is itself a tuning surface — wrong regex categories
  could yield WORSE clustering than the simple char-by-char approach.
  Phase B should add a regression-style measurement comparing match-rate
  before vs after each masking-config change.

- **Tree-depth sensitivity untested.** Spike used DEPTH=4 only. Phase B
  may want to test DEPTH=3 (more aggressive merging) and DEPTH=5 (more
  splitting) to confirm the route plan's default-4 choice. Parameter-
  sensitivity tests should land in Phase B golden-file suite.

- **`max_clusters` LRU eviction not exercised.** Spike has unbounded
  cluster count. Phase B's `max_clusters=1000` cap with LRU eviction
  introduces a state-mutation path that needs explicit tests for
  correctness (evict the right cluster on overflow) + measurement
  (eviction latency does not blow the p99 budget).

- **Persistence schema not designed.** Phase B will persist the template
  tree to corpus SQLite (chunk #68 substrate). Tree serialization format
  TBD; bincode-with-schema-version is the most natural choice (matches
  chunk #61 corpus persistence pattern). Phase B planning should
  surface this choice.

- Spike crate `crates/triage-experimental/` remains gitignored locally;
  developer may delete the directory at any time without affecting main.

- Phase B implementation re-derives Drain from clean specifications
  informed by this document; it does NOT promote spike code as-is per
  security-plan §Code Patterns hygiene.

- This findings document is an append-only audit-trail artifact per
  security-plan §Security Decisions Log convention; corrections go in a
  follow-up entry rather than retroactive edits.
