data.head: ### Chunk route#1: "Cargo workspace + 10 crate stubs — rustc 1.85+ Edition 2024 toolchain pin + workspace Cargo.toml"

body: **Constraints across domains:**

- (arch) Workspace MUST consist of exactly 10 members with reserved names LOCKED — `ingest`, `buffer`, `viz`, `ui-bridge`, `snapshot`, `workspace-detector`, `plugins`, `mcp-server` (8 library crates) + `pulse-app` (binary) + `xtask` (per arch §Occupied Resources Cargo workspace crate names + §Inherited Defaults Module boundaries).

- (arch) Library crates MUST live under `crates/<module-name>/`; binary crate is `pulse-app/` at workspace root; `xtask/` at workspace root (per arch §Infrastructure Patterns Project directory structure).

- (security) Workspace `Cargo.toml` MUST establish 10 reserved crate names exactly; module-boundary enforcement is via Cargo dependency graph not review discipline (per security plan §Threat Model Summary IPC trust boundary + CLAUDE.md Occupied Resources crate-name reservation).
- (arch) Rust edition is 2024; `rust-toolchain.toml` MUST pin to rustc 1.85+ minimum (per arch §Stack Primary language / runtime + §Established Decisions [Primary Language]).

- (security) `rust-toolchain.toml` MUST pin minimum `1.85.0` to align with workspace `edition = "2024"`; toolchain drift below 1.85 forfeits Edition 2024's security-positive defaults (`unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn`, `unsafe extern`, `static mut` reference denial, tightened `if let` temporary scopes) (per security plan §Anti-Patterns Universal + §Decisions Log open question on 1.84 → 1.85 bump).

- (arch) Cargo features MUST use `kebab-case`; defaults are minimal — `mcp-server` and `otap-ingest` are off by default; flag-specific deps (`rmcp`, OTAP-specific) only enter the build graph when feature is enabled (per arch §Conventions Feature flags + §Cross-cutting Patterns Feature-gate hygiene).
- (arch) File naming: Rust files are `snake_case.rs`; WIT files are `kebab-case.wit`; standard `cargo clippy` `style` group enforced (per arch §Conventions File naming + Variable / function naming).

- (arch) Module visibility: each crate exposes only its public contract via `pub`; cross-crate utilities use `pub(crate)`; no `pub use` across crate boundaries except in contract module (per arch §Conventions Module visibility discipline).

- (arch) Module dependency direction: dependencies flow toward `pulse-app` binary; no library depends on the binary; the dependency graph is a DAG with `pulse-app` as the only root (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns Module dependency direction).
- (arch) Build profile (release) MUST set `lto = "thin"`, `codegen-units = 1`, `strip = true` for distribution bundles in workspace `Cargo.toml` (per arch §Infrastructure Patterns Build system).

- (security) Pin every dependency by minimum version in workspace `[workspace.dependencies]` rather than per-crate floating; leave space for `tonic` / `axum` / `wasmtime` / `duckdb` resolved-version reconciliation against open Inherited Defaults questions (per security plan §Dependency Security Pinning paragraph).

- (security) `.gitignore` MUST be initialized covering `*.p12`, `*.pem`, `*.cer`, `.env*`, `*.key`, `~/.tauri/*.key` even at scaffold time so any later key-generation step (chunk 3) cannot accidentally commit private material (per security plan §Secret Management + §Anti-Patterns Secrets).

- (obs) Workspace `Cargo.toml` MUST include workspace-level entries for `tracing` 0.1, `tracing-subscriber` 0.3 (`json` + `env-filter` features), `tracing-appender` 0.2, `tracing-error` 0.2 — all 10 stubs inherit identical versions; NO OTel SDK crate (`opentelemetry`, `opentelemetry_sdk`, `opentelemetry-otlp`, `opentelemetry-stdout`) permitted as a dep of any self-observation path (per obs plan §3 Tracing init crate set + §11 Universal anti-pattern row 4).

- (obs) The 10 crate stubs MUST be named exactly per workspace reservation because span `target` values + per-module log-level mapping + per-module allowlist scrubbing keys all derive from these names (per obs plan §6 Per-module log levels table; §8 Per-module allowlist).

- (obs) The `pulse-app` binary crate MUST be the only crate that owns subscriber init / panic hook install / file appender setup; library crates MUST NOT call `tracing_subscriber::registry().init()` (per obs plan §3 Tracing init §Init order).

- (obs) `mcp-server` crate MUST be feature-gated at workspace level via `--features mcp-server` (default off); subscriber writer for that crate forced to stderr-only because stdout is reserved for JSON-RPC 2.0 framing (per obs plan §3 Logging stack last paragraph; §11 Universal anti-pattern row 5).

- (tests) Workspace MUST keep `cargo-nextest` 0.9.x as the run-time test runner contract; `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` valid as canonical `run` invocation (per test-plan §3 Bootstrap phase 1 "test-runner-install" + §4 Framework + §9 CI Pipeline structure).

- (tests) Workspace MUST keep `cargo-llvm-cov` 0.8.5 viable on all three CI matrix runners (Windows/macOS/Linux) — toolchain pin (rustc 1.85+) MUST not exclude llvm-tools-preview / llvm coverage instrumentation (per test-plan §3 Bootstrap phase 7 "coverage-tooling-install" + §10 Coverage thresholds Standard-tier).

- (tests) Tests live co-located in each crate's `src/` as `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { … }`; chunk #1 crate stubs MUST NOT introduce a separate top-level `tests/` directory pattern (per test-plan §2 Test directory + naming + §4 Conventions Test file location).

- (tests) `cargo deny check bans` MUST be enforceable at workspace level; workspace manifest + lockfile posture MUST keep `multiple-versions = "deny"` viable (no `tonic` 0.14 ↔ 0.13 duplicate via `opentelemetry-otlp 0.31`) (per test-plan §9 Cargo deny enforcement + §11 NEVER skip cargo deny check bans).

- (tests) `--features mcp-server` MUST exist as a workspace-recognized cargo feature flag from chunk #1 (default off) — even if `mcp-server` crate body lands later (per test-plan §1 Coverage triggers `security-vector-coverage: MCP feature + runtime gating`).

- (tests) Workspace + Tauri scaffold MUST resolve filesystem locations consistently with the 5-command harness PID file + log dir contract (`~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/`, `~/.andromeda-pulse/run/andromeda-pulse.pid` Linux fallback / `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` / `%LOCALAPPDATA%`) since chunk #4 wires the harness against these paths (per test-plan §3 PID file + §3 `logs` Location).
**Patterns to follow:**

- (arch) **Crate template shape**: each library crate exposes a public contract module (the only `pub` surface), `pub(crate)` internals, `thiserror`-derived error enum, and (where applicable) a TauRPC-router module mounted by `pulse-app` (per arch §Project Intent Template patterns).

- (arch) **Workspace manifest pattern**: `[workspace] members = [...]` enumerating all 10 crates plus `[workspace.dependencies]` for shared 3rd-party pins (`tokio`, `serde`, `thiserror` 2.x, `anyhow` 1.x); per-crate `Cargo.toml` references via `tokio = { workspace = true }` (per arch §Stack + §Inherited Defaults).

- (security) **Module dependency direction is unidirectional toward `pulse-app` binary**: `[workspace.members]` lists 10 crates; library crates depend only on siblings whose contract requires it; no library depends on the binary (per security plan §Threat Model Summary IPC trust boundary + CLAUDE.md Cross-cutting Patterns Module dependency direction).

- (security) **Crate scaffolding template**: per CLAUDE.md Project Intent template patterns — each library crate is "a public contract module (the only `pub` surface), `pub(crate)` internals, `thiserror`-derived error enum, and (where applicable) a TauRPC-router module mounted by `pulse-app`"; scaffold stubs even at chunk 1 should establish that shape (per security plan §Error Handling TauRPC bridge + CLAUDE.md Conventions Module visibility).

- (obs) **Workspace dependency pin pattern**: pin `tracing`-family versions in `[workspace.dependencies]` and let each crate `Cargo.toml` reference them via `tracing = { workspace = true }` (per obs plan §3 Logging stack "versions tracked in obs-research catalog; pinned at workspace level").

- (obs) **Service identity defaults pattern**: `service.name = env!("CARGO_PKG_NAME")` fallback at compile-time for crate-local resolution; bundle identifier `com.andromeda.pulse` from `tauri.conf.json` is the canonical primary value at the binary boundary (per obs plan §3 Service identity bullet 1).

- (obs) **Module-naming-as-target pattern**: crate names map directly to `tracing` event `target` field (`ingest::grpc`, `buffer::appender`, etc.) — keep crate identifiers stable from chunk #1 (per obs plan §6 Log format JSON schema example).

- (obs) **Service identity for `mcp-server` sidecar**: `service.name = "andromeda-pulse-mcp"` distinct from main app — reserved per crate name + arch convention (per obs plan §3 Service identity bullet 1 sub-clause).

- (tests) **Crate-per-module workspace shape** — each library crate is the natural home for `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { … }` and per-crate fixture builders (`MockTraceSpan`, `MockArrowBatch`, `MockMetricPoint`) (per test-plan §3 Bootstrap phase 6 + §4 What unit tests cover).

- (tests) `cargo nextest` 0.9.x with `--profile ci` and per-process isolation as the default test invocation — chosen over `cargo test` from chunk #1 onwards so port-binding integration tests in later epochs do not collide (per test-plan §9 Pipeline structure + §12 Decisions Log).
**Anti-patterns to avoid:**

- (arch) **NEVER rename or repurpose any of the 10 reserved workspace crate names** — collapsing modules into a single-crate `mod` directory voids the modular-monolith boundary discipline (per arch §Established Decisions Module Boundaries + §Occupied Resources).
- (arch) **NEVER add a library-crate → `pulse-app` dependency** — the dependency graph is a DAG with `pulse-app` as the only root (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns Module dependency direction).

- (arch) **NEVER add `rmcp` or OTAP-specific dependencies to the default build graph** — both must enter only behind their respective `--features` flags (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns Feature-gate hygiene).

- (security) NEVER let `rust-toolchain.toml` ship below `1.85.0`; the security plan §Decisions Log explicitly flags the prior `1.84` minimum as a residual issue requiring bump before any release (per security plan §Anti-Patterns Universal + §Decisions Log).

- (obs) NEVER add any OTel SDK crate (`opentelemetry`, `opentelemetry_sdk`, `opentelemetry-otlp`, `opentelemetry-stdout`) to workspace `[dependencies]` for self-observation; only `tonic` / `axum` / `prost` / `opentelemetry-proto` (wire-format-only) are permitted, and only in `ingest` for external OTLP decoding (per obs plan §11 Universal anti-pattern row 4; §12 Decisions Log 2026-05-02 user review pivot).

- (obs) NEVER hardcode `service.name = "andromeda-pulse"` or any literal string in a library crate — always derive from `env!("CARGO_PKG_NAME")` or read bundle identifier from `tauri.conf.json` (per obs plan §11 "NEVER hardcode service identity").
- (obs) NEVER let library crates initialize a subscriber in tests / examples — only `pulse-app/src/main.rs` owns init order (per obs plan §3 Tracing init §Init order).

- (tests) NEVER introduce a separate top-level `tests/` directory at workspace root for unit tests — co-located `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` is the convention; a `tests/fixtures/plugins/` for WASM fixtures is the only sanctioned exception (per test-plan §2 + §7 WASM fixtures).

- (tests) NEVER admit a `tonic` 0.13 transitive duplicate via `opentelemetry-otlp` (or any other dep) into the workspace lockfile — must keep `cargo deny check bans multiple-versions = "deny"` green (per test-plan §11 + §9 Cargo deny enforcement).
**Acceptance criteria contributions:**

- (arch) Workspace `Cargo.toml` declares exactly 10 members with reserved names; `cargo metadata --format-version 1 | jq '.workspace_members | length'` returns `10`; names match reserved set in arch §Occupied Resources.
- (arch) `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` passes with all 8 library crates resolving as `crates/<module-name>/` and `pulse-app/` + `xtask/` at workspace root.
- (arch) `rust-toolchain.toml` pins `channel = "1.85.0"` (or higher); `edition = "2024"` is set in workspace `Cargo.toml` (or per-crate); `cargo --version` in CI produces the pinned version.
- (arch) Module dependency direction enforced: `cargo tree --workspace` shows zero edges from any `crates/*` library crate back to `pulse-app`; `pulse-app` is the only root of the DAG.

- (arch) Cargo features default-off discipline: `cargo metadata` shows `mcp-server` and `otap-ingest` features defined but not in default feature set; `rmcp` does not appear in default-feature dependency closure.
- (security) `rust-toolchain.toml` declares `channel = "1.85.0"` (or higher); `grep -E '^channel = "1\.(8[5-9]|9[0-9])'` matches.
- (security) Workspace `Cargo.toml` `[workspace] members` list contains exactly the 10 reserved names; no extra crates, no missing crates.
- (security) `.gitignore` includes patterns `*.p12`, `*.pem`, `*.cer`, `.env*`, `*.key`, `~/.tauri/*.key`; `git check-ignore` passes for each.

- (obs) Workspace `Cargo.toml` `[workspace.dependencies]` table contains: `tracing = "0.1"`, `tracing-subscriber = { version = "0.3", features = ["json", "env-filter"] }`, `tracing-appender = "0.2"`, `tracing-error = "0.2"`; `cargo tree -e normal` shows ZERO crate matching `^opentelemetry($|_sdk|-otlp|-stdout)` in dependency closure of any non-`ingest` crate.
- (obs) The 10 reserved crate names appear verbatim in `[workspace.members]`; `cargo metadata --format-version 1 | jq -r '.workspace_members[]'` lists exactly these.
- (tests) `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` is a valid invocation against the chunk #1 workspace (zero tests acceptable; runner must resolve and exit 0).
- (tests) `cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --lcov --output-path lcov.info --summary-only` runs to completion against chunk #1 workspace on Linux/macOS/Windows hosts.
- (tests) `cargo deny check bans` passes against workspace lockfile — no banned crates and no duplicate `tonic` versions.
- (tests) Chunk #1 workspace contains exactly the 10 reserved members; `cargo metadata --format-version 1 | jq '.workspace_members | length'` returns 10.

title: Chunk route#2: "Tauri 2 scaffold + capability JSON files — `pulse-app/` + `tauri.conf.json` + 5 capabilities + bundle id `com.andromeda.pulse`"

data.head: ### Chunk route#2: "Tauri 2 scaffold + capability JSON files — `pulse-app/` + `tauri.conf.json` + 5 capabilities + bundle id `com.andromeda.pulse`"

body: **Constraints across domains:**

- (arch) Tauri 2 bundle identifier is locked to `com.andromeda.pulse`; binary name is `andromeda-pulse` (Linux/macOS) / `andromeda-pulse.exe` (Windows); rmcp sidecar binary (when feature enabled) is `andromeda-pulse-mcp` (per arch §Occupied Resources Process / service identity).

- (arch) The 5 capability identifiers reserved at arch level are exactly: `pulse:default`, `pulse:tray`, `pulse:notification`, `pulse:updater`, `pulse:plugin-fs`. Concrete capability JSON files MUST live in `pulse-app/capabilities/` (per arch §Occupied Resources Tauri capability identifiers).

- (arch) Webview IPC capability policy is negative-default: `pulse:default` permits exactly the TauRPC procedures enumerated in Occupied Resources and nothing else; Tauri core APIs (`fs`, `shell`, `dialog`, `http`) are NOT granted to `pulse:default` (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns Webview IPC capability policy).

- (security) `pulse-app/capabilities/` MUST contain exactly 5 capability JSON files for `pulse:default`, `pulse:tray`, `pulse:notification`, `pulse:updater`, `pulse:plugin-fs`; Tauri capabilities are negative-default — webview not matching any capability has zero IPC access (per security plan §API Security TauRPC capability authorization + §Anti-Patterns API).

- (security) `pulse:default` capability JSON at scaffold time MUST enumerate only the 5 top-level introspection procedures (`app_info`, `health`, `ready`, `get_settings`, `update_settings`); per-router procedures (`traces.*`, `metrics.*`, etc.) get added when the owning crate lands its router (per security plan §Input Validation TauRPC bridge boundary + §API Security TauRPC capability authorization).

- (security) `pulse:updater` capability MUST NOT be exposed to webview JavaScript — bound to `tauri-plugin-updater` flow only; `pulse:notification` and `pulse:tray` MUST be outbound-emit-only (no webview-side input handlers / notification action callbacks / tray-menu IPC re-entry); `pulse:plugin-fs` MUST stay scoped to host's read of canonicalized plugin dir (per security plan §Anti-Patterns API + §Threat Model Summary trust boundaries).

- (security) `tauri.conf.json` `app.security.csp` MUST be explicit: `"default-src 'self' ipc: http://ipc.localhost; img-src 'self' data:; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; script-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' ipc: http://ipc.localhost; worker-src 'self' blob:"` — `worker-src blob:` required for WebGPU; NEVER add `'unsafe-inline'` to `script-src`; NO remote content (per security plan §API Security CSP).

- (security) `tauri.conf.json` MUST embed only the Tauri updater Minisign **public** key (no private key, no `.key` file in repo); private key custody belongs in Azure Key Vault (per security plan §Secret Management + §Anti-Patterns Data Protection / Secrets — full key generation lands in chunk 3).

- (security) Bundle identifier MUST be exactly `com.andromeda.pulse`; binary name MUST be `andromeda-pulse` / `andromeda-pulse.exe`; binary crate MUST be `pulse-app` (per security plan §Threat Model Summary Process / service identity via Occupied Resources).

- (design) `pulse-app/tauri.conf.json` MUST set `"decorations": false` on the main window so the custom-drawn 32px titlebar can be implemented downstream (per design-system.md §Surface: desktop-webview / Component Patterns / Navigation / App Shell / Platform-Specific Notes).

- (design) `pulse-app/tauri.conf.json` (or scaffolded webview HTML/CSS shell) MUST establish `prefers-color-scheme: dark` as the default color scheme; light and auto are downstream Settings options only (per design-system.md §Surface: desktop-webview / Tokens "Dark mode default" + §Brand Identity "dark-first aesthetic").

- (design) The CSP policy in `tauri.conf.json` MUST be `script-src 'self'` with NO third-party CDN allowance — fonts (JetBrains Mono / IBM Plex Sans WOFF2) and WGSL shaders bundle locally (per design-system.md §Surface: desktop-webview / "CSP policy" + §Typography "Loading: Bundled self-hosted WOFF2 ... no CDN").

- (design) The `pulse-app/ui/` webview source root MUST be scaffolded so downstream Foundation chunks (design tokens bundle, iconography registry) can land Tailwind v4 `@theme` block + WOFF2 fonts at `pulse-app/ui/public/fonts/` + custom SVG icons at `pulse-app/ui/src/components/icons/` (per design-system.md §Typography "Loading" + §Iconography + §Downstream Readiness).

- (layouts) Tauri window configuration MUST support frameless / custom-titlebar windows for both compact widget and full dashboard surfaces — both webview surfaces use `data-tauri-drag-region` on a custom titlebar container (per layout-templates.md §desktop-webview Component — Custom titlebar).

- (layouts) Tauri tray substrate MUST support a single monochrome SVG glyph plus a secondary always-on-top click-through composited overlay window (for the WebGPU Halo Pulse layer) — initial scaffold capability JSON cannot lock the tray into a single-window-only model (per layout-templates.md §desktop-native Component — Tray icon, Option A WebGPU preferred).

- (layouts) Compact widget window scaffold MUST permit always-on-top + snap-to-edge + fixed quarter-screen sizing semantics; full dashboard window scaffold MUST permit resizable defaults — distinct window configurations in `tauri.conf.json` (per layout-templates.md §desktop-webview Primary screens + §IA notes Navigation model).

- (layouts) Close-button behavior on the compact widget MUST minimize-to-tray rather than terminate the process — only the tray menu "Quit" terminates (per layout-templates.md §desktop-native Tray menu wireframe + §desktop-webview IA notes).

- (layouts) The 5 capability JSON files MUST account for the three planned surfaces — `pulse:default` for the main webview windows (compact widget + full dashboard share TauRPC procedures), `pulse:tray` for the OS-native tray, `pulse:notification` for OS-native toasts; `pulse:updater` and `pulse:plugin-fs` are non-surface capabilities (per CLAUDE.md §Occupied Resources cross-referenced with layout-templates.md §desktop-native Component — Notifications).

- (a11y) Tauri webview HTML root MUST declare `lang="en"` (single-language English app per a11y plan §1 SC 3.1.1 explicit non-applicability decision); scaffold this attribute when `pulse-app/ui/` index.html is created so SC 3.1.1 baseline is met from first render (per a11y plan §1 WCAG SCs explicitly not applicable).

- (a11y) Tauri main webview window scaffolded in `tauri.conf.json` MUST plan for keyboard-accessible window chrome — close → minimize-to-tray policy + Esc as escape path; chunk #2 must not scaffold a window config that prevents later Esc handler binding (per a11y plan §5 Keyboard Navigation).

- (a11y) The 5 capability JSON files MUST follow the negative-default discipline so later UI surfaces depend on a known capability surface — `pulse:notification` and `pulse:tray` are outbound-emit only at this scaffold (per a11y plan §3 Critical Paths P3 OS notification surface).

- (a11y) `service.name` MUST be the compile-time constant `"com.andromeda.pulse"` and the Tauri bundle identifier in `tauri.conf.json` MUST match exactly — a11y violation JSON emissions tag with this value for cross-correlation with obs traces (per a11y plan §1 Service Identity Tagging row + §9 CI-specific resource attributes).

- (a11y) Webview index.html scaffolded by chunk #2 MUST set up a single-`<main>` landmark structure expectation (no scaffold that injects multiple `<main>` landmarks or omits `<main>` entirely) — a literal placeholder `<main>` in the scaffolded index.html anchors this invariant (per a11y plan §7 Landmark roles + §4 desktop-webview required landmarks).

- (a11y) Tauri build profile + `tauri.conf.json` MUST NOT enable any mode that prevents later WebView2 / WKWebView DevTools Protocol attachment in CI — devtools must be reachable from `@axe-core/playwright` 4.11.x at route#13+ (per a11y plan §1 desktop-webview "Tauri webview a11y tree exposed via DevTools Protocol").

- (obs) The Tauri bundle identifier in `tauri.conf.json` MUST be exactly `com.andromeda.pulse`; this string IS the compile-time `service.name` constant for every JSON log line and the source-of-truth for `service.name` field at subscriber init (per obs plan §3 Service identity row 1; §Standard Contracts in CLAUDE.md `app_info.name`).

- (tests) Tauri 2 scaffold MUST preserve `tauri::test::mock_builder()` + `get_ipc_response()` integration-test path — `tauri.conf.json` + capability files MUST not block the `tauri::test` module integration usage (per test-plan §3 `status` command body + §5 Drivers Module ↔ TauRPC IPC + §6 E2E Drivers).

- (tests) Capability JSON files in `pulse-app/capabilities/` MUST stay in lockstep with TauRPC procedure registration — drift between crate-side router and capability JSON entries MUST be caught by an `xtask capability-drift` check (per test-plan §1 Coverage triggers `security-vector-coverage: Tauri IPC capability gating`).
**Patterns to follow:**

- (arch) **Tauri scaffold layout**: `pulse-app/` contains `Cargo.toml`, `tauri.conf.json`, `capabilities/` (one JSON file per capability identifier), `icons/`, `src/main.rs` + `src/lib.rs`, and `ui/` for webview source root (per arch §Infrastructure Patterns Project directory structure).

- (arch) **Updater public-key embedding**: Tauri updater public key (Minisign Ed25519) shipped baked into `tauri.conf.json` (the `latest.json` updater channel anchor) — placeholder is acceptable in chunk #2; real key generation lands in chunk #3 (per arch §Occupied Resources Updater channel).

- (arch) **Reserved env-var namespace `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_*`**: 9 reserved env vars (`*_CONFIG_PATH`, `*_DATA_DIR`, `*_OTLP_GRPC_PORT`, `*_OTLP_HTTP_PORT`, `*_RETENTION_SECONDS`, `*_LOG_LEVEL`, `*_MCP_ENABLED`, `*_PLUGIN_DIR`, plus `RUST_LOG` fallback); new env vars require scope-arch (per arch §Occupied Resources Environment variables).

- (security) **Capability JSON shape matches existing project conventions**: each of the 5 files declares `identifier` + `windows` (the webview window) + `permissions` array; `pulse:default` permissions list is the authoritative procedure-allowlist that `xtask capability-drift` (chunk 4) compares against TauRPC routers (per security plan §API Security TauRPC capability authorization).

- (design) **Frameless main window with custom-drawn 32px titlebar** (drag region + window controls) is the established App Shell pattern across all three platforms; `tauri.conf.json` enables it via `decorations: false` so downstream titlebar implementation is unblocked (per design-system.md §Surface: desktop-webview Component Patterns + Platform-Specific Notes for Windows/macOS/Linux).

- (design) **Window close behavior is "minimize-to-tray, not terminate-process"** (terminate requires explicit Quit menu item) — `tauri.conf.json` window event configuration must align so the tray-icon-as-always-on surface contract holds (per CLAUDE.md @architecture.md §Cross-cutting Patterns Tray icon policy + design-system.md §Surface: desktop-native).

- (design) **Local-bundled assets pattern**: any future visual assets (fonts, icons, shaders) live under `pulse-app/ui/` rooted at the bundle, NEVER referenced from a third-party CDN — applies retroactively from chunk #2 (per design-system.md §Typography "Loading" + §Surface: desktop-webview "CSP policy" + Universal Bans).

- (layouts) **Custom frameless titlebar shared between compact widget and full dashboard**: `[app-icon + title | grow | settings-button | window-controls]` flex layout with `data-tauri-drag-region` on the container — `tauri.conf.json` must support this (per layout-templates.md §desktop-webview Component — Custom titlebar).

- (layouts) **Three-surface coherence pattern**: compact widget (glance), full dashboard (exploration), tray icon (ambient status) all share the same TauRPC data feed via broadcast channels — capability JSON should not artificially partition these three surfaces from the shared `traces.*` / `metrics.*` / `logs.*` IPC surface (per layout-templates.md §desktop-webview IA notes Multi-surface coordination + §desktop-native IA notes Cross-surface coordination).

- (layouts) **Platform-native tray adapter pattern**: tray icon uses `NSStatusItem` (macOS), `NotifyIcon` (Windows), `AppIndicator`/`StatusNotifier` (Linux); Tauri scaffold should leave platform-specific tray protocol selection to Tauri 2 abstractions rather than locking to a single-platform impl (per layout-templates.md §desktop-native Platform-specific notes).

- (a11y) **Semantic HTML first, ARIA second**: when `pulse-app/ui/` index.html is scaffolded, use native `<main>` / `<nav>` / `<header>` / `<button>` placeholders rather than `<div role="...">` (per a11y plan §4 ARIA Patterns + §11 ARIA anti-pattern).

- (a11y) **Capability JSON file naming uses kebab-case identifiers** (`pulse:default` / `pulse:tray` / `pulse:notification` / `pulse:updater` / `pulse:plugin-fs`) per architecture.md §Occupied Resources reserved set; this naming surface is the same hook the later TauRPC procedure surface attaches to (per a11y plan §3 Critical Paths P5 tray-icon + P3 OS notification).

- (a11y) **Foundation epoch a11y dev stack absorbs all 9 a11y bootstrap items at route#13** — chunks #1–#2 must NOT pre-empt or fragment this consolidated install; defer all `npm install` of a11y libraries to route#13 (per a11y plan §3.5 Bootstrap phases).

- (tests) **5 capability JSON files mirror the architecture's reserved capability identifiers** — the negative-default capability discipline is what makes the capability-drift test enforceable (per test-plan §1 Coverage triggers `security-vector-coverage: Tauri IPC capability gating`).
**Anti-patterns to avoid:**

- (arch) **NEVER grant Tauri core APIs (`fs`, `shell`, `dialog`, `http`) to `pulse:default`** without an explicit per-feature capability addition with stated rationale (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns Webview IPC capability policy).
- (arch) **NEVER expose `pulse:updater` to webview JavaScript** — bound to `tauri-plugin-updater` flow only (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns Webview IPC capability policy).

- (security) NEVER omit a capability JSON entry for any TauRPC procedure declared in a router — even at scaffold time the 5 top-level introspection procedures need their entries in `pulse:default` or the bridge call is silently rejected at runtime (per security plan §Anti-Patterns API).

- (security) NEVER widen `pulse:plugin-fs` to webview JavaScript / write / execute scope at scaffold time — converts an internal plugin-loader capability into an unconstrained filesystem-read primitive (per security plan §Anti-Patterns API).

- (design) NEVER configure the webview to allow third-party CDN script/font/style sources in CSP — even at scaffolding stage; relaxing it now creates a downstream regression surface (per design-system.md §Surface: desktop-webview "CSP policy: `script-src 'self'`").

- (design) NEVER ship `tauri.conf.json` with default OS-decorations enabled — losing the frameless window invalidates the custom titlebar + traffic-light/control-button positioning conventions (per design-system.md §Per-Surface Bans / desktop-webview + §Component Patterns titlebar specification).
- (design) NEVER configure default light-mode-only color scheme — dark-first is brand identity, not a preference (per design-system.md §Brand Identity "dark-first aesthetic" + Universal Bans).

- (layouts) Do NOT scaffold a single fixed Tauri window definition that conflates compact widget + full dashboard semantics — they have distinct sizing, distinct always-on-top behavior, and distinct chrome (per layout-templates.md §desktop-webview Primary screens).

- (layouts) Do NOT enable Tauri's default OS-chrome titlebar in chunk 2's `tauri.conf.json` — both webview surfaces use a custom frameless titlebar (per layout-templates.md §desktop-webview Component — Custom titlebar).

- (layouts) Do NOT scaffold a tray capability that forbids secondary always-on-top click-through windows — the WebGPU Halo Pulse overlay around the tray glyph requires a secondary composited surface (per layout-templates.md §desktop-native Component — Tray icon Option A).
- (a11y) NEVER scaffold the webview index.html (chunk #2) without `<html lang="en">` — would create an SC 3.1.1-violating baseline (per a11y plan §1 explicit non-applicability claim).

- (a11y) NEVER hardcode `outline: none` / `*:focus { outline: 0 }` in any scaffolded global stylesheet shipped with chunk #2 — would violate SC 2.4.7 Focus Visible (per a11y plan §11 Keyboard anti-pattern). Chunk #2 should ship either no global focus reset or one that preserves the browser default until the design tokens bundle (route#10) introduces `--border-focus`.

- (a11y) NEVER scaffold `tauri.conf.json` with `"identifier"` mismatched against `service.name` `"com.andromeda.pulse"` — a11y violation JSON cross-correlation with obs traces depends on the bundle ID being canonical service identity (per a11y plan §9 CI-specific resource attributes).

- (tests) NEVER add a TauRPC procedure entry to a capability JSON file that is not paired with an actual router registration — the capability-drift xtask check is meant to fail the build on either-side-only entries (per test-plan §1 + §1 Anti-Pattern).

title: Phase 1 Plan — chunks route#1..route#2: "Cargo workspace + 10 crate stubs + Tauri 2 scaffold + capability JSON files"

data.head: # Phase 1 Plan — chunks route#1..route#2: "Cargo workspace + 10 crate stubs + Tauri 2 scaffold + capability JSON files"

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase Phase 4. Read by /andromeda-implement.
Manual edits between runs are fine; do not edit during /implement run._
- **Phase number:** 1

- **Route chunks covered:**
  - route#1 "Cargo workspace + 10 crate stubs — rustc 1.85+ Edition 2024 toolchain pin + workspace Cargo.toml"
  - route#2 "Tauri 2 scaffold + capability JSON files — `pulse-app/` + `tauri.conf.json` + 5 capabilities + bundle id `com.andromeda.pulse`"
- **Epoch:** Epoch 1 — Foundation

Materialize the Cargo workspace + Tauri 2 scaffold that every subsequent Foundation chunk and every feature epoch depends on, locking ten reserved crate names (`ingest`, `buffer`, `viz`, `ui-bridge`, `snapshot`, `workspace-detector`, `plugins`, `mcp-server`, `pulse-app`, `xtask`) at the workspace level and pinning `rustc 1.85+ Edition 2024` so security-positive defaults (`unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn`, tightened `if let` temporary scopes) are in force from the first commit. The workspace also declares the obs `tracing`-family dependencies (`tracing` 0.1, `tracing-subscriber` 0.3 with `json+env-filter`, `tracing-appender` 0.2, `tracing-error` 0.2) and reserves the `mcp-server` and `otap-ingest` cargo features default-off — so the no-OTel-SDK self-observation invariant and the feature-gate hygiene rule are enforceable from `cargo deny check bans` onward (per arch §Inherited Defaults + obs plan §3 + security plan §Anti-Patterns Universal + tests plan §3 Bootstrap).

The Tauri 2 layer (chunk #2) lands the binary scaffold inside `pulse-app/` — `tauri.conf.json` with bundle identifier `com.andromeda.pulse` (the obs `service.name` source-of-truth + a11y violation JSON tag), CSP `script-src 'self'` with `worker-src 'self' blob:` for WebGPU, frameless windows for the compact widget + full dashboard surfaces, and the negative-default capability JSON inventory (`pulse:default`, `pulse:tray`, `pulse:notification`, `pulse:updater`, `pulse:plugin-fs`) that the `xtask capability-drift` check will diff against TauRPC routers from chunk #4 onward. The webview source root `pulse-app/ui/` is established with `<html lang="en">` + a single `<main>` landmark so SC 3.1.1 and SC 4.1.2 baselines hold from the first render — no design tokens or a11y harness yet (those land at routes #10-#15) but the substrate must not preclude them.

The pre-baked agent-run.sh / agent-run.ps1 harness already encodes the binding contract (`cargo run --bin pulse-app`, `cargo xtask harness:status`, `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci`, env vars `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_*`); chunks #1-#2 must satisfy its assumptions without modifying it. After this phase, `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo deny check bans` pass against an empty-but-structurally-correct workspace; `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` resolves with zero tests; the Tauri 2 binary builds (`cargo tauri build` — though full bundle output deferred to chunk #3 once signing keys land).

title: From route#1: "Cargo workspace + 10 crate stubs — rustc 1.85+ Edition 2024 toolchain pin + workspace Cargo.toml"

data.head: ### From route#1: "Cargo workspace + 10 crate stubs — rustc 1.85+ Edition 2024 toolchain pin + workspace Cargo.toml"

body: 1. Create `rust-toolchain.toml` at workspace root pinning `channel = "1.85.0"` with `components = ["rustfmt", "clippy", "llvm-tools-preview"]` (llvm-tools-preview required for chunk #5's `cargo-llvm-cov` coverage gate).

2. Create workspace-root `Cargo.toml` declaring `[workspace] resolver = "2"`, `members = ["crates/*", "pulse-app", "xtask"]`, `[workspace.package]` shared `edition = "2024"` + `rust-version = "1.85"` + `license = "MIT"` + repository fields. Add `[workspace.dependencies]` with the obs-required pins (`tracing`, `tracing-subscriber` with `json+env-filter`, `tracing-appender`, `tracing-error`) plus tokio (workspace-level pin to whatever current stable resolves) + serde (with `derive` feature) + thiserror 2.x + anyhow 1.x. Set release profile `lto = "thin"`, `codegen-units = 1`, `strip = true`.

3. Create `deny.toml` minimal cargo-deny config: `[bans] multiple-versions = "deny"` (with empty skip list — the `tonic 0.14 ↔ tonic 0.13` reconciliation is open and surfaces here when ingest body lands), `[licenses]` allowlist of OSS-compatible licenses (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-3-Clause, ISC, Unicode-DFS-2016, MPL-2.0), `[advisories]` defaults, `[sources] unknown-registry = "warn"`.

4. Create `crates/<name>/Cargo.toml` + `crates/<name>/src/lib.rs` for each of the 8 library crates (`ingest`, `buffer`, `viz`, `ui-bridge`, `snapshot`, `workspace-detector`, `plugins`, `mcp-server`). Each `Cargo.toml`: `[package] name = "<name>"`, `version.workspace = true`, `edition.workspace = true`, `rust-version.workspace = true`, `license.workspace = true`. Each `lib.rs`: `pub mod contract;` placeholder + a `thiserror`-derived `Error` enum at `pub` boundary. NO subscriber init in any library crate. NO cross-crate dependencies at this stage.
5. Create `mcp-server` crate with `[features] default = []` empty; rmcp dependency stays absent until route#42-43 (mcp-server crate body chunks).

6. Create `pulse-app/Cargo.toml` declaring `[package] name = "pulse-app"`, `[[bin]] name = "pulse-app" path = "src/main.rs"`. Initially minimal `[dependencies]` (tokio + tracing) — chunk #2 expands. Declare `[features] default = []`, `mcp-server = ["mcp-server-crate"]` (where `mcp-server-crate = { path = "../crates/mcp-server", optional = true }`) + `otap-ingest = []` placeholder.
7. Create `pulse-app/src/main.rs` minimal `fn main() {}` placeholder; chunk #2 wires `tauri::Builder`.

8. Create `xtask/Cargo.toml` declaring `[package] name = "xtask"`, `[[bin]] name = "xtask"`. Initially minimal `[dependencies]` (e.g., `clap` or `argh` for arg parsing — choose one for entire phase-1; `clap` recommended for ecosystem familiarity). NO library content.
9. Create `xtask/src/main.rs` placeholder that prints "xtask placeholder" or invokes the unimplemented `harness:status` subcommand stub (full implementation lands at route#4).

10. Verify `cargo metadata --format-version 1 | jq '.workspace_members | length'` returns `10`. Verify `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` passes (no compile errors). Verify `cargo deny check bans` passes against the lockfile (no banned crates, no duplicate versions). Verify `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` resolves (zero tests acceptable; runner exits 0).

title: From route#2: "Tauri 2 scaffold + capability JSON files — `pulse-app/` + `tauri.conf.json` + 5 capabilities + bundle id `com.andromeda.pulse`"

data.head: ### From route#2: "Tauri 2 scaffold + capability JSON files — `pulse-app/` + `tauri.conf.json` + 5 capabilities + bundle id `com.andromeda.pulse`"

body: 1. Modify workspace `Cargo.toml` `[workspace.dependencies]` adding `tauri = { version = "2", features = ["..."] }` + `tauri-build = { version = "2", features = [] }` (initial features minimal; subsequent chunks add `tauri-plugin-updater`, `tauri-plugin-notification` via their respective Foundation chunks).

2. Modify `pulse-app/Cargo.toml` adding `tauri = { workspace = true, features = ["custom-protocol"] }` to `[dependencies]` and `tauri-build = { workspace = true }` to `[build-dependencies]`. Add `[lib] crate-type = ["staticlib", "cdylib", "rlib"]` if Tauri 2 conventions require it (verify against current Tauri 2 docs at materialize time — Tauri 2 typically uses `pulse-app/src/lib.rs` + a thin `pulse-app/src/main.rs` shim).
3. Create `pulse-app/build.rs`: `fn main() { tauri_build::build() }`.

4. Create `pulse-app/tauri.conf.json` with `productName: "andromeda-pulse"`, `identifier: "com.andromeda.pulse"`, `version: "0.1.0"`, `build.frontendDist: "../ui/dist"` (or appropriate per Tauri 2 schema; design tokens chunk later wires the actual bundler). Declare `app.windows: [{ "label": "compact-widget", width: 480, height: 270, alwaysOnTop: true, resizable: false, decorations: false, visible: false }, { "label": "main", width: 1280, height: 800, decorations: false, resizable: true, visible: false }]`. Declare `app.security.csp` literal: `"default-src 'self' ipc: http://ipc.localhost; img-src 'self' data:; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; script-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' ipc: http://ipc.localhost; worker-src 'self' blob:"`. Declare `bundle.targets: ["msi", "dmg", "appimage", "deb"]` + `bundle.icon: ["icons/32x32.png", "icons/128x128.png", "icons/128x128@2x.png", "icons/icon.icns", "icons/icon.ico"]`. Declare `plugins.updater.endpoints: []` (chunk #3 wires `latest.json` URL) and `plugins.updater.pubkey: ""` placeholder.

5. Create placeholder icon files at `pulse-app/icons/{32x32.png, 128x128.png, 128x128@2x.png, icon.icns, icon.ico}` — 1×1 transparent PNG / minimal valid ICO + ICNS. Final artwork from design specialist deferred.

6. Create `pulse-app/capabilities/default.json` declaring `identifier: "default"`, `description`, `local: true`, `windows: ["compact-widget", "main"]`, `permissions: []` (initially empty per Phase 6 open-question note — populated as routers land via chunk #4 capability-drift gate; Phase 6 user review should resolve whether to pre-populate the 5 introspection procedure permissions in chunk #2 or defer to chunk #22).

7. Create `pulse-app/capabilities/tray.json` (`identifier: "tray"`, scoped to outbound-emit), `notification.json` (`identifier: "notification"`, scoped to outbound-emit), `updater.json` (`identifier: "updater"`, scoped to `tauri-plugin-updater` flow only — NOT exposed to webview JavaScript; `windows: []` or omit), and `plugin-fs.json` (`identifier: "plugin-fs"`, scoped to host's read of canonicalized plugin dir; NOT widened to webview/write/execute).

8. Create `pulse-app/ui/index.html` minimal: `<!doctype html><html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><title>andromeda-pulse</title></head><body><main></main></body></html>`. NO global `outline: none`; NO third-party CDN script/font references; no inline scripts (CSP `script-src 'self'`).

9. Create `pulse-app/ui/src/.gitkeep` and `pulse-app/ui/public/.gitkeep` so the directories exist for design tokens (route#10) and a11y dev stack (route#13) to scaffold into without further parent-directory creation.

10. Modify `pulse-app/src/main.rs` to wire a minimal `tauri::Builder::default().invoke_handler(tauri::generate_handler![]).run(tauri::generate_context!()).expect("...")` entry point. Subscriber init does NOT land here (route#7 wires `tracing-subscriber` JSON registry).

11. Verify `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` still passes after Tauri deps added. Verify `jq '.identifier' pulse-app/tauri.conf.json` returns `"com.andromeda.pulse"`. Verify `pulse-app/capabilities/` has exactly 5 JSON files. Verify `grep -E "script-src 'self'" pulse-app/tauri.conf.json` matches and `grep '"unsafe-inline"' pulse-app/tauri.conf.json | grep "script-src"` returns nothing. Verify `grep -E '"core:(fs|shell|dialog|http)' pulse-app/capabilities/default.json` returns empty. Verify `pulse-app/ui/index.html` contains `<html lang="en">`.

body: - `pulse-app/tauri.conf.json` — Tauri 2 config with `productName: "andromeda-pulse"`, `identifier: "com.andromeda.pulse"`, `version: "0.1.0"`. `app.windows` declares two webview windows (compact-widget: 480×270 fixed alwaysOnTop decorations:false; main: 1280×800 resizable decorations:false visible:false). `app.security.csp` literal per security extract. `bundle.targets: ["msi", "dmg", "appimage", "deb"]`. `plugins.updater.pubkey: ""` placeholder (chunk #3 fills with real Minisign Ed25519 public key). `bundle.icon` references `icons/{32x32.png, 128x128.png, 128x128@2x.png, icon.icns, icon.ico}` (placeholder transparent PNGs at minimum).

Per Tauri 2 capability schema, `identifier` is the local name; the namespace is the bundle id prefix added implicitly. Verify via Tauri 2 docs in implementation.); `windows: ["compact-widget", "main"]`; `permissions: []` initially or just listing the 5 introspection TauRPC procedure permission identifiers when their definitions land. title: Phase 10 Plan — chunk route#13: "A11y dev stack install"

data.head: # Phase 10 Plan — chunk route#13: "A11y dev stack install"

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase Phase 4. Read by /andromeda-implement.
Manual edits between runs are fine; do not edit during /implement run._
- **Phase number:** 10

- **Route chunks covered:**
  - route#13 "A11y dev stack install — axe-core/playwright 4.11 + Lighthouse 12 + pa11y 9 + react-aria-components 1.17 + focus-trap-react 12 + tabbable 6.4 + eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y 6.10"
- **Epoch:** 1 — Foundation

Land the accessibility dev-stack substrate the project needs before any UI surface chunk (#21+ Visualization) can be shipped: a runtime ARIA primitive layer (`react-aria-components` + `focus-trap-react` + `tabbable`), an automated assertion harness (`@axe-core/playwright` + `axe-core` + `lighthouse` + `pa11y` + `pa11y-ci`), and a compile-time gate (`eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y` + the ESLint base it requires). Per a11y-plan §3.5 Bootstrap phases (a11y-tooling-install + focus-management-library-install + aria-component-library-install + a11y-linting-install), tier=Standard targeting WCAG 2.1 AA + AAA escalation for SC 2.3.3. Per arch §Infrastructure Patterns, all webview tooling colocates under `pulse-app/ui/` with `cargo xtask <task>` providing the cross-platform agent-driven canonical command surface; chunk #13 reserves `xtask lint` (functional) + `xtask test:a11y` (placeholder, activates at chunk #25 webview shell + chunk #46 CI gate).

This is install-only scope: dependencies land, ESLint flat config wires `plugin:jsx-a11y/recommended`, axe-core configuration is captured in a smoke fixture, but no runtime DOM is asserted yet (no UI shell exists; `Icon.test.tsx` from chunk #11 is the only existing webview test). Downstream consumption: chunk #25 webview shell wraps `react-aria-components` Tabs/Dialog/Form primitives in token-styled wrappers; chunk #46 wires `npm run test:a11y` into `ci.yml` as a separate job mirroring the supply-chain gate pattern.

The chunk title abbreviates 7 packages; the functional install requires implicit peers (`@playwright/test` for `@axe-core/playwright`, `axe-core` standalone for the runtime API per a11y rule file, `eslint` 9.x base + `typescript-eslint` + `eslint-plugin-react` + `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` + `globals` for jsx-a11y to function per a11y plan anti-pattern "NEVER install without extending plugin:jsx-a11y/recommended"). Total: 15 new packages — 12 devDependencies + 3 dependencies. This expansion is surfaced explicitly in Phase 6 user review.

1. **Add devDependencies + dependencies to `pulse-app/ui/package.json`** (single `npm install --save-dev <list> --save <list>` invocation; `package-lock.json` regenerates).
   - `devDependencies` additions: `@axe-core/playwright@^4.11.0`, `axe-core@^4.11.0`, `@playwright/test@^1.x` (latest 1.x at install time), `lighthouse@^12.0.0`, `pa11y@^9.0.0`, `pa11y-ci@^4.0.0`, `eslint@^9.x`, `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y@^6.10.0`, `typescript-eslint@^8.x`, `eslint-plugin-react@^7.x`, `eslint-plugin-react-hooks@^5.x`, `globals@^15.x`.
   - `dependencies` additions: `react-aria-components@^1.17.0`, `focus-trap-react@^12.0.0`, `tabbable@^6.4.0`.
   - Verify via `npm ls @headlessui/react` returns empty (a11y constraint: react-aria-components XOR Headless UI; chunk picks react-aria-components).
   - Verify post-install: no transitive dep with HTTP/network probe at test/build time (per security constraint); Playwright + Lighthouse will spin headless Chrome but only against loopback servers — Playwright's `postinstall` browser-binary download is the documented exception.

2. **Add `lint` + `lint:a11y` + `test:a11y` placeholder npm scripts to `pulse-app/ui/package.json`**.
   - `"lint": "eslint ."` — runs ESLint on the project per the new flat config.
   - `"lint:a11y": "eslint . --rule 'jsx-a11y/*: error'"` — re-runs with jsx-a11y rules elevated to error severity (smoke verification that the gate is wired; placeholder for richer per-rule scoping).
   - `"test:a11y": "echo 'A11y test suite deferred to chunk #25 webview shell + chunk #46 CI gate; chunk #13 install-only' && exit 0"` — placeholder; CI matrix can call it without restructuring per tests acceptance #6.
   - Preserve existing scripts (`build`, `dev:css`, `test`, `typecheck`, `verify:contrast`) unchanged.

3. **Create `pulse-app/ui/eslint.config.mjs`** (ESLint 9 flat config). - Imports: `eslint/js`, `typescript-eslint`, `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y`, `eslint-plugin-react`, `eslint-plugin-react-hooks`, `globals`. - `ignores: ["dist/**", "node_modules/**", "coverage/**", "playwright-report/**", "test-results/**", ".lighthouseci/**", "pa11y-results/**"]`. - Base config: `eslint.configs.recommended`. - TypeScript layer: `tseslint.configs.recommended` for `**/*.{ts,tsx}`. - React layer: `react.configs.flat.recommended` for `**/*.{tsx,jsx}` with `settings.react.version: "detect"`. - React Hooks: enable `react-hooks/rules-of-hooks` + `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps`. - **jsx-a11y layer**: extends `jsxA11y.flatConfigs.recommended`. Custom Icon component recognition: configure `"jsx-a11y/alt-text": ["error", { elements: ["img"], img: ["NextImage"] }]` (ensures the rule applies only to `` and Next.js Image, not to custom `` per design extract acceptance #2 / design-system §Iconography). Add `"jsx-a11y/anchor-is-valid": "off"` (Tauri webview has no router-navigated ``s yet — would false-positive); revisit at chunk #25. - Globals: `{ ...globals.browser, ...globals.node }` (test files run under jsdom; build scripts under Node).

4. **Create `pulse-app/ui/playwright.config.ts`** (skeleton).
   - `import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';`
   - `export default defineConfig({ testDir: './tests-e2e', testIgnore: ['**/*'], reporter: [['json', { outputFile: '../../target/playwright-report/results.json' }]] });`
   - `testIgnore: ['**/*']` ensures `npx playwright test` exits 0 with "no tests found" until chunk #25 populates `tests-e2e/`. Skeleton-only config; the file's purpose at chunk #13 is to anchor `@axe-core/playwright`'s peer-discovery + give chunk #25 a starting point.

5. **Modify `xtask/src/main.rs`** — add 2 new subcommands.
   - Add `Lint { #[arg(trailing_var_arg = true)] extra: Vec<String> }` to `enum Cmd` with `#[command(name = "lint", about = "npm run lint (ESLint flat config)")]`.
   - Add `TestA11y { #[arg(trailing_var_arg = true)] extra: Vec<String> }` with `#[command(name = "test:a11y", about = "a11y harness — placeholder until chunk #25 webview shell")]`.
   - Dispatch `Cmd::Lint { extra }` → new `async fn run_npm(script: &str, cwd: &Path, extra: Vec<String>) -> Result<ExitCode>` shelling out to `npm run lint` from `pulse-app/ui/` cwd; resolve npm executable via `if cfg!(target_os = "windows") { "npm.cmd" } else { "npm" }` per cross-platform discipline (see existing `invoke_heartbeat_check` 286-298 for Windows shell pattern). Wire `extra` args appended after `--`.
   - Dispatch `Cmd::TestA11y { extra: _ }` → returns `println!("xtask test:a11y: deferred to chunk #25 webview shell + chunk #46 CI gate (chunk #13 install-only)"); Ok(ExitCode::SUCCESS)`. Placeholder body; trivial.
   - Tests live as `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in `xtask/src/main.rs` if any (none expected — xtask helpers are exec wrappers).

6. **Modify `.gitignore`** — append a11y / Playwright / Lighthouse output paths.
   - Add lines under existing "--- Test artifacts ---" section: `pulse-app/ui/playwright-report/`, `pulse-app/ui/test-results/`, `pulse-app/ui/.lighthouseci/`, `pulse-app/ui/pa11y-results/`.
   - These directories may be created by tool runs even at chunk #13 if a developer experiments locally (e.g., `npx pa11y http://localhost`); pre-emptive ignore prevents accidental commits per security extract acceptance #5.

7. **Smoke test the install end-to-end** before committing.
   - `cd pulse-app/ui && npm install` → succeeds; `package-lock.json` updated.
   - `npm ls @headlessui/react` → returns empty/not-found (a11y exclusivity verified).
   - `npm ls react-aria-components focus-trap-react tabbable` → all three resolve at pinned majors with no peer warnings.
   - `npm run typecheck` → `tsc --noEmit` exit 0; new dep types resolve cleanly.
   - `npm run lint` → ESLint runs on `pulse-app/ui/src/`; **expected output: 0 errors, possibly some warnings on icon files which we will then fix in eslint.config.mjs by tuning `jsx-a11y/alt-text` if any false-positive surfaces**. If existing Icon component triggers false-positive, refine eslint.config.mjs §3 jsx-a11y settings until 0 warnings.
   - `npm run test` (existing Vitest) → 64 tests pass, no regression.
   - `npm run verify:contrast` → 12 pairs pass, exit 0; contrast harness from chunk #12 unaffected.
   - From workspace root: `cargo build --workspace` → builds clean; `cargo nextest run --workspace` → 36/36 pass.
   - `cargo xtask lint` → invokes `npm run lint` from `pulse-app/ui/`, exit 0.
   - `cargo xtask test:a11y` → emits placeholder message, exit 0.
   - `cargo deny check bans licenses sources` → passes; no new Rust dep changes (npm-only chunk).
- `pulse-app/ui/eslint.config.mjs` — ESLint 9 flat config wiring jsx-a11y/recommended + TypeScript + React + Hooks + custom Icon recognition (per Step 3).
- `pulse-app/ui/playwright.config.ts` — Playwright skeleton; testIgnore: ['**/*'] until chunk #25 (per Step 4).
- `pulse-app/ui/package.json` — devDependencies + dependencies + scripts (per Steps 1-2).
- `pulse-app/ui/package-lock.json` — regenerated by npm install; commit alongside (per security plan §Dependency Security).
- `xtask/src/main.rs` — add `Lint` + `TestA11y` subcommands + npm shellout helper (per Step 5).
- `.gitignore` — append a11y output paths under "--- Test artifacts ---" section (per Step 6).
- `pulse-app/ui/vite.config.mjs` — no a11y dep needs Vite plugin wiring at chunk #13.
- `pulse-app/ui/vitest.config.mjs` — axe-core matchers are not wired into Vitest at this chunk (would belong to chunk #25 webview shell tests). Setup file chain stays as-is.
- `pulse-app/ui/tsconfig.json` — no `paths` / `types` changes needed; new dep types resolve via standard `@types` or shipped `.d.ts`.
- `pulse-app/ui/src/test-setup.ts` — no axe matchers added at this chunk.

- `pulse-app/ui/src/components/icons/*` — chunk #11 deliverable; ESLint config must NOT flag these (per design extract acceptance #2); plan touches only eslint.config.mjs to make this work, not the icons themselves.
- `pulse-app/ui/src/contrast/*` — chunk #12 deliverable; not modified (per design extract acceptance #4 + tests acceptance #4).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — chunk #13 install is precondition only; CI step wiring lands at chunk #46. Plan does NOT add a `npm run lint` step to ci.yml at this chunk.
- `xtask/Cargo.toml` — no new Rust deps; npm shellout uses existing `tokio::process::Command`.
Per tests-plan §3 5-command discipline + chunk-specific verification.

```bash
# Webview unit tests (existing 64 — must not regress)
cd pulse-app/ui && npm test

# TypeScript typecheck (verifies new dep types resolve)
cd pulse-app/ui && npm run typecheck

# ESLint (new — should pass with 0 errors after eslint.config.mjs tuning)

# xtask wrappers

cargo xtask harness:status     # smoke check (existing)

cd pulse-app/ui && npm ls @headlessui/react   # expected: empty / not-found
cd pulse-app/ui && npm ls react-aria-components focus-trap-react tabbable   # expected: pinned majors, no peer warnings
```

Coverage / flakiness gates per test-plan §10 — no new Rust crate code introduced at this chunk, so coverage gate remains at session-handoff baseline (chunks #1-#12); webview presentational EXCLUDED from gate at Foundation pre-shell (per testing rule §Framework webview row).
Each criterion verifiable; trace to combined.md per-domain contributions.

- (security) `pulse-app/ui/package-lock.json` is committed in the same commit as `package.json` edit; `git diff --name-only HEAD~1 HEAD` shows both files (per combined.md §Per-chunk extracts security #1).

data.head: ### Chunk route#14: "A11y screen reader test spec scaffold — NVDA/VoiceOver/Orca per-surface fixtures + structured JSON output per manual pass"

body: **Constraints across domains:**

- (security) Any net-new third-party dependency added by this chunk (npm or cargo) MUST pass `cargo audit` + `cargo deny check bans licenses sources` in the next CI run (per security plan §Dependency Security CI integration). Chunk #13 already installed axe-core/playwright + react-aria-components + tabbable + focus-trap-react + eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y; chunk #14 should reuse rather than add.

- (security) Test-fixture JSON files MUST NOT contain real OTLP attribute values harvested from any host application (per security plan §Logging & Monitoring "What NEVER to log" + §Threat Model Summary Sensitivity note). Fixtures use synthetic example data only.

- (security) New JSON-output directories MUST be added to `.gitignore` so screen-reader-pass outputs (which may reference real assistive-technology product strings, OS-version strings, or local user paths) are NOT committed (per security plan §Secret Management `.gitignore` discipline + `.claude/rules/security.md` Session Additions §13 chunk-#13 pattern under "Test artifacts").

- (security) The structured JSON output schema MUST NOT include any field intended to carry raw clipboard contents, snapshot file contents, or OTLP attribute values from an actual ingest run (per security plan §Logging & Monitoring "What NEVER to log").

- (security) If structured-JSON-output paths are configured via env var or CLI arg, the path MUST canonicalize via `strict-path` and assert resolution under the repo root (per security plan §Input Validation row "CLI / env var inputs" + §Security Anti-Patterns § Input). If chunk #14 uses only hard-coded relative paths, this is vacuously satisfied.

- (security) No new TauRPC procedure / capability JSON entry expected; if one surfaces, MUST add both router registration AND `pulse-app/capabilities/` JSON entry (per CLAUDE.md §Critical Warnings + security plan §API Security TauRPC capability authorization).

- (arch) Webview source root MUST be `pulse-app/ui/` per arch §Infrastructure Patterns project directory structure; chunk #14 fixtures + scaffold land under this root, not under any `crates/` library crate.

- (arch) Chunk #14 MUST NOT introduce a new Cargo workspace crate or reserve any new env var, port, IPC procedure, capability identifier, filesystem subpath (per arch §Occupied Resources LOCKED + §Inherited Defaults).

- (arch) xtask command surface MUST follow the agent-driven harness convention (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns Development Style "deterministic harness invocations, machine-parseable outputs, schema-stable contracts, `cargo xtask` task surfaces"); chunk #14 invocable via `cargo xtask` (extending the chunk #13 `test:a11y` placeholder is the natural home).

- (arch) Structured JSON output for manual screen-reader passes MUST be schema-stable per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns Development Style; per-surface fixtures emit JSON with stable keys consumable by downstream chunk #46 (a11y CI gate).

- (tests) Manual-pass screen reader fixtures fall under the "untestable" / "agent-driven discipline" carve-out: scaffold MUST emit structured JSON output per pass so an agent can read pass/fail signals via `jq` without human review of the raw screen-reader log (per test-plan §1 Agent-runnable invariants + §11 Universal "NEVER include manual smoke step" / "human reviews canvas").

- (tests) Fixture spec files MUST be co-located near the surface they describe so co-location discipline holds (per test-plan §4 Conventions Test file location). Chunk #14 surfaces don't yet exist (#28/#33/#36/#37/#38) — scaffold with placeholder per-surface stubs is acceptable.

- (tests) Structured JSON output of each manual pass MUST be machine-parseable to the same shape the harness already consumes (exit code + JSON line/file `jq`-able, per test-plan §1 Agent-runnable invariants + §3 Log format Agent-parseable signals). One JSON file per (surface × screen-reader × pass-date) tuple under a non-tracked output dir.

- (tests) Chunk MUST NOT block CI on real screen-reader execution. Runtime artifacts MUST stay deferred-no-op OR run only under explicit env-var opt-in (per test-plan §11 Universal + the chunk #13 `xtask test:a11y` placeholder precedent).

- (tests) `.gitignore` extends "Test artifacts" section with any new screen-reader manual-pass output dir(s) — chunk #13 precedent (4 a11y output paths added under "Test artifacts") generalizes (per test-plan §11 Test Data + chunk #13 precedent).

- (obs) A11y manual-pass JSON output MUST follow the binding log-format JSON schema fields (`timestamp` ISO 8601, `level`, `target`, `message`, `fields {}`) verbatim — project-wide self-observation contract joins all structured-JSON-emitting deliverables (per obs-plan §3 Log format JSON schema + §6 Required fields binding contract from tests Section 5).

- (obs) Per-pass `target` field MUST follow `{module}.{operation}` naming (e.g., `a11y.screen_reader.pass.{surface}`) — no high-cardinality names, no per-tester-name targets (per obs-plan §11 Spans/Traces "NEVER use high-cardinality span names").

- (obs) Per-pass `fields` map MUST be default-deny: NO raw OTLP attribute content (Vector 1), NO full canonicalized plugin/file paths (Vector 3 — basename only), NO DuckDB query parameters/SQL text (Vector 5) (per obs-plan §8 Default-deny posture + §11 Logs anti-patterns).

- (obs) `service.name` / `service.version` / `deployment.environment` apply IF outputs ride the same `tracing-subscriber` sink — if a11y outputs land in a separate path (e.g., `pulse-app/ui/test-results/a11y/*.jsonl`), document the separation explicitly (per obs-plan §3 Service identity).

- (obs) Foundation epoch obs constraint preserved: NO OTel SDK, no proprietary APM SDK, no Sentry calls in fixture/scaffold code — `tracing` ecosystem only (per obs-plan §1 architectural choice + §11 Universal "NEVER link an OTel SDK into the product's self-observation runtime").

- (a11y) Three SR per platform pairings are FIXED and cannot be substituted: **NVDA 2025.3 + Chrome on Windows**, **VoiceOver + Safari on macOS 15.3+**, **Orca 48.x + Firefox on Linux** (per a11y-plan §3 Screen Reader Test Pattern + §7 Per-surface SR test pattern table).

The scaffold lives under a new `pulse-app/ui/tests-a11y/screen-reader/` subtree per arch §Infrastructure Patterns webview-source colocation discipline.

The scaffold preserves agent-driven invariants via two defenses: (a) the existing `cargo xtask test:a11y` placeholder stays at exit 0 (deferred-to-#25/#46) so CI matrix stays green, and (b) every documented fixture pass emits one JSON record per the same structured-log schema the rest of the harness consumes (per obs-plan §3 + tests-plan §3 binding contract — `timestamp / level / target / message / fields {}` shape; `target = a11y.screen_reader.pass.{surface}` with bounded enumerated `screen_reader` / `wcag_sc` / `status` field values; output to `pulse-app/ui/test-results/a11y-sr/` which is gitignored). Surface enumeration uses layout-templates.md vocabulary verbatim (9 distinct targets across desktop-webview compact-widget + full-dashboard/{traces,metrics,logs,snapshots,settings} + desktop-native tray-icon/tray-menu/notifications), so future implementation chunks (#28 / #33 / #36 / #37 / #38) can bind their concrete UI surfaces back to the right fixture without re-naming.

The chunk introduces ZERO new runtime artifacts, ZERO new dependencies, ZERO new TauRPC procedures, ZERO new env vars / ports / capabilities — surface area is documentation + schema + ignore-globs only. Per security plan §Logging anti-patterns, schema constrains `fields` to bounded values + free-text observed-behavior strings authored by humans, never live OTLP attribute values. Per a11y-plan §11 anti-patterns, scaffold explicitly documents itself as supplemental (automated axe-core / Lighthouse / pa11y remain primary CI gates from chunk #13 + #46).

1. **Create `pulse-app/ui/tests-a11y/screen-reader/` directory tree.** New sibling to `pulse-app/ui/src/` and `pulse-app/ui/scripts/`; conforms to arch §Infrastructure Patterns webview-source colocation (per research.md "Conventions to follow" — Webview source root).

2. **Author `pulse-app/ui/tests-a11y/screen-reader/README.md`.** Top-level orientation document. Sections: Scope (manual SR pass, supplemental to chunk #13 automated dev stack), Output path (`pulse-app/ui/test-results/a11y-sr/<sr>-<surface>-<ISO-date>.jsonl`, gitignored), Supplemental-not-sole-gate disclaimer (per a11y-plan §3 + §11), Surface inventory (9 surface targets per layouts), Per-platform spec links (a11y-sr-nvda.md / -voiceover.md / -orca.md), Schema reference link, Activation status (deferred to chunks #25 webview shell + #46 CI gate).

3. **Author `pulse-app/ui/tests-a11y/screen-reader/schema.json`.** JSON Schema document (draft 2020-12; documentation-only, no runtime validator dependency added). Fields:

data.head: ### Chunk route#15: "Motion tokens library install — motion/react useReducedMotion hook + Tailwind v4 motion-reduce variants + canvas frame loop wiring"

body: **Domain relevance:**
- (a11y) **HIGHLY RELEVANT** — chunk IS the dedicated bootstrap phase that closes the motion-sensitive AAA-escalation infrastructure track per a11y-plan §3.5 `motion-tokens-respect-install`

- (design) RELEVANT — chunk wires the motion-tokens dimension authored in design plan §Motion + §Surface: desktop-webview Tokens; sets the runtime substrate every later chrome transition + Halo State Pulse degradation will consume

- (security / layouts / tests / obs / arch) PARTIALLY-RELEVANT — webview-only Foundation install + wiring; intersects supply-chain CI gates / per-surface motion budgets / Vitest layer / `metric.webgpu.frame_duration_ms` future emission site / locked WebGPU canvas substrate respectively
**Constraints across domains:**

- (a11y) Chunk MUST install `motion@12.x` and wire `useReducedMotion` from `motion/react` into the WebGPU canvas frame loop AND animation triggers — this is the named bootstrap phase `motion-tokens-respect-install` (per a11y-plan §3 Bootstrap phases).

- (a11y) Tailwind v4 `motion-reduce:` variants MUST be applied to all CSS transition / animation elements; `motion-safe:` permitted as inverse where defaults are non-animating (per a11y-plan §11 Visual anti-pattern + §12 Decisions Log "Motion / reduced-motion handling").

- (a11y) `useReducedMotion` hook MUST gate JS-driven motion (canvas frame loop, skeleton animation, investigation collapse scale, Halo State Pulse) — vanilla canvas frame loops require explicit `window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches` check (per a11y-plan §11 Motion anti-pattern bullet 4).

- (a11y) Reduced-motion override MUST degrade `--duration-fast` / `--duration-standard` / `--duration-investigation-collapse` / `--easing-out` / `--easing-in-out` motion tokens (already shipped by chunk #10) to `0s` / instant under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` (per a11y-plan §6 Motion tokens row).

- (a11y) State changes MUST stay conveyed via color + text + focus ring even when motion is disabled — motion is a SUPPLEMENT, never the only signal (per a11y-plan §11 Motion anti-pattern + WCAG SC 1.4.1 + creator-brief motion-as-data principle).

- (a11y) Test-side assertion MUST use Playwright `page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' })` to verify computed `transition-duration: 0s` / `animation-duration: 0s` per `motion-reduce:` Tailwind variant (per a11y-plan §6 Motion tokens verification).

- (a11y) WCAG 2.1 AAA SC 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions is the ONLY AAA escalation in this project's tier mapping — this chunk is the load-bearing infrastructure for that escalation (per a11y-plan §1 + §3 motion-sensitive trigger row). WCAG 2.1 AA SC 2.3.1 Three Flashes covered transitively (no flashing > 3 times per second).

- (design) Motion duration tokens MUST come from locked `--duration-fast: 150ms` / `--duration-standard: 200ms` `@theme` block scaffolded in chunk #10 — chunk #15 wires consumers, no new duration custom properties (per design plan §Surface: desktop-webview Tokens + §Motion duration scale).

- (design) Easing tokens restricted to `--easing-out` / `--easing-in-out` (both `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)`); Tailwind v4 motion-reduce variants MUST collapse animations to instant (0ms) for chrome transitions, NOT swap to alternate easings (per design plan §Motion Easing line + §Motion Accessibility row).

- (design) `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` override for chrome transitions MUST collapse 150ms hover and 200ms fade to 0ms (instant); `motion/react` `useReducedMotion()` is the canonical detection surface for React, paired with Tailwind v4 `motion-reduce:` variant for CSS-only consumers (per design plan §Motion Accessibility "Other transitions become instant").

- (design) Halo State Pulse reduced-motion degradation is data-driven and EXEMPT from chrome motion budget — degraded mode MUST keep LCH hue interpolation per error rate (Earth Blue ↔ Alert Burgundy) but MUST suppress sinusoidal pulse + blur radius cycling; canvas frame loop's reduced-motion gate MUST set frequency Hz → 0 + blur radius → fixed midpoint (~10px) while leaving color shader uniform updates active (per design plan §Motion Accessibility row + §Brand Identity Signature element).

- (design) Investigation Capture Collapse (250–350ms supporting moment) is EXEMPT from chrome motion ≤200ms hard limit but MUST still respect reduced-motion: in reduced mode the scale + opacity ease becomes instant; aria-busy/aria-live announcement timing unchanged (per design plan §Motion Supporting moments row + Hard limits subsection).

- (design) Canvas frame loop wiring MUST honor reduced-motion BEFORE issuing WebGPU draw calls — gate is at the rAF tick, not inside the WGSL shader; emits `frame_duration_ms` per frame for obs telemetry handshake (per design plan §Downstream Readiness obs hook bullet 1: "Log Halo pulse frequency... clamped to 0.8–2.4 Hz...").

- (layouts) Per-surface expression-level budgets bound motion scope: desktop-webview surfaces cap at expression `0.35` (skeleton pulsing, panel transitions, form state confirmation, command-palette emergence); desktop-native (tray) caps at `0.2` (icon state changes, badge emergence, traffic-light transitions, no custom chrome animation) (per layout-templates.md §Surface: desktop-webview Expression level + §Surface: desktop-native Expression level).

- (layouts) Halo State Pulse data-driven WebGPU shader motion is exempt from chrome motion budget across all three surfaces, but reduced-motion variant is layout-mandated: halo MUST degrade to static glow (no pulsing rhythm) while hue still updates per error rate (per layout-templates.md §Component — Halo State Pulse canvas Reduced motion + §Component — Tray icon Reduced motion + §Decisions Log "data-driven, not decorative").

- (layouts) Tray-surface notification emergence MUST be instant (no fade-in animation) per `0.2` desktop-native expression level — `motion-reduce:` variant must not introduce regression by accidentally adding fade-in behavior (per layout-templates.md §Component — Notifications Reduced motion).

- (layouts) WebGPU canvas frame-loop reduced-motion gate operates at THREE distinct surfaces: (a) compact widget aggregated halo, (b) full dashboard per-service constellation halos, (c) tray icon unified halo (with SVG-filter fallback when WebGPU unavailable in tray context). Frame-loop gate must not assume single-canvas topology (per layout-templates.md §Decisions Log Signature placement + §Component — Tray icon Halo State Pulse Option A/B).

- (layouts) Investigation Capture Collapse motion (modal scale + opacity ease-out) is the named "supporting moment" inside `0.35` webview budget; chunk #15's `useReducedMotion` wiring must permit downstream chunk #28 to honor reduced-motion by collapsing to instant modal emergence without re-architecting (per layout-templates.md §Component — Investigation modal Motion).

- (layouts) Panel transitions (Settings modal open/close) ease over `duration-standard` within `0.35` webview budget; Tailwind v4 `motion-reduce:` variant config must apply to these transition utilities so reduced-motion users see instant open/close (per layout-templates.md §Decisions Log Motion trigger placement Panel transitions).

- (security) New npm dependency `motion` (motion/react) MUST flow through `pulse-app/ui/package.json` only — do NOT add Rust workspace deps; this chunk is pure webview/JS install (per security plan §Dependency Security Pinning paragraph + Cross-cutting Patterns "no Docker, no external runtime").

- (security) Webview CSP in `pulse-app/tauri.conf.json` `app.security.csp` MUST remain `script-src 'self'` (no `'unsafe-inline'` / `'unsafe-eval'` added for motion library) — motion/react resolves at build time via Vite bundler so no inline scripts required (per security plan §API Security CSP row).

- (security) Canvas frame loop reduced-motion gate MUST NOT introduce log emissions that capture OTLP attribute values, span/log/metric content, or telemetry payload data — `tracing::event!` calls in frame-loop wiring stay structural-only (frame_count, hz, reduced_motion=bool) per §Logging "What NEVER to log" + universal anti-pattern in CLAUDE.md.

- (security) `motion` package version pin in `package.json` MUST follow same version-pin discipline as Rust deps — pin specific minimum (e.g., `"motion": "^11.x.x"` matching adjacent chunk #13 style), not `"latest"` or `"*"` (per §Dependency Security Pinning paragraph + adjacent chunk #13 install pattern).

- (security) `cargo deny check bans licenses sources` and `cargo audit` CI gates remain authoritative; for npm side, this chunk MUST NOT introduce a license-incompatible package (motion/react is MIT — verify) per §Dependency Security CI integration.

- (tests) Webview unit tests for any new motion-related React hook wrapper or component MUST land as co-located `*.test.tsx` adjacent to source under `pulse-app/ui/src/`, run through `vitest` 3.x with `jsdom` 26 + `@testing-library/react` 16, emit JUnit XML to `target/junit-ui.xml` (per test-plan §4 Webview unit tests row).

- (tests) Webview tests MUST be DOM-shape only — no visual diff, no Percy / Chromatic / Applitools, no canvas pixel inspection (per test-plan §11 Universal "NEVER include visual regression checks requiring human approval"). Reduced-motion behavior verified by asserting on rendered DOM attrs / props / class lists / callback-invocation count, not frame-buffer reads.

- (tests) Test-time `prefers-reduced-motion` MUST be deterministically injected via `window.matchMedia` mock in `setupFiles: ["./src/test-setup.ts"]`; tests MUST NOT depend on real browser media queries (per test-plan §11 Universal "NEVER use real time / non-deterministic").

- (tests) Webview presentational components remain EXCLUDED from ≥75% line / ≥70% branch / ≥85% function coverage gate at Foundation pre-shell stage; gate engages when `tauri-driver` E2E lands at chunk #25 (per test-plan §4 explicit Foundation-stage exclusion). Chunk #15 webview tests are validation-of-contract.

- (tests) The 5-command harness `run` step (`cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` + `npm run test` in `pulse-app/ui/`) MUST stay green after this chunk (per test-plan §3 5-command implementation `run` contract + §10 build failure conditions).

- (tests) Zero-flakiness budget applies: any motion-related test (especially async callbacks / `requestAnimationFrame` / debounce timers) MUST pass deterministically without retry (per test-plan §10 Zero-flakiness budget).

- (obs) Webview frontend MUST NOT link a browser OTel SDK; any frame-time / motion-mode signal must flow through TauRPC `telemetry.frontend.record_frame_ms` to backend `tracing::info!(target: "metric.webgpu.frame_duration_ms", ...)` (per obs-plan §1 desktop-webview row + §3 Frontend bridge + §12 Decisions Log).

- (obs) WebGPU canvas frame timing emission convention is fixed: `metric.webgpu.frame_duration_ms` target with `duration_ms`, `wgpu_backend`, `webview_backend`, `timing_method` labels (per obs-plan §5 Per-surface metric events table).

- (obs) Frame loop wiring MUST level-gate any heavy `tracing` event payload formatting if backend bridge is invoked per frame — wrap in `if tracing::enabled!(Level::DEBUG) { ... }` for ~60 Hz tick rate (per obs-plan §11 Metrics anti-pattern).

- (obs) When `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` flips loop to throttled-tick or static state, metric event frequency MUST still emit at sufficient cadence to compute p99 ≤ 33ms post-test; document reduced-motion behavior so log-tail aggregation in CI doesn't misread sparse emission as a stall (per obs-plan §10 perf budgets row + §10 CI gates).

- (obs) The TauRPC bridge contract `telemetry.frontend.record_frame_ms` schema is **deferred** per obs-plan §12 Open questions — chunk #15 should NOT define or implement the backend handler; only stub the frontend emission shape (or no-op the bridge call) so wiring is testable without backend handler binding.
- (arch) Webview source MUST live under `pulse-app/ui/` per directory-structure pattern (per arch §Infrastructure Patterns project directory structure).

- (arch) Visualization surface is locked to webview WebGPU (`<canvas>` + `navigator.gpu`, WGSL) — canvas frame loop MUST target WebGPU canvas, not native `wgpu` or DOM-only `<canvas>` 2D context (per arch §Established Decisions [WebGPU Visualization Surface] + §Stack and Technologies Visualization surface row).

- (arch) Frame loop MUST NOT introduce a frontend dev server port at arch level — webview manages its own dev server internally; arch reserves no frontend port (per arch §Occupied Resources network-ports row).

Per obs-plan §12 Open questions the `telemetry.frontend.record_frame_ms` TauRPC handler is deferred to ui-bridge impl phase — chunk #15 stubs the bridge call site with a `// TODO(chunk #25)` comment, preserving the wiring pattern without forcing an unresolved schema decision.

1. **Install `motion@12.x` runtime dependency.** Edit `pulse-app/ui/package.json` `dependencies` block: add `"motion": "^12.x.x"` (caret-pin to a concrete latest 12.x at install time, matching adjacent chunk #13 pinning style for `react-aria-components: ^1.17.0` / `focus-trap-react: ^12.0.0`).
