2. **Create `pulse-app/ui/src/hooks/use-reduced-motion.ts`.** Re-export `useReducedMotion` from `motion/react` as the single canonical import path consumed by all three surfaces (compact widget / full dashboard / tray Halo overlay) per layouts §three-surface-coherence. Limit named imports to `useReducedMotion` only (per a11y constraint: "only `motion/react` `useReducedMotion` (and any explicit additional named imports) should land in this chunk; full library import bloats bundle"). File contents: a single `export { useReducedMotion } from "motion/react";` line plus brief JSDoc comment describing the surface contract.

3. **Create `pulse-app/ui/src/hooks/mock-reduced-motion.ts`.** Test helper exporting `mockReducedMotion(value: boolean): void` per test-plan §7 Builder factories pattern. Sets `window.matchMedia` to a deterministic mock with `{ matches: value, media: "(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)", addEventListener, removeEventListener, addListener (legacy), removeListener (legacy), dispatchEvent, onchange: null }` shape per matchMedia spec; uses `vi.fn()` for `addEventListener` / `removeEventListener` so test code can spy on listener registration counts. Co-locate as a pure helper (not a test file) so future chunks #28 / #29 / #30 / #46 can import.

4. **Extend `pulse-app/ui/src/test-setup.ts`.** Add a baseline `window.matchMedia` mock at module load (before any test imports the hook) so jsdom does not throw `ReferenceError: matchMedia is not defined` when the hook subscribes. Default state: `{ matches: false }` (motion enabled). Tests that need reduced-motion call `mockReducedMotion(true)` from the helper to flip the value. Preserve the existing `afterEach(() => cleanup())` import + invocation.

5. **Create `pulse-app/ui/src/hooks/use-reduced-motion.test.tsx`.** Vitest unit tests using `renderHook` from `@testing-library/react`:
   - "returns false when prefers-reduced-motion media query does not match" — default jsdom state, hook returns `false`.
   - "returns true when prefers-reduced-motion: reduce media query matches" — call `mockReducedMotion(true)` before render, hook returns `true`.
   - "subscribes to media query change events on mount" — verify `window.matchMedia(...).addEventListener` invoked with `"change"` listener via `vi.fn()` spy.
   - "unsubscribes on unmount" — verify `removeEventListener` invoked with the same listener reference (no leak).
   Follow `pulse-app/ui/src/components/icons/Icon.test.tsx` style: `describe("...")` + nested `it("...")` blocks; container/spy assertions only; no visual diff.

6. **Create `pulse-app/ui/src/canvas/frame-loop.ts` + `pulse-app/ui/src/canvas/types.ts`.** Frame-loop scaffold:
   - `types.ts` declares `FrameLoopOptions` (`onFrame: (timestamp: DOMHighResTimeStamp) => void`, `prefersReducedMotion: boolean`, optional `onReducedMotionFrame?: (timestamp: DOMHighResTimeStamp) => void`) and `FrameLoopHandle` (`start: () => void`, `stop: () => void`).
   - `frame-loop.ts` exports `createFrameLoop(options: FrameLoopOptions): FrameLoopHandle`. Internal state holds the current rAF id. `start()` schedules a `requestAnimationFrame(tick)`; if `options.prefersReducedMotion === true`, the tick branch invokes `options.onReducedMotionFrame?.(timestamp)` exactly once on first start (static-paint pattern per design constraint "frequency Hz → 0 + blur radius → fixed midpoint") and does NOT re-schedule; otherwise invokes `options.onFrame(timestamp)` and re-schedules via rAF. `stop()` cancels the pending rAF id. Add a `// TODO(chunk #25): replace with TauRPC telemetry.frontend.record_frame_ms call` comment at the per-frame emit point so the deferred bridge surface is documented in code (per obs constraint).
   - Document via short JSDoc that hue interpolation is NOT gated by `prefersReducedMotion` (Halo State Pulse data-driven motion exemption per design + layouts) — reduced-motion gates the rhythm envelope ONLY; consumers in chunks #25 / #28 wire color uniform updates outside the gate.

7. **Create `pulse-app/ui/src/canvas/frame-loop.test.ts`.** Vitest unit tests using `vi.useFakeTimers()` + `vi.spyOn(window, "requestAnimationFrame")`:
   - "invokes onFrame on each rAF tick when prefersReducedMotion is false" — spy onFrame, advance timers, expect ≥1 invocation.
   - "does NOT invoke onFrame when prefersReducedMotion is true" — spy onFrame, advance timers, expect 0 invocations.
   - "invokes onReducedMotionFrame once on start when prefersReducedMotion is true" — spy onReducedMotionFrame, expect exactly 1 invocation post-start.
   - "stop() cancels pending rAF" — start, advance partial, stop, advance more, expect onFrame call count frozen at pre-stop value.
   Mirrors test-plan §8 time-mocking discipline + §11 anti-pattern "NEVER use real `requestAnimationFrame`".

data.head: ### Chunk route#16: "OTLP gRPC receiver — tonic 0.14 :4317 bound 127.0.0.1, TraceService/MetricsService/LogsService, .max_decoding_message_size 8MB"

body: **Constraints across domains:**

- (security) OTLP/gRPC receiver MUST bind to `127.0.0.1` only — loopback is the de-facto authorization boundary; binding to `0.0.0.0` or any non-loopback interface invalidates the entire Minimal-tier risk model (per security plan §Security Anti-Patterns § API + §Threat Model Summary).

- (security) Each `tonic` 0.14 `*ServiceServer` builder (TraceService / MetricsService / LogsService) MUST set `.max_decoding_message_size(8 * 1024 * 1024)` — `tonic` historically accepted 1 GB+ unary requests by default (per security plan §Input Validation row 1 + §Security Anti-Patterns § Input).

- (security) Post-`prost` decode invariant checks MUST run before handing batches downstream — `prost` only validates wire format; `span_id` must be 8 bytes, `trace_id` must be 16 bytes, attribute keys/values bounded (per security plan §Input Validation row 1). NOTE: per chunk grouping, attribute-bound enforcement is shared with chunk #18 — chunk #16 wires the `*ServiceServer` decode-size cap and MUST leave hooks for the chunk #18 invariant layer.

- (security) The `tonic` 0.14 ↔ `opentelemetry-otlp` 0.31 / `tonic` 0.13 transitive-duplicate caveat MUST be enforced via `cargo deny check bans` (`multiple-versions = "deny"` already wired in Foundation chunk #6 `deny.toml`); adding `tonic 0.14` to `crates/ingest/Cargo.toml` MUST NOT silently regress the bans gate (per security plan §Dependency Security Pinning).

- (security) gRPC errors collapse to standard `tonic::Status` codes per OTLP spec — non-2xx-equivalent gRPC responses MUST NOT leak stack traces, file paths, internal hostnames, library versions, or Rust struct names (per security plan §Error Handling "OTLP receiver" row).

- (security) The `ingest` crate MUST NOT log raw OTLP payload contents — service requests can incidentally contain secrets, IDs, URLs, error messages, SQL fragments from the instrumented host (per security plan §Logging & Monitoring NEVER-log list).

- (security) The `ingest` crate MUST NOT instrument its own work via an OTLP network exporter pointed at the product's own `:4317` — infinite recursion + bypasses loopback authorization model; `tracing` ecosystem only for self-observation (per security plan §Security Anti-Patterns § API + CLAUDE.md universal invariant).

- (arch) Chunk code MUST live in `crates/ingest/` per workspace boundary rules; `ingest` is the reserved crate name for OTLP receivers (per arch §Occupied Resources Cargo workspace crate names + §Project Directory Structure).

- (arch) gRPC server stack is LOCKED to `tonic` 0.14.x + `prost` 0.14 codegen against `opentelemetry-proto`; alternatives (raw hyper, poem+tonic, actix+tonic) are explicitly rejected (per arch §Stack and Technologies + §Established Decisions [Backend Framework — OTLP receiver]).

- (arch) Wire format MUST be OpenTelemetry spec-conformant — `:4317` implements `TraceService`, `MetricsService`, `LogsService` from `opentelemetry-proto`; no project-specific envelope, no URL versioning prefix beyond OTLP spec (per arch §Standard Contracts + §Conventions "External wire — OTLP receiver").

- (arch) Port `:4317` is reserved at arch level and MUST be honored as default, with `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_GRPC_PORT` env var as the only authorized override mechanism; port type MUST be `u16` with `TryFrom<u16>` validation (per arch §Occupied Resources Network ports + Environment variables + §Conventions "Configuration units").
- (arch) gRPC errors MUST collapse to standard `tonic::Status` codes — no custom error envelope at the OTLP receiver boundary (per arch §Conventions "Error response schema (OTLP receiver)").

- (arch) The `ingest` crate's TauRPC procedures (if any are exposed in this chunk) MUST follow the `<router>.<verb>` dotted namespace convention with `snake_case` segments; module-internal errors use `thiserror` 2.x and convert to `AppError::Ingest { message }` at the bridge if/when crossing TauRPC (per arch §Conventions "Endpoint naming" + "Error response schema (Tauri IPC)").

- (arch) Tokio runtime is owned by `pulse-app/` binary crate (single multi-threaded runtime serves both OTLP ports and IPC); `crates/ingest/` consumes `tokio` for async primitives but MUST NOT spawn its own runtime (per arch §Stack "Async runtime" + §Established Decisions [Backend Framework]).

- (arch) Module dependency direction: `crates/ingest/` MUST NOT depend on `pulse-app` (the binary crate); dependencies flow toward `pulse-app` only. The `ingest` crate exposes its public contract via `pub`; cross-crate utilities use `pub(crate)` (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns "Module dependency direction" + §Conventions "Module visibility discipline").

- (arch) `ingest` crate hands off decoded OTLP payloads to the `buffer` crate via `tokio::sync::mpsc` (with built-in backpressure); broadcast fan-out from `buffer` to subscribers is NOT this chunk's concern (per arch §Established Decisions [In-Process Channel Architecture]). Mpsc producer side ownership lands here; appender consumer lands in chunk #20 (Storage epoch).

- (arch) Self-observation guard: this OTLP receiver chunk MUST NOT instrument with an OTLP network exporter pointed at the product's own `:4317` — infinite recursion (per arch §Established Decisions [Self-Observation] + §Cross-cutting Patterns "Self-observation discipline").

- (obs) Manual `#[tracing::instrument(skip(req), fields(rpc.system = "grpc", rpc.service, rpc.method, span_count, traceparent))]` REQUIRED on every tonic gRPC service method handler (`TraceService`, `MetricsService`, `LogsService`); skip(req) keeps the raw OTLP payload out of the span (per obs-plan §4 Instrumentation per surface row "API service gRPC `:4317`" + §3 Tracing init).

- (obs) W3C trace context extraction at gRPC boundary entry via manual tonic interceptor: read `grpc-trace-bin` metadata header, attach value to local `tracing` span as plain `traceparent` field — treated as opaque string, NOT bound to any OTel SDK trace context (per obs-plan §3 Trace context propagation gRPC bullet + §11 anti-pattern).

- (obs) NO OTel SDK linked into self-observation runtime; the only OTLP-aware crates allowed at the receiver are `tonic` 0.14 + `prost` + `opentelemetry-proto` for wire-format decode (per obs-plan §3 Tracing init "Why this approach" + §12 Decisions Log 2026-05-02 user-pivot).

- (obs) Ingest boundary span `otlp.grpc.export.request` MUST emit ONLY allowlisted fields per obs-plan §8 whitelist for `ingest`: `span_count`, `service` (sanitized service.name tag), `trace_ids` list — NOT raw `span.attributes` dict (per obs-plan §5 + §11 Spans anti-pattern).

- (obs) Inner `parse.protobuf` child span wraps OTLP payload parse latency; on schema violation emit `ingest.grpc.parse.error` span at `error` level with `span_field_invalid`, `expected_length`, `actual_length`, `rejection_reason` (per obs-plan §1 chaos-instrumentation row + §6 Log levels error-row example). **Anti-patterns to avoid:**
- (security) NEVER bind to `0.0.0.0`, `[::]`, or `Ipv4Addr::UNSPECIFIED` — even as a "temporary" debugging affordance behind a feature flag (per security plan §Security Anti-Patterns § API).

- (security) NEVER omit `.max_decoding_message_size(8 * 1024 * 1024)` from any of the three `*ServiceServer` builders — default is 1 GB+ which is a documented memory-exhaustion DoS vector (per security plan §Security Anti-Patterns § Input).

- (security) NEVER log raw OTLP request / batch payloads, service-request bodies, attribute values, span/log/metric content, or `tonic::Status::message` strings derived from request data — the `ingest` crate sees user-controlled content and the product is the local observer (per security plan §Security Anti-Patterns § Logging + CLAUDE.md universal invariant).

- (arch) Do NOT introduce a custom error envelope on gRPC responses or invent a project-specific OTLP wire variant — `:4317` is OpenTelemetry-spec-fixed, errors collapse to `tonic::Status` (per arch §Conventions "Error response schema (OTLP receiver)" + §Established Decisions [API Style — OTLP Receiver Surface 1]).
- (arch) Do NOT spawn an independent tokio runtime inside `crates/ingest/` — `pulse-app` owns the single multi-threaded runtime; `crates/ingest/` consumes it (per arch §Stack "Async runtime").

- (arch) Do NOT introduce a `pub use` re-export from `crates/ingest/` across a sibling crate boundary except through the explicit contract module of each crate; do NOT depend on `pulse-app` from `crates/ingest/` (per arch §Conventions "Module visibility discipline" + §Cross-cutting Patterns "Module dependency direction").

- (arch) Do NOT add a new env var beyond the reserved `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_*` namespace (specifically `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_GRPC_PORT` for this chunk) — env-var additions require scope-arch (per arch §Occupied Resources Environment variables).

- (obs) NEVER include raw OTLP `span.attributes` dict in span attributes or log fields — emit only `attributes_count` + sanitized `service_name_tag` (PII Vector 1 — per obs-plan §1 logging-sensitive trigger + §11 Spans anti-pattern + §8 PII allowlist `ingest` row).

- (obs) NEVER use high-cardinality span names (per-trace-ID names, per-service-name span names) — span names are bounded `{module}.{operation}` strings; `service_name` lives as a span field, not in the span name (per obs-plan §11 Spans).

- (obs) NEVER hold a `tracing::Span` guard across `.await` without `.in_current_span()` — span context bleeds into unrelated tokio tasks, breaking trace_id correlation; tonic gRPC handlers are async by definition, so this is the live failure mode for THIS chunk (per obs-plan §11 Spans anti-pattern bullet 4).

- (obs) NEVER log `info`-level inside the per-RPC hot path beyond the boundary entry/exit pair — use `trace`/`debug` gated by `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_LOG_LEVEL` for inner decode detail; `info`-spam at gRPC throughput costs receiver throughput (per obs-plan §11 Logs anti-pattern bullet 4 + §6 Per-module log levels `ingest` row).

- (obs) NEVER skip trace context propagation at the gRPC boundary — agent loses trace continuity for multi-surface debugging across P1 (per obs-plan §11 Spans anti-pattern bullet 3 + §3 Trace context propagation gRPC bullet).

- (obs) NEVER over-instrument the appender inner loop with spans — span overhead matters; this chunk's inner `parse.protobuf` span is the only inner span warranted at the gRPC boundary (per obs-plan §11 Telemetry Strategy bullet 1).

- (tests) NEVER mock the gRPC receiver under test — every receiver-relevant test drives the live binding via `tonic` 0.14.5 native client at loopback `:4317` (per test-plan §11 Anti-Patterns Mocking + §8 What NOT to mock).

- (tests) NEVER assert on raw OTLP protobuf bytes (`assert_eq!(response.encode(), expected_bytes)`) — assert on decoded fields (`service_name`, `trace_id`, `duration_ms`) that survive `prost` decode (per test-plan §11 Anti-Patterns Integration row 3).

- (tests) NEVER use `unwrap()` in receiver tests without explicit panic context — use `expect("gRPC bind on loopback :4317 must succeed in test")` with diagnostic message (per test-plan §11 Anti-Patterns Unit row 3).

- (tests) NEVER run receiver tests with shared port between tests — each test gets ephemeral port via `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_GRPC_PORT=0` (let OS assign) or `cargo-nextest`'s per-process isolation guarantees the bind doesn't collide (per test-plan §3 boot env vars + §4 Framework choice rationale).

- (tests) NEVER add a flaky-retry policy if a receiver bind test flakes — flake = real bug; quarantine via `#[ignore]` + open issue + root-cause; zero-flakiness budget is non-negotiable (per test-plan §10 Zero-flakiness budget).

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase Phase 4. Read by /andromeda-implement.
Manual edits between runs are fine; do not edit during /implement run._
- **Phase number:** 13

- **Route chunks covered:**
  - route#16 "OTLP gRPC receiver — tonic 0.14 :4317 bound 127.0.0.1, TraceService/MetricsService/LogsService, .max_decoding_message_size 8MB"
- **Epoch:** Epoch 2 — Ingest pipeline (opens this phase; Foundation closed at chunk #15)

Open Epoch 2 — Ingest pipeline by giving the `crates/ingest/` crate a real OTLP/gRPC receiver bound to `127.0.0.1:4317` (loopback only). The chunk introduces three OpenTelemetry-spec service implementations (`TraceService`, `MetricsService`, `LogsService` from `opentelemetry-proto`) wired into a single `tonic::transport::Server::builder()` chain, where each `*ServiceServer` builder applies `.max_decoding_message_size(8 * 1024 * 1024)` to defend against the documented `tonic` 1 GB-default DoS vector (per security plan §Input Validation row 1 + arch §Established Decisions [Backend Framework — OTLP receiver]). The gRPC server task starts during Tauri `setup()` and updates a shared `IngestState` plus a new bind-status slot in `HeartbeatState` so the existing `health` TauRPC envelope (`subsystems.otlp_grpc_receiver.{status,error_msg}`) reflects reality instead of the chunk-#4 placeholder.

The receiver participates in the existing self-observation harness (`tracing` only; NO OTel SDK per arch §Established Decisions [Self-Observation] + obs-plan §3 + CLAUDE.md universal invariant) by emitting `otlp.grpc.export.request` boundary spans with allowlisted fields (`rpc.system`, `rpc.service`, `rpc.method`, `span_count`, `traceparent`), an inner `parse.protobuf` child span on every decode, an `app.boot.otlp.grpc.bind` event on bind, and an `ingest.grpc.parse.error` scaffold whose body chunk #18 will populate. The existing `ingest.tick` heartbeat (chunk #4) starts carrying real `span_count` + `broadcast_subscribers` from the new shared `IngestState` instead of zero defaults. Trace context flows from `grpc-trace-bin` request metadata into `tracing::Span::current()` so chunks #18/#20/#22/#25 inherit `trace_id` for the P1 critical-path span chain (per obs extract Patterns row 4).

The chunk leaves a clean `Result<DecodedBatch, IngestError>` seam between `prost`-decode and `tokio::sync::mpsc` send so chunk #18 (post-decode invariants + AppError::Ingest variant) can attach without restructuring; the mpsc producer side and rate-limiting `tower::Layer` slot are architected but inert (rate limiting lands in chunk #19, mpsc consumer in storage-epoch chunks). `cargo deny check bans` stays green — the `tonic <0.14` deny canary in `deny.toml:39` is the safety net for the documented `tonic 0.14 ↔ opentelemetry-otlp 0.31 (pinned tonic 0.13)` duplicate concern (per security extract + arch extract + session-handoff Tier 2 testing.md note).

1. **Resolve Q1 (`opentelemetry-proto` 0.31 transitive `tonic` version)** before adding code:
   - Add `opentelemetry-proto = { version = "0.31", default-features = false, features = ["gen-tonic", "trace", "metrics", "logs"] }` + `tonic = { version = "0.14", features = ["transport"] }` + `prost = "0.14"` to `Cargo.toml` `[workspace.dependencies]`.
   - Add `tonic.workspace = true`, `prost.workspace = true`, `opentelemetry-proto.workspace = true` to `crates/ingest/Cargo.toml`.
   - Run `cargo deny check bans`. If a `tonic 0.13` duplicate appears (canary fires), STOP — switch to vendored-proto fallback: vendor the OTLP `.proto` files into `crates/ingest/proto/`, add `crates/ingest/build.rs` invoking `tonic-build = "0.14"` to generate stubs locally, and remove `opentelemetry-proto` from the dep set. Either path satisfies arch §Standard Contracts spec-conformance.

2. **Add shared `IngestState`** at `crates/ingest/src/state.rs`:
   - `pub struct IngestState { span_count: AtomicU64, broadcast_subscribers: AtomicU32 }` (atomics for lock-free hot-path reads).
   - `pub fn new() -> Self`, `pub fn snapshot(&self) -> IngestStateSnapshot`, `pub fn record_export(&self, span_count: u64)` for handler increments.
   - Co-located `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` with one positive concurrency test (`#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]`) showing concurrent `record_export` calls accumulate correctly.

3. **Implement gRPC server module** at `crates/ingest/src/grpc.rs` (single-file module; no need for sub-module split):
   - `pub async fn serve(addr: SocketAddr, state: Arc<IngestState>) -> Result<(), Error>` — entry point.
   - Define `TraceServiceImpl(Arc<IngestState>)`, `MetricsServiceImpl(Arc<IngestState>)`, `LogsServiceImpl(Arc<IngestState>)` structs implementing the three `opentelemetry_proto::tonic::collector::*::v1::*Service` traits.
   - Each handler: `#[tracing::instrument(skip(req), fields(rpc.system = "grpc", rpc.service = "...", rpc.method = "Export", span_count = tracing::field::Empty, traceparent = tracing::field::Empty))]`. Inside, extract `traceparent` from `req.metadata().get_bin("grpc-trace-bin")` via a small helper (`extract_traceparent`), record span fields via `tracing::Span::current().record(...)`. Wrap the prost-decode boundary in `let _decode_span = tracing::debug_span!("parse.protobuf").entered();` block. Increment `state.record_export(span_count)`. Return `Ok(Response::new(default_response()))` on success.
   - Build `Server::builder().add_service(TraceServiceServer::new(impl).max_decoding_message_size(8 * 1024 * 1024)).add_service(MetricsServiceServer::new(impl).max_decoding_message_size(8 * 1024 * 1024)).add_service(LogsServiceServer::new(impl).max_decoding_message_size(8 * 1024 * 1024)).serve(addr).await`.
   - Map `tonic::transport::Error` to `Error::BindFailed { reason: <sanitized message> }` — sanitize by stripping struct names / paths / library versions per security plan §Error Handling.
   - **DO NOT** introduce any `opentelemetry-otlp` exporter or any OTLP-network-export construct (per CLAUDE.md universal invariant + security extract criterion #5).

4. **Extend the contract module** at `crates/ingest/src/contract.rs`:
   - Add to `Error` enum: `BindFailed { reason: String }`, `InvalidPort { value: String }`. Display strings stay sanitized one-liners.
   - Modify `IngestHeartbeat` struct usage: `heartbeat_payload(state: &IngestState) -> IngestHeartbeat` reads from the shared state instead of returning `Default::default()`. (Preserve the original signature as `heartbeat_payload_default()` for backward-compat OR change call site in `pulse-app/src/heartbeat.rs:52` to pass the state — prefer the latter, fewer abstractions.)
   - Update co-located test `heartbeat_payload_is_callable` to construct an `IngestState` and pass it.
5. **Extend `crates/ingest/src/lib.rs`**: add `pub mod grpc;` and `pub mod state;` alongside existing `pub mod contract;`.

6. **Wire bind-status slot into `HeartbeatState`** at `crates/ui-bridge/src/health.rs`:
   - Define `pub enum BindStatus { Ok, Failed(String) }` (Display strings sanitized).
   - Add `otlp_grpc_bind: Mutex<Option<BindStatus>>` field to `HeartbeatState` + `record_otlp_grpc_bind(&self, status: BindStatus)` setter + `otlp_grpc_bind(&self) -> Option<BindStatus>` reader.
   - Modify `current_health()` to populate `subsystems.otlp_grpc_receiver.status` from `state.otlp_grpc_bind()` (Ok → `"ok"` + `error_msg = None`; Failed(reason) → `"bind_failed"` + `error_msg = Some(reason)`); leave `last_tick_at` from `state.last_ingest()` (already present — wire is `ingest_channel.last_tick_at`, but `otlp_grpc_receiver.last_tick_at` may also be set to `state.last_ingest()` since the heartbeat covers the receiver's liveness).
   - Co-located test extension: `current_health_reports_otlp_grpc_bind_status_when_recorded` (Ok and Failed both) + ensure `otlp_grpc_receiver.{status,error_msg}` reflect the slot.

7. **Update `pulse-app/src/heartbeat.rs:51-61`** so `emit_ingest_tick` reads real values:
   - Pass `Arc<ingest::state::IngestState>` into `spawn(...)` (extend signature).
   - `emit_ingest_tick(state: &HeartbeatState, ingest_state: &ingest::state::IngestState)` calls `ingest::contract::heartbeat_payload(ingest_state)` instead of the no-arg version.
   - Update the four existing co-located tests in `pulse-app/src/heartbeat.rs` (`emit_ingest_tick_emits_target_and_fields`, `emit_buffer_tick_*`, `emit_viz_tick_*`, `emit_plugins_tick_*`, `spawn_returns_four_handles_*`) to construct an `IngestState` and pass it through. Keep field assertions intact.

8. **Spawn the gRPC server in `pulse-app/src/main.rs`**:
   - Before the Tauri builder, instantiate `let ingest_state = Arc::new(ingest::state::IngestState::new());` and `let heartbeat_state = Arc::new(HeartbeatState::new());` (already exists).
   - Resolve port: `let port: u16 = env::var("ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_GRPC_PORT").ok().and_then(|s| s.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(4317);` with `TryFrom<u16>` discipline (per arch §Conventions Configuration units). 0 is honored to allow OS-assigned port for tests.
   - Construct `let addr = SocketAddr::from(([127, 0, 0, 1], port));` — explicit `[127, 0, 0, 1]` literal, NEVER `[0, 0, 0, 0]` or `Ipv4Addr::UNSPECIFIED`.
   - Inside `.setup(move |_app| { ... })`, spawn the gRPC task: `let grpc_state = Arc::clone(&ingest_state); let bind_announcer = Arc::clone(&heartbeat_state); tauri::async_runtime::spawn(async move { match ingest::grpc::serve(addr, grpc_state).await { Ok(()) => bind_announcer.record_otlp_grpc_bind(BindStatus::Ok), Err(e) => { tracing::error!(target: "app.boot.otlp.grpc.bind", reason = %e, bind_address = %addr, "bind failed"); bind_announcer.record_otlp_grpc_bind(BindStatus::Failed(format!("{}", e))); } } });`. (Note: the bind status flips to `Ok` only after the server returns — for a long-running server, mark `Ok` immediately after successful initial bind by splitting the task into bind-then-serve; plan recommends a small helper `try_bind_and_serve` returning `Result<impl Future, Error>` so we can record `Ok` as soon as the listener is up.)
   - Pass `ingest_state` into `heartbeat::spawn(heartbeat_state.clone(), ingest_state.clone())`.

9. **Extend the PII allowlist** at `pulse-app/src/observability.rs:108-119`:
   - Extend the existing `ingest` target entry with: `"rpc.system"`, `"rpc.service"`, `"rpc.method"`, `"traceparent"`, `"latency_ms"`, `"method"`, `"status"`, `"attributes_count"`, `"service_name_tag"`, `"trace_ids"`.
   - Register new target keys: `"app.boot.otlp.grpc.bind"` with allowlist `["bind_address", "reason"]`; `"ingest.grpc.parse.error"` with allowlist `["span_field_invalid", "expected_length", "actual_length", "rejection_reason"]`.
   - Per the Session Additions 2026-05-03 plural-vs-singular gotcha: the keys above use the verbatim `tracing` target strings; the `for_target` strip-suffix lookup will resolve `ingest.grpc.export.request` → `ingest` (existing entry handles it).

10. **Author integration tests** at `crates/ingest/tests/grpc_loopback.rs`:
    - Test fixture helper `start_test_server() -> (SocketAddr, Arc<IngestState>, JoinHandle)` binds an ephemeral port (`ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_GRPC_PORT=0` semantics).
    - Positive test: live `tonic::TraceServiceClient::connect(...)` → send a synthetic `ExportTraceServiceRequest` with valid 16-byte `trace_id` + 8-byte `span_id` → assert response status OK + `state.snapshot().span_count >= 1`.
    - Negative test "max_decoding_message_size enforced": send a 9 MB payload (e.g., a span batch padded to ≥9 MB) → assert response code matches the tonic 0.14 oversized-message error variant (likely `tonic::Code::ResourceExhausted` per chunk title; verify against tonic 0.14 actual surface during /implement; if it differs, document in test comment).
    - Negative test "non-loopback bind rejected" (unit-level alternative since OS may not allow non-loopback bind in test env): grep `crates/ingest/src/` for `0.0.0.0` / `Ipv4Addr::UNSPECIFIED` literals — assert zero matches via `cargo nextest` test that runs the grep.
    - Each test gets fresh `tempfile::TempDir` + sets `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR=$TMPDIR/test-...`. Use `#[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread")]` (NOT `start_paused = true` — workspace tokio lacks `test-util` feature per `.claude/rules/testing.md` Session Additions 2026-05-03).

11. **Run the full quality gate locally** before commit:
    - `cargo fmt --check` + `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`.
    - `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci`.
    - `cargo deny check bans licenses sources` — verify the `tonic <0.14` canary still fires only on intent (no skip-list addition for `tonic`).
    - `cargo audit`.
    - `cargo llvm-cov nextest -p ingest --lcov` — verify ≥75% line / ≥70% branch / ≥85% function on new code (excluding any `prost`/`tonic-build` generated stubs).
    - `cargo xtask test` — agent harness wrapper.
- `crates/ingest/src/grpc.rs` — tonic gRPC server module; three `*ServiceImpl` types + `serve()` entry; per combined.md acceptance criteria security #2 + arch + obs #1.
- `crates/ingest/src/state.rs` — `IngestState` shared atomic-counter state for handler hot-path + heartbeat read; per combined.md (obs heartbeat criterion + arch mpsc producer ownership).
- `crates/ingest/tests/grpc_loopback.rs` — integration tests: positive E2E + 9 MB rejection negative + `0.0.0.0` grep gate negative; per combined.md (tests acceptance criteria 3-7).
- `crates/ingest/proto/` + `crates/ingest/build.rs` (CONDITIONAL — only if Q1 fallback path is taken; default plan does NOT create these).
- `Cargo.toml` (workspace root) — add `tonic`, `prost`, `opentelemetry-proto`, `tempfile`, `rstest`, `proptest` to `[workspace.dependencies]`. (per arch + tests acceptance criteria; resolves Q1.)
- `crates/ingest/Cargo.toml` — opt into the new workspace deps + add `[dev-dependencies]` for test fixtures. (per arch acceptance criterion #1.)
- `crates/ingest/src/lib.rs` — add `pub mod grpc;` and `pub mod state;`.
- `crates/ingest/src/contract.rs` — extend `Error` enum with `BindFailed`, `InvalidPort` variants; modify `heartbeat_payload` signature to accept `&IngestState`. Update existing co-located test.

- `crates/ui-bridge/src/health.rs` — extend `HeartbeatState` with `otlp_grpc_bind` slot + `BindStatus` enum + reader/writer methods; populate `subsystems.otlp_grpc_receiver.{status,error_msg}` in `current_health()` from the slot. Add a co-located test for the new slot.

- `pulse-app/src/heartbeat.rs:10-95` — extend `spawn(...)` signature with `Arc<ingest::state::IngestState>`; update `emit_ingest_tick` to pass it through to `ingest::contract::heartbeat_payload(...)`. Update co-located tests to construct + pass `IngestState`.

body: - (security) `crates/ingest/src/` source tree contains zero occurrences of `0.0.0.0`, `Ipv4Addr::UNSPECIFIED`, `Ipv6Addr::UNSPECIFIED`, `[::]`, or `SocketAddr::from(([0, 0, 0, 0], _))` — verified via grep gate (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions security #1).

- (security) Each of the three `*ServiceServer` builders (TraceService / MetricsService / LogsService) calls `.max_decoding_message_size(8 * 1024 * 1024)` — verified via grep for the literal `8 * 1024 * 1024` (or named const) appearing 3× adjacent to `*ServiceServer::new(...)` chains, OR via the negative test that rejects a 9 MB request with `tonic::Code::ResourceExhausted` (per combined §security #2).

- (security) `cargo deny check bans licenses sources` passes after adding `tonic 0.14`, `prost 0.14`, and `opentelemetry-proto` to the workspace dep tree — no new duplicate-version regressions; `tonic <0.14` deny canary remains in `deny.toml` (per combined §security #3 + §Cross-domain bindings security ↔ tests/CI).
- (security) `cargo audit` passes with zero new advisory findings introduced by chunk #16's dep additions (per combined §security #4).

- (security) `crates/ingest/src/` source tree contains zero occurrences of an `opentelemetry-otlp` exporter or any OTLP-network-export construct pointed at `:4317` — `tracing` is the only self-observation runtime per CLAUDE.md universal invariant (per combined §security #5).
- (security) `crates/ingest/src/` `tracing::*!` calls do NOT include `attributes`, `body`, `request`, or `payload` field bindings — verified via grep gate (per combined §security #6).

- (arch) Receiver code lives in `crates/ingest/src/` per workspace boundary rules; `crates/ingest/Cargo.toml` declares `tonic = "0.14"` + `prost = "0.14"` + uses `opentelemetry-proto` for service definitions (or vendored proto via `tonic-build` if Q1 fallback) (per combined §arch #1).
- (arch) `crates/ingest/Cargo.toml` does NOT depend on the `pulse-app` binary crate; `cargo tree -p ingest` confirms no path-edge to `pulse-app` (per combined §arch #2).

- (arch) Server bind respects `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_GRPC_PORT` env var override (parsed via `u16::from_str` with `TryFrom<u16>` validation downstream); default port is `:4317`; bind address is `127.0.0.1`-only (per combined §arch #3).
- (arch) gRPC services implemented are `TraceService`, `MetricsService`, `LogsService` from `opentelemetry-proto` exactly — no project-specific envelope, no fork (per combined §arch #4).
- (arch) `*ServiceServer` builders set `.max_decoding_message_size(8 * 1024 * 1024)` (cross-binding to security #2 above; double-counted intentionally for both audit trails) (per combined §arch #5).

- (arch) The `health` TauRPC command's `subsystems.otlp_grpc_receiver` field reports `"ok"` when bound, `"bind_failed: <reason>"` when degraded — verified via integration test that pre-binds the port to force a failure (per combined §arch #7).

- (obs) `otlp.grpc.export.request` span emitted on every gRPC `Export` call (TraceService / MetricsService / LogsService) with required attributes: `rpc.system = "grpc"`, `rpc.service`, `rpc.method`, `span_count`, `traceparent` (when extracted from `grpc-trace-bin` metadata) — verified via `jq` over `agent-latest.jsonl` after a synthetic export (per combined §obs #1).

- (obs) PII Vector 1 enforced at gRPC boundary: `grep -E '(span\.attributes|attribute_value)' ~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/agent-latest.jsonl` returns empty after a synthetic OTLP export with secret-shaped attribute values (per combined §obs #2).

- (obs) `ingest.tick` heartbeat fires every 15s carrying real (non-zero after activity) `span_count` from the new `IngestState`; CI gate fails if no `ingest.tick` event observed within 45s (per combined §obs #3).

- (obs) Bind failure emits structured `error!(target: "app.boot.otlp.grpc.bind", reason = %err, bind_address = "127.0.0.1:4317")` line; `health` IPC subsystem field `otlp_grpc_receiver` reflects `"bind_failed: address in use"` on test that pre-binds the port (per combined §obs #4).

- (obs) `parse.protobuf` inner child span emitted on every successful payload decode with `duration_ms` field; `ingest.grpc.parse.error` scaffold present (chunk #18 populates the body) (per combined §obs #5).

- (obs) Default subscriber fields (`service.name = "com.andromeda.pulse"`, `service.version`, `deployment.environment`) appear on every gRPC-boundary log line — verified by `jq -e '.fields["service.name"] == "com.andromeda.pulse"'` (per combined §obs #6).

- (obs) NO OTel SDK crate (`opentelemetry`, `opentelemetry_sdk`, `opentelemetry-otlp`, `opentelemetry-stdout`) appears in `cargo tree -p ingest` output — only `tonic` 0.14, `prost`, `opentelemetry-proto` (per combined §obs #7).
- (tests) `cargo nextest run --filter-expr 'package(ingest)'` passes for new tests; zero failures, zero flakes (per combined §tests #1).

- (tests) Coverage gate: `cargo llvm-cov nextest -p ingest --lcov` reports ≥75% line / ≥70% branch / ≥85% function on new `crates/ingest/src/` code (excluding generated stubs) (per combined §tests #2).

body: **Constraints across domains:**

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase Phase 4. Read by /andromeda-implement.
Manual edits between runs are fine; do not edit during /implement run._
- **Phase number:** 14

- **Route chunks covered:**
  - route#17 "OTLP HTTP receiver — axum 0.8 :4318 bound 127.0.0.1, POST /v1/{traces,metrics,logs}, DefaultBodyLimit + Host-header allowlist + CORS deny"
- **Epoch:** Epoch 2 — Ingest pipeline (chunk #16 gRPC receiver completed; chunk #17 HTTP receiver this phase)

Land the second OTLP receiver — an axum 0.8 HTTP server bound to `127.0.0.1:4318` exposing exactly `POST /v1/traces`, `POST /v1/metrics`, `POST /v1/logs` per the OpenTelemetry HTTP profile spec — and bring its security middleware stack live: `axum::DefaultBodyLimit::max(8 * 1024 * 1024)` (per security plan §Input Validation row 2 + §API Security Request size limit row), Host-header allowlist (DNS-rebinding mitigation per §API Security Host header row + the Coder Agent CVE-2025-09-19 / MCP TypeScript SDK CVE-2025-66414 anchor), and CORS default-deny via `tower_http::cors::CorsLayer::new()` with no `allow_origin` calls (per §API Security CORS row).

The implementation mirrors chunk #16's gRPC receiver (`crates/ingest/src/grpc.rs`) by reusing the established `try_bind() -> TcpListener` + `serve_on(listener) -> Future` split for early bind-status reporting, the `HeartbeatState.otlp_*_bind` slot pattern in `crates/ui-bridge/src/health.rs` for `health` envelope reporting, the vendored OTLP `.proto` types from `ingest::grpc::proto::*` for shared protobuf decode (no new `opentelemetry-proto` runtime dep — preserves obs criterion #7 strict-grep forbid per `.claude/rules/observability.md` Session Additions 2026-05-04), the per-target field allowlist registry in `pulse-app/src/observability.rs::AllowList::production()` for PII default-deny (Vector 1, per security plan §Logging & Monitoring), and the loopback-only security grep gate at `crates/ingest/tests/grpc_loopback.rs::no_non_loopback_bind_literals_in_ingest_src` which AUTOMATICALLY scans the new `crates/ingest/src/http.rs` once added.

The HTTP/protobuf path (`Content-Type: application/x-protobuf`) is the canonical decoding required by the chunk title and ships in this phase with full integration coverage; the HTTP/JSON path (`Content-Type: application/json`) is also part of OTLP HTTP spec conformance and ships behind the same handlers via content-type dispatch — see Implementation notes for scoping confirmation at user review.

1. **Add HTTP-stack workspace dependencies.** In root `Cargo.toml` `[workspace.dependencies]` (after the chunk #16 ingest pipeline block, with a one-line provenance comment `# OTLP HTTP receiver (route#17 — Epoch 2 continues)`): add `axum = { version = "0.8", default-features = false, features = ["http1", "tokio", "macros"] }`, `tower = "0.5"`, `tower-http = { version = "0.6", features = ["cors", "limit", "trace"] }`, `bytes = "1"`, `http = "1"`, `serde_json = "1"`, plus dev-side `axum-test = "18"` and `reqwest = { version = "0.12", default-features = false, features = ["json", "rustls-tls"] }`. Run `cargo deny check bans licenses sources` after adding; if a transitive duplicate fires, add a one-line provenance entry to `deny.toml [bans] skip` per chunk #16 precedent (`foldhash` block at lines 89-92) — never relax `multiple-versions = "deny"`.

2. **Opt the ingest crate into the new workspace deps.** In `crates/ingest/Cargo.toml`, add to `[dependencies]`: `axum.workspace = true`, `tower.workspace = true`, `tower-http.workspace = true`, `bytes.workspace = true`, `http.workspace = true`, `serde_json.workspace = true`. Add to `[dev-dependencies]`: `axum-test.workspace = true`, `reqwest.workspace = true`.

3. **Create `crates/ingest/src/http.rs`.** New file mirrors the shape of `crates/ingest/src/grpc.rs`:
   - `pub const DEFAULT_HTTP_PORT: u16 = 4318;`
   - `pub const MAX_DECODING_BODY_SIZE: usize = 8 * 1024 * 1024;`
   - `pub async fn try_bind(addr: SocketAddr) -> Result<tokio::net::TcpListener, Error>` — reuses `crate::contract::Error::BindFailed { reason }`; emits via `sanitize_error` helper (local copy of `grpc.rs:237-243`).
   - `pub async fn serve_on(listener: tokio::net::TcpListener, state: Arc<IngestState>) -> Result<(), Error>` — calls `axum::serve(listener, build_router(state).into_make_service())`; converts axum errors via `Error::ServeFailed { reason }`.
   - Private `fn build_router(state: Arc<IngestState>, port: u16) -> axum::Router` — constructs 3 POST routes (`/v1/traces`, `/v1/metrics`, `/v1/logs`); applies the middleware stack via `tower::ServiceBuilder` in this order (outermost → innermost):
     1. `tower_http::trace::TraceLayer` (plain `tracing` spans, NOT OTel-flavored — per `.claude/rules/observability.md` §Trace context propagation)
     2. `axum::middleware::from_fn` Host-header allowlist (rejects with `StatusCode::FORBIDDEN` if Host not in `{127.0.0.1:port, localhost:port, [::1]:port}`)
     3. `axum::DefaultBodyLimit::max(MAX_DECODING_BODY_SIZE)` (8 MB)
     4. `tower_http::cors::CorsLayer::new()` (default-deny — no `allow_origin` calls)
   - Per-handler async fns: `handle_traces / handle_metrics / handle_logs(State(state), headers, bytes)`. Each:
     - `#[tracing::instrument(skip(state, body, headers), fields(http.method = "POST", http.route, content_type, body_size_bytes, status_code = tracing::field::Empty, span_count = tracing::field::Empty, traceparent = tracing::field::Empty))]`
     - Extract `traceparent` header via `extract_traceparent_http(headers)` → `tracing::Span::current().record("traceparent", ...)`
     - Dispatch on `Content-Type` header: `application/x-protobuf` → `prost::Message::decode(bytes)` of the appropriate vendored proto type from `crate::grpc::proto::opentelemetry::proto::collector::{trace,metrics,logs}::v1::Export*ServiceRequest`; `application/json` → `serde_json::from_slice` of the same generated type (note: `pbjson` derive may be needed; see Implementation notes / Open question #1 for HTTP/JSON scoping decision)
     - Inner debug span `parse.protobuf` (or `parse.json`) brackets the decode call (mirrors `grpc.rs:121-123`)
     - Reuse `count_spans` / `count_metric_data_points` / `count_log_records` (re-implemented locally; do NOT promote to `pub(crate)` in grpc.rs — keeps grpc.rs unchanged per research.md "Conventions to follow")
     - Record decoded count via `state.record_*(count)`; record `span_count` field on span; record `status_code = 200` field
     - Return empty `Export*ServiceResponse` serialized as protobuf or JSON to match content-type, with HTTP 200
   - `fn extract_traceparent_http(headers: &http::HeaderMap) -> Option<String>` reads the `traceparent` header (already a hex string per W3C Trace Context — no encoding step needed unlike gRPC's `grpc-trace-bin`)
   - `async fn host_header_allowlist(port: u16, request, next) -> Response` middleware — inspects request `Host` header; if value is not in `{format!("127.0.0.1:{port}"), format!("localhost:{port}"), format!("[::1]:{port}")}` (or no `Host` header), emits `tracing::warn!(target: "ingest::http", host_header_rejected = true, expected_host_class = "loopback", "host header rejected")` and returns `StatusCode::FORBIDDEN`. Never log raw Host header value verbatim (per combined.md anti-pattern + obs Vector 1).
   - `#[cfg(test)] mod tests {...}` with: `try_bind_succeeds_on_ephemeral_port`, `try_bind_returns_bind_failed_on_collision`, `extract_traceparent_http_returns_none_when_missing`, `extract_traceparent_http_returns_value_when_present`, `host_allowlist_accepts_127_0_0_1`, `host_allowlist_rejects_evil_example`, `max_decoding_body_size_is_8_mb`, `count_spans_sums_across_resource_and_scope`.
4. **Register the new module.** In `crates/ingest/src/lib.rs` add `pub mod http;` line after the existing `pub mod grpc;`.

5. **Extend the `BindStatus` slot pattern in ui-bridge.** In `crates/ui-bridge/src/health.rs`:
   - Add `otlp_http_bind: Mutex<Option<BindStatus>>` field to `HeartbeatState` struct (line 30, immediately after `otlp_grpc_bind`).
   - Add `record_otlp_http_bind(&self, status: BindStatus)` setter (mirror of `record_otlp_grpc_bind` at line 49-51).
   - Add `otlp_http_bind(&self) -> Option<BindStatus>` reader (mirror at line 65-67).
   - Extend `current_health()` (lines 134-172): after the existing `match state.otlp_grpc_bind() {...}` block (lines 147-158), add a parallel `match state.otlp_http_bind() {...}` block that populates `subsystems.otlp_http_receiver.{status, last_tick_at, error_msg}` and flips `overall_ok = false` on `Some(BindStatus::Failed(reason))`. The `last_tick_at` field reuses `state.last_ingest()` since the `ingest.tick` heartbeat covers both receivers' shared `IngestState`.
   - Add 2 co-located unit tests mirroring the gRPC slot tests (lines 263-279): `heartbeat_state_otlp_http_bind_slot_starts_empty` + `heartbeat_state_records_otlp_http_bind_ok_and_failed`.

6. **Wire HTTP receiver boot in pulse-app/main.rs.** In `pulse-app/src/main.rs`:
   - Add `const ENV_OTLP_HTTP_PORT: &str = "ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_HTTP_PORT";` near the existing `ENV_OTLP_GRPC_PORT` constant (line 14).
   - Add `fn resolve_http_port() -> u16` symmetric to `resolve_grpc_port` (lines 16-31), referencing `ingest::http::DEFAULT_HTTP_PORT` for fallback. Emit `tracing::warn!(target: "app.boot.otlp.http.port", raw_len = raw.len(), ...)` on parse failure.
   - In `setup()` block (lines 110-148), after the existing gRPC `tauri::async_runtime::spawn(async move {...})` block (which ends near line 145) and before `let _heartbeat_handles = heartbeat::spawn(...)`: add a SECOND `tauri::async_runtime::spawn(async move {...})` block. The closure clones `bind_announcer = Arc::clone(&heartbeat_state)` and `http_state = Arc::clone(&ingest_state)`; computes `let http_port = resolve_http_port(); let http_addr = SocketAddr::from(([127, 0, 0, 1], http_port));`; calls `ingest::http::try_bind(http_addr)` → on `Ok` records `BindStatus::Ok` via `bind_announcer.record_otlp_http_bind(...)` + emits `tracing::info!(target: "app.boot.otlp.http.bind", bind_address = %http_addr, "OTLP HTTP receiver bound")` + calls `ingest::http::serve_on(listener, http_state).await` with serve-error handling identical to gRPC; on `Err` records `BindStatus::Failed(reason)` + emits `tracing::error!(target: "app.boot.otlp.http.bind", reason = %reason, bind_address = %http_addr, "bind failed")`.
   - The variable that bridges the two ports MUST be named distinctly (`grpc_addr`, `http_addr`, `grpc_state`, `http_state`, `grpc_announcer`, `http_announcer`) so each spawn closure captures its own clones cleanly.

7. **Extend the observability allowlist registry.** In `pulse-app/src/observability.rs::AllowList::production()`:
   - Extend the existing `ingest` entry's `HashSet` (lines 111-132) with new HTTP-boundary fields: `"http.method"`, `"http.route"`, `"http.status_code"`, `"content_type"`, `"route"`, `"body_size_bytes"`, `"limit_bytes"`, `"http_response_code"`, `"host_header_rejected"`, `"expected_host_class"`. (10 added entries.)
   - Add new top-level `by_target` entries adjacent to the existing `app.boot.otlp.grpc.*` entries (after line 258):
     - `"app.boot.otlp.http.bind"` → fields `["bind_address", "reason"]`
     - `"app.boot.otlp.http.port"` → fields `["raw_len"]`
     - `"ingest.http.parse.error"` → fields `["span_field_invalid", "expected_length", "actual_length", "rejection_reason"]` (mirror of existing `ingest.grpc.parse.error` at lines 261-272)
     - `"ingest.http.body_size.exceeded"` → fields `["body_size_bytes", "limit_bytes", "http_response_code"]`

8. **Create `crates/ingest/tests/http_loopback.rs`.** New integration suite mirrors `tests/grpc_loopback.rs`:
   - `start_test_http_server() -> (SocketAddr, Arc<IngestState>, JoinHandle<()>)` helper: ephemeral-port `try_bind` on `[127, 0, 0, 1]:0` → `tokio::spawn(serve_on(listener, state_clone))` → 50ms accept-loop wait.
   - Synthetic OTLP builders: duplicate `make_span` / `make_export_request` from `grpc_loopback.rs:26-53` (no premature shared-helper extraction per research.md Open question #4).
   - Tests:
     1. `p1_http_post_protobuf_traces_roundtrip` — `reqwest::Client` POSTs prost-encoded `ExportTraceServiceRequest` (100 spans) to `http://{addr}/v1/traces` with `Content-Type: application/x-protobuf`; asserts response 200 + `state.span_count() == 100`.
     2. `p1_http_post_protobuf_metrics_roundtrip` — analogous for `/v1/metrics` + `state.metric_data_point_count`.
     3. `p1_http_post_protobuf_logs_roundtrip` — analogous for `/v1/logs` + `state.log_record_count`.
     4. `body_over_8mb_returns_413` — POST with 9 MB body asserts HTTP 413 (Payload Too Large) and state counters unchanged.
     5. `host_header_evil_example_returns_403` — POST `/v1/traces` with `Host: evil.example.com:4318` asserts HTTP 403 + state.span_count unchanged.
     6. `cors_preflight_no_allow_origin_header` — `OPTIONS /v1/traces` with `Origin: https://evil.example.com` + `Access-Control-Request-Method: POST` headers; asserts response carries no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header (default-deny posture).
     7. `try_bind_rejects_collision_with_bind_failed` — second `try_bind` on already-bound port returns `Error::BindFailed`.
   - The existing `no_non_loopback_bind_literals_in_ingest_src` test in `tests/grpc_loopback.rs` AUTOMATICALLY covers the new `src/http.rs` (it walks `crates/ingest/src/` recursively); no duplicate test needed.

9. **Verify supply-chain + build hygiene.** Run `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo deny check bans licenses sources`, `cargo audit`. If `cargo deny check bans` fires any new transitive duplicate (e.g., `tower` 0.4 vs 0.5, `http-body` 0.4 vs 1, etc.), append entries to `deny.toml [bans] skip` with one-line provenance comments — do NOT relax `multiple-versions = "deny"`. Verify `cargo tree -p ingest | grep opentelemetry` returns empty (obs criterion #7 strict-grep forbid).

body: - (security) `crates/ingest/src/http.rs` contains zero forbidden bind literals — existing `no_non_loopback_bind_literals_in_ingest_src` test (in `tests/grpc_loopback.rs`) walks the full `crates/ingest/src/` tree and asserts no `0.0.0.0` / `Ipv4Addr::UNSPECIFIED` / `Ipv6Addr::UNSPECIFIED` / `[::]` / `([0, 0, 0, 0]` literals (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions).

- (security) Integration test `body_over_8mb_returns_413` posts a >8 MB body to `POST /v1/traces` and asserts response is HTTP 413; `axum::DefaultBodyLimit::max(8 * 1024 * 1024)` is wired (per combined §Constraints + JFrog axum-core advisory anchor).

- (security) Integration test `host_header_evil_example_returns_403` posts with `Host: evil.example.com:4318` to `POST /v1/traces` against the loopback listener and asserts HTTP 403; Host-header allowlist middleware is wired (DNS-rebinding mitigation per combined §Constraints + Coder Agent CVE-2025-09-19 / MCP TypeScript SDK CVE-2025-66414 anchors).

- (security) Integration test `cors_preflight_no_allow_origin_header` posts `OPTIONS /v1/traces` with `Origin: https://evil.example.com` + `Access-Control-Request-Method: POST` and asserts response carries no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header; CORS default-deny posture proven (per combined §Constraints).

- (security) `cargo deny check bans licenses sources` continues to pass after axum 0.8 + tower-http stack lands; any new transitive duplicates in `deny.toml [bans] skip` carry one-line provenance comments per Session Additions convention; `tonic <0.14` deny canary remains outside the skip list (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions).

- (arch) HTTP receiver code lives in `crates/ingest/src/http.rs`; `cargo tree -p ingest` shows `axum`, `hyper`, `tower` with no opentelemetry-* runtime deps (cargo tree | grep opentelemetry returns empty) and no second Tokio runtime (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions + obs criterion #7 strict-grep forbid).

- (arch) `axum::Router` exposes exactly `POST /v1/traces`, `POST /v1/metrics`, `POST /v1/logs` (no extra paths, no URL versioning prefix); `Content-Type: application/x-protobuf` accepted as the canonical decoding (per combined §Constraints + arch §Standard Contracts "OTLP receiver").

- (arch) HTTP server bind/serve uses the same `try_bind() -> TcpListener` + `serve_on(listener) -> Future` split as chunk #16 gRPC; `pulse-app/src/main.rs` records `BindStatus::Ok` for `subsystems.otlp_http_receiver` immediately after listener accepts; bind failure flips overall `health.status` to `"degraded"` and populates failure reason string (per combined §Patterns to follow + arch §Standard Contracts `health`).

- (arch) `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_OTLP_HTTP_PORT` env var is the only HTTP-receiver-specific knob added; `resolve_http_port()` mirrors `resolve_grpc_port()` (env > default `:4318`) with `u16` parse + warn-on-invalid fallback (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions + arch §Occupied Resources Environment variables).

- (tests) `cargo nextest run -p ingest` passes with new HTTP integration suite at `crates/ingest/tests/http_loopback.rs`; minimum cases: protobuf POST roundtrip per `/v1/traces` + `/v1/metrics` + `/v1/logs`, 9 MB payload returns 413, Host-header negative returns 403, CORS preflight returns no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, bind-collision yields `Error::BindFailed`. ≥ 7 new integration tests + ≥ 8 unit tests in `src/http.rs` (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions).

- (tests) `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` exit code 0; final-line regex `test result: ok. (\d+) passed` parses; total count strictly increases from 55 (chunk #16 close) (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions).

- (tests) Coverage gate: `cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --lcov` reports ≥ 75% line / ≥ 70% branch / ≥ 85% function for `crates/ingest/src/http*.rs` (Standard tier per test-plan §10) (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions).

- (tests) `cargo xtask harness:boot` (or `bash scripts/agent-run.sh boot`) reports `subsystems.otlp_http_receiver.status == "ok"` within 10 s timeout; pre-occupied port test reports `subsystems.otlp_http_receiver.status == "bind_failed"` with non-null `error_msg` (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions).

- (obs) Every successful `POST /v1/{traces,metrics,logs}` emits exactly one `ingest::http`-targeted server-kind boundary span with required fields `route`, `status_code`, `body_size_bytes`, `traceparent` (when client provided), `span_count`, `content_type` — verified by post-test `jq` filter on `agent-latest.jsonl` (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions).

- (obs) Body-size rejection (`body_over_8mb_returns_413` test) emits `ingest.http.body_size.exceeded` span at WARN/ERROR with `body_size_bytes`, `limit_bytes: 8388608`, `http_response_code: 413` — verified by chaos test `jq` filter (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions).

- (obs) PII grep on `agent-latest.jsonl` after sending HTTP POST containing a secret in OTLP attribute value returns empty for the secret value — `attributes_count` + `service_name_tag` may appear but raw attribute content MUST NOT (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions + Vector 1).

- (obs) `pulse-app/src/observability.rs::AllowList::production()` registry contains entries for `ingest.http.parse.error`, `ingest.http.body_size.exceeded`, `app.boot.otlp.http.bind`, `app.boot.otlp.http.port` with explicit field allowlists; default-deny posture verified by injecting non-allowlisted field through HTTP handler and confirming it appears as `<redacted>` in the sink (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions).

- **HTTP/JSON content-type scoping confirmation:** the OTLP HTTP spec requires both `application/x-protobuf` AND `application/json` content-types. The vendored prost-generated types do NOT have `serde::Deserialize` derives by default. Two paths: (a) add `pbjson` codegen to `crates/ingest/build.rs` to generate JSON-compatible wire types alongside protobuf; (b) defer HTTP/JSON to a follow-on chunk and ship chunk #17 with HTTP/protobuf as the canonical decoding (which is what the chunk title's `application/x-protobuf` literal mentions). **Recommend Phase 6 user review choice:** "ship HTTP/JSON in chunk #17 (full spec conformance now)" vs "defer HTTP/JSON" (matches chunk title literal + reduces scope creep). If user picks "ship HTTP/JSON," `crates/ingest/build.rs` gains a `pbjson-build` invocation alongside `tonic-prost-build`, and handlers add a `Content-Type` dispatch arm. If "defer," handlers reject non-`application/x-protobuf` with HTTP 415 (Unsupported Media Type).

- **Implementation order:** steps must be sequential because each builds on the previous: deps first (1-2) → module + tests (3-4, can be parallel for unit tests vs lib.rs) → ui-bridge slot pattern (5) → main.rs spawn (6) → observability allowlist (7) → integration tests (8) → supply-chain + verification (9-10). The ui-bridge slot pattern (step 5) is a precondition for `record_otlp_http_bind` in step 6; the observability allowlist (step 7) is a precondition for the integration tests (step 8) to assert PII fields are passed/redacted.

- **Tower middleware ordering pitfall:** `tower::ServiceBuilder` applies layers outermost-first. The order in step 3 (`TraceLayer` → host allowlist → DefaultBodyLimit → CorsLayer) means: (a) tracing wraps everything (so all rejected requests still emit boundary spans for observability); (b) Host allowlist runs early to short-circuit on rebind attempts before body read; (c) DefaultBodyLimit runs before parsing (essential — bypassing this is the JFrog axum-core advisory root cause); (d) CORS innermost is fine for default-deny since it never adds permissive headers — its job is only to NOT echo `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`. Verify ordering at /implement time by reviewing axum 0.8 `ServiceBuilder` ergonomics; `axum::middleware::from_fn` for the Host allowlist is recommended over a custom `tower::Layer` impl per research.md Open question #2.

- **Span guard discipline across `.await`:** axum handlers are async — never hold a `tracing::Span` guard across `.await` without `.in_current_span()`. The `#[tracing::instrument]` macro handles this correctly. If hand-rolling spans for the inner `parse.protobuf` block, use the `.entered()` form (returns an `Entered` guard that's safe at sync points) and DROP it before any `.await` (per `.claude/rules/observability.md` §Span discipline + combined.md anti-patterns).

- **Edition 2024 unsafe wrapping:** `protoc-bin-vendored` build.rs invocation in chunk #16 required `unsafe { std::env::set_var(...) }` per Edition 2024's `set_var` unsafe contract. No new build.rs additions in chunk #17 (vendored proto compilation is reused), so this contract does not surface again.

- **`tower` 0.5 vs `tower` 0.4 transitive risk:** `axum` 0.8 targets `tower` 0.5 + `tower-http` 0.6 + `hyper` 1; `tonic` 0.14 ALSO targets `tower` 0.5 + `hyper` 1, so the transitive risk for `tower` duplicate is low. If `cargo deny check bans` fires anyway (e.g., a transient transitive pulls 0.4), add a provenance entry to `deny.toml [bans] skip` per chunk #16 pattern — do NOT relax `multiple-versions = "deny"`.

- **Axum 0.8 macros feature:** the `axum/macros` feature enables `#[debug_handler]` for clearer error messages on handler signatures. Recommended for development; not required for production. Include in workspace deps to ease debugging, then optionally trim at chunk #17 review if footprint matters.

- (tests) `rstest` 0.26.1 fixture composition: `#[fixture] fn mock_span() -> TraceSpan { … }` + `#[rstest] fn test_ingest_accepts_valid_span(mock_span: TraceSpan)` parameterized over invariant boundary cases (per test-plan §4 Fixture pattern unit-level snippet).

- (tests) Existing chunk #17 precedent for ingest integration tests: `crates/ingest/tests/http_loopback.rs` ephemeral-port helper + synthetic OTLP builders + 8 boundary-condition tests; chunk #18 should land an analogous suite under `crates/ingest/tests/invariants.rs` (or extend co-located `grpc.rs` / `http.rs` `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`) keeping the same shape.

- (tests) Status-endpoint binding: chunk #17 wired `record_otlp_http_bind` slot; chunk #18 should wire `subsystems.ingest_channel.{status, broadcast_subscribers}` once the mpsc + invariant gate exists, so the agent-driven harness `status` command shows ingest channel readiness.

- (tests) Loopback ingest as fixture seeding: tests do NOT pre-populate DuckDB; they send synthetic OTLP through the live receiver path (`tonic` client to `:4317`, `reqwest` to `:4318`) and verify via buffer query — same pattern chunks #16/#17 established.

- (obs) `#[tracing::instrument(skip(req), fields(rpc.system = "grpc", rpc.service, rpc.method, span_count, traceparent))]` on tonic gRPC handlers; `#[tracing::instrument]` + tower-http TraceLayer on axum HTTP handlers (already established by chunks #16 + #17) — reuse for the post-decode invariant span layer (per obs-plan §3 Trace context propagation + §4 Instrumentation per surface).

- (obs) Span naming `{module}.{operation}` with `span.kind` field: `ingest.grpc.parse.error` / `ingest.http.parse.error` for invariant violations; `ingest.channel.send` / `ingest.channel.full` for mpsc backpressure events; `ingest.tick` for heartbeats (per obs-plan §4 Span naming + Span kind convention).

- (obs) Default subscriber fields (`service.name = "com.andromeda.pulse"`, `service.version`, `deployment.environment`) registered once at boot via `Layer::with_default_fields(...)` — do not repeat in `info!` macro calls inside this chunk's code (per obs-plan §3 Service identity + §2 Default subscriber fields).

- (obs) Trace context inheritance via `tracing::Span::current()` for downstream tasks; if mpsc consumer task is spawned via `tokio::spawn`, use `.in_current_span()` extension trait to propagate the trace_id from receiver entry into the appender task (per obs-plan §3 Trace context propagation + §11 Spans/Traces "NEVER hold guard across .await").

- (obs) AllowList registration pattern (already established by chunk #17 in `pulse-app/src/observability.rs`): add `ingest.{grpc,http}.parse.error` + `ingest.tick` + `ingest.channel.send` to `by_target` registry; register fields `span_field_invalid`, `expected_length`, `actual_length`, `rejection_reason`, `attributes_count`, `service_name_tag`, `capacity_pct`, `subscribers` in the `ingest` allowlist (per obs-plan §8 Default-deny posture + Whitelist per module).
**Anti-patterns to avoid:**

- (arch) **DO NOT introduce a new workspace crate for the channel** — chunk #18 lives in the existing `ingest` crate. Workspace crate names are LOCKED reserved names; new functionality is added inside an existing crate when the contract permits (per arch §Occupied Resources Cargo workspace crate names + §Project Intent How new functionality is added).

- (arch) **DO NOT depend on `buffer` from `ingest`** — sibling crate dependency violates §Cross-cutting Patterns Module dependency direction. The wiring (mpsc receiver half handed to buffer consumer) is owned by `pulse-app` at startup; the dependency graph stays a DAG with `pulse-app` as the only root.

- (arch) **DO NOT serialize `anyhow::Error` or `thiserror`-derived `IngestError` across the TauRPC bridge** — only `AppError` is `serde`-friendly and bridge-stable. Internal error types stay internal; conversion via `From` impl at the bridge crossing.

- (arch) **DO NOT add a validation crate dependency** (`garde` / `validator` / `gen_validator`) for post-decode invariants — arch §Inherited Defaults Validation row LOCKS "no validation library by default"; `serde` + smart enum types + `TryFrom<u16>`-style cover the surface. Documented upgrade trigger (cross-field plugin manifest validation) does NOT apply to OTLP invariants.

- (security) NEVER skip post-`prost`-decode invariant checks on OTLP payloads — `prost` only validates wire format; missing this is the §Anti-Patterns Input bullet 3 violation that chunk #18 exists to close.

- (security) NEVER log raw OTLP attribute values, span/log/metric content payloads, or DuckDB-bound parameters in invariant-rejection events — they may carry incidentally captured secrets from the instrumented host application (per §Anti-Patterns Logging bullets 1, 3).

- (security) NEVER serialize `anyhow::Error` directly across TauRPC; module-internal `thiserror` enums + the `From … for AppError` impl are the only authorized path to surface ingest invariant failures to the webview (per §Anti-Patterns Code Patterns bullet 4).

- (security) NEVER leak Rust struct names, file paths, or library versions into `AppError::Ingest { message }` — sanitize at the conversion site (per §Anti-Patterns Logging bullet 4 applied to `Ingest` variant by parity with `Internal`).

- (tests) NEVER skip post-`prost` OTLP invariant checks — span_id != 8 bytes, trace_id != 16 bytes, oversized attributes must be rejected with `AppError::Ingest`; negative tests MUST validate this at the request boundary (per test-plan §11 Project-specific row 3).

- (tests) NEVER mock the OTLP receiver / mpsc channel under test — always exercise the live receiver against loopback `:4317`/`:4318` and a real bounded `tokio::sync::mpsc::channel` (per test-plan §11 Mocking row 1, §11 Integration row 1).

- (tests) NEVER assert on raw OTLP protobuf bytes (`assert_eq!(response.encode(), expected_bytes)`); assert on decoded fields and on the `AppError::Ingest` variant + reason string for negative cases (per test-plan §11 Integration row 3).

- (tests) NEVER write retry/sleep-based synchronization for backpressure or invariant tests — wait on explicit signal (`health` poll, `subsystems.buffer.rows_ingested` increment, channel-event arrival) (per test-plan §11 E2E row 2 "NEVER use `sleep(N)` for synchronization").
- (tests) NEVER use `unwrap()` in tests on receiver/channel boundaries without context — use `expect("…")` so failure messages explain the broken invariant (per test-plan §11 Unit row 3).

- (obs) NEVER log full post-decode `prost`-deserialized attribute values, span body content, or trace_id raw bytes (Vector 1) — use `attributes_count` + `service_name_tag` enumerated tags; chaos test verifies secret payload absence in `agent-latest.jsonl` (per obs-plan §11 Project-specific + §1 Vector 1).

- (obs) NEVER emit per-message spans inside the mpsc `send` hot path — span overhead matters at 10k spans/sec; use heartbeat-tick aggregation (per obs-plan §11 Telemetry Strategy "NEVER over-instrument hot paths" + §5 Update frequency rows).

- (obs) NEVER hold a `tracing::Span` guard across an `.await` on the mpsc `send().await` or receive loop without `.in_current_span()` — span context bleeds into unrelated tokio tasks, breaks trace_id correlation, bloats memory until guard drops (per obs-plan §11 Spans/Traces row 4).
**Contract bindings:**

- **arch ↔ obs**: arch §Standard Contracts `ready` envelope `ingest_mpsc_capacity_pct` + `health` envelope `ingest_channel` subsystem are the introspection surfaces. obs domain owns the tracing fields / heartbeat ticks on the channel (`ingest.channel.tick`, `ingest.parse.error` events) — arch fixes the names of the introspection fields, obs fixes the event allowlist.

- **arch ↔ tests**: §Cross-cutting Patterns Test-time telemetry injection mandates synthetic OTLP via the running receiver (`:4317` / `:4318`), NOT a mock-channel back-door. Chunk #18 invariant tests therefore go through the real receiver path; no `#[cfg(test)]` test-mode bypass added to the channel sender. Tests inspect channel state via `health` / `ready` IPC.

- **arch ↔ security**: chunk #18's post-decode invariants implement security plan's "post-prost invariant checks at every boundary" Universal rule. `AppError::Ingest { message }` payload sanitization (no stack traces / internal paths / library versions) is the security plan's responsibility on the `message` String content; arch defines the variant shape.

- **arch ↔ ui-bridge (downstream chunks)**: `AppError::Ingest { message }` enum variant addition is a wire-stable contract bump for any TauRPC procedure that returns `Result<T, AppError>`. Chunk #18 introduces the variant; downstream consumers (viz query routers, snapshot generator) inherit the addition. Variant set is LOCKED — no rename / reorder permitted.

- **security ↔ tests**: post-decode invariant checks need negative-path coverage at the `crates/ingest` test surface — pathological payloads with `span_id` ≠ 8 bytes, `trace_id` ≠ 16 bytes, oversize attribute keys/values, oversize batch counts. Synthetic OTLP injected via the same `:4317`/`:4318` surface chunks #16/#17 already exercise. Tests assert `tonic::Status` / HTTP response shape AND that `AppError::Ingest` does not leak any §Anti-Patterns Logging-banned strings.

- **security ↔ obs**: invariant rejection emits structured `tracing` events with bounded fields per the existing `AllowList::production().ingest` registry; chunk #18 adds new field names (`op="invariant"`, `field`, `expected`, `actual`, `mpsc.capacity_pct`) to the allowlist + adds new `by_target` registry entries for `ingest.{grpc,http}.parse.error` (already pre-registered in chunk #17 handoff observability work). Redaction is applied at the subscriber layer; call sites pass bounded primitives only, not raw OTLP attributes.

- **security ↔ dependency hygiene**: any new `ingest` dep candidate must clear `cargo deny check bans licenses sources` and `cargo audit`; the `tonic 0.14 ↔ tonic 0.13` duplicate canary in `deny.toml` MUST stay outside any skip list (handoff Tier 2 Session Additions 2026-05-03 + §Anti-Patterns Universal bullet 2).

- **obs ↔ tests (binding hub)**: Test Harness Contract JSON schema (verbatim §3 + §6) is the binding for chunk #18 telemetry — invariant rejection tests will assert specific log line shape (`{timestamp, level: "ERROR", target: "ingest.grpc.parse.error", fields: {span_field_invalid, expected_length, actual_length}}`) by `jq` aggregation over `agent-latest.jsonl`. Heartbeat `ingest.tick` presence asserted by smoke harness via `health` IPC command. Both sides RECIPROCATE.

- **obs ↔ security (Vector 1+2)**: Vector 1 (no raw OTLP attribute values), Vector 2 (`AppError::Ingest` sanitized — strip `source()` chain + struct names + paths) bind directly — security defines the redact list, obs enforces it via `#[instrument(skip(req))]` at source + custom subscriber Layer at the formatter stage. Negative test (security-driven): inject OTLP span with secret in attribute value → grep log file for secret → must return empty. Both sides RECIPROCATE.

- **obs ↔ arch**: `health` IPC command Standard Contract envelope requires `subsystems.ingest_channel` slot — chunk #18 populates it via `record_ingest_channel_status` (parallel to existing `record_otlp_grpc_bind` / `record_otlp_http_bind` slots) so obs heartbeat fields and arch's IPC liveness probe share the same source-of-truth state. RECIPROCATES with arch ↔ obs above.

- **tests ↔ tests harness**: chunk #18 extends the existing harness — adds invariant negative tests + backpressure stress test + IPC contract test for `AppError::Ingest` serialization. No new 5-command surface; the existing `boot/run/status/cleanup/logs` discipline absorbs new tests via `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci`.
**Acceptance criteria contributions:**

- (arch) Channel sender + post-decode invariants + `IngestError` enum live in `crates/ingest/` per arch §Inherited Defaults workspace crate placement; no new crate added; no sibling-crate dependency introduced (`crates/ingest/Cargo.toml` MUST NOT have a `[dependencies]` line for `buffer`, `viz`, `snapshot`, `workspace-detector`, `plugins`, `mcp-server`, `ui-bridge`, or `pulse-app`).

- (arch) `AppError::Ingest { message }` variant exists on the `AppError` enum in `crates/ui-bridge/src/...` with `serde::Serialize` derive; `From<IngestError> for AppError` impl converts module-internal errors at the bridge crossing per arch §Conventions Error response schema (Tauri IPC) + §Established Decisions [Error Handling Pattern].

- (arch) Channel substrate is `tokio::sync::mpsc` (verified by `cargo tree -p ingest | grep -E '(crossbeam|flume)'` returning empty); no validation library added (`cargo tree -p ingest | grep -E '(^|\s)(garde|validator)\s' ` returning empty) per arch §Established Decisions [In-Process Channel Architecture] + [Validation Library].

- (arch) `health` envelope `subsystems.ingest_channel` field is populated by chunk #18 wiring (mirroring `otlp_grpc_receiver` / `otlp_http_receiver` pattern from chunks #16/#17); `ready` envelope `checks.ingest_mpsc_capacity_pct` field reports a numeric 0–100 derived from the live mpsc state per arch §Standard Contracts `health` + `ready` schemas.

- (security) Post-decode invariant test suite passes: payloads with `span_id` ≠ 8 bytes, `trace_id` ≠ 16 bytes, attribute key over bound, attribute value over bound, attribute count over bound — each rejected with the OTLP-spec error envelope; `cargo nextest run -p ingest` covers the negative paths.

- (security) Grep gate passes: invariant-rejection log events do NOT contain raw OTLP attribute values, span/log/metric content payloads, or DuckDB-bound query parameters — verified by structured-log fixture assertion in the test suite (per §Logging & Monitoring NEVER-log list).

- (security) `AppError::Ingest { message }` payload audit: bridge-conversion test asserts the surfaced message does NOT contain Rust struct names, file paths, library versions, internal hostnames, or raw user input — per §Error Handling TauRPC bullet + §Anti-Patterns Logging bullet 4.

- (security) `cargo deny check bans licenses sources` + `cargo audit` remain green after the chunk lands (no new banned crate, no new advisory, `tonic 0.14` duplicate canary undisturbed) — per §Dependency Security CI integration.

- (tests) `cargo nextest run -p ingest --profile ci` passes including new invariant negative tests (span_id length != 8 → rejected; trace_id length != 16 → rejected; attribute key/value over bound → rejected) for both gRPC `:4317` and HTTP `:4318` receivers.

- (tests) `cargo nextest run -p ui-bridge --profile ci` passes including a new test asserting `AppError::Ingest` variant serializes to a stable, sanitized JSON shape (variant tag + reason field; no stack trace, no file path, no Rust struct name).
- (tests) Coverage gate: `cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --lcov` reports new ingest channel + invariant code at ≥75% line / ≥70% branch / ≥85% function (per test-plan §10).

- (tests) Backpressure test under saturation passes deterministically (no flake; uses `tokio::time::pause()` or bounded channel inspection rather than wallclock sleeps); asserts (a) sender returns `AppError::Ingest`-equivalent on saturation, (b) no panic, (c) buffer eventually catches up after relief.

- (tests) Property-based test (`proptest` 1.10.0) for invariant boundaries runs with `proptest-regressions/` checked into the crate so any failing seed replays deterministically (per test-plan §7 randomized data row, §11 test-data row 3).

- (tests) Critical path P1 (test-plan §6) regression sanity: existing 100-span gRPC ingest E2E continues green after invariant gate + mpsc + `AppError::Ingest` lands (no regression in valid-payload path; `subsystems.buffer.rows_ingested >= 100` within 5s).

- (obs) `ingest.{grpc,http}.parse.error` event emitted at `error` level on every post-decode invariant violation (span_id ≠ 8 bytes / trace_id ≠ 16 bytes / attribute bounds exceeded) with required fields `span_field_invalid`, `expected_length`, `actual_length`, `rejection_reason` — verified by `jq '. | select(.target == "ingest.grpc.parse.error" or .target == "ingest.http.parse.error") | .fields' agent-latest.jsonl` after chaos test injects malformed OTLP.

- (obs) `AppError::Ingest` variant sanitization: no Rust struct names / file paths / library versions / `source()` chain text in any error log line — verified by `jq '.[] | select(.fields.error_kind == "Ingest") | .fields.message' agent-latest.jsonl | grep -E '(::|/[a-z]+/|0\.[0-9]+)'` returns empty (per obs-plan §1 Vector 2).

- (obs) `ingest.tick` heartbeat present at ≤30s intervals with required fields `span_count` / `buffer_capacity_pct` / `broadcast_subscribers` — verified by `jq '. | select(.target == "ingest.tick") | .timestamp' agent-latest.jsonl` shows max consecutive delta ≤ 45000ms (per obs-plan §10 CI gate "heartbeat-stall detection").
