data.head: # Phase 20 Plan — chunk route#23: "Broadcast fan-out + Tauri Channel API"

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase Phase 4. Read by /andromeda-implement.
Manual edits between runs are fine; do not edit during /implement run._
- **Phase number:** 20

- **Route chunks covered:**
  - route#23 "Broadcast fan-out + Tauri Channel API — tokio broadcast → pulse://stream/{spans,metrics,logs} binary Arrow IPC + _trace_context metadata + size cap"
- **Epoch:** Epoch 3 — Storage & query (this chunk closes Epoch 3; next chunk #24 opens Epoch 4 — Webview shell + TauRPC bridge)

Close Epoch 3 by adding the push-stream complement to chunk #22's pull-query routers: a single in-process `tokio::sync::broadcast` fan-out from buffer-side appender, encoded once into Arrow IPC stream bytes (with 8 MB hard size cap) and forwarded over Tauri 2's `Channel` API to webview consumers under the canonical `pulse://stream/{spans,metrics,logs}` event names. Per arch §Standard Contracts Real-time push contract + §Established Decisions In-Process Channel Architecture (mpsc ingest → DuckDB appender → broadcast fan-out to viz/MCP/snapshot subscribers), this chunk anchors the binary-Arrow-not-JSON contract that downstream Epoch 5 visualization surfaces (Halo State Pulse, full dashboard constellation, tray icon Halo) consume directly into WebGPU compute shaders without VDOM diffing tax.

The chunk introduces two new surfaces only — a `crates/buffer/src/broadcast.rs` module exposing 3 named Senders + Arrow IPC encoder + size-cap discipline, and a `pulse-app/src/streams.rs` composition layer holding 3 TauRPC procedures (`StreamsApi.subscribe_{spans|metrics|logs}`) each accepting a `tauri::ipc::Channel<Vec<u8>>` and spawning a forwarding task. Chunk-internal cycle-break per chunk #22 deviation: trait+impl pairs land in `pulse-app/src/streams.rs` (binary crate), keeping `crates/buffer` cycle-free. Existing `IngestState.broadcast_subscribers` AtomicU32 (added in chunk #18) becomes the live subscriber counter — populated each 15s heartbeat tick by summing `BroadcastSenders.{spans|metrics|logs}.receiver_count()`. Per security plan §Logging & Monitoring + obs-plan §11, broadcast-emission tracing logs `channel_name`, `arrow_schema`, `row_count`, `payload_size_bytes`, `schema_match`, `traceparent`, `duration_ms` only — never Arrow batch contents, OTLP attribute values, or row data.
1. Add `bytes` to workspace dependencies (verify `Cargo.toml` workspace-root `[workspace.dependencies]`; add `bytes = "1"` if not present from chunk #17 ingest http body limit).

2. Create `crates/buffer/src/broadcast.rs` with:
   - 3 string constants `STREAM_NAME_SPANS = "pulse://stream/spans"`, `STREAM_NAME_METRICS = "pulse://stream/metrics"`, `STREAM_NAME_LOGS = "pulse://stream/logs"` — these MUST appear verbatim per layouts + a11y grep gates.
   - `pub const MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES: usize = 8 * 1024 * 1024;` (8 MB; matches OTLP receiver `DefaultBodyLimit` per security plan §API Security Request size limit).
   - `pub const BROADCAST_CAPACITY: usize = 128;` (per-stream Sender ring buffer capacity).
   - `pub struct BroadcastSenders { pub spans: tokio::sync::broadcast::Sender<bytes::Bytes>, pub metrics: ..., pub logs: ... }`.
   - `pub fn create() -> BroadcastSenders` factory using `broadcast::channel(BROADCAST_CAPACITY).0` per stream (drop the initial Receiver — subscribers attach via `sender.subscribe()`).
   - `pub fn encode_spans(batch: &arrow::record_batch::RecordBatch) -> Result<bytes::Bytes, Error>` (and same for metrics/logs): serialize via `arrow::ipc::writer::StreamWriter::try_new(&mut buf, &batch.schema())?` + `writer.write(&batch)?` + `writer.finish()?`. After encode, check `if buf.len() > MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES` and return `Error::BroadcastSizeCapExceeded { payload_bytes: buf.len() }` BEFORE returning the bytes. On any `arrow::error::ArrowError`, map to `Error::BroadcastEncode { reason: "encode_failed" }` (sanitized — never include the Arrow library version / file path / library struct name).

3. Add 2 new variants to `crates/buffer/src/contract.rs::Error`:
   - `#[error("buffer broadcast encode failed: {reason}")] BroadcastEncode { reason: String }`
   - `#[error("buffer broadcast payload exceeded size cap: {payload_bytes} bytes")] BroadcastSizeCapExceeded { payload_bytes: usize }`

4. Update `crates/buffer/src/lib.rs` — `pub mod broadcast;` + re-export `broadcast::{BroadcastSenders, MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES, BROADCAST_CAPACITY, STREAM_NAME_SPANS, STREAM_NAME_METRICS, STREAM_NAME_LOGS, create, encode_spans, encode_metrics, encode_logs}`.
5. Update `crates/buffer/Cargo.toml` — add `bytes.workspace = true`.

6. Update `crates/buffer/src/consumer.rs::run_consumer` signature — add `broadcast_senders: Arc<BroadcastSenders>` as 4th parameter. After successful `dispatch_batch(...)` returns Ok, encode the corresponding batch type via `broadcast::encode_*` (clone `Arc<RecordBatch>` is unavailable since dispatch consumes the batch — need to either re-fetch from DuckDB OR pre-encode in dispatch; cleanest path: pre-encode inside `dispatch_batch` against the input `Batch::Spans/Metrics/Logs` proto data, returning `(rows_appended, encoded_bytes_per_kind)`). Match on encode result: `Ok(bytes)` → `senders.{spans|metrics|logs}.send(bytes).ok()` (returns `Ok(num_recv)` if any; `Err` only when zero subscribers — silently drop, not an error). `Err(BroadcastEncode | BroadcastSizeCapExceeded)` → `tracing::error!(target = "tauri.channel.emit.size_exceeded" or "tauri.channel.emit.error", channel_name = "pulse://stream/{kind}", payload_size_bytes, limit_bytes = MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES, error_type)` and continue (do not propagate; broadcast emission is best-effort).

7. Update `crates/ui-bridge/src/contract.rs::From<BufferError> for AppError` — extend match arms for `BroadcastEncode` → `AppError::Storage { message: "buffer broadcast encode failed" }`, `BroadcastSizeCapExceeded` → `AppError::Storage { message: "buffer broadcast payload exceeded size cap" }`. Add 2 sanitization tests asserting no leakage of `payload_bytes` numeric / Rust struct names / library versions in the wire-visible message.

8. Create `pulse-app/src/streams.rs` with:
   - 3 TauRPC trait+impl pairs `TracesStreamApi` (path = "streams" or "traces.streams"; choose `streams` namespace per arch §Conventions to consolidate), each containing one `subscribe(channel: tauri::ipc::Channel<Vec<u8>>) -> Result<(), AppError>` method.
   - Each impl `::new(broadcast_senders: Arc<BroadcastSenders>, ingest_state: Arc<IngestState>)`.
   - Resolver pattern: clone the relevant `broadcast::Sender`, call `.subscribe()` to get a `Receiver`. Spawn a tokio task with `#[tracing::instrument(skip(channel, receiver))]` target `tauri.channel.emit` that loops: `match receiver.recv().await { Ok(bytes) => { let payload = bytes.to_vec(); /* re-check size */ if payload.len() > MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES { tracing::error!(target = "tauri.channel.emit.size_exceeded", ...) } else { let _ = channel.send(payload); /* swallow Channel errors — webview disconnect is normal */ } }, Err(broadcast::error::RecvError::Lagged(n)) => tracing::warn!(target = "tauri.channel.lag", channel_name, dropped_count = n, ...), Err(broadcast::error::RecvError::Closed) => break }`. On task entry, `ingest_state.add_subscriber()` (or recompute via receiver_count later — see step 9). Return `Ok(())` immediately after spawn (subscribe is fire-and-forget per Tauri Channel API semantics).

9. Update `pulse-app/src/heartbeat.rs::spawn(...)` signature — add `broadcast_senders: Arc<BroadcastSenders>` parameter. Pass through to `run_ingest`. Inside `emit_ingest_tick(...)`: before calling `ingest::contract::heartbeat_payload(...)`, compute `total_subs = bs.spans.receiver_count() + bs.metrics.receiver_count() + bs.logs.receiver_count()` and call `ingest_state.set_broadcast_subscribers(total_subs as u32)`. Optionally emit one `metric.ingest.channel.broadcast_subscribers` event per stream with `channel_name` label.

10. Update `pulse-app/src/main.rs`:
    - After `viz_state` init: `let broadcast_senders = Arc::new(buffer::broadcast::create());`
    - In `run_consumer` spawn (line ~226): pass `Arc::clone(&broadcast_senders)` as 4th arg.
    - Construct `TracesStreamApiImpl::new(Arc::clone(&broadcast_senders), Arc::clone(&ingest_state))` (×3) and `.merge(...)` into the `taurpc::Router` in the Some-arm.
    - In `heartbeat::spawn(...)` call (line ~331): pass `Arc::clone(&broadcast_senders)` as final arg.

11. Update `pulse-app/src/observability.rs::AllowList::production()` — add 4 new entries with allowlisted fields per research.md "Files to modify" item (`tauri.channel.emit`, `tauri.channel.emit.size_exceeded`, `tauri.channel.emit.error`, `tauri.channel.lag`, `metric.ingest.channel.broadcast_subscribers`). Add 5 pass + 5 redact co-located tests following chunks #20/#21/#22 precedent (10 total).

12. Verify `pulse-app/Cargo.toml` and `pulse-app/src/main.rs` use cases compile cleanly with `tauri::ipc::Channel` from `tauri.workspace = true` (Tauri 2.11 includes the API; no new feature flag needed).

13. Run full test suite + supply-chain gates per Test Commands section. Verify cycle-break: `cargo tree -p buffer --depth 1 | grep -v "^buffer\b" | grep -v "(\*)"` — should show only sanctioned `ingest` sibling (existing) plus `bytes` (new external).

- `crates/buffer/src/broadcast.rs` — broadcast Senders trio + Arrow IPC encoders + 8 MB size cap + 3 stream-name constants. ~250 lines including 15-20 unit tests (encode round-trip per stream type, size-cap rejection, send-with-zero-subscribers no-op, 3-subscriber fan-out, lag detection on capacity overrun, STREAM_NAME constants match arch literals).

- `pulse-app/src/streams.rs` — 3 TauRPC trait+impl pairs for `subscribe_{spans|metrics|logs}` over `Channel<Vec<u8>>` with broadcast forwarding task. ~250 lines including 8-12 unit tests (subscribe spawns forwarding task, RecvError::Lagged emits structured event, size-cap re-check at emit site, ingest_state subscriber count tracking).
- `Cargo.toml` (workspace root) — add `bytes = "1"` to `[workspace.dependencies]` if not present.
- `crates/buffer/Cargo.toml` — add `bytes.workspace = true` to `[dependencies]`.
- `crates/buffer/src/contract.rs` — add 2 `Error` variants (`BroadcastEncode`, `BroadcastSizeCapExceeded`) + 2 display tests.
- `crates/buffer/src/lib.rs` — `pub mod broadcast;` + re-exports.
- `crates/buffer/src/consumer.rs` — extend `run_consumer` signature with `broadcast_senders` Arc param; fan out post-append; existing tests extended to drive 3 concurrent broadcast subscribers.
- `crates/ui-bridge/src/contract.rs` — extend `From<BufferError> for AppError` for the 2 new variants + 2 sanitization tests.
- `pulse-app/src/main.rs` — instantiate `BroadcastSenders`; thread Arc into `run_consumer`, `heartbeat::spawn`, and `StreamsApiImpl::new` × 3 procedures; merge 3 new TauRPC routers.

- `pulse-app/src/heartbeat.rs` — extend `spawn(...)` signature with `broadcast_senders`; populate `IngestState.broadcast_subscribers` on each tick from `Sender.receiver_count()` sum; +3 tests for new wiring.

- `pulse-app/src/observability.rs` — extend `AllowList::production()` with 5 new targets (`tauri.channel.emit`, `tauri.channel.emit.size_exceeded`, `tauri.channel.emit.error`, `tauri.channel.lag`, `metric.ingest.channel.broadcast_subscribers`); +10 co-located pass+redact tests.

- `pulse-app/capabilities/default.json` — Tauri 2 capabilities are router-level for TauRPC (per session-additions 2026-05-03); 3 new TauRPC procedures land via single invoke handler, no per-procedure permissions entry needed. Chunk #27 `xtask capability-drift` widening owns the drift surface.
- `crates/buffer/src/state.rs` — broadcast subscriber accounting lives in `IngestState` (chunk #18 precedent), not BufferState.
- `crates/ui-bridge/src/health.rs` — no new health enum variant needed; broadcast-emission errors flow through existing `From<BufferError>` and surface as `AppError::Storage` at the bridge.
- `crates/viz/*` — no viz crate changes (cycle-free property preserved per session-handoff Key Decisions chunk #22).
Per test-plan §3 5-command discipline + chunk-specific tests. Tests must pass for /implement to exit Phase 2 fix loop with success.

```bash

cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features --profile ci

# Format + lint gate
cargo fmt --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings

# Per-crate cycle-break verification (chunk #22 precedent)

# Self-observation negative gate (obs criterion #7 strict-grep — must remain empty)
cargo tree -p viz | grep opentelemetry

# Security grep gates (chunk #22 precedent extended)
grep -rnE "format!.*(CREATE|SELECT|INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE|WHERE|FROM|JOIN)" crates/buffer/src/
grep -rnE "(payload|value|service_name|span_name|attribute).*tracing::(info|debug|warn|error|trace)" crates/buffer/src/ pulse-app/src/streams.rs
grep -rn 'pulse://stream/' pulse-app/src/ crates/buffer/src/   # must return exactly the 3 canonical names per layouts + a11y gates
```

body: - (arch) `cargo tree -p buffer --depth 1` shows ZERO new sibling-crate deps after chunk #23 (existing `ingest` sanctioned edge preserved; only `bytes` external dep added) (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions arch row 7).

- (arch) Three event names emitted EXACTLY: `pulse://stream/spans`, `pulse://stream/metrics`, `pulse://stream/logs` — verified by `grep -rn 'pulse://stream/' pulse-app/src/ crates/buffer/src/` returning the three canonical names from `STREAM_NAME_*` constants in `crates/buffer/src/broadcast.rs` and the per-stream `tracing` instrumentation `channel_name` field; reject any rename to `pulse:stream/...` or `pulse://stream/span` (singular) (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions arch row 2 + layouts row 1 + a11y row 1).

- (arch) Payload format is binary Arrow IPC over Tauri 2 `Channel` API — verified by `grep -rn 'serde_json::to_string\|JSON.stringify' crates/buffer/src/broadcast.rs pulse-app/src/streams.rs` returning empty (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions arch row 3 + design row 1).

- (arch) Broadcast uses `tokio::sync::broadcast` only — verified by `grep -rn 'crossbeam\|sse\|websocket' crates/buffer/src/broadcast.rs pulse-app/src/streams.rs` returning empty (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions arch row 4).

- (arch + tests) `IngestState.broadcast_subscribers` field reflects live subscriber count (sum across 3 streams) — heartbeat-tick test asserts subscribing then dropping a Channel changes the value (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions arch row 5 + tests row 6).

- (arch) No new TauRPC procedure landed without router registration AND single-invoke-handler dispatch (capability JSON unchanged per arch default; chunk #27 owns drift-check widening) (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions arch row 6).

- (security) `grep -rnE "(payload|value|service_name|span_name|attribute).*tracing::(info|debug|warn|error|trace)" crates/buffer/src/ pulse-app/src/streams.rs` returns empty after chunk #23 (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions security row 1).

- (security) Outbound Arrow IPC payload size cap is enforced before `Channel::send` — runtime test asserts oversize batch (>8 MB) is rejected via `Error::BroadcastSizeCapExceeded`, surfaces as sanitized `AppError::Storage { message: "buffer broadcast payload exceeded size cap" }`, and emits `tauri.channel.emit.size_exceeded` event with `payload_size_bytes` + `limit_bytes = 8388608` (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions security row 2 + obs row 3).

- (security) `cargo deny check bans licenses sources` + `cargo audit` + `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` + `cargo fmt --check` all pass after chunk #23 (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions security row 4).

- (security) `cargo tree -p viz | grep opentelemetry` AND `cargo tree -p buffer | grep opentelemetry` continue to return empty (preserves obs criterion #7 self-observation discipline) (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions security row 5).

- (security) `From<BufferError> for AppError` extended for new `BroadcastEncode` and `BroadcastSizeCapExceeded` variants — sanitization tests assert no Rust struct name / numeric payload bytes leakage / file paths / library versions in wire-visible message (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions security row 6).

- (design + arch) Tauri Channel signature uses `Channel<Vec<u8>>` (binary path) — verified by inspection of `pulse-app/src/streams.rs` TauRPC procedure signatures (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions design row 1).

- (design) Stream namespace claimed by chunk #23 is exactly the three names — `pulse://stream/snapshot-progress` and `pulse://stream/plugin-events` NOT consumed (verified by grep) (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions design row 2).

- (design + layouts) Broadcast topology supports ≥3 simultaneous subscribers per stream without per-subscriber filtering — fan-out integration test asserts 3 subscribers each receive equivalent batch counts (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions design row 3 + layouts row 2).
- (tests) `cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features --profile ci` passes for all new tests (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions tests row 1).

- (tests) Coverage gate: line ≥75% / branch ≥70% / function ≥85% via `cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --all-features --lcov` for `crates/buffer/src/broadcast.rs` + `pulse-app/src/streams.rs` new code paths (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions tests row 2).

- (tests) E2E path P6 (test-plan §6 Scenario P6): subscribe to broadcast (via internal `Sender::subscribe()` direct in test, OR via Channel mock) → trigger ingest of 50 synthetic gRPC trace spans to `:4317` → await broadcast event within 5s timeout → decode Arrow IPC `StreamReader::try_new(bytes, None)` succeeds → assert `RecordBatch.num_rows() > 0` and required column-name set present (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions tests row 3).

- (tests) Cross-surface consistency: data observed on broadcast spans channel matches rows returned by TauRPC `traces.query` for the same time window (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions tests row 4).

- (tests) Negative test: oversized Arrow IPC payload (>8 MB cap) is rejected without panic; `Error::BroadcastSizeCapExceeded` raised; broadcast emit suppressed; `IngestState.broadcast_subscribers` count unchanged on rejection (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions tests row 5).

- (tests) Health contract: heartbeat-tick test asserts `IngestState.broadcast_subscribers` increments by 1 on subscribe and decrements by 1 on subscriber drop (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions tests row 6).
- (tests) Zero-flakiness: any new broadcast test that flakes once is quarantined with `#[ignore]` + open issue (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions tests row 7).

- (obs) `tauri.channel.emit` span emitted on every broadcast Channel send with `span.kind = "internal"`, `#[tracing::instrument(skip(channel, bytes))]`, fields `channel_name` (enumerated to 3 streams), `arrow_schema`, `row_count`, `payload_size_bytes`, `schema_match`; verifiable via `jq` on captured JSON lines (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions obs row 1).

- (obs) `metric.ingest.channel.broadcast_subscribers` gauge event in `ingest.tick` heartbeat (15s cadence) with `value` = current sum-of-receiver_counts + `channel_name` label enumerated (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions obs row 2).

- (obs) Arrow IPC payload 8 MB size-cap enforced — payloads exceeding cap emit `tauri.channel.emit.size_exceeded` event with sanitized fields (`payload_size_bytes` + `limit_bytes = 8388608` + `error_type`); negative test asserts event present + emit aborted (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions obs row 3).

- (obs) Trace context propagation: `_trace_context` Arrow metadata column carries opaque W3C `traceparent` string (no OTLP attribute values); verified via Arrow IPC decode + schema metadata inspection in integration test (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions obs row 4).

- (obs) PII scrubbing extended for new targets via 5 pass + 5 redact tests in `pulse-app/src/observability.rs`; raw row content / OTLP attribute values NEVER appear in JSON file (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions obs row 5).

- (obs) Heartbeat continuity: `ingest.tick` continues to fire every 15s ±5s through chunk #23 implementation — chunk MUST NOT regress the >45s gap-detection invariant (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions obs row 6).

- (a11y) Broadcast frame envelope distinguishes payload frames from broadcast-status events at the obs-event level — payload frames flow via `tauri.channel.emit` target with row_count>0; status events via `tauri.channel.lag` (with dropped_count) and `tauri.channel.emit.size_exceeded` (with payload_size_bytes); future P4 webview routes status frames to `aria-live="polite"` and payload frames to silent updates (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions a11y row 2).

- (a11y) 8 MB size-cap rejection emits a structured event (not silent drop, not panic) with rejection reason recoverable downstream — verifiable via integration test injecting >8 MB Arrow batch and asserting `tauri.channel.emit.size_exceeded` event present in JSON log (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions a11y row 3).

- (a11y) Broadcast cadence throttle knob: **DEFERRED to chunk #29** (Halo State Pulse implementation, where `useReducedMotion`-aware consumer-side throttle naturally lives); broadcast Sender capacity 128 provides natural backpressure at chunk #23 — Decisions Log entry added to `.andromeda/route.md` Section 3 documenting deferral OR plan.md self-documents the deferral here and route §3 untouched (per combined §Acceptance criteria contributions a11y row 4 + research.md Open Questions).

- (tests) Total test count grows from 288 (post-chunk-#22) to ~320-340 (chunk #23 adds ~30-50 tests across broadcast.rs + streams.rs + consumer.rs extensions + observability.rs AllowList tests + ui-bridge sanitization tests + heartbeat.rs wiring tests).
- (arch + tests) `cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features --profile ci` returns 0 (all tests pass after implementation).

Files inspected referenced in this plan:
- `crates/buffer/Cargo.toml` — referenced as deps source for `bytes` workspace addition
- `crates/buffer/src/contract.rs` — referenced as Error enum extension target (chunk #21 precedent for variant addition + display test)
- `crates/buffer/src/lib.rs` — referenced as module declaration target for `pub mod broadcast`
- `crates/buffer/src/consumer.rs` — referenced as `run_consumer` signature extension target + fan-out injection point post-`dispatch_batch`
- `crates/buffer/src/state.rs` — referenced as "Files to leave untouched"; broadcast subscriber accounting lives in IngestState
- `pulse-app/src/main.rs` — referenced as composition root for BroadcastSenders instantiation + Arc threading
- `pulse-app/src/heartbeat.rs` — referenced as `spawn(...)` signature extension target + `IngestState.set_broadcast_subscribers` per-tick wiring
- `pulse-app/src/viz_routers.rs` — referenced as TauRPC trait+impl cycle-break pattern source for `pulse-app/src/streams.rs`
- `pulse-app/src/observability.rs` — referenced as `AllowList::production()` extension target + 5+5 test pattern source
- `crates/ui-bridge/src/contract.rs` — referenced as `From<BufferError>` extension target + sanitization test pattern source
- `crates/ui-bridge/src/health.rs` — referenced as "Files to leave untouched"; no new health enum variant needed
- `pulse-app/capabilities/default.json` — referenced as "Files to leave untouched"; Tauri 2 capability is router-level not per-procedure

- **Cycle-break:** trait+impl pairs MUST land in `pulse-app/src/streams.rs` (binary crate composition layer), NOT in `crates/buffer/src/`. Buffer's `taurpc-runtime` feature does NOT exist (chunk #22 deviation rationale: cargo feature unification creates real cycle when buffer would depend on ui-bridge for AppError). Mirrors `pulse-app/src/viz_routers.rs` precedent.

- **Pre-encode in `dispatch_batch`:** to avoid re-fetching from DuckDB after append, encode the Arrow `RecordBatch` directly from the input `Batch::Spans/Metrics/Logs` before the DuckDB append call. The buffer's `appender.rs` already converts the input into RecordBatches for the DuckDB Arrow appender — chunk #23 reuses those RecordBatches for broadcast encoding. Coordinate the order: encode BEFORE append (so encoder sees the same batch DuckDB will store), but only emit to broadcast AFTER append succeeds (so subscribers see only durably-stored data).

- **`Arc<Vec<u8>>` vs `bytes::Bytes`:** `bytes::Bytes` is cheap-clonable (refcounted slab). Prefer `bytes::Bytes` over `Arc<Vec<u8>>` for the broadcast Sender payload type — broadcast clones across N subscribers, and `Bytes::clone` is just an Arc bump rather than full Vec clone.

- **`Channel<Vec<u8>>` conversion:** at the `streams.rs` Channel-send site, convert via `bytes.to_vec()` (cheap because Bytes-backed Vec is already in single-owner state by then). Or use Channel<bytes::Bytes> if Tauri 2 accepts — verify at impl time, default to Vec<u8> if uncertain.

- **Receiver count tracking:** `tokio::sync::broadcast::Sender::receiver_count()` returns `usize` (live subscriber count). Heartbeat tick polls + sums + writes to IngestState.broadcast_subscribers. NOT reactive — accuracy is bounded by 15s tick cadence, which is acceptable for a heartbeat-driven gauge.

- **No need to alter `crates/ingest/src/state.rs`:** chunk #18 already added `broadcast_subscribers: AtomicU32` + `set_broadcast_subscribers(n)`. Chunk #23 only POPULATES this field from the heartbeat tick context (not a code change to ingest crate).

- **a11y throttle knob deferral:** documented in Acceptance Criteria a11y row 4. NO Decisions Log entry added to `.andromeda/route.md` Section 3 at chunk #23 — the deferral is internal to plan.md provenance + chunk #29 phase research will pick up the obligation. /implement does NOT touch route.md.

title: Chunk route#24: "Tauri webview shell — WebView2/WKWebView, frameless + custom titlebar with drag region, close→minimize-to-tray policy"

data.head: ### Chunk route#24: "Tauri webview shell — WebView2/WKWebView, frameless + custom titlebar with drag region, close→minimize-to-tray policy"

body: **Constraints across domains:**

- (arch) Webview shell code MUST live in the `pulse-app` binary crate (NOT a library crate); the `pulse-app/` directory hosts `main.rs` / `lib.rs` / `tauri.conf.json` / `capabilities/` (per arch §Infrastructure Patterns Project directory structure + §Occupied Resources Cargo workspace crate names).

- (arch) Webview surface MUST use Tauri 2.x desktop shell with WebView2 (Windows) and WKWebView (macOS/Linux); native `wgpu` overlay surface rejected for v1 (per arch §Established Decisions [Platform] Tauri 2 desktop shell + [WebGPU Visualization Surface]).
- (arch) Bundle identifier MUST be `com.andromeda.pulse` and binary names `andromeda-pulse` (Linux/macOS) / `andromeda-pulse.exe` (Windows) (per arch §Occupied Resources Process / service identity).

- (arch) Main webview window MUST run under capability `pulse:default`; tray icon MUST gate on `pulse:tray`; Tauri core APIs (`fs`, `shell`, `dialog`, `http`) MUST NOT be granted to `pulse:default` without explicit per-feature capability addition (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns Webview IPC capability policy).

- (arch) Close-button behavior MUST minimize the window to tray, not terminate the process; Quit menu item or OS-level kill is the only termination path (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns Tray icon policy).

- (arch) Module dependency direction MUST flow toward `pulse-app` only — no library crate may depend on `pulse-app`; DAG with `pulse-app` as the only root (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns Module dependency direction).

- (arch) Cross-bridge data MUST be `serde::Serialize`; `AppError` enum is the only error shape across the bridge (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns Cross-bridge data shape + §Conventions Error response schema).

- (arch) No new env var, capability identifier, IPC procedure namespace, or filesystem location may be introduced beyond §Occupied Resources without `/andromeda-scope-arch` (per arch §Occupied Resources canonical reservation rule).

- (security) `tauri.conf.json` `app.security.csp` MUST contain canonical CSP literal — `default-src 'self' ipc: http://ipc.localhost; img-src 'self' data:; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; script-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' ipc: http://ipc.localhost; worker-src 'self' blob:`; `worker-src blob:` is load-bearing for chunk #28 WebGPU compute; `'unsafe-inline'` MUST NOT be added to `script-src` (per security plan §API Security row "CSP (webview content)").

- (security) Any `pulse-app/capabilities/` file added/modified for the new shell MUST NOT grant `fs`/`shell`/`dialog`/`http` core APIs without explicit per-feature capability + rationale (per security plan §API §Webview IPC capability policy + §Anti-Patterns API row 4).

- (security) close→minimize-to-tray transition is window-state-only (Tauri internal), NOT an inbound capability widening; `pulse:tray` MUST stay outbound-emit-only (per security plan §API row "Plugin host capability sandbox" + §Anti-Patterns API row 6).

- (security) Webview shell MUST NOT expose `pulse:updater` to webview JavaScript; updater interaction stays bound to `tauri-plugin-updater` flow (per security plan §API row "Updater capability isolation" + §Anti-Patterns API row 5).

- (security) Every TauRPC procedure invokable from the new window MUST exist as a capability JSON entry (router registration AND capability JSON dual-enforcement); xtask drift check enforces at chunk #27 (per security plan §API row "TauRPC capability authorization" + §Anti-Patterns API row 3).

- (security) Window/state errors crossing the TauRPC bridge MUST collapse to `serde`-friendly `AppError` variants; never serialize `anyhow::Error` directly (per security plan §Error Handling §TauRPC bridge + §Anti-Patterns Code Patterns row 4).

- (design) Custom titlebar MUST be 32px height with app icon (16px) + title text "andromeda-pulse" + settings button (aperture icon, 20px) + OS-appropriate window controls (Windows/Linux right-aligned; macOS traffic-light left-aligned); drag region spans titlebar background except buttons (per design plan §Surface: desktop-webview Component Patterns "Navigation / App Shell" titlebar bullet).

- (design) Window MUST be frameless via Tauri config `"decorations": false`; no browser-style navigation chrome (per design plan §Surface: desktop-webview Platform-Specific Notes Windows bullet + §Anti-Patterns Per-Surface Bans desktop-webview).

- (design) Page background MUST use `--color-base` (#1A1D24, Deep Control Gray); no shadows, gradients, or glassmorphic effects on chrome (per design plan §Color Palette Surface Scale Base + §Depth Strategy + §Anti-Patterns Universal Bans).

- (design) Window-control hover/active states MUST use motion tokens `--duration-fast` 150ms with `--easing-out` (cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)); no spring physics, no opacity fades >200ms, no entrance animation on window open (per design plan §Motion Duration scale + Hard limits).
- (design) All chrome motion MUST respect `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` (150ms hover → 0ms, 200ms fade → 0ms) (per design plan §Motion Accessibility).

- (design) Settings button MUST use `aperture` icon at 20px from icon registry (`<Icon glyph="aperture" />`); no Lucide/Heroicons fallback (per design plan §Iconography Primary custom set + Size grid 20px row).

- (design) Title "andromeda-pulse" MUST use IBM Plex Sans 500 weight at Label size (12px), 0 tracking; banned font fallbacks (Inter/Roboto/Arial/Helvetica/Open Sans/Lato/system-ui/Space Grotesk) (per design plan §Typography Label row + §Anti-Patterns Universal Bans).

- (design) Right-click context menu and text-selection on non-text elements MUST be hidden/disabled at the webview level (per design plan §Anti-Patterns Per-Surface Bans desktop-webview "NEVER ship with visible Chromium/WebView2 artifacts").
- (design) CSP for the webview MUST be `script-src 'self'` (no eval / remote scripts / CDN); WOFF2 fonts already bundled locally (per design plan §Surface: desktop-webview CSP policy).

- (layouts) Both webview surfaces (compact widget + full dashboard) MUST use a custom frameless titlebar at `height: space-lg`, `padding: 0 space-sm`, `gap: space-sm`, `background: color-base`, full-width drag region except button hit-targets — implemented via Tauri 2 `data-tauri-drag-region` attribute (per layout-templates.md §Component — Custom titlebar Layout).

**Anti-patterns to avoid:**

- (security) NEVER add `'unsafe-inline'` (or `'unsafe-eval'`) to `script-src` in CSP; `style-src 'unsafe-inline'` is conscious risk acceptance, further loosening of `script-src` requires nonce/hash mitigation (per security plan §API row "CSP (webview content)").

- (security) NEVER widen `pulse:tray` to accept input (notification action callbacks, tray menu IPC re-entry) — converts outbound surface into phishing/IPC-abuse vector (per security plan §Anti-Patterns API row 6).
- (security) NEVER expose `pulse:updater` or any `tauri-plugin-updater` invocation to webview JavaScript context (per security plan §Anti-Patterns API row 5).

- (design) NEVER use generic font families as primary in titlebar/chrome labels: Inter / Roboto / Arial / Helvetica / Open Sans / Lato / system-ui / Space Grotesk are banned; IBM Plex Sans is the locked sans choice (per design plan §Anti-Patterns Universal Bans).

- (design) NEVER ship OS-default decorations alongside custom titlebar — `decorations: false` is mandatory; mixing creates double-bar artifact (per design plan §Surface: desktop-webview Platform-Specific Notes Windows + Per-Surface Bans).

- (design) NEVER use `alert()` / `confirm()` / `prompt()` for close-confirmation or minimize-to-tray hint — styled modals only (deferred to chunk #33; chunk #24 must NOT introduce native browser dialogs as stopgap) (per design plan §Anti-Patterns Per-Surface Bans desktop-webview).
- (design) NEVER make window non-resizable; both compact widget + full dashboard are resizable (per design plan §Anti-Patterns Per-Surface Bans desktop-webview).

- (design) NEVER add entrance/scroll animations or shadows on window-open/focus-restore — chrome motion is state-confirming only, never decorative; entrance "none" (per design plan §Motion Hard limits + Duration scale).

- (layouts) Do NOT render OS-provided chrome (no `tauri.conf.json` with `decorations: true`) — frameless is mandatory (per layout-templates.md §Wireframe — Compact widget + §Component — Custom titlebar).
- (layouts) Do NOT make drag region cover button hit-targets — buttons must remain clickable (per layout-templates.md §Component — Custom titlebar Layout Drag region).

- (layouts) Do NOT terminate process on window close — close minimizes to tray; quit only via tray Quit / OS-level kill (per layout-templates.md §IA notes Navigation model + CLAUDE.md §Cross-cutting Patterns Tray icon policy).
- (layouts) Do NOT introduce hard CSS breakpoints for compact widget — fixed quarter-screen, no media-queries (per layout-templates.md §Decisions Log Responsive breakpoints).

- (tests) NEVER `sleep(N)` to wait for window appearance, drag-region attachment, or close→tray transition — wait for explicit IPC signal (`health` poll, `ready` poll, Channel event) (per test-plan §11 E2E).
- (tests) NEVER pixel-inspect WebGPU canvas / frameless chrome / custom titlebar / tray icon glyph in agent-driven tests — IPC contract assertion only (per test-plan §6 P1 step 7 + §11 Universal).
- (tests) NEVER assert via xpath / brittle CSS hashed-class-name selectors on shell DOM — use role/data-testid (per test-plan §11 E2E).
- (obs) NEVER link a browser OTel SDK into the webview — frontend telemetry MUST go through TauRPC bridge → backend `tracing` event (per obs-plan §11 Universal + §1 row 41 + §3 Tracing init).
- (obs) NEVER emit unstructured stderr text from window-state/tray boundary handlers — always JSON-per-line via `tracing::info!` (per obs-plan §11 Logs anti-pattern).

- (obs) NEVER use unbounded label cardinality for `webview_backend` / `wgpu_backend` / `tray_api` — enumerate to {WebView2, WKWebView, GTKWebKit} / {vulkan, metal, dx12} / {NotifyIcon, NSStatusItem, AppIndicator} (per obs-plan §5 + §11 Metrics anti-pattern).
- (obs) NEVER emit `app.boot.*` spans before `tracing-subscriber::registry().init()` completes — events silently dropped, masking gaps (per obs-plan §3 Tracing init order).
- (a11y) NEVER omit window-control button labels (icon-only `<button><svg/></button>` without `aria-label="Minimize"`) — SC 4.1.2 (per a11y plan §11 Screen Reader).
- (a11y) NEVER make drag region a focusable element (`tabindex="0"`) — phantom Tab stop with no operable behavior; SC 2.1.2 (per a11y plan §11 Keyboard + §1 Critical Paths P5).
- (a11y) NEVER trap focus inside titlebar/shell with no Escape — close→minimize handler MUST work from any focused descendant; SC 2.1.2 (per a11y plan §3 Critical Paths P5 + §11 Keyboard).

- (a11y) NEVER ship `outline: none` reset on focus styles without replacement — Tauri 2 webview default focus ring is engine-dependent (WebView2 vs WKWebView differ), shell MUST establish project-controlled `--border-focus` (per a11y plan §11 Visual + SC 2.4.7).

- (arch) DO NOT introduce a `wgpu`-native overlay surface or any non-Tauri native window for v1 (Tauri 2 native-overlay flickering issue #9220) (per arch §Established Decisions [WebGPU Visualization Surface]).
- (arch) DO NOT terminate the process on close-button click — close-to-tray invariant non-negotiable (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns Tray icon policy).

- (arch) DO NOT grant Tauri core APIs (`fs` / `shell` / `dialog` / `http`) to `pulse:default` without explicit per-feature capability + rationale (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns Webview IPC capability policy).
- (arch) DO NOT introduce new capability identifiers beyond the 5 reserved without `/andromeda-scope-arch` cycle (per arch §Occupied Resources).
- (arch) DO NOT make any library crate depend on `pulse-app` — DAG-root invariant (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns Module dependency direction).

data.head: # Phase 21 Plan — chunk route#24: "Tauri webview shell — WebView2/WKWebView, frameless + custom titlebar with drag region, close→minimize-to-tray policy"

body: _Generated by /andromeda-phase Phase 4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not edit during /implement run._
- **Phase number:** 21

- **Route chunks covered:**
  - route#24 "Tauri webview shell — WebView2/WKWebView, frameless + custom titlebar with drag region, close→minimize-to-tray policy"
- **Epoch:** Epoch 4 — Webview shell + TauRPC bridge

Stand up the desktop-webview surface that every later UI chunk inherits: render the frameless main window with a custom 32px titlebar (drag region + platform-conditional window controls + aperture settings glyph), wire close→minimize-to-tray window-state policy, and emit platform-tagged boot spans (`app.boot.webview.init` / `app.boot.gpu.check` / `app.boot.tray.init`) with enumerated backend labels per obs §1 multi-platform-exporter-compat trigger. The shell honors the canonical CSP literal already pinned in `tauri.conf.json` (`worker-src 'self' blob:` for chunk #28's WebGPU compute), keeps `pulse:default` capability as the negative-default trust boundary (no `fs`/`shell`/`dialog`/`http` core API grants), and binds AppError as the only error shape crossing TauRPC. Frontend is the first React 19 + Tailwind v4 surface to consume the design tokens scaffolded in chunk #10 + the `useReducedMotion` hook from chunk #15 — semantic `<header>` landmark hosts the titlebar, native `<button>` window controls carry `aria-label`s, and the drag region is `aria-hidden` non-focusable so Tab sequence skips it. The chunk does NOT scaffold the `telemetry.frontend.record_*` TauRPC bridge (deferred to chunk #28/#29 web-vitals/WebGPU frame-timing landing), does NOT create the actual tray icon glyph or menu (deferred to chunk #32), and does NOT expose `pulse:updater` to webview JS — close-to-tray is internal Tauri window-state handling and requires no inbound capability widening.

1. Update `pulse-app/tauri.conf.json` `compact-widget` window: flip `resizable: false` → `resizable: true` (per design constraint "compact widget is resizable" + per-surface ban on non-resizable windows). Keep `decorations: false` and `visible: false` on both windows; `main` stays `resizable: true`. Verify CSP literal stays unchanged (already matches security canonical).

2. Verify `pulse-app/capabilities/default.json` continues to declare both `compact-widget` + `main` with `permissions: ["core:default", "updater:default"]` — chunk #24 introduces NO new permission entries; `core:default` already permits the window-control APIs the webview hook will invoke (`window.minimize` / `.maximize` / `.hide`). If `tauri permission list` reveals these need explicit `core:window:allow-*` entries beyond `core:default`, add them with stated rationale per security plan §Anti-Patterns API row 4.
3. Verify `pulse-app/capabilities/tray.json` continues to declare both windows with `permissions: []` (outbound-only, populated at chunk #32).

4. Create `pulse-app/src/window.rs`:
   - `pub fn detect_webview_backend() -> &'static str` returning enumerated `"WebView2" | "WKWebView" | "GTKWebKit"` based on `cfg!(target_os = "windows" | "macos" | "linux")` + Tauri version compile-time fact.
   - `pub fn detect_tray_api() -> &'static str` returning `"NotifyIcon" | "NSStatusItem" | "AppIndicator"` analogously.
   - `pub fn detect_wgpu_backend() -> &'static str` returning `"dx12" | "metal" | "vulkan"` (compile-time per OS — actual runtime adapter check lands at chunk #28).
   - `pub fn emit_boot_spans()` invoked from main.rs after `observability::init` returns: emits `tracing::info!(target: "app.boot.webview.init", webview_backend = detect_webview_backend(), ...)`, `tracing::info!(target: "app.boot.gpu.check", gpu_available = false, wgpu_backend = detect_wgpu_backend(), ...)` (boot-time pre-render — `gpu_available` resolves at chunk #28), `tracing::info!(target: "app.boot.tray.init", tray_api = detect_tray_api(), ...)`. All three emit AFTER `tracing-subscriber::registry().init()` (already done in observability::init at line 171).
   - `pub fn handle_close_requested(window: &tauri::WebviewWindow, api: &tauri::CloseRequestedApi)` — calls `api.prevent_close()` + `window.hide()` and emits `tracing::info!(target: "ui.layout.transition", layout_mode_from = "main", layout_mode_to = "hidden", tray_visible = true, ...)`. Returns `Result<(), AppError>` collapsed to `AppError::Internal` on failure (no anyhow leak).
   - Co-located `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` covering `detect_*` enumerated outputs (assert exact-string match against allowed values; cargo-nextest per-process isolation per existing main.rs test discipline).

5. Modify `pulse-app/src/main.rs`:
   - Add `mod window;` next to existing `mod heartbeat; mod observability; mod streams; mod viz_routers;` declarations.
   - After `observability::init` and `record_start()`, call `window::emit_boot_spans()` (line ~173, before `write_pid_file`).
   - On the `tauri::Builder::default()` chain, insert `.on_window_event(|window, event| match event { tauri::WindowEvent::CloseRequested { api, .. } => { let _ = window::handle_close_requested(window, api); } _ => {} })` between `.invoke_handler(...)` and `.setup(...)`.
   - In the `setup` closure, after spawning consumer/retention/heartbeat tasks, call `app.get_webview_window("compact-widget")?.show()?` to make the compact-widget window visible (the `main` window stays hidden until user expands — kept `visible: false`). Wrap show() failure in a tracing warn rather than panicking (boot continues even if compact widget fails to surface).

6. Modify `pulse-app/src/observability.rs::AllowList::production()`:
   - Insert new entries (each is a separate registry key per chunk #20-23 precedent + session-additions 2026-05-05 dotted-target rule):
     - `"app.boot.webview.init"` → `["webview_backend"]`
     - `"app.boot.gpu.check"` → `["gpu_available", "wgpu_backend"]`
     - `"app.boot.tray.init"` → `["tray_api"]`
     - `"ui.layout.transition"` → `["layout_mode_from", "layout_mode_to", "tray_visible"]`
     - `"tray.visibility.toggle"` → `["tray_visible"]` (target registered now; first emission at chunk #32)
     - `"tray.menu.interaction"` → `["menu_item"]` (placeholder field; populated at chunk #32 with bounded enum)
     - `"tray.notification.dismiss"` → `["notification_id"]` (bounded — UUID-shape only)
     - `"tray.notification.action"` → `["notification_id", "action"]`
   - Add 5+5 co-located pass+redact tests (5 pass + 5 redact) covering the 5 chunk-#24-emitted targets (`app.boot.webview.init` / `app.boot.gpu.check` / `app.boot.tray.init` / `ui.layout.transition` + one tray.* placeholder). Mirror chunk #20-23 precedent — assert allowlisted fields pass through verbatim, non-allowlisted fields (e.g., `window_title = "user-app-name"`) are redacted to `<redacted>`.
7. Verify `pulse-app/ui/index.html` has `<html lang="en">` and `<title>andromeda-pulse</title>`. If absent or wrong, set them.

8. Replace `pulse-app/ui/src/App.tsx` stub with the shell composition:
   - Top-level `<>` containing `<Titlebar />` + `<main id="main-content" tabIndex={-1}>...</main>` + `<div role="status" aria-live="polite" id="shell-status" />`.
   - `useEffect(() => { document.title = "andromeda-pulse"; }, [])` for SC 2.4.2 Page Titled.
   - Listen for window minimize event (via Tauri 2 `getCurrentWindow().listen("tauri://blur" / "tauri://focus")` if needed) and announce "Minimized to tray" / "Window restored" via the status region. If listener wiring exceeds chunk scope, leave the announcer region empty for now and document for chunk #28.

9. Create `pulse-app/ui/src/components/Titlebar.tsx`: - Renders `
` (32px height via Tailwind utility composing `--spacing-lg` token; height = `space-lg` per layouts extract). - Inner flex layout: `[ + andromeda-pulse] + [grow] + [] + []`. - The `
` carries `data-tauri-drag-region` attribute (full bg drag region except button hitboxes — buttons ARE NOT inside the drag region). - Settings button uses `` from `pulse-app/ui/src/components/icons`. - Title text uses Tailwind classes consuming `--font-body` (IBM Plex Sans 500 12px). - Hover/focus styles: `:focus-visible` outline `--border-focus` (3px solid `#4A90E2`); transitions consume `--duration-fast` 150ms `--easing-out`. Wrap motion-sensitive transitions in `motion-reduce:duration-0 motion-reduce:transition-none` per a11y plan §6.

10. Create `pulse-app/ui/src/components/WindowControls.tsx`:
    - Detects platform via `usePlatform()` hook.
    - On macOS: returns `null` (OS provides traffic-light buttons left side; `decorations: false` does NOT remove these on macOS by default — verify behavior at /implement).
    - On Windows / Linux: returns three native `<button>` elements stacked horizontally — `aria-label="Minimize"` / `"Maximize"` / `"Close to tray"`. Each button ≥ 24×24 CSS px (use `--target-button-min` 44px). Hover bg uses `--color-raised-2`. Click handlers invoke `useWindowControls()` hook actions.

11. Create `pulse-app/ui/src/hooks/use-platform.ts`:
    - Returns `"macos" | "windows" | "linux"` based on `navigator.userAgent` substring match (Tauri webview always exposes this). Co-located test asserts each branch.

12. Create `pulse-app/ui/src/hooks/use-window-controls.ts`:
    - Wraps `@tauri-apps/api/window` `getCurrentWindow().minimize()` / `.toggleMaximize()` / `.close()`. The `.close()` action triggers Tauri's `WindowEvent::CloseRequested` which the Rust handler at step 4 intercepts to hide-instead-of-quit. Returns `{ minimize, maximize, close }` async functions.

13. Create co-located vitest tests (each `*.test.tsx` next to source per chunk #11 precedent):
    - `Titlebar.test.tsx` — DOM-shape assertions: `<header>` landmark present, `data-tauri-drag-region` attribute on container, exactly one `<button aria-label="Open settings">`, settings button contains an SVG (Aperture glyph), `<main id="main-content">` is sibling of titlebar (asserted in App.test.tsx).
    - `WindowControls.test.tsx` — given mocked `usePlatform` returning `"macos"`, returns null; given `"windows"`, renders three `<button>`s with `aria-label`s "Minimize" / "Maximize" / "Close to tray".
    - `use-platform.test.ts` — userAgent matrix asserts each branch.
    - `App.test.tsx` — composition: titlebar + main landmark + status region all present; `document.title === "andromeda-pulse"` after mount.
- `pulse-app/src/window.rs` — Rust window lifecycle + boot detection + close-to-tray handler. Implements arch §Cross-cutting Patterns Tray icon policy + obs §1 multi-platform-exporter-compat trigger.

- `pulse-app/ui/src/components/Titlebar.tsx` — Frameless custom titlebar React component. 32px height, drag region, segment order [app-icon | title | grow | settings | window-controls]. Implements design + layouts + a11y constraints.
- `pulse-app/ui/src/components/Titlebar.test.tsx` — Co-located vitest DOM-shape tests.

data.head: ### Chunk route#25: "TauRPC routers + TypeScript bindings — derive macros generate .d.ts per crate router, tsc --noEmit gate"

body: **Constraints across domains:**

- (arch) Workspace placement: bindings emitted from each crate's TauRPC router (routers live in `ui-bridge` / `viz` / `snapshot` / `plugins` / `mcp-server` / `workspace-detector`); generation invocation mounted in `pulse-app/`. No new crate, no rename of any reserved workspace name (per arch §Conventions + §Occupied Resources Cargo workspace crate names + §Project Intent Template patterns).

- (arch) TauRPC procedure naming MUST conform to the two authorized shapes — top-level bare `snake_case` for the cross-cutting envelope (`app_info`/`health`/`ready`/`get_settings`/`update_settings`); `<router>.<verb>` dotted for per-crate routers. Both segments `snake_case` (per arch §Conventions "Endpoint naming"). Generated `.d.ts` MUST preserve verbatim — no camelCase, no flat prefixing.

- (arch) Every type appearing in any `#[taurpc::procedure]` arg or return MUST be `serde::Serialize` (and `Deserialize` for inputs) — enforced by derive macros at compile time (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns "Cross-bridge data shape"). Chunk #25 generation depends on this constraint already being satisfied across existing routers.

- (arch) AppError serde envelope: every TauRPC procedure must already return `Result<T, AppError>` per arch §Conventions "Error response schema (Tauri IPC)" with stable variants. Chunk #25 generates bindings against this contract but does NOT introduce or modify AppError surface (chunk #26 owns the canonical AppError + From impls).

- (arch) `tsc --noEmit` is the Inherited-Defaults-locked typecheck gate for the webview side (per arch §Stack "Code quality (lint/typecheck)" + §Infrastructure Patterns Build system + §Inherited Defaults). Chunk #25 wires this command into local agent harness AND CI; webview TS sources consume only generated `.d.ts` (no manual TS re-declaration of command signatures).

- (arch) Generated bindings MUST cover the canonical procedure list in arch §Occupied Resources Tauri IPC routes (top-level `app_info`/`health`/`ready`/`get_settings`/`update_settings` plus `traces.*`/`metrics.*`/`logs.*`/`snapshot.*`/`plugins.*`/`workspace.*`/`mcp.*` when feature-gated). The `mcp.*` router is feature-gated `--features mcp-server`; generation must respect feature-gate hygiene (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns).

- (arch) Webview IPC capability policy: main webview window runs under `pulse:default`, which permits exactly the procedures enumerated in §Occupied Resources. The `streams.*` namespace from chunk #23 is NOT in §Occupied Resources (D3 drift carry-over per state.yaml.drift_warnings); chunk #25 surfaces this as a typed binding with no canonical-resources backing if it enumerates router namespaces. Defer remediation to chunk #27 (xtask capability-drift); flag in plan implementation notes only.

- (security) Every `#[taurpc::procedure]` argument struct MUST run through `serde` deserialization with smart enum types and `TryFrom<u16>` for ports (per security-plan §Input Validation row 3 TauRPC bridge boundary). No `&str` blobs that bypass per-field validation.

- (security) Every `#[taurpc::procedure]` MUST return `Result<T, AppError>` with `AppError` `serde`-friendly enum variants (per security-plan §Error Handling §TauRPC bridge bullet + Conventions Error response schema). Pre-existing routers (HealthApi #14, TracesApi/MetricsApi/LogsApi #22, StreamsApi #23) MUST already conform; chunk #25 MUST verify no new method returns `Result<T, anyhow::Error>` or `Result<T, String>`.

- (security) NEVER serialize `anyhow::Error` directly across the TauRPC bridge — must convert to `serde`-friendly `AppError` enum first (per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns §Code Patterns row 4). Derive macros enforce `Serialize` so this fails at compile time, but chunk MUST grep for `anyhow::Error.*Serialize` to confirm no manual impl exists.

- (security) Any new dependency added (e.g., `taurpc` typegen support, `typescript`/`tsc` install) MUST pass `cargo deny check bans licenses sources` and `cargo audit` (per security-plan §Dependency Security CI integration). `multiple-versions = "deny"` MAY require new skip-list entries with one-line provenance comments (per `.claude/rules/security.md` §Session Additions 2026-05-03) — do NOT relax `multiple-versions`.

- (security) `tsc --noEmit` gate sits in `ci.yml` matrix alongside `cargo audit` + `cargo deny` (per security-plan §Dependency Security CI integration). No new workflow file, no relaxed `permissions:` block.

- (security) TauRPC bindings emission target directory MUST be writable only inside the workspace (e.g., `pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/`); generated `.d.ts` files MUST NOT be written outside the workspace via path traversal — if `taurpc` accepts an output-path argument, that path MUST be canonicalized via `strict-path` + asserted under workspace root (per security-plan §Input Validation "Plugin host inputs" + §Code Patterns row 2 path-confine pattern).

- (tests) `tsc --noEmit` MUST be wired into CI Lint stage alongside `cargo clippy --workspace` + `cargo fmt --check` (per test-plan §9 CI Integration "Lint" row). Build failure conditions explicitly include "Lint / typecheck failure" (per test-plan §10 row 5) — typecheck failure MUST block pipeline at exit-code level identical to clippy `-D warnings`.

- (tests) TauRPC-generated `.d.ts` files MUST be EXCLUDED from coverage measurement per existing precedent: "Exclude generated code (`prost` protobuf stubs, `taurpc` IPC bindings), test fixtures, and mock implementations from coverage" (per test-plan §10 Cumulative across workspace). Chunk #25 formalizes this exclusion now that bindings actually exist.

- (tests) The webview unit-test framework `vitest` 3.x with `jsdom` 26 + `@testing-library/react` 16 (per test-plan §4) MUST consume the generated `.d.ts` types through the same TS resolution path that `tsc --noEmit` exercises — vitest emits JUnit XML to `target/junit-ui.xml`; binding-import failure must surface there, not be silently swallowed.

- (tests) `tauri::test::mock_builder()` + `get_ipc_response()` integration pattern (per test-plan §5 "Module ↔ TauRPC IPC" row) MUST remain the in-process Rust-side IPC contract verifier — chunk #25 adds the typed TS surface, but Rust contract tests assert procedure routing + AppError serialization regardless of TS bindings.

- (tests) Coverage gate ≥75% line / ≥70% branch / ≥85% function (per test-plan §10 Standard tier) applies to library-crate router code hosting the `#[taurpc::procedures]` derive — macro expansion is generated code (excluded), but hand-written router method bodies remain in-scope.

- (tests) Zero-flakiness budget (per test-plan §10) means `tsc --noEmit` gate MUST be deterministic — no transient typecheck failures from npm install timing, no `?` retries; if it flakes, quarantine + root-cause per the policy.

- (obs) Every TauRPC router method exposed via this chunk's bindings MUST be wrapped with `#[tracing::instrument(skip_all, fields(traceparent = %tp))]` where the IPC envelope optionally carries a `traceparent` field (per obs-plan §3 Trace context propagation IPC boundaries + §4 IPC-internal row).

- (obs) TauRPC router methods MUST emit boundary-call wrapper logs with `method_name`, `argument_digest` (hash, not content), `result_type`, `latency_ms` per obs-plan §6 "TauRPC invocation"; argument content NEVER logged verbatim (Vector 2 sanitization at IPC bridge).

- (obs) Service identity default subscriber fields (`service.name = "com.andromeda.pulse"`, `service.version = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")`, `deployment.environment = "production"`) MUST attach to every TauRPC handler emission via the existing `Layer::with_default_fields(...)` registered at boot (per obs-plan §3); chunk MUST NOT regress by hardcoding identity per-handler.

- (obs) NO OTel SDK auto-instrumentation crates may be linked transitively as a side-effect of TauRPC binding generation — self-observation runtime is `tracing` 0.1 + `tracing-subscriber` 0.3 + `tracing-appender` 0.2 + `tracing-error` 0.2 ONLY (per obs-plan §3 + §11 anti-pattern). Verify via `cargo tree -p pulse-app | grep opentelemetry` returning empty.

- (obs) Errors crossing the TauRPC bridge MUST sanitize per obs-plan §11 anti-pattern; binding-generation step MUST NOT emit `.d.ts` types that expose `anyhow::Error` / Rust struct names / file paths / library versions to the frontend. Chunk #26 implements `AppError` enum + `From` impls; chunk #25's job is to ensure generated bindings reference the eventual `AppError` shape, not internal `thiserror` variants.
**Patterns to follow:**

- (arch) Per-crate TauRPC router + `pulse-app/` mount pattern: each library crate exposes a router type via its public contract module; `pulse-app/src/main.rs` (or sibling module per chunk #23 `streams.rs` precedent) instantiates and merges them into a single TauRPC IPC handler. Binding generation runs over the merged surface (per arch §Project Intent + §Cross-cutting Patterns "Module dependency direction").

- (arch) Feature-gate hygiene for `mcp-server`: `mcp.*` router bindings only emitted when `--features mcp-server` is enabled at build/generate time; not in default-build `.d.ts` artifact (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns + §Conventions "Feature flags"). The double-gate (compile-time + runtime `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED=true`) is enforced at the rmcp boundary; chunk #25 only handles the compile-time gate at binding generation.

- (arch) TypeScript binding emission location under `pulse-app/ui/`: per arch §Infrastructure Patterns project directory tree, `pulse-app/ui/` is the webview source root; emitted `.d.ts` lives under that tree (precise path is implementation detail, not arch-locked).

- (arch) TauRPC IPC handler is a single integrated invoke handler: per `.claude/rules/security.md` §Session Additions 2026-05-03, `taurpc::create_ipc_handler(...)` dispatches all router methods at the channel level — chunk #25's binding generation runs over this same merged surface. Per-procedure capability JSON entries are NOT generated by TauRPC (only `core:default` + plugin-level perms appear in capabilities/JSON). Chunk #27 (xtask capability-drift) introspects at router-level granularity, not per-procedure.

- (arch) Module visibility discipline: each crate's TauRPC router type and procedure traits must be `pub` from the crate's contract module; internals `pub(crate)`; no `pub use` re-export across crate boundaries except in the explicit contract module (per arch §Conventions "Module visibility discipline").

- (security) Capability JSON pairing pattern: each TauRPC router crate that lands a derive macro entry MUST have its capability surfaced in `pulse-app/capabilities/` JSON; existing baseline `pulse:default` enumerates exactly the procedures from arch §Occupied Resources. For TauRPC the unit of capability JSON is the router (`core:default` + plugin-level perms), not per-procedure (per `.claude/rules/security.md` §Session Additions 2026-05-03).

- (security) `From<thiserror::Error> for AppError` conversion at the bridge: module-internal `thiserror` 2.x enums convert to `serde`-friendly `AppError` at the TauRPC procedure boundary via `From` impls (per security-plan §Error Handling §TauRPC bridge bullet). Existing routers already follow this pattern; new procedures emitted via derive MUST follow same `From` impl convention.

- (security) CSP unchanged from chunk #24 baseline: `tauri.conf.json` `app.security.csp` block remains the chunk #24 value. Chunk #25 wiring is in-process IPC (`ipc:` + `http://ipc.localhost`), no new origin/script-src additions required. Chunk MUST verify CSP is unchanged.

- (security) 40-char SHA pinning for any new GitHub Action introduced by typecheck CI step: if a new `setup-node` action or `npm` action is added to `ci.yml`, it MUST be pinned by 40-char commit SHA (per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns §Secrets row 3). NEVER `@v2` or floating tag.

- (tests) Co-located webview tests `*.test.tsx` adjacent to source under `pulse-app/ui/src/` discovered via `vitest.config.mjs include: ["src/**/*.{test,spec}.{ts,tsx}"]` (per test-plan §4 Conventions). Any new binding-import smoke test follows this layout.

- (tests) Builder/factory fixture pattern via `rstest` 0.26.1 `#[fixture]` decorators (per test-plan §4 + §7). Rust-side tests exercising typed TauRPC procedure signatures continue to use these factories rather than typing test arguments by hand.

- (tests) JUnit XML output discipline — Rust uses `cargo nextest --message-format junit --output-file target/nextest/junit.xml`; webview uses `vitest` emitting to `target/junit-ui.xml` (per test-plan §1). New typecheck step output should follow the same agent-parseable convention (exit code + structured stderr).

- (tests) Self-bootstrapping fixtures — no developer-seeded data; all fixture data generated at test runtime (per test-plan §2 + §7). Binding-consuming tests build mock IPC payloads via builders, never read pre-staged JSON.

- (tests) The 5-command harness `boot`/`run`/`status`/`cleanup`/`logs` (per test-plan §3) — chunk #25 does not add a 6th command; the new `tsc --noEmit` gate wires into the `run` body's pre-flight or into CI Lint stage, not into a separate harness command.

- (obs) Manual `#[tracing::instrument(skip_all, fields(traceparent = %tp))]` on each TauRPC router method (per obs-plan §4 surface-table IPC-internal row + §3) — existing precedent in HealthApi/TracesApi/MetricsApi/LogsApi/StreamsApi (chunks #22-23).

- (obs) `metric.*` target prefix convention for any frontend-telemetry-bridge events: `tracing::info!(target: "metric.{module}.{measure}", value = N, ...)` (per obs-plan §5 + §3). If frontend-bridge TauRPC commands (`telemetry.frontend.record_*`) are scaffolded, follow this pattern.

- (obs) Default subscriber field reuse: TauRPC binding-generation step does NOT need to bake `service.name` / `service.version` into the `.d.ts` — these are runtime tracing default fields, not bindings concerns. Bindings expose ONLY the procedure surface; identity is a tracing-layer concern.

- (obs) Boundary-call wrapper precedent from chunks #22-23: existing query routers (TracesApi/MetricsApi/LogsApi) and StreamsApi already follow `method_name + argument_digest + result_type + latency_ms` boundary-log shape; new bindings inherit this — no new instrumentation needed unless this chunk adds NEW router methods (chunk title suggests it does not).
**Anti-patterns to avoid:**

- (arch) Manual TypeScript re-declaration of any TauRPC command signature in webview sources — direct violation of arch §Conventions "Workspace API style" and §Established Decisions [Tauri IPC Bridge — Surface 2] rationale. Webview must consume only generated bindings.

- (arch) Inventing a new IPC procedure naming shape (e.g., `streams_subscribe_spans` flat snake_case, or `streamsSubscribeSpans` camelCase) — only the two authorized shapes from arch §Conventions "Endpoint naming" are permitted.

- (arch) Bypassing the TauRPC bridge by exposing stock `#[tauri::command]` handlers alongside TauRPC procedures — TauRPC was chosen explicitly over stock per arch §Established Decisions; mixing creates capability-policy ambiguity.
- (arch) Coupling chunk #25 binding generation to OTLP receiver wire shape, DuckDB schema, or any other §Standard-Contracts external surface — chunk #25 is internal-IPC only.

- (security) NEVER add a TauRPC procedure to a router crate without a matching entry in `pulse-app/capabilities/` (silent runtime rejection per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns §API row 3). Carry-over: chunk #23 `streams.*` namespace D3 drift is alive — if derive macro now emits `streams.subscribe_*` `.d.ts` types, chunk MUST flag (not fix; deferred to #27).

- (security) NEVER serialize `anyhow::Error` directly across the TauRPC bridge. Derive macros' `Serialize` trait bound makes this a compile-time failure; do NOT hand-impl `Serialize for anyhow::Error` to work around it.

- (security) NEVER let `AppError::Internal { message }` carry stack traces, file paths, library versions, or Rust struct names (per security-plan §Security Anti-Patterns §Logging row 4). If chunk #25 introduces a stub `AppError` ahead of #26, the stub MUST already sanitize.
- (security) NEVER reference any new third-party GitHub Action by `@v2` or floating tag — pin by 40-char commit SHA. Anchor: `tj-actions/changed-files` CVE-2025-30066, 23k repos.
- (tests) NEVER add retry-once policies for `tsc --noEmit` to mask transient failures (per test-plan §11 Quality). If TS resolution flakes, fix the resolver, do not `--retries 1`.
- (tests) NEVER lower the lint/typecheck gate threshold to ship the binding wiring — gate is binary pass/fail; if `tsc --noEmit` complains, fix the type or macro expansion.
- (tests) NEVER bypass the typecheck step locally and rely on CI to catch it — the `npm run typecheck` script exists at `pulse-app/ui/package.json:11`; CI runs it identically to local.
- (tests) NEVER include the generated `.d.ts` files in `cargo llvm-cov` coverage measurement (per test-plan §10 exclusion list). Including them inflates denominators and hides real coverage gaps.

- (obs) NEVER scaffold a `telemetry.frontend.*` TauRPC namespace as a side-effect of chunk #25 without explicit arch §Occupied Resources update or Decisions Log entry — precedent: D3 streams.* drift from chunk #23. Recommend KEEP `telemetry.frontend.*` DEFERRED to chunks #28-29 when web-vitals + WebGPU frame-timing have actual consumers.
- (obs) NEVER let TauRPC `.d.ts` emission introduce a build-time OTel SDK dependency (e.g., `opentelemetry-rust` macros pulled transitively by a TauRPC plugin) — would silently regress §11 invariant.

- (obs) NEVER emit a build-time `app.boot.bindings.check` or similar runtime span for `.d.ts` freshness verification — bindings are build-time artifacts, not runtime entities. The `tsc --noEmit` gate is a CI step, not an obs signal.
**Contract bindings:**

- **arch ↔ tests**: `tsc --noEmit` gate is a tests-domain CI step per arch §Stack "Code quality (lint/typecheck)" + §Infrastructure Patterns Build system; tests-domain owns gate's CI wiring + agent-harness invocation; arch fixes the command and the input.

- **arch ↔ security**: chunk #25 generates bindings against existing TauRPC router surface; security owns AppError sanitization (chunk #26) and §Cross-cutting Patterns Webview IPC capability policy enforcement (chunk #27). Chunk #25 must not introduce typed surface for procedures whose existence violates the policy — D3 streams.* drift is the active example.
- **arch ↔ obs**: TauRPC bindings type the procedures that emit/consume telemetry events; obs owns heartbeat/`{module}.tick` event format and self-observation discipline.

- **security ↔ tests**: `tsc --noEmit` gate is part of §Dependency Security CI integration cluster (lives in `ci.yml` alongside `cargo audit` + `cargo deny`). Tests owns runner mechanics + per-PR cadence; security owns SHA-pinning + `permissions: { contents: read }` workflow-level discipline.

- **security ↔ obs**: Capability-rejected IPC calls MUST log at the subscriber layer (per security-plan §Logging "What to log" row 1). Field redaction at subscriber layer MUST NOT log raw OTLP attribute values, query parameters, or snapshot/clipboard/MCP-tool-response bodies.

- **security ↔ arch**: Chunk #27 (`xtask capability-drift` check) is the enforcement substrate; chunk #25 derive-macro wiring is the *signal source*. Chunk MUST emit procedure metadata in a form chunk #27 can introspect, but per `.claude/rules/security.md` §Session Additions the granularity is router-level (TauRPC integrates at single-handler level) — chunk MUST document this so chunk #27 does not false-positive expecting per-procedure entries.

- **tests ↔ obs**: `tsc --noEmit` failure must emit a structured signal (non-zero exit + stderr line per file:line:col TS error format) the harness can grep — same agent-parseable contract as `tracing-subscriber` JSON log lines (per test-plan §3 + obs-plan §3).

- **tests ↔ arch**: TauRPC-generated `.d.ts` are the typed surface for arch §Standard Contracts (`app_info`/`health`/`ready` envelope + `<router>.<verb>` dotted procedures). Integration test rows assert the Rust side; `tsc --noEmit` asserts the TS side stays in lockstep with Rust router signatures.

- **tests ↔ security**: Capability-drift coverage from chunk #27 consumes the same router introspection surface chunk #25 wires; `tsc --noEmit` is the proximate canary that catches a router signature change before the capability drift check runs. Tests-domain responsibility: verify both gates fail-closed when wired to a stale binding fixture.

- **tests ↔ harness 5-command discipline**: `run` command in test-plan §3 currently invokes `cargo nextest run --workspace --message-format libtest-json --profile ci`. After chunk #25, same `run` invocation in CI must be preceded (or composed) with the webview typecheck step, OR CI Lint stage must encompass both — harness contract at §3 stays unchanged for product-side test invocation; new gate lives in CI Lint per §9.

- **obs ↔ tests**: Test Harness Contract JSON schema (obs-plan §3 + tests excerpt §5) governs structured log shape that TauRPC handler boundary-call logs MUST emit. Tests harness asserts log shape via post-test `jq` aggregation; chunk #25 bindings inherit this via existing `#[tracing::instrument]` (no new contract surface).

- **obs ↔ security**: PII scrubbing at TauRPC bridge — `#[tracing::instrument(skip(...))]` MUST exclude raw IPC argument content from spans (per obs-plan §8 Vector 2 + security plan §logging vector 2). `argument_digest` field replaces verbatim content. Generated `.d.ts` types MUST NOT expose internal Rust struct names / file paths to the frontend.

- **obs ↔ arch (Occupied Resources)**: Any new TauRPC namespace introduced by binding generation requires concurrent arch §Occupied Resources update or §Decisions Log entry — D3 streams.* drift precedent (1 wrap age) is the cautionary tale. Plan EXPLICITLY enumerates "no new TauRPC namespaces; bindings only for HealthApi / TracesApi / MetricsApi / LogsApi / StreamsApi" to avoid a second drift entry.

- **obs ↔ a11y / design**: Frontend telemetry bridge (`telemetry.frontend.record_*`) is the eventual route for web-vitals + WebGPU frame timing — DEFERRED out of chunk #25; lands at chunks #28-29 when consumers exist.

- **(D3 carry-over) security ↔ arch ↔ obs**: D3 drift `streams.*` namespace (introduced chunk #23, age 1 wrap) surfaces in chunk #25 as the derive macros now make the typed surface visible in `.d.ts`. Defer remediation to chunk #27 (option a — natural carry; not yet stale per >3-wrap escalation threshold). Chunk #25 MUST NOT proactively fix arch §Occupied Resources or capability JSON; MUST flag in plan implementation notes.
**Acceptance criteria contributions:**

- (arch) TauRPC-generated `.d.ts` artifact emits per-router types covering canonical procedure surface in §Occupied Resources (top-level envelope + `traces.*`/`metrics.*`/`logs.*`/`snapshot.*`/`plugins.*`/`workspace.*` and `mcp.*` when feature-gated); naming preserves the two authorized shapes per arch §Conventions "Endpoint naming". Verifiable: inspect emitted `.d.ts` against §Occupied Resources list.
- (arch) `tsc --noEmit` runs cleanly against webview TS sources consuming only generated `.d.ts` (no manual TS re-declaration). Verifiable: `tsc --noEmit` exit code 0.

- (arch) No new crate, no rename of any reserved workspace name; no new TauRPC procedure introduced beyond existing surface. Verifiable: `git diff --name-only` against `crates/` shows no new top-level subdir; `cargo metadata --no-deps` member list unchanged.
- (arch) Webview frontend imports only TauRPC-generated `.d.ts` for IPC types. Verifiable: grep webview sources for manual `interface`/`type` declarations of any §Occupied Resources procedure name.

- (security) `cargo deny check bans licenses sources` passes with no banned crates added; skip-list additions if any include one-line provenance comments per `.claude/rules/security.md` §Session Additions.

title: Phase 22 Plan — chunk route#25: "TauRPC routers + TypeScript bindings — derive macros generate .d.ts per crate router, tsc --noEmit gate"

data.head: # Phase 22 Plan — chunk route#25: "TauRPC routers + TypeScript bindings — derive macros generate .d.ts per crate router, tsc --noEmit gate"

body: _Generated by /andromeda-phase Phase 4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not edit during /implement run._
- **Phase number:** 22

- **Route chunks covered:**
  - route#25 "TauRPC routers + TypeScript bindings — derive macros generate .d.ts per crate router, tsc --noEmit gate"
- **Epoch:** Epoch 4 — Webview shell + TauRPC bridge

Wire `taurpc` 0.7 + `specta` 2.0.0-rc.22 to auto-generate TypeScript bindings for the existing five TauRPC routers (`HealthApi` from chunk #14 in `crates/ui-bridge/src/health.rs`; `TracesApi`/`MetricsApi`/`LogsApi` from chunk #22 in `pulse-app/src/viz_routers.rs`; `StreamsApi` from chunk #23 in `pulse-app/src/streams.rs`), and land the `tsc --noEmit` typecheck gate that arch §Stack + §Inherited Defaults declares as the locked webview-side typecheck. Per arch §Established Decisions [Tauri IPC Bridge — Surface 2] the rationale is drift elimination: the webview frontend will import generated `.d.ts` rather than re-declaring command signatures, eliminating the manual TS↔Rust synchronization tax across the 8-module monolith. The `tsc --noEmit` gate runs against the merged source-tree (existing `pulse-app/ui/src/**/*` + newly emitted `pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/**/*`) and joins CI's existing Lint stage alongside `cargo fmt --check` + `cargo clippy ... -D warnings` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` `lint-test-build` job (per security-plan §Dependency Security CI integration + test-plan §9 Lint row).

The chunk introduces NO new TauRPC procedures, NO new capability JSON entries, NO new runtime spans (binding generation is build-time per obs extract Anti-pattern), NO modifications to `AppError` (chunk #26 territory), NO modifications to `tauri.conf.json` `app.security.csp`, and NO drift remediation for the carried-over D3 `streams.*` namespace (chunk #27 territory per the route#23 wrap recommendation; chunk #25 surfaces the typed `streams.subscribe_*` bindings while flagging the absence in arch §Occupied Resources). Specta `derive(specta::Type)` is already wired across all router types (chunk #14 conditional `cfg_attr` for `AppError`/`HealthEnvelope` + chunk #22/#23 unconditional for `viz` query types) — this chunk consumes that wiring at the binding-emission step rather than extending it.

The implementation has one upstream probe (taurpc 0.7's actual `.ts` emission mechanism — macro arg `export_to = "..."` vs build script vs runtime dev-mode bake) + four downstream wiring concerns (binding directory + tsc gate + xtask wrapper + CI step). Plan synthesis defers the probe to /implement Step 1 because taurpc-version-specific API surface is below the abstraction threshold of phase planning.
1. Read taurpc 0.7 README + `Cargo.toml` macro feature flags via `cargo doc --open -p taurpc` (or read `~/.cargo/registry/src/.../taurpc-0.7.*/README.md`).

2. Confirm exact emission API. Likely candidates (in priority order):
   - **(a) Macro arg**: `#[taurpc::procedures(path = "streams", export_to = "../ui/src/bindings/streams.ts")]` — emission at compile time per call-site, output path relative to the source file. Most idiomatic for taurpc; matches the per-router-file pattern already established.
   - **(b) Build script**: `pulse-app/build.rs` invoking `taurpc::ts::export_to(...)` or similar; runs at `cargo build` time.
   - **(c) Runtime dev-mode bake**: `taurpc::Router::new()...export_to(...).build()` in main.rs `setup` closure, gated by `cfg!(debug_assertions)` or `--features ts-export`.

3. Pick (a) if available — minimal blast radius (modifies the 5 declaration sites only). Fall back to (b) if (a) is unsupported in 0.7. Reject (c) for production builds (binding emission MUST not depend on runtime execution; CI must be able to regenerate bindings without booting the app).

4. Document the chosen mechanism + path semantics (relative-to-source-file vs relative-to-Cargo.toml vs absolute-from-workspace-root) in a session-learning candidate for `/wrap-session` curation if non-obvious.
