data.head: ### Chunk route#26: "AppError serde enum + From impls — Validation/NotFound/Internal/Plugin/Storage/Ingest with sanitization (no stack traces / paths)"

body: **Constraints across domains:**

- (security) The TauRPC bridge MUST emit only the six stable `AppError` variants (`Validation { field, reason }` / `NotFound { resource }` / `Internal { message }` / `Plugin { plugin_id, message }` / `Storage { message }` / `Ingest { message }`); module-internal `thiserror` 2.x enums convert via `From` impls AT the bridge boundary, not at the call site (per security plan §Error Handling TauRPC bridge bullet + Conventions Error response schema (Tauri IPC)).

- (security) `AppError::Internal { message }` MUST carry a sanitized one-liner — no stack traces, no file paths (absolute or relative), no Rust struct names, no library/crate version strings, no internal hostnames or IPs (per security plan §Error Handling External-responses preamble + §Anti-Patterns Logging line "NEVER expose stack traces, Rust struct names, file paths, or library versions in `AppError::Internal { message }`").

- (security) The full pre-sanitization error chain MUST stay accessible inside `tracing-error` SpanTrace / internal log via the structured logger — sanitization only applies to the surface that crosses the bridge, not to the `tracing` event emitted internally (per security plan §Error Handling Internal-logging bullet + project rules `security.md` §Error sanitization).

- (security) DuckDB query parameter values MUST NOT appear in any `AppError::Storage { message }` string — error mappers from `viz`/`buffer` errors include only `query_id` + `param_count` (or equivalent placeholder), never echoed user-controlled telemetry data (per security plan §Logging "NEVER log DuckDB query parameter values" + project rules `security.md` §Logging "use `query_id` + `param_count` + `param_types` instead").

- (security) Plugin path strings MUST NOT appear verbatim in `AppError::Plugin { plugin_id, message }` — only the canonicalized basename or a stable plugin identifier is acceptable (per security plan §Logging "NEVER log full plugin file paths" + §Anti-Patterns Logging line 409).

- (security) OTLP attribute values, snapshot file contents, clipboard contents, and MCP tool response bodies MUST NEVER appear in any `AppError` variant payload (per security plan §Logging NEVER-log list + project CLAUDE.md "Critical Warnings" universal invariant).

- (security) OTLP-receiver and MCP error surfaces are OUT of scope for `AppError` — OTLP errors collapse to `tonic::Status` codes / OTLP `Status` proto in body, MCP errors use JSON-RPC 2.0 error objects (per security plan §Error Handling sub-bullets for OTLP receiver + MCP server).

- (arch) AppError MUST carry exactly six stable variants (`Validation { field, reason }`, `NotFound { resource }`, `Internal { message }`, `Plugin { plugin_id, message }`, `Storage { message }`, `Ingest { message }`) and remain serde-friendly across the TauRPC bridge (per architecture §Conventions Error response schema (Tauri IPC) + §Established Decisions [Error Handling Pattern]).

- (arch) AppError lives in `crates/ui-bridge/` only — no other library crate may declare or re-export AppError; module-internal code uses crate-local `thiserror`-derived enums and converts at the bridge via `From` impls (per architecture §Inherited Defaults Error handling row + §Cross-cutting Patterns Module dependency direction).

- (arch) Module-internal errors MUST stay `thiserror` 2.x; `anyhow::Result` MUST stay confined to `pulse-app/src/main.rs` and non-IPC top-level code; `anyhow::Error` MUST NEVER cross the TauRPC bridge (per architecture §Stack and Technologies Error handling row + §Conventions Error response schema (Tauri IPC)).

- (arch) Every type that crosses the TauRPC bridge — including AppError and its variants — MUST be `serde::Serialize`; new From-impl source types and embedded fields (`field` / `reason` / `message` / `plugin_id` / `resource`) MUST stay String-shaped and Serialize-clean (per architecture §Cross-cutting Patterns Cross-bridge data shape).

- (arch) AppError variant names + `#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "snake_case")]` discriminator wire shape are LOCKED — chunk #26 may add From impls but MUST NOT rename, add, remove, or reorder variants without an arch amendment, because the TypeScript bindings emitted in chunk #25 already mirror the wire shape (per architecture §Conventions Error response schema (Tauri IPC) inventory + §Established Decisions [TauRPC]).

- (arch) Internal-source enums emitting `From<E> for AppError` MUST live inside their own crate's contract module; AppError's From impls MUST import via the crate's public contract path (e.g., `ingest::contract::Error`, `buffer::Error`, `viz::Error`) and NEVER reach into a sibling crate's `pub(crate)` internals (per architecture §Conventions Module visibility discipline + §Project Intent Template patterns).

- (tests) Every `AppError` variant MUST round-trip through `serde_json` deterministically — unit tests assert each of the 6 stable variants serializes к stable JSON shape that the TauRPC bridge contract envelope expects (per test-plan §1 ui-bridge testable row + §11 "agent-driven, schema-stable contracts").

- (tests) Sanitization invariant tests REQUIRED on every `From<E> for AppError` impl that lands in this chunk — assert resulting `AppError` strings contain NO file path (`/`, `\`, `crates/`, `pulse-app/`), NO Rust struct name (`thiserror::Error`, `tonic::Status`, `duckdb::Error`), NO library version, NO stack trace fragment (per test-plan §11 Universal "NEVER expose secrets in test output" + §11 Project-specific anti-pattern echo + security plan §Error sanitization).

- (tests) Negative tests MUST cover sanitization: feed each upstream error a synthetic message containing path-shaped (`/etc/passwd`), struct-shaped (`Custom { … }`), and version-shaped (`opentelemetry-otlp 0.31.0`) substrings, assert `From` impl strips them before they reach the boundary (per test-plan §1 coverage trigger row "AppError sanitization" + §11 anti-pattern).
- (tests) Co-located `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { … }` inside `crates/ui-bridge/src/contract.rs` (or a sibling `error.rs` if extracted) — no `tests/` directory, per test-plan §4 Conventions.

- (tests) Test functions MUST follow `#[test] fn test_<entity>_<scenario>()` naming; tests MUST use `expect("reason why this must succeed")` — never bare `unwrap()` (per test-plan §4 + §11 Unit anti-patterns).

- (tests) Coverage gate: ui-bridge crate's new error code paths MUST contribute ≥75% line / ≥70% branch / ≥85% function (per test-plan §10 Standard tier thresholds). AppError + From impls are NOT excluded from coverage.

- (obs) `AppError::Internal { message }` carried across the bridge MUST be a sanitized one-liner — strip Rust struct names, library versions, kernel/stdlib file paths, and source() chains; the full chain stays in the local `tracing-error` SpanTrace via the user-defined-span path only (per obs-plan §7 Error Capture & Reporting / §8 PII row "AppError enum variants").

- (obs) Every `From<{Module}Error> for AppError` impl MUST emit a `tracing::warn!` or `tracing::error!` at the conversion boundary BEFORE returning the lossy variant — the conversion site is the only place where the rich source-chain still exists (per obs-plan §10 "Module-boundary error logging").

- (obs) The `From` impl MUST NOT serialize raw upstream error fields verbatim into the `message` string — fields like full plugin paths (Vector 3 basename-only), DuckDB query parameters (Vector 5 query_id+param_count only), MCP response bodies (Vector 4 result_type+result_count only), and raw OTLP attribute values (Vector 1) collapse to category strings (per obs-plan §5 logging-sensitive triggers Vector 1-6).

- (obs) Errors emitted within an active `tracing` span automatically inherit `trace_id` / `span_id` from the surrounding `#[tracing::instrument]` context — `From` impls MUST emit via `tracing::error!`/`warn!` macros NOT via raw `eprintln!` or unspanned writers (per obs-plan §7 "Error → span correlation").

- (obs) The whitelist for `ui-bridge` module fields per the default-deny posture is `method_name`, `argument_digest` (hash), `result_type`, `latency_ms` — `AppError` boundary logs MUST stay within this allowlist (per obs-plan §8 "Default-deny posture — whitelist per module — ui-bridge").

- (obs) `AppError::Validation { field, reason }` `field` MUST be a stable enum-like identifier (`"port"`, `"retention_seconds"`, `"plugin_id"`), NEVER include the rejected user value (per obs-plan §8 Vector 1 + Vector 2 row).

- (a11y) AppError variant message strings (`reason`, `message`) MUST be authored in plain language with simple terminology — no technical jargon, no Rust struct names, no library version strings, no file paths (per a11y-plan §11 Forms & Validation phase-1 baseline disciplines + WCAG SC 3.3.3 Error Suggestion baseline).

- (a11y) `AppError::Validation { field, reason }` MUST shape `field` as a stable machine identifier (downstream UI binds it to `aria-describedby` on the offending input per a11y-plan §10 Forms & Validation pattern + SC 3.3.1 Error Identification, SC 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions). A single bag-of-text `reason` field that conflates field name and error message breaks the SC 3.3.1 pattern downstream.

- (a11y) The serialized AppError JSON shape MUST be discriminated-union compatible with TypeScript bindings (chunk #25 emitted `AppError` as 6-variant union in `pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts`) so downstream UI can pattern-match per variant and render context-appropriate aria-live region polarity (per a11y-plan §11 Status Messages region-type table).

- (a11y) AppError sanitization MUST NOT strip the `field` identifier from `Validation` or the `plugin_id` from `Plugin` — those structured handles are how downstream UI wires aria-describedby + aria-labelledby relationships (per a11y-plan §10).
**Patterns к follow:**

- (security) Boundary conversion via `From<ModuleError> for AppError` impls — already established for `From<IngestError>` / `From<BufferError>` / `From<VizError>`; this chunk extends the matrix to whichever sibling crates need it (per security plan §Error Handling TauRPC bridge bullet + project rules `security.md` §Error sanitization).

- (security) Sanitization happens AT the `From` impl, not at the procedure handler — extract message-shape transformation into the `From<thiserror::Error>` body so every code path that returns the underlying error gets sanitized identically (per security plan §Anti-Patterns Logging line 411).

- (security) `AppError::Validation { field, reason }` is the canonical rejection variant for `serde` deserialize failures + `TryFrom<u16>` failures + smart-enum out-of-range failures on TauRPC procedure args (per security plan §Input Validation TauRPC bridge row).

- (security) Module-internal code keeps using `thiserror` 2.x enums (no boundary leakage); `anyhow::Result` is permitted only inside `main.rs` and non-IPC top-level (per security plan §Anti-Patterns Code-Patterns line 419).

- (arch) Existing `From<IngestError>`, `From<BufferError>`, `From<VizError>` in `crates/ui-bridge/src/contract.rs` already collapse internal variants to constant sanitized one-liners discarding the source `reason: String`; chunk #26 From-impl additions MUST follow the same constant-string collapse pattern rather than `format!`-ing source error fields into the wire message (per architecture §Conventions Error response schema (Tauri IPC) sanitization commitment).

- (arch) Variant routing taxonomy is precedent-set: `IngestError::*` → `AppError::Ingest`; `BufferError::*` → `AppError::Storage`; `VizError::QueryFailed/ConnectionLost/Decode` → `AppError::Storage` while `VizError::InvalidArgument { field }` → `AppError::Validation { field, reason: "invalid query argument" }`. Future from-impl additions MUST route by domain category (storage queries → Storage; user-supplied parameter rejection → Validation; missing resource → NotFound; plugin-host telemetry → Plugin; cross-cutting → Internal) (per architecture §Conventions Error response schema (Tauri IPC) variant inventory + §Established Decisions [Error Handling Pattern]).

- (arch) Helper constructor `AppError::internal(message: impl Into<String>)` already exists in `crates/ui-bridge/src/contract.rs` — chunk #26 callers should reach for it rather than typing `AppError::Internal { message: ... }` literally (per architecture §Project Intent Template patterns single-public-contract discipline).

- (arch) Per-crate `thiserror` enums in placeholder crates (`snapshot`, `workspace-detector`, `plugins`, `mcp-server` currently expose `Error::Placeholder`) MUST stay placeholder-shaped until those crates' real chunks land; chunk #26 either (a) adds TODO `From<PlaceholderError>` no-op routes that compile against `Error::Placeholder`, OR (b) defers those From impls — choose the option that preserves the workspace dependency graph DAG (per architecture §Cross-cutting Patterns Module dependency direction).

- (tests) Co-located unit tests with `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` inside `crates/ui-bridge/src/contract.rs` mirroring chunks #19–#22 patterns (where ingest/buffer/viz crates already host From-impl conversion tests for IngestError/BufferError/VizError → AppError).

- (tests) `rstest` 0.26.1 fixtures with builder pattern for parametric AppError test scenarios — `#[fixture] fn ingest_err_with_path() -> IngestError { … }` + `#[rstest] fn test_from_ingest_strips_path(err: IngestError)` (per test-plan §7 Fixture library + §4 unit fixture pattern).

- (tests) `serde_json::to_string` + `serde_json::from_str` round-trip assertions to validate stable shape across the TauRPC bridge — assert deserialized variant matches input. Rust-side serde tests pin the wire shape that chunk #25's TS types depend on (per test-plan §5 Cross-module patterns).

- (tests) Negative-test discipline via single-table parameterized inputs — use `#[rstest] #[case(input, expected_sanitized)]` for path-leak / struct-leak / version-leak fixtures. Echoes chunk #22 (`viz` crate) From<VizError> impl test scaffold.
- (tests) No `unwrap()` without context, no manual `assert_eq!` against raw JSON bytes — assert on decoded `serde_json::Value` field paths instead (per test-plan §11 Integration anti-patterns echo).

- (obs) Module-boundary error pattern: each `From<{Module}Error> for AppError` impl wraps `tracing::warn!(target: "ui-bridge.error.from_{module}", error_category = "...", source_kind = ?<thiserror variant discriminant>, "...")` then returns the sanitized variant — mirrors the existing `From<IngestError>` / `From<BufferError>` / `From<VizError>` impls (per obs-plan §3 Tracing init + §10 Module-boundary error logging).

- (obs) Sanitized chain capture pattern: surrounding `#[tracing::instrument]` uses `tracing-error::ErrorLayer` so `SpanTrace::capture()` records user-defined-span breadcrumbs only — NEVER `std::backtrace::Backtrace`. The boundary-side `tracing::error!` event embeds `spantrace = ?SpanTrace::capture()` as a structured field (per obs-plan §3 Tracing init crate set + §7 Panic hook snippet).

- (obs) Per-variant `tracing` target convention: emit conversion logs at `target: "ui-bridge.error.{variant}"` (e.g., `"ui-bridge.error.validation"`, `"ui-bridge.error.plugin"`) so `jq` filtering by target groups by error class (per obs-plan §2 Naming conventions span/target prefix `{module}.{operation}`).

- (obs) Default subscriber fields propagate identity automatically: every emitted `tracing::error!` JSON line already carries `service.name` / `service.version` / `deployment.environment` from the `Layer::with_default_fields(...)` registered at boot — `From` impls do NOT need to re-emit these (per obs-plan §3 Service identity / §2 Default subscriber fields).

- (a11y) Six-variant stable discriminated-union shape preserved per chunk #25 emitted bindings — downstream UI consumers (toast, banner, modal) can switch on `AppError.type` and choose ARIA live-region polarity per a11y-plan §11 region-type table without prop-drilling severity from the backend.

- (a11y) Plain-language `reason` / `message` author convention matching a11y-plan §11 phase-1 baseline ("Save" / "Cancel" / "Invalid field" register, not stack-trace register). Existing `AppError` strings in `crates/ui-bridge/src/contract.rs` are the calibration baseline; new From-impl conversions must preserve this register.
**Anti-patterns к avoid:**

- (security) NEVER serialize `anyhow::Error` directly across the TauRPC bridge — must convert to `AppError` first via the appropriate variant (per security plan §Anti-Patterns Code-Patterns line 419).

- (security) NEVER include stack traces, Rust struct names, file paths, library versions, or internal hostnames/IPs in any string field of any `AppError` variant — sanitize at the `From` impl, not in a downstream layer (per security plan §Anti-Patterns Logging lines 411-412).

- (security) NEVER let `Debug` formatting (`{:?}`) of an underlying error leak into `AppError::Internal { message }` — `Debug` typically renders module paths, struct names, source-code spans (per security plan §Error Handling External-responses preamble).

- (arch) NEVER serialize `anyhow::Error` directly across the TauRPC bridge — convert via `From<E> for AppError` at the procedure boundary (per architecture §Cross-cutting Patterns Cross-bridge data shape + §Established Decisions [Error Handling Pattern]).

- (arch) NEVER let an internal Rust struct name, library version, file path, or stack-trace fragment leak into `AppError::Internal { message }` / `Storage { message }` / `Ingest { message }` / `Plugin { message }`. The wire one-liner is constant-shaped per source variant; the full chain stays in the local `tracing-error` SpanTrace (per architecture §Conventions Error response schema (Tauri IPC) sanitization commitment).

- (arch) NEVER add a 7th AppError variant or rename existing variants without a route-decision-log entry + chunk #25 TypeScript binding regeneration sequence (per architecture §Conventions Error response schema (Tauri IPC) inventory + §Established Decisions [TauRPC]).

- (tests) NEVER let any `From<E> for AppError` impl emit `format!("{:?}", err)` directly on the upstream `thiserror`/`anyhow` chain — `Debug` formatter spills paths + struct names + library versions verbatim (per test-plan §11 Project-specific + security plan §Error sanitization at boundaries).

- (tests) NEVER assert `error_msg.contains("specific debug substring")` — assertions must invert: `!error_msg.contains("/")` / `!error_msg.contains("crates/")` / `!error_msg.contains("at line")` (per test-plan §11 Universal).
- (tests) NEVER skip the `cargo deny check bans` gate when adding new `thiserror` From impls per chunk #21 wrap-session learning on deny skip-list provenance discipline.

- (tests) NEVER run AppError serde tests with shared mutable state (e.g., env vars set mid-test) — each test case is hermetic via `rstest` fixture composition (per test-plan §11 Mocking anti-pattern).

- (obs) NEVER serialize `anyhow::Error` directly across the IPC boundary — `From<anyhow::Error> for AppError` (if introduced) MUST collapse to `AppError::Internal { message: "<sanitized one-liner>" }`, never `Internal { message: format!("{:?}", e) }` (per obs-plan §11 Spans/Traces).

- (obs) NEVER include `e.to_string()` of an upstream `thiserror`-derived enum directly in `AppError::Internal { message }` if that enum's `Display` impl interpolates user-controlled fields — review each upstream `#[error("…{field}…")]` macro before deciding whether `{e}` is safe; default to category-string mapping (per obs-plan §11 Logs Vector 1-5 row).
- (obs) NEVER emit conversion telemetry below `WARN` level — module-boundary errors are SLO signals (per obs-plan §11 Logs + §10 Standard+ invariants).

- (a11y) Do not author `AppError::Internal { message }` strings that contain Rust panic boilerplate (`thread 'main' panicked at`, `RUST_BACKTRACE=1`, `core::result::Result`) — those leak to a UI surface that screen-readers will then read aloud verbatim, violating SC 3.3.3 (per a11y-plan §11 phase-1 disciplines).

- (a11y) Do not collapse `Validation { field, reason }` into a single concatenated `String` — destroys the SC 3.3.1 / SC 3.3.2 binding handle that downstream UI needs for `aria-describedby` association (per a11y-plan §10 Forms & Validation pattern table).
**Contract bindings:**

- **security ↔ obs**: PII scrubbing rules cross-cut. The redaction discipline applied to `AppError::Internal { message }` mirrors the `tracing` subscriber redaction layer obs owns — the `From<thiserror::Error> for AppError` sanitizer must be consistent with the obs PII scrubber's allowlist so downstream `tracing` events don't re-leak the data the bridge stripped. Reciprocated: obs §8 Vector 2 (security plan + obs plan jointly own); security plan defines WHAT must not cross; obs defines HOW the rich chain is preserved internally via `tracing-error` SpanTrace + structured fields in `agent-latest.jsonl`. The `From` impl is the SINGLE site where both contracts converge.

- **security ↔ tests**: Sanitization is verifiable only via boundary tests. Tests assert each `From` impl produces `AppError` variants whose string payloads do NOT match the leakage classes (regex deny: `/[A-Z]:\\|\\\\|/.*?/|::[A-Z][a-zA-Z]+|v?\d+\.\d+\.\d+/`). Reciprocated: tests extract confirms "chunk #26 AppError sanitization is the test materialization of security plan §Error sanitization at boundaries". CI invariant grep (`grep "anyhow::Error.*Serialize" pulse-app/src/ crates/`) MUST stay empty.

- **security ↔ arch**: Variant set is closed (six variants). Adding a seventh requires arch decision (Established Decisions Error Handling Pattern) — chunk #26 MUST NOT introduce new variants for downstream crates' errors that haven't shipped; map provisionally to `Internal { message: "<crate> error: <sanitized one-liner>" }` until those crates land their own enum and the plan amends the variant set.

- **arch ↔ obs**: Sanitized AppError variants MUST NOT reach the JSON log file unredacted either — the obs-plan §PII scrubbing default-deny visitor (`pulse-app/src/observability.rs::JsonFieldVisitor`) handles this on the logging side, but chunk #26 ensures that even if a future site emits `tracing::error!(error = ?app_err)`, the wire-bound representation is already sanitized at construction. NEVER log multi-line stack traces; `tracing-error` SpanTrace is the one-line side-channel.

- **arch ↔ tests**: Coverage on AppError variants and every `From<E>` route is part of the ≥85% function-coverage gate; tests MUST live colocated under `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { ... }` in `crates/ui-bridge/src/contract.rs`; chunk #26 extends the existing 19-test suite with parallel assertions for any newly-added From source.

- **tests ↔ obs**: AppError sanitization tests bind to obs-plan §Logging redaction — the test must assert the boundary surface is sanitized while the `tracing` log target retains the full chain. Test-side: assert serialized AppError JSON has clean message; obs-side: the `tracing` JSON log line still carries `error.chain` field with full provenance.

- **a11y ↔ security**: AppError sanitization scope (strip stack traces / file paths / library versions / Rust struct names) is jointly owned. Security mandates redaction for incidentally-captured-secrets reasons; a11y mandates redaction so downstream screen-reader output meets SC 3.3.3 plain-language baseline. The chunk's sanitization implementation satisfies both simultaneously. No additional a11y-specific assertion needed at the Rust layer — a11y verification of error display happens at the future UI chunk.

- **a11y ↔ obs**: Out-of-band coordination only — obs emits the one-liner `message`; a11y owns alert-region semantics at the future UI rendering site; AppError content shape MUST be terse + non-secret + ARIA-`role="alert"` safe per obs-plan §3 Logging stack frontend bridge. (a11y violation JSON schema is unrelated to runtime AppError type — different categories, no binding in this chunk.)
**Acceptance criteria contributions:**

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase Phase 4. Read by /andromeda-implement.
Manual edits between runs are fine; do not edit during /implement run._
- **Phase number:** 23

- **Route chunks covered:**
  - route#26 "AppError serde enum + From impls — Validation/NotFound/Internal/Plugin/Storage/Ingest with sanitization (no stack traces / paths)"
- **Epoch:** Epoch 4 — Webview shell + TauRPC bridge

Complete the `AppError` From-impl matrix at the TauRPC bridge boundary so every module-internal error category has a sanctioned, sanitized conversion path that the webview can pattern-match. The 6-variant `AppError` enum in `crates/ui-bridge/src/contract.rs` is locked (per arch §Established Decisions [Error Handling Pattern] + §Conventions Error response schema (Tauri IPC)) with three live From impls (Ingest/Buffer/Viz) covering chunks #18–#22 sources; chunk #26 (a) extends the matrix to the four placeholder crates (snapshot / plugins / workspace-detector / mcp-server) with `From<{crate}::contract::Error>` routes that map to `AppError::Internal { message: "<crate>: placeholder error" }` (replaceable as each downstream crate ships real error enums in later chunks), (b) wires `tracing::warn!` emission inside every From impl per obs §10 module-boundary error logging discipline (Standard+ tier requirement — the From site is the only place where the rich source chain still exists), (c) adds serde round-trip tests for all six standalone variants (current tests cover Ingest + viz QueryFailed only), (d) verifies the a11y plain-language register (`grep -rE '(panicked at|RUST_BACKTRACE|core::result|::ErrorKind|alloc::|std::io::Error)' crates/*/src/ pulse-app/src/` returns empty), and (e) extends `pulse-app/src/observability.rs` `AllowList::production()` so the new `ui-bridge.error.*` event fields (`error_category`, `source_kind`, plus per-variant `field` / `plugin_id` / `resource`) are not silently redacted by the default-deny scrubber. Per security plan §Error sanitization at boundaries + obs plan §8 PII Vector 2 + arch §Cross-cutting Patterns Cross-bridge data shape, this chunk is the load-bearing implementation of the universal invariant "Errors crossing the TauRPC bridge MUST be `serde`-friendly `AppError` enum variants — convert from `thiserror`/`anyhow` via `From` impls; strip stack traces, file paths, library versions, Rust struct names" — fully verified by extending the existing 19-test invariant suite to 30+ tests.

1. **Extend `crates/ui-bridge/Cargo.toml` `[dependencies]`** with `tracing.workspace = true` (workspace already declares `tracing = "0.1"`); add four sibling-crate path deps `snapshot = { path = "../snapshot" }` / `plugins = { path = "../plugins" }` / `workspace-detector = { path = "../workspace-detector" }` / `mcp-server = { path = "../mcp-server" }` so the new `From<{crate}::contract::Error>` impls compile. Verify via `cargo tree -p ui-bridge` that the resulting graph stays a DAG with `pulse-app` as the only root (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns Module dependency direction); ui-bridge already depends on three sibling library crates so adding four more is consistent.

2. **Extend `crates/ui-bridge/Cargo.toml` `[dev-dependencies]`** with `rstest.workspace = true` (workspace declares `rstest = "0.26"`) for parametric From-impl test scenarios. /implement decides whether to additionally add `tracing-test = "0.2"` to workspace + ui-bridge dev-deps (for `#[traced_test]` macro asserting tracing-event emission per obs criterion #2) OR to use a 30-line in-process subscriber assertion (no extra workspace dep) — the latter is preferred if maintainers are dep-conservative. Document the choice in the chunk wrap-session learnings.

3. **Modify `crates/ui-bridge/src/contract.rs` — wire `tracing::warn!` emission in three existing From impls** (`From<IngestError>` / `From<BufferError>` / `From<VizError>`). For each impl, inside the match arm but BEFORE constructing the `AppError` variant, emit:

```
   tracing::warn!(
       target: "ui-bridge.error.{variant}",  // e.g., "ui-bridge.error.ingest"
       error_category = "{variant}",         // e.g., "ingest"
       source_kind = "{thiserror discriminant}",  // e.g., "bind_failed", "channel_full"
       "{constant sanitized message}"
   );
   ```

The constant message stays the existing one-liner (`"OTLP receiver bind failed"` etc.). Do NOT include source-error fields (`reason`, `value`, `payload_bytes`) in the tracing event payload — those carry potentially-leakable substrings; the `target` + `error_category` + `source_kind` triple is sufficient for `jq` aggregation per obs §2 naming convention.

4. **Modify `crates/ui-bridge/src/contract.rs` — add four placeholder From impls.** For each of `snapshot::contract::Error` / `plugins::contract::Error` / `workspace_detector::contract::Error` / `mcp_server::contract::Error`, wire:

Each placeholder route maps to `AppError::Internal { message }` with a stable one-liner (`"snapshot: placeholder error"` / `"plugins: placeholder error"` / `"workspace-detector: placeholder error"` / `"mcp-server: placeholder error"`); these routes are explicitly replaceable when each downstream crate lands its real error enum in subsequent chunks (per arch extract Q2 option (a)). The `source_crate` field on the tracing event distinguishes which placeholder fired without leaking implementation details.

5. **Modify `crates/ui-bridge/src/contract.rs` — extend `mod tests`** with the following groups (mirror existing naming `from_<source>_<scenario>_<assertion>` per research.md "Patterns detected"):
   - **6 round-trip tests** for standalone variants — `app_error_validation_round_trip`, `app_error_not_found_round_trip`, `app_error_internal_round_trip`, `app_error_plugin_round_trip`, `app_error_storage_round_trip`, `app_error_ingest_round_trip` — each constructs the variant directly (not via From), `serde_json::to_string` + `serde_json::from_str`, asserts decoded `serde_json::Value` field paths `v["kind"]` + per-variant fields (`v["field"]`, `v["resource"]`, `v["message"]`, `v["plugin_id"]`).
   - **1 helper test** for `AppError::internal(...)` — asserts the helper produces `AppError::Internal { message }` matching input.
   - **4 placeholder From-impl tests** — `from_snapshot_placeholder_collapses_to_constant_message_no_leak` / `from_plugins_placeholder_...` / `from_workspace_detector_placeholder_...` / `from_mcp_server_placeholder_...`. Each: trigger the From conversion, match `AppError::Internal { message }`, assert constant message + invariant grep set (`!message.contains("/")` / `!message.contains("::")` / `!message.contains(/v?\d+\.\d+\.\d+/)`).
   - **3 plain-language register tests** — one parametric `#[rstest]` per existing live From source family (Ingest/Buffer/Viz) feeding a synthetic upstream error with `"thread 'main' panicked at"` + `"RUST_BACKTRACE=1"` + `"core::result::Result"` + `"::ErrorKind"` + `"alloc::"` + `"std::io::Error"` substrings, asserts none appear in the resulting `AppError` serialized JSON. Replaces the security-domain Vector-by-vector approach with the a11y-domain plain-language overlay.
   - **(optional) 7 tracing-event presence tests** — one per From impl (3 existing + 4 new placeholder). If using `tracing-test`: `#[traced_test]` macro + `assert!(logs_contain("ui-bridge.error.{variant}"))` per impl. If using in-process subscriber: a small `TestSubscriber` with `Vec<String>` capture, `tracing::subscriber::with_default(subscriber, || ...)` per test, asserts at least one event at level `WARN` with target prefix `ui-bridge.error.`. /implement chooses based on dev-dep budget per Step 2.

6. **Modify `pulse-app/src/observability.rs` — extend `AllowList::production()` `ui-bridge` registry entry** to permit the new tracing-event field set: `error_category`, `source_kind`, `source_crate` (cross-cuts all variants), plus `field` (Validation), `plugin_id` (Plugin), `resource` (NotFound). Verify via `for_target("ui-bridge.error.ingest")` resolver behavior — per session-learnings 2026-05-03, the `for_target` `::`-prefix-strip resolver collapses dotted targets. /implement should: (a) probe whether `ui-bridge.error.ingest` strips to `ui-bridge.error` (not in registry — falls through), then to `ui-bridge` (existing entry), in which case widening the existing entry's allowed-fields HashSet is the minimal fix; OR (b) introduce six new `ui-bridge.error.{variant}` registry entries keyed exactly per the prefix-strip rule. Preserve the singular `plugin` vs plural `plugins` discipline — error-category is `"plugin"` (singular, per AppError variant name); the existing workspace crate name `plugins` (plural) registry entry is unrelated.

7. **Run the full sanitization gate locally before commit** — execute the test-command block below; verify zero new flaky tests; confirm the existing 19 contract.rs tests still pass with new tracing emissions added (tracing-event side-effect MUST NOT change AppError variant or message field).
- (none) — chunk #26 modifies existing files only.

- `crates/ui-bridge/Cargo.toml` — add `tracing.workspace = true` to `[dependencies]`; add four sibling-crate path deps (`snapshot` / `plugins` / `workspace-detector` / `mcp-server`); add `rstest.workspace = true` to `[dev-dependencies]`; (optional) add `tracing-test = "0.2"` to `[dev-dependencies]` if Step 2 chooses the crate over in-process subscriber. Preserve `default = ["taurpc-runtime"]` + optional `[dependencies]` block (taurpc/tauri/specta/tokio).

- `crates/ui-bridge/src/contract.rs` — three categories of change: (a) add four sibling-crate Error type imports; (b) wire `tracing::warn!` emission in 3 existing + 4 new From impls; (c) extend `mod tests` block with ~14 new tests (6 round-trip + 1 helper + 4 placeholder From + 3 plain-language register + optional 7 tracing-event presence).

- `pulse-app/src/observability.rs` — extend `AllowList::production()` `ui-bridge` registry entry (or add 6 new `ui-bridge.error.{variant}` entries per /implement's resolver-probe choice in Step 6) so the new tracing-event fields (`error_category`, `source_kind`, `source_crate`, `field`, `plugin_id`, `resource`) survive default-deny redaction.
- `Cargo.lock` — auto-regenerate side-effect from `cargo build` after `Cargo.toml` mutations; commit alongside.

- `crates/snapshot/src/contract.rs` / `crates/plugins/src/contract.rs` / `crates/workspace-detector/src/contract.rs` / `crates/mcp-server/src/contract.rs` — placeholder Error enums stay placeholder-shaped; chunk #26 routes from them, does not modify them. Each crate's real error enum lands in the chunk that introduces real functionality.

- `pulse-app/src/{viz_routers,streams,main}.rs` — TauRPC procedure signatures already use `Result<_, AppError>` per chunk #25 (verified via `grep -RE 'Result<.*AppError' pulse-app/src/`); no procedure-level changes needed.

- `pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` — auto-regenerated by chunk #25's `emit_taurpc_bindings` `#[tokio::test]` on next `cargo nextest -p pulse-app` run; AppError variant set is unchanged (same 6 variants), so the emitted TypeScript discriminated-union shape stays identical. The chunk #26 placeholder From impls do not introduce new AppError variants — they map to the existing `Internal` variant.

- `.andromeda/architecture.md` / `.andromeda/route.md` — no Decisions Log entry needed (chunk lands within locked Established Decision [Error Handling Pattern] + Conventions Error response schema (Tauri IPC) — no spec amendment).

data.head: ### Chunk route#27: "IPC introspection + capability-drift check — app_info/health/ready/get_settings/update_settings + xtask diff procedures vs capabilities/ JSON"

body: **Constraints across domains:**

- (security) Capability-drift check MUST detect the `streams.*` D3 drift case — chunk #23's `streams.{subscribe_spans, subscribe_metrics, subscribe_logs}` TauRPC procedures lack matching `pulse-app/capabilities/` JSON entries (per security plan §API Security TauRPC capability authorization + §Anti-Patterns API ban + session-handoff D3 carry-over).

- (security) Drift check MUST introspect at TauRPC router-level granularity, NOT per-procedure — `taurpc::create_ipc_handler` is a single invoke handler; capability JSON `permissions` arrays carry `core:default` + plugin-level perms, not per-procedure entries (per security.md Session Addition 2026-05-03).

- (security) The 5 introspection procedures are TauRPC bridge boundaries — every argument struct MUST be `serde::Deserialize`; `update_settings` MUST use `serde` + smart enum + `TryFrom<u16>` on port fields (per security plan §Input Validation row 3 + Established Decisions Validation Library).

- (security) Errors from these 5 procedures MUST return `Result<T, AppError>` collapsing module-internal `thiserror` via chunk #26 `From` impl matrix; `AppError::Internal { message }` content MUST be sanitized one-liner (no stack traces / file paths / Rust struct names / library versions) (per security plan §Error Handling + §Anti-Patterns Logging).

- (security) The xtask drift check MUST be wired into `ci.yml` matrix as `dep-security-ci-gate` step and fail the build on mismatch (per security plan §Bootstrap phases `dep-security-ci-gate` + §API Security TauRPC capability authorization).

- (security) `health`/`ready`/`app_info` response payloads MUST NOT leak internal hostnames, IPs, library versions, file paths, or full plugin paths (per security plan §Logging NEVER-log list + §Error Handling sanitization).

- (security) `get_settings`/`update_settings` MUST NOT expose secrets — `tauri.conf.json` carries only the Tauri updater Minisign **public** key; never the private key in IPC responses (per security plan §Secret Management + §Anti-Patterns Data Protection).

- (security) The chunk MUST NOT widen the 5 capability scoping rules from arch §Cross-cutting Patterns — `pulse:default` enumerates only Occupied Resources procedures; `pulse:updater` NOT exposed to webview JS; `pulse:notification`/`pulse:tray` outbound-emit-only; `pulse:plugin-fs` scoped to plugin-dir read; `fs`/`shell`/`dialog`/`http` core APIs NOT granted to `pulse:default` (per security plan §Anti-Patterns API bans).

- (design) Settings procedures (`get_settings` / `update_settings`) MUST expose a `theme` enum that includes `dark` (default), `light`, and `auto` (follow-system) (per design plan §Surface: desktop-webview "Dark mode default" + §Decisions Log 2026-05-02 "Color World locked").

- (design) Settings wire shape MUST NOT inline any hex / pixel / duration literal — semantic enum tags only (e.g., `theme: "dark" | "light" | "auto"`) (per design plan §Token Test self-validation + §Surface: desktop-webview Tokens).

- (design) If `update_settings` accepts a `motion_preference` override, the field MUST be a 3-value enum (`auto` / `enabled` / `reduced`) so frontend can degrade Halo State Pulse to static glow without ambiguity (per design plan §Motion Accessibility + §Brand Identity Halo State Pulse).
- (design) `app_info` returned name string MUST remain `"andromeda-pulse"` (titlebar render contract consumes verbatim) (per design plan §Surface: desktop-webview Component Patterns "Titlebar").

- (design) `xtask capability-drift` violation messages MUST stay terse + observational (≤2 lines / contemplative voice — no exclamation marks / no decorative ASCII art) (per design plan §Brand Identity "design direction" + §Surface: desktop-native "Tray Menu").

- (tests) TauRPC `health` MUST return the `status / subsystems / pid / uptime_ms` JSON shape verbatim — `boot` 5-command polls these fields every 500 ms up to 10 s (per test-plan §3 5-command implementation + §3 Status endpoint shape).

- (tests) TauRPC `ready` MUST return a `ready` boolean plus `checks` object whose keys include `duckdb_connection` and `ingest_mpsc_capacity_pct` (per test-plan §5 Cross-module patterns "ready contract").
- (tests) TauRPC `app_info` MUST return at minimum `name, version, rust_version, tauri_version, features` (per test-plan §5 Cross-module patterns "app_info contract").

- (tests) `xtask capability-drift` MUST be invocable via `cargo xtask <task>` discipline and exit non-zero when TauRPC procedures and `pulse-app/capabilities/` JSON disagree (per test-plan §1 trigger `security-vector-coverage: Tauri IPC capability gating` + §3 5-command `run`).

- (tests) New procedures MUST round-trip through `tauri::test::mock_builder() + get_ipc_response()` in-process harness — no live webview overhead (per test-plan §5 Drivers "Module ↔ TauRPC IPC" + §6 E2E drivers row).

- (tests) Negative test REQUIRED: invoking an undeclared procedure (router AND capabilities JSON missing) MUST reject with `AppError`; positive test invokes each declared procedure and asserts success (per test-plan §1 trigger `security-vector-coverage`).

- (obs) All 5 introspection procedures MUST be wrapped with `#[tracing::instrument(skip_all, fields(traceparent = %tp, method_name, argument_digest, result_type, latency_ms, span.kind = "server"))]` (per obs-plan §3 IPC boundaries + §4 Instrumentation per surface table + §6 boundary-call wrappers TauRPC).

- (obs) `health` IPC command MUST expose synchronous-snapshot equivalents of heartbeat tick fields (`status`, `subsystems`) — active liveness probe paired with passive heartbeat tick stream (per obs-plan §3 Heartbeat ticks).

- (obs) `ready` IPC command MUST surface readiness fields (`duckdb_connection`, `ingest_mpsc_capacity_pct`, `broadcast_subscribers`, `plugins_loaded`, `mcp_server_enabled`) consistent with metric-event names (per obs-plan §5 Metric Coverage + arch §Standard Contracts ready envelope).

- (obs) `update_settings` MUST NOT log raw setting-value payloads — only `setting_keys_changed` count + enumerated key names allowlisted at subscriber Layer; `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_*_PATH` / `*_DIR` paths basename-only per Vector 6 (per obs-plan §8 PII Scrubbing default-deny + Vector 6 path sanitizer).

- (obs) `xtask capability-drift` MUST produce structured JSON output (drift count + missing/extra procedure list); `tracing::info!(target: "xtask.capability_drift", missing_count, extra_count, drift_state, ...)` with NO raw procedure body content logged; report file uploaded as CI artifact (per obs-plan §9 CI Integration `xtask test` row).

- (obs) Errors crossing the bridge from these procedures MUST flow through the `AppError`-conversion path with `tracing::warn!(target: "ui-bridge.error.{variant}", ...)` emission established at chunk #26 (per obs-plan §10 Standard+ "module-boundary error logging" + §11 Spans/Traces).

- (arch) `app_info` / `health` / `ready` commands MUST conform exactly to the JSON envelopes specified in arch §Standard Contracts — `app_info` returns `{name, version, rust_version, tauri_version, features, build_profile}`; `health` returns `{status, checked_at, subsystems}` with `status ∈ {"ok", "degraded"}`; `ready` returns `{ready, checked_at, checks}` with documented checks keys. Hard subsystem failure converts at bridge to `Err(AppError::Internal { ... })` (per arch §Standard Contracts).
- (arch) All 5 top-level procedures MUST be `snake_case` bare verbs and registered in the `ui-bridge` crate (per arch §Conventions "Endpoint naming" + §Occupied Resources "Tauri IPC routes").

- (arch) Every TauRPC procedure registered in the workspace MUST have a corresponding (router-level) entry in `pulse-app/capabilities/` JSON (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns "Webview IPC capability policy").
- (arch) Every type returned MUST be `serde::Serialize` (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns "Cross-bridge data shape").

- (arch) Errors crossing the bridge MUST collapse to `AppError` variants (`Validation`/`NotFound`/`Internal`/`Plugin`/`Storage`/`Ingest`); nothing leaks `anyhow::Error` directly (per arch §Conventions "Error response schema (Tauri IPC)").

- (arch) `xtask capability-drift` lives in the existing `xtask` crate (no new workspace member) — invoked locally as `cargo xtask capability-drift` and wired into `ci.yml` (per arch §Established Decisions [CI Task Runner] cargo-xtask + §Infrastructure Patterns CI/CD).

- (arch) `update_settings` MUST honor Config management precedence (env vars > `~/.andromeda-pulse/config.toml` > defaults); writes from IPC land in the `config.toml` layer; settings field names use units-explicit shape (`retention_seconds`, ports as `u16` via `TryFrom<u16>`) (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns "Config management" + §Conventions "Configuration units").
**Patterns to follow:**

- (security) TauRPC procedure → capability JSON pairing pattern: chunk #25's router scaffolding established two-piece enforcement (router registration + capabilities JSON entry); 5 introspection procedures + existing routers (`traces.*`/`metrics.*`/`logs.*`/`snapshot.*`/`plugins.*`/`mcp.*`/`workspace.*`/`streams.*`) are the introspection target set.

- (security) AppError sanitization on every TauRPC procedure boundary — chunk #26 already shipped From-impl matrix with `tracing::warn!` emission at every conversion site; 5 procedures share this pattern.

- (security) Static-introspection at compile time: `taurpc` derive macro generates router metadata at compile time; xtask check should introspect static metadata (e.g., generated `*.d.ts` bindings from chunk #25, or `taurpc::create_ipc_handler` registry walking) rather than spawning the app.

- (security) `xtask` task pattern follows existing harness discipline — chunk #4 wired the xtask agent-run 5-command harness with structured/JSON output; the new `xtask capability-drift` task follows the same discipline.
- (design) IPC introspection envelope as token-free semantic JSON: `app_info` returns build-time data with no design surface; design's contribution is preserving `name = "andromeda-pulse"` literal.

- (design) Settings field nomenclature: `snake_case` shape + semantic-enum values mapping to design tokens at render-time (e.g., `widget_position: "top-left" | "top-right" | "bottom-left" | "bottom-right"` for snap-to-edge).
- (design) `health` / `ready` JSON booleans + status-string contracts (`"ok"` / `"degraded"`) consumed downstream by tray icon Halo color encoding (Earth Blue ↔ Alert Burgundy).

- (tests) TauRPC IPC contract tests via `tauri::test::mock_builder()` + `get_ipc_response()` for in-process unit-level coverage; response shape asserted by deserializing into a contract struct (existing chunks #24-26 already use this harness).
- (tests) `rstest` 0.26.1 fixtures for reusable IPC test setup — `#[fixture] fn ipc_harness()` + `#[rstest]` test functions composing the fixture (per test-plan §7 fixture library + §3.5 phase 6).
- (tests) `cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features --profile ci` is canonical test runner; per-process isolation prevents port-binding collisions (per test-plan §3 5-command + §4 framework).
- (tests) New tests co-located in `crates/ui-bridge/src/` and `pulse-app/src/` as `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { … }` (per test-plan §4 conventions test-file-location).

- (tests) The `xtask capability-drift` task is a Rust binary in workspace; tests live in `xtask/src/` exercising both happy-path (synthetic match → exit 0) and drift-path (mismatch → exit non-zero with structured stderr).

- (obs) IPC-internal handler instrumentation: `#[tracing::instrument(skip_all, fields(traceparent = %tp))]` already used by chunk #25's TauRPC routers; chunk #27 extends with `method_name`/`argument_digest`/`result_type`/`latency_ms`.

- (obs) Heartbeat tick contract reuse: `health` response `subsystems` map MUST mirror field set already emitted by `ingest.tick` / `buffer.tick` / `viz.tick` / `plugins.tick` — passive (tick) + active (probe) surfaces stay schema-identical.
- (obs) Default subscriber fields ride: `service.name` / `service.version` / `deployment.environment` automatically via `Layer::with_default_fields(...)` — handlers do not repeat per-call.

- (obs) AllowList per-leaf entry discipline (project lesson 2026-05-07): each new IPC procedure target needs explicit AllowList entry at `pulse-app/src/observability.rs::AllowList::production()` — falling through `split('.').next()` collapses to crate-level entries with mismatched field sets.
- (obs) xtask capability-drift CI artifact pattern: emits structured drift JSON to `target/capability-drift/report.json` + tail-friendly `tracing::info!` line in `agent-latest.jsonl`.

- (arch) Each library crate exposes its public contract via single `pub` contract module + `thiserror`-derived error enum + TauRPC-router module mounted by `pulse-app` (per arch §Project Intent "Template patterns").

- (arch) The `AppError` From-impl matrix from chunk #26 is the conversion pattern; chunk #27's `health` / `ready` aggregation reads sibling-crate state via existing contracts and surfaces failures as `AppError::Internal { message }`.

- (arch) Module dependency direction stays as DAG with `pulse-app` as only root — `ui-bridge` may depend on sibling crates' contract modules; no library crate imports `pulse-app`; `xtask` may shell out / parse JSON but must not link Tauri-linking library crates.

- (arch) Capability JSON files at `pulse-app/capabilities/` (5 files: `pulse:default`/`pulse:tray`/`pulse:notification`/`pulse:updater`/`pulse:plugin-fs`); drift check parses these + TauRPC router-export at compile-introspection at router-level (per security Session Additions 2026-05-03).
- (arch) `cargo xtask <task>` is local-and-CI single-source pattern — drift check runs identically locally and in CI.
**Anti-patterns to avoid:**
- (security) NEVER add a TauRPC procedure to a router crate without a matching entry in `pulse-app/capabilities/` — silent runtime rejection per Tauri 2 docs; xtask drift check is the enforcement.

- (security) NEVER expose stack traces, Rust struct names, file paths, or library versions in `AppError::Internal { message }` content surfaced from the 5 procedures — sanitize at the `From` impl per chunk #26 discipline.
- (security) NEVER expose Tauri updater Minisign private key, Azure Key Vault credentials, or any secret in `app_info` / `get_settings` response payloads.
- (security) NEVER widen any of the 5 capability identifiers — particularly NEVER expose `pulse:updater` to webview JS or grant Tauri core APIs (`fs`/`shell`/`dialog`/`http`) to `pulse:default`.
- (security) NEVER reference any third-party GitHub Action by `@v2` / floating tag — pin by 40-char commit SHA per `tj-actions/changed-files` CVE-2025-30066 retroactive-tag-rewrite class.

- (design) NEVER inline raw hex / pixel / motion duration values into `update_settings` argument shapes or capability-drift error message strings — every visual value MUST trace back to design-system tokens.

- (design) NEVER expose color-only state encoding via the IPC contract without a paired text/label channel — if `health` adds a `severity` color enum, MUST be paired with `severity_label` string (not-color-alone discipline).
- (design) NEVER name procedures or settings fields with generic productivity-app vocabulary that betrays the Observatory / Mission Control domain.
- (tests) NEVER assert on raw JSON byte equality for IPC responses — assert on decoded fields (parallel rule for IPC payload, per test-plan §11 Integration anti-pattern).
- (tests) NEVER use `sleep(N)` to wait for `health` / `ready` readiness — poll the IPC command per §3 boot-readiness pattern (every 500 ms up to 10 s).

- (tests) NEVER expose stack traces / file paths / library versions / Rust struct names in `AppError::Internal { message }` strings via the new IPC procedures (chunk #26 sanitization must not regress).
- (tests) NEVER lower coverage threshold to make new IPC-procedure code pass; new functions contribute to ≥75% line / ≥70% branch / ≥85% function targets.
- (tests) NEVER let drift between TauRPC procedure registrations and capabilities JSON merge to main — `xtask capability-drift` IS the gate.
- (obs) NEVER log full setting values in `update_settings` — `*_PATH` / `*_DIR` env-var values subject to Vector 6 (CWE-22 sanitizer).
- (obs) NEVER use unbounded label cardinality on the new procedures — `method_name` enum bounded to 5 procedure names; `subsystems` keys bounded to known modules.

- (obs) NEVER serialize the full TauRPC procedure inventory or capability JSON body inside the `xtask capability-drift` `tracing::info!` event — emit only summary fields; full diff in JSON CI artifact.
- (obs) NEVER run `xtask capability-drift` as side-effect of every `tracing::info!` during normal app boot — CI/xtask-time gate, not a runtime telemetry event.
- (arch) DO NOT deviate from JSON envelope keys / values specified in arch §Standard Contracts — adding fields, renaming `status` → `state`, swapping `checked_at` ISO format would break the contract.

- (arch) DO NOT introduce per-procedure capability JSON entries (e.g., `"core:command:allow-health"` strings) — TauRPC integrates via single invoke handler; drift check enforces router-level coverage.
- (arch) DO NOT add new env vars beyond those reserved in arch §Occupied Resources without `/andromeda-scope-arch`; `update_settings` writes into `config.toml` only.
- (arch) DO NOT introduce new TauRPC procedure namespace prefix (e.g., debug-only `debug.*`) in the drift check — it reports drift from existing reserved namespaces only.
- (arch) DO NOT have a library crate depend on `pulse-app` — drift check belongs in `xtask`, which orchestrates introspection without inverting the DAG.
**Contract bindings:**

- **security ↔ tests** (CI gate / capability-drift): xtask capability-drift wired into `ci.yml` as `dep-security-ci-gate` step; tests owns CI workflow + matrix definition; security owns gate semantics (router introspection, mismatch = failure, SHA-pinned action references).

- **security ↔ arch**: 5 introspection procedures' response payload shapes are arch-owned (Standard Contracts envelopes); security owns sanitization discipline applied to those payload field values. The streams.* D3 drift resolution lives in arch §Occupied Resources — chunk #27's check surfaces mismatch but reconciliation is an arch decision.

- **security ↔ obs**: chunk #26 wired `tracing::warn!` emission at every From-impl conversion site at `target: "ui-bridge.error.{variant}"` against AllowList. The 5 procedures' error paths inherit this discipline; obs owns AllowList resolver semantics; security owns boundary-sanitization invariant ensuring tracing log content (which DOES carry rich source chain) never leaks across IPC bridge to webview.

- **obs ↔ tests** (harness 5-command discipline): obs-plan §3 logging stack + log format JSON schema is binding contract consumed by tests' 5-command harness (`status` command); chunk #27's `health` IPC command returns SAME shape that `status` harness command surfaces externally (`{status, checked_at, subsystems}` per arch §Standard Contracts). Tests' P5 must-trace path calls `ipc.health.check`; obs supplies `tracing::info!` on entry/exit so harness can correlate by `trace_id`. Reciprocal — tests acknowledges, obs declares.

- **obs ↔ tests** (capability-drift CI gate): chunk #27's xtask capability-drift output consumed by tests' CI gates (build fails on drift); drift JSON artifact upload is obs's contribution; assertion / fail-build wiring is tests' responsibility.

- **obs ↔ security** (Vector 6 path sanitization): `update_settings` mutating `*_PATH` / `*_DIR` MUST canonicalize via `strict-path` per security rules (CWE-22) before logging basename only; obs binds via Vector 6 trigger emitting `config.update.path_validation` span with `canonical_dir_basename` field.

- **design ↔ a11y**: `update_settings` motion-preference enum (if exposed) binds to a11y SC 2.3.3 prefers-reduced-motion override; wire shape MUST permit "force-reduced" so a11y harness can verify Halo degrades to static glow regardless of OS preference. Note: a11y extract emitted "No domain coverage" for chunk #27 itself (UI consumption deferred to chunk #34); this binding is forward-compatibility only.
- **design ↔ arch**: design owns `theme` enum vocabulary (`dark` / `light` / `auto`) consumed by `update_settings`; arch owns procedure envelope shape; convergence at `Settings` struct definition.

- **design ↔ tests**: tests will lint settings JSON for banned hex literals + banned font names; chunk #27 settings-shape design must not introduce new hex/font value fields requiring later exemption.

- **tests ↔ arch (D3 carry-over)**: chunk #23 `streams.*` namespace not in arch §Occupied Resources; new `xtask capability-drift` is canonical resolution venue; tests for drift command must assert streams.* namespace correctly classified (drift detected vs clean).

- **arch ↔ obs**: `health` / `ready` subsystem strings (`otlp_grpc_receiver`, `otlp_http_receiver`, `buffer`, `ingest_channel`, `duckdb_connection`, `broadcast_subscribers`, `plugins_loaded`, `mcp_server_enabled`) align with heartbeat `{module}.tick` event names (chunk #9) and AllowList-style observability redaction patterns (chunk #26 `ui-bridge.error.{variant}` entries). Obs traces failure paths; arch fixes field names.

- **arch ↔ tests**: `health` / `ready` are IPC introspection probe surface; E2E tests inspect buffer/ingest/MCP state via these procedures (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns "Test-time telemetry injection"); `xtask capability-drift` is agent-harness gate tests can call as structured assertion.

- **arch ↔ a11y** (forward-compatibility): `update_settings` writes (a11y-relevant fields like `notifications_enabled`, color-scheme, retention) round-trip through JSON-stable settings shape so future webview Settings modal (chunk #34) reads back exactly what it wrote.

- (security) `cargo xtask capability-drift` wired into `ci.yml` matrix (Linux/macOS/Windows) as step under `dep-security-ci-gate` and fails build on mismatch; any third-party action SHA-pinned.

- (security) `health`/`ready`/`app_info`/`get_settings`/`update_settings` responses inspected at TauRPC bridge contain no stack traces / Rust struct names / file paths / library versions / internal hostnames / IPs / signing material — verified by serialization-roundtrip test or grep against captured response samples returning empty.

- (security) `update_settings` argument struct deserialization rejects out-of-range ports (`TryFrom<u16>` failure path) and invalid enum field values via `AppError::Validation { field, reason }` — sanitized error output.

- (security) No new capability identifier introduced beyond 5 reserved; none widened to expose `fs`/`shell`/`dialog`/`http` core APIs or expose `pulse:updater` to webview JS — verified via capability JSON diff.
- (arch) Five top-level procedures registered in `ui-bridge` crate's TauRPC router and live in `crates/ui-bridge/src/`.

- (tests) New test count strictly increases vs current baseline (368 nextest workspace + 64 ui-bridge + 117 pulse-app); minimum: 1 test per procedure × 5 + 2 xtask drift tests = ≥7 new tests.

- **Epoch:** Epoch 4 — Webview shell + TauRPC bridge (final chunk; closes epoch)

Land the cross-cutting introspection envelope (`app_info` / `health` / `ready` / `get_settings` / `update_settings`) and the workspace-level `xtask capability-drift` gate that mechanically enforces arch §Cross-cutting Patterns "Webview IPC capability policy". title: Chunk route#28: "WebGPU canvas + WGSL render pipeline"

data.head: ### Chunk route#28: "WebGPU canvas + WGSL render pipeline"

body: **Constraints across domains:**

- (security) The `tauri.conf.json` `app.security.csp` literal MUST be `"default-src 'self' ipc: http://ipc.localhost; img-src 'self' data:; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; script-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' ipc: http://ipc.localhost; worker-src 'self' blob:"` — `worker-src 'self' blob:` is required for WebGPU compute pipelines; `'unsafe-inline'` MUST NOT be added to `script-src` (per security plan §API Security row "CSP (webview content)").

- (security) WGSL shader sources MUST be first-party — bundled with webview build, served via `'self'` origin; never loaded from remote URL or plugin guest bytes (per security plan §Threat Model Summary "webview content" trust boundary).

- (security) The webview's `pulse:default` capability MUST stay scoped — chunk #28 MUST NOT widen to grant `fs`/`shell`/`dialog`/`http` core APIs (per security plan §API Security row "Updater capability isolation" + §Anti-Patterns API row 4).
- (security) Fallback message DOM MUST render entirely from first-party assets — no remote image/font/script (per security plan §API Security CSP row + §Threat Model Summary "webview content").

- (security) Errors from WebGPU init failure crossing TauRPC MUST be sanitized at `From<...> for AppError` boundary — no raw browser error strings, file paths, library versions (per security plan §Anti-Patterns Logging row 4 + §Code Patterns row "NEVER serialize an `anyhow::Error` directly").
- (design) WebGPU canvas containers MUST use `--color-inset` (#0F1117) as background per Surface: desktop-webview Component Patterns §Canvas Container.

- (design) Trace timeline / flamegraph / metrics chart shaders MUST consume only Color Palette tokens — Earth Blue #4A90E2, Alert Burgundy #C7556A, Status White-Blue #E8EEF7, Stellar Indigo #2C3E7F, Feedback Cyan #17B3A3, Deep Control Gray #1A1D24 — no random hex per §Color Palette + Self-Validation Protocol §Token Test.
- (design) Canvas-rendered text MUST use JetBrains Mono 12px tabular-nums for data values and IBM Plex Sans 12px (Label role) for axis/category labels per §Typography table.

- (design) Render pipeline animations MUST respect `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` — degrade to instant render with hue still updated per data per §Motion Accessibility (mirrors Halo State Pulse degradation).
- (design) WGSL shaders MUST be first-party inline or module-imported — NO external shader CDN per Surface: desktop-webview §CSP policy.

- (layouts) WebGPU `<canvas>` MUST fill its container (`position: relative`, `width: 100%`, `height: 100%`); `devicePixelRatio` scaling handled by browser per layout-templates.md §Component — Halo State Pulse canvas Layout.

- (layouts) Canvas container chrome (`color-inset` bg, 1px subtle border with `radius-md`, `space-md` padding) lives on the wrapper element, NOT on `<canvas>` itself per §Component — Halo State Pulse canvas Layout.

- (layouts) WebGPU-unavailable fallback MUST render as `font-body` text in `color-text-tertiary` reading "WebGPU not supported in this context" inside the `<canvas>` container (DOM, not canvas-painted) per §Component — Halo State Pulse canvas Fallback. ⚠ See Cross-domain rot warnings — design extract has different fallback text wording.

- (layouts) Canvas substrate MUST be agnostic to surface placement — same shader logic / adapter handle for all three downstream signature placements (compact widget hero, full dashboard hero, tray icon overlay window) per §Decisions Log Cross-surface IA decisions.

- (tests) Webview unit tests for new React components MUST be co-located `*.test.tsx` adjacent to source under `pulse-app/ui/src/` (Vitest 3.x + jsdom 26 + `@testing-library/react` 16) per §4 (framework landed chunk #11).

- (tests) WebGPU canvas pixel inspection MUST NOT appear as a test step — agent-driven discipline §1: "WebGPU canvas rendering is out of E2E agent scope; assert IPC contract and WebGPU compile success."
- (tests) Fallback-message branch MUST be exercised by Vitest test stubbing `navigator.gpu = undefined` and asserting fallback DOM-shape (text + role) — assertion on contract per §4.
- (tests) Adapter-detection tests MUST be deterministic — mock `navigator.gpu.requestAdapter()` via `vi.stubGlobal()` or constructor injection; no real GPU calls in unit tests.
- (tests) Coverage gate per §10 Standard tier (≥75% line / ≥70% branch / ≥85% function) applies — webview presentational-components exclusion sunset since chunk #24 webview shell landed.

- (obs) Frontend instrumentation MUST go through TauRPC bridge to backend `tracing` event stream — NO browser OTel SDK linked into webview, NO direct file writes (per obs-plan §1 Telemetry surfaces + §3 Frontend bridge + §11 Universal anti-pattern).

- (obs) WebGPU frame timing MUST use DOM `performance.now()` + `device.queue.onSubmittedWorkDone()` and emit through TauRPC `telemetry.frontend.record_frame_ms(duration_ms, wgpu_backend)` → backend `tracing::info!(target: "metric.webgpu.frame_duration_ms", ...)` (per obs-plan §3 Frontend bridge + §5).

- (obs) Adapter acquisition MUST emit a startup-phase event `app.boot.gpu.check` with bounded fields `gpu_available: bool`, `wgpu_backend: vulkan|metal|dx12` per obs-plan §1 Telemetry triggers; fallback path emits at `warn` level. ⚠ See Cross-domain rot warnings — a11y extract uses `viz.webgpu` target instead.
- (obs) Metric label cardinality bounded: `wgpu_backend ∈ {vulkan,metal,dx12}`, `webview_backend ∈ {WebView2,WKWebView,GTKWebKit}`, `timing_method ∈ {cpu,gpu}` per obs-plan §5.

- (obs) Render-pipeline spans cannot be hot-loop-instrumented at `info` level — frame loop ~60 Hz; use `tracing::trace!` gated by `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_LOG_LEVEL`; the metric event itself rides at `info` (sampled per frame) per obs-plan §11 Logs anti-pattern.
- (obs) `record_frame_ms` resolver in `ui-bridge` MUST follow chunk #26 AppError sanitization discipline: stripped one-liners, no stack traces / paths / Rust struct names crossing the bridge.

- (a11y) WebGPU `<canvas>` has no built-in accessibility tree — semantic context MUST be enforced via wrapper `role="region"` + `aria-label="Telemetry traces chart"` (or per chart type) per a11y plan §1 + §7 Landmark roles.

  - route#28 "WebGPU canvas + WGSL render pipeline — navigator.gpu adapter, render shaders for trace timeline / flamegraph / metrics charts, fallback message"
- **Epoch:** Epoch 5 — Visualization surfaces (Epoch 5 opens with this chunk)

Chunk #28 lands the WebGPU rendering substrate that Epoch 5's nine downstream chunks (#29-#37) consume. The substrate has four parts: (a) `navigator.gpu` adapter detection with graceful-degrade fallback (mirrors `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED` precedent per arch §Established Decisions); (b) three WGSL render-pipeline factories aligned to the viz query routers (`traces.*` → trace timeline + flamegraph; `metrics.*` → metrics charts; `logs.*` reserved for chunk #35); (c) a semantic React canvas wrapper (`role="region"` + `aria-label`) carrying design-token chrome (`--color-inset` bg, 1px subtle border, `radius-md`, `space-md` padding) and respecting `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` via the chunk #15 `useReducedMotion` hook + chunk #15 `createFrameLoop` reduced-motion-gated rAF; (d) a fallback message component (`role="alert"`) rendered when `navigator.gpu` is undefined or `requestAdapter()` returns null, screen-reader-accessible via `aria-live="assertive"`.

The chunk is substrate-only: no per-surface composition (compact widget hero / full dashboard hero / tray icon overlay all land at chunks #30/#31/#33/#34/#35/#36) and no per-frame timing telemetry (the TauRPC `telemetry.frontend.record_frame_ms` resolver lands at chunk #29 with the 10k spans/sec compute aggregation budget). Chunk #28 wires the frame-timing measurement point in the rAF tick and registers the `metric.webgpu.frame_duration_ms` AllowList entry so chunk #29 can attach the resolver without re-architecting the render loop. Per security plan §API Security CSP row + §Threat Model Summary "webview content" all WGSL shader sources are first-party-bundled (`'self'` origin); no remote shader CDN, no `'unsafe-inline'`/`'unsafe-eval'` script-src widening; no `pulse:default` capability changes.

Per cross-domain rot warnings flagged at Phase 2 merge: (1) fallback message canonical text uses design-extract wording "WebGPU not supported in this browser" (chosen over layouts-extract "in this context" since "browser" is the more user-conventional noun for the WebGPU-context concept); (2) fallback event tracing target uses obs-extract canonical `app.boot.gpu.check` (already in AllowList line 668 from chunk #24) rather than a11y-extract descriptive `viz.webgpu`; (3) explicit CSP-regression test added to the tests list (security supplied invariant; tests own assertion mechanism).

1. **Add `metric.webgpu.frame_duration_ms` to AllowList::production().** Open `pulse-app/src/observability.rs`. After the existing `app.boot.gpu.check` entry (line 668), insert `by_target.insert("metric.webgpu.frame_duration_ms", ["duration_ms", "wgpu_backend", "webview_backend", "timing_method"].iter().copied().collect());`. Add an `allowlist_for_target_resolves_metric_webgpu_frame_duration_ms` test under `mod tests` (mirroring chunk #26's `allowlist_for_target_resolves_*_namespace` pattern) verifying `for_target("metric.webgpu.frame_duration_ms")` returns the entry containing `duration_ms`.

2. **Update existing canvas/ TODO + comment chunk references.** Open `pulse-app/ui/src/canvas/frame-loop.ts`. Update the line-15 TODO from `TODO(chunk #25)` to `TODO(chunk #29)` to accurately reflect that chunk #29 (compute aggregation + frame metric) wires the TauRPC resolver. Open `pulse-app/ui/src/canvas/types.ts`. Update the comment block: `consumed by chunks #25 (WebGPU canvas + WGSL pipeline) and #28 (Halo State Pulse signature element)` → `consumed by chunks #28 (WebGPU canvas + WGSL pipeline) and #31 (Halo State Pulse signature element)`.

3. **Create `webgpu-adapter.ts`.** New file `pulse-app/ui/src/canvas/webgpu-adapter.ts`. Export `requestWebGPUAdapter(): Promise<AdapterResult>` where `AdapterResult = { kind: 'available'; adapter: GPUAdapter; device: GPUDevice; backendKind: 'vulkan'|'metal'|'dx12'|'unknown' } | { kind: 'unavailable'; reason: 'navigator.gpu undefined' | 'requestAdapter returned null' | 'requestDevice failed' }`. Short-circuit on `typeof navigator.gpu === 'undefined'`. On `requestAdapter()` returning null, return `unavailable`. On adapter found but `requestDevice()` throwing, catch + sanitize error to one-liner reason (no stack traces / file paths per security extract). Backend kind from `adapter.info?.backend ?? 'unknown'` (WebGPU spec `GPUAdapterInfo.backend` returns `vulkan|metal|dx12|opengl`). NO TauRPC call here — that's chunk #29.

4. **Create `webgpu-adapter.test.ts`.** New file `pulse-app/ui/src/canvas/webgpu-adapter.test.ts`. Vitest cases: (a) `vi.stubGlobal('navigator', { gpu: undefined })` → `requestWebGPUAdapter()` resolves to `{ kind: 'unavailable', reason: 'navigator.gpu undefined' }`; (b) `vi.stubGlobal('navigator', { gpu: { requestAdapter: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(null) } })` → resolves to `{ kind: 'unavailable', reason: 'requestAdapter returned null' }`; (c) successful adapter + device → `{ kind: 'available', backendKind: 'vulkan' }`; (d) `requestDevice()` throws → caught + returns `{ kind: 'unavailable', reason: 'requestDevice failed' }` with sanitized one-liner.

5. **Create three WGSL shader files.** New files: `pulse-app/ui/src/canvas/shaders/trace-timeline.wgsl`, `pulse-app/ui/src/canvas/shaders/flamegraph.wgsl`, `pulse-app/ui/src/canvas/shaders/metrics-chart.wgsl`. Each is a minimal substrate-shader: vertex stage outputting a normalized triangle / quad covering the canvas; fragment stage reading uniforms (color tokens) and writing fragment color. Color uniforms are read from CSSOM at canvas-init time per a11y extract Constraint "WGSL color literals bypass the design token system and break the contrast harness" — shader source must NOT contain hardcoded `vec4<f32>(0.X, 0.Y, ...)` color literals (only `vec4<f32>(0.0, ...)` for clear-to-transparent / position-output structural literals). Initial substrate is a placeholder render: clear + draw a token-driven background gradient (Earth Blue ↔ Stellar Indigo subtle band per design-system Brand Identity LCH-precedent). Full data binding lands at chunks #34/#35.

6. **Create `render-pipeline.ts`.** New file `pulse-app/ui/src/canvas/render-pipeline.ts`. Export three factory functions: `createTraceTimelinePipeline(device, format)`, `createFlamegraphPipeline(device, format)`, `createMetricsChartPipeline(device, format)`. Each: import the corresponding WGSL source (Vite handles `?raw` suffix for inline-import); `device.createShaderModule({ code })`; `device.createRenderPipeline({ vertex, fragment, primitive })`. Each returns the `GPURenderPipeline` handle. Catch shader-compile errors and re-throw with sanitized one-liner per security extract Constraint "Errors from WebGPU init failure crossing TauRPC MUST be sanitized at `From<...> for AppError` boundary". The actual TauRPC error path lands in chunk #29; chunk #28 just ensures the error message is sanitized at JS-side.

7. **Create `render-pipeline.test.ts`.** New file `pulse-app/ui/src/canvas/render-pipeline.test.ts`. Vitest cases: (a) `createTraceTimelinePipeline()` invokes `device.createShaderModule()` exactly once with a non-empty `code` string; (b) `createTraceTimelinePipeline()` returns the result of `device.createRenderPipeline()`; (c) `createFlamegraphPipeline()` and `createMetricsChartPipeline()` follow same shape with their respective WGSL sources; (d) shader compile error (mocked `createShaderModule` throws) → factory re-throws with sanitized one-liner (no `error.stack` / `error.fileName` passthrough). Mocks `GPUDevice` via `{ createShaderModule: vi.fn().mockReturnValue({}), createRenderPipeline: vi.fn().mockReturnValue({}) }`.

8. **Create `Fallback.tsx`.** New file `pulse-app/ui/src/canvas/Fallback.tsx`. React 19 functional component with no props (or single optional `reason` prop for future debug-display). Renders `
` containing `

` with text "WebGPU not supported in this browser". Inline-style `color: var(--color-text-tertiary)`, `font-family: var(--font-body)`, centered via flexbox. NO color-alone signaling (text + optional telescope icon, never red/yellow indicator without text) per a11y extract.

9. **Create `Fallback.test.tsx`.** New file `pulse-app/ui/src/canvas/Fallback.test.tsx`. Vitest cases: (a) `screen.getByRole('alert')` returns the element; (b) `screen.getByText('WebGPU not supported in this browser')` returns the `

`; (c) the `role="alert"` element has `aria-live="assertive"` attribute; (d) inline-style includes `var(--color-text-tertiary)`.

10. **Create `CanvasContainer.tsx`.** New file `pulse-app/ui/src/canvas/CanvasContainer.tsx`. React 19 functional component accepting `{ ariaLabel: string; mirrorTable?: ReactNode }` props. On mount: `requestWebGPUAdapter()`. Renders `<section role="region" aria-label={ariaLabel}>` outer wrapper (semantic landmark per a11y extract). Inside: chrome-styled `<div>` (`bg: var(--color-inset)`, `border: 1px solid rgba(74,144,226,0.3)`, `borderRadius: var(--radius-md)`, `padding: var(--spacing-md)`). When adapter is `available`, renders `<canvas>` with `position: relative; width: 100%; height: 100%` filling the chrome container, and on `useEffect` initializes device + 3 render pipelines via `createTraceTimelinePipeline`/etc. When adapter is `unavailable`, renders `<Fallback />` instead of canvas. `useReducedMotion()` hook gates the `createFrameLoop({ onFrame, prefersReducedMotion: reducedMotion })` from chunk #15 — when reduced-motion is true, render once via `onReducedMotionFrame`. The `mirrorTable` prop slot is reserved for downstream chunks (#34/#35) to inject a `<table>` DOM mirror for chart text per a11y extract Constraint "equivalent semantic data MUST be exposed via DOM siblings". Chunk #28 itself doesn't populate the slot.

11. **Create `CanvasContainer.test.tsx`.** New file `pulse-app/ui/src/canvas/CanvasContainer.test.tsx`. Vitest cases: (a) renders `<section role="region" aria-label="Telemetry traces chart">` wrapper; (b) WebGPU available (stubbed adapter) → `<canvas>` element present, `<Fallback />` absent; (c) WebGPU unavailable (`vi.stubGlobal('navigator', { gpu: undefined })`) → `<Fallback />` present, `<canvas>` absent; (d) `vi.mock('../hooks/use-reduced-motion', () => ({ useReducedMotion: () => true }))` → render-loop scheduling absent (verify via spy on `requestAnimationFrame`); (e) container chrome inline-style includes `var(--color-inset)` background. Stubs use `vi.stubGlobal('navigator', ...)` with `afterEach` cleanup (auto via test-setup).

Replace the comment `{/* Canvas + downstream surfaces land in chunks #28+ */}` (line 29) with an `import { CanvasContainer } from "./canvas/CanvasContainer";` at the top + `<CanvasContainer ariaLabel="Telemetry visualization canvas" />` inside `<main>`.
