data.head: ### Chunk route#7: "Tracing self-observation harness — tracing + tracing-subscriber JSON + tracing-appender daily + tracing-error + service.name (no OTel SDK)"

body: **Constraints across domains:**

- (security) Self-observation runtime MUST be `tracing` + `tracing-subscriber` JSON + `tracing-appender` daily file sink ONLY — NO OTel SDK linked into the product binary for self-observation; never add an OTLP network exporter pointed at the product's own `:4317`/`:4318` (per security plan §Security Anti-Patterns API "infinite loop" ban + Cross-cutting Patterns Self-observation discipline).

- (security) `AppError::Internal { message }` content surfaced to the webview MUST NOT contain stack traces, Rust struct names, file paths, or library versions; sanitization happens at the `From<thiserror::Error> for AppError` impl. Full chain stays in the internal `tracing-error` SpanTrace (per security plan §Error Handling + §Security Anti-Patterns Logging).

- (security) Logs directory `~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/` MUST inherit OS user permissions (mode 0700 on Unix-like, ACL-restricted to current user on Windows) and the daily-rotation default is "last 7 days on disk" pending obs spec (per security plan §Logging & Monitoring "Access controls" + "Log retention").

- (security) The `service.name` discipline (chunk #7's Layer::with_default_fields including `service_name`, `service_version`, `deployment_environment`) MUST treat `deployment_environment` reads from `CI_RUN_ID`/`GIT_COMMIT_SHA` as untrusted env input — bound them via `serde`/`TryFrom` and never inject the raw env string into a path or shell command (per security plan §Input Validation row "CLI / env var inputs" + §Security Anti-Patterns Code Patterns `tokio::process::Command` ban).

- (tests) The harness `logs` command (test-plan §3 Test Harness Contract — `logs` body) MUST tail JSON-lines emitted by `tracing-subscriber::fmt().json().init()`; chunk #7 subscriber output MUST emit one JSON object per line with required fields `timestamp` (ISO-8601 UTC), `level` (`INFO`/`WARN`/`ERROR` etc.), `target` (crate path), `message`, `fields` (object) so agent parsers `jq 'select(.level == "ERROR")'` and `grep "listening on 127.0.0.1:4317"` keep working (per test-plan §3 Log format example + Bootstrap phase 4 `log-format-bind-with-obs`).

- (tests) Chunk #7 `tracing-appender` daily file sink MUST land at `~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/` (or `$ANDROMEDA_PULSE_LOG_DIR` override) so `logs` command's `cat ~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/*.log` fallback chain resolves (per test-plan §3 Test Harness Contract — `logs` body + §1 5-Command Requirements Command 5 `logs.Location`).
- (tests) Chunks #7-#8 implementation MUST be agent-runnable end-to-end by exit code + structured JSON line (no human verification), per the agent-driven invariants in test-plan §2 Test Strategy.

- (tests) `service.name` / `service.version` / `deployment.environment` default fields (chunk #7 `Layer::with_default_fields([...])`) MUST be present on every JSON line so harness can `jq '.fields.service' logs.jsonl` for cross-test attribution (per test-plan §3 Bootstrap phase 4).

- (obs) Self-observation runtime MUST be `tracing` 0.1 + `tracing-subscriber` 0.3 (JSON formatter) + `tracing-appender` 0.2 (daily-rolling, non-blocking writer) + `tracing-error` 0.2 (SpanTrace) — and ONLY these crates. NO OTel SDK linked into the self-runtime; the file-sink JSON line IS the agent-readable surface (per obs-plan §1 Telemetry surfaces + §3 Tracing init "Why this approach" + §3 opening paragraph).

- (obs) Init order MUST be: (1) load env vars + `EnvFilter::from_env("ANDROMEDA_PULSE_LOG_LEVEL")` with fallback `RUST_LOG`; (2) build `tracing_subscriber::registry()` composing stderr layer + non-blocking file appender layer + `ErrorLayer::default()`; (3) install panic hook calling `tracing::error!(target: "app.panic.fatal", ...)` with `SpanTrace::capture()`; (4) spawn Tauri app + bind OTLP receivers — all init before HTTP/gRPC bind (per obs-plan §3 Tracing init "Init order" + §7 Panic hook).

- (obs) Service identity MUST be set as default subscriber fields once at init via `tracing_subscriber::fmt::Layer::with_default_fields([service.name, service.version, deployment.environment])`: `service.name = "com.andromeda.pulse"` (compile-time bundle id), `service.version = env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")`, `deployment.environment = "production"` hardcoded for desktop bundle (per obs-plan §3 Service identity).

- (obs) CI runs MUST extend default subscriber fields with `ci.run.id` (`$GITHUB_RUN_ID`) and `git.commit.sha` (`$GITHUB_SHA`); `deployment.environment` becomes `"dev"` for branch builds, `"staging"` for alpha/beta, `"production"` for release tags (per obs-plan §9 CI-specific default fields).

- (obs) Log file path MUST be `~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/agent-latest.jsonl` (Linux canonical) with per-platform resolution (`%APPDATA%\Andromeda Pulse\logs\` Windows; `~/Library/Application Support/com.andromeda.pulse/logs/` macOS) configurable via `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR`; daily rotation via `tracing_appender::rolling::daily(...)` (per obs-plan §3 Log file location).

- (obs) Every JSON log line MUST emit the binding-contract schema `{timestamp, level, target, message, fields}` verbatim (the schema is owned by the tests harness contract; obs aligns to tests, not vice versa) (per obs-plan §3 Log format JSON schema + §6 Required fields).

- (obs) For mcp-server sidecar contexts, stderr MUST be forced JSON (no TTY check) — stdout is reserved for JSON-RPC 2.0 framing; any accidental stdout write corrupts the protocol (per obs-plan §3 Logging stack + §11 Universal anti-patterns "rmcp stdio sidecar"). Wiring may be conditional in chunk #7 with the actual sidecar feature gate landing later (route#39); chunk #7 must not block this path.

- (obs) Panic hook MUST emit one structured `tracing::error!(target: "app.panic.fatal", ...)` line with `panic_message`, `location`, `spantrace = ?SpanTrace::capture()`; if Sentry is enabled, hook ALSO calls `sentry::capture_message(...)` after the tracing line — both surfaces capture (per obs-plan §7 Panic hook + §10 Zero unlogged panics).

- (a11y) A11y violation JSON emissions MUST be aligned to the obs Section 6 structured-log format produced by the chunk #7 `tracing-subscriber` JSON layer; required fields are `timestamp` (RFC 3339) / `level` ("ERROR" for WCAG violations) / `target` ("a11y::assertion") / `message` / `fields.{wcag_criterion, violation_type, severity, surface, selector, remediation, tool, tool_result_id}` (per a11y plan §3 Structured Violation JSON Schema).

- (a11y) A11y violation JSON emissions MUST tag with `service.name = "com.andromeda.pulse"` (compile-time constant per Tauri bundle identifier) and `deployment.environment = "production"` as resource attributes baked into chunk #7's `Layer::with_default_fields(...)` discipline (per a11y plan §1 Service Identity Tagging column + §9 CI-specific resource attributes).

- (a11y) A11y violation JSON emissions MUST also tag with `ci.run.id` from `$GITHUB_RUN_ID` and `git.commit.sha` from `$GITHUB_SHA` when set, matching chunk #7's "reading workflow env (CI_RUN_ID, GIT_COMMIT_SHA) when present" discipline (per a11y plan §9 CI-specific resource attributes).

- (a11y) A11y violation JSON emissions MUST have machine-parseable JSON output usable by GitHub Actions artifact upload + per-PR `jq`-style regression diff; chunk #7's daily file sink is the destination per the canonical a11y artifact paths (per a11y plan §3 CI integration + §9 Per-pipeline-stage a11y artifacts).

- (arch) Self-observation runtime is `tracing` + `tracing-subscriber` JSON + `tracing-appender` daily file sink only — NO OTel SDK linked; an OTLP network exporter pointed at the product's own `:4317`/`:4318` is forbidden by construction (per architecture.md §Established Decisions [Self-Observation] + §Cross-cutting Patterns "Self-observation discipline").

- (arch) Daily file sink target on every platform is the resolved `<data_dir>/logs/` subpath (Linux `~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/`, macOS `~/Library/Application Support/com.andromeda.pulse/logs/`, Windows `%APPDATA%\andromeda-pulse\logs\`); `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` overrides the resolved root (per architecture.md §Occupied Resources Filesystem locations).

- (arch) Log-level filter precedence MUST honor `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_LOG_LEVEL` (`trace|debug|info|warn|error`) with `RUST_LOG` as fallback (per architecture.md §Occupied Resources Environment variables) — no new env var beyond this reserved set may be introduced by chunk #7 or #8 without scope-arch.

- (arch) Subscriber default fields MUST encode the `service.name` / `service.version` / `deployment_environment` envelope identity that mirrors the `app_info` standard contract (`name`, `version`, `rust_version`, `tauri_version`, `features`, `build_profile`) — the introspection envelope is the canonical service identity (per architecture.md §Standard Contracts `app_info` command).

- (arch) Tracing harness code lives within the `pulse-app` binary (it is the runtime owner) and any reusable scrubber/Layer types live in a workspace library crate consumed by `pulse-app`; no library crate may depend on `pulse-app` (per architecture.md §Cross-cutting Patterns "Module dependency direction").

- (arch) Workspace crate names are LOCKED — chunks #7-#8 may NOT introduce a new crate named outside the reserved set `ingest, buffer, viz, ui-bridge, snapshot, workspace-detector, plugins, mcp-server, pulse-app, xtask` (per architecture.md §Occupied Resources Cargo workspace crate names).
**Patterns to follow:**

- (security) Structured (JSON) `tracing` + `tracing-subscriber` with redaction Layer is the canonical Rust-ecosystem pairing the security plan calls out — no custom log envelope (per security plan §Logging & Monitoring "Log format").
- (tests) Co-located unit tests under `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { … }` in the crate that owns the subscriber + scrubber code (per test-plan §4 Unit Test Strategy `Test file location`).

- (tests) `cargo-nextest` 0.9.x with `--profile ci` for unit + integration test invocation (per test-plan §3 Test Harness Contract — `run` body); chunks #7-#8 are exercised under the same `cargo nextest run --workspace` invocation already wired in chunk #5.

- (tests) Per-test isolation via `tempfile::TempDir` for any test that exercises `tracing-appender` daily file sink output; `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR=$TMPDIR/test-$$` keeps the daily file sink off the developer's real `~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/` (per test-plan §3 Test data bootstrap + §7 Test Data & Fixtures).

- (obs) **Init body sketch (≤5 lines)** from obs-plan §3 Tracing init: `let (file_writer, _guard) = tracing_appender::non_blocking(rolling::daily(log_dir, "agent-latest.jsonl")); tracing_subscriber::registry().with(fmt::layer().json().with_writer(file_writer)).with(EnvFilter::from_env("ANDROMEDA_PULSE_LOG_LEVEL")).with(ErrorLayer::default()).init(); std::panic::set_hook(Box::new(panic_to_tracing_error));` — keep init local + minimal; the `_guard` is the non-blocking writer flush guard and MUST be held for the lifetime of the app (per obs-plan §3 Tracing init body sketch).

- (a11y) Resource-attribute discipline: chunk #7's `Layer::with_default_fields([service_name, service_version, deployment_environment, ci.run.id, git.commit.sha])` is the canonical mechanism that downstream a11y violation JSON emissions inherit; design chunk #7 so the same Layer construction can be reused unchanged for the future `target = "a11y::assertion"` events (per a11y plan §9 CI-specific resource attributes).

- (a11y) Log file-sink layout: a11y CI emits `a11y-axe-core-results.jsonl` / `a11y-lighthouse-results.json` / `a11y-pa11y-results.json` / `a11y-keyboard-focus-results.jsonl` / `a11y-violations-summary.json` to `~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/`; chunk #7's `tracing-appender` daily sink targeting the same logs directory is the canonical destination (per a11y plan §3 A11y testing tool pick CI integration).

- (arch) Each library crate exposes a public contract module (the only `pub` surface), `pub(crate)` internals, `thiserror`-derived error enum (per architecture.md §Project Intent "Template patterns" + §Conventions "Module visibility discipline"); a self-observation Layer / scrubber crate follows the same shape.

- (arch) Standard Contracts `app_info` envelope is the canonical service-identity source — emit subscriber default-fields keyed off the same identity columns (`name`, `version`, `rust_version`, `tauri_version`, `features`, `build_profile`) so log lines and IPC introspection agree (per architecture.md §Standard Contracts).

- (arch) Existing `pulse-app/src/main.rs` already wires a basic JSON subscriber via chunk #4; chunk #7 extends that subscriber stack via `Layer` composition rather than replacing it (per route §3 phase-5 starting point note + architecture.md §Established Decisions [Error Handling Pattern]).
**Anti-patterns to avoid:**

- (security) NEVER instrument the product's own telemetry with an OTLP network exporter pointed at the product's own `:4317`/`:4318` ports — infinite loop + bypasses loopback authorization model (per security plan §Security Anti-Patterns API "Self-observation discipline" + §Universal CLAUDE.md invariant).

- (tests) NEVER monkey-patch the tracing subscriber at runtime (`tracing::subscriber::set_global_default` mid-test without cleanup) — use constructor injection: register the scrubber Layer through a builder-style API and inject test instances per `#[fixture]` (per test-plan §11 Mocking).

- (tests) NEVER use `unwrap()` in subscriber-init tests without context — chunk #7 init failure paths must `expect("subscriber init must succeed when no other subscriber set")` (per test-plan §11 Unit).

- (tests) NEVER use real `std::time::Instant::now()` / `chrono::Utc::now()` for daily-rotation tests — use `tokio::time::pause()` to advance across midnight rollover deterministically (per test-plan §11 Universal).

- (obs) NEVER link an OTel SDK (`opentelemetry`, `opentelemetry-sdk`, `opentelemetry-otlp`, `opentelemetry-stdout`) into the self-observation runtime — re-introduces the recursion concern this project explicitly chose to eliminate by construction (per obs-plan §11 Universal anti-patterns + §12 Decisions Log 2026-05-02 pivot).

- (obs) NEVER write to stdout from any subsystem when running as the rmcp stdio sidecar — stdout is reserved for JSON-RPC 2.0 framing; any accidental `println!` / `dbg!` / library stdout write corrupts the protocol (per obs-plan §11 Universal anti-patterns).

- (obs) NEVER hardcode service identity (`service.name = "myapp"` literal) — use compile-time `env!()` / Tauri bundle id with a single source of truth registered as a default subscriber field (per obs-plan §11 Universal anti-patterns).
- (obs) NEVER use unstructured stderr text or multi-line stack traces — always JSON-per-line; use `SpanTrace` (tracing-error) instead of raw backtrace (per obs-plan §11 Logs).

- (obs) NEVER hold a `tracing::Span` guard across `.await` without `.in_current_span()` — span context bleeds into unrelated tokio tasks, breaking trace_id correlation (per obs-plan §11 Spans / Traces).

- (a11y) NEVER ship a chunk #7 logger configuration that produces non-JSON output for `target = "a11y::assertion"` events — non-JSON breaks the per-PR `jq`-style regression diff at the CI gate (per a11y plan §3 CI integration + §11 Universal).

- (a11y) NEVER add a soft / warning-only level for a11y violations in chunk #7's Layer filter — WCAG violations emit at `level = "ERROR"` per the a11y plan schema (per a11y plan §11 CI + §3 Structured violation JSON schema `level` field).

- (arch) DO NOT link the OpenTelemetry SDK into the product binary; DO NOT point any OTLP network exporter at the product's own ports — bypasses self-observation invariant (per architecture.md §Established Decisions [Self-Observation]).

- (arch) DO NOT introduce a new crate name outside the reserved set; DO NOT make a library crate depend on `pulse-app` (per architecture.md §Occupied Resources Cargo workspace crate names + §Cross-cutting Patterns "Module dependency direction").

- (arch) DO NOT add a new `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_*` env var beyond the reserved set in §Occupied Resources for chunks #7-#8; settings belong either in `config.toml` (under existing precedence) or behind a Cargo feature flag (per architecture.md §Occupied Resources Environment variables).
**Contract bindings:**

- **obs ↔ tests (harness binding)**: the JSON log schema `{timestamp, level, target, message, fields}` is owned by the tests harness contract; obs-plan §3 explicitly states "obs aligns to tests, not vice versa". Chunk #7 is the producer; tests' 5-command discipline + status endpoint readers are the consumers. Default subscriber fields MUST appear on every line.

- **obs ↔ tests (heartbeat ticks)**: chunk #7 lays the subscriber; the actual `{module}.tick` events are emitted by chunk #9 (next chunk). Chunk #7 must therefore not block heartbeat-event emission and must be ready to receive `tracing::info!(target: "{module}.tick", ...)` lines from chunk #9 onwards.

- **obs ↔ frontend (web-vitals + WebGPU bridge)**: frontend telemetry flows through TauRPC `telemetry.frontend.record_*` commands → backend `tracing::info!(target: "metric.{name}", ...)` events. Chunk #7 must register the JSON formatter on the same subscriber so backend bridge events land alongside backend events.

- **a11y ↔ obs (chunk #7)**: a11y violation JSON schema is a binding contract on top of obs Section 6 structured-log format; chunk #7 owns the underlying tracing-subscriber JSON Layer + tracing-appender daily sink + with_default_fields discipline; a11y owns the `target = "a11y::assertion"` event shape + required fields.

- **a11y ↔ tests (downstream binding)**: chunk #7's daily-file sink + JSON Layer is the substrate the future a11y CI gate (route#46) will consume — getting the resource-attribute + JSON envelope right at chunk #7 means immediately schema-conformant artifacts later.

- **arch ↔ obs**: chunk #7's subscriber MUST encode the `app_info` standard-contract identity fields as default-fields on every log line so obs's machine-parseable tracing JSON and the IPC introspection envelope agree on service identity (architecture.md §Standard Contracts).
- **arch ↔ tests**: log sink subpath `<data_dir>/logs/` is read by the xtask 5-command harness `cargo xtask logs` action (chunk #4 binding) — the path layout is fixed by §Occupied Resources.

- **security ↔ arch (self-observation)**: arch's "no OTel SDK in self-runtime" Established Decision is enforced by chunk #7's library choice (`tracing` ecosystem only). If chunk #7 ever adds `opentelemetry-sdk` or `opentelemetry-otlp`, that's the regression the security plan §Security Anti-Patterns API ban catches at review.
**Acceptance criteria contributions:**

- (security) `grep -nE "opentelemetry-sdk|opentelemetry-otlp|opentelemetry-stdout" pulse-app/Cargo.toml crates/*/Cargo.toml` returns empty for chunks #7 and #8 deliverables — no OTel SDK linked into self-observation runtime (per §Security Anti-Patterns API + §Universal Self-observation discipline).

- (security) `AppError::Internal { message }` rendering in the JSON log + webview surface contains no `at /home/...`, no `at C:\\...`, no `panicked at 'src/...'`, no Rust struct path (`crates::ingest::...`), and no library version string; a synthetic error fixture exercises the `From<thiserror>` boundary (per §Error Handling "External responses" + §Security Anti-Patterns Logging).

- (security) `~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/` is created with mode 0700 on Unix-like and current-user-only ACL on Windows by the `tracing-appender` daily sink initializer; a startup-time test asserts the resolved permissions (per §Logging & Monitoring "Access controls").

- (security) `gitleaks` pre-commit + per-PR continues to pass against the new `tracing-error`/PII-scrubber source files; `.gitignore` continues to cover `*.p12`/`*.pem`/`*.cer`/`.env*`/`*.key`/`~/.tauri/*.key` (per §Secret Management + §Security Anti-Patterns Secrets — chunks 5-6 wired this; chunks 7-8 must not regress).

- (tests) `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` passes with new chunk #7 / #8 unit tests included; final-line regex `test result: ok. ([0-9]+) passed` matches per test-plan §3 `run.Output format`.

- (tests) `bash scripts/agent-run.sh logs` (or PowerShell equivalent) returns at least one JSON line with required fields `timestamp` / `level` / `target` / `message` / `fields` after a boot, parseable by `jq 'select(.level == "INFO") | .target' logs/*.log` per test-plan §3 Log format.

- (tests) Coverage gate met for new code: `cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --lcov --output-path lcov.info --summary-only` reports ≥ 75% line / ≥ 70% branch / ≥ 85% function for chunks #7-#8 modules per test-plan §10 Quality Gates Standard tier.

- (tests) Zero-flake discipline observed: chunks #7-#8 tests run without retries; daily-rotation test uses `tokio::time::pause()` + `advance(Duration::from_secs(86_500))` for deterministic rollover (per test-plan §10 + §11 Universal).

- (tests) Subscriber init is idempotent under test repetition: `#[fixture]` setup re-uses or re-creates a non-global subscriber per test (constructor-injected, not `set_global_default`) — verified by running the chunk #7 test module twice in a row in nextest (per test-plan §11 Mocking).

- (obs) Crate set on chunk #7: `tracing` 0.1, `tracing-subscriber` 0.3 with `json` + `env-filter` features, `tracing-appender` 0.2, `tracing-error` 0.2 are pinned in workspace `Cargo.toml`; verify via `cargo tree -p pulse-app -e features | grep -E '^(tracing|tracing-subscriber|tracing-appender|tracing-error) '` lists all four crates exactly once and zero `opentelemetry*` crates appear.

- (obs) Init order verified: subscriber + panic hook installed BEFORE any `tonic` / `axum` server bind in `pulse-app/src/main.rs` — boot run with `cargo xtask agent-run` produces a JSON log line BEFORE the first ingest receiver readiness log line (per obs-plan §3 Tracing init order).

- (obs) JSON log schema verified: every line in `~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/agent-latest.jsonl` parses as JSON with all five required keys; verify via `jq -e 'has("timestamp") and has("level") and has("target") and has("message") and has("fields")' agent-latest.jsonl` returns true for every line (per obs-plan §3 Log format JSON schema + §6 Required fields).

- (obs) Default subscriber fields present: every emitted JSON line carries `fields.service.name == "com.andromeda.pulse"`, `fields.service.version == <CARGO_PKG_VERSION>`, `fields.deployment.environment == "production"` (or `"dev"` / `"staging"` in CI per env override) (per obs-plan §3 Service identity).

- (obs) Log file path resolves correctly per platform: file written to `%APPDATA%\Andromeda Pulse\logs\agent-latest.jsonl` on Windows / `~/Library/Application Support/com.andromeda.pulse/logs/agent-latest.jsonl` on macOS / `~/.local/share/com.andromeda.pulse/logs/agent-latest.jsonl` on Linux when `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` is unset, and to `<DATA_DIR>/logs/agent-latest.jsonl` when set (per obs-plan §3 Log file location).

- (obs) `EnvFilter` honors `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_LOG_LEVEL` with `RUST_LOG` fallback: setting `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_LOG_LEVEL=debug` produces `level: "DEBUG"` lines that are absent under default `info` filter (per obs-plan §3 Tracing init step 1).

title: Chunk route#8: "PII scrubbing rules wire — span attribute scrubber + log formatter Layer + Sentry before_send pattern (if enabled)"

data.head: ### Chunk route#8: "PII scrubbing rules wire — span attribute scrubber + log formatter Layer + Sentry before_send pattern (if enabled)"

body: **Constraints across domains:**

- (security) Field redaction MUST be applied at the `tracing-subscriber` layer, not at log call sites (per security plan §Logging & Monitoring "Log format" — redaction at subscriber layer is the single enforcement point).

- (security) The NEVER-log list is binding for every `tracing` event the harness emits: OTLP attribute values, span/log/metric content payloads, snapshot file contents, clipboard contents, MCP tool response bodies, full plugin file paths (basename of canonicalized path only), DuckDB query parameter values, Tauri updater download URL query strings, and anything matching the §Secret Management "What counts as secret" list (per security plan §Logging & Monitoring "What NEVER to log" + §Security Anti-Patterns Logging).

- (security) If a Sentry-style `before_send` pattern is wired (currently no Sentry dep present, so no-op skeleton), the same NEVER-log list MUST be enforced inside `before_send` before any payload leaves the process boundary, and Sentry transmission MUST require explicit user opt-in per local-first principle (per security plan §Error Handling "Error reporting integration").

- (tests) Chunk #8 PII scrubber MUST guarantee that no OTLP attribute values, snapshot file contents, clipboard contents, MCP response bodies, plugin paths, or DuckDB query parameter values appear in any tracing output line — these are the universal logging anti-patterns the harness's `! grep 'query parameters:' test.log` data-leakage assertion is designed to catch (per test-plan §11 Universal anti-pattern + §3 Log format `Data leakage check`).

- (tests) Sentry `before_send` (chunk #8 conditional) — if no Sentry dep is present in workspace, the integration MUST be a no-op skeleton; tests MUST NOT fail when Sentry is absent (per test-plan §2 agent-runnable invariants).

- (obs) PII scrubbing MUST be applied at multiple layers (defense-in-depth): (a) at source via `#[tracing::instrument(skip(...))]` parameter list + explicit `fields(...)` allowlist, (b) at subscriber Layer via custom `tracing-subscriber` Layer iterating emitted event fields with per-module allowlist before serialization, (c) at Sentry boundary via `before_send` callback (only if Sentry enabled) — all three layers MUST agree on the same scrubbing rules (per obs-plan §8 Integration points + §11 PII Scrubbing).

- (obs) Default-deny scrubbing posture: unknown attribute types redacted by default; only the per-module allowlist (obs-plan §8) is permitted in logs — `ingest`: `{span_count, service}`; `buffer`: `{rows_ingested, eviction_count, memory_bytes, retention_window_seconds}`; `plugin`: `{plugin_name, plugin_path_basename, capability_name, error_msg, duration_ms}`; `snapshot`: `{token_budget, token_count_actual, dedup_count, time_range_start, time_range_end}`; `viz`: `{query_id, param_count, row_count, latency_ms}`; `workspace-detector`: `{workspace.root_path, workspace.project_name, vcs_type, vcs_root, marker_present, detection_latency_ms}`; `ui-bridge`: `{method_name, argument_digest, result_type, latency_ms}`; `mcp-server`: `{method, result_type, result_count, feature_flag_enabled, duration_ms}` — explicitly NOT `result_content` (per obs-plan §8 Default-deny posture).

- (obs) Sentry integration is opt-in / default OFF: enabled only when `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_SENTRY_DSN` env var is non-empty; empty/unset = Sentry no-op. If enabled, `before_send` MUST scrub OTLP request payloads, file-path stack frames beyond project root, Rust struct names / library versions, plugin paths (basename only), DuckDB query parameters (query_id + param_count only), and explicitly check event source so MCP response bodies are never captured (per obs-plan §7 Default state + `before_send` scrubbing pattern).

- (a11y) Optional violation JSON extension fields `token_name` (e.g., `--color-text-primary`), `measured_value` / `required_value` (numeric contrast ratios), `affected_component` (React component / layout type) MUST flow through chunk #8's PII scrubbing log formatter Layer unscrubbed — these are non-PII a11y diagnostic fields (per a11y plan §3 Structured violation JSON schema Extensions).

- (arch) Sentry `before_send` pattern is conditional — if a Sentry path is wired, the dependency MUST sit behind a Cargo feature flag in `kebab-case` (off by default), preserving small-binary baseline (per architecture.md §Conventions "Feature flags" + §Cross-cutting Patterns "Feature-gate hygiene"). Lacking a Sentry feature decision in arch today, a no-op skeleton is acceptable.

- (arch) Any toggle introduced by chunk #7 or #8 (e.g., `pii_scrub_enabled`, `log_format`) MUST follow layered config precedence: process env vars (`ANDROMEDA_PULSE_*`) > `~/.andromeda-pulse/config.toml` > built-in defaults (per architecture.md §Cross-cutting Patterns "Config management").

- (arch) Scrubber input domain — span attribute values, log message bodies, and any scrubber-emitted text crossing the IPC bridge — must remain `serde::Serialize` (per architecture.md §Cross-cutting Patterns "Cross-bridge data shape"); scrubber output written to `AppError::Internal { message }` shape MUST be a sanitized one-liner (per architecture.md §Conventions "Error response schema (Tauri IPC)").
**Patterns to follow:**

- (security) Snapshot/clipboard/MCP-tool-response hygiene model: user-facing warning at the medium boundary instead of attempted attribute-value sanitization (the data is user-instrumented). Apply the same posture to log redaction — redact known-secret-class fields at the Layer; do NOT attempt to scan free-form OTLP attribute values for secrets at log time (per security plan §Logging & Monitoring "Snapshot / clipboard / MCP-tool-response hygiene").

- (security) The plugin-path basename pattern (canonicalize via `strict-path`, log basename only) is the existing template for any chunk that emits paths into log fields (per security plan §Bootstrap phases + §Security Anti-Patterns Logging "basename of canonicalized path only").

- (security) DuckDB query logging shape: `query_id` + `param_count` + `param_types` only — never the parameter values. The PII scrubber Layer should treat any field name matching `*query_param*`, `*db_param*`, or DuckDB-specific `?`-bind metadata as drop-class fields by default (per security plan §Security Anti-Patterns Logging + §Input Validation row "DuckDB query parameters").

- (security) `AppError`-shaped error sanitization at boundary: existing `From` impls strip stack/path/version content; the `tracing-error` SpanTrace captures the unsanitized chain in the internal log only — same Layer split is the model for the PII scrubber (sanitize on emit, retain raw in-memory only if absolutely needed, never persist to disk) (per security plan §Error Handling "Internal logging").
- (tests) `rstest` 0.26.1 fixtures + builder factories for any synthetic span / log-line generator the scrubber test needs (per test-plan §4 Unit Test Strategy + §7 Test Data & Fixtures).

- (tests) Round-trip JSON-line assertion pattern: scrubbed `tracing` event → JSON line → `serde_json::from_str` → assert field absence/presence (favor structured assertions over regex when checking PII redaction); regex (`! grep -E '(password|token|api_key|trace_id=[0-9a-f]{32})'`) is the harness-level smoke check, structured assertion is the unit-test discipline.

- (obs) **Source-level scrubbing pattern**: every handler / boundary fn carrying potential PII is annotated `#[tracing::instrument(skip(<sensitive_param>...), fields(<allowlist>...))]` so sensitive parameters never enter the span — first line of defense (per obs-plan §8 Integration points "At source").

- (obs) **Subscriber Layer scrubbing pattern (defense-in-depth)**: custom `tracing-subscriber` Layer wrapping the JSON formatter; iterates emitted event fields and redacts based on the per-module allowlist — applied before serialization to file (per obs-plan §8 Integration points "At subscriber Layer").

- (obs) **Sentry `before_send` callback shape** (only when Sentry enabled): `before_send: Box::new(|event| { scrub_otlp_payloads(&event); scrub_file_paths(&event); scrub_query_params(&event); event })` (sentry-tauri 0.5 callback signature) (per obs-plan §7 `before_send` scrubbing pattern).

- (obs) **Plugin path basename extraction**: `path.file_name().and_then(|s| s.to_str())` before any `tracing::info!` field emission — never log the full canonicalized path (per obs-plan §8 Plugin file paths row).

- (obs) **DuckDB query anonymization**: emit `query_id: "q_abc123"` + `param_count: 2` + `param_types: ["string", "timestamp"]`; never emit raw `params` list or query text (per obs-plan §8 DuckDB query parameters row + Section 5 Vector 5).

- (obs) **MCP response redaction**: emit `result_type: "traces"` + `result_count: 42` only; explicitly check span event type before any `result_content` field emission would be possible (per obs-plan §8 MCP response bodies row + Section 5 Vector 4).

- (obs) **Secret-named env var redaction**: env-var names matching `*_SECRET`, `*_TOKEN`, `*_KEY` redacted by naming convention even if otherwise low-classification (per obs-plan §8 Environment variables row).

- (a11y) Field naming convention alignment: chunk #8's PII scrubber field rules MUST treat the a11y violation JSON Required-fields list (§3) as a non-redacted allowlist; do NOT scrub `wcag_criterion` / `violation_type` / `severity` / `surface` / `selector` / `remediation` / `tool` / `tool_result_id` / `token_name` / `measured_value` / `required_value` / `affected_component` (per a11y plan §3 Structured Violation JSON Schema canonical fields list).

- (arch) Cargo features are `kebab-case` with minimal defaults — examples in arch are `mcp-server`, `otap-ingest` (per architecture.md §Conventions "Feature flags"); a Sentry path under chunk #8 follows that shape (e.g., `sentry-redaction`, off by default).
**Anti-patterns to avoid:**

- (security) NEVER log raw OTLP attribute values, span/log/metric content payloads, snapshot file contents, clipboard contents, MCP tool response bodies, full plugin file paths, or DuckDB query parameter values — incidentally captured secrets from instrumented host applications. Even debug-level emissions count (per security plan §Security Anti-Patterns Logging — top item, no severity carve-out).

- (security) NEVER rely on call-site discipline ("just don't log secrets") instead of subscriber-layer redaction — the security plan explicitly mandates "Field redaction is applied at the subscriber layer, not at log call sites" because per-call-site discipline regresses the moment a new module forgets the rule (per security plan §Logging & Monitoring "Log format").

- (tests) NEVER expose secrets in test output (log PII, raw OTLP payloads with credentials) — chunks #7-#8 tests MUST sanitize fixtures so test failure dumps do not leak (per test-plan §11 Universal "NEVER expose secrets in test output").
- (tests) NEVER serialize the scrubber's allow/deny rules into log files — scrubber config is test infrastructure only (per test-plan §11 Mocking).
- (obs) NEVER scrub only at sink stage — scrub at processor stage so failures upstream don't leak; rules MUST live at multiple layers, not one location (per obs-plan §11 PII Scrubbing).
- (obs) NEVER ship a real Sentry DSN in dev / committed to repo; default Sentry off; `before_send` scrubbing required when enabled (per obs-plan §11 Error Reporting + §7 Default state).

- (obs) NEVER include raw OTLP attributes, query parameters, plugin full paths, MCP response bodies, AppError stack traces with Rust struct names, or canonicalized file paths in logs (Vectors 1–6) (per obs-plan §11 Spans / Traces + Logs).

- (a11y) NEVER let chunk #8's PII scrubber over-redact a11y violation JSON `selector` (DOM selector path like `.settings-modal form input[type='text']`) or `remediation` (plain-language fix referencing design tokens like `--color-text-primary`) — these are essential WCAG diagnostic fields, not PII; over-redaction silently breaks a11y CI gate (per a11y plan §3 Structured Violation JSON Schema Required fields list, specifically `selector` and `remediation` rows).

- (arch) DO NOT widen Sentry / scrubber types to `pub use` re-exports across crate boundaries beyond each crate's explicit contract module (per architecture.md §Conventions "Module visibility discipline").
**Contract bindings:**

- **security ↔ obs (PII scrubbing)**: PII scrubbing rules cross-cut. Security owns the NEVER-log list (snapshot files / clipboard / MCP responses / OTLP attribute values / plugin paths / DuckDB params / updater URL query strings); obs owns the `tracing` Layer wiring + field-name conventions. Chunk #8 is the wire-up point — security's NEVER-log list MUST be the authoritative input to the redaction Layer's drop-list, not a parallel obs-defined list.

- **security ↔ tests**: CI security gate ties to test harness — secret-scanning runs pre-commit + per-PR (already wired in chunks 5-6) and any new Sentry/PII fixture data MUST contain no real secrets (test plan owns no-real-PII-in-fixtures rule; security plan §Security Anti-Patterns Secrets bans real `.env`/`*.key`/`*.pem` commits to git).

- **tests ↔ security (PII regression)**: tests for chunk #8 must fail when any of these vectors leak; the harness `! grep 'query parameters:' test.log` data-leakage assertion is the canonical regression check (test-plan §3 Log format `Data leakage check`).

- **obs ↔ security (PII vectors)**: chunk #8 is the obs-side instantiation of security plan §Logging Vectors 1–6 (raw OTLP attribute values, AppError stack traces, plugin file paths, MCP response bodies, DuckDB query parameters, path env var canonicalization). Security plan defines WHAT must never be logged; chunk #8 implements WHERE the scrubbing happens.

- **obs ↔ security (error sanitization)**: the `AppError` enum sanitization at the IPC bridge (route#21 in epoch 4) consumes `tracing-error` SpanTrace from chunk #7; chunk #7 must install `ErrorLayer::default()` so SpanTrace is captured at the bridge boundary later.

- **a11y ↔ obs (chunk #8)**: PII scrubbing rules wire (chunk #8) MUST treat the a11y violation JSON Required-fields list (§3) + Extensions list (§3) as a non-redacted allowlist — `wcag_criterion`, `violation_type`, `severity`, `surface`, `selector`, `remediation`, `tool`, `tool_result_id`, `token_name`, `measured_value`, `required_value`, `affected_component` flow through unscrubbed.

- **arch ↔ security (AppError sanitization)**: chunk #8's scrubber Layer is the upstream-of-IPC redaction step that feeds `AppError::Internal { message }` sanitization at the TauRPC bridge — both sides ensure no stack traces / file paths / library versions / Rust struct names leak across the bridge.
**Acceptance criteria contributions:**

- (security) The redaction Layer drops or replaces every field name matching the NEVER-log classes (`otlp.attr.*`, `snapshot.body`, `snapshot.path` non-basename, `clipboard.contents`, `mcp.response.body`, `plugin.path` non-basename, `duckdb.param.value*`, `updater.url.query*`); a unit test asserts a synthetic event carrying each class is rendered without the sensitive value before the JSON Layer writes to disk (per security plan §Logging & Monitoring NEVER-log list + §Security Anti-Patterns Logging).

- (security) If a Sentry `before_send` skeleton is added in chunk #8, the function MUST run the same redaction Layer ruleset and a unit test asserts a synthetic Sentry event carrying every NEVER-log class is dropped or scrubbed before transmission; if Sentry is not enabled (the current state), the no-op skeleton MUST be `cfg(feature = "sentry")`-gated so the dep is not in the default build graph (per §Error Handling "Error reporting integration" + §Dependency Security default-features-minimal pattern).

- (tests) Data-leakage smoke check passes on a fixture-driven synthetic ingest run: `! grep -E '(password|token|api_key|secret|bearer )' ~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/*.log` exits 0 — chunk #8 scrubber unit tests cover the universal logging anti-pattern vectors (per test-plan §11 Universal + §3 Log format Data leakage check).

- (obs) PII scrubbing — source layer (chunk #8): every `#[tracing::instrument]` annotation in repo carrying potential PII params has an explicit `skip(...)` list excluding raw OTLP attribute dicts, query params, plugin file paths, MCP response bodies, AppError sources; verified by lint pass or grep convention check that flags `instrument(skip_all)` on boundary fns and requires explicit `fields(...)` allowlist (per obs-plan §8 Integration points "At source").

- (obs) PII scrubbing — subscriber Layer (chunk #8): a custom `tracing-subscriber` Layer is registered between the JSON formatter and the file appender; iterates emitted event fields and redacts any not in the per-module allowlist before serialization. Negative test: emit a `tracing::info!(target: "ingest", message = "test", attribute_value = "secret123")` and verify `secret123` does NOT appear in `agent-latest.jsonl` (per obs-plan §8 Default-deny posture + §11 PII Scrubbing).

- (obs) PII scrubbing — Sentry off path (chunk #8): with `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_SENTRY_DSN` unset, no `sentry-rust` or `sentry-tauri` calls are made, no network egress occurs to Sentry hosts, and `cargo audit` / `cargo deny check` do not require Sentry crate auditing for the default build profile (per obs-plan §7 Default state).

- (obs) PII scrubbing — Sentry on path (chunk #8 skeleton): if `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_SENTRY_DSN` is set, the `before_send` callback is installed and scrubs OTLP payloads, file paths beyond project root, query parameters, and explicitly checks event source so MCP response bodies (target prefix `mcp.tools.call.response`) never reach the Sentry transport. Scaffold may be a no-op skeleton at chunk #8 if Sentry crate is not yet a workspace dependency — but the `before_send` shape MUST be wired so adding the dep later is a single-line activation (per obs-plan §7 `before_send` scrubbing pattern + §11 Error Reporting).

- (obs) Plugin path basename helper exists (chunk #8): a public helper `fn log_basename(path: &Path) -> Option<&str>` (or equivalent) is available to all crates that emit plugin path fields; calling it on `/home/user/.andromeda-pulse/plugins/my-plugin.wasm` returns `"my-plugin.wasm"` and never the full path (per obs-plan §8 Plugin file paths + §11 Spans / Traces "Vector 3").

- (a11y) Chunk #8's PII scrubber, when applied to a synthetic a11y violation event with `fields.selector = ".settings-modal form input[type='text']"` and `fields.remediation = "Increase foreground darkness to meet 4.5:1 minimum per SC 1.4.3 (AA); use --color-text-primary token instead"`, produces output where neither field is redacted / replaced with a placeholder — verifiable via unit test asserting the post-scrubber JSON contains those exact field values.

- (arch) If a Sentry path is wired in chunk #8, the `sentry` (or equivalent) dependency sits behind a `kebab-case` Cargo feature off by default, and `cargo tree --no-default-features -p pulse-app | grep sentry` returns empty (per architecture.md §Conventions "Feature flags" + §Cross-cutting Patterns "Feature-gate hygiene").

- (arch) Any new toggle introduced (e.g., `pii_scrub_enabled`, `log_format`) follows config precedence env > `config.toml` > built-in default; no toggle hardcoded above its precedence layer (per architecture.md §Cross-cutting Patterns "Config management").

Out-of-domain count: 2 / 7 (design + layouts). Within sanity threshold (≤3 warning trip; pure-backend tracing chunks expected to be UI-domain-irrelevant).
All bindings reciprocate per Phase 1 Check 1.C aggregate validation:

- **obs ↔ tests (heartbeat ticks forward-binding)** — obs extract notes; tests extract notes. Chunk #9 (next) is the heartbeat producer that piggybacks on chunk #7's subscriber.

title: Phase 5 Plan — chunks route#7..route#8: "Tracing self-observation harness + PII scrubbing rules wire"

data.head: # Phase 5 Plan — chunks route#7..route#8: "Tracing self-observation harness + PII scrubbing rules wire"

body: _Generated by /andromeda-phase Phase 4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not edit during /implement run._
- **Phase number:** 5

- **Route chunks covered:**
  - route#7 "Tracing self-observation harness — tracing + tracing-subscriber JSON + tracing-appender daily + tracing-error + service.name (no OTel SDK)"
  - route#8 "PII scrubbing rules wire — span attribute scrubber + log formatter Layer + Sentry before_send pattern (if enabled)"
- **Epoch:** Foundation (Epoch 1)

Promote the chunk #4 starter tracing scaffold (live in `pulse-app/src/main.rs:38-94`) into a dedicated `pulse-app/src/observability` module that satisfies the obs-plan §3 binding contract end-to-end: every JSON line carries the canonical service-identity envelope (`service.name` / `service.version` / `deployment.environment`, plus `ci.run.id` / `git.commit.sha` when present), the `tracing` ecosystem stack stays the only self-observation runtime (no OTel SDK linked), and a custom `FormatEvent` injects the default fields at serialization time so chunk #9's heartbeat ticks and chunk #15+'s a11y `target = "a11y::assertion"` events inherit identity automatically. Then layer in chunk #8's PII scrubber as a `tracing-subscriber::Layer` between `EnvFilter` and the JSON formatter, enforcing a per-module field allowlist (obs-plan §8 default-deny posture) so the security plan §Logging Vectors 1-6 NEVER-log list cannot leak through call-site discipline regression.

The plan is intentionally additive against the existing scaffold rather than a rewrite — chunk #4 already wired the daily file appender at `~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/agent-latest.jsonl`, the `EnvFilter` precedence (`ANDROMEDA_PULSE_LOG_LEVEL` → `RUST_LOG` → "info"), the `ErrorLayer::default()` for SpanTrace capture, and the `app.panic.fatal` hook that xtask `ci-gates` already greps. Chunks 7-8's scope is to (a) move the init body into a module so the scrubber can compose cleanly, (b) replace per-event identity emission with a default-fields injection so identity rides every line, (c) add CI env-var bounding + Unix mode-0700 hardening on the logs dir, (d) introduce the scrubber Layer + per-module allowlist, (e) add a `log_basename` helper for forthcoming plugin-path emitters, and (f) document a Sentry `before_send` shape as a comment-only stub (Sentry dep deferred per arch §Conventions feature-gate hygiene). Net result: the harness `logs` command (test-plan §3) sees fully-attributed JSON lines with PII scrubbed, and the `app.panic.fatal` xtask gate continues to pass without regression.

1. **Create `pulse-app/src/observability.rs`** as a new module owning the tracing init + service-identity envelope. Single file (~250-300 lines including tests) per research.md "New files to create" recommendation.

2. **Move** `init_tracing(data_dir: &Path) -> WorkerGuard` from `pulse-app/src/main.rs:38-72` into `observability.rs` as `pub(crate) fn init(data_dir: &Path) -> WorkerGuard`. Move the `SERVICE_NAME` and `DEPLOYMENT_ENVIRONMENT` constants from `main.rs:12-13` alongside it.
3. **Move** `install_panic_hook` from `pulse-app/src/main.rs:74-94` into `observability.rs` as `pub(crate) fn install_panic_hook()`. Body unchanged — already correct per obs-plan §7.

4. **Introduce `DefaultFields` struct** holding `service_name: &'static str`, `service_version: &'static str`, `deployment_environment: &'static str`, `ci_run_id: Option<String>`, `git_commit_sha: Option<String>`. Build once at init via a `from_env()` constructor that reads `GITHUB_RUN_ID` (charset-validate `^[0-9]{1,32}$`) and `GITHUB_SHA` (charset-validate `^[0-9a-f]{7,64}$`); on validation fail, emit `tracing::warn!(target: "app.boot.ci-fields", reason, raw_len, ...)` and proceed without the bad field. Resolves research.md Open Question 2.

5. **Implement a custom `FormatEvent`** wrapping `tracing_subscriber::fmt::format::Json` (or composing on top of it) that prepends `DefaultFields` keys before invoking the inner Json formatter. Per research.md Open Question 1 recommendation: option (a). Approximately 30 lines of glue.

6. **Compose registry** in `init()` as: `tracing_subscriber::registry().with(env_filter).with(scrub_layer).with(json_layer_with_default_fields).with(ErrorLayer::default())`. Layer ordering locked per research.md Open Question 4 (filter first, then mutate, then serialize, then capture span trace).

7. **Apply mode-0700** to the logs directory on Unix-like via `std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt::set_mode(0o700)` after `fs::create_dir_all`. On Windows, accept the OS-default ACL inherited from `%APPDATA%` and add a `// TODO(security)` comment per research.md Open Question 5; no code change for Windows ACL hardening in this chunk.

8. **Replace** the one-shot `tracing::info!(target: "app.boot.tracing.init", service_name = ..., service_version = ..., deployment_environment = ..., ...)` boot event (currently at `main.rs:62-69`) with a slimmer boot event that only logs `log_dir = ?logs_dir` and `default_fields_active = true` — service identity is now inherent in every line via the FormatEvent injection, so per-event restatement becomes redundant.

9. **Refactor `pulse-app/src/main.rs`** to import the new module: `mod observability;`. Replace the inline `let _guard = init_tracing(&data_dir);` + `install_panic_hook();` with `let _guard = observability::init(&data_dir); observability::install_panic_hook();`. The `resolve_data_dir` function stays in main.rs (entry-point concern, not observability). Net main.rs target: ≤ 60 lines.

title: From route#8: PII scrubbing rules wire

data.head: ### From route#8: PII scrubbing rules wire

body:
1. **Add `PiiScrubLayer` struct** in `pulse-app/src/observability.rs`:
   - Field `allowlist: HashMap<&'static str, HashSet<&'static str>>` keyed by `target` prefix (e.g., `"ingest"`, `"buffer"`, `"plugin"`, `"snapshot"`, `"viz"`, `"workspace-detector"`, `"ui-bridge"`, `"mcp-server"`).
   - Allowlist values exactly per combined.md §Chunk route#8 Constraints (obs) "Default-deny scrubbing posture": e.g., `ingest → {"span_count", "service"}`, `buffer → {"rows_ingested", "eviction_count", "memory_bytes", "retention_window_seconds"}`, etc. — verbatim from obs-plan §8.
   - Special-case targets: `"app.boot.*"`, `"app.panic.fatal"`, `"a11y::assertion"`, `"metric.*"`, `"{module}.tick"` get their own allowlists.

2. **Implement `tracing_subscriber::Layer<S> for PiiScrubLayer`**:
   - Override `on_event(&self, event: &Event<'_>, _ctx: Context<'_, S>)` with a custom `Visit` impl that walks event fields, looks up the event's `target` against the allowlist map, and constructs a *redacted* clone of the event for the inner formatter. Field names not in the allowlist are replaced with the literal value `"<redacted>"` (or dropped, per implementation taste — but replace is preferable for diff legibility).
   - The a11y violation JSON Required-fields list (combined.md §Chunk route#8 Patterns) — `wcag_criterion`, `violation_type`, `severity`, `surface`, `selector`, `remediation`, `tool`, `tool_result_id`, `token_name`, `measured_value`, `required_value`, `affected_component` — must appear in the `"a11y::assertion"` allowlist verbatim so chunk #15+'s violation events flow through unscrubbed.
   - Approximately 80-120 lines of `Layer` impl + visitor.

3. **Insert `PiiScrubLayer`** in the registry composition (step 6 above) between `env_filter` and `json_layer_with_default_fields`. Test the ordering with a unit test that emits a synthetic event with a non-allowlisted field and asserts the field is absent (or `"<redacted>"`) in JSON output.

4. **Add `pub(crate) fn log_basename(path: &Path) -> Option<&str>`** in `observability.rs` — implementation `path.file_name().and_then(|s| s.to_str())`. Co-located unit test asserts `/home/user/.andromeda-pulse/plugins/my-plugin.wasm` returns `Some("my-plugin.wasm")` and the full path is never returned. Resolves research.md Open Question 7 (placement: pub(crate) in observability.rs for now; promote to ui-bridge if a second consumer arrives).
5. **Add Sentry `before_send` skeleton comment** at the bottom of `observability.rs`:

- **Order sensitivity:** implement chunk #7 steps 1-9 in order *before* starting chunk #8 step 1. Chunk #8's `PiiScrubLayer` composes into the registry that chunk #7 builds — without the registry refactored to take Layer composition, chunk #8 can't insert cleanly. The single-PR approach is fine; just keep commits sequenced.

- **Layer ordering is testable and load-bearing.** The `EnvFilter` → `PiiScrubLayer` → `json_layer_with_default_fields` → `ErrorLayer::default()` ordering is locked. A unit test that constructs a registry with the layers in the wrong order should fail (e.g., an EnvFilter after the scrubber would let scrubbed-but-still-emitted events through; a json_layer before the scrubber would serialize unscrubbed fields). This isn't strictly required for the chunk to pass, but it documents the invariant.

If the implementation phase finds the FormatEvent API too thorny against `tracing-subscriber 0.3.x`, the fallback is the root-span pattern (info_span! at main scope + `with_current_span(true)` already set on the layer at `main.rs:53`). Either approach satisfies the obs-plan §3 binding; the FormatEvent path is preferred because it doesn't require every tokio task to use `.in_current_span()` to inherit identity.

- **`temp_env` crate for env-isolated tests:** the CI env-var validation tests need to set/unset `GITHUB_RUN_ID` and `GITHUB_SHA` per-test without leaking state between tests. The comment-only stub in `observability.rs` is the entire chunk #8 Sentry deliverable.

- **Windows mode-0700 deferral with TODO:** the security plan §Logging "Access controls" specifies "ACL-restricted to current user on Windows" but `%APPDATA%` already inherits a user-restricted ACL by default. Adding explicit `windows-permissions` crate dependency to chmod-equivalent the logs dir would expand the dependency surface for limited security gain at this stage. The TODO comment marks the gap for a future security-scope-arch entry.

This avoids "subscriber already set" panics under `cargo nextest run` per-process isolation.
- **Explicit `target` on every emitted event** (project-wide convention, see "Patterns detected"): always pass `target: "{module}.{operation}"` — never rely on default `module_path!()`.

  - Custom `FormatEvent` (or root-span pattern) that injects `DefaultFields` onto every emitted event before JSON serialization. Implementation choice flagged as Open Question 1 below.
  - `pub(crate) struct PiiScrubLayer { allowlist: HashMap<&'static str, HashSet<&'static str>> }` impl `tracing_subscriber::Layer<S>` — iterates `on_event` field visitor, redacts non-allowlisted field names per per-module allowlist (obs-plan §8 Default-deny posture).

No `cfg(feature = "sentry")` block until the dep is wired.

- `pulse-app/src/main.rs` — refactor: add `mod observability;` declaration; replace inline `init_tracing` + `install_panic_hook` with `let _guard = observability::init(&data_dir);` + `observability::install_panic_hook();`. The `resolve_data_dir` function stays in main.rs (entry-point concern, not observability). Service identity constants move to `observability.rs`. Net effect: main.rs shrinks to ~50 lines.

- `.claude/rules/observability.md` — already complete per the system reminder content; **no modification needed** (the rule already covers chunks 7-8 verbatim, including the `tracing` ecosystem ban on OTel SDK, default-field discipline, log sink path, span discipline, PII scrubbing Vectors 1-6, heartbeat-ticks forward-binding, frontend bridge, Sentry opt-in pattern). This is a pleasant surprise — the rule was prescient at chunk #4 commit time.
- `pulse-app/Cargo.toml` — no change (all crates already listed via `.workspace = true`).
- workspace `Cargo.toml` — no change (all crates already pinned).

1. **`with_default_fields` implementation choice.** The obs-plan body sketch references `Layer::with_default_fields([service.name, service.version, deployment.environment])` but `tracing-subscriber 0.3.x` `fmt::Layer` does not expose a method by that name. The three workable approaches:
   - (a) **Custom `FormatEvent` impl** — small wrapper around the JSON formatter that prepends `DefaultFields` keys before invoking inner formatter. Cleanest; ~30 lines of glue.
   - (b) **Root info span pattern** — call `tracing::info_span!("app.session", service.name = ..., service.version = ..., ...).entered()` at the top of `main` and hold the entered guard for the app lifetime; configure the JSON layer with `with_current_span(true)` (already set at main.rs:53). Events inherit parent-span fields. Brittle: requires every spawned tokio task to use `.in_current_span()` to inherit.
   - (c) **Custom `Layer<S>::on_event` impl** — intercept events, mutate fields before forwarding to inner layer. Most flexible but ties the scrubber and default-fields concerns together.
   
   **Recommendation for plan.md:** option (a) — custom `FormatEvent` impl. Keeps the scrubber Layer (chunk #8) and default-fields (chunk #7) cleanly separable; `FormatEvent` is the documented extension point.

2. **CI env var bounding.** `GITHUB_RUN_ID` is a numeric string (≤20 chars typically); `GITHUB_SHA` is a 40-char lowercase hex string. Per security plan §Input Validation row "CLI / env var inputs", both should be bounded before injecting into tracing fields. **Recommendation for plan.md:** validate `ci.run.id` matches `^[0-9]{1,32}$` and `git.commit.sha` matches `^[0-9a-f]{7,64}$`; if validation fails, emit `tracing::warn!(target: "app.boot.ci-fields", ...)` and proceed without the bad field set.

3. **Sentry skeleton scope.** Two options:
   - (i) Add `sentry-rust = "0.46"` and `sentry-tauri = "0.5"` as workspace optional deps + `sentry-redaction` feature flag in `pulse-app/Cargo.toml`, with a real (but minimal) `before_send` body.
   - (ii) Defer entirely — comment-only stub in `observability.rs` documenting the future shape; no Cargo.toml change.
   
   **Recommendation for plan.md:** option (ii) — defer. Per arch "no Sentry feature decision in arch today, a no-op skeleton is acceptable" + per security plan §Dependency Security default-features-minimal pattern. Keep dependency closure tight; activate Sentry in a future scope-arch.

4. **PII scrubber Layer ordering in registry composition.** Layers in `tracing_subscriber::registry().with(...).with(...).with(...)` are stacked outermost-first. The order matters for filtering vs mutation:
   - `EnvFilter` first (filter out events below configured level — never see them)
   - `PiiScrubLayer` second (mutate field set on surviving events)
   - `json_layer` third (serialize the mutated event to file)
   - `ErrorLayer::default()` fourth (capture SpanTrace context for later retrieval at error-bridge boundary)
   
   **Recommendation for plan.md:** lock this ordering; document in observability.rs init body comments. Lock is testable: a unit test enables `tracing_subscriber::registry().with(EnvFilter::new("debug")).with(PiiScrubLayer::new()).with(json_layer)`, emits a synthetic event with a non-allowlisted field, asserts the field is absent in JSON output.

5. **Logs-dir mode 0700 on Windows.** Linux/macOS support is straightforward via `std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt::set_mode(0o700)` after `fs::create_dir_all`. Windows has no chmod; ACL-restricting the dir to the current user requires either `windows-permissions` crate, manual `windows-rs` `SetSecurityInfo`, or accepting the OS default ACL (which on a typical Windows install is already restricted to the user via `%APPDATA%`).
   
   **Recommendation for plan.md:** Implement chmod 0700 on Unix-like in chunk #7. Document Windows as "OS default ACL inherited from `%APPDATA%`" with a TODO comment for future explicit ACL hardening if a security review demands it. The security plan §Logging "Access controls" specifies the goal but allows OS-inherited Windows ACLs as a starting state; tightening is a security-scope-arch concern, not chunk #7.

6. **Daily-rotation deterministic test.** `tracing-appender::rolling::daily(...)` uses internal time tracking; it is not directly mockable via `tokio::time::pause()`. Three options:
   - (i) Skip the rotation test entirely; rely on integration smoke at chunk #8 commit (a real overnight run during CI).
   - (ii) Hand-write a small `MockClock` + custom `Rotation` impl for a unit test (maintenance burden).
   - (iii) Test the file-name-formatting + appender-builder behavior independently (not the actual rotation event).
   
   **Recommendation for plan.md:** option (iii) — assert the resolved file-name pattern (`agent-latest.jsonl.YYYY-MM-DD`) is correct via inspecting the appender's directory after a synthetic write; defer real rotation verification to operational testing.

7. **`log_basename` helper placement.** Options:
   - (i) Inline in `pulse-app/src/observability.rs` as `pub(crate) fn`.
   - (ii) Add to `crates/ui-bridge/src/lib.rs` as `pub fn` (since ui-bridge already imports `strict-path` and is the natural shared-utilities home).
   - (iii) New file `crates/ui-bridge/src/path_safe.rs`.
   
   **Recommendation for plan.md:** option (i) — keep it `pub(crate)` in `observability.rs` for now. Chunks 7-8 are the only consumers; later chunks (e.g., plugin loader at route#37) can elevate to a shared crate when there's a second user. Avoids premature abstraction.

data.head: ### Chunk route#53: "Distribution channels — Homebrew tap + Scoop manifest via update-channels.yml triggered on release.yml completion"

body: **Constraints across domains:**

- (security) Pin every third-party GitHub Action in `update-channels.yml` by 40-char commit SHA с `# vX.Y.Z` provenance comment — NEVER `@v2` / `@latest` / floating tag (per security plan §Security Anti-Patterns §Secrets row 3; tj-actions/changed-files CVE-2025-30066 retroactive-tag-rewrite anchor; mirrors chunk #52 release.yml SHA-pin discipline).

- (security) Workflow-level `permissions:` MUST start at `contents: read`; elevate to `contents: write` per-job ONLY on the publish-to-tap / publish-to-bucket step (per security plan §Security Anti-Patterns §Secrets row 4 + §Secret Management GitHub Environment scoping).

- (security) All cross-repo push secrets (`HOMEBREW_TAP_PUSH_TOKEN`, `SCOOP_BUCKET_PUSH_TOKEN`) MUST live в the GitHub Environment named `production-release` with manual approval gate — never at repo-level secrets (per security plan §Secret Management "What counts as secret" + §Security Anti-Patterns §Secrets row 5; production-release-environment.md runbook lines 139-140 already names these).

- (security) `step-security/harden-runner` (SHA-pinned) MUST be the first step of every job в update-channels.yml; `egress-policy: audit` initially, promoted к `block` с allowlist after а clean audit window (per security plan §Bootstrap phases `dep-security-ci-gate`).

- (security) Bundle SHA-256 hashes consumed from chunk #52's `sha256-${runner.os}` artifact MUST be validated integrity-end-to-end against the Minisign-signed bundles produced upstream — Tauri updater Minisign Ed25519 verification cannot be disabled (per security plan §Data Protection in-transit row 3 + §Security Anti-Patterns §Data Protection row 2).

- (security) `cargo-deny check licenses` SPDX allowlist gate is load-bearing для this chunk — Homebrew/Scoop distribution channels are documented as the at-risk path for dependency-license downgrade incidents (per security plan §Dependency Security CI integration).

- (security) `workflow_run` trigger consuming chunk #52's release.yml completion MUST scope token elevation к the publish step only — а compromised release.yml feeding into update-channels.yml is the documented privilege-escalation pivot path (per security plan §Security Anti-Patterns §Secrets row 4).

- (arch) The `update-channels.yml` workflow MUST run on completion of `release.yml` (per arch §Infrastructure Patterns CI/CD approach). `workflow_run` trigger is the spec-fixed mechanism; no manual `workflow_dispatch`-only path satisfies arch.

- (arch) Distribution targets are FIXED at three channels: GitHub Releases (primary) + Homebrew tap + Scoop manifest (per arch §Stack [Distribution channels] + §Established Decisions + §Inherited Defaults). No fourth channel (Chocolatey, winget, Snap, Flatpak) may be added without `/andromeda-scope-arch` legitimization.

- (arch) Bundle artifact names consumed from `release.yml` MUST match the canonical list (per arch §Occupied Resources "Bundle artifact names"): `andromeda-pulse_<version>_x64-setup.msi` (Scoop), `andromeda-pulse_<version>_x64.dmg` + `andromeda-pulse_<version>_aarch64.dmg` (Homebrew macOS), `andromeda-pulse_<version>_amd64.AppImage` + `andromeda-pulse_<version>_amd64.deb` (Homebrew Linux).
- (arch) Workflow file MUST live at `.github/workflows/update-channels.yml` (per arch §Infrastructure Patterns project directory structure tree line 229). No alternative path.

- (arch) All shared release/publish logic that needs Rust MUST live in the `xtask` crate (per arch §Infrastructure Patterns CI/CD approach last line). If pure YAML + shell + `gh` CLI suffice, chunk stays workflow-only; if Rust needed, place in `xtask`.
- (arch) No new workspace crate; no new `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_*` env var introduced (per arch §Occupied Resources reserved lists).

- (tests) Workflow YAML SHA-pin discipline: every third-party Action в `.github/workflows/update-channels.yml` MUST be pinned by 40-char commit SHA с `# vX.Y.Z` provenance comment (per test-plan §11 Anti-Patterns CI row 1).

- (tests) Standard gate baseline per chunk plan unconditional: `cargo fmt --check` + `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` + `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` + `cargo xtask capability-drift` + `npm run lint --prefix pulse-app/ui` + `npm run typecheck --prefix pulse-app/ui` + `npm run test --prefix pulse-app/ui` (per test-plan §12 Decisions Log 2026-05-10 chunk-gate-baseline-coverage).

- (tests) Boot-smoke gate NOT triggered: chunk #53 touches workflow YAML + optional `pulse-app/tests/*.rs` + manifest template fixtures only; no boot/setup paths modified (per test-plan §12 Decisions Log 2026-05-09 boot-smoke-coverage).

- (tests) Agent-runnable invariants apply: every new test layer must produce machine-parseable output (exit code + structured stdout/JSON); cross-repo push verification IS operator-driven DEFERRED (per test-plan §2 agent-runnable invariants).
- (tests) Zero-flakiness budget: no real network calls к external Homebrew tap / Scoop bucket repos in tests (per test-plan §11 Anti-Patterns Universal row 5).

- (tests) `cargo deny check bans licenses sources` + `cargo audit` MUST remain clean; multiple-versions = "deny" canary intact (per test-plan §11 Anti-Patterns Test Strategy row 4 + §9 Cargo deny enforcement).
- (tests) Workspace coverage targets unchanged (≥75% line / ≥70% branch / ≥85% function per test-plan §10 Standard tier); new Rust-side validation tests participate в normal coverage gates.

- (design) Package-manager description / caveats copy MUST use contemplative, observational voice — consistent с Brand Identity ambient-constellation personality (per design plan §Brand Identity — "calm precision of a mission-control station"; tray-menu tone discipline в §Surface: desktop-native).

- (design) IF Scoop manifest includes `icon` field pointing к а raster image, that asset MUST be one of the 5 registered custom domain glyphs (aperture / telescope / constellation-grid / star / circular-pulse) rendered against `#1A1D24` Deep Control Gray, NOT а generic library icon (per design plan §Iconography + §Anti-Patterns Universal Bans).

- (design) Any color value referenced в package-manager assets MUST trace к the locked NASA Deep Space Mission Control palette tokens (#1A1D24 / #4A90E2 / #C7556A / #E8EEF7 / #2C3E7F / #17B3A3) — no Tailwind defaults, no purple gradients (per design plan §Color Palette Core Colors + §Anti-Patterns Universal Bans).

- (design) Homebrew Formula `desc` string (≤80 chars, no period, no leading article) and Scoop manifest `description` MUST both originate the same canonical product-summary copy (per design plan §Brand Identity domain anchors).
**Patterns к follow:**

- (security) **SHA-pin convention с provenance comment**: `<owner>/<repo>@<40-char-SHA> # vX.Y.Z` on every `uses:` line; reuse 7 existing SHAs from ci.yml + release.yml (harden-runner, checkout, rust-toolchain, rust-cache, setup-node, install-action, upload-artifact) per chunk #52 precedent.
- (security) **Workflow self-lint grep**: zero floating-tag matches as post-implementation verification (per chunk #52 precedent — "11/11 release.yml `uses:` SHA-pinned").
- (security) **Environment-scoped secret access**: `environment: production-release` job-level setting gates secret access behind manual approval (mirrors chunk #52's release.yml binding).

- (security) **Pre-built / DEFERRED operator-driven scope split**: workflow file lands now consuming secrets that don't yet exist; external-tap-repo bootstrap + PAT provisioning + Environment secret population stays operator-driven per chunk #3 + chunk #52 ACTIVE/DEFERRED Path A precedent.

- (security) **Bundle URL + SHA-256 pairing**: Homebrew Formula `andromeda-pulse.rb` + Scoop bucket `andromeda-pulse.json` MUST pair each bundle URL с its sha256 hash (per arch §Established Decisions [Distribution Channels]).

- (arch) **Three-channel-from-one-workflow** pattern (per arch §Established Decisions [Distribution Channels]: "three channels driven from the same workflow via `taiki-e/upload-rust-binary-action`-style patterns"). `release.yml` (chunk #52) produces; `update-channels.yml` consumes via `workflow_run`.
- (arch) **`workflow_run` `types: [completed]` + `conclusion == 'success'` guard** is the standard chain pattern between two workflows (skip channel-update if release.yml conclusion is not success).
- (arch) **Renumber-stable chunk #53 position** (per route §3 Decisions Log 2026-05-11): chunk #53 sits between chunk #52 (release pipeline) and chunk #54 (a11y audit) post-renumber.

- (tests) **Chunk #52 lightweight config-validation tests precedent**: `pulse-app/tests/config_validation.rs` (~150 lines, 4 tests) parses static fixtures с pure file-read + JSON-parse + value-assert (no Tauri runtime context). Mirror for chunk #53 manifest validation if added.
- (tests) **Workflow self-lint grep pattern**: enforce SHA-pin discipline post-implementation via grep — `uses:` lines match 40-char SHA pattern; zero floating-tag matches.
- (tests) **JUnit XML output format**: any new Rust tests follow `cargo nextest --message-format junit --output-file target/nextest/junit.xml` shape.
- (tests) **Per-test isolation via `tempfile::TempDir`**; in-memory fixture content preferred (per test-plan §7 Test Data lifecycle).

- (tests) **Self-bootstrapping test data**: manifest fixtures generated at runtime via Rust builders or inline string literals — no pre-baked `.rb` / `.json` snapshot files committed (per test-plan §7 Self-bootstrapping requirement).

- (tests) **DEFERRED-scope documentation pattern**: cross-repo push verification follows chunk #52 Path A precedent — workflow lands consuming Environment secrets; full E2E happens when operator populates PATs (pre-v0.1.0 release blocker).

- (design) **Custom-glyph-as-brand-asset pattern**: reuse `<Root>/src/components/icons/` registered custom SVGs for any iconography reference; do NOT introduce а new "marketing" icon outside the registered set.

- (design) **Terse-output convention**: Homebrew Formula `desc` + Scoop manifest `description` follow same brevity rule as OS notifications ("terse, 2 lines max"; "Snapshot ready | 2.5k tokens, 42 spans" exemplar).
**Anti-patterns к avoid:**

- (security) NEVER reference `peter-evans/create-pull-request@v6` or `Homebrew/actions/setup-homebrew@master` or any third-party Action by floating tag в update-channels.yml — pin by 40-char SHA с `# vX.Y.Z` comment (per security plan §Security Anti-Patterns §Secrets row 3).
- (security) NEVER write `permissions: { contents: write }` at workflow level — set workflow к `contents: read` + elevate per-job (per security plan §Security Anti-Patterns §Secrets row 4).

- (security) NEVER store `HOMEBREW_TAP_PUSH_TOKEN` / `SCOOP_BUCKET_PUSH_TOKEN` as repository-level secrets — they MUST live в Environment `production-release` с manual approval gate (per security plan §Secret Management).

- (arch) **Do not bypass release.yml as the artifact source.** Chain MUST be `release.yml → update-channels.yml`; do NOT have `update-channels.yml` re-build bundles from source (defeats per-arch invariant that signed/notarized bundles flow from one signing pipeline).
- (arch) **Do not introduce a new workspace crate or a new `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_*` env var.** No new arch §Occupied Resources entry permitted; CI/CD wiring only.
- (arch) **Do not embed signing/Minisign/Notarization logic в `update-channels.yml`.** Those are chunk #52's domain (release.yml); update-channels consumes hashes + URLs only.

1. **Create `.github/workflows/update-channels.yml`** (~150-200 lines). Workflow shape:
   - `name: update-channels`
   - `on: workflow_run: workflows: ["release"] types: [completed]` triggering от chunk #52's release.yml (verify `name:` field в release.yml line 24 → `name: release`)
   - Top-level `permissions: contents: read`

   - Two jobs (per Open Question 5 recommendation: separate-jobs):
     - **`update-homebrew`** — `runs-on: ubuntu-22.04` (Homebrew Formula push is Linux-friendly via gh CLI); `environment: production-release`; `permissions: contents: read` (cross-repo write is via PAT not GITHUB_TOKEN); `if: github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'` job guard
     - **`update-scoop`** — `runs-on: ubuntu-22.04` (Scoop manifest is JSON-only, push from any runner); `environment: production-release`; same permissions + if guard
   - Each job's step list:
     1. `step-security/harden-runner@a5ad31d6a139d249332a2605b85202e8c0b78450 # v2.19.1` first (reuse ci.yml/release.yml SHA)
     2. `actions/checkout@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5 # v4` (reuse) к check out THIS repo (read the workflow + any template files)

   - Comment blocks above each step explaining purpose (mirror release.yml convention at lines 95-101, 109-117, 137-144, etc.)

2. **(Optional, recommended Path A) Create `pulse-app/tests/distribution_manifests.rs`** (~100-150 lines). 3-5 lightweight tests mirroring chunk #52's `config_validation.rs` shape:

   - `fn pulse_app_root() -> PathBuf { PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")) }`
   - `fn read_text(relative_path: &str) -> String { ... }` (Homebrew Formula DSL is Ruby, not JSON — pure text read)
   - Tests:
     - `homebrew_formula_template_contains_required_placeholders` — assert Formula template (loaded от an inline `const HOMEBREW_FORMULA_TEMPLATE: &str = r#"..."#` constant OR от а small fixture file) contains `{{VERSION}}` + `{{MACOS_X64_URL}}` + `{{MACOS_X64_SHA256}}` + `{{MACOS_AARCH64_URL}}` + `{{MACOS_AARCH64_SHA256}}` + `{{LINUX_AMD64_APPIMAGE_URL}}` + ... placeholders.
     - `scoop_manifest_template_is_valid_json_after_substitution` — substitute fixture values into а template + assert `serde_json::from_str::<Value>(...)` succeeds + required fields (`version`, `architecture.64bit.url`, `architecture.64bit.hash`) populated.
     - `homebrew_formula_desc_under_80_chars` — assert Formula `desc` string ≤ 80 chars (Homebrew convention; per design plan §Brand Identity).
     - `bundle_url_pattern_matches_arch_canonical_names` — assert URL templates match `andromeda-pulse_<version>_*-setup.msi` / `.dmg` / `.AppImage` / `.deb` pattern (per arch §Occupied Resources Bundle artifact names).
   - Pure file-read + parse + value-assert; no Tauri runtime context; no network calls.
   - If templates live inline в Rust constants: zero new template files committed; templates rendered к stdout at workflow runtime via `sed` substitution against bash-quoted heredoc strings (simpler than `xtask render-manifests`).
   - If templates live in repo (e.g., `pulse-app/tests/fixtures/homebrew-formula.template.rb`): fixture files committed under `pulse-app/tests/fixtures/`.
   - Recommendation: inline Rust constants (simpler; no template files к maintain; tests own the canonical shape).
