data.head: # Phase 58 Plan — chunk route#62: "Attention cue emitter"

body: _Generated by /andromeda-phase Phase 4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not edit during /implement run._
- **Phase number:** 58

- **Route chunks covered:**
  - route#62 "Attention cue emitter — Background tick task (1-2s) reads all trackers, evaluates thresholds (3.0× error rate multiplier, 2.5× latency multiplier — calibration values loaded from config), emits `AttentionCue` to broadcast with `priority_tier` classification (Hard / Medium / Baseline based on confidence and magnitude). Tier-2 cues additionally emit to `cadence-triggers` channel for Cadence Coordinator (#72). **Threshold multipliers loaded from config or hardcoded defaults for now; hot-reload wiring added in #86.**"
- **Epoch:** Epoch 9 — Foundation v0.2.0

Chunk #62 transforms the triage crate from passive primitives (chunk #60 contract types + chunk #61 streaming baseline trackers — `EwmaTracker` / `TDigestPair` / `RollingWindow` exposed via `triage::contract`) into the first **algorithmic detection layer** of pulse v0.2.0. The chunk delivers three coordinated pieces: (a) a 1-second background tick task that reads all per-service and per-operation baselines, compares current values against threshold multipliers (3.0× for error rates, 2.5× for latencies), classifies each above-threshold deviation into a `PriorityTier` (`Autonomous` / `Suggested` / `Curious` per chunk #60 contract — see Implementation note 1 for the route §62 "Hard / Medium / Baseline" → contract-name mapping), and emits the resulting `AttentionCue` payloads to a new broadcast topic `pulse://stream/attention-cues`; (b) the boot-wiring that chunk #61 explicitly deferred to chunk #62 per `crates/triage/src/baseline/mod.rs:5` — tapping the OTLP ingest hot path so each decoded span feeds `BaselineState::observe_span(...)`, spawning the chunk #61 corpus persist loop at boot, and registering the on-shutdown persist hook; (c) a parallel `cadence-triggers` channel that re-emits Tier-2 (`Suggested`) cues for downstream consumption by the future Cadence Coordinator (chunk #72).

Per route §3 Decisions Log 2026-05-17 chunk #62 amendment, the chunk implements capability P-021 (Algorithmic Attention Cues) and partial P-019 (PriorityTier classification — Autonomous / Suggested / Curious). Threshold multipliers are loaded from a `Thresholds` config struct with hardcoded defaults this chunk; hot-reload wiring lands in chunk #86. The chunk introduces NO new TauRPC procedure (emission-only via broadcast); arch §Occupied Resources registry acknowledgment of the new broadcast topic + cadence-triggers channel is deferred to a post-impl `/andromeda-evolve --allow-arch-registry` Type 6 amendment per route §3 Decisions Log + likely doubles as the first live test of P7 narrative-cascade per session-handoff.md.

The chunk fits inside the existing 13-crate workspace (`crates/triage/` is the home; the 13th workspace member acknowledged at chunk #60). It follows the trait-in-lower-crate + impl-in-pulse-app pattern from chunk #59 (`ReceiverBindStatus`) to keep the ingest crate workspace-boundary-clean while tapping its hot path. Boot wiring lives in `pulse-app/src/main.rs` setup closure alongside the existing connection-state poller, retention task, and heartbeat spawn — single tokio runtime per arch §Established Decisions [In-Process Channel Architecture].

1. **Convert `crates/triage/src/cue.rs` (2-line stub) to a `cue/` directory.** Delete the existing single-file stub; create `crates/triage/src/cue/mod.rs` with module declarations `mod thresholds; mod classify; mod evaluate; mod broadcast; mod emitter;` plus a single doc comment header documenting the L1 detection layer. `crates/triage/src/lib.rs` line 11 already declares `pub(crate) mod cue;` — Cargo resolves `cue.rs` OR `cue/mod.rs` transparently, so no edit to lib.rs needed.

2. **Create `crates/triage/src/cue/thresholds.rs`.** Declare module-level constants `pub const DEFAULT_ERROR_RATE_MULTIPLIER: f64 = 3.0;`, `pub const DEFAULT_LATENCY_MULTIPLIER: f64 = 2.5;`, `pub const DEFAULT_TICK_INTERVAL: Duration = Duration::from_secs(1);`, `pub const DEFAULT_MIN_PERSISTENCE_SECONDS: u64 = 30;`, `pub const DEFAULT_BASE_ERROR_RATE: f64 = 0.01;` (1% nominal floor — see Implementation note 3), `pub const DEFAULT_LATENCY_PERCENTILE: f64 = 0.95;` (which percentile chunk evaluates against the multiplier). Plus `pub const MIN_EWMA_SAMPLES: u64 = 10;` (warm-up gate — see Implementation note 3). Declare `pub struct Thresholds { pub error_rate_multiplier: f64, pub latency_multiplier: f64, pub tick_interval: Duration, pub min_persistence_seconds: u64, pub base_error_rate: f64, pub latency_percentile: f64 }` with `#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Serialize, Deserialize)]` + `impl Default for Thresholds` reading the constants. Add a `Thresholds::validate(&self) -> Result<(), BaselineError>` (or a new triage-side error variant) rejecting negative / NaN / out-of-range values per security plan §Input Validation Configuration row — needed for future serde-deserialization path even though chunk #62 uses defaults only.

3. **Create `crates/triage/src/cue/classify.rs`.** Declare `pub fn classify_priority(magnitude: f64, confidence: f64, persistence_seconds: u64) -> PriorityTier`. Heuristic (final values land at /implement; tests anchor whichever shape): `if magnitude >= 5.0 && confidence >= 0.9 && persistence_seconds >= 30 { Autonomous } else if magnitude >= 3.0 && confidence >= 0.7 { Suggested } else { Curious }`. Plus `pub fn dual_condition_bypass(magnitude: f64, absolute_value: f64, kind: CueKind) -> bool` per capability spec P-057 (`magnitude > 10.0 || absolute_value > 0.05` → true for ErrorRateSpike; analogous threshold for LatencyRegression). Pure synchronous functions; unit-testable without runtime context.

4. **Create `crates/triage/src/cue/evaluate.rs`.** Declare `pub fn evaluate_thresholds(state: &BaselineState, thresholds: &Thresholds, now_nanos: i64) -> Vec<AttentionCue>`. Pure synchronous evaluator (the testable-helper-extraction pattern per `crates/buffer/src/retention.rs::run_one_sweep` + `crates/ingest/src/connection.rs::compute_state`). Implementation:
   - Iterate `state.services` via `DashMap::iter()` (pattern mirrors `swap_tdigest_pairs_on_tick` at baseline/mod.rs:181)
   - For each service: read EWMA value via `state.error_rate(service_name)`; read sample count via accessing the tracker; if `samples ≥ MIN_EWMA_SAMPLES` (warm-up gate) AND value ≥ `thresholds.base_error_rate * thresholds.error_rate_multiplier`, construct an `ErrorRateSpike` `AttentionCue` with `scope = CueScope::Service`, `scope_id = Some(service_name.to_string())`, `magnitude = value / thresholds.base_error_rate`, `absolute_value = value`, `persistence_seconds = derived from last_update_nanos - first_update_nanos`, `confidence = derived from samples count (more samples → higher confidence)`, `priority_tier = classify_priority(magnitude, confidence, persistence_seconds)`, `suppression_bypassed = dual_condition_bypass(...)`.
   - Iterate `state.operations` via `DashMap::iter()`; for each operation: read p95 latency via `state.latency_percentile(service_name, operation_name, thresholds.latency_percentile)`; compare against a per-operation rolling baseline (use the t-digest's previous bucket via `TDigestPair::previous_percentile(q)` — see Implementation note 4). If current p95 ≥ baseline × thresholds.latency_multiplier, construct `LatencyRegression` cue with `scope = CueScope::Operation` etc.
   - Aggregate results into `Vec<AttentionCue>` returned to caller.
   - Pure: no tracing emission, no broadcast send — caller handles side effects.

5. **Create `crates/triage/src/cue/broadcast.rs`.** Mirror `crates/ingest/src/connection.rs:25-227` pattern:
   - `pub const STREAM_NAME_ATTENTION_CUES: &str = "pulse://stream/attention-cues";`
   - `pub const CHANNEL_NAME_CADENCE_TRIGGERS: &str = "cadence-triggers";` (in-process channel label for tracing)
   - `const BROADCAST_CAPACITY: usize = 32;`
   - `pub struct AttentionCueBroadcast { sender: broadcast::Sender<AttentionCue> }` with `new() / sender() / subscribe() / subscriber_count() / Default` (verbatim shape from `ConnectionBroadcast`).
   - `pub struct CadenceTriggerChannel { sender: broadcast::Sender<AttentionCue> }` with same accessors (per Open question 5; if /implement Phase 1 confirms mpsc is preferred, the contract surface remains `Arc<CadenceTriggerChannel>` with internal field swapped to `mpsc::Sender` — caller-facing API stable).

6. **Create `crates/triage/src/cue/emitter.rs`.** Declare:
   - `pub async fn start_emitter(state: Arc<BaselineState>, broadcast_handle: Arc<AttentionCueBroadcast>, cadence_handle: Arc<CadenceTriggerChannel>, thresholds: Arc<Thresholds>) -> ()` — the spawned task body. Pattern mirrors `crates/ingest/src/connection.rs::start_poller` (line 238):
     - `let mut interval = tokio::time::interval(thresholds.tick_interval);`
     - Call `interval.tick().await;` once at top (skip immediate-fire — both retention.rs:44 and connection.rs:243 use this; OR keep first tick to surface initial heartbeat — choose at /implement)
     - Loop forever: `interval.tick().await;` → `let now_nanos = current_unix_nanos();` → `let cues = run_one_emit_cycle(&state, &thresholds, now_nanos)` → for each cue in cues: `let _ = broadcast_handle.sender().send(cue.clone());` + tier-2 (`PriorityTier::Suggested`) ALSO `let _ = cadence_handle.sender().send(cue.clone());` → emit `triage.cue.tick` heartbeat with `cues_evaluated`, `cues_emitted`, `services_tracked`, `operations_tracked` structural counts → emit `metric.cue.emit_count_total` per-cue counter event with bounded `kind` (`CueKind` enum label) + `priority` (`PriorityTier` enum label) labels.
   - `pub(crate) fn run_one_emit_cycle(state: &BaselineState, thresholds: &Thresholds, now_nanos: i64) -> Vec<AttentionCue>` — extracted synchronous helper. Calls `evaluate_thresholds(...)`. Returns cues. Testable without tokio runtime.
   - `#[tracing::instrument(skip_all, fields(cues_evaluated = tracing::field::Empty, cues_emitted = tracing::field::Empty))]` on the tick-body helper; record fields via `span.record(...)` after computation per `pulse-app/src/connection_router.rs:68-72` precedent.
   - Per-cue emission helper `fn emit_cue_to_broadcast(cue: &AttentionCue, broadcast_handle: &AttentionCueBroadcast, cadence_handle: &CadenceTriggerChannel)` that issues the broadcast send + cadence-trigger send (if tier-2) + tracing event emission.
   - **Tracing event field discipline (per combined.md security + obs rows):** structural fields only — `kind` (enum label via `cue_kind_label(c.kind)` lookup fn returning `&'static str`), `priority` (enum label via `priority_tier_label(c.priority_tier)` lookup), `scope` (enum label), `magnitude`, `absolute_value`, `persistence_seconds`, `confidence`, `suppression_bypassed`. **NEVER `scope_id`** (carries user-controlled service.name) — log `service_name_tag = "scope_value_present"` boolean instead, OR omit entirely.

7. **Update `crates/triage/src/lib.rs` `pub(crate) mod cue;` line.** No change needed if directory replacement works transparently. If issues arise (rare), explicitly declare `pub(crate) mod cue { pub use ... }` or convert to full module path. Verify at /implement.

8. **Update `crates/triage/src/contract.rs` re-exports.** Append `pub use crate::cue::{AttentionCueBroadcast, CadenceTriggerChannel, STREAM_NAME_ATTENTION_CUES, CHANNEL_NAME_CADENCE_TRIGGERS, Thresholds, start_emitter, evaluate_thresholds, classify_priority, DEFAULT_ERROR_RATE_MULTIPLIER, DEFAULT_LATENCY_MULTIPLIER, DEFAULT_TICK_INTERVAL, DEFAULT_MIN_PERSISTENCE_SECONDS};` after the existing baseline re-exports block (line 17). Mirrors chunk #61's contract-re-export precedent.

9. **Create `crates/ingest/src/observer.rs` (NEW module).** Declare `pub trait SpanObserver: Send + Sync { fn observe_span(&self, service_name: &str, operation_name: &str, status_code: u8, latency_ms: u64, now_nanos: i64); }`. Mirrors `ingest::connection::ReceiverBindStatus` trait precedent. Doc comment cites trait-in-lower-crate pattern + chunk #59 reference. Plus `pub struct NoopSpanObserver;` with `impl SpanObserver for NoopSpanObserver { fn observe_span(...) {} }` — used as default in tests + as a fallback if baseline state init fails.
10. **Update `crates/ingest/src/lib.rs`.** Add `pub mod observer;` declaration. +1 line.

11. **Update ingest hot path to invoke `SpanObserver::observe_span`.** Two files modified:
    - `crates/ingest/src/grpc.rs::serve_on(...)` signature OR the per-batch handler accepts `Arc<dyn SpanObserver>` in addition to `Arc<IngestState>` + `Arc<IngestSender>`. Each decoded span (post-prost-decode invariant pass) calls `observer.observe_span(service_name, operation_name, status_code, latency_ms, now_nanos)`. The fields are already extracted at decode site for the mpsc send.
    - `crates/ingest/src/http.rs::serve_on(...)` analogous modification.
    - Existing tests' helper builders (`start_test_*_server` in `crates/ingest/tests/{grpc_loopback,http_loopback}.rs`) need either an extra argument with default `Arc::new(NoopSpanObserver)` OR an overload pair. Prefer overload pair to avoid touching ~15 existing test invocations; OR accept a single argument with a default helper `fn observer_or_noop(o: Option<Arc<dyn SpanObserver>>) -> Arc<dyn SpanObserver>`.

12. **Create `pulse-app/src/baseline_observer.rs` (NEW).** `pub struct BaselineObserverAdapter { state: Arc<BaselineState> }` + `impl ingest::observer::SpanObserver for BaselineObserverAdapter { fn observe_span(&self, service_name: &str, operation_name: &str, status_code: u8, latency_ms: u64, now_nanos: i64) { self.state.observe_span(service_name, operation_name, status_code, latency_ms, now_nanos); } }` + `pub fn new(state: Arc<BaselineState>) -> Self`. Mirrors `pulse-app/src/connection_router.rs::HeartbeatBindStatus` adapter precedent.
13. **Update `pulse-app/src/lib.rs`.** Add `pub mod baseline_observer;` declaration. +1 line.

14. **Update `pulse-app/src/main.rs` (substantial — ~30 line addition in setup phase).** Specifically:
    - Add `init_baseline_state(data_dir: &Path) -> Arc<BaselineState>` helper near `init_buffer` (line 527). Implementation: resolve corpus path via `triage::contract::resolve_corpus_path(data_dir)`; call `triage::contract::bootstrap_state(corpus_path, DEFAULT_MAX_SIZE_BYTES, DEFAULT_SERVICE_COUNT_CAP, current_unix_nanos)`; wrap in `Arc::new(...)`.
    - In `main()` after `let buffer_state = ...` (line 227), add `let baseline_state = init_baseline_state(&data_dir);`.

1. **PriorityTier naming reconciliation (Open question 2 resolved).** Route §2 chunk text says "(Hard / Medium / Baseline based on confidence and magnitude)" but chunk #60 contract at `crates/triage/src/contract.rs:48-54` declares `pub enum PriorityTier { Autonomous, Suggested, Curious }`. The plan uses contract types (canonical). Mapping convention documented for future readers: `Autonomous` ≈ "Hard" (high-confidence, prominent halo shift, surfaces with counter increment per capability spec P-019 doc string); `Suggested` ≈ "Medium" / Tier-2 (likely-problem with reservations, quiet counter increment, minimal halo; **THIS is the tier that fan-outs to `cadence-triggers` channel** per route §62 text); `Curious` ≈ "Baseline" (worth recording for pattern learning, no interruption — Findings dropdown collapsed section). No route §2 amendment required; route §3 Decisions Log already cites the chunk text verbatim.

2. **Ingest hot-path tap scope (Open question 1 resolved).** Chunk #62 scope INCLUDES ingest-tap wiring per chunk #61 baseline/mod.rs:5 deferral note. If user prefers narrower scope (just emitter; skip ingest-tap until a later chunk), surface at Phase 6 review BEFORE /implement runs. Skipping ingest-tap means BaselineState never receives spans → emitter has nothing to evaluate → cue emission rate is zero → the chunk is functionally inert as shipped. Strong recommendation to keep ingest-tap in scope.

3. **Base error-rate floor + warm-up gate (Open question 3 resolved).** Chunk text says "3.0× error rate multiplier" — the multiplier applies to a base error rate (proposed `DEFAULT_BASE_ERROR_RATE: f64 = 0.01` = 1%) for ErrorRateSpike detection. Cues fire only when EWMA value ≥ `base_error_rate × multiplier` (= 0.03 = 3% with defaults) AND samples ≥ `MIN_EWMA_SAMPLES` (= 10) (warm-up gate to avoid noise during cold-start). The "multiplier" is NOT "× the EWMA itself" because that's mathematically degenerate at cold start. /implement Phase 1 may refine if a different semantic is preferred — anchor the test for whichever shape lands.

4. **Latency baseline reference (Open question 4 resolved).** Chunk text says "2.5× latency multiplier" applied to per-operation latencies. The cleanest implementation reads from the t-digest pair's **previous** bucket as the "baseline" (current bucket as the "live" signal); per chunk #61 `TDigestPair::swap_on_tick` semantics — the previous bucket holds the prior persist-interval's data. Cues fire when `live_p95 ≥ previous_p95 × thresholds.latency_multiplier`. If chunk #61 `TDigestPair` does NOT expose `previous_percentile(q)` API, /implement Phase 1 may need to add a minor accessor — flag as a sub-step if so. (Research did not confirm this API; check at /implement.)

5. **Tauri 2 shutdown hook surface (Open question 5 resolved).** Plan proposes attaching the `persist_on_shutdown` call via `tauri::Builder::default().run(|app_handle, event| match event { tauri::RunEvent::ExitRequested { .. } => { triage::contract::persist_on_shutdown(&state, &corpus_path); } _ => {} })`. If /implement Phase 1 finds the Tauri 2.10+ shutdown event semantics insufficient (e.g., shutdown event fires AFTER Tokio runtime stops, breaking the call), fall back to: (a) periodic persist via `run_persist_loop` covers most data; (b) on graceful Ctrl+C / SIGTERM signal-handler attached at `main()` start, hook via `tokio::signal::ctrl_c()` future spawned alongside emitter; (c) accept that an ungraceful exit loses ≤60s of baseline data (run_persist_loop covers most). Document the trade-off at /implement if the cleaner Tauri hook is unavailable.

6. **Test fixture reuse from chunk #61.** The `CapturingSubscriber` + `FieldCollector` struct in `crates/triage/src/baseline/mod.rs::tests` (lines 541-599) is ~60 lines. Three options for chunk #62 tests: (a) copy-paste into `crates/triage/src/cue/emitter.rs::tests` (~60 lines duplicated; simplest); (b) factor to `crates/triage/src/test_support.rs` shared module gated by `#[cfg(test)]` (cleaner but adds a module-structure decision); (c) leave duplicated and refactor across both modules when a 3rd consumer appears. **Plan recommends (a) for chunk #62** — duplication acceptable at small scale; (b) refactor when 3+ modules need the same fixture.

7. **CueKind selection.** Chunk #62 implements detection for `CueKind::ErrorRateSpike` + `CueKind::LatencyRegression` ONLY (the two kinds backed by chunk #61 EWMA + t-digest trackers). `RestartEvent` is chunk #63 territory. `ServiceWentSilent` requires absence-tracking (RollingWindow inactivity), feasible in chunk #62 if scope is acceptable but proposed as **out-of-scope this chunk** to keep the diff bounded; flag at /implement if user wants it. `RetryStorm` requires retry-correlation across spans, not chunk #62.

8. **Workspace dependency direction sanity.** ingest currently does NOT depend on triage; triage does NOT depend on ingest. The `SpanObserver` trait lives in ingest (its call site); the impl lives at pulse-app boundary (`baseline_observer.rs`) wrapping triage's BaselineState. pulse-app already depends on both ingest and triage. This preserves the arch §Cross-cutting Module dependency direction DAG.

9. **No bindings.ts regeneration expected.** Chunk #62 introduces no new TauRPC procedures. The `emit_taurpc_bindings` test in `pulse-app/src/main.rs::tests` is unchanged. However per testing.md Session Additions 2026-05-13 / 2026-05-17, the default-features nextest run during /implement may transiently overwrite bindings.ts (removing `mcp.*` namespace under default features). Post-test restore via `git checkout HEAD -- pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` BEFORE staging for commit; verify `grep -c '"mcp":' bindings.ts ≥ 1` immediately before `git add`.

10. **Bundled commit shape (out of /implement scope; for wrap-session).** When chunk #62 wraps, the natural Type 6 cascade is the arch §Occupied Resources update for `pulse://stream/attention-cues` + `cadence-triggers` channel — likely candidate for the first live test of Proposal 7 narrative-cascade scan (per session-handoff.md). Wrap-session may sequence this as the post-impl cascade.

Chunk #62 adds `triage.cue.tick` / `triage.cue.evaluate` / `triage.cue.emit` / `metric.cue.emit_count_total`.

Chunk #62 mirrors with `evaluate_thresholds(state: &BaselineState, thresholds: &Thresholds, now_nanos: i64) -> Vec<AttentionCue>` pure synchronous fn — testable without tokio runtime.

- `pulse-app/src/connection_router.rs` (full, 187 lines) — chunk #59 TauRPC router; **not** a chunk #62 pattern reference (no new TauRPC), but the `HeartbeatBindStatus` adapter (lines 27-44) demonstrates the trait-impl-at-pulse-app pattern that chunk #62 may need for `SpanObserver` (see below).

- `crates/buffer/src/retention.rs` (full, 422 lines) — canonical retention-task pattern. Key for chunk #62: `run_one_sweep` (line 56) is the testable async helper extracted from `run_retention` (line 34); chunk #62 should extract `run_one_emit_cycle` (or `evaluate_thresholds`) helper for the same purpose — testable without timer orchestration per testing.md Session Additions 2026-05-06. `#[tokio::test]` tests pattern (lines 346-403) drive `run_one_sweep` directly without spawning the outer loop.

- `pulse-app/src/streams.rs` (full, 122 lines) — Tauri Channel API ↔ broadcast topic plumbing for span/metric/log streams. **Chunk #62 does NOT need to extend this** — `pulse://stream/attention-cues` is emit-only at chunk #62 scope; the corresponding `streams.subscribe_attention_cues` IPC procedure (or extension to the existing `streams` namespace) lands in the future UI-consumption chunk. The broadcast topic constant + `AttentionCueBroadcast` sender live in `crates/triage/`; consumption is deferred.

- `crates/ui-bridge/src/contract.rs` (lines 1-200) — `Settings` struct (line 110) and `AppError` enum (line 16) definitions. Chunk #62 does NOT need to extend `Settings` (hardcoded threshold defaults this chunk; hot-reload + Settings extension lands in #86). `AppError` enum already has `Validation`/`Internal`/`Storage`/`Ingest` variants suitable for any future error path from chunk #62 emitter — no new variant needed.

Chunk #62 introduces NO new xtask commands. `cargo xtask capability-drift` (line 87) verifies TauRPC procedures sync; since chunk #62 has no new procedures, `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` list (defined later in xtask/src/main.rs) requires NO modification.

- **Broadcast topic naming + thin wrapper struct** (`crates/ingest/src/connection.rs:25-227`): `pub const STREAM_NAME_X: &str = "pulse://stream/{kebab-slug}";` + `pub struct XBroadcast { sender: broadcast::Sender<XPayload> }` + `new()` / `sender()` / `subscribe()` / `subscriber_count()` accessors + `Default` impl. Chunk #62 mirrors verbatim for `AttentionCueBroadcast` carrying `AttentionCue` from `triage::contract`.

- **Pure synchronous evaluation helper extracted from async loop** (`crates/buffer/src/retention.rs:56-108` + `crates/ingest/src/connection.rs:172-201`): testable without tokio paused-clock orchestration; called from the async loop body. Chunk #62 must extract `evaluate_thresholds(state: &BaselineState, thresholds: &Thresholds, now_nanos: i64) -> Vec<AttentionCue>` for direct unit-test invocation (per testing.md Session Additions 2026-05-06 + tests extract).

Chunk #62 emitter integration tests follow this shape; chunk #62 ALSO has the synchronous `evaluate_thresholds` direct-call path (no spawned task needed) for the threshold-classification matrix.

- **Tracing target convention `{module}.{operation}` + `metric.{module}.{measure}`** (`crates/triage/src/baseline/mod.rs:43-50`): chunk #61 already uses `triage.baseline.tick` / `metric.baseline.ewma_short_window_size` / `pipeline.l1b.persist_count_total`. Chunk #62 follows the same shape: `triage.cue.tick` (heartbeat tick) / `triage.cue.evaluate` (evaluation span) / `triage.cue.emit` (per-emission span) / `metric.cue.emit_count_total` (counter per route §3 amendment).

- **In-process `CapturingSubscriber` + `FieldCollector` for asserting tracing event field VALUES** (`crates/triage/src/baseline/mod.rs:541-599`): chunk #61's own test pattern, ALREADY in this crate. Chunk #62 tests reuse the existing struct via `#[cfg(test)] use crate::baseline::tests::CapturingSubscriber` — but actually it's defined in a local `mod tests`, so chunk #62 tests can copy-paste the ~60-line struct OR factor it to a shared test util module. Lighter touch: copy-paste into cue tests (~60 lines duplicated; acceptable given module-test scope).

- **Const-bound default thresholds at module level** (`crates/plugins/src/engine.rs::MAX_WASM_HTTP_FIELDS_SIZE_BYTES` per security plan precedent + `crates/ingest/src/connection.rs:39-44` IDLE_THRESHOLD_NANOS / STALLED_THRESHOLD_NANOS): chunk #62 declares `pub const DEFAULT_ERROR_RATE_MULTIPLIER: f64 = 3.0;` + `pub const DEFAULT_LATENCY_MULTIPLIER: f64 = 2.5;` + `pub const DEFAULT_TICK_INTERVAL: Duration = Duration::from_secs(1);` + `pub const DEFAULT_MIN_PERSISTENCE_SECONDS: u64 = 30;` (matches chunk #59's 30s stalled threshold rough magnitude). Module-level `const _: () = { assert!(...) };` sanity blocks per testing.md Session Additions 2026-05-11 if invariants warrant.

- **Trait-in-lower-crate + impl-in-pulse-app pattern for cross-crate state delivery** (`crates/ingest/src/connection.rs:160-164` `ReceiverBindStatus` trait + `pulse-app/src/connection_router.rs:27-44` `HeartbeatBindStatus` adapter): canonical pattern for delivering state into a workspace-boundary-clean crate. Chunk #62 likely needs the parallel `SpanObserver` trait in `crates/ingest/` so ingest's hot path can invoke `BaselineState::observe_span` without ingest depending on triage. **Verify at /implement Phase 1 whether this trait is required OR a lighter alternative exists** (see Open questions below).

- **Workspace-deps already present** (chunk #61 added tdigest / dashmap / bincode); chunk #62 introduces NO new workspace dependencies. The cargo deny `multiple-versions` check stays single-canary (`tonic 0.14 ↔ 0.13`).

- **Module visibility:** `crates/triage/src/lib.rs` declares `pub mod contract` + `pub(crate) mod cue`. Chunk #62 keeps `cue` as `pub(crate)`; expand to `crates/triage/src/cue/{mod.rs, emitter.rs, evaluate.rs, classify.rs, thresholds.rs, broadcast.rs}` directory if size warrants. Public surface via `triage::contract::*` re-exports only — no new top-level `pub use` outside contract (per arch §Conventions Module visibility discipline + chunk #60 precedent).

- **Contract re-exports**: chunk #61's pattern at `crates/triage/src/contract.rs:8-17` re-exports baseline primitives via `pub use crate::baseline::{...}`. Chunk #62 adds analogous block: `pub use crate::cue::{AttentionCueEmitter, AttentionCueBroadcast, Thresholds, STREAM_NAME_ATTENTION_CUES, evaluate_thresholds, start_emitter, DEFAULT_ERROR_RATE_MULTIPLIER, DEFAULT_LATENCY_MULTIPLIER, DEFAULT_TICK_INTERVAL};` (or similar — final set settled at /implement).

- **Derive constants for `AttentionCue::PartialEq` not `Eq`** (contract.rs:117): `AttentionCue` already derives `PartialEq` (the f64 fields prevent `Eq`). Chunk #62 tests assert payload equality via `PartialEq` — sufficient for the field set since `f64::NaN != f64::NaN` is desired behavior.

- **`#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]` for enum-tagged JSON serialization** (contract.rs:22-90): all enums in `triage::contract` use snake_case. Chunk #62's tracing event field values that carry enum tags (e.g., `kind = "error_rate_spike"`, `priority = "suggested"`) use the lowercase / snake_case form via `serde_json::to_string(&variant).unwrap()` OR a const lookup table `fn cue_kind_label(k: CueKind) -> &'static str`. Per the obs `metric.cue.emit_count_total{kind, priority}` cardinality discipline (combined.md obs row), tracing event field values must be STRING-typed; `CapturingSubscriber` will see them as `String`s.

- **`tokio::time::interval` first-tick-fires-immediately discipline** (`crates/buffer/src/retention.rs:43-44` + `crates/ingest/src/connection.rs:243`): both chunk #20 retention and chunk #59 connection-state pollers acknowledge `tokio::time::interval` fires immediately on first poll; both call `interval.tick().await;` once at top to skip the immediate fire. Chunk #62 emitter follows the same pattern.

- **`broadcast::Sender::send()` returns Result with `Err` when no subscribers — silently ignore**: pattern at connection.rs:258 (`let _ = broadcast_handle.sender().send(payload);`). Chunk #62 emitter mirrors — no-subscribers is a benign state (broadcast still useful for future subscribers; cue lost is acceptable until UI consumption chunk lands).

- **Severity field semantics matching design extract**: route §62 says "priority_tier classification (Hard / Medium / Baseline based on confidence and magnitude)". Code uses `Autonomous` / `Suggested` / `Curious`. The mapping convention is: high-confidence-high-magnitude → `Autonomous`; medium-confidence-or-medium-magnitude → `Suggested`; low-confidence-or-low-magnitude → `Curious`. Threshold details fixed in `classify(magnitude, confidence, persistence_seconds) -> PriorityTier`. Tier-2 (`Suggested`) is the value that additionally emits to `cadence-triggers` channel per route §62 text.

- `crates/triage/src/cue/mod.rs` — module entry point. Declares `mod emitter; mod evaluate; mod classify; mod thresholds; mod broadcast;` + `pub use` of public types. Replaces the current 2-line `crates/triage/src/cue.rs` stub (the existing single-file `cue.rs` is converted to a directory; Cargo handles either form transparently).

- `crates/triage/src/cue/thresholds.rs` — `pub struct Thresholds { error_rate_multiplier: f64, latency_multiplier: f64, tick_interval: Duration, min_persistence_seconds: u64 }` + `impl Default for Thresholds` reading hardcoded const defaults + `pub const DEFAULT_ERROR_RATE_MULTIPLIER: f64 = 3.0;` + `pub const DEFAULT_LATENCY_MULTIPLIER: f64 = 2.5;` + `pub const DEFAULT_TICK_INTERVAL: Duration = Duration::from_secs(1);` + `pub const DEFAULT_MIN_PERSISTENCE_SECONDS: u64 = 30;` + `serde::Deserialize` derive for future config-file path (validated via `serde` bounded-range rejection per security extract).

- `crates/triage/src/cue/classify.rs` — `pub fn classify_priority(magnitude: f64, confidence: f64, persistence_seconds: u64) -> PriorityTier` pure synchronous classifier. Heuristic suggestion (final values pinned at /implement): magnitude≥5 ∧ confidence≥0.9 ∧ persistence≥30s → `Autonomous`; magnitude≥3 ∧ confidence≥0.7 → `Suggested`; else → `Curious`. Plus `pub fn dual_condition_bypass(magnitude: f64, absolute_value: f64, kind: CueKind) -> bool` per P-057 (magnitude > 10× OR absolute_error_rate > 5% → bypass restart-window suppression).

- `crates/triage/src/cue/evaluate.rs` — pure synchronous evaluator: `pub fn evaluate_thresholds(state: &BaselineState, thresholds: &Thresholds, now_nanos: i64) -> Vec<AttentionCue>`. Iterates per-service via `state.services` DashMap iteration (mirroring `swap_tdigest_pairs_on_tick`'s pattern); for each service computes EWMA error rate vs threshold (a constant `BASE_ERROR_RATE: f64 = 0.01` representing the 1% nominal threshold the multiplier multiplies); for each (service, operation) computes p95 latency vs baseline; for each above-threshold case constructs `AttentionCue` with classified `priority_tier`. Returns `Vec<AttentionCue>` for caller to emit.

- `crates/triage/src/cue/broadcast.rs` — `pub const STREAM_NAME_ATTENTION_CUES: &str = "pulse://stream/attention-cues";` + `pub struct AttentionCueBroadcast { sender: broadcast::Sender<AttentionCue> }` + `new() / sender() / subscribe() / subscriber_count() / Default` mirroring `ingest::connection::ConnectionBroadcast`. Plus `pub struct CadenceTriggerChannel { sender: broadcast::Sender<AttentionCue> }` (broadcast for fan-out symmetry with attention-cues; in-process; consumed by chunk #72 Cadence Coordinator). Capacity constant `const BROADCAST_CAPACITY: usize = 32` (matches connection precedent).

- `crates/triage/src/cue/emitter.rs` — async loop wiring: `pub async fn start_emitter(state: Arc<BaselineState>, broadcast_handle: Arc<AttentionCueBroadcast>, cadence_handle: Arc<CadenceTriggerChannel>, thresholds: Arc<Thresholds>)` + `#[tracing::instrument(skip_all, fields(cues_evaluated, cues_emitted, services_tracked))]` on the tick-body helper. Each tick: call `evaluate_thresholds(...)` → emit each cue to broadcast → tier-2 (`PriorityTier::Suggested`) cues additionally emit to cadence-triggers channel → emit `triage.cue.tick` heartbeat with structural counts + `metric.cue.emit_count_total` event per cue.

- `crates/ingest/src/observer.rs` (NEW; new module within ingest crate) — `pub trait SpanObserver: Send + Sync { fn observe_span(&self, service_name: &str, operation_name: &str, status_code: u8, latency_ms: u64, now_nanos: i64); }`. Lives in ingest because ingest is the call site; impl lives at pulse-app boundary. Mirrors `ingest::connection::ReceiverBindStatus` trait precedent.

data.head: ### Chunk route#63: "Restart event detector + dual-condition bypass"

body: **Domain relevance:**
- (security) partially-relevant — outbound broadcast topic + tracing discipline + config field validation + telemetry-as-user-content classification
- (tests) fully-relevant — pure-Rust algorithmic logic with high unit-test surface area; rstest table-driven bypass scenarios; channel subscription contract
- (obs) relevant — new tick task, new AllowList entries (6 targets), new bypass metric, heartbeat-stall discipline
- (arch) relevant — workspace placement, broadcast topic registry-grade identifier, cross-bridge data shape, module dependency direction
- (design) out-of-scope — pure backend, no React component, no design tokens consumed
- (layouts) out-of-scope — no surface/region/component/focus-order entry created
- (a11y) out-of-scope — no UI surface introduced, no WCAG criterion exercised
**Constraints across domains:**

- (security) Restart event evidence on `pulse://stream/restart-events` MUST be redacted to OTLP-derived identifiers only (service.name + last-seen-ts + gap duration) — NEVER raw OTLP attribute values or span content payloads (per security plan §Logging & Monitoring NEVER-log list).

- (security) Cue suppression decisions emitted to `tracing` MUST NOT log AttentionCue evidence-derived attribute values — only `service_name` + `cue_kind` enum + `suppression_reason` enum + `bypass_triggered` bool (per security plan §Logging & Monitoring NEVER-log list rows 1, 4).

- (security) Dual-condition bypass thresholds (`magnitude_bypass_multiplier`, `absolute_bypass_threshold`) MUST go through `serde` deserialization with bounded numeric range checks (multiplier > 1.0, threshold ∈ (0.0, 1.0]) per security plan §Input Validation row "Configuration values".
- (security) Broadcast payload size MUST be capped before `Channel::send` per security plan §Input Validation row "Tauri IPC Channel API streaming payloads".

- (security) Restart-window suppression MUST be surgical-not-blanket: explicit allowlist of suppressable cue kinds (`ErrorRateSpike` with `persistence < 30s`) + persistence/window bounds, NOT a blanket "skip all cues" branch (per security plan §Security Anti-Patterns + chunk spec behavioral note).

- (security) All new `serde::Deserialize` structs for restart event payloads + suppression config MUST use smart enum types for kind/reason fields (per security plan §Input Validation row "TauRPC bridge" + §Established Decisions Validation Library).

- (security) Process command surface is FORBIDDEN — restart detection MUST derive solely from in-process OTLP-derived signals; NEVER `tokio::process::Command::new(...)` (per security plan §Security Anti-Patterns § Code Patterns row 1).

- (tests) Coverage gate Standard tier: ≥75% line / ≥70% branch / ≥85% function via `cargo-llvm-cov` 0.8.5 for `crates/triage/pattern/` + modified `crates/triage/cue/` (per test-plan §10 Quality Gates + §4).
- (tests) Tests co-located inside the modified crates as `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { … }` within `crates/triage/src/pattern/*.rs` and `crates/triage/src/cue/*.rs` (per test-plan §4 + arch convention).
- (tests) All new tests MUST use `rstest` 0.26.1 fixture pattern; dual-condition bypass (8×/3%, 12×/4%, 6×/7%) is natural `#[rstest]` table-driven parametric (per test-plan §7 Fixture library + §4).

- (tests) Synthetic span stream fixtures driving restart-gap detection MUST avoid chunk #54 collision trap (>250 spans need monotonic counter ≥3 bytes of `span_id`) (per testing.md §Session Additions 2026-05-14).

- (tests) Deterministic time discipline: gap-detection logic MUST be driven via `tokio::time::pause()` + `tokio::time::advance(Duration)`; NEVER real time without injection (per testing.md §Synchronization + test-plan §11 Anti-Patterns Universal).
- (tests) `start_paused = true` × `flavor = "current_thread"` constraint: timing tests MUST drop `flavor = "multi_thread"` (per testing.md §Session Additions 2026-05-06).

- (tests) Cue-emission verification MUST use in-process `CapturingSubscriber` `tracing::Subscriber` pattern (`with_default` sync / `set_default` async); NOT `tracing-test` crate (per testing.md §Session Additions 2026-05-07 + 2026-05-09 + 2026-05-11).
- (obs) All new tracing events MUST use `tracing` 0.1 macros only — NO OTel SDK / Meter / Counter / Histogram instruments (per obs-plan §3 "NO OTel SDK linked into the self-observation runtime").

- (obs) Bypass-trigger metric emitted as `tracing::info!(target: "metric.pipeline.l2.magnitude_bypass_triggered_total", value = 1, reason = "relative" | "absolute", ...)` per `metric.{module}.{measure}` convention; `reason` bounded cardinality (exactly 2 values) (per obs-plan §5 Metric naming conventions).

- (obs) RestartDetector tick task MUST emit `tracing::info!(target: "triage.pattern.tick", ...)` every 15s via `tokio::time::interval(Duration::from_secs(15))`; absence >45s = stall signal that fails CI build (per obs-plan §3 Heartbeat ticks + §10 SLO invariants).
- (obs) Restart event emission MUST log only metadata fields — `service.name` allowed, NEVER span content/attributes (per obs-plan §8 Vector 1 + project rule observability.md PII scrubbing).

- (obs) Suppression decisions MUST emit at `info` level with structured fields (`suppression_bypassed: bool`, `bypass_reason: "relative" | "absolute" | "none"`, `service`, `restart_window_active: bool`); the `suppression_bypassed` field already registered at `pulse-app/src/observability.rs:1068` (chunk #62 AllowList) (per obs-plan §6 + §8).

- (obs) Span naming follows `{module}.{operation}` convention: `triage.pattern.restart_detect`, `triage.pattern.restart_emit`, `triage.cue.suppression_check`, `triage.cue.suppression_bypass` — avoid high-cardinality names (per obs-plan §4).

- (obs) Broadcast payload size discipline: emit only `service` (scrubbed) + `gap_seconds` + `last_seen_unix_nano` + `resume_unix_nano`; NEVER triggering span content (per obs-plan §11 Anti-Patterns size cap analog).

- (arch) Work lands inside `crates/triage/pattern` (RestartDetector) + `crates/triage/cue` (suppression rules) — both already declared in `crates/triage/src/lib.rs` per chunk #60 scaffold; `triage` already reserved in arch §Occupied Resources Cargo workspace crate names (LOCKED).

- (arch) Broadcast topic name MUST be exactly `pulse://stream/restart-events` per chunk #63 spec — conforms to `pulse://stream/*` naming convention at arch §Occupied Resources + §Standard Contracts Real-time push contract.

- (arch) Anticipated arch registry delta is one entry under §Occupied Resources Tauri IPC events (broadcast channels) via Type 6 amendment `/andromeda-evolve --allow-arch-registry` POST-impl (per arch §Architecture Registry Updates 2026-05-17 precedent).

- (arch) Zero TauRPC procedure delta — no `pulse-app/capabilities/` JSON edit, no `xtask EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` extension, no `emit_taurpc_bindings` test update (per arch §Cross-cutting "Webview IPC capability policy" 4-place binding only triggers when new TauRPC procedure lands).

- (arch) Module dependency direction inside triage: `cue::evaluate` MAY depend on `pattern` (restart window state) within the same crate; cross-crate dep direction unchanged (`triage` depends on `curation::contract` + workspace common deps; no reverse edges) (per arch §Cross-cutting "Module dependency direction").
**Patterns to follow:**

- (security/arch) **Outbound broadcast topic shape**: existing `pulse://stream/connection-state` (chunk #59) + `pulse://stream/attention-cues` (chunk #62) — per-module `STREAM_NAME_*` `pub const &str` + `BROADCAST_CAPACITY: usize = 32` + thin `Clone`-able wrapper struct around `tokio::sync::broadcast::Sender<T>` with `new()` / `sender()` / `subscribe()` / `subscriber_count()`. Mirror at `crates/triage/src/pattern/broadcast.rs` with `STREAM_NAME_RESTART_EVENTS = "pulse://stream/restart-events"` (per security plan §Threat Model + arch §Standard Contracts Real-time push + chunk #62 precedent at `crates/triage/src/cue/broadcast.rs:8`).

Apply same pattern if restart detector internally signals cue emitter — internal channels without `pulse://` prefix do not occupy security-registry surfaces.

- (security) **Tracing redaction discipline**: existing `tracing` harness writes JSON to `~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/agent-latest.jsonl`; identifier-class fields only (`service_name`, `cue_kind` enum, `gap_seconds` numeric, `bypass_triggered` bool) per security plan §Logging proven at chunks #45 (basename), #47 (id), #59 (state enum).

- (security) **Config field bounded-validation**: `Settings::load_from_data_dir()` is the LOWER-COST path to expose `[triage.suppression.*]` to webview without new TauRPC namespace — sidesteps capability-drift triple binding per security.md §Session Additions 2026-05-09 entry 2.

- (security) **TauRPC namespace ban**: chunk spec declares "TauRPC delta: none yet" — DO NOT introduce new procedure for restart events; webview consumes `pulse://stream/restart-events` directly via existing Tauri Channel subscription pattern (per security.md §Session Additions 2026-05-12).

- (tests) **Reuse `tdigest` / `dashmap` / `bincode`** already landed at chunk #61 — restart-detector per-service last-seen tracking can reuse `dashmap` for concurrent-map state (no new workspace deps).

- (tests) **Channel subscription contract pattern** for new broadcast topic mirrors chunk #62's `pulse://stream/attention-cues` integration test scaffold at `crates/triage/src/cue/broadcast.rs` — subscribe via `tokio::sync::broadcast::Receiver`, trigger synthetic gap-then-resume, assert payload schema (per test-plan §5 + §6 P6).

- (tests) **Synthetic OTLP-stream fixture pattern**: `MockTraceSpan::builder()` (in `ingest`) supplies span input; restart-detector test feeds spans via internal API, advances `tokio::time` past 20s gap, emits resume span, asserts event broadcast (per test-plan §7 Self-bootstrapping).

- (tests) **Dual-condition bypass parametric coverage** (8×/3%, 12×/4%, 6×/7%): `#[rstest]` `#[case]` rows per scenario; each case = (relative_magnitude, absolute_rate, expected_bypass_decision). Assert (a) cue emitted DESPITE active restart window, (b) `pipeline.l2.magnitude_bypass_triggered_total{reason}` event fires with correct `reason` (per testing.md §Session Additions 2026-05-11 field-collector).

- (tests) **Threshold-config round-trip**: tests verify both default values (10× and 5%) when config absent + override via config file. Use `tempfile::TempDir` + `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR=$TMPDIR/test-$$` for per-test isolation.

- (obs) **Canonical triage-module tick pattern** from chunk #62 at `crates/triage/src/cue/emitter.rs:147` (`tokio::time::interval(thresholds.tick_interval)` + first-tick skip + per-cycle `run_one_emit_cycle`); chunk #63 RestartDetector follows same shape (per obs-plan §4 + §5).

- (obs) **AllowList block pattern** from chunks #61/#62 at `pulse-app/src/observability.rs:970-1080` — chunk #63 adds 6 new entries (`triage.pattern.tick` + `triage.pattern.restart_detect` + `triage.pattern.restart_emit` + `triage.cue.suppression_check` + `triage.cue.suppression_bypass` + `metric.pipeline.l2.magnitude_bypass_triggered_total`) as separate per-leaf entries (per observability.md §Session Additions 2026-05-07 exact-match precedence).

- (obs) **Precedent metric registry shape**: `metric.cue.emit_count_total` at `pulse-app/src/observability.rs:1075` with `{value, kind, priority, scope}` — register `metric.pipeline.l2.magnitude_bypass_triggered_total` with `{value, reason, service, kind}` (bounded cardinality on `reason`).
- (obs) **`pulse://stream/{topic}` broadcast emission pattern** from chunk #59 at `crates/ingest/src/connection.rs:25` — chunk #63 follows same Type 6 amendment registration path.

- (obs) **Boundary span pattern for suppression hook**: wrap cue-emit decision in `triage.cue.suppression_check` `#[instrument]` span emitting `info`-level event with `suppression_bypassed: bool` + `bypass_reason` enum; on bypass, same handler emits `metric.pipeline.l2.magnitude_bypass_triggered_total` event (per obs-plan §6 Boundary-call wrappers).

- (arch) **`triage::contract` re-export pattern** from chunks #60/#61/#62 at `crates/triage/src/contract.rs:23-30` — newly-introduced public API types (`RestartEvent` struct + broadcast wrapper + constants) re-exported from `crate::pattern::*` so downstream callers import one shape (per arch §Conventions "Module visibility discipline").

- (arch) **Internal in-process channel pattern** from chunk #62 `CHANNEL_NAME_CADENCE_TRIGGERS` at `crates/triage/src/cue/broadcast.rs:13` — if restart window state is shared between `pattern` detector and `cue` evaluator across module boundaries, use internal label without `pulse://` prefix.

- (arch) **TauRPC-free cross-crate state delivery pattern** (session 80 Session Additions 2026-05-16) — abstraction trait in lower crate, adapter impl in `pulse-app/`, `Arc<dyn Trait>` threaded through resolver constructor. Not needed this chunk; documented for chunk #80+ webview integration.
**Anti-patterns to avoid:**

- (security) NEVER include raw OTLP attribute values, span/log/metric content payloads, or full `instrumentation_scope.name` strings on `RestartEvent` payload — restart evidence is identifier-class only (per security plan §Logging NEVER-log list).

- (security/arch) NEVER make restart-window suppression a blanket "if-restart-active-skip-all-cues" branch — chunk spec demands surgical suppression (only `ErrorRateSpike` with `persistence < 30s` within 60s window). Blanket skip silently swallows real `LatencyOutlier` / `CardinalitySpike` / `MagnitudeBypass` cues that P-057 is designed to surface (per chunk spec behavioral note + arch §Cross-cutting + capability P-016).

- (security) NEVER spawn `tokio::process::Command::new(...)` for restart correlation against any OTLP/MCP/workspace-detector-sourced string — direct hit on MCP STDIO command-injection cluster (CVE-2025-49596 etc.) and §Security Anti-Patterns § Code Patterns row 1. Restart detection MUST be pure in-process gap-detection on `LastSpanSeenTracker` data structures.

- (tests) NEVER blanket-suppress all cues during restart window — test naming pattern: positive bypass assertions (`bypass_triggered_when_relative_magnitude_8x_absolute_rate_3pct_*`) NOT negative suppression assertions.

- (tests) NEVER use `sleep(N)` for sync between gap-emit and resume-emit — use deterministic time injection (`tokio::time::advance`) OR explicit broadcast-channel event subscription (per test-plan §11 + testing.md §Synchronization).
- (tests) NEVER assert restart-event payload via raw protobuf bytes — assert on decoded fields (`service_name`, `gap_duration_ms`, `resume_timestamp_ns`) (per test-plan §11).

- (tests) NEVER quarantine flaky timing tests with `#[ignore]` retry-once — flake = real bug; commonly missing `tokio::task::yield_now().await` between `advance()` and `recv()` (per test-plan §10 Zero-flakiness).
- (obs) NEVER log raw span attributes from the triggering span that caused gap detection — include only `attributes_count` + `service_name_tag` (per obs-plan §8 Vector 1 + §11).
- (obs) NEVER use high-cardinality span names for restart events (no `triage.pattern.restart_my-service-a`) — `service` belongs in fields, not span name (per obs-plan §11).

- (obs) NEVER emit the suppression / bypass metric at `trace` level inside a tight loop — cue-emit decision runs once per tick (1-2s cadence inherited from chunk #62); per-cycle `info`-level events are fine, but level-gate any per-event sub-evaluation (per obs-plan §11 Metrics).

- (arch) DO NOT create a new workspace member crate for the restart detector — chunk #63 is fully scoped to existing `crates/triage/{pattern,cue}` submodules; new crate would violate arch §Occupied Resources reserved-list discipline.

- (arch) DO NOT register `pulse://stream/restart-events` in arch §Occupied Resources via direct edit during /implement — the Type 6 amendment via `/andromeda-evolve --allow-arch-registry` is the canonical path AFTER impl lands (mirrors chunk #62 precedent).

- (arch) DO NOT introduce reverse cross-crate dependencies (e.g., `triage → ingest` or `triage → ui-bridge`) — arch §Cross-cutting "Module dependency direction" requires all deps flow toward `pulse-app`.
**Contract bindings:**

- **security ↔ obs**: Restart event + suppression + bypass events instrumented via existing `tracing` harness; identifier-class fields only on both sides. obs adds `metric.pipeline.l2.magnitude_bypass_triggered_total{reason}`; security ensures `reason` is an enum tag (e.g., `relative`, `absolute`), NOT free-form string from OTLP attribute value.

- **security ↔ arch**: New broadcast topic `pulse://stream/restart-events` requires arch §Occupied Resources Tauri IPC events acknowledgment via Type 6 amendment when impl lands (per route §3 chunk #63 entry + chunk #59 + chunk #62 precedents). Security side: the topic name + payload shape is part of the IPC trust-boundary surface, so arch acknowledgment also closes security-registry implicit drift.

- **tests ↔ obs**: New tracing metric `pipeline.l2.magnitude_bypass_triggered_total{reason: relative | absolute}` consumed by chunk's three bypass test scenarios. Tests MUST assert event-emission contract using `CapturingSubscriber` + `FieldCollector` pattern; obs domain MUST allow-list the new target string in PII scrubber. Without obs-side allowlist registration, scrubber redacts the `reason` field — test asserts on field value will fail.

- **tests ↔ arch (Occupied Resources)**: New broadcast topic `pulse://stream/restart-events` is registry-grade identifier requiring Type 6 amendment `--allow-arch-registry` when chunk #63 impl lands. Integration test asserting subscription contract works PRE-amendment (broadcast topics are tokio-channel for internal subscribers), but capability-drift gate cleanliness requires post-impl arch update.

- **tests ↔ standard-gate baseline**: chunk plan §Test Commands MUST include FULL standard gate set: `cargo fmt --check` + `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` + `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` + `cargo xtask capability-drift`. Webview gates EXCLUDED (chunk #63 is pure Rust per chunk spec).
- **tests ↔ boot-smoke discipline**: chunk #63 does NOT touch boot/setup paths — `npx @tauri-apps/cli dev` smoke gate is NOT required.

- **tests ↔ bindings.ts canonical-state discipline**: chunk #63 adds no new TauRPC procedures (only internal tokio broadcasts), so `emit_taurpc_bindings` four-place-binding cascade is NOT required. (But if mid-session default-features test runs overwrite `pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts`, pre-commit recovery via `cargo nextest run -p pulse-app --features mcp-server -E 'test(emit_taurpc_bindings)'` before `git add` per testing.md §Session Additions 2026-05-17.)

body: _Generated by /andromeda-phase Phase 4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not edit during /implement run._
- **Phase number:** 59

  - route#63 "Restart event detector + dual-condition bypass" (Epoch 9 — Foundation v0.2.0 seventh chunk; depends on #60 triage scaffold + #62 cue emitter — both implemented and committed)
- **Epoch:** Epoch 9 — Foundation v0.2.0

Chunk #63 closes the L1b → L2 distillation loop: introduce a per-service `RestartDetector` in `crates/triage/src/pattern/` that emits `RestartEvent` payloads to a new broadcast topic `pulse://stream/restart-events` whenever an OTLP span gap exceeds 20s followed by a resume, then wire surgical suppression into the chunk #62 cue emitter so `ErrorRateSpike` cues with `persistence < 30s` are dropped during a 60s post-restart window — EXCEPT when the dual-condition magnitude bypass (P-057) trips (relative magnitude > 10× baseline OR absolute error rate > 5%). The bypass overrides restart suppression so catastrophic regressions remain visible during restart-induced noise (per chunk spec behavioral note + capability P-016 surgical-not-blanket invariant). Configurable thresholds via the existing `Thresholds` struct (extended with `magnitude_bypass_multiplier`, `absolute_bypass_error_rate`, `absolute_bypass_latency_ms`, `restart_gap_threshold_seconds`, `restart_suppression_window_seconds`, `suppression_persistence_cutoff_seconds`) preserve the chunk #62 hardcoded-defaults-now / hot-reload-later cadence (per chunk spec note "Threshold multipliers loaded from config or hardcoded defaults for now; hot-reload wiring added in #86"). Capabilities enabled: P-015 (Restart Event Detection) + P-016 (Restart-Window Suppression Surgical) + P-057 (Dual-Condition Suppression Bypass). Per arch + obs extracts, the broadcast handle stays internal to `crates/triage/` this chunk (no Tauri stream subscription yet — that lands at chunk #80+); the topic name is nevertheless a registry-grade identifier requiring a Type 6 amendment (`/andromeda-evolve --allow-arch-registry`) post-impl, mirroring chunks #59/#62 precedent.

data.head: ### Per route#63: "Restart event detector + dual-condition bypass"

body: 1. **Restructure `pattern.rs` to a directory module.** Delete `crates/triage/src/pattern.rs` (3-line stub) and create `crates/triage/src/pattern/mod.rs` mirroring `cue/mod.rs:1-42` shape: `mod broadcast; mod detector; mod suppression;` + `pub use` re-export block surfacing the new public API (`RestartEvent`, `RestartEventBroadcast`, `STREAM_NAME_RESTART_EVENTS`, `BROADCAST_CAPACITY`, `RestartDetector`, `run_one_detect_cycle`, `start_restart_detector`, `SuppressionState`, `evaluate_with_suppression`) + `pub(crate) const TARGET_PATTERN_TICK / TARGET_PATTERN_RESTART_DETECT / TARGET_PATTERN_RESTART_EMIT / TARGET_CUE_SUPPRESSION_CHECK / TARGET_CUE_SUPPRESSION_BYPASS / TARGET_METRIC_MAGNITUDE_BYPASS` tracing-target literals. `lib.rs:16` declaration `pub(crate) mod pattern;` is unchanged (Rust resolves module to either `pattern.rs` OR `pattern/mod.rs` transparently).

2. **Create `crates/triage/src/pattern/broadcast.rs` mirroring `cue/broadcast.rs:1-163` exactly.** Constants: `STREAM_NAME_RESTART_EVENTS: &str = "pulse://stream/restart-events"` + `BROADCAST_CAPACITY: usize = 32`. New struct `RestartEvent` with fields `service: String, gap_seconds: u64, last_seen_unix_nano: i64, resume_unix_nano: i64` (PII-redacted-by-construction per security plan §Logging NEVER-log list — no span/log/metric content payloads, no `instrumentation_scope.name`) + `#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]`. `RestartEventBroadcast` wrapper struct over `tokio::sync::broadcast::Sender<RestartEvent>` with `new() / sender() / subscribe() / subscriber_count()` + `Clone` + `Default` impls. Co-located `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` with 8 tests: subscribers_zero / subscribe_increment / round_trips_payload / send_no_subscribers_benign / stream_name_matches_pulse_uri_convention (asserts string starts with `pulse://stream/` AND equals `"pulse://stream/restart-events"` verbatim) / payload_serde_round_trips_through_serde / payload_has_no_pii_fields negative-canary (asserts payload struct fields are exactly the 4 identifier-class fields enumerated; no fields containing `attribute`, `span_id`, `trace_id`, `scope_name`, `body`, `description` substrings) / broadcast_capacity_matches_cue_precedent.

3. **Create `crates/triage/src/pattern/detector.rs`.** `RestartDetector` struct holds `last_seen: DashMap<String, i64>` (service → last_seen_unix_nano) + `last_emit: DashMap<String, i64>` (service → resume_unix_nano of last emitted RestartEvent, used to suppress duplicate emissions within a tick interval). Methods: `pub fn new() -> Self` / `pub fn observe_span(&self, service: &str, ts_unix_nano: i64)` (drops empty `service` per chunk #61 discipline; updates `last_seen` if new ts > current; also detects gap-then-resume in one method if the gap from previous `last_seen` to incoming `ts_unix_nano` exceeds the configured threshold) / `pub fn run_one_detect_cycle(&self, broadcast: &RestartEventBroadcast, now_nanos: i64, gap_threshold_secs: u64) -> DetectCycleStats` (returns stats struct for tracing emission: `gap_threshold_seconds`, `services_tracked`, `restart_events_emitted`). `pub async fn start_restart_detector(detector: Arc<RestartDetector>, broadcast: Arc<RestartEventBroadcast>, tick_interval: Duration, gap_threshold_secs: u64)` follows `cue/emitter.rs:141-156` shape: `tokio::time::interval(tick_interval)` + first-tick skip + per-cycle `run_one_detect_cycle` + `tracing::info!(target: TARGET_PATTERN_TICK, value = 1u64, gap_threshold_seconds = ..., services_tracked = ..., restart_events_emitted = ...)`. Restart event emission: `tracing::info!(target: TARGET_PATTERN_RESTART_EMIT, cue_kind = "restart_event", gap_seconds = ...)`. Co-located `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` with 9+ tests including: `observe_span_with_empty_service_dropped` (per chunk #61 discipline) / `gap_below_threshold_does_not_emit` / `gap_above_threshold_then_resume_emits_one_event` / `gap_above_threshold_without_resume_does_not_emit` / `multiple_services_tracked_independently` / `tracing_emission_uses_identifier_class_fields_only` (CapturingSubscriber + FieldCollector negative-canary asserting `service` value appears but `secret-canary-token-12345` does NOT) / `restart_detector_tick_emits_heartbeat` / `detect_cycle_stats_match_emitted_count` / `restart_event_payload_excludes_attribute_values` (negative-canary: feed `observe_span("svc-x-with-secret-attr", ts)` then assert `RestartEvent.service == "svc-x-with-secret-attr"` but no other field contains an "attr" substring).

4. **Create `crates/triage/src/pattern/suppression.rs`.** `SuppressionState` struct holds `windows: DashMap<String, i64>` (service → suppression_window_end_unix_nano). Methods: `pub fn new() -> Self` / `pub fn record_restart(&self, event: &RestartEvent, window_seconds: u64)` opens a window ending at `event.resume_unix_nano + (window_seconds as i64) * 1_000_000_000` for `event.service` / `pub fn is_active(&self, service: &str, now_nanos: i64) -> bool` checks window membership / `pub fn evaluate_with_suppression(cues: Vec<AttentionCue>, state: &SuppressionState, thresholds: &Thresholds, now_nanos: i64) -> SuppressionOutcome` filters cues per the surgical rule (drop iff `cue.kind == ErrorRateSpike` AND `cue.persistence_seconds < thresholds.suppression_persistence_cutoff_seconds` (default 30s) AND `state.is_active(cue.scope_id.as_deref().unwrap_or(""), now_nanos)` AND `!cue.suppression_bypassed`); when a cue's `suppression_bypassed=true` causes it to survive during an active window, increment a `bypass_triggered_count` field + record `bypass_reason: "relative" | "absolute"` (derived from comparing `cue.magnitude > thresholds.magnitude_bypass_multiplier` vs `cue.absolute_value > thresholds.absolute_bypass_error_rate`). `SuppressionOutcome` struct: `cues_kept: Vec<AttentionCue>, cues_suppressed: usize, bypass_triggers: Vec<BypassTrigger>` where `BypassTrigger = { cue_kind: CueKind, reason: BypassReason }`. Co-located `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` with 12+ rstest-parametric tests covering the suppression-surgicality matrix + the three bypass scenarios (8×/3%, 12×/4%, 6×/7%) — see Acceptance Criteria below.

5. **Extend `crates/triage/src/cue/thresholds.rs::Thresholds`** with 6 new fields per Research §Files to modify: `magnitude_bypass_multiplier: f64` (default `DEFAULT_MAGNITUDE_BYPASS_MULTIPLIER = 10.0`), `absolute_bypass_error_rate: f64` (default `DEFAULT_ABSOLUTE_BYPASS_ERROR_RATE = 0.05`), `absolute_bypass_latency_ms: f64` (default `DEFAULT_ABSOLUTE_BYPASS_LATENCY_MS = 1000.0`), `restart_gap_threshold_seconds: u64` (default `DEFAULT_RESTART_GAP_THRESHOLD_SECONDS = 20`), `restart_suppression_window_seconds: u64` (default `DEFAULT_RESTART_SUPPRESSION_WINDOW_SECONDS = 60`), `suppression_persistence_cutoff_seconds: u64` (default `DEFAULT_SUPPRESSION_PERSISTENCE_CUTOFF_SECONDS = 30`). Extend `Default` impl, extend `validate()` (multiplier > 1.0 finite; error rate ∈ (0.0, 1.0] finite; latency_ms > 0.0 finite; durations > 0). Extend module-level `const _: () = { ... };` sanity block at lines 125-131. Extend the existing `default_thresholds_match_chunk_spec_constants` test + add 6 new `validate_rejects_*` tests for each new field.

6. **Modify `crates/triage/src/cue/classify.rs::dual_condition_bypass`** to accept `&Thresholds` (or `&SuppressionConfig`-shaped accessor) as a 4th parameter instead of using hardcoded thresholds. New signature: `pub fn dual_condition_bypass(magnitude: f64, absolute_value: f64, kind: CueKind, thresholds: &Thresholds) -> bool`. Body: `if magnitude > thresholds.magnitude_bypass_multiplier { return true; } match kind { ErrorRateSpike => absolute_value > thresholds.absolute_bypass_error_rate, LatencyRegression => absolute_value > thresholds.absolute_bypass_latency_ms, RestartEvent | ServiceWentSilent | RetryStorm => false, }`. Update the 2 callers in `cue/evaluate.rs` (lines 47-48 + 82-83) + extend the 7-case `dual_condition_bypass_matrix` rstest test + the `dual_condition_bypass_nan_inputs_return_false` test to pass `Thresholds::default()`.

7. **Modify `crates/triage/src/cue/evaluate.rs`** to thread the `Thresholds` reference into both `dual_condition_bypass` call sites (lines 47-48 + 82-83). No other behavioral change to `evaluate_thresholds` — it still returns the unfiltered `Vec<AttentionCue>`; suppression is applied downstream by `emitter::run_one_emit_cycle`.

8. **Modify `crates/triage/src/cue/emitter.rs::start_emitter` signature** to add `restart_broadcast: Arc<RestartEventBroadcast>` + `suppression_state: Arc<SuppressionState>` parameters. Tick loop body extended: (a) subscribe to `restart_broadcast` ONCE before the loop via `let mut rx = restart_broadcast.subscribe();`, (b) inside the loop body, drain pending restart events non-blockingly via `while let Ok(event) = rx.try_recv() { suppression_state.record_restart(&event, thresholds.restart_suppression_window_seconds); }` (handle `RecvError::Lagged` by re-subscribing + logging via `tracing::warn!`), (c) after `run_one_emit_cycle`'s `evaluate_thresholds` call, invoke `suppression::evaluate_with_suppression(cues, &suppression_state, &thresholds, now_nanos)` to filter, (d) iterate the `SuppressionOutcome.cues_kept` for emit step (broadcast + cadence-triggers), (e) for each entry in `SuppressionOutcome.bypass_triggers`, emit `tracing::info!(target: TARGET_METRIC_MAGNITUDE_BYPASS, value = 1u64, reason = trigger.reason_label(), cue_kind = cue_kind_label(trigger.cue_kind), priority = priority_tier_label(...))`, (f) per evaluated cue, emit `tracing::info!(target: TARGET_CUE_SUPPRESSION_CHECK, cue_kind = ..., persistence_seconds = ..., restart_window_active = ..., suppression_bypassed = ..., bypass_reason = ...)` so the suppression decision is observable. Tests: extend `crates/triage/src/cue/emitter.rs::tests` with 4+ new tests for the suppression integration (full-tick path with synthetic restart event + active window + bypass trigger).

9. **Modify `crates/triage/src/contract.rs`** to extend the `pub use` block at lines 12-30 with pattern-module re-exports: `pub use crate::pattern::{RestartEvent, RestartEventBroadcast, RestartDetector, SuppressionState, start_restart_detector, run_one_detect_cycle, STREAM_NAME_RESTART_EVENTS};` — note `BROADCAST_CAPACITY` already exported from `cue` module; aliasing to avoid collision is unnecessary (Rust `pub use` would error on duplicate, so use `pub use crate::pattern::BROADCAST_CAPACITY as RESTART_BROADCAST_CAPACITY` if pattern also re-exports a `BROADCAST_CAPACITY` const — preferable to omit pattern's re-export since both share the same value `32`). Decision: omit `BROADCAST_CAPACITY` re-export from pattern; share the chunk #62 export. No new contract-types tests; `RestartEvent` round-trip lives in `pattern/broadcast.rs::tests` per chunk #62 precedent (its `AttentionCue` round-trip lives in `contract.rs::tests` because the type itself is declared there).

10. **Extend `pulse-app/src/observability.rs::AllowList::production()`** after line 1080 with 6 new `by_target.insert(...)` entries (one per new tracing target leaf) — per Research §Files to modify field lists. Place the block after the chunk #62 block at lines 1026-1080 with a `// Chunk #63 — restart event detector + dual-condition bypass ...` comment header following the chunks #61/#62 commenting convention. Negative-canary tests in `pulse-app/src/observability.rs::tests` should add per-target redact tests for the 6 new entries (mirroring chunk #62 chunk #41 patterns referenced in testing.md Session Additions 2026-05-10 `tracing::warn!` target literal constraint).

11. **Wire boot in `pulse-app/src/main.rs`** per Research §Files to modify. Import block extension at line 16-19. After line 272 `let cue_broadcast = Arc::new(AttentionCueBroadcast::new());` add: `let restart_broadcast = Arc::new(RestartEventBroadcast::new()); let restart_detector = Arc::new(RestartDetector::new()); let suppression_state = Arc::new(SuppressionState::new());`. **Identify the existing span-observer wiring** (per Research §Open questions item 3 — `BaselineState::observe_span` is the chunk #61 sink; the wiring site is likely in `pulse-app/src/main.rs` setup closure OR `crates/buffer/src/`); add `RestartDetector::observe_span(service, ts_unix_nano)` as a parallel sink alongside `BaselineState`. Spawn the new detector task near line 552 with `tauri::async_runtime::spawn(start_restart_detector(restart_detector.clone(), restart_broadcast.clone(), thresholds.tick_interval, thresholds.restart_gap_threshold_seconds))`. Pass `restart_broadcast.clone()` + `suppression_state.clone()` as the new arguments to the existing `start_emitter(...)` spawn call (per Step 8 signature change).

Webview gates excluded (chunk touches zero `pulse-app/ui/**` paths). Boot smoke (`npx @tauri-apps/cli dev`) NOT required (chunk touches zero `pulse-app/src/main.rs` boot-failure paths beyond the well-tested Arc-broadcast spawn pattern; out of scope per `boot-smoke-coverage` trigger).
