data.head: ### Chunk route#9: "Heartbeat ticks mechanism — long-running subsystem tick interval (10–30s) + {module}.tick event format for ingest/buffer/viz/plugins"

body: **Constraints across domains:**

- (security) Heartbeat tick events MUST NOT log raw OTLP attribute values, span/log/metric content payloads, snapshot file contents, clipboard contents, or MCP tool response bodies — incidentally captured secrets from instrumented host applications (per security plan §Logging & Monitoring "What NEVER to log" + §Security Anti-Patterns § Logging row 1).

- (security) Heartbeat tick events MUST NOT log full plugin file paths — basename of canonicalized path only when emitting `plugins.tick` (per security plan §Logging & Monitoring + §Security Anti-Patterns § Logging row 2; binds к chunk #8's `pulse-app/src/observability.rs` `log_basename` helper).

- (security) Heartbeat tick events MUST NOT log DuckDB query parameter values — log query identifier + parameter count instead (per security plan §Security Anti-Patterns § Logging row 3); applies к `buffer.tick` and `viz.tick` payload shapes that surface query / retention metadata.

- (security) Heartbeat tick mechanism MUST use `tracing` + `tracing-subscriber` JSON only — NEVER instrument tick emission with an OTLP network exporter pointed at the product's own `:4317`/`:4318` ports (per security plan §Security Anti-Patterns § API + Cross-cutting Patterns Self-observation discipline).

- (security) Heartbeat tick payload field redaction MUST flow through the existing subscriber-layer redaction (chunk #8 `JsonWithDefaults` formatter + per-module `AllowList` whitelist) — NEVER perform redaction at log call sites (per security plan §Logging & Monitoring "Field redaction is applied at the subscriber layer").

- (security) If chunk #9 adds any new crate dependency, the new crate MUST land via Cargo.toml workspace pin + clean `cargo deny check bans licenses sources` + clean `cargo audit` (per security plan §Dependency Security CI integration); the `multiple-versions = "deny"` rule (`tonic 0.14 ↔ 0.13` canary) MUST stay outside any skip list.

- (obs) Tick interval MUST be `tokio::time::interval(Duration::from_secs(15))` for the four long-running subsystems (`ingest`, `buffer`, `viz`, `plugins`); a separate 100ms ticker is reserved for the realtime throughput counter only and is NOT covered by this chunk's stall-gate (per obs plan §3 Heartbeat ticks → Tick interval).

- (obs) Tick event format MUST be `tracing::info!(target: "{module}.tick", ..., "heartbeat")` emitted at `info` level with the fixed message string `"heartbeat"`, riding the same `tracing-subscriber` JSON file sink wired in chunk #7 (per obs plan §3 Heartbeat ticks → Tick event format + §6 Log Coverage `info` row).

- (obs) Per-module field allowlist contract: `ingest.tick` emits `span_count` + `buffer_capacity_pct` + `broadcast_subscribers`; `buffer.tick` emits `rows_ingested` + `retention_window_active` + `eviction_count` (mapped к §8 allowlist `rows_ingested` / `eviction_count` / `memory_bytes` / `retention_window_seconds`); `viz.tick` emits `query_latency_ms` + `subscribers_active`; `plugins.tick` emits `loaded_count` + `active_invocations` (per obs plan §1 Telemetry surfaces row Heartbeat ticks + §8 Default-deny allowlist).

- (obs) Stall threshold: missing tick for >45s on any of `ingest.tick` / `buffer.tick` / `viz.tick` / `plugins.tick` is the stall signal; `health` IPC command MUST expose the same fields synchronously (per obs plan §3 Heartbeat ticks → Stall detection + §10 Standard+ invariants).

- (obs) Tick events MUST NOT be over-instrumented as spans inside the timer body — bare `tracing::info!` macro calls only (no `#[instrument]`, no span guard, no `.in_current_span()`); the tick is a state snapshot, not a request-scoped operation (per obs plan §11 Telemetry Strategy + §11 Spans / Traces "NEVER hold a `tracing::Span` guard across `.await` points").

- (obs) Per-tick gauge naming: when a tick ALSO emits a `metric.{module}.{measure}` event, the metric event uses target prefix `metric.{module}.{measure}` with numeric `value` field — these are SEPARATE events from the `{module}.tick` heartbeat (per obs plan §5 Per-surface metric events).

- (obs) Tick task MUST be spawned with `tokio::spawn` on the same multi-threaded runtime as ingest/buffer; timer body MUST stay non-blocking and avoid synchronous I/O (per obs plan §3 Heartbeat ticks + §10 Heartbeat ticks invariant).

- (tests) Heartbeat unit tests MUST use `tokio::time::pause()` + `tokio::time::advance(Duration)` for deterministic clock control — never `std::thread::sleep`, never wall-clock waits, never real `tokio::time::interval` ticks (per test-plan §11 Universal "NEVER use real time without injection" + §7 Time-sensitive data row).

- (tests) Per-module heartbeat tasks MUST be unit-tested in their owning crate with co-located `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` blocks; spawn/cancel lifecycle is a public boundary (per test-plan §4 Conventions + §11 Unit "test public module boundaries").

- (tests) Tick-event log lines MUST be agent-parseable as JSON via `jq` against the harness `logs` command output (per test-plan §3 Log format Agent-parseable signals + §11 Universal "machine-parseable output").
- (tests) Heartbeat tests MUST be deterministic with zero retry budget; one flake = immediate quarantine (per test-plan §10 Zero-flakiness budget + §11 Quality "NEVER add retry-once policies").

- (tests) Heartbeat tasks MUST be cancellable on graceful shutdown — `cleanup` command must terminate within 5s SIGTERM window without hung timer tasks (per test-plan §3 5-command implementation `cleanup` + §1 5-Command Requirements Command 4).

- (tests) The tick event target naming convention `{module}.tick` MUST match the PII allowlist's `for_target` strip-suffix lookup wired in chunk #8 (per session-handoff "PiiScrubLayer's per-module allowlist already covers the .tick suffix" — orchestrator surfaces к user that test-plan §3 Log format is silent on tick-target naming convention).

- (arch) Heartbeat task ownership lives in the `pulse-app` binary crate (the runtime owner) per Module dependency direction "dependencies flow toward pulse-app; no library crate depends on a sibling unless its declared contract requires it" (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns row 8); library crates expose only the public contract function the heartbeat task calls.

- (arch) Tick target labels MUST use the reserved crate names verbatim (`ingest.tick`, `buffer.tick`, `viz.tick`, `plugins.tick`) — those four names are LOCKED in arch §Occupied Resources Cargo workspace crate names; no new crate name may be introduced for a heartbeat source.

- (arch) Heartbeat emission MUST go through the `tracing` ecosystem ONLY — never via OTLP self-dial — per arch §Established Decisions [Self-Observation] + §Cross-cutting Patterns "Self-observation discipline."

- (arch) Tokio primitives are LOCKED to the single multi-threaded runtime + `tokio::time::interval` family per arch §Stack + §Inherited Defaults; no second runtime, no `std::thread::sleep` heartbeat loop, no `crossbeam` substitute.

- (arch) If heartbeat exposes a freshness signal к the IPC introspection envelope, surface MUST conform to the locked `health` / `ready` envelopes — extending the `subsystems` map (health) or `checks` map (ready) is acceptable; introducing a new top-level IPC procedure is NOT (per arch §Conventions §Endpoint naming + §Cross-cutting Patterns "Webview IPC capability policy").

- (arch) Any new env var to tune the tick interval MUST live under the reserved `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_*` namespace AND be added to arch §Occupied Resources environment variables — current reserved set does NOT include a tick interval var; orchestrator should surface this к user before adding.

- (arch) Configuration units MUST follow arch §Conventions "Configuration units" — durations are seconds with explicit units in field names (e.g., `heartbeat_interval_seconds`), not millis or `Duration` strings.
**Patterns к follow:**

- (security) Subscriber-layer redaction via the chunk #8 `JsonFieldVisitor` (with per-module `AllowList` and `for_target` strip-suffix `.tick` lookup) — heartbeat targets `ingest.tick` / `buffer.tick` / `viz.tick` / `plugins.tick` resolve to allowlists already exercised by chunks #7-#8 (per security plan §Logging & Monitoring "Log format" + session-handoff §Key Decisions This Session).

- (security) Self-observation runtime is `tracing` + `tracing-subscriber` JSON + `tracing-appender` daily file sink ONLY — heartbeat ticks emit through the same `JsonWithDefaults` formatter that injects `service.name` / `service.version` / `deployment.environment` envelope (per security plan Cross-cutting Patterns Self-observation discipline + chunk #7 already-implemented harness).

- (security) Sensitive payload fields MUST surface as numeric counts / identifiers / aggregates (e.g., `eviction_count`, `memory_bytes`, `mpsc_capacity_pct`, `subscribers`, `frame_duration_ms`) — never as raw OTLP attribute strings (per security plan §Security Anti-Patterns § Logging row 3 DuckDB parameter-count idiom).

- (obs) **Bare `tracing::info!` per tick (no span guard)**: emit one structured event per interval per module with the fixed message `"heartbeat"` and module-prefixed target (per obs plan §3 Heartbeat ticks → Tick event format + handoff).

- (obs) **`{module}.tick` target taxonomy**: the four targets are reserved for stall detection; do NOT introduce additional `*.tick` targets and do NOT collapse the four into a shared `app.tick` target — the CI gate parses each independently (per obs plan §10 CI gates).

- (obs) **Field-arg cheapness**: tick fields are simple primitives (`u64` / `f64` / `usize`) read from already-tracked counters; do NOT format expensive payloads inside the timer body (no `format!`, no `serde_json::to_string`) (per obs plan §11 Metrics anti-patterns).

- (obs) **Trace context at tick boundary**: ticks are NOT request-scoped; do NOT synthesize a fake trace_id field. The `service.name` / `service.version` / `deployment.environment` / `ci.run.id` / `git.commit.sha` default fields injected by chunk #7's `JsonWithDefaults` formatter are sufficient identity (per obs plan §3 Service identity + §9 CI-specific default fields).

- (obs) **Health command parity**: the `health` TauRPC command exposes the same per-subsystem snapshot fields the ticks emit, so the source of truth (a `Arc<AtomicU64>` counter / channel-capacity probe / `COUNT(*)` etc.) MUST be readable both from the tick task AND the health handler. Plumb the shared state once; the tick reads + emits, the health handler reads + returns (per obs plan §3 Heartbeat ticks → Stall detection + chunk #4 health command established).

- (tests) Co-located `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` per crate with `#[tokio::test(start_paused = true)]` for clock-driven tests — pattern shown in test-plan §4 Conventions + §7 Time-sensitive data row + §8 Mocking time row (the retention-test pattern is the direct template).
- (tests) `rstest` 0.26.1 fixtures with `#[fixture]` decorators for shared heartbeat task harness (per test-plan §4 Fixture pattern at unit level).

- (tests) Builder factory pattern for constructing per-module tick test inputs (Rust builders, not raw struct literals) — consistent with test-plan §3 Test data bootstrap + §7 Self-bootstrapping requirement.

- (tests) Per-process test isolation via `cargo-nextest` 0.9.x — heartbeat tests share the global `tokio::time` clock pause state, so per-process isolation prevents cross-test interference (per test-plan §3 Bootstrap phase 1 + §4 Framework + §9 Pipeline structure).

- (tests) Harness `logs` command parsing pattern: `RUST_LOG=debug cargo nextest run … 2>&1 | tee target/test-run.log` then `jq 'select(.target | startswith("buffer.tick"))' target/test-run.log` for tick-event verification (per test-plan §3 5-command implementation `logs` + Agent parsing example).

- (arch) **Tick task ownership in pulse-app, library crate exposes a public contract callable**: each of the four library crates exposes a small `pub` "snapshot the heartbeat payload" function that pulse-app's heartbeat task calls every interval; the library crate does not own the timer (per arch §Project Intent §Template patterns + §Cross-cutting Patterns "Module dependency direction").

- (arch) **Heartbeat events flow through the existing JSON `tracing-subscriber` stack from chunk #7**: `tracing::info!(target: "{module}.tick", ...)` — no new log sink, no new crate dependency. The existing `JsonWithDefaults` formatter from `pulse-app/src/observability.rs` already injects `service.name` / `service.version` / `deployment.environment` fields.

- (arch) **Field shape on the tick event matches the per-module heartbeat-payload taxonomy from §Standard Contracts `health` / `ready` checks**: `ingest_mpsc_capacity_pct`, `broadcast_subscribers`, `plugins_loaded`, etc. are the existing field-name vocabulary; tick events should reuse field names where the payload is the same metric (avoid `ingest_pct` vs `ingest_mpsc_capacity_pct` drift).

- (arch) **Rust naming convention for per-module module/function**: `snake_case` for the `pub fn heartbeat_payload()`, `UpperCamelCase` for the payload struct (e.g., `IngestHeartbeat`), per arch §Conventions "Variable / function naming."
**Anti-patterns к avoid:**

- (security) NEVER include any OTLP-derived attribute string, plugin source path, DuckDB SQL fragment, snapshot/clipboard/MCP body, or secret-list value in tick event field values (per security plan §Logging & Monitoring "What NEVER to log" + §Security Anti-Patterns § Logging rows 1-3, 5).

- (security) NEVER add an OTel SDK or `opentelemetry-otlp` exporter for heartbeat emission — pointing self-telemetry at own `:4317`/`:4318` is infinite recursion (per security plan §Security Anti-Patterns § API + Cross-cutting Patterns Self-observation discipline).

- (security) NEVER perform redaction at the heartbeat call site — redaction MUST live in the subscriber-layer formatter so future telemetry call sites cannot regress (per security plan §Logging & Monitoring + chunk #8 architectural decision in `.claude/rules/observability.md`).
- (obs) NEVER over-instrument the tick body with `#[tracing::instrument]` + nested child spans (per obs plan §11 Telemetry Strategy + §11 Spans/Traces).

- (obs) NEVER include unbounded labels in tick fields (e.g., `service_name` from external OTLP, per-trace-ID values, arbitrary request paths) — bounded enumerated values only (per obs plan §11 Metrics + §5 Metric label cardinality discipline).

- (obs) NEVER emit ticks at `debug` or `trace` level (would drop in production `EnvFilter::info` default and break the §10 CI stall gate); NEVER emit at `warn` / `error` level (would pollute panic-detection grep) — `info` only with the `"heartbeat"` message string (per obs plan §6 Log levels + §10 CI gates).
- (obs) NEVER format the timestamp manually inside the tick body — chunk #7's `JsonWithDefaults` formatter is the single timestamp authority (per obs plan §6 Required fields + §10 CI gates).
- (tests) NEVER use `std::time::Instant::now()` / `chrono::Utc::now()` / wall-clock `tokio::time::sleep` in heartbeat tests (per test-plan §11 Universal "NEVER use real time").
- (tests) NEVER assert on tick wall-clock cadence — assert on advance-driven invariants instead (per test-plan §11 E2E "NEVER use `sleep(N)` for synchronization").
- (tests) NEVER share mutable state across parallel heartbeat tests (per test-plan §11 Test Data).
- (tests) NEVER mock `tokio::time::interval` itself — use the built-in `pause()` / `advance()` API (per test-plan §11 Mocking).

- (arch) Do NOT introduce a new TauRPC procedure to expose heartbeat data without scope-arch precedent — IPC procedure list is reserved/closed in §Occupied Resources, and TauRPC's capability-pairing requirement means a new procedure needs both router registration and `pulse-app/capabilities/` JSON entry. If freshness is needed in IPC surface, extend existing `health.subsystems` / `ready.checks` maps.
- (arch) Do NOT reach for `crossbeam-channel` or a second tokio runtime to host heartbeat tasks (rejected at arch §Established Decisions; arch §Inherited Defaults locks to a single tokio runtime).

- (arch) Do NOT emit heartbeat events on the `pulse://stream/*` Tauri Channel API surface — those events are the reserved set in §Occupied Resources; heartbeat ticks are a self-observation surface, not a UI-stream surface, and live in the `tracing` JSON log only.
**Contract bindings:**

- **security ↔ obs (PII allowlist + per-module field schemas)**: heartbeat tick redaction lives entirely within the chunk #8 PiiScrubLayer / `JsonFieldVisitor` (subscriber-side); per-module `AllowList` for `ingest.tick` / `buffer.tick` / `viz.tick` / `plugins.tick` MUST permit only the obs-defined per-module field schemas. Security domain enforces "no raw attribute / path / SQL fragment values"; obs domain owns the heartbeat-stall detection (>45s gap CI gate) and the per-module field shape itself. Reciprocates fully: obs explicitly cites "obs ↔ security (chunk #8 PII scrubbing wire) — each `{module}.tick` target MUST be covered by the per-module `AllowList` registered in chunk #8's `PiiScrubLayer`".

- **security ↔ tests (CI gates regression discipline)**: heartbeat tick emission feeds into the obs CI gates `cargo xtask ci-gates`. Tests verify (a) zero-spans NEUTRAL → ACTIVE transition once ticks emit, (b) heartbeat-gap >45s detection arms, (c) zero-panic invariant holds across long-running tick tasks. Security side: per-test fixture assertions on tick payload field allowlist ARE the security regression gate (since `gitleaks` per-PR scan cannot inspect ephemeral runtime logs).

- **security ↔ arch (tokio runtime ownership)**: heartbeat tick mechanism uses `tokio::time::interval(Duration::from_secs(15))` within the `tokio` runtime that already serves OTLP receivers + IPC + buffer fan-out per arch §Established Decisions In-Process Channel Architecture. No new top-level dependency required if the chunk stays inside `tokio::time` + `tracing::info!`; if any supervisor crate is introduced, the §Dependency Security gate applies.

- **tests ↔ obs (5-command discipline + harness §3)**: the `xtask harness:status` command MUST surface per-subsystem `last_tick_at` / `tick_count_since_boot` derived from the same shared state the ticks read. Tests asserts ticks are present in `agent-latest.jsonl` AND that the status endpoint reflects them. obs reciprocates: "obs ↔ tests (5-command discipline + harness §3): the `xtask harness:status` command MUST surface per-subsystem `last_tick_at` / `tick_count_since_boot`."

Heartbeat ticks introduce a new dimension — last-tick timestamp per module (or "subsystem stale" boolean derived from last-tick > 45s). body: _Generated by /andromeda-phase Phase 4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not edit during /implement run._
- **Phase number:** 6

- **Route chunks covered:**
  - route#9 "Heartbeat ticks mechanism — long-running subsystem tick interval (10–30s) + {module}.tick event format for ingest/buffer/viz/plugins"
- **Epoch:** Foundation (Epoch 1)

Wire the long-running-subsystem heartbeat tick mechanism specified by obs-plan §3 onto the existing chunk #4 + #7 + #8 self-observation substrate. Four `tokio::spawn`'d tasks, each driven by `tokio::time::interval(Duration::from_secs(15))`, emit `tracing::info!(target: "{module}.tick", ..., "heartbeat")` events for `ingest`, `buffer`, `viz`, and `plugins` per the locked target taxonomy in `xtask/ci/heartbeat-gap-check.{sh,ps1}`. Tick payload fields are bounded numeric snapshots of per-module liveness state (no OTLP attribute strings, no SQL fragments, no PII per security plan §Logging & Monitoring). Field names align with the obs §8 default-deny per-module allowlist; chunk #8's `JsonFieldVisitor` strip-suffix `.tick` lookup already routes tick events through the right allowlist (existing test `scrubber_passes_tick_suffix_fields` confirms). Heartbeat task ownership lives in `pulse-app/` per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns "Module dependency direction" — library crates expose only a `pub` `heartbeat_payload()` contract callable, never own the timer themselves.

The `health` IPC envelope gains parity with the tick stream per the obs ↔ arch contract binding: each `SubsystemStatus` gains an additive `last_tick_at: Option<DateTime<Utc>>` field; `SubsystemStatuses` gains two new entries (`viz`, `plugins`) so all four tick targets correspond to a queryable subsystem record. The pulse-app boot wires shared heartbeat state via a `OnceLock<Arc<HeartbeatState>>` mirror of the existing `APP_START` pattern in `crates/ui-bridge/src/health.rs`. The xtask CI gate `cargo xtask ci-gates` already calls into `xtask/ci/heartbeat-gap-check.{sh,ps1}` (which has been waiting in INACTIVE state since chunk #6) — once chunk #9 ships, the gate transitions from NEUTRAL to ACTIVE the first time integration tests boot pulse-app long enough to emit ticks.

This is a single-substantial chunk per the route grouping heuristic: it crosses ingest / buffer / viz / plugins / pulse-app / ui-bridge / xtask configuration files, but is not coupled to chunk #10 (Design tokens bundle — frontend Tailwind/CSS, separate concern).

1. **Define per-module heartbeat payload structs in each library crate's `contract` module** (one Rust file modified per crate). Each struct contains the obs-plan §1 + §8 enumerated bounded-numeric fields:
   - `crates/ingest/src/contract.rs`: `IngestHeartbeat { span_count: u64, buffer_capacity_pct: f64, broadcast_subscribers: u32 }` + a `pub fn heartbeat_payload() -> IngestHeartbeat` zero-default placeholder (Foundation-stub; real values land at route#16+ ingest implementation).
   - `crates/buffer/src/contract.rs`: `BufferHeartbeat { rows_ingested: u64, retention_window_active: bool, eviction_count: u64 }` + zero-default `heartbeat_payload()`.
   - `crates/viz/src/contract.rs`: `VizHeartbeat { query_latency_ms: f64, subscribers_active: u32 }` + zero-default `heartbeat_payload()`.
   - `crates/plugins/src/contract.rs`: `PluginsHeartbeat { loaded_count: u32, active_invocations: u32 }` + zero-default `heartbeat_payload()`.
   - Each crate's contract module gets a smoke test: `#[test] fn heartbeat_payload_is_callable() { let _ = heartbeat_payload(); }` — confirms the contract surface compiles and stays зero-cost in the stub state.

2. **Create `pulse-app/src/heartbeat.rs`** with the four tick-emitting tasks + shared state aggregation:
   - `pub(crate) struct HeartbeatState` aggregates four `Arc<RwLock<Option<DateTime<Utc>>>>` last-tick timestamps (or equivalent `Mutex`/`OnceLock` discipline). Default constructs all `None`.
   - `pub(crate) fn spawn(state: Arc<HeartbeatState>) -> Vec<tokio::task::JoinHandle<()>>` spawns four `tokio::spawn` tasks. Each task body: `let mut interval = tokio::time::interval(Duration::from_secs(15)); loop { interval.tick().await; let payload = {ingest|buffer|viz|plugins}::contract::heartbeat_payload(); update state lock with current Utc::now(); tracing::info!(target: "{module}.tick", <fields>=<payload>, "heartbeat"); }`.
   - Tick body emits ONLY the obs-plan §3 enumerated fields per module — bare `tracing::info!` macro call (NO `#[instrument]`, NO span guard, NO `.in_current_span()`).
   - Fields evaluate eagerly (cheap primitives; no `format!`); no expensive payload formatting per obs-plan §11 anti-pattern.
   - **Tests in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`**: paused-clock `#[tokio::test(start_paused = true)]` advances 15s and asserts exactly one tick event emitted per module via a captured `VecMakeWriter` subscriber (clone the pattern from `pulse-app/src/observability.rs:528-577`); separate negative test injects a non-allowlisted field and asserts it's redacted to `<redacted>` in the captured JSON output.

4. **Extend `crates/ui-bridge/src/health.rs` additively** (preserves existing JSON shape per arch ↔ tests "additive only" binding):
   - Add `pub last_tick_at: Option<chrono::DateTime<chrono::Utc>>` field к `SubsystemStatus`. Update `SubsystemStatus::initialized()` and any other constructors с `last_tick_at: None`.
   - Add two new fields к `SubsystemStatuses`: `pub viz: SubsystemStatus, pub plugins: SubsystemStatus`. Update `SubsystemStatuses::placeholders()` к initialize all six entries.
   - Add `pub fn register_heartbeat_state(state: std::sync::Arc<HeartbeatStateLike>)` (where `HeartbeatStateLike` is а minimal trait in ui-bridge OR ui-bridge owns the state struct itself — final decision in implement; either keeps the heartbeat-tick-state-to-health-envelope binding loosely coupled). Use `OnceLock<Arc<...>>` static mirroring the existing `APP_START` pattern (line 10).
   - Update `current_health()` к read the latest tick timestamps from the registered state and populate each subsystem's `last_tick_at` field. Subsystems with no registered state stay `None`.
   - **Tests**: extend `#[cfg(test)]` (ui-bridge currently has no test module; add one). Tests cover (a) `last_tick_at` defaults к `None` before register, (b) `register_heartbeat_state` + simulated tick advance produces non-`None` `last_tick_at`, (c) JSON serialization shape preserves all six subsystems plus existing top-level fields.

5. **Extend `pulse-app/src/observability.rs::AllowList::production()`** to cover the new heartbeat fields per the obs §3 + §8 contract:
   - `ingest`: add `buffer_capacity_pct`, `broadcast_subscribers` (existing: `span_count`, `service`).
   - `buffer`: add `retention_window_active` (existing: `rows_ingested`, `eviction_count`, `memory_bytes`, `retention_window_seconds`).
   - `viz`: add `query_latency_ms`, `subscribers_active` (existing: `query_id`, `param_count`, `row_count`, `latency_ms` — both `latency_ms` and `query_latency_ms` coexist per Q6 resolution).
   - **NEW entry `plugins` (plural, workspace crate name)**: `["loaded_count", "active_invocations"]`. The existing `plugin` (singular) entry stays — different concern (plugin invocation events).
   - Add unit tests in the same `mod tests` block: (a) per-module tick allowlist passes through expected fields without redaction (positive cases for all four modules); (b) injected non-allowlisted field on each tick target is redacted to `<redacted>` (negative cases). Extends the existing 18-test harness.

6. **Update `.claude/rules/verification-harness.md` §Status endpoint shape** к reflect the new envelope shape (TIER 2 RULE EDIT — additive, justified by additive contract extension):
   - Add `last_tick_at` field к each subsystem entry в the JSON shape sample.
   - Add `viz` and `plugins` subsystems к the JSON shape sample.
   - Add а one-line "Agent reads" bullet referencing per-subsystem `last_tick_at` for stall verification.
   - This rule edit is the harness contract — keeping it in sync с the actual envelope is а binding deliverable per the rule's own preamble ("Edits to either side must keep both in sync").

7. **Verify CI gate transition** (no code change — verification-only step): `cargo xtask ci-gates` continues к pass с heartbeat-gap output transitioning from "NEUTRAL (no log file)" к "PASS" once the integration test infrastructure (chunks #15+) boots pulse-app long enough к emit ticks. Until then: ci-gates stays NEUTRAL because nothing boots the binary in CI; new local-test verification covered in §Test Commands below.

Includes paused-clock unit tests covering tick-emit + cancel-on-drop + allowlist redaction.

body: **Constraints across domains:**

- (security) Internal tracing emissions for ServiceWentSilent decisions, bootstrap-suppression state, and bucket transitions MUST follow the §Logging NEVER-log list — log derived statistics (p95 quiet-duration ms, current quiet-duration, bucket count) and `service.name` as bounded identifier, but NEVER log raw OTLP attribute values that prompted the histogram update (per security plan §Logging & Monitoring "What NEVER to log" row 1).

- (tests) Property test idiom: `proptest! { #[test] fn prop_24h_rolling_invariant(events in vec(any::<(u64, EventKind)>(), 0..10_000)) { /* assert: histogram total bucket-coverage ≤ 24h; sum of bucket counts ≤ total events; after `advance` past 24h, oldest bucket evicted */ } }` (per test-plan §2 Test pyramid property-based row + §8 Mocking randomized data).

- (tests) Bursty pattern → ServiceWentSilent NOT emitted during learned quiet (specialist-plan explicit test touch): seed histogram with bursty quiet/active oscillation, advance clock past p95 quiet duration during a known-quiet phase, assert no `Incident::ServiceWentSilent` cue surfaces; then advance past p95 during active-expected phase, assert cue DOES surface (positive control).

- (tests) Histogram round-trip via serialization (specialist-plan explicit test touch even in in-memory-only scope — proves the structure is corpus-flush-ready when chunk #69 lands): use `serde` round-trip (`serde_json::to_value` → `from_value`) on the histogram struct; assert byte-equivalent bucket counts post-round-trip (deferred-but-shaped per pulse-v0_2_0-route §64 deferred items list).

- (obs) Per-service unbounded-cardinality emission at evaluation/tick time only (NOT time-series-stored) — mirror the precedent set by `metric.trace.latency_percentiles` per obs-plan §5 Per-surface metric events table + cardinality discipline exception.

- (obs) Heartbeat tick pattern from obs-plan §3 Heartbeat ticks + §10 SLO invariants: if the activity floor tracker runs a background tick task (e.g., per-bucket rotation every 5min or per-service evaluation every 1-2s), it MUST emit `tracing::info!(target: "triage.baseline.tick", ...)` per the convention; stall detection (>45s gap) applies to any new long-running subsystem.

- (obs) Default subscriber field inheritance — `service.name` / `service.version` / `deployment.environment` already populated globally per obs-plan §3 Service identity; new code MUST NOT manually re-add these fields per `tracing::info!` call.

- (obs) Span instrumentation via `#[tracing::instrument(skip(...))]` attribute on baseline tracker methods, with explicit `fields(...)` allowlist when service_name or other tracked data needs to appear in the span — same pattern as obs-plan §4 Instrumentation per surface table.

- (obs) Bootstrap suppression state transition MUST emit a one-shot `tracing::info!` event when a service crosses from `learning` → `ready` (after 1h cold-start window), with target `triage.baseline.activity_floor.bootstrap_complete` — gives agent visibility into when ServiceWentSilent emission first becomes possible per service.
**Anti-patterns to avoid:**

- (security) NEVER let unbounded distinct `service.name` values from OTLP attributes drive uncapped histogram allocation — apply the same in-process cardinality discipline that security plan §Input Validation post-`prost`-decode bounds applies at the receiver edge (attribute keys/values bounded extends to in-process aggregation keys when they're derived from user-controlled OTLP attributes); without a cap, a buggy or malicious instrumented host emitting random service identifiers triggers OOM on the local desktop process.

- (security) NEVER log raw OTLP attribute values (including the resource attributes that produced the `service.name` if they appear in error context, or any span attribute that triggered a histogram update) in baseline-tracker debug/trace emissions — basename / bounded identifier only per security plan §Logging NEVER-log list rows 1, 2, and 4.

- (security) NEVER serialize an `anyhow::Error` directly out of `crates/triage/baseline/` if a future chunk wires this state to a TauRPC namespace — convert to `AppError` enum first per security plan §Code Patterns anti-pattern row 4; even though this phase has no TauRPC delta, any helper that returns `anyhow::Result<T>` is a future regression risk if a router consumes it without the `From` impl seam.

- (arch) Do NOT introduce a new TauRPC procedure, new broadcast topic, new env var, new workspace crate, or new Tauri capability — pulse-v0_2_0-route §64 explicitly states all deltas are "none"; introducing one would require `/andromeda-evolve --allow-arch-registry` BEFORE merge per arch §Occupied Resources discipline (see chunk #59 / #62 / #63 amendment precedents).

- (arch) Do NOT introduce filesystem I/O for histogram persistence in this phase — IN-MEMORY-ONLY scope per user ordering decision (path a); flush-to-corpus / load-on-startup deferred to subsequent /andromeda-evolve cycle once #69 corpus scaffold lands. Adding `strict-path` canonicalization or any path env var here would expand scope beyond plan + would require coordination with the deferred corpus scaffold's path resolution.

- (arch) Do NOT introduce a reverse dep edge (triage depending on `ui-bridge`, `tauri`, `ingest`, or `pulse-app`) — would invert the arch §Cross-cutting Patterns "Module dependency direction" DAG; any cross-crate state delivery should follow the chunk #59 trait-in-lower-crate + impl-in-pulse-app pattern (documented in `.claude/rules/security.md` Session Additions 2026-05-16) which preserves the dependency direction.

- (tests) NEVER `sleep(N)` to wait for bucket rotation or bootstrap-window expiry — use `tokio::time::pause()` + `tokio::time::advance()` (per test-plan §11 E2E + Universal rows; `.claude/rules/testing.md` §Synchronization).

- (tests) NEVER assert on histogram internal bucket-index values (e.g., `assert_eq!(histogram.buckets[42].count, 5)`) — assert on public contract: current quiet duration, p95 quiet duration, ServiceWentSilent gating boolean (per test-plan §11 Unit row 1 — no implementation detail tests + row 2 — no builder-internal asserts).

- (tests) NEVER use `proptest` without seed-control / regression files — every property test must reproduce via `proptest-regressions/` (per test-plan §8 Mocking → Random sources + §11 Test Data row 3).

- (tests) NEVER use real `std::time::Instant::now()` / `chrono::Utc::now()` inside the histogram or its tests — inject clock through trait or use `tokio::time` exclusively (per test-plan §11 Universal agent-driven specific row 6).
- (tests) NEVER share an `ActivityFloor` instance across parallel `#[test]` functions — each test constructs its own (per test-plan §11 Test Data row 2 — no shared mutable state).

- (obs) NEVER emit ServiceWentSilent observation logs at `info` level inside a per-event hot path — span/log/metric overhead matters at 10k spans/sec ingest rate; use `debug`/`trace` gated by `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_LOG_LEVEL` for per-event detail (per obs-plan §11 Metrics "NEVER format expensive `tracing` event payloads inside hot paths without level-gating" + Logs "NEVER log in hot path at `info` level").

- (obs) NEVER include raw OTLP attribute values from observed spans in triage logs — even when computing activity floor against `service.name`, the per-event payload data (attribute keys/values from the original spans) MUST NOT enter triage's `tracing` events (per obs-plan §11 Spans "NEVER include raw OTLP attributes" + Vector 1 + project CLAUDE.md "Telemetry is user-controlled content").

- (obs) NEVER skip the explicit bootstrap-state field on ServiceWentSilent emission logs — without it, an agent cannot distinguish "service is genuinely silent" from "we haven't learned the baseline yet" when post-test analyzing the JSON log (per obs-plan §1 agent-driven invariant + pulse-v0_2_0-route §64 obs deliverable).

data.head: # Phase 60 Plan — chunks route#64: "Activity floor learning + corpus persistence (IN-MEMORY-ONLY scope)"

body: _Generated by /andromeda-phase Phase 4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not edit during /implement run._
- **Phase number:** 60

- **Route chunks covered:**
  - route#64 "Activity floor learning + corpus persistence — per-service 24h rolling histogram; ServiceWentSilent gated by p95 quiet duration (capabilities P-013/P-014; detail in pulse-v0_2_0-route §64)"
- **Epoch:** Epoch 9 — Foundation v0.2.0 (terminal registered chunk as of session 83)

- **Scope decision:** IN-MEMORY-ONLY per user ordering decision (path a). The corpus persistence sub-scope (60s flush + load-on-startup with state-age check identical to chunk #61) is DEFERRED to a subsequent /andromeda-evolve cycle once #69 corpus scaffold lands. This phase covers per-service 24h rolling histogram + 1h bootstrap suppression + ServiceWentSilent gating + cardinality cap in-memory only.

Add per-service activity-floor learning to the L1b streaming distillation layer (`crates/triage/baseline/`) so the platform can emit `ServiceWentSilent` attention cues only when a service's current quiet duration meaningfully exceeds its own learned historical quiet-duration distribution — solving the "developer-on-lunch" false-positive class while preserving chunk #63's restart-window discipline. Each per-service tracker maintains a 24h rolling activity-density histogram (288 buckets of 5-min intervals) plus a streaming distribution of observed inter-observation gaps used as the p95 gate; ServiceWentSilent emission is universally suppressed during the first 1-hour bootstrap window for that service (cold-start blindness elimination per pulse-v0_2_0-route §64). Cardinality is bounded per-instance (security plan §Input Validation OTLP user-content boundary) to prevent the local desktop process from OOMing under malicious or buggy instrumented hosts emitting unbounded distinct service identifiers.

Implementation extends the existing `ServiceBaseline` struct in `crates/triage/src/baseline/mod.rs` with one new field (`activity_floor: ActivityFloor`), routes the per-span observation through the new tracker via the existing `BaselineState::observe_span()` entry point (no new SpanObserver adapter — chunk #62's `BaselineObserverAdapter` already delivers spans here), and adds a sibling pure synchronous evaluator `evaluate_service_went_silent` consumed by the existing 1-2s `run_one_emit_cycle` tick. ServiceWentSilent cues piggyback on the chunk #62 `pulse://stream/attention-cues` broadcast topic + the `AttentionCue` envelope using the already-declared `CueKind::ServiceWentSilent` variant (chunk #60 scaffold) — zero new broadcast topics, zero new TauRPC procedures, zero new env vars, zero new workspace crates per pulse-v0_2_0-route §64 "all deltas: none". The chunk #63 surgical-suppression filter `evaluate_with_suppression` already passes ServiceWentSilent cues through unchanged (it only filters `CueKind::ErrorRateSpike`), so no integration change at the suppression layer.

Per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns "Self-observation discipline" + obs plan §3, all new instrumentation uses the `tracing` ecosystem (NO OTel SDK link); new tracing targets follow the established `triage.baseline.{operation}` naming convention and require corresponding `AllowList::production()` entries in `pulse-app/src/observability.rs` per the default-deny + per-leaf-registry pattern (testing.md 2026-05-07 lesson). Per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns "Module dependency direction", no new sibling-crate dependency is introduced (triage continues to depend only on serde / thiserror / tracing / tdigest / dashmap / tokio per the chunk #61 dep set).
Create `crates/triage/src/baseline/activity_floor.rs` containing:

1. Module-level public constants — `BUCKET_COUNT` (= 288), `BUCKET_INTERVAL_SECONDS` (= 300), `WINDOW_DURATION_SECONDS` (= 86_400 = 24h), `BOOTSTRAP_WINDOW_SECONDS` (= 3_600 = 1h), `DEFAULT_QUIET_DURATION_PERCENTILE` (= 0.95). Wrap in a module-level `const _: () = { assert!(...); };` block per the chunk #61 / #62 / #63 pattern documented at `crates/triage/src/cue/thresholds.rs:207-219` and `.claude/rules/testing.md` Session Additions 2026-05-11 (clippy `assertions_on_constants` forbidden in `#[test] fn`).

2. Public enum `BootstrapState { Learning, Ready }` (snake_case `serde` rename per the contract.rs precedent for `CueKind` / `CueScope` / `PriorityTier`). Bounded enumeration; no `Other(String)` catch-all.

3. body: _Generated by /andromeda-phase Phase 4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not edit during /implement run._
- **Phase number:** 61

- **Route chunks covered:**
  - route#65 "Span events ingestion — extend OTLP decode in appender.rs to populate span_events table; redaction layer preserved (capability P-006; detail in pulse-v0_2_0-route §65)"
- **Epoch:** Epoch 9 — Foundation v0.2.0

Wire OTLP span-event decoding through the existing buffer ingestion path so `Span.events[]` (currently traversed by `validate_resource_spans` only down to `span.attributes`) populates the already-reserved `span_events` DuckDB table with `exception.type` / `exception.message` / `exception.stacktrace` attribute values. This extends the L0 (schema population) + L1c (decode in ingestion path) distillation layers per `docs/v0_2_0/pulse-v0_2_0-route.md` §Phase 2 line 225-238 and enables capability P-006 (Exception Event Capture). The chunk is storage-side only — no new TauRPC procedure, no new broadcast topic, no new workspace crate, no arch registry mutation; the `span_events` table is already declared in `crates/buffer/src/schema.rs` (chunk #20 substrate) but unused until now.

Two adjacent disciplines land alongside: (a) the post-`prost`-decode invariant traversal in `crates/ingest/src/invariants.rs::validate_resource_spans` extends into `span.events[].attributes` (closing a documented gap that maps directly to security plan §Input Validation row 1); (b) the production-path `duckdb.append` tracing emission moves from `#[cfg(test)]` wrappers into `crates/buffer/src/consumer.rs::dispatch_batch` (matching the per-table emission shape across all 4 reserved-table writes — spans / span_events / metrics_points / log_records — that the obs plan §4 must-trace P1 contract requires but the current production hot path doesn't actually emit, only tests do). A `duckdb` allowlist entry in `pulse-app/src/observability.rs::AllowList::production()` is added so the new emission's `rows_appended` / `duration_ms` / `table_name` fields aren't silently redacted to `[redacted]` by the default-deny `JsonFieldVisitor` per observability rules 2026-05-03 + 2026-05-07.

Per security plan §Logging "What NEVER to log" rows 1-2, the exception attribute values themselves NEVER reach self-observation logs — only counters + bounded enum tags. A PII negative-canary test (canary string in `exception.message`, asserted absent across the decode + append path via the `CapturingSubscriber + FieldCollector` pattern per testing.md Session Additions 2026-05-11) verifies the redaction discipline at chunk-authoring time. The `span_events.fingerprint BLOB NULL` column is created as a substrate for chunk #66 (exception fingerprinting + retry storm detector) but NOT populated by chunk #65 — verified via "fingerprint accepts NULL inserts" round-trip assertion.

1. **Extend `crates/buffer/src/schema.rs` `CREATE_SPAN_EVENTS` const + `SCHEMA_DDL` concat block in lockstep** so the `ddl_constants_match_concatenated_schema` test (line 332) continues to pass. New column set (preserving the existing `(trace_id, span_id, event_index, ts, ts_unix_nano)` head + composite PK on `(trace_id, span_id, event_index)`):
   - `name VARCHAR NOT NULL DEFAULT ''` (OTLP `Event.name` per trace.proto:58)
   - `exception_type VARCHAR NULL` (OTLP `exception.type` attribute when present)
   - `exception_message VARCHAR NULL` (OTLP `exception.message` attribute when present)
   - `exception_stacktrace VARCHAR NULL` (OTLP `exception.stacktrace` attribute when present)
   - `fingerprint BLOB NULL` (chunk #66 substrate — populated NULL in chunk #65)

2. **Extend `crates/ingest/src/invariants.rs::validate_resource_spans`** by adding a per-event loop after the existing `validate_attributes(&span.attributes)?` call at line 45. Per-event invariants reuse the existing constants + helpers:
   - Per-event attribute-count cap: `event.attributes.len() > MAX_ATTRIBUTES_PER_SPAN` → `Error::InvariantViolation { kind: "event_attributes_count", expected: MAX_ATTRIBUTES_PER_SPAN, actual: event.attributes.len() }`
   - Per-event-attribute key + value bounds: reuse `validate_attributes(&event.attributes)?`
   - Add per-event tests mirroring the existing `validate_spans_rejects_attribute_value_string_over_limit` shape but seeding the canary attribute into `span.events[0].attributes` instead of `span.attributes`.

3. **Add `build_span_events_record_batch(batch: &[ResourceSpans]) -> Result<Option<RecordBatch>, Error>`** to `crates/buffer/src/appender.rs`. Follow the `build_spans_record_batch` template (lines 27-99):
   - Outer loop on `rs in batch`; for each, extract `service_name` (unused for span_events table but consistent with span ownership)
   - Middle loop on `ss in &rs.scope_spans` then inner loop on `span in &ss.spans`
   - Defensive skip per existing pattern: `if span.trace_id.is_empty() || span.span_id.is_empty() { continue; }`
   - Innermost loop: `for (event_index, event) in span.events.iter().enumerate()`. Append per-event row to accumulators:
     - `trace_id` from parent span
     - `span_id` from parent span
     - `event_index` from `.enumerate()` (i32; cast from usize with `as i32`)
     - `ts` from `event.time_unix_nano / 1_000` as Microsecond TimestampTZ
     - `ts_unix_nano` from `event.time_unix_nano as i64`
     - `name` from `event.name`
     - `exception_type` / `exception_message` / `exception_stacktrace` extracted from `event.attributes` via a new helper `extract_string_attribute(attrs: &[KeyValue], key: &str) -> Option<String>` that walks the KeyValue list and returns the StringValue when key matches (returns None for missing key OR non-string value — mirrors the pattern used in `extract_service_name` at line 101 but parametric over key + returning Option<String>)
   - Build Arrow `BinaryArray` / `Int32Array` / `TimestampMicrosecondArray` / `Int64Array` / `StringArray` columns; nullable strings via `StringArray::from(Vec<Option<String>>)` (Arrow handles nulls natively)
   - Build schema: `Field::new("trace_id", DataType::Binary, false)` (NOT NULL), `Field::new("name", DataType::Utf8, false)` (NOT NULL with default), `Field::new("exception_type", DataType::Utf8, true)` (NULL), etc.
   - `fingerprint` column: `Field::new("fingerprint", DataType::Binary, true)`; populate as `Vec<Option<Vec<u8>>>` of all `None` for chunk #65 (chunk #66 will compute + populate)
   - On `RecordBatch::try_new(...)` error: `Error::Append { reason: format!("record_batch(span_events): {}", short_err(&e.to_string())) }` per the existing 4 build_*_record_batch error patterns

4. **Add `#[cfg(test)] pub(crate) fn append_span_events_batch(conn: &Connection, batch: &[ResourceSpans]) -> Result<u64, Error>`** to `appender.rs` mirroring `append_spans_batch` at lines 310-327. Same shape; `table_name = "span_events"` in the `tracing::info!(target: "duckdb.append", ...)` emission at function tail.

5. **Wire production span_events append into `crates/buffer/src/consumer.rs::dispatch_batch::Batch::Spans` branch (lines 87-94)**. After the existing `append_record_batch_to_table(&guard, "spans", rb)?` call, add (BEFORE `drop(guard)` at line 113 so both appends share the same lock guard):

Span events row count is intentionally NOT added to `rows` (the `BufferState::rows_ingested` field stays parent-spans semantics; span_events surface as their own log-event field count via the production `duckdb.append` emission added in step 6).

6. **Add production-path `duckdb.append` emission to `consumer::dispatch_batch`** so each table append surfaces uniformly:
   - Before `append_record_batch_to_table` call: capture `let start = Instant::now();` (add `use std::time::Instant;` to consumer.rs imports)
   - After the call: emit `tracing::info!(target: "duckdb.append", rows_appended = rows, duration_ms = start.elapsed().as_millis() as u64, table_name = "spans" /* or "span_events" / "metrics_points" / "log_records" */, "Arrow appender wrote rows")`
   - One emission per table touched; for the Batch::Spans branch, this means TWO emissions per batch (one for spans, one for span_events) when span_events are present. The span_events emission MUST cite `table_name = "span_events"` so jq aggregation by table works.
   - The `#[cfg(test)]` wrapper emissions in appender.rs (lines 318/342/365) stay as-is (test wrappers are independent of production dispatch path).

7. **Add `"duckdb"` key to `pulse-app/src/observability.rs::AllowList::production()`** (alongside the existing `"buffer"` entry at lines 145-157) with allowed fields:
   - `rows_appended`
   - `duration_ms`
   - `table_name`
   - `reject_reason` (already used at consumer.rs:62/70 with target `duckdb.append` for failure paths)
   - Optional future-proofing: include `events_decoded` if needed (recommendation: do NOT include in chunk #65; add only when actually emitted)
   - Per observability rules 2026-05-07 resolver-order: `target: "duckdb.append"` resolves via `split('.').next()` → `"duckdb"` → the new entry's allowlist applies. No per-leaf entry needed unless a sub-namespace under `duckdb` introduces different field semantics.

8. **Add PII negative-canary test** in `crates/buffer/src/appender.rs::tests`:
   - Define a local `CapturingSubscriber + FieldCollector` helper (copy from `pulse-app/src/snapshot_runtime.rs::tests` lines 307-356 — cross-crate workspace direction prevents direct import; copy is the accepted convention per chunks #41 + #44 precedent)
   - Test body: seed a Span with `events: vec![Event { time_unix_nano: ..., name: "exception", attributes: vec![ KeyValue { key: "exception.type".into(), value: Some(AnyValue::String("ValueError")) }, KeyValue { key: "exception.message".into(), value: Some(AnyValue::String("secret-canary-EXCEPTION-MESSAGE-PII-12345".into())) }, KeyValue { key: "exception.stacktrace".into(), value: Some(AnyValue::String("/home/user/.creds/private.key:42".into())) } ], dropped_attributes_count: 0 }]`
   - Drive `append_span_events_batch(&conn, &wrapped)` under `tracing::subscriber::with_default(subscriber, || { ... })` (sync test body — see snapshot_runtime.rs:438)
   - Assert: for each captured `(target, fields)` tuple, `assert!(!target.contains(canary) && !fields.contains(canary), ...)` where `canary` ∈ {"secret-canary-EXCEPTION-MESSAGE-PII-12345", "/home/user/.creds/private.key", "ValueError"} — these substrings MUST NOT appear verbatim anywhere in the captured tracing emissions

9. **Add round-trip + composite-PK tests** in `crates/buffer/src/appender.rs::tests`:
   - `append_span_events_batch_inserts_rows_and_returns_count` — seed N=3 events on one span, assert `count == 3` + SQL `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM span_events = 3`
   - `append_span_events_batch_round_trips_exception_attributes` — seed event with all 3 exception attributes, query `SELECT exception_type, exception_message, exception_stacktrace FROM span_events`, assert each round-trips verbatim into the column
   - `append_span_events_batch_round_trips_name` — seed events with various names, assert `name` column reads back
   - `append_span_events_batch_handles_missing_exception_attributes_as_null` — seed event with only `name` (no exception.* attrs), assert exception_type / message / stacktrace all NULL via DuckDB `IS NULL`
   - `append_span_events_batch_assigns_monotonic_event_index_per_span` — seed 4 events on one span, assert `SELECT event_index FROM span_events WHERE trace_id = ? AND span_id = ? ORDER BY event_index` yields `[0, 1, 2, 3]` without gaps
   - `append_span_events_batch_skips_when_parent_span_ids_empty` — seed span with empty trace_id, assert zero rows appended (defensive skip propagates from existing pattern)
   - `append_span_events_batch_empty_input_returns_zero` — empty batch returns Ok(0)
   - `build_span_events_record_batch_returns_none_when_no_events_in_any_span` — span with empty events Vec → Ok(None)
   - `append_span_events_batch_accepts_null_fingerprint_for_chunk_66_substrate` — INSERT a row with fingerprint=NULL succeeds + read-back confirms NULL (proves the column is properly NULL-able for chunk #66 to populate later)

10. **Add invariant tests** in `crates/ingest/src/invariants.rs::tests`:
    - `validate_spans_rejects_event_attribute_count_over_limit` — span with 1 event whose attributes.len() = MAX_ATTRIBUTES_PER_SPAN + 1 → `Error::InvariantViolation { kind: "event_attributes_count", .. }`
    - `validate_spans_rejects_event_attribute_value_string_over_limit` — span with 1 event whose attribute value is `MAX_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE_BYTES + 1` bytes → `Error::InvariantViolation { kind: "attribute_value_length", .. }` (kind name reused from existing helper — events share the same per-attribute kind label since `validate_attributes` is the shared callee)
    - `validate_spans_accepts_event_with_attribute_within_limit` — happy path positive control
    - `validate_spans_accepts_span_with_no_events` — explicit positive control for the empty `events` Vec case

11. **Add 1 consumer-side round-trip test** in `crates/buffer/src/consumer.rs::tests`:
    - `dispatch_batch_writes_span_events_alongside_spans_under_same_lock_guard` — drive a span batch with events through `run_consumer`, assert both `spans` and `span_events` tables have rows + `BufferState::rows_ingested` reflects parent spans only (not span events) per the design decision in step 5

12. **Update `pulse-app/src/observability.rs::AllowList::production()` tests** if the existing tests have a probe pattern like `allowlist_for_target_resolves_*` covering buffer / plugin / etc. — add an `allowlist_for_target_resolves_duckdb_append_to_arrow_appender_fields` test mirroring the chunk #52 + chunk #44 test-naming convention.
(None — chunk #65 is in-place extension of existing source files.)

- `crates/buffer/src/schema.rs` — extend `CREATE_SPAN_EVENTS` (lines 38-46) AND `SCHEMA_DDL` concat (lines 116-123) in lockstep with 5 new columns (`name` NOT NULL DEFAULT '', `exception_type` NULL, `exception_message` NULL, `exception_stacktrace` NULL, `fingerprint` BLOB NULL); preserve composite PK `(trace_id, span_id, event_index)`. Existing `ddl_constants_match_concatenated_schema` test (line 332) enforces parity — both edits in same commit.

data.head: ### Chunk route#66: "Exception fingerprinting + retry storm detector"

body: **Domain relevance summary:**
- (security) Relevant. Two touchpoints: fingerprint hash discipline (must not leak exception content); ingestion hot-path write to `span_events.fingerprint` BLOB.
- (arch) Relevant. Workspace placement across two existing crates + reuse-only of contracts/broadcast/columns; zero arch registry delta.

- (tests) Relevant. Pure-Rust algorithmic detector + write-path edit; needs unit + integration test discipline for hashing determinism, stack normalization, time-window storm detection, severity-tier thresholding, redaction discipline.
- (obs) Relevant. Hot-path fingerprint write (perf budget concern) + new storm-detector subsystem requiring heartbeat tick + cue-emission instrumentation.
- (design) Out-of-domain — pure backend chunk, no UI surface, no design tokens, no visual rendering.
- (layouts) Out-of-domain — no new surface, screen, wireframe, component, modal, focus, or responsive breakpoint.
- (a11y) Out-of-domain — no UI surface, no DOM, no interactive elements, no animation, no contrast, no focus management.
**Constraints across domains:**

- (security) Fingerprint computation MUST hash ONLY `exception.type` + normalized first-3-frame stack — normalization MUST strip absolute paths, memory addresses, and line numbers BEFORE hashing so the hash is content-stable across host-environment differences AND incidental path/address secrets do not co-mingle with the fingerprint bytes (per security plan §Logging & Monitoring NEVER-log list generalization + chunk #66 callout per `pulse-v0_2_0-route.md` line 250).

- (security) Existing chunk #65 redaction layer for `exception.message` content MUST be preserved unchanged — chunk #66 adds the `span_events.fingerprint` write column but MUST NOT regress the message-redaction discipline carried by `appender.rs` (per chunk #65 summary at `pulse-v0_2_0-route.md` line 238).

- (security) NEVER log raw exception.type / exception.message / exception.stacktrace contents in the fingerprinting hot path or the storm-detector tick (per security plan §Logging & Monitoring "What NEVER to log" first bullet).

- (security) Storm-detector tick emissions onto `pulse://stream/attention-cues` MUST NOT include raw fingerprint hash preimage OR raw exception content in the AttentionCue payload — only opaque fingerprint hash digest + occurrence count + service identity + Suggested/Autonomous severity hint may cross the broadcast boundary (per security plan §Logging snapshot/clipboard/MCP hygiene generalization).
- (security) New workspace dependency (`DashMap`) MUST pass `cargo deny check bans licenses sources` in `ci.yml` per security plan §Dependency Security CI integration.

- (security) Buffer-crate ingestion hot-path additions MUST continue to use DuckDB prepared statements with `?` placeholders — NEVER `format!(...)` interpolation (per security plan §Security Anti-Patterns § Input row 2 + Dagster GHSA-mjw2-v2hm-wj34 cluster).

- (arch) Code MUST live in the two existing reserved workspace crates `triage` (storm detector + fingerprint normalization) and `buffer` (fingerprint write into `span_events.fingerprint` via appender hot path); no new workspace crate, no rename (per arch §Occupied Resources Cargo workspace crate names + §Inherited Defaults Module boundaries).

- (arch) Retry storm detector MUST emit `AttentionCue` records via the existing `triage::cue::broadcast` plumbing on the existing `pulse://stream/attention-cues` topic — no new broadcast topic, no new TauRPC procedure (per chunk #66 spec + arch §Occupied Resources Tauri IPC events list).

- (arch) Fingerprint computation in `buffer::appender` MUST happen on the OTLP-decode → DuckDB-appender hand-off path and write a `BLOB`/sized hash into the existing `span_events.fingerprint` column (added by chunk #65); no new column, no schema migration (per arch §Established Decisions [Database] + chunk #65 substrate already-landed).

- (arch) `ExceptionFingerprint` + `RecentOccurrences` + any storm-detector public types in the `triage` crate MUST follow the contract-module discipline (`pub` only via `triage::contract` re-exports, internals `pub(crate)`) and the `thiserror` 2.x in-module error pattern; types crossing no IPC bridge do NOT need `serde::Serialize` (per arch §Conventions Module visibility discipline + §Cross-cutting Patterns Cross-bridge data shape + §Inherited Defaults Error handling).

- (arch) `triage` storm-detection state (`DashMap<ExceptionFingerprint, RecentOccurrences>` with 60s window) lives in-memory only; persistence is OUT OF SCOPE for this chunk (corpus SQLite is chunk #69) (per arch §Established Decisions [Telemetry Retention Surface] + chunk #66 spec carry-over from chunks #61/#64).

- (arch) Module dependency direction MUST flow toward `pulse-app`: `triage` MUST NOT take a new dep on `buffer` (or vice versa) — if shared type needed, lower crate exposes trait or type is duplicated and `buffer` writes opaque bytes (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns Module dependency direction + chunk #59 trait-in-lower-crate precedent per CLAUDE.md session-learnings 2026-05-16).

- (arch) `DashMap` (the cited concurrent map) is a NEW direct dep candidate if not already in either crate — adding it must respect §Inherited Defaults supply-chain hygiene and `cargo deny check bans` (per arch §Infrastructure Patterns CI/CD + project session-learnings 2026-05-03 deny.toml multiple-versions discipline).

- (tests) Test tier is Standard (1) with coverage gates ≥ 75% line / ≥ 70% branch / ≥ 85% function on the new triage/pattern fingerprint + storm modules and the buffer/appender fingerprint write path (per test-plan §1 Test Scope Summary + §10 Quality Gates).
- (tests) Unit tests are co-located via `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { … }` within each crate's source; flat function naming `test_<entity>_<scenario>` (per test-plan §4 Unit Test Strategy Conventions).

- (tests) Self-bootstrapping fixtures only — no pre-baked DuckDB snapshots, no `.sql` scripts; test data seeded via OTLP ingest builders or `rstest` 0.26.1 fixture decorators (per test-plan §7 + §1 agent-driven-discipline trigger).

- (tests) Time-sensitive tests for the 60s rolling window + 30s storm-detection window MUST use `tokio::time::pause()` + `advance(Duration)` rather than real `sleep`/`Instant::now()`; paused-clock tests require `flavor = "current_thread"` only (per test-plan §8 + Session Addition 2026-05-06 on `start_paused` × `multi_thread` incompatibility).

- (tests) Fingerprint-write path in `crates/buffer/appender.rs` integration coverage MUST use the live `tonic` 0.14.5 gRPC client against loopback `:4317` per boundary discipline — NEVER mock the receiver under test (per test-plan §8 Mocking & Stubbing + §11 Integration anti-pattern).

- (tests) Storm detector emission MUST be verified end-to-end against the live attention-cues broadcast channel (existing `crates/triage/src/cue/broadcast.rs` topic from chunk #62) — assert via subscribed `broadcast::Receiver`, NOT via mocking the emitter (per test-plan §5 boundary types covered).

- (tests) Negative-canary tests for fingerprint hash discipline require the in-process `CapturingSubscriber` + `FieldCollector` pattern from chunks #26 / #44 (per testing.md §Session Additions 2026-05-07 + 2026-05-11).

- (obs) Self-observation runtime is `tracing` 0.1 + `tracing-subscriber` JSON formatter ONLY — fingerprint computation + storm detection emit via `tracing::info!` / `tracing::error!` events; NO OTel SDK Meter / Counter / Histogram instruments may be introduced (per obs-plan §3 Tracing init + §5 metric emission convention).

- (obs) Span attribute scrubbing at ingest boundary: `appender.rs` MUST NOT emit raw `exception.message` / `exception.stacktrace` field values into `tracing` events — emit `fingerprint_hex` (8-byte hash prefix) + `frame_count_normalized: 3` + `exception_type` (already classification-grade per chunk #65 redaction discipline) only (per obs-plan §8 PII Scrubbing data classification "Raw OTLP telemetry payloads" High → scrub-required + §11 Spans/Traces Vector 1).

- (obs) Storm-detector emission MUST inherit trace context from the parent ingest span via `tracing::Span::current()` — `RetryStorm` AttentionCue events must carry `trace_id` so agents can correlate the cue with the originating gRPC export request (per obs-plan §10 SLO invariants "Trace context propagation" + §3 Trace context propagation Internal async boundaries).

- (obs) Fingerprint computation in the ingestion hot path is perf-budget-sensitive — wrap `tracing` event emission in level-gating (e.g., `if tracing::enabled!(Level::DEBUG) { ... }`) for per-record fingerprint trace events; only the storm-trigger (≥5 / ≥10 thresholds crossed) emits at `info` / `warn` (per obs-plan §11 Metrics + §11 Logs hot-path discipline).

- (obs) `DashMap<ExceptionFingerprint, RecentOccurrences>` 60s window MUST not be the sole storm-detection signal — emit a heartbeat tick from the storm-detector subsystem every 15s carrying `tracked_fingerprints_count`, `active_storm_count`, `window_seconds: 60` so agents can detect stall via the >45s rule (per obs-plan §10 SLO invariants Standard+ "Heartbeat ticks" + §3 Heartbeat ticks).

- (obs) Label cardinality discipline: `exception_type` is client-controlled (unbounded by design like `service_name`) — keep storm-detector metric emission scoped to query-time / event-time only; do NOT introduce a long-running time-series gauge keyed by `(service_name, exception_type, fingerprint)` tuple (per obs-plan §5 cardinality discipline note + §11 Metrics cardinality).
**Patterns to follow:**

- (security) Preserve chunk #65 appender.rs redaction discipline as the template — when extending `appender.rs` to compute and bind the fingerprint BLOB, follow the same per-attribute redaction-then-bind shape that #65 established for `exception.message` (per `pulse-v0_2_0-route.md` line 238).

- (security) AppError sanitization at crate boundaries — fingerprint or storm-detector errors that surface to any IPC boundary (none in this chunk, but bridging surfaces use `serde`-friendly `AppError::Internal { message: <sanitized one-liner> }` with NO stack traces / file paths / Rust struct names / library versions (per security plan §Error Handling TauRPC bridge bullet).

- (security) Cargo workspace dep addition for `DashMap` follows the standard `crates/{triage,buffer}/Cargo.toml` `[dependencies]` entry pattern — pin a specific minor version, let Dependabot bump; do NOT use `"*"` or unbounded `"latest"` (per security plan §Dependency Security Pinning).

- (security) Hot-path fingerprint computation is structured-logging friendly — emit `tracing` events with the fingerprint hash digest (hex-encoded, fixed length) as a span/event field, NEVER the preimage strings; field names follow the obs-plan span-field-naming convention (per security plan §Logging & Monitoring "Log format" `tracing` paragraph + the corrected self-observation surface at `~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/agent-latest.jsonl` per 2026-05-08 Decisions Log entry).

- (arch) Two-crate split with locked module boundary respected: storm-detector + fingerprint normalization in `crates/triage/src/pattern/` (alongside existing `broadcast.rs` / `detector.rs` / `suppression.rs` from chunk #63), fingerprint write in `crates/buffer/src/appender.rs` — matches chunks #62/#63 precedent of adding sub-modules under `triage/src/pattern/` (per arch §Project Intent Template patterns).

- (arch) Reuse existing `triage::cue` `AttentionCue` contract types (`CueKind`, `PriorityTier`, `Severity`, `EvidenceRefs`) introduced in chunk #60 + emit via existing chunk #62 cue broadcast plumbing — do not invent a parallel "storm event" channel; spec maps storms to `CueKind::RetryStorm` with hint variants Suggested vs Autonomous (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns + chunk #60 triage scaffold landed).

- (arch) Fingerprint write follows the chunk #65 ingestion-hot-path pattern: decode → normalize → hash → write into the already-allocated `span_events.fingerprint` column inside the same `Appender::append_record_batch()` round; zero round-trip back to DuckDB (per arch §Stack Apache Arrow zero-copy + §Established Decisions [Database] Arrow zero-copy ingest sidesteps marshalling tax).

- (arch) Concurrent state shared between appender hot path (writes occurrences) and storm-detection emitter task (reads + emits cues) follows the chunk #59 pattern: `Arc<DashMap<…>>` or `Arc<RwLock<…>>` constructed in `pulse-app/src/main.rs` setup closure and injected into both consumers via `Arc::clone` (per CLAUDE.md session-learnings 2026-05-16 trait-state-injection precedent).

- (arch) Storm-detector tick task follows the chunk #62 spawn pattern from `pulse-app/src/main.rs` setup closure — see chunks #62/#63 `broadcast.rs` `#[derive(Clone)]` sender struct passed into the spawned task (per arch §In-Process Channel Architecture + chunk #62 precedent).

- (tests) **Streaming-statistics quantile-bucket-design discipline** for any threshold tests involving `(≥5/30s, ≥10/30s)` counts: design seed counts so the position lands in the intended bucket of the sorted observation distribution, not just absolute counts (per testing.md §Session Additions 2026-05-17 session 84 "quantile gate trap" — generalizes to count-window thresholds where boundary-exact counts can flap based on sample ordering).

- (tests) **In-process `tracing::Subscriber` capture** for assertions on tracing events emitted by the storm detector + fingerprint writer (no `tracing-test` workspace dep needed): use `CapturingSubscriber` + `tracing::subscriber::with_default` (sync test bodies) or `set_default` returning `DefaultGuard` (async test bodies, per Session Addition 2026-05-09) — reference impls at `crates/ui-bridge/src/contract.rs::tests::CapturingSubscriber` (chunk #26) + `pulse-app/src/snapshot_runtime.rs::tests::FieldCollector` (chunk #44).

- (tests) **Receiver-held-alive discipline** for any test spawning the storm-detector consumer task or subscribing to attention-cues broadcast: hold the matching `broadcast::Receiver` alive for the full test duration via return-tuple OR spawn-drainer (per testing.md §Session Additions 2026-05-05).

- (tests) **`tracing::instrument` `skip(...)` discipline** for any new instrument annotations on functions taking non-Debug types like `DashMap<ExceptionFingerprint, RecentOccurrences>` — be explicit about `skip(state)` rather than relying on default capture (per testing.md §Session Additions 2026-05-11).
- (tests) **`rstest` parametric fixtures** for the fingerprint determinism + stack-normalization test matrix — composable via `#[fixture]` + `#[rstest]` per test-plan §4 + §7.

- (tests) **Standard chunk-gate baseline (unconditional)**: `cargo fmt --check` + `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` + `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` + `cargo xtask capability-drift` (per testing.md §Decisions Log 2026-05-10 + chunk #66 has no `pulse-app/ui/**` touches → webview gates excluded).

- (obs) `{module}.{operation}` span naming: storm detector emits `triage.pattern.storm.evaluate` (per-tick check) + `triage.pattern.storm.detected` (threshold crossing) + `triage.pattern.storm.cue_emit` (broadcast emission); appender extension emits `buffer.appender.exception.fingerprint` as child span of existing `duckdb.append` (per obs-plan §4 span naming convention + Scenario P1 instrumentation pattern).

- (obs) Metric event naming `metric.{module}.{measure}` with `value` field: emit `metric.triage.pattern.fingerprints_tracked` (gauge, per tick), `metric.triage.pattern.storm_detected_count` (counter, per cue emission with `severity_hint: suggested | autonomous` label field), `metric.buffer.appender.fingerprint_compute_ms` (distribution, per appender invocation; debug-gated) (per obs-plan §5 Metric Coverage + naming convention).

- (obs) Allowlist-only field emission in the `triage` and `buffer` modules: extend the §8 per-module allowlists with `fingerprint_hex` + `frame_count_normalized` + `severity_hint` + `tracked_fingerprints_count` + `active_storm_count` + `window_seconds` + `occurrences_in_window` — anything outside the allowlist gets default-redacted (per obs-plan §8 default-deny posture per-module allowlist).

- (obs) `#[tracing::instrument(skip(...))]` discipline at fingerprint compute site: skip the raw `exception_message` / `exception_stacktrace` parameters; declare only `fields(exception_type, fingerprint_hex)` explicit fields — sensitive parameters never enter the span at source (per obs-plan §8 Integration points "At source (preferred)").

- (obs) Trace context inheritance via `tracing::Span::current()` for any `tokio::spawn` used in storm-detector tick task — call `.in_current_span()` extension trait so trace_id propagates into the spawned task and the emitted cue inherits the originating ingest span's trace_id (per obs-plan §3 Trace context propagation + §11 Spans).
**Anti-patterns to avoid:**

- (security) NEVER include raw `exception.message` / `exception.stacktrace` text in the fingerprint hash preimage — the hash is meant to be a STABLE identifier; folding raw message text destabilizes the fingerprint AND creates a path for incidentally captured secrets to influence a re-emitted value (per security plan §Logging NEVER-log list bullet 1 generalized).

- (security) NEVER `format!("...{}'", fingerprint_or_exception_field)` against the `duckdb` crate `Connection` when writing `span_events.fingerprint` BLOB — always `Connection::prepare` + `?` placeholders + `Statement::execute` parameter binding (per security plan §Security Anti-Patterns § Input row 2).

- (security) NEVER log fingerprint preimages, raw `exception.*` attribute values, or DuckDB query parameter values from the storm-detector tick or fingerprint-write code path — log the opaque hex digest + occurrence count + service identity only (per security plan §Security Anti-Patterns § Logging bullets 1 + 3).

- (arch) Do NOT introduce a new TauRPC procedure / namespace for storm events or fingerprint queries — chunk spec says "TauRPC delta: none yet"; adding one triggers the quadruple-binding pattern per CLAUDE.md session-learnings 2026-05-09 / 2026-05-12; out of scope.

- (arch) Do NOT add a new broadcast topic (e.g., `pulse://stream/storm-events`) — spec routes storm detection through existing `pulse://stream/attention-cues` channel; a new topic would require `/andromeda-evolve --allow-arch-registry` (per chunks #59/#62/#63 precedent).
- (arch) Do NOT add a reverse dependency edge `crates/buffer → crates/triage` to share an `ExceptionFingerprint` newtype — would violate arch §Cross-cutting Module dependency direction DAG.

- (arch) Do NOT widen the `span_events` schema or add new columns — the `fingerprint` substrate landed in chunk #65; expanding schema in #66 would conflict with arch §Established Decisions [ORM / Migrations] "create on startup" only.

- (tests) NEVER use `sleep(N)` for the 60s rolling window or 30s storm detection window — use `tokio::time::pause()` + `advance(Duration::from_secs(N))` per test-plan §11 E2E anti-patterns + Session Addition 2026-05-06.

- (tests) NEVER mock `DashMap<ExceptionFingerprint, RecentOccurrences>` or the storm-detector trait at unit boundary — test the real storm-detection logic directly with synthetic span-event inputs (per test-plan §8 + §11 Mocking anti-patterns).

- (tests) NEVER assert on raw OTLP protobuf bytes or raw `exception.stacktrace` strings in test output — assert on decoded fields + fingerprint value equivalence (per test-plan §11 Integration anti-patterns).

- (tests) NEVER log raw `exception.message` / `exception.stacktrace` content in either production paths under test OR in test assertions (per test-plan §11 Project-specific anti-patterns extended via chunk #66 `Specialist plan touches: security`).

- (tests) NEVER use modulo-cycle `(i % 250)` for synthetic span_id generation in load tests injecting >250 spans — encode batch_idx LE-bytes into trace_id + monotonic counter into span_id (per testing.md §Session Additions 2026-05-14 chunk #54 lesson; applies if chunk #66 includes any load test).
- (tests) NEVER pre-populate DuckDB with fixture span_events — seed via the live `tonic` ingest path that chunk #65 implemented (per test-plan §11 Test Data anti-patterns).

- (obs) NEVER emit raw `exception.message` or `exception.stacktrace` field VALUES into `tracing` events — fingerprint computation hashes them but the hash inputs MUST stay out of self-observation logs (per obs-plan §11 Logs Vector 1 + §8 data classification High → scrub-required).

- (obs) NEVER emit a `tracing::info!` event in the per-record fingerprint compute hot path inside `appender.rs` — at 10k spans/sec with multiple span_events per span this becomes log spam; use `tracing::trace!` / `tracing::debug!` (level-gated) for per-record detail (per obs-plan §11 Logs hot-path rule).

- (obs) NEVER let the `DashMap<ExceptionFingerprint, RecentOccurrences>` grow unbounded — the 60s window MUST actively evict expired fingerprints; emit `metric.triage.pattern.fingerprint_evicted_count` per tick so the agent can verify memory bound (per obs-plan §11 Metrics cardinality discipline + §10 perf budgets).

- (obs) NEVER use the existing snapshot pipeline (curated markdown of EXTERNAL OTLP data) as a sink for storm-detection state — storm detector's tracked-fingerprint corpus is SELF-OBSERVATION runtime state and belongs in the `tracing` JSON log file via heartbeat tick (per obs-plan §11 project-specific).
**Contract bindings:**

- **security ↔ obs (PII scrubbing + structured logging)**: chunk emits new `tracing` events from fingerprint computation site (in `crates/buffer/appender.rs` extension) and from storm-detector tick (in `crates/triage/pattern`); both MUST conform to subscriber-layer redaction rules established by security plan §Logging NEVER-log list AND obs-plan PII-scrubbing schema. Security defines WHAT cannot appear in logs (raw exception.* values, fingerprint preimage, DuckDB parameter values); obs defines HOW the redaction Layer enforces it at subscriber configuration time. Both extracts acknowledge — reciprocal.

- **security ↔ tests (CI dep-gate + fingerprint-stability test fixtures)**: chunk adds the `DashMap` workspace dep, which must pass `cargo deny check bans licenses sources` CI gate; tests cases (identical type+stack → identical fingerprint; same type different paths → identical fingerprint via normalization; different line numbers → different fingerprints) MUST use SYNTHETIC exception payloads in fixtures, NEVER real PII / real secrets / real production stack traces. Both sides acknowledge — reciprocal.
