title: Phase 62 Plan — chunk route#66: "Exception fingerprinting + retry storm detector"

data.head: # Phase 62 Plan — chunk route#66: "Exception fingerprinting + retry storm detector"

body: _Generated by /andromeda-phase Phase 4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not edit during /implement run._
- **Phase number:** 62

- **Route chunks covered:**
  - route#66 "Exception fingerprinting + retry storm detector — hash(exception.type + normalized stack) per span event; ≥5/30s emits Suggested cue, ≥10 Autonomous (capabilities P-017/P-018; detail in pulse-v0_2_0-route §66)."
- **Epoch:** Epoch 9 — Foundation v0.2.0

Add per-span-event exception fingerprinting + a retry storm detector that emits attention cues when the same exception fingerprint reoccurs ≥5 times within a 30-second sliding window (Suggested tier) or ≥10 times (Autonomous tier). The fingerprint = blake3(`exception.type` + normalized first-3-frame stacktrace) truncated to 16 bytes; normalization strips absolute paths, memory addresses, and line numbers so the hash is stable across host-environment differences and never co-mingles incidentally captured PII bytes from instrumented host applications (per security plan §Logging "What NEVER to log" + chunk #66 `Specialist plan touches: security` annotation). Fingerprints are written to the existing `span_events.fingerprint BLOB NULL` column (chunk #65 substrate) on the OTLP-decode → DuckDB-appender ingestion hot path, and emitted in-process to a new `RetryStormDetector` that holds a `DashMap<[u8; 16], FingerprintState>` with a 60-second rolling window. The detector emits `AttentionCue { kind: CueKind::RetryStorm, priority_tier: Suggested|Autonomous }` payloads through the existing `pulse://stream/attention-cues` broadcast channel (chunk #62 substrate; no new TauRPC procedure, no new broadcast topic, no arch registry delta). Per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns Module dependency direction, fingerprint computation lives in the lower buffer crate (no `triage` dep) via a new `FingerprintObserver` trait declared in `crates/buffer/src/fingerprint.rs`; the storm-detection state machine lives in `crates/triage/src/pattern/storm.rs` (sibling к chunks #62/#63 cue emitter + restart detector); the cross-crate bridge `StormObserverAdapter` lives at the `pulse-app` binary boundary in `pulse-app/src/storm_observer.rs` (mirrors `RestartObserverAdapter` chunk #63 + `BaselineObserverAdapter` chunk #62 precedent). Self-observation discipline preserved per security plan §Logging + obs-plan §8 default-deny posture: no raw `exception.message`/`exception.stacktrace` content enters `tracing` events (verified by negative-canary tests injecting `SECRET_CANARY_*` substrings); per-target field allowlist in `pulse-app/src/observability.rs::AllowList::production()` extends with new entries listing ONLY identifier-class fields per chunks #62/#63/#64 convention (`fingerprint_hex` 8-char prefix, `severity_hint`, `occurrence_count`, `window_seconds`, `tracked_fingerprints_count`, `active_storm_count` — never `exception_message` / `service_name` / `scope_id`).

1. **Workspace dep + crate dep**: Add `blake3 = "1"` to `Cargo.toml [workspace.dependencies]` with a one-line provenance comment ("chunk #66 — exception fingerprint hash для retry storm detection; deterministic, content-stable, hot-path-fast ~3 GB/s; dual-licensed Apache-2.0/CC0"). Add `blake3.workspace = true` к `crates/buffer/Cargo.toml [dependencies]`. **Pre-merge `cargo deny check bans licenses sources`** verifies (a) license in SPDX allowlist, (b) no new `multiple-versions = "deny"` regression. **Fallback path (if deny rejects):** drop blake3 + use already-in-lockfile `sha2 = "0.10"` workspace-level pin instead; fingerprint contract unchanged.

2. **Create `crates/buffer/src/fingerprint.rs`** with:
   - `pub trait FingerprintObserver: Send + Sync { fn on_fingerprint(&self, fingerprint: [u8; 16], service_name: &str, ts_unix_nano: i64); }` (mirrors `ingest::observer::SpanObserver` shape but for span-event-level callbacks)
   - `pub struct NoopFingerprintObserver;` implementing the trait as no-op (test + boot fallback)
   - `pub fn compute_exception_fingerprint(exception_type: Option<&str>, stacktrace: Option<&str>) -> Option<[u8; 16]>` — returns `None` if `exception_type` is `None`/empty; otherwise hashes `(exception_type.as_bytes(), normalize_stacktrace(stacktrace.unwrap_or("")).as_bytes())` via `blake3::Hasher::new().update(...).update(...).finalize()`, takes first 16 bytes
   - `pub(crate) fn normalize_stacktrace(raw: &str) -> String` — splits on newlines, drops empty lines, takes first 3 non-empty lines, strips absolute paths (regex matches OS-specific path patterns: `[A-Za-z]:\\` Windows, `/[a-zA-Z0-9_./-]+` Unix), strips memory addresses (hex pointer pattern `0x[0-9a-fA-F]+`), strips line numbers (`:[0-9]+(:[0-9]+)?` after path), joins back with `\n`
   - `pub(crate) fn fingerprint_to_hex_prefix(fingerprint: &[u8; 16]) -> String` — formats first 4 bytes as 8-char lowercase hex для tracing field emission (per obs-plan field naming convention; bounded cardinality)
   - Unit tests covering: (a) `None`/empty exception_type returns `None`; (b) determinism — identical inputs → identical output; (c) path normalization — same type+frame-function-names с different file paths → same fingerprint; (d) line-number stripping — same type+frames с different line numbers → same fingerprint; (e) address stripping — same type+frames с different memory addresses → same fingerprint; (f) truncation — same type с 5-frame stack VS 3-frame stack of identical first-3 → same fingerprint; (g) different exception_type → different fingerprint; (h) different first-3 frames → different fingerprint; (i) `NoopFingerprintObserver::on_fingerprint` safe-to-call test; (j) `FingerprintObserver` trait-object callable test. Use `rstest` for the determinism matrix.
3. **Add `pub mod fingerprint;` к `crates/buffer/src/lib.rs`** (between existing `pub mod broadcast;` and `pub mod consumer;` — alphabetical insertion).

4. **Modify `crates/buffer/src/appender.rs::build_span_events_record_batch`**:
   - Extend signature: `pub(crate) fn build_span_events_record_batch(spans: &[ResourceSpans], fingerprint_observer: Option<&Arc<dyn FingerprintObserver>>) -> Result<Option<RecordBatch>, Error>` (Option-wrapped so `#[cfg(test)]` test wrappers that don't care about storm detection can pass `None`).
   - Inside the existing event-walking loop (lines ~290-325), after collecting `exception_types`, `exception_messages`, `exception_stacktraces`, also collect `fingerprints: Vec<Option<Vec<u8>>>` per row via `fingerprint::compute_exception_fingerprint(exception_type.as_deref(), stacktrace.as_deref()).map(|fp| fp.to_vec())`.
   - Replace the all-NULL `let fingerprint_array = BinaryArray::from_iter((0..row_count).map(|_| None::<&[u8]>));` at line ~346 with `let fingerprint_array = BinaryArray::from_iter(fingerprints.iter().map(|f| f.as_deref()));`.
   - AFTER the RecordBatch is built (after line ~378 `Ok(Some(record_batch))`), call `if let Some(observer) = fingerprint_observer { for (row_idx, fp_opt) in fingerprints.iter().enumerate() { if let Some(fp_bytes) = fp_opt { let fp_array: [u8; 16] = fp_bytes.as_slice().try_into().expect("16-byte fingerprint"); observer.on_fingerprint(fp_array, &services_per_row[row_idx], ts_unix_nanos[row_idx]); } } }` — requires also collecting `services_per_row: Vec<String>` in the loop (currently the function only collects per-row column data; service_name lives at the parent ResourceSpans level, so derive per-row by tracking the outer-loop service_name on each row push). **Implementation note:** simpler shape — observer fan-out happens INSIDE the event-walking loop (per push), not as a separate post-loop pass; that avoids the extra `services_per_row` Vec.
   - Update existing `#[cfg(test)] append_span_events_batch` wrapper к pass `None` для fingerprint_observer (preserves chunk #65 test semantics — fingerprint NULL when no observer wired).
   - Add tests: `build_span_events_record_batch_populates_fingerprint_for_exception_events` (synthetic ResourceSpans с 1 exception event → assert resulting BinaryArray row 0 IS Some + bytes length 16); `build_span_events_record_batch_leaves_fingerprint_null_for_non_exception_events` (event с only `name = "non-exception"` → assert BinaryArray row IS None); `build_span_events_record_batch_observer_invoked_per_exception_event` (mock FingerprintObserver capturing calls → assert on_fingerprint called once per exception event).

5. **Modify `crates/buffer/src/consumer.rs`**:
   - Extend `run_consumer` signature: add `fingerprint_observer: Option<Arc<dyn FingerprintObserver>>` parameter after `span_observer`.
   - Pass `fingerprint_observer.as_ref()` к the `build_span_events_record_batch(&s, fingerprint_observer.as_ref())` call inside `dispatch_batch::Batch::Spans` arm (line ~98).
   - **Backward compat:** existing test call sites passing only the original arg-set need to be updated к pass `None` (no-op observer); production call site in pulse-app passes `Some(Arc<dyn FingerprintObserver>)`.
   - Add test `consumer_invokes_fingerprint_observer_on_exception_span_events` (in-process consumer mounted с mock observer → push synthetic Batch::Spans с exception event → assert observer.on_fingerprint called с correct (fingerprint, service, ts) tuple).

6. **Create `crates/triage/src/pattern/storm.rs`** with:
   - `pub const DEFAULT_STORM_WINDOW_SECONDS: u64 = 60;`
   - `pub const DEFAULT_SUGGESTED_THRESHOLD: u64 = 5;`
   - `pub const DEFAULT_AUTONOMOUS_THRESHOLD: u64 = 10;`
   - `pub const DEFAULT_DETECTION_SUB_WINDOW_SECONDS: u64 = 30;` (the "30s" в "≥5/30s" — count occurrences в the most recent 30s sub-window of the 60s state-retention window)
   - `#[derive(Debug)] pub struct RetryStormDetector { fingerprints: DashMap<[u8; 16], FingerprintState>, window_seconds: u64, detection_window_seconds: u64, suggested_threshold: u64, autonomous_threshold: u64, storms_detected_total: AtomicU64, fingerprints_evicted_total: AtomicU64 }` + constructor `pub fn new(window_seconds: u64, detection_window_seconds: u64, suggested_threshold: u64, autonomous_threshold: u64) -> Self`
   - `#[derive(Debug)] struct FingerprintState { service: String, timestamps_nanos: Vec<i64>, last_emitted: Option<(i64, PriorityTier)> }`
   - `pub fn record_occurrence(detector: &RetryStormDetector, fingerprint: [u8; 16], service: &str, now_nanos: i64) -> Option<AttentionCue>`:
     - Empty `service` → return None (mirror chunk #63 `observe_span` discipline)
     - Acquire DashMap entry для `fingerprint`; insert default `FingerprintState { service: service.to_string(), timestamps_nanos: Vec::new(), last_emitted: None }` if absent
     - Push `now_nanos` к `state.timestamps_nanos`
     - Prune: retain only timestamps where `now_nanos - ts <= window_seconds * 1e9`
     - Count occurrences в detection sub-window: `count = state.timestamps_nanos.iter().filter(|ts| now_nanos - *ts <= detection_window_seconds * 1e9).count() as u64`
     - Threshold check + dedup logic:
       - If `count >= autonomous_threshold` AND `last_emitted.map_or(true, |(ts, tier)| tier != PriorityTier::Autonomous || now_nanos - ts > detection_window_seconds * 1e9)` → set `last_emitted = Some((now_nanos, Autonomous))`; bump `storms_detected_total`; return `Some(synthesize_cue(fingerprint, service, count, PriorityTier::Autonomous, now_nanos, &state.timestamps_nanos))`
       - Else if `count >= suggested_threshold` AND `last_emitted.is_none() || (last_emitted.map_or(true, |(ts, tier)| tier == PriorityTier::Suggested && now_nanos - ts > detection_window_seconds * 1e9))` → set `last_emitted = Some((now_nanos, Suggested))`; bump `storms_detected_total`; return `Some(synthesize_cue(fingerprint, service, count, PriorityTier::Suggested, now_nanos, &state.timestamps_nanos))`
       - Else → return None
   - `fn synthesize_cue(fingerprint: [u8; 16], service: &str, count: u64, tier: PriorityTier, now_nanos: i64, timestamps: &[i64]) -> AttentionCue`:
     - `magnitude = count as f64 / DEFAULT_SUGGESTED_THRESHOLD as f64` (so 5 occ → 1.0, 10 occ → 2.0)
     - `absolute_value = count as f64`

- **Service-id semantics for cross-service fingerprint reuse (Open Question 1)**: a single exception fingerprint occurring across multiple services within the 60s window updates a SINGLE `FingerprintState` keyed by fingerprint (NOT by `(fingerprint, service)` tuple). The `service` field on the state is set к the first-observed service and NOT updated on subsequent observations from different services. This means cross-service propagation of the same exception fingerprint contributes к ONE storm cue, attributed к the first-observed service. **Validate в Phase 6 user review** — alternative semantics (per-service-per-fingerprint keying) is possible but doubles cardinality and changes the storm-detection semantics (a fanout across 5 services of the same fingerprint would emit 5 separate Suggested cues instead of 1).

- **Storm-cue dedup window (Open Question 2)**: per-tier one-shot dedup — `Suggested` cue fires once on first 5th crossing per fingerprint; `Autonomous` cue fires once on first 10th crossing (escalation from Suggested к Autonomous); subsequent occurrences silent until detection-window-resets via timestamp-pruning + recrossing. Avoids duplicate-cue log-spam under sustained high-rate exception storms.

3. **AttentionCue magnitude/absolute_value derivation for storm cues**: the chunk #62 `AttentionCue` shape has `magnitude: f64` + `absolute_value: f64` + `confidence: f64` fields that don't have natural analogs для discrete-count storm detection. data.head: ### Chunk route#67: "Service registry + lifecycle state machine"

body: **Constraints across domains:**

- (arch) Lifecycle state machine code MUST live inside the existing `triage` workspace crate as new internal submodules (`crates/triage/src/lifecycle/` + extend `crates/triage/src/baseline/` for state queries); no new top-level workspace crate permitted (per arch §Occupied Resources Cargo workspace crate names — closed set of 12; chunk #60 already legitimized `triage`).

- (arch) New TauRPC procedure MUST follow `<router>.<verb>` dotted snake_case shape — `services.list_with_states` — returning `Result<T, AppError>` (per arch §Conventions Endpoint naming Authorized Shape b + §Conventions Error response schema).

- (arch) New broadcast topic MUST conform to `pulse://stream/{name}` URI scheme — `pulse://stream/service-lifecycle` — riding Tauri 2 IPC `Channel` API (per arch §Occupied Resources Tauri IPC events + §Standard Contracts Real-time push contract; precedents chunks #59/#62/#63).

- (arch) New resources MUST be legitimized post-merge via `/andromeda-evolve --allow-arch-registry` cycle producing §Architecture Registry Updates entries (per established pattern from #59/#60/#62/#63).

- (arch) **"new schema table `service_registry`" tension with §Established Decisions [Telemetry Retention Surface]** — DuckDB ring buffer holds OTLP entities only; resolve in plan.md by preferring in-memory triage-crate state (Arc<RwLock<HashMap<...>>> or DashMap mirroring chunk #61 baseline pattern); flag to user at Phase 6 if DuckDB table is required.

- (arch) Cross-crate state delivery: trait in lower crate (`triage::lifecycle::ServiceRegistry`) + adapter in pulse-app (chunk #59 `ReceiverBindStatus` precedent); never reverse dep edges (triage → ui-bridge/tauri) per arch §Cross-cutting Module dependency direction.

- (security) New `service_registry` DuckDB table reads/writes MUST use `Connection::prepare` + `?` placeholders + `Statement::execute([&param])` — service names flow from OTLP `service.name` (user-controlled). NEVER `format!("INSERT INTO service_registry ... '{}'")` (per security plan §Input Validation row 5 + §Anti-Patterns Input row 2 — 2026 DuckDB CVE cluster).

- (security) `services.list_with_states()` MUST follow quadruple binding: (1) router registration; (2) `pulse-app/capabilities/default.json` permissions; (3) `xtask/src/main.rs::EXPECTED_PROCEDURES`; (4) `emit_taurpc_bindings` test `.merge(...)` chain in `pulse-app/src/main.rs::tests` (per `.claude/rules/security.md` Session Additions 2026-05-12).

- (security) Two new config keys `[triage.lifecycle.dormant_after_secs]` (default 3600) + `[triage.lifecycle.archived_after_secs]` (default 86400) MUST go through `serde` derive + bounded-numeric validation; reject zero / negative / pathological values (per security plan §Input Validation row 6 — Configuration values).
- (security) Service-state transition logs MUST NEVER include OTLP attribute values from host application (per security plan §Logging & Monitoring NEVER-log list).

- (security) `AppError` variants across `services.list_with_states()` boundary MUST sanitize — no `duckdb::Error` debug output, no Rust struct names, no file paths in `message` field (per security plan §Error Handling TauRPC bridge row).

- (obs) Self-observation runtime is `tracing` only — no OTel SDK; new lifecycle module emits via `tracing` macros writing to `~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/agent-latest.jsonl` (per obs-plan §3 Tracing init).

- (obs) Default-deny field allowlist — every new `tracing` target leaf MUST be registered in `pulse-app/src/observability.rs::AllowList::production()` with explicit per-target field set; unregistered fields silently redact to `[redacted]` (per obs-plan §8 default-deny + `.claude/rules/observability.md` Session Addition 2026-05-07).

- (obs) **No per-service PII in self-observation events** for triage-namespace targets — `service.name`/`service_id`/`scope_id`/`span_id`/`trace_id`/`operation_name` MUST NOT appear as `tracing` event fields on `triage.lifecycle.*` events (per `.claude/rules/observability.md` Session Addition 2026-05-17 session 84 + obs-plan §11 Metrics row 1 cardinality discipline).

- (obs) Lifecycle module MUST emit a 15s heartbeat tick `triage.lifecycle.tick` with registry size + per-state-bucket counts; >45s gap = stall signal (per obs-plan §3 Heartbeat ticks + §10 SLO Heartbeat-stall detection CI gate).
- (obs) State transitions: WARN level on degraded (Active→Silent, Silent→Dormant, Archived→Active corpus restore); INFO on benign; aggregate counts only (per obs-plan §6 Log levels mapping).
- (obs) Corpus lookup on Archived→Active emits `pipeline.l1b.bootstrap_count_total{kind = "restored"}` event mirroring chunk #61 precedent (per v0.2.0-plan §68 + obs-plan §5).
- (tests) Standard tier coverage: ≥75% line / ≥70% branch / ≥85% function over new `crates/triage/lifecycle` + `crates/triage/baseline` code (per test-plan §10 + §4).
- (tests) Co-locate Rust unit tests via `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { … }` inside each new file under `crates/triage/src/lifecycle/` (per test-plan §4 Test file location).

- (tests) Time-sensitive transitions MUST use `tokio::time::pause()` + `tokio::time::advance()` for determinism — Active→Quiet→Silent→Dormant→Archived gated by configurable thresholds (per test-plan §7 Time-sensitive data + §11 universal).

- (tests) New TauRPC procedure MUST have integration contract test asserting paginated envelope shape (`items`/`total`/`next_cursor` per arch §Standard Contracts) + `AppError` serde-friendly error path (per test-plan §5).

- (tests) New broadcast topic MUST have real-time channel integration test: subscribe via Tauri test client, trigger transition, assert event payload schema (per test-plan §1 entity `Real-time push channels` + §5 boundary type).

- (design) Settings → Services pane MUST reuse the established Modal primitive surface (Raised-3 `#343A45` background + 1px subtle border + radius-lg padding) per design-system.md §Surface: desktop-webview — Component Patterns; no new modal shell variant.
- (design) Services list MUST render as a data table per design-system.md §Surface: desktop-webview — Tables (telemetry data) row; service identity in JetBrains Mono 12px tabular-nums.

- (design) Lifecycle state badges MUST use `radius-full` (9999px) + Semantic Color border/text pairing (Success / Warning / Info / Error tokens) — never arbitrary hues for the seven states (per design-system.md §Border Radius + §Color Palette Semantic Colors).

- (design) State-color + label pairing MANDATORY: each badge pairs Semantic Color with text label (Active/Quiet/Silent/Dormant/Archived/Bootstrapping/Unknown) per design-system.md §Anti-Patterns Universal Bans + §Decisions Log 2026-05-03 (binds to a11y SC 1.4.1).

- (layouts) Settings → Services override UI MUST nest inside existing Settings modal form (overlay backdrop + inner card); appended to existing vertical form-section stack (Theme → Widget snap → Retention → MCP toggle → **Services**) preserving `gap: space-lg` (per layout-templates.md §Component — Settings modal).
- (layouts) Settings modal trigger remains existing aperture-icon-in-titlebar OR Settings tab — no new launcher (per layout-templates.md §Settings modal — Trigger).

- (layouts) Compact widget surface MUST NOT gain a lifecycle override entry point; tray menu MUST NOT gain a service-lifecycle override action (per layout-templates.md §IA notes — Navigation model + §Component — Tray menu).

- (a11y) Settings → Services manual-override surface MUST extend existing settings-modal focus contract — initial focus on modal title, Tab cycles top-to-bottom, Esc closes + restores focus to Settings trigger (per a11y plan §5 Keyboard Navigation — settings-modal entry).

- (a11y) Services list MUST use semantic HTML first — native `<table>` or `<ul>/<li>` with `<button>` controls, NOT `<div role="button">`/`<div role="row">` patterns (per a11y plan §11 ARIA anti-patterns row 1).
- (a11y) Override action controls MUST convey state via text label + icon, NEVER color alone (per a11y plan §6 + §11 Visual row 1 — SC 1.4.1).
- (a11y) All interactive controls in override pane MUST meet `--target-button-min` (≥24×24 CSS px) per SC 2.5.8 (per a11y plan §6).

- (a11y) Status messages for lifecycle transitions MUST use `aria-live="polite"` (never assertive unless interrupting); broadcast events MUST NOT steal focus (per a11y plan §7 + §1 Critical Path P4 contract).
**Patterns к follow:**
- (arch) TauRPC namespace addition 4-place binding (router + capabilities JSON + EXPECTED_PROCEDURES + emit_taurpc_bindings test) per security.md Session Additions 2026-05-12.

- (arch) Broadcast topic addition: define `pulse_stream_service_lifecycle()` const in `crates/triage/src/lifecycle/broadcast.rs`, instantiate `tokio::sync::broadcast::Sender<ServiceLifecycleEvent>` (per chunks #59/#62/#63 precedent + arch §Standard Contracts Real-time push).

- (arch) `ServiceLifecycleState` enum with 7 variants + `#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]` + `#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]` for TypeScript binding stability (per arch §Cross-cutting Cross-bridge data shape).

- (arch) Configurable thresholds via existing `Settings` extension path: extend `Settings` struct in `crates/ui-bridge/src/contract.rs` with two `u64` fields rather than introducing a new TauRPC namespace (per security.md Session Additions 2026-05-09 second entry — sidesteps capability-drift triple binding).

- (arch) Submodule organization: `crates/triage/src/lifecycle/{mod.rs, state_machine.rs, registry.rs, broadcast.rs}` following chunks #61 baseline + #62 cue + #63 pattern internal layout precedents (chunk #60 already reserved the `lifecycle` slot).

- (security) Trait-in-lower-crate + adapter-in-pulse-app pattern for cross-crate state (chunk #59 `ReceiverBindStatus` precedent) — `Arc<dyn ServiceRegistry>` threaded through `pulse-app/src/services_router.rs::ServicesApiImpl::new(...)`.

- (security) DuckDB schema-add pattern from chunk #65 `span_events` table — if a DuckDB-backed `service_registry` is implemented, follow same `CREATE TABLE` + prepared-statement Insert shape (per security plan §Input Validation row 5).

- (security) Configuration field validation: follow `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_RETENTION_SECONDS` precedent — serde derive on `LifecycleConfig` struct, bounded-numeric helper; no new validation library install.

- (obs) Per-target AllowList registration pattern with workspace-crate-name discipline: register `triage.lifecycle.tick`, `triage.lifecycle.transition`, `triage.lifecycle.corpus_restore`, `services.list_with_states.request`, `pipeline.l1b.tracked_services_total`, `metric.triage.lifecycle.state_distribution` as separate exact-match entries (mirrors chunks #61/#62/#63/#66; per `.claude/rules/observability.md` Session Addition 2026-05-03 + 2026-05-07).

- (obs) Heartbeat tick pattern: `tokio::time::interval(Duration::from_secs(15))` + `tracing::info!(target: "triage.lifecycle.tick", tracked_services_total = N, services_active = A, ..., "heartbeat")` — bounded enum tags + numeric counts only (per chunk #61 `triage.baseline.tick` pattern at `pulse-app/src/observability.rs:995`).

- (obs) Aggregate-only transition event: emit `triage.lifecycle.transition` once per tick with counts grouped by `from_state`/`to_state` enum tag, NOT one event per per-service transition (per chunk #64 ServiceWentSilent Path A' precedent + obs-plan §11 Logs row 4).

- (obs) `pipeline.l1b.tracked_services_total` metric: `tracing::info!(target: "pipeline.l1b.tracked_services_total", value = N, "metric")` mirroring chunk #61 `pipeline.l1b.persist_count_total` shape (per dist-arch v3 §Pipeline observability).
- (obs) Settings → Services manual override emits via existing `ui-bridge.update_settings` allowlist; no new target needed for override telemetry (per `pulse-app/src/observability.rs:474-486`).

- (tests) Builder fixture factory: add `MockServiceLifecycleEvent::builder()` (or compose from `MockTraceSpan::builder()` driving baseline tracker) under triage crate test module (per test-plan §3 + §7).
- (tests) `rstest` 0.26.1 parameterized fixtures with `#[fixture]` for reusable lifecycle scenarios (per test-plan §4).

data.head: # Phase 63 Plan — chunk route#67: "Service registry + lifecycle state machine"

body: _Generated by /andromeda-phase Phase 4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not edit during /implement run._
- **Phase number:** 63

- **Route chunks covered:**
  - route#67 "Service registry + lifecycle state machine — seven states (Unknown→Bootstrapping→Active→Quiet→Silent→Dormant→Archived) per service; corpus history lookup on Archived→Active (capability P-027; detail in pulse-v0_2_0-route §68)"
- **Epoch:** Epoch 9 — Foundation v0.2.0 (final chunk)

- **Numbering note:** route#67 corresponds to **pulse-v0_2_0-route.md §68** (Service registry + lifecycle state machine) — not §67 (Drain Rust + template profiling, blocked on Pre-D2 spike validation). Route.md positional numbering diverges from v0.2.0-plan numbering starting here per user-confirmed amendment 2026-05-17T23-51-55 in session 89.

Implement the L1b service identity formal lifecycle layer (capability P-027 — Service Constellation Auto-Discovery, formal lifecycle) as the final chunk of Epoch 9 Foundation v0.2.0. The chunk introduces a 7-state per-service finite state machine (Unknown → Bootstrapping → Active → Quiet → Silent → Dormant → Archived) in a new internal submodule `crates/triage/src/lifecycle/`, with transitions driven by inputs from chunk #61 baseline trackers (per-service activity via `BaselineState`/`RollingWindow`) and chunk #63 restart detector (restart events feed Bootstrapping transition). Configurable thresholds (`dormant_after_secs` default 3600 / `archived_after_secs` default 86400) flow through the existing `Settings` struct extension path (per security.md Session Additions 2026-05-09 lower-cost pattern). Per-service registry state lives in-memory via `DashMap<String, ServiceRegistryEntry>` mirroring chunk #61 `BaselineState` precedent — the v0.2.0-plan §68 reference to a DuckDB `service_registry` schema table is dropped per arch §Established Decisions [Telemetry Retention Surface] guardrail (OTLP-spec entities only). State transitions emit on the new `pulse://stream/service-lifecycle` broadcast topic via `ServiceLifecycleBroadcast` (mirrors chunk #63 `RestartEventBroadcast` pattern). The new `services.list_with_states` TauRPC procedure (located in `pulse-app/src/services_router.rs` per chunk #59 `connection_router.rs` precedent) exposes per-service state to the webview. The Settings → Services manual-override UI pane is **deferred to a follow-up chunk** (per chunk #43 → #44 substrate-then-UI precedent); the backend support for manual overrides (per-service `manual_override: Option<ServiceLifecycleState>` storage + Settings field for threshold knobs) lands in this chunk so the follow-up UI chunk has a TauRPC + state surface ready.

The chunk follows the quadruple-binding discipline for new TauRPC namespaces (router registration + `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` extension + `emit_taurpc_bindings` test merge — capability JSON requires no edit per router-level coverage) and the per-target AllowList registration pattern for 6 new tracing targets (`triage.lifecycle.{tick, transition, corpus_restore}`, `services.list_with_states.request`, `pipeline.l1b.tracked_services_total`, `metric.triage.lifecycle.state_distribution`) per `.claude/rules/observability.md` Session Addition 2026-05-17 session 84 tighter aggregate-only convention. Post-merge, two `--allow-arch-registry` amendments legitimize the new `services.list_with_states` TauRPC route + `pulse://stream/service-lifecycle` broadcast topic in arch §Occupied Resources (mirrors chunks #59/#62/#63 precedents). Corpus history lookup on Archived→Active is a no-op stub until chunk #69 corpus SQLite scaffold lands; the `pipeline.l1b.bootstrap_count_total{kind = "restored"}` event emits the no-op signal so chunk #69 wiring becomes a 1-line update.

1. **Create new directory module `crates/triage/src/lifecycle/`** replacing the current 2-line stub at `crates/triage/src/lifecycle.rs`. Delete the file; create `lifecycle/mod.rs` with `pub use` re-exports + private mod declarations + tracing target consts. The misnamed `//! Incident auto-resolution and cool-down` doc on the deleted file is moved as a doc comment into `crates/triage/src/incident.rs` (semantic placement; small housekeeping; out-of-scope to expand).

2. **Define `ServiceLifecycleState` enum** in `crates/triage/src/lifecycle/state_machine.rs` with 7 variants (Unknown, Bootstrapping, Active, Quiet, Silent, Dormant, Archived) + `#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]` + `#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]` per chunk #59 `ConnectionState` precedent. Add transition validity matrix as a Rust function `is_valid_transition(from: ServiceLifecycleState, to: ServiceLifecycleState) -> bool` returning true for spec-valid edges only (Unknown→Bootstrapping, Bootstrapping→Active, Active↔Quiet, Quiet→Silent, Silent→Dormant, Dormant→Archived, Archived→Active special edge for corpus restore, plus any-state→any-state via manual override).

3. **Define `ServiceRegistry` trait + `InMemoryServiceRegistry` struct** in `crates/triage/src/lifecycle/registry.rs`. Trait surface: `fn current_state(service: &str) -> Option<ServiceLifecycleState>`, `fn list_all() -> Vec<ServiceListItem>` (returns `(service, state, last_seen_unix_nano, manual_override)`), `fn set_manual_override(service: &str, override_state: Option<ServiceLifecycleState>)`, `fn tick_all(now_unix_nano: i64, baseline: &BaselineState, dormant_after_secs: u64, archived_after_secs: u64) -> Vec<ServiceLifecycleEvent>` (evaluates each entry, emits transitions). Per-service entry: `ServiceRegistryEntry { state, first_seen_unix_nano, last_seen_unix_nano, last_transition_unix_nano, manual_override: Option<ServiceLifecycleState> }`. Implementation uses `DashMap<String, ServiceRegistryEntry>` for lock-free per-shard access mirroring chunk #61 `BaselineState`.

4. **Define `ServiceLifecycleEvent` + `TransitionTrigger` + `ServiceLifecycleBroadcast`** in `crates/triage/src/lifecycle/broadcast.rs` mirroring chunk #63 `crates/triage/src/pattern/broadcast.rs` exactly. Const `STREAM_NAME_SERVICE_LIFECYCLE: &str = "pulse://stream/service-lifecycle"` + `BROADCAST_CAPACITY: usize = 32`. `ServiceLifecycleEvent` fields: `service: String`, `from_state: ServiceLifecycleState`, `to_state: ServiceLifecycleState`, `transitioned_at_unix_nano: i64`, `trigger: TransitionTrigger`. `TransitionTrigger` enum: `Activity | Restart | ThresholdExpiry | ManualOverride | CorpusRestore` (snake_case serde). `ServiceLifecycleBroadcast` wrapper with `sender() / subscribe() / subscriber_count() / Default impl`.

5. **Write PII negative-canary test** `service_lifecycle_event_has_no_pii_fields` in `crates/triage/src/lifecycle/broadcast.rs::tests` asserting (a) presence of allowed identifier-class fields (`service`, `from_state`, `to_state`, `transitioned_at_unix_nano`, `trigger`); (b) absence of banned substrings (`attribute`, `attributes`, `span_id`, `trace_id`, `scope_name`, `instrumentation_scope`, `body`, `description`, `message`). Mirror `crates/triage/src/pattern/broadcast.rs:119-160` pattern.

6. **Define `start_lifecycle_heartbeat` task** in `crates/triage/src/lifecycle/mod.rs` — a `tokio::time::interval(Duration::from_secs(15))` loop that (a) reads `BaselineState::service_count()` + per-service activity, (b) calls `registry.tick_all(...)`, (c) emits each returned `ServiceLifecycleEvent` on the broadcast topic, (d) emits the heartbeat tick `tracing::info!(target: "triage.lifecycle.tick", tracked_services_total = N, services_unknown = U, ..., "heartbeat")` with bounded enum count fields only. Also emit one aggregate transition event per tick `tracing::info!(target: "triage.lifecycle.transition", from_state = "active", to_state = "quiet", count = 3, "...")` per `from_state→to_state` bucket — NOT one event per per-service transition (per `.claude/rules/observability.md` Session Addition 2026-05-17 session 84 aggregate-only).

7. **Subscribe to `pulse://stream/restart-events` broadcast** in `start_lifecycle_heartbeat` task setup. Each `RestartEvent` triggers an immediate `registry.set_state_on_restart(&restart_event.service)` call, transitioning the service to `Bootstrapping` regardless of activity state. Service-first-seen transitions (Unknown→Bootstrapping) derive from `BaselineState::service_count()` + per-service entry existence checks at tick time.

8. **Add tracing target consts** to `crates/triage/src/lifecycle/mod.rs`: `TARGET_LIFECYCLE_TICK: &str = "triage.lifecycle.tick"`, `TARGET_LIFECYCLE_TRANSITION: &str = "triage.lifecycle.transition"`, `TARGET_LIFECYCLE_CORPUS_RESTORE: &str = "triage.lifecycle.corpus_restore"`, `TARGET_PIPELINE_L1B_TRACKED_SERVICES_TOTAL: &str = "pipeline.l1b.tracked_services_total"`, `TARGET_METRIC_LIFECYCLE_STATE_DISTRIBUTION: &str = "metric.triage.lifecycle.state_distribution"`.

9. **Re-export from `crates/triage/src/contract.rs`** — add `pub use crate::lifecycle::*;` block mirroring chunks #58/#61/#62/#63 precedent. Specifically re-export `ServiceLifecycleState`, `ServiceLifecycleEvent`, `ServiceLifecycleBroadcast`, `ServiceRegistry`, `InMemoryServiceRegistry`, `ServiceRegistryEntry`, `ServiceListItem`, `STREAM_NAME_SERVICE_LIFECYCLE`, `TransitionTrigger`, `start_lifecycle_heartbeat`, `is_valid_transition`.

10. **Extend `Settings` struct** in `crates/ui-bridge/src/contract.rs:108-127` (per security.md Session Additions 2026-05-09 lower-cost pattern):
    - Add `#[serde(default = "default_lifecycle_dormant_after_secs")] pub lifecycle_dormant_after_secs: u64,`
    - Add `#[serde(default = "default_lifecycle_archived_after_secs")] pub lifecycle_archived_after_secs: u64,`
    - Add sibling `fn default_lifecycle_dormant_after_secs() -> u64 { 3600 }` + `fn default_lifecycle_archived_after_secs() -> u64 { 86400 }`
    - Update `impl Default for Settings { fn default() -> Self { ... }` block to include new fields
    - Update `Settings::validate()` (or equivalent setter) to reject values < 60 OR > i64::MAX with `AppError::Validation { field, reason }` per security plan §Input Validation row 6
    - Add unit tests asserting defaults + validation rejection paths

11. **Optionally** also extend `Settings` with `lifecycle_manual_overrides: HashMap<String, ServiceLifecycleState>` for the manual override surface (Settings-based path per Q2 recommendation), OR defer manual override storage to the chunk #67 follow-up UI chunk (registry-based with a dedicated `services.set_manual_override` procedure). **For chunk #67 scope: defer manual override storage to follow-up UI chunk; keep registry's `set_manual_override` method available but not wired through Settings.** Document this deferral in plan acceptance criteria.

12. **Create `pulse-app/src/services_router.rs`** mirroring `pulse-app/src/connection_router.rs:1-187` exactly. Define `#[taurpc::procedures(path = "services")] pub trait ServicesApi { async fn list_with_states() -> Result<ServiceListPayload, AppError>; }` + `#[derive(Clone)] pub struct ServicesApiImpl { registry: Arc<dyn ServiceRegistry>, broadcast: Arc<ServiceLifecycleBroadcast> }` + `ServicesApiImpl::new(...)` constructor + `#[taurpc::resolvers] impl ServicesApi for ServicesApiImpl { ... }`. Resolver instruments with `#[tracing::instrument(skip_all, fields(item_count = field::Empty, traceparent = field::Empty))]` + emits `tracing::info!(target: "services.list_with_states.request", item_count = N, "services.list_with_states returned")` after span.record. Maps `ServiceRegistry::list_all()` to `ServiceListPayload { items: Vec<ServiceListItem>, total: usize, next_cursor: Option<String> }` per arch §Standard Contracts paginated list shape (next_cursor=None for initial implementation; pagination deferred).
13. **Add `pub mod services_router;`** to `pulse-app/src/lib.rs` mirroring existing pattern `pub mod connection_router;` + `pub mod restart_observer;` etc.

title: Chunk route#68: "Corpus SQLite scaffold + schema + encryption + PII scrubber"

data.head: ### Chunk route#68: "Corpus SQLite scaffold + schema + encryption + PII scrubber"

body: **Constraints across domains:**

- (security) Corpus SQLite file MUST be encrypted at rest using a key from OS-native secret store (macOS Keychain / Linux Secret Service / Windows DPAPI / Credential Manager) — never plaintext, never hardcoded, never derived from non-secret material; passphrase fallback REQUIRED only when keychain unavailable, salted-KDF derived (Argon2id/scrypt) (per security plan §Data Protection §At rest per-medium row + §Code Patterns NEVER ban + capability P-049).

- (security) DuckDB encryption MUST remain DISABLED — corpus uses `rusqlite` SEPARATE from the existing in-memory `pulse_buffer` DuckDB; CVE-2025-64429 ban on DuckDB encryption-at-rest is unaffected (per security plan §Data Protection §At rest line 151 + §Code Patterns Data Protection ban line 394).

- (security) All SQL against corpus MUST use `rusqlite` prepared statements with `?` placeholders + parameter binding — NEVER `format!(...)`. Same prepared-statement discipline as DuckDB extends to SQLite (per security plan §Input Validation "DuckDB query parameters" + §Code Patterns Input ban line 382).

- (security) Corpus file path MUST canonicalize via `strict-path` + assert resolved path lives under per-platform resolved data dir or `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` override (per security plan §Input Validation "Configuration values" + §Code Patterns CWE-22 ban line 384).

- (security) PII scrubber primitive MUST run at corpus ingestion BEFORE persistence — never store raw OTLP attribute values that could echo back through `storage.inspect()`, future export (P-046), or LLM retrieval (P-044); 7 scrubber categories (email/JWT/bearer/API-key/credit-card/SSN/secret-like KV) per capability spec P-047 (per security plan §Logging NEVER list line 329 — extends "never log" to "never persist").
- (security) `storage.inspect` + `storage.path` TauRPC procedures MUST follow the quadruple-binding pattern (per security.md Session Additions 2026-05-12).

- (security) Corpus storage default per-workspace scoping with no cross-workspace / cross-device / external endpoint sharing (per capability P-050 + security plan §Cross-cutting Self-observation discipline).

- (security) Encryption-key custody class MUST NOT leak into logs / error messages / `AppError::Internal { message }`; sanitize at `From<thiserror::Error> for AppError` (per security plan §Logging NEVER ban line 421).

- (design) First-run keychain-access prompt, if materialized in-app, MUST use desktop-webview modal pattern (`#343A45` Raised-3 bg + 1px subtle border + radius-lg 8px + space-md padding); NEVER `confirm()` / `alert()` (per design-system §Anti-Patterns Per-Surface Bans desktop-webview row 7).
- (design) Any Settings → Storage UI MUST consume Tailwind v4 `@theme` tokens; no hardcoded hex (per design-system §Surface: desktop-webview Tokens + §Self-Validation Protocol Token Test).

- (design) Destructive "Delete corpus" confirmation MUST use the modal primitive (chunk #41 modal scaffold) with styled Dialog component (per design-system §Anti-Patterns Per-Surface Bans + §Component Patterns Cards/Panels).
- (design) OS-native first-run keychain prompts MUST defer to OS conventions (no custom chrome over keychain dialogs) (per design-system §Anti-Patterns Per-Surface Bans desktop-native row 1).

- (design) Error state messaging ("keychain access denied", "corpus encryption failed") MUST pair `--color-accent` (#C7556A) with text label or icon — not color alone (per design-system §Anti-Patterns Universal Bans row 5).

- (design) UI motion (modal entrance, confirmation collapse) MUST respect chrome budget 0.35: 150ms ease-out hover/focus, 200ms ease-out panel transitions, no spring/bounce/parallax (per design-system §Motion hard limits).

- (layouts) Settings modal: overlay backdrop + inner card with `color-raised-3` bg + 1px subtle border + `radius-lg` + `padding: space-md`, max-width/height ~80% viewport, scrollable overflow (per layout-templates §Surface desktop-webview / Component Settings modal form).

- (layouts) Confirm-on-delete pattern MUST reuse existing modal primitive (overlay + card + close button + focus trap), not introduce new dialog primitive (per layout-templates §Component Investigation modal + Settings modal Layout).

- (layouts) Platform-specific confirmation button ordering: macOS Cancel-left/Confirm-right; Windows Confirm-left/Cancel-right; Linux standard (per layout-templates §Surface desktop-native Platform-specific notes).

- (layouts) Settings panel content lives in Full dashboard "Settings" tab/route (`/settings`); first-run keychain prompt is the only Storage element that may render outside Settings (occurs at boot) (per layout-templates §IA notes Deep-link convention).
- (tests) Standard tier coverage gates: ≥75% line / ≥70% branch / ≥85% function for new `crates/corpus/` code (per test-plan §10 Quality Gates).

data.head: # Phase 64 Plan — chunks route#68: "Corpus SQLite scaffold + schema + encryption + PII scrubber"

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase Phase 4. Read by /andromeda-implement.
Manual edits between runs are fine; do not edit during /implement run._
- **Phase number:** 64

- **Route chunks covered:**
  - route#68 "Corpus SQLite scaffold + schema + encryption + PII scrubber — new `crates/corpus/`; OS-keychain encryption; security-crate PII scrubber primitive (capabilities P-041/P-047–P-051; detail in pulse-v0_2_0-route §69)"
- **Epoch:** Foundation v0.2.0 (final chunk of Epoch 9)

Chunk #68 lays the persistence foundation that unlocks 9 subsequent v0.2.0 chunks (#64 activity-floor wiring, #66 fingerprint persistence, #70 incidents, #71+ digest pipeline, #74 LLM retrieval, #78/#84/#85 etc.). It creates TWO NEW workspace crates: `crates/corpus/` with SQLite-backed persistent storage for the incident corpus (distinct from the existing `triage::baseline::corpus` bincode-backed baseline-state persistence — naming carefully separated in module docs); AND `crates/security/` housing the PII scrubber primitive consolidated per v0.2.0 plan §69 language ("security-crate PII scrubber primitive"). Six schema tables (`baseline_state`, `service_registry`, `pipeline_metrics`, `incidents`, `incident_events`, `digest_archive`) land as DDL per dist-arch v3 §Schema Additions. Encryption-at-rest uses an OS-keychain-stored key (macOS Keychain / Linux Secret Service / Windows DPAPI via the `keyring` crate, with user-passphrase fallback when keychain unavailable) + per-cell AES-256-GCM encryption via the `aes-gcm` crate. The `crates/security/` crate exposes the PII scrubber as a reusable primitive consumed both by `crates/corpus/` (at ingestion, before persistence) AND by `pulse-app/src/observability.rs` subscriber Layer (defense-in-depth before file write). Two TauRPC procedures land: `storage.inspect()` (read-only corpus metadata query, no arguments — read-only-by-design discipline per security plan §P-051) and `storage.path()` (returns structured envelope with corpus DB path + size + schema version).

Per combined.md cross-domain reconciliation: a11y is out-of-domain (pure backend); design + layouts are deferred (no Settings → Storage UI in this chunk — OS-native keychain prompt only); arch / security / tests / obs are fully in scope. Per research.md: the new crate scaffold mirrors `curation` (chunk #58) and `triage` (chunk #60) precedents; the TauRPC router at the binary boundary mirrors `services_router.rs` (chunk #67) and `connection_router.rs` (chunk #59) including the trait-in-lower-crate + impl-in-pulse-app cross-state-delivery pattern (`CorpusReader` trait in `crates/corpus/src/contract.rs`; impl threaded into `StorageApiImpl` via `Arc<dyn CorpusReader>`).

Per arch §Established Decisions [Database] + [Telemetry Retention Surface] and security plan §Data Protection §At rest: this chunk DELIBERATELY EXTENDS the prior "in-memory DuckDB ring buffer only" scope decision by introducing the FIRST persistent on-disk database in the project. Two SCHEMA-LEVEL plan-amendment follow-ups required at wrap time per security ↔ arch contract binding: (a) security plan §Data Protection §At rest — per medium gains a new "persistent disk database" row; (b) security plan §Secret Management "What counts as secret" gains a new "corpus encryption key" entry. Both deferred to follow-up `/andromeda-security` re-run (NOT in this chunk's commit) — only flagged here.

1. **Add `crates/corpus/` + `crates/security/` workspace members.** Edit `Cargo.toml` (workspace root) to insert BOTH `"crates/corpus"` AND `"crates/security"` into `[workspace] members = [...]` (between `crates/triage` and `crates/workspace-detector` per concept grouping; see research.md "Conventions to follow"). Extend `[workspace.dependencies]` with `rusqlite = { version = "0.32", features = ["bundled"] }` (bundled = static linking, no system SQLite dep — cross-platform reproducible builds), `keyring = { version = "3", default-features = false, features = ["apple-native", "windows-native", "linux-native-sync-persistent"] }` (per security extract OS keychain wrapper choice — explicit per-platform features avoid pulling excess transitive deps), `aes-gcm = "0.10"` (RustCrypto AEAD; small footprint; default features only — no plat-specific assembly intrinsics), and `regex = "1"` (PII pattern catalog compilation in the security crate). Document version-pin rationale in comment blocks mirroring the chunk #61 tdigest/dashmap/bincode + chunk #66 blake3 comment shape. Verify `cargo deny check bans licenses sources` post-add — extend `deny.toml [bans] skip` list with one-line provenance comments for any new known-benign duplicates (per security.md Session Additions 2026-05-03).

2. **Scaffold `crates/corpus/` crate per the curation+triage template.** Create `crates/corpus/Cargo.toml` with `serde + thiserror + tracing + rusqlite + keyring + strict-path + chrono + bincode` deps; dev-deps `tempfile + rstest + proptest + serde_json`. Create `crates/corpus/src/lib.rs` exposing ONLY `pub mod contract;` with `pub(crate)` internals: `db`, `schema`, `encryption`, `keychain`, `scrubber`, `error`. The `lib.rs` module docstring MUST explicitly distinguish "incident corpus" (this crate; SQLite-backed persistent store for v0.2.0 capability cluster P-041/P-047–P-051) from "baseline corpus" (`triage::baseline::corpus`; bincode-backed in-memory baseline-state persistence from chunk #61) — cite both chunk numbers for future readers (per research.md "New files to create" docstring requirement).

3. **Define corpus public contract in `crates/corpus/src/contract.rs`.** Declare `pub struct Corpus` (or `pub trait CorpusStore` if testability requires trait abstraction — pick `trait` to mirror `ServiceRegistry` precedent and enable in-memory test impls). Public surface methods: `open(path: &Path, keychain: Arc<dyn KeychainBackend>) -> Result<Self, Error>` + `path(&self) -> &Path` + `inspect(&self) -> Result<InspectionMetadata, Error>` + `metadata-only field accessors`. Define `pub struct InspectionMetadata { record_counts: BTreeMap<String, u64>, total_bytes_on_disk: u64, schema_version: u32 }`. Define `pub trait CorpusReader: Send + Sync + Debug { fn inspect(&self) -> Result<InspectionMetadata, Error>; fn path(&self) -> PathBuf; }` for cross-crate state delivery into the TauRPC resolver (per research.md "Cross-crate state via trait-in-lower" pattern + session-learnings 2026-05-16). Define `pub enum Error` via `thiserror::Error` with variants `KeyringUnavailable | MigrationFailed | EncryptionFailed | QueryFailed | ScrubberMatch | PathTraversal | SizeCapExceeded | SchemaVersionMismatch` — sanitize Display impls (no file paths / library versions / stack traces) per combined §Constraints + arch §Conventions Error response schema.

4. **Implement `crates/corpus/src/db.rs` rusqlite connection helper.** `pub(crate) fn open_with_key(path: &Path, key: &EncryptionKey) -> Result<Connection, Error>` opens (or creates) the SQLite file. Apply prepared-statement-only discipline at the boundary: any caller-facing query helpers (e.g., `pub(crate) fn count_table(conn: &Connection, table: &str) -> Result<u64, Error>`) use `conn.prepare("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ?")` + parameter binding — NEVER `format!("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM {}", table)`. Define a fixed allowlist of table names (the 6 schema tables); reject any other input. Atomic write convention for any side-file artifacts (e.g., salt file if KDF used) — mirror `triage::baseline::corpus::persist_state` lines 54-67 tmp + rename pattern. Path resolution via `strict-path::PathBoundary::try_new_create(data_dir)?.virtual_join("corpus/corpus.db")` (or equivalent) to canonicalize + assert under resolved data dir per arch §Occupied Resources Filesystem locations.

5. **Implement `crates/corpus/src/schema.rs` schema versioning + DDL.** Define `pub(crate) const SCHEMA_VERSION: u32 = 1;`. DDL statements as `pub(crate) const CREATE_*_SQL: &str = "..."` constants for each of the 6 tables — `snake_case` table + column names per arch §Conventions Database entity naming; nullable columns reserved for spec-optional fields; surrogate INTEGER PRIMARY KEY (rowid alias) acceptable for corpus tables where no OTLP-native composite identity exists (per arch §Conventions Primary key + Nullable patterns, documented in chunk plan rather than assumed). Implement `pub(crate) fn apply_migrations(conn: &Connection) -> Result<u32, Error>` that reads `PRAGMA user_version`; if 0, runs all DDL inside a transaction + sets `PRAGMA user_version = SCHEMA_VERSION`; if equals SCHEMA_VERSION, no-op; if higher or unexpected, returns `Error::SchemaVersionMismatch`. First-launch idempotent (re-running migration produces same end state).

6. **Implement `crates/corpus/src/encryption.rs`.** **DECISION (DEFAULT, surfaces at Phase 6 review):** use OS-keychain-stored 256-bit key + cell-level encryption via the `rusqlite::types` blob round-trip pattern, NOT SQLCipher. Rationale: avoids C-side dep chain (`-DSQLITE_HAS_CODEC=1` + SQLCipher source), keeps `rusqlite = "bundled"` dep self-contained, smaller cross-platform build matrix. Trade-off: granularity is per-cell not per-page; row + column metadata visible without the key (only cell payloads opaque). For chunk #68 scaffold scope (no real incident content yet), this trade-off is acceptable; if future chunks need full-file opacity, swap to SQLCipher in a follow-up chunk + accept the C-dep cost then. **ALTERNATIVE: full-file encryption via `age` crate.** Encrypts the entire SQLite file at close; decrypts at open into a tempfile that lives only in memory or under restrictive perms. Higher overhead per open/close cycle but full opacity. Phase 6 user review chooses ONE; defer the alternative to a follow-up chunk if rejected. Define `pub(crate) struct EncryptionKey([u8; 32])` (zeroize on drop via `zeroize` crate if added). Define `pub(crate) fn cell_encrypt(key: &EncryptionKey, plaintext: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8>` + `cell_decrypt` round-trip via AES-256-GCM (use the `aes-gcm` crate, RustCrypto-maintained, ~10 KB transitive footprint). Test fixtures use a fake-keychain backend returning a deterministic key.

7. **Implement `crates/corpus/src/keychain.rs` keychain backend abstraction.** Define `pub trait KeychainBackend: Send + Sync + Debug { fn fetch_or_create_key(&self, service_id: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>, KeychainError>; }`. Production impl `pub struct OsKeychainBackend` wraps `keyring::Entry::new("com.andromeda.pulse", "corpus-key")` — calls `set_password()` with a freshly-generated 32-byte key on first launch (after user keychain consent), `get_password()` on subsequent launches. Returns `KeychainError::Unavailable` if keychain unreachable (passphrase fallback path triggers in caller). Test impl `pub struct FakeKeychainBackend { keys: Arc<Mutex<HashMap<String, Vec<u8>>>> }` returns deterministic in-memory keys for tests (per tests extract trait-injected fake backend pattern + test-plan §8 Anti-monkey-patching). NO real OS keychain API call from CI tests (per combined §Anti-patterns + test-plan §6 P5 surrogate pattern). First-run UX: keychain prompt fires via `keyring::Entry::set_password()` triggering OS-native dialog (per security extract observable signal); on user reject OR platform without keychain support (e.g., headless CI), fall back to passphrase prompt with explicit "loss of passphrase = permanent corpus loss" warning text (per capability P-049 + open question 5 mitigation).

8. **Scaffold `crates/security/` crate + implement PII scrubber primitive.** Per Phase 6 user decision (NOT default — diverged from chunk #68 in-place option): create `crates/security/Cargo.toml` with `serde + thiserror + tracing + regex` deps + dev-deps `proptest + rstest`. Create `crates/security/src/lib.rs` exposing `pub mod scrubber;` as the public surface. Implement `crates/security/src/scrubber.rs` with `pub fn scrub_attribute(value: &str) -> ScrubbedValue` returning `enum ScrubbedValue::{Allowed(String), Redacted { category: &'static str }}`. Pattern catalog: 7 P-047 categories (email / JWT / bearer / API-key / credit-card / SSN / secret-like KV). Implementation uses a `OnceLock<Vec<(Regex, &'static str)>>` for compiled-pattern caching (lazy init on first call); each pattern carries a stable `category` label (no value content) for redacted-form output. Latency target ≤1ms p99 per insertion (per security extract acceptance criterion); enforce in scrubber unit-test microbenchmark. Co-located `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` covers per-category positive + per-category negative cases + property-based fuzz via `proptest` (random strings → invariant assertions: scrubber output never longer than input + never contains raw secret patterns). The `crates/corpus/` crate depends on `crates/security/` for the `scrub_attribute` primitive used at ingestion; `pulse-app/src/observability.rs` subscriber Layer ALSO depends on `crates/security/` for defense-in-depth scrubbing before file write — both layers MUST agree on the same scrubbing rules per obs-plan §8 Integration points. **Arch impact:** Adds `security` to the canonical workspace crate-names list in arch §Occupied Resources — `/andromeda-evolve --allow-arch-registry` amendment expands to cover BOTH new crates (corpus + security).

9. **Implement `crates/corpus/src/error.rs`.** `thiserror`-derived `pub enum Error` variants per Step 3. From impls for `rusqlite::Error -> Error::QueryFailed { message: String }` (extract sanitized one-liner from the rusqlite error; never embed schema column names / file paths). From impl for `io::Error -> Error::PathTraversal | Error::SizeCapExceeded` based on error kind.

10. **Implement `crates/corpus/src/contract.rs::Corpus` concrete struct.** Holds `Arc<Connection>` (wrapped in `Mutex` if mutable from multiple async tasks; otherwise `RwLock` if reads dominate). `Corpus::open(path, keychain)` flow: (a) `keychain.fetch_or_create_key("corpus-key")` → `EncryptionKey`; (b) `db::open_with_key(&path, &key)` → `Connection`; (c) `schema::apply_migrations(&conn)` → schema_version; (d) wrap in `Corpus { conn: Arc::new(Mutex::new(conn)), path: path.to_path_buf(), schema_version }` + return. Implement `CorpusReader for Corpus { fn inspect(&self) -> Result<InspectionMetadata, Error>; fn path(&self) -> PathBuf; }` — `inspect()` iterates the 6 tables via `db::count_table()` + returns `InspectionMetadata`.

11. **Create `pulse-app/src/storage_router.rs` TauRPC router.** Mirror `services_router.rs` shape verbatim — replace `services` with `storage`, `ServiceRegistry` with `CorpusReader`, `ServiceListPayload` with `StorageInspectPayload + StoragePathPayload`. Two `#[taurpc::procedures(path = "storage")]` methods: `async fn inspect() -> Result<StorageInspectPayload, AppError>` (NO arguments — read-only-by-design) + `async fn path() -> Result<StoragePathPayload, AppError>` (returns `StoragePathPayload { path: String, size_bytes: u64, last_write_at_unix_nano: Option<i64>, schema_version: u32 }` structured envelope per research.md "Open question 6" decision). `#[tracing::instrument(skip_all, fields(record_count = tracing::field::Empty))]` decorators. From impl `From<corpus::Error> for AppError` lives in this file (binary boundary; avoids ui-bridge dep on corpus — per research.md "Files to modify" decision deferred-to-Phase-4).

12. **Extend `pulse-app/src/main.rs` setup closure.** Construct `OsKeychainBackend::new()` → `Arc<dyn KeychainBackend>`; resolve corpus path under `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` resolved root via `strict-path` canonicalization; construct `Corpus::open(corpus_path, keychain_backend)?` → `Arc<dyn CorpusReader>`; construct `StorageApiImpl::new(corpus_reader)`; add `.merge(storage_impl.clone().into_handler())` to the production router builder chain. Also extend `pub mod storage_router;` declaration in `pulse-app/src/lib.rs` (mirror connection_router / services_router pub mod declarations). Boot failure on `Corpus::open` error: log structured `tracing::error!(target: "corpus.open.error", ...)` with sanitized error message (no file path) + return early. Document the boot path behavior in `pulse-app/src/main.rs` setup closure comment.

13. **Extend `emit_taurpc_bindings` test in `pulse-app/src/main.rs::tests`.** Construct a test `StorageApiImpl` (use `FakeKeychainBackend` + in-memory `Corpus` instance via test helper) + merge into the test router via `.merge(storage_impl.clone().into_handler())`. Without this step, the test's bindings.ts emission omits the `storage.*` namespace and `cargo xtask capability-drift` reports `missing` — per session-learnings 2026-05-12 quadruple-binding place 4.

14. **Update `pulse-app/capabilities/default.json` description.** Append one sentence mentioning chunk #68 adds `storage.{inspect,path}` (router-level coverage, mirroring the existing chunk #47 plugins + chunk #49 mcp + chunk #67 services per-chunk note). NO `permissions` array changes (TauRPC dispatches through single invoke handler — router-level coverage suffices per CLAUDE.md Session Additions 2026-05-03 + security.md Session Additions 2026-05-03).

15. **Extend `xtask/src/main.rs::EXPECTED_PROCEDURES`.** Add `"storage.inspect"` and `"storage.path"` entries (lines 655-681 region). Add new test `expected_procedures_includes_storage_namespace_at_chunk_68` mirroring `expected_procedures_includes_services_list_with_states_at_chunk_67` (lines 938-944) — asserts both procedures present in the list.

1. **Encryption approach: SQLCipher vs. OS-keychain-key + age-encrypted DB file vs. application-level cell encryption?** SQLCipher is the canonical SQLite encryption-at-rest solution but adds C-side dependency (requires building with `-DSQLITE_HAS_CODEC=1` + SQLCipher source). Alternative: OS-keychain-stored encryption key + `age` (or libsodium) encryption of the entire SQLite file at open/close boundaries (less granular but simpler dep graph). Recommend starting MINIMAL — chunk #68 ships `inspect()` with empty filter returning corpus metadata (record counts per table + total bytes) + `path()` returning the path string; richer query DSL deferred to chunk #70 incident records + chunk #71+ digest pipeline integrations.

4. **Heartbeat tick: does corpus subsystem need `corpus.tick` heartbeat emission?** obs extract recommends emission ("if corpus subsystem maintains background tasks"). Chunk #68 scaffold may NOT have background tasks (synchronous open + on-demand write + lazy schema migration on first launch) → tick emission deferred to chunk #70+ when persistent incident tracking adds write loops. Recommend Phase 4 documents this decision explicitly (no `corpus.tick` in chunk #68; emit on first background-task introduction).

5. **First-run keychain prompt UI: in-app modal vs. OS-native dialog only?** design + layouts extracts both flag this as "if materialized in-app modal" vs. "if OS-native". Per a11y extract: a11y deferral assumed no in-app modal in chunk #68. Recommend Phase 4 CHOOSES OS-native only for chunk #68 (`keyring` crate surfaces the OS dialog; no Pulse-owned wrapper); in-app explainer modal (showing what the OS prompt will ask for) deferred to a follow-up chunk that introduces the full Settings → Storage UI. This collapses design + layouts + a11y surfaces to zero new UI files in chunk #68 (matching the a11y "No domain coverage" assessment).

6. **`storage.path()` return type: bare String vs. structured envelope?** TauRPC convention prefers structured envelopes (`StoragePathPayload { path: String }` allows future expansion like `{path, size_bytes, last_write_at, schema_version}` without breaking change). Recommend Phase 4 chooses structured envelope from start.

7. **`storage.inspect()` write-rejection by typing?** security rot warning surfaced no explicit test for "verify storage.inspect signature has only read-typed inputs." Recommend Phase 4 makes `inspect()` take NO arguments in chunk #68 scaffold (returns corpus metadata only); future filter-bearing inspect variant goes through a separate procedure (e.g., `storage.query_incidents(filter)`) that maintains the read-only-by-design discipline.

data.head: ### Chunk route#69: Drain Rust implementation + template profiling diagnostics (Phase A spike only)

body: **Constraints across domains:**

- (security) Dependency audit gates apply to spike dependencies if any are added to workspace `Cargo.toml` — preferred path is throwaway branch (zero CI footprint); alternative is `crates/triage-experimental/` gitignored crate but any deps added must be SPDX-allowlisted + non-banned + non-duplicate per `deny.toml` policy (per security plan §Dependency Security CI integration).

- (security) LogHub corpus handling: public datasets (Apache 2.0), no upstream PII concerns, but corpus files MUST NOT commit into the repo — would inflate clone footprint + bind `cargo deny check sources` if registry-vendored. Document fetch path in findings doc; spike harness loads from a local cache outside git (per security plan §Data Protection "data lifecycle" framing).

- (security) No OTLP attribute values or verbatim log lines in spike output / findings doc — Phase A measurements are pure statistical aggregates (LOC count, % match rate, p99 μs, memory bytes); illustrative examples (if any) must be sanitized synthetic log lines (per security plan §Logging anti-patterns "NEVER log raw OTLP attribute values").

- (security) Spike code MUST NOT mutate workspace `Cargo.toml` source list, dependabot.yml, or `deny.toml` allowlist — throwaway branch avoids re-triggering §Dependency Security CI gates against the spike's footprint (per security plan §Dependency Security update policy + §Bootstrap phases `dep-audit-tooling-install`).

- (security) Spike MUST NOT introduce SQL-shaped patterns that could carry forward into Phase B violating §Code Patterns — if any DuckDB lookup is prototyped, it must use `Connection::prepare` + `?` placeholders even at spike level (per security plan §Input Validation row "DuckDB query parameters" + §Code Patterns ban).

- (security) Throwaway branch / gitignored crate semantics MUST be enforced via `.gitignore` BEFORE any spike file written — add `crates/triage-experimental/` to `.gitignore` first (per security plan §Secret Management `.gitignore` discipline).

- (tests) Standard gate baseline MUST stay GREEN on main throughout Phase A: `cargo fmt --check` + `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` + `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` + `cargo xtask capability-drift` + `npm run lint --prefix pulse-app/ui` + `npm run typecheck --prefix pulse-app/ui` + `npm run test --prefix pulse-app/ui` (per test-plan §12 Decisions Log 2026-05-10 `chunk-gate-baseline-coverage` trigger).

- (tests) Spike code MUST NOT enter the workspace nextest harness — `crates/triage-experimental/` (if used) is gitignored and excluded from the workspace `Cargo.toml` members list; throwaway-branch alternative achieves the same isolation (per chunk spec + test-plan §10 zero-flakiness budget).

- (tests) LogHub corpus subset (Apache web logs + Linux syslog + HDFS) MUST NOT be committed to the repo — fetched at spike run time by the spike harness (per test-plan §7 Test Data & Fixtures "self-bootstrapping requirement" + §11 Test Data "NEVER use production telemetry dumps in tests").

- (tests) Phase A measurement methodology MUST yield reproducible numeric outputs (LOC count via `tokei` / `cloc`; per-event latency p99 via histogram across ≥N events; template tree memory footprint via `std::mem::size_of_val` or heap profiler) (per test-plan §1 agent-driven invariant for machine-parseable evidence).

- (tests) Phase A findings document at `.andromeda/decisions/pre-d2-drain-spike.md` MUST contain the four explicit decision outcomes (PROCEED / REVISE / SPLIT / DEFER) with quantitative evidence supporting the chosen outcome (per chunk's internal two-phase discipline gating Phase B).
- (tests) Boot-smoke gate is NOT required for Phase A — Phase A modifies zero boot-path files (per test-plan §12 Decisions Log 2026-05-09 `boot-smoke-coverage` trigger).

- (obs) Phase A spike measurements MUST be captured via deterministic, agent-readable discipline — `criterion` 0.5 for per-event latency p99 (project-canonical regression tool); `std::time::Instant` + structured aggregation acceptable for one-shot LOC / memory / count captures (per obs-plan §10 SLO Invariants & Telemetry Budgets).

- (obs) Spike code MUST NOT link an OTel SDK or instantiate any OTLP exporter — preserves project-universal invariant by construction (no production runtime to instrument) (per obs-plan §1 line 26 + §11 Universal anti-pattern).

- (obs) Phase A findings doc MUST capture numeric measurements in machine-parseable form — per-event latency p99 in **microseconds (NOT milliseconds)** since the v0.2.0 metric name is `drain_assignment_latency_p99_microseconds`; template-count integer; template-tree memory bytes (per obs-plan §5 Metric Coverage cardinality + unit discipline).

- (obs) Spike code MUST NOT `println!` / `dbg!` to stdout if intended to be invoked under any agent harness — spike standalone bench-binary may use stdout for one-shot reports but `tracing-subscriber` (if instantiated) MUST be configured to stderr-JSON (per obs-plan §11 anti-pattern + §3 Logging stack).

- (obs) Phase A findings doc structure MUST include a Phase B forward-reference section listing planned production telemetry signal names (`metric.pipeline.l1c.drain_template_count_total` Counter; `metric.pipeline.l1c.drain_assignment_latency_p99_microseconds` Distribution) per obs-plan §5 Metric Coverage naming convention `metric.{module}.{measure}`.

- (arch) Phase A spike code MUST NOT be added to the production `Cargo.toml` workspace `members` array — gitignored path requires explicit exclusion from workspace `members` (per arch §Inherited Defaults Module boundaries).

- (arch) Workspace crate name `triage-experimental` is NOT reserved at arch §Occupied Resources Cargo workspace crate names — Phase A spike using this name MUST NOT trigger an Architecture Registry Update (per arch §Occupied Resources reservation discipline).

**Patterns to follow:**

data.head: # Phase 65 Plan — chunk route#69 (Phase A spike): Drain Rust spike validation

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase Phase 4. Read by /andromeda-implement.
Manual edits between runs are fine; do not edit during /implement run._
- **Phase number:** 65

- **Route chunks covered:**
  - route#69 "Drain Rust implementation + template profiling diagnostics — Drain3 Rust port (depth/similarity/masking); two-phase spike-then-production; diagnostics.template_distribution() panel (capability P-007; detail in pulse-v0_2_0-route §67)" — **Phase A (Drain spike validation) scope only**
- **Epoch:** Epoch 9 — Foundation v0.2.0

- **Phase B gate:** Phase B (production implementation) blocked on `.andromeda/decisions/pre-d2-drain-spike.md` returning PROCEED / REVISE / SPLIT decision. DEFER closes chunk #69 and v0.2.0 ships without Drain (capability P-007 documented as v0.3.0+ deferred).

Validate the Drain log-template-mining algorithm in Rust through a minimal prototype tested against a LogHub corpus subset, capturing measurements (LOC count, template assignment quality, per-event latency p99 in microseconds, template tree memory footprint) and committing a decision document at `.andromeda/decisions/pre-d2-drain-spike.md` (NEW directory) with one of four outcomes: PROCEED (initial 1000-1500 LOC estimate confirmed), REVISE (estimate adjusted with rationale), SPLIT (chunk #69 should split into sub-chunks), or DEFER (Drain pushed to v0.3.0+). The deliverable is the findings document — NOT production code. Spike code lives in a throwaway branch OR `crates/triage-experimental/` (gitignored); does NOT commit to main and does NOT modify production crates (`ingest` / `buffer` / `viz` / `ui-bridge` / `snapshot` / `curation` / `triage` / `workspace-detector` / `plugins` / `mcp-server` / `corpus` / `security` / `pulse-app`). Phase A explicitly EXCLUDES persistence, max_clusters cap with LRU eviction, custom masking via regex config, performance optimization beyond observation, production-quality tests, TauRPC `diagnostics.template_distribution()` procedure, `log_templates` table schema, `log_records.template_id` column population, and the Settings → Diagnostics panel UI — all of these are Phase B scope, planned in a future /andromeda-phase invocation IF the findings doc returns PROCEED / REVISE / SPLIT. Per combined.md cross-domain reconciliation, the spike preserves arch §Cross-cutting Patterns (no production code commits + no module dependency direction inversion), security plan §Dependency Security (zero workspace dep additions to main; throwaway branch is the preferred path), obs-plan §10 (criterion 0.5 measurement discipline reusable in spike's local Cargo.toml without touching the production xtask crate), test-plan §10 (zero-flakiness budget preserved — spike is excluded from `cargo nextest run --workspace`), and arch §Occupied Resources (zero registry-update entries — no IPC route / broadcast topic / env var / capability / crate name / filesystem path additions).

1. **Choose spike-code placement path** (per research.md Open Question Q1). Two options:
   - **Path A (PREFERRED — security extract Constraint #1)**: create a throwaway branch off `main` (e.g., `spike/drain-prototype`); spike code lives entirely on this branch and never merges to main. Zero footprint on main except for the findings doc commit.
   - **Path B (Alternative)**: implement spike code in `crates/triage-experimental/` (gitignored). Requires `.gitignore` entry added BEFORE creating any spike file.

2. **If Path B chosen**: append `crates/triage-experimental/` to `.gitignore` as the FIRST step (single-line edit; lands before any spike artifact). Do NOT add `triage-experimental` to root `Cargo.toml` `[workspace] members` array (per arch extract Constraint #1 + Anti-pattern #1 — would either pollute the dependency graph for all contributors OR cause `cargo check --workspace` failures on machines without the directory).

3. **Implement minimal Drain prototype** (in the chosen spike location):
   - Fixed-depth parse tree (depth=4) per chunk text + pulse-v0_2_0-route §Phase 3 line 276.
   - Similarity matching (threshold=0.5) per chunk text.
   - Basic masking config covering numbers, hex addresses (0x...), file paths (`/...`, `C:\...`).
   - Template extraction with parameter substitution producing `<*>`-style mask placeholders.
   - Reference: Drain3 Python algorithm (https://github.com/logpai/Drain3) — Rust port re-derives the algorithm; does NOT vendor Python source.
   - Spike code keeps its own local `Cargo.toml` (if Path B); workspace deps are NOT touched (per security extract Constraint #4 + arch extract Anti-pattern #1).

4. **Acquire LogHub corpus subset for measurements** (per chunk text + obs/tests extracts):
   - Recommended subset: Apache web logs + Linux syslog + HDFS application logs (per pulse-v0_2_0-route §Phase 3 line 277). Suggested 2k-sample fixture variants (Apache_2k.log, Linux_2k.log, HDFS_2k.log) which are well-documented LogHub research baselines.
   - Fetch path: local cache outside git (e.g., `~/loghub-corpus/` or per-developer choice). Document the fetch path in the findings doc Setup section; do NOT commit corpus files to the repo (per security extract Constraint #2 + Anti-pattern #1 + tests extract Constraint #3 + Anti-pattern #1).
   - Fetch method choice (curl recipe documented in findings doc OR build-time script in spike crate) is /implement Phase 1 discretion per research.md Open Question Q3.

5. **Run measurements against the LogHub subset** (per chunk text "Measurements captured" + obs extract acceptance criterion #1):
   - **LOC count**: spike-crate Rust source line count via `tokei` / `cloc` / `find ... | xargs wc -l` (any deterministic tool). Excludes test code; counts implementation lines only.
   - **Template assignment quality (% match rate)**: ratio of correctly-extracted templates against an oracle baseline. Oracle baseline either (a) hand-curated from a small subset for measurement purposes, OR (b) the Drain3 Python reference run against the same input (cross-reference). Tests extract anti-pattern #3 bans "human evaluates by eye" — match-rate must be a numerically-computed scalar.
   - **Per-event latency p99 (microseconds)**: via `criterion` 0.5 benchmark harness in spike-crate's `benches/` directory (if Path B) OR via standalone benchmark binary (if Path A). MUST emit microseconds, NOT milliseconds (per obs extract Constraint #3).
   - **Template tree memory footprint (bytes)**: via `std::mem::size_of_val(&tree)` snapshot after processing the corpus, OR via heap-profiler (e.g., `jemallocator` `mallctl`) if more accurate measure needed.

6. **Author the Phase A findings document** at `.andromeda/decisions/pre-d2-drain-spike.md` (creating the new `.andromeda/decisions/` directory implicitly via the file write). Required sections:
   - **Setup**: path option chosen (A or B), LogHub corpus subset identifiers, fetch method, run environment (rustc version, hardware), date.
   - **Measurements** (structured per obs extract acceptance criterion #1): table with at minimum `loc_count` (int), `template_count_total` (int per corpus), `template_assignment_match_rate_percent` (float per corpus), `per_event_latency_p99_microseconds` (float), `template_tree_memory_bytes` (int). Each measurement cell cites its capture discipline. Embedded JSON measurement blocks per obs extract pattern #2 for replicability.
   - **Phase B forward-reference**: planned production telemetry signal names `metric.pipeline.l1c.drain_template_count_total` (Counter) + `metric.pipeline.l1c.drain_assignment_latency_p99_microseconds` (Distribution) per obs extract acceptance criterion #2 — anchors future Phase B obs-plan amendment. Schema-name reconciliation per research.md Open Question Q4: cite the production-canonical names `log_records.template_id` column + new `log_templates` table (NOT "logs.template_id" from chunk text — production schema uses `log_records`).
   - **Decision**: one of `PROCEED` / `REVISE` / `SPLIT` / `DEFER` as a machine-grep-able token in either YAML front-matter (`decision: PROCEED`) or fenced JSON block (`{"decision": "PROCEED", ...}`) per tests extract acceptance criterion #4 + obs extract acceptance criterion #4.
   - **Rationale**: 1-3 paragraphs supporting the chosen decision with quantitative reference to the measurements section.
   - **Risks / unknowns** (if any): items worth flagging for Phase B planning even on PROCEED decision.

7. **Verify spike-isolation invariants before treating Phase A as complete**:
   - `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` MUST pass GREEN on main (spike work has not affected production crates).
   - `git ls-files | grep -i "triage-experimental"` MUST return empty on main (per security extract acceptance criterion #1 + arch extract acceptance criterion #1).
   - `git diff main..HEAD -- Cargo.lock` MUST show no additions on main (per security extract acceptance criterion #2).
   - `git diff main -- .andromeda/architecture.md` MUST return empty (per arch extract acceptance criterion #2).

- `.andromeda/decisions/` (NEW directory created implicitly) — first decision-record location under `.andromeda/`. Sibling to existing `.andromeda/context/`, `.andromeda/phases/`, `.andromeda/runs/`, `.andromeda/scope-validation/` directories per research.md `.andromeda/` artifact pattern.
- `.andromeda/decisions/pre-d2-drain-spike.md` (NEW file) — Phase A findings document. Format per Implementation Step 6 above.

- `.gitignore` — APPEND `crates/triage-experimental/` IF Path B chosen. ONE-LINE edit; lands BEFORE any spike file is created (per security extract Constraint #6). If Path A (throwaway branch) chosen, this modification is NOT required.

- `Cargo.toml` (workspace root) — MUST NOT add `triage-experimental` to `[workspace] members` (per arch extract Constraint #1 + Anti-pattern #1). MUST NOT add `criterion` or any other dep to `[workspace.dependencies]` (per security extract Constraint #4).

- `crates/triage/` and ALL other production crates (`ingest` / `buffer` / `viz` / `ui-bridge` / `snapshot` / `curation` / `corpus` / `security` / `workspace-detector` / `plugins` / `mcp-server` / `pulse-app` / `xtask`) — production code surface is owned by `/andromeda-implement` chunks, not research spikes (per arch extract Constraint #6).
