data.head: # Codebase Research — phase-65: chunk route#69 (Phase A spike)

body: _Generated by /andromeda-phase Phase 3 from targeted reads informed by combined.md._

- **Research depth:** minimal-to-moderate. Phase A is a throwaway spike that does not modify production code; research focuses on (a) workspace placement guardrails (Cargo.toml `members`, .gitignore patterns), (b) directory precedents for the new `.andromeda/decisions/` location, (c) confirming downstream Phase B integration points exist (logs table schema, triage crate structure) without modifying them, (d) operational hygiene preventing the standard-gate side effects documented in session-learnings (bindings.ts regen cascade).
- **Reads performed:** 8 full files + 1 partial range
- **Globs / Greps:** 6 (workspace structure + decisions dir presence + drain references)
- **Parallel batches:** 2

- `Cargo.toml` (full) — workspace `members` array lists 14 production members: 12 library crates (ingest / buffer / viz / ui-bridge / snapshot / curation / triage / corpus / security / workspace-detector / plugins / mcp-server) + `pulse-app` binary + `xtask`. No `triage-experimental` entry; the workspace dep table also does not declare `criterion` (the obs-plan canonical regression tool is referenced but not yet wired). Phase A workspace placement decision: spike crate (if chosen) MUST stay outside this members list.

- `.gitignore` (full) — 89 lines covering `.andromeda/runs/`, `target/`, `node_modules/`, `~/.andromeda-pulse/`, plus signing-key + secret patterns. Notably absent: `crates/triage-experimental/`. Phase A MUST add this entry BEFORE creating any spike file to enforce the chunk's gitignored-discipline (per security extract + arch extract).

- `.andromeda/` directory listing (via `ls -la`) — sibling artifact directories: `context/`, `phases/`, `runs/`, `scope-validation/`. NO `decisions/` directory present yet — Phase A creates this as a NEW peer directory. Pattern matches the existing `.andromeda/`-rooted artifact convention (mirrors arch extract Constraint #4).

- `crates/triage/src/lib.rs` (full, 17 lines) — confirms current production triage crate exposes `pub mod contract` + `pub(crate) mod { baseline, cue, digest, incident, interpretation, lifecycle, pattern }`. NO `drain` module yet — this confirms the chunk #69 Phase B integration point (`crates/triage/src/drain/`) does not exist on main, validating Phase A's "no production code commits" boundary. Phase A spike code, if placed in `crates/triage-experimental/`, lives entirely outside this production crate.

- `crates/buffer/src/schema.rs` (lines 1-60) — `RESERVED_TABLES` constant lists 7 tables: `spans`, `span_events` (with fingerprint BLOB column from chunk #65), `span_links`, `metrics_points`, `log_records`, `resources`, `instrumentation_scopes`. Chunk text references "logs table schema" but the actual reserved table name is `log_records`. Phase B work would ADD `log_templates` table + `log_records.template_id` column — outside Phase A scope. Note: chunk #69 route text and pulse-v0_2_0-route §67 both say "logs table"; orchestrator records the table-name reconciliation: production calls it `log_records`, Phase B amendment will need to use the production name. Out of Phase A scope.

- `xtask/Cargo.toml` (full) — current xtask deps: anyhow, chrono, clap, tokio (macros/process/rt-multi-thread), serde_json, ui-bridge, ingest, prost, reqwest, tempfile. NO `criterion` dependency. NO `[[bench]]` targets. NO `xtask/benches/` directory exists (verified via Glob). obs-plan §10 SLO Invariants references "criterion 0.5 in `xtask benches/`" as project-canonical, but this is a NOT-YET-WIRED reference. Phase A spike's criterion usage MUST live in the spike's local Cargo.toml (gitignored crate context) rather than wiring into the production xtask crate.

- `crates/ingest/proptest-regressions/.gitkeep` — confirms proptest-regressions pattern is in use; `proptest` is a workspace dev-dep already. If Phase A spike uses proptest for seeded LogHub corpus subsampling, it can reference the workspace dep.

- `crates/buffer/src/consumer.rs`, `crates/triage/src/cue/emitter.rs`, etc. (grep `drain|Drain|template_id|log_template` returned 11 files) — Hits are incidental substring matches (`drain()` collection method, `ServiceWentSilent`, etc.), NOT references to the Drain log-template-mining algorithm. Confirms zero existing implementation footprint. Greenfield for Phase B; pure research input for Phase A.

- `.claude/rules/testing.md` Session Additions (loaded via path-scoped rules system-reminder during Phase 3 research) — relevant entries: 2026-05-13 (`pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` regenerates transiently on every default-features workspace nextest; `git checkout HEAD -- ...` restores canonical state) + 2026-05-17 (recovery procedure relies on HEAD itself being in full-set state; pre-commit grep verification `grep -c '"mcp":' pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts ≥1` required). These ground the spike-isolation discipline pattern (Phase A spike crate MUST be excluded from `cargo nextest run --workspace` to avoid triggering the bindings.ts regen cascade).

- `.claude/rules/observability.md` Session Additions (loaded via path-scoped rules system-reminder during Phase 3 research) — relevant entries: 2026-05-03 (`tracing-subscriber 0.3 `Layer<S>` is read-only callback; redaction lives in `FormatEvent`; `pulse-app/src/observability.rs::JsonWithDefaults`) + 2026-05-17 session 84 (chunks #62/#63/#64 established AGGREGATE-ONLY tracing target convention without per-service identifiers in triage/cue/baseline targets). These confirm that Phase A spike, if it emits any `tracing::info!` calls, MUST follow the default-deny redaction pattern; but Phase A is gitignored so the production `pulse-app/src/observability.rs::AllowList` is not invoked by spike code anyway.

- **`.andromeda/`-rooted artifact directory pattern** (`.andromeda/runs/` + `.andromeda/phases/` + `.andromeda/context/` + `.andromeda/scope-validation/`): consistent layout for skill-output artifacts. `.andromeda/decisions/` fits this pattern naturally — Phase A's findings doc location is consistent with existing conventions (per arch extract pattern #2 + security extract pattern #2).

- **Workspace deps with one-line provenance comments** (`Cargo.toml` lines 52-172): every workspace dep is paired with a multi-line comment citing the chunk where it was introduced + rationale + arch/specialist plan section. Phase A spike MUST NOT pollute this pattern by adding entries since the spike is gitignored; spike-local `Cargo.toml` (inside `crates/triage-experimental/`) keeps its own dep declarations.

- **Spike-isolation discipline** (per session-learnings 2026-05-13 + 2026-05-17 bindings.ts regen cascade): ANY workspace nextest run that includes `pulse-app::tests::emit_taurpc_bindings` regenerates `pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts`. Cgf-gated `.merge(McpApiImpl)` is only active under `--features mcp-server`. To avoid triggering this cascade from spike code, Phase A spike crate MUST be excluded from `cargo nextest run --workspace` via .gitignored-path + workspace-members-exclusion (both already required by the chunk; this is a derivative effect, not a new requirement).

- **`.gitkeep` for empty-but-tracked directories** (`crates/ingest/proptest-regressions/.gitkeep`): convention for placeholder directories. If Phase A creates `.andromeda/decisions/` ahead of writing the findings doc, no .gitkeep is needed because the findings doc IS the directory's first content.

- **Composite primary key for span-events table schema** (`crates/buffer/src/schema.rs` lines 38-51): `span_events` table uses `PRIMARY KEY (trace_id, span_id, event_index)` with fingerprint BLOB column. Phase B will follow analogous shape for `log_templates` table — orchestrator notes the schema-design pattern for Phase B forward reference (not Phase A scope).

- **Module-level doc comment style** (per session-learnings 2026-05-14 entry): module-level `//! ...` doc blocks MUST NOT use the "Word: list1, list2, list3" colon-introduced multi-line list pattern (triggers `clippy::doc_lazy_continuation` lint under `-D warnings`). Use parenthetical-aside form or continuous prose. Phase A spike code, if it has any module docs, follows this discipline.

- **Throwaway-branch placement OR gitignored crate** (per CLAUDE.md + chunk text): both options valid. The throwaway-branch path has zero workspace footprint AND zero risk of accidentally committing to main; the gitignored-crate path has the advantage of being inspect-able locally without branch-switching. Plan documents both options + the user's chosen path at /implement time.

- **Findings-doc as audit-trail artifact** (per security extract pattern #2): once written, do not retroactively edit `.andromeda/decisions/pre-d2-drain-spike.md` — corrections go in a follow-up entry to preserve the decision lineage.

- **Decision-token structure** (per chunk text + tests/obs extracts): findings doc embeds the PROCEED / REVISE / SPLIT / DEFER decision as a machine-grep-able token (e.g., YAML front-matter field `decision: PROCEED` or fenced JSON code block `{"decision": "PROCEED", ...}`).

- **Measurement-discipline citation** (per obs extract acceptance criterion #1): each measurement cell in the findings doc cites its capture method (criterion bench / `std::time::Instant` harness / `std::mem::size_of_val` snapshot) so downstream Phase B planning can re-run the same measurements for cross-validation.

- **Unit convention for latency**: microseconds (μs) NOT milliseconds (per obs extract Constraint #3) — the Phase B production metric name is `metric.pipeline.l1c.drain_assignment_latency_p99_microseconds`, so Phase A's measurements must use the same unit for cross-reference.
- `.andromeda/decisions/` (NEW directory) — first decision-record location under `.andromeda/`. Created implicitly by writing the findings doc.

- `.andromeda/decisions/pre-d2-drain-spike.md` (NEW file) — Phase A findings document with structured measurement table + PROCEED / REVISE / SPLIT / DEFER decision token + Phase B forward-reference metric names. Format per combined.md obs extract patterns: YAML front-matter or fenced JSON for the decision; markdown body with structured JSON measurement blocks.

- **Path Option A — Throwaway branch (PREFERRED per security extract Constraint #1)**: zero new files on main. Spike code lives in a throwaway branch (e.g., `spike/drain-prototype`); branch never merged. Only the findings doc on main carries the spike's output.

- **Path Option B — `crates/triage-experimental/` (gitignored alternative)**: if chosen, creates:
  - `crates/triage-experimental/Cargo.toml` (LOCAL ONLY; gitignored) — spike-crate manifest with its own dep declarations (NOT touching workspace deps).
  - `crates/triage-experimental/src/lib.rs` and/or `crates/triage-experimental/src/main.rs` (LOCAL ONLY; gitignored) — Drain prototype implementation.
  - `crates/triage-experimental/benches/drain_bench.rs` (LOCAL ONLY; gitignored) — criterion bench harness for per-event latency p99.

- `.gitignore` — APPEND `crates/triage-experimental/` IF Path Option B is chosen. The append must land BEFORE any spike file is written (per security extract Constraint #6). One line, single edit. If Path Option A (throwaway branch) is chosen, no .gitignore modification is needed on main.

- **Q1: Path Option A vs B chosen at /implement time?** Both are valid per chunk text. Security extract prefers Option A (throwaway branch — zero CI footprint). Path Option B gives easier local inspection. /implement Phase 1 chooses; document the choice in `.andromeda/decisions/pre-d2-drain-spike.md` "Setup" section so future Phase B planning knows where the spike code lived.

- **Q2: LogHub corpus subset — which exact subsets?** Chunk text says "Apache web logs + Linux syslog + HDFS application logs recommended." LogHub's GitHub repo at https://github.com/logpai/loghub publishes 16 corpora; the recommendation is a subset. /implement Phase 1 picks the subset (e.g., Apache_2k.log, Linux_2k.log, HDFS_2k.log — the 2k-sample fixture variants are well-documented research baselines).

- **Q3: Should Phase A pre-allocate LogHub corpus fetch into a Makefile-style script?** Optional. /implement Phase 1 decides based on time budget — a `scripts/fetch-loghub-corpus.sh` (local-only / gitignored OR documented in findings doc as a curl recipe) is the lightweight option; in-spike-crate `build.rs` hitting curl is the deeper option. Either is consistent with the chunk's gitignored discipline.

- **Q4: Findings-doc table-name reconciliation for Phase B forward reference?** Chunk text says "logs table"; production schema name is `log_records`. The findings doc Phase B forward-reference section should cite the production-canonical name (`log_records.template_id` column; new `log_templates` table) so future Phase B planning has the precise schema target.
1. ✓ Read at least one file mentioned in combined.md "Files к modify" — read `Cargo.toml` (referenced as the do-not-modify list source), `.gitignore` (the one file Phase A may modify).
2. ✓ Patterns cited to specific file:line locations — `Cargo.toml:1-18` workspace members, `crates/buffer/src/schema.rs:7-15` RESERVED_TABLES, etc.

3. ✓ New-files-to-create paths consistent with arch §Workspace + existing `.andromeda/` directory pattern — `.andromeda/decisions/pre-d2-drain-spike.md` mirrors `.andromeda/runs/{datetime}-X/` + `.andromeda/phases/phase-N/` precedent.

- Phase B scope: production Drain3 Rust port with bincode-serde persistence to corpus SQLite (chunk #68 substrate) + LRU eviction at `max_clusters=1000` + regex-config-driven masking via `[triage.drain.masking_patterns]`; hot-path integration at `crates/buffer/appender.rs` (<50μs p99 budget); `log_templates` schema + `log_records.template_id` column; TauRPC `diagnostics.template_distribution()` with 4+1-place binding; Settings → Diagnostics "Template Distribution" panel + restart-required notice per P-055; golden-file LogHub tests + parameter sensitivity tests; template content passes PII scrubber per P-047 BEFORE persistence

data.head: ### Chunk route#69: Drain Rust implementation + template profiling diagnostics (Phase B)

body: **Constraints across domains:**

- (security) Template content MUST pass through `security::scrub_attribute()` (chunk #68 primitive) BEFORE any persistence to `log_templates` table or `log_records.template_id` column — templates can crystallize incidentally captured secrets from OTLP `LogRecord.body` (per security plan §Logging & Monitoring "What NEVER to log" + §Threat Model Summary data classification "Sensitivity note").

- (security) All DuckDB operations on `log_templates` table MUST use `Connection::prepare` + `?` placeholder binding — NEVER `format!()` interpolation (per security plan §Input Validation "DuckDB query parameters" row + §Security Anti-Patterns Input second bullet: 2026 DuckDB CVE cluster).

- (security) `diagnostics.template_distribution()` TauRPC procedure requires the quadruple binding: (1) router registration, (2) `pulse-app/capabilities/` JSON, (3) `xtask EXPECTED_PROCEDURES`, (4) `emit_taurpc_bindings` test merge — without all four, `cargo xtask capability-drift` reports missing (per security plan §API Security "TauRPC capability authorization" + security.md session additions 2026-05-12).

- (security) New `regex` workspace dependency (required for regex-config-driven masker) MUST be vetted via `cargo audit` + `cargo deny check bans licenses sources` before merging (per security plan §Dependency Security CI integration + §Bootstrap phases `dep-security-ci-gate`).

- (security) Template content MUST NOT be logged at any level — only template ID (integer) + occurrence count; template body strings can contain crystallized PII (per security plan §Logging & Monitoring "What NEVER to log" first bullet).

- (security) Cross-crate errors (DrainError, corpus errors) crossing into TauRPC bridge MUST use free-function `map_err` pattern in `diagnostics_router.rs` rather than `impl From<DrainError> for AppError` — orphan rule E0117 applies (per security.md session addition 2026-05-18).
- (security) Phase B re-derives Drain from clean specifications; does NOT promote spike code per `pre-d2-drain-spike.md` §Cleanup discipline + security plan §Code Patterns hygiene.

- (design) `TemplateDistribution.tsx` data cells MUST use `--font-code` (JetBrains Mono 12px tabular-nums) for counts/metrics + `--font-body` (IBM Plex Sans 14px) for headers/labels (per design-system §Typography Data + Body rows).

- (design) All color values in `TemplateDistribution.tsx` MUST be `@theme` CSS custom properties (`--color-raised-1` card bg, `--color-text-*` hierarchy, `--color-accent` drift indicators); NO hardcoded hex (per design-system §Surface: desktop-webview Tokens).
- (design) Drift indicator column MUST NOT use color alone — paired text label or icon required (per design-system §Anti-Patterns Universal Bans "Every color communicates meaning").

- (design) Restart-required notice (P-055) uses Warning state tokens: `--color-base` bg + `--color-accent` border (1px, rgba 50% opacity) + `--color-text-primary` message text (per design-system §Color Palette Semantic Colors Warning row + Design Decisions Log 2026-05-03).

- (design) Diagnostics panel card uses `--color-raised-1` bg + 1px subtle border + `--radius-md` + `--spacing-md` padding (per design-system §Component Patterns Cards / Panels + §Depth Strategy borders-only).

- (layouts) The Diagnostics panel lands under the **Settings tab** (or Settings sub-page) — no new top-level tab without explicit layout-templates spec amendment (per layout-templates §Full Dashboard Shell — current tab nav: Traces / Metrics / Logs / Snapshots / Settings).

- (layouts) Template distribution table uses **compact row height + monospace** for Sample Message column + truncation with tooltip/modal expansion — chart-first density (per layout-templates §Design Philosophy + §Trace Timeline pattern).
- (layouts) Sample Message column is flex-grow; Template ID / Occurrence Count / Drift Indicator columns are fixed-width (per layout-templates §Trace Timeline column layout precedent).
- (layouts) Restart-required notice renders **inline adjacent to the affected field group** in Settings — NOT a toast or modal-over-modal (per layout-templates §Settings Modal Form).

- (tests) New `crates/buffer/drain.rs` module MUST have co-located `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` unit tests; Standard tier coverage ≥75% line / ≥70% branch / ≥85% function (per test-plan §10 Quality Gates).

- (tests) `log_templates` table + `log_records.template_id` column additions MUST be covered by a migration scenario test verifying existing rows tolerate NULL `template_id` (per Route §Risk Notes "Schema migration discipline" + test-plan §7).

- (tests) Golden-file tests MUST use committed LogHub fixture files (Apache_2k / Linux_2k / HDFS_2k) under `tests/fixtures/drain/` — deterministic, not synthetic without seed control (per test-plan §11 anti-pattern "NEVER use non-deterministic generators without seed control").

- (tests) `diagnostics.template_distribution()` requires full 4+1-place binding; `emit_taurpc_bindings` test MUST include `DiagnosticsApiImpl` in `.merge()` chain (per security.md session addition 2026-05-12).

- (tests) Every chunk plan MUST include unconditional standard gate baseline: `cargo fmt --check` + `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` + `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` + `cargo xtask capability-drift` + `npm run lint/typecheck/test --prefix pulse-app/ui` (per test-plan §12 Decisions Log 2026-05-10).
- (tests) `TemplateDistribution.tsx` MUST have co-located `*.test.tsx` vitest tests asserting DOM-shape contracts (per test-plan §4 + §2 Framework vitest 3.x with jsdom 26).

- (obs) Two metric target strings from Phase A findings doc MUST be used VERBATIM: `metric.pipeline.l1c.drain_template_count_total` (Counter) + `metric.pipeline.l1c.drain_assignment_latency_p99_microseconds` (Distribution) (per obs-plan §5 Metric Coverage naming `metric.{module}.{measure}` + Phase A findings doc §Phase B forward reference).

- (obs) `drain_assignment_latency_p99_microseconds` MUST be emitted as individual per-event `tracing` events (NOT pre-aggregated) — agent computes p99 offline via `jq` (per obs-plan §5 "NEVER skip p50/p95/p99 coverage on perf-budget metrics — emit raw per-event value field").

- (obs) Per-event latency metric MUST be level-gated at `trace` level (not `info`) to avoid hot-path log spam at throughput (per obs-plan §11 "NEVER log in hot path at info level" + §6 trace level mapping).

- (obs) Template content (even PII-scrubbed) MUST NOT appear as structured log fields; default-deny allowlist for `buffer` module covers metrics only, not content (per obs-plan §8 PII Scrubbing default-deny + §11 anti-pattern).

- (obs) `diagnostics.template_distribution` TauRPC MUST have `#[tracing::instrument(skip_all, fields(top_n = %top_n))]` wrapper; span name `diagnostics.template_distribution.request` per `{module}.{operation}` convention (per obs-plan §4 IPC-internal instrumentation + §2 Naming).
- (a11y) `TemplateDistribution.tsx` falls under WCAG 2.1 AA Standard tier; text must meet SC 1.4.3 4.5:1 contrast minimum (per a11y-plan §1 A11y Scope Summary).

- (a11y) Template distribution rows MUST use semantic `<table>` with `<th scope="col">` column headers — not `<div>` grids (per a11y-plan §7 + SC 1.3.1 Info and Relationships).
- (a11y) Interactive controls (sort, filter, pagination) MUST be keyboard-operable (Tab/Enter/Space, Arrow navigation for listboxes) (per a11y-plan §5 Keyboard Navigation; SC 2.1.1).
- (a11y) `TemplateDistribution.tsx` MUST NOT use `role="button"` on `<div>` — semantic `<button>` required (per a11y-plan §11 Anti-Patterns ARIA; eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y enforced).

- (arch) Module dependency direction: `crates/buffer/drain.rs` lives in `buffer` crate; MUST NOT add `buffer → corpus`, `buffer → ui-bridge`, or `buffer → triage` dep edges. Persistence injected via trait (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns "Module dependency direction" + CLAUDE.md §Session Additions 2026-05-16 trait-in-lower-crate pattern).
- (arch) DuckDB query discipline: prepared statements with `?` placeholders ONLY for `log_templates` operations (per arch §Critical Warnings + §Established Decisions [Database]).

- (arch) `diagnostics.template_distribution()` 4+1-place binding INCLUDES the arch §Occupied Resources update via `/andromeda-evolve --allow-arch-registry` (per CLAUDE.md §Session Additions 2026-05-12).
- (arch) Tauri capability negative-default: missing `pulse-app/capabilities/` JSON entry = silent runtime rejection (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns "Webview IPC capability policy").
- (arch) Drain params (`depth=4`, `similarity=0.5`, `max_clusters=1000`) honor env vars > `config.toml` > built-in defaults precedence (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns "Config management").

- (arch) Reserved table name is `log_records` (not "logs"); new sibling table `log_templates` + new column `log_records.template_id` added via `/andromeda-evolve --allow-arch-registry` (per arch §Occupied Resources "DuckDB database / schema names").
- (arch) Cross-crate errors crossing TauRPC bridge use free-function `map_err` in `diagnostics_router.rs` — orphan rule E0117 (per CLAUDE.md §Session Additions 2026-05-18).
**Patterns to follow:**

- (security) PII scrubber integration at persistence boundary: call `security::scrub_attribute()` on template body BEFORE write — matches chunk #68 corpus "scrub at ingestion AND at persistence" defense-in-depth (per security plan §Logging & Monitoring).

- (security) Dependency addition: record `regex` in workspace `Cargo.toml` with explicit version pin; extend `deny.toml [bans] skip` with provenance comment if transitive duplicates arise (per security.md session addition 2026-05-03).

- (security) Hot-path tracing: emit `tracing::info!(target: "metric.pipeline.l1c.drain_assignment_latency_p99_microseconds", value = N)` per event with template_id integer attribute only (per security plan §Logging & Monitoring NEVER-log list).

- (design) Data table pattern: telemetry table rows with transparent bg, hover `rgba(74, 144, 226, 0.1)`, header bg `#1A1D24` weight-600 12px, data cells JetBrains Mono 12px tabular-nums, 1px subtle borders, `--spacing-sm` (8px) cell padding (per design-system §Component Patterns Tables).

- (design) Restart-required notice follows Input Field / Form Controls error-state convention (Burgundy 50% border + `--color-accent` text via `--color-text-primary` body), NOT a custom alert component (per design-system §Component Patterns Input Fields / Form Controls Error state).

- (design) Card/panel container: Raised-1 spec (`#262A33` bg, subtle border, `radius-md`, `space-md` padding) matching Settings modal panel surfaces (per design-system §Component Patterns Cards / Panels).

- (layouts) Settings sub-panel pattern: Drain config fields (depth/similarity/max_clusters) as labeled input + inline constraint hint + restart-required badge (per layout-templates §Settings Modal Form).

- (layouts) Sortable data table inside dashboard: reuse trace-timeline column pattern (Trace ID / Service / Latency / Error → Template ID / Count / Drift / Sample) (per layout-templates §Trace Timeline + per-service constellation).
- (layouts) Modal primitive for expanded sample: overlay card + focus trap + aria-busy/aria-live, NOT inline expansion (per layout-templates §Modal Primitive Scaffold).

- (tests) Golden-file tests using committed LogHub fixtures: commit fixture files under `tests/fixtures/drain/` matching `tests/fixtures/plugins/` pre-compiled-WASM precedent; compare `DrainMiner::assign()` output against committed expected template strings (per test-plan §7 + §11 anti-patterns).

- (tests) `rstest` fixtures for builder factories: define `MockLogRecord::builder()` in `crates/buffer/` following `MockTraceSpan::builder()` / `MockArrowBatch::builder()` pattern (per test-plan §4 + §7).

- (tests) Per-event latency tests use deterministic measurement (`tokio::time::pause()` advance OR `std::time::Instant` with seeded corpus) — NEVER CI wall-clock jitter (per test-plan §8 + §11 universal anti-pattern).

- (tests) TauRPC IPC test pattern: `DiagnosticsApiImpl` constructed with in-memory `DrainMiner`, invoke via `tauri::test::mock_builder()` + `get_ipc_response()`, assert JSON response shape (per test-plan §5 Integration Test Strategy).
- (tests) Parameter sensitivity tests as `#[rstest(depth => [3, 4, 5], similarity => [0.4, 0.5, 0.6])]` matrix — readable + individually retryable (per test-plan §4 rstest parameterized).

- (obs) Heartbeat tick coverage: EXTEND `buffer.tick` (or add sibling `drain.tick`) to emit `drain_template_count` (gauge) + `drain_lru_eviction_count` (counter since tick) (per obs-plan §3 Heartbeat ticks + §5 Metric Coverage).

- (obs) Counter metric via `tracing::info!(target: "metric.pipeline.l1c.drain_template_count_total", value = N)` emitted per heartbeat tick (15s interval), NOT per assignment (per obs-plan §5 Counter row + Phase A findings doc forward reference).

- (obs) Distribution metric via per-event `tracing::trace!` (not `info`) for `drain_assignment_latency_p99_microseconds` — agent toggles `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_LOG_LEVEL=trace` to collect sample (per obs-plan §5 + §6 trace level).

- (obs) `duckdb.append` span boundary: instrument Drain assignment as CHILD span `drain.assign` within the `duckdb.append` span (not sibling) to preserve trace context continuity (per obs-plan §4 P1 must-trace + §3 trace context propagation).

- (obs) `buffer` module log allowlist extension: add `drain_template_id`, `drain_occurrence_count`, `drain_lru_evictions_since_tick`; NEVER add template tokens / sample messages (per obs-plan §8 default-deny `buffer:` row).
- (a11y) Restart-required notice as `aria-live="polite"` status region following snapshot-progress P2/P6 pattern; NOT `role="alert"` (per a11y-plan §7 live regions table).
- (a11y) Data table with `<table>` semantic structure + `<th scope="col">` column headers following critical path P1 trace list pattern (per a11y-plan §4 ARIA Patterns).

- (a11y) Not-color-alone state signaling: drift indicators use `--color-accent` + icon + text label; `--color-feedback-success` for healthy templates also pairs with icon/text (per a11y-plan §6 State color tokens; SC 1.4.1).
- (a11y) eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y compile-time gate: already installed (Foundation epoch); new `.tsx` automatically covered (per a11y-plan §3 Bootstrap phases).

- (a11y) Focus management: if implemented as tabpanel/accordion disclosure within Settings, use `<button>` with `aria-expanded` + `aria-controls` (per a11y-plan §4 ARIA Patterns Accordion); NO focus trap required (not a modal).

- (arch) Trait-in-lower-crate + impl-in-pulse-app for cross-crate persistence: define `DrainPersistence` trait in `crates/buffer/`; implement corpus-backed adapter in `pulse-app/src/drain_persistence.rs`; inject `Arc<dyn DrainPersistence>` into Drain constructor (per CLAUDE.md §Session Additions 2026-05-16).

- (arch) Free-function map_err for cross-crate errors: `pub fn drain_error_to_app_error(err: DrainError) -> AppError` in `pulse-app/src/diagnostics_router.rs`; callers use `.map_err(drain_error_to_app_error)?` (per CLAUDE.md §Session Additions 2026-05-18).

- (arch) D3 capability-drift coupling: `diagnostics.*` EXPECTED_PROCEDURES extension + `emit_taurpc_bindings` test update MUST land in same commit as router registration + capability JSON (per CLAUDE.md §Session Additions 2026-05-10).

- (arch) Schema evolution via `PRAGMA user_version`: bump schema version, ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS, CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS (per arch §Established Decisions [Database] — pattern from chunk #68 corpus).

- (arch) Two-phase chunk wrap-state discipline: Phase B completes chunk #69; `state.yaml.last_completed_chunk` advances to 69 only when Phase B done; intermediate wrap commits use `chore(wrap):` prefix to avoid D6 false fire (per CLAUDE.md §Session Additions + session-handoff.md).
**Anti-patterns to avoid:**

- (security) NEVER log template body string in `tracing` events or `AppError::Internal` surfaced to webview — log template cluster ID (integer) only (per security plan §Security Anti-Patterns Logging + §Logging & Monitoring NEVER-log).

- (security) NEVER use string interpolation for `log_templates` SQL: `format!("INSERT INTO log_templates VALUES ('{}')", template_str)` is the exact 2026 DuckDB CVE cluster anti-pattern (per security plan §Security Anti-Patterns Input).

- (security) NEVER promote spike crate code from `crates/triage-experimental/` into production workspace; Phase B re-derives from specifications (per `pre-d2-drain-spike.md` §Cleanup Discipline + security plan §Code Patterns hygiene).
- (design) NEVER hardcode hex colors in `TemplateDistribution.tsx`; all values trace to `@theme` CSS custom properties (per design-system §Self-Validation Protocol §4 Token Test).
- (design) NEVER use gradient overlays or glassmorphic effects on diagnostics panel chrome; flat matte surfaces are the discipline (per design-system §Anti-Patterns Universal Bans).
- (design) NEVER encode drift/anomaly state with color alone; paired text label or icon mandatory (per design-system §Anti-Patterns Universal Bans + Downstream Readiness for a11y SC 1.4.1).
- (layouts) NEVER introduce new top-level Diagnostics tab without explicit layout-templates spec amendment (per layout-templates §Full Dashboard Shell).
- (layouts) NEVER use spacious consumer-app table layout (wide padding, large row heights, card-per-row); chart-first density required (per layout-templates §Design Philosophy).
- (layouts) NEVER use a toast for restart-required notice; inline adjacent to field group only (per layout-templates §Settings Modal Form + OS notification policy cross-constraint).
- (layouts) NEVER inline full sample message in table cell without truncation; truncate + tooltip / modal expansion only (preserves row density).

- (tests) NEVER use pre-baked DuckDB snapshots or committed `.db` files for schema migration tests; use ephemeral in-memory DuckDB with migration applied at runtime + Arrow appender seed (per test-plan §11 Anti-Patterns).
- (tests) NEVER promote spike code from `crates/triage-experimental/` as golden-file reference implementation; Phase B re-derives (per `pre-d2-drain-spike.md` §Cleanup Discipline).

- (tests) NEVER assert on raw template-tree internals (node counts, depth indices); assert on public contract (template string content, occurrence count, sample messages) (per test-plan §11 Anti-Patterns "NEVER test implementation details").

- (obs) NEVER instrument Drain assignment inner loop at `info` level or create per-event spans; allocation overhead consumes 48μs latency headroom; use `tracing::trace!` for metric event + single `drain.assign` child span per batch (per obs-plan §11 "NEVER over-instrument hot paths").
- (obs) NEVER log template content (even PII-scrubbed) as structured log field; obs allowlist for `buffer` covers metrics not content (per obs-plan §8 default-deny posture + §11 anti-pattern).
- (obs) NEVER pre-aggregate `drain_assignment_latency_p99_microseconds` before emission; raw per-event `value` fields required for `jq`-over-jsonl agent-side aggregation (per obs-plan §5).
- (a11y) NEVER emit restart-required notice as `role="alert"` / `aria-live="assertive"`; config-changed is non-blocking, not urgent interruption (per a11y-plan §7 live regions table).
- (a11y) NEVER render template distribution rows as unstructured `<div>` grids; use semantic `<table>` with `<th scope="col">` (per a11y-plan §11 Anti-Patterns Screen Reader; SC 1.3.1).

- (a11y) NEVER suppress focus styles on template rows or Diagnostics interactive elements (`outline: none` without `--border-focus` replacement is SC 2.4.7 violation) (per a11y-plan §11 Anti-Patterns Keyboard).
- (arch) NEVER add reverse dep edges (`buffer → corpus`, `buffer → ui-bridge`, `buffer → triage`); persistence injected via trait (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns).
- (arch) NEVER use `format!()` SQL construction for `log_templates` / `log_records` queries (per arch §Critical Warnings).
- (arch) NEVER merge `diagnostics.template_distribution()` without all 5 binding points AND arch §Occupied Resources update (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns "Webview IPC capability policy").
- (arch) NEVER use `impl From<DrainError> for AppError` in `buffer` or `ui-bridge` (orphan rule); use free-function in router file (per CLAUDE.md §Session Additions 2026-05-18).
- (arch) NEVER link `opentelemetry` / OTLP SDK or network exporter pointed at `:4317`/`:4318` for Drain metrics; use `tracing` events only (per arch §Critical Warnings Self-observation).
- (arch) NEVER use `logs` as table name; reserved name is `log_records`; new table is `log_templates` (not `drain_templates` / `templates`) (per arch §Occupied Resources).
**Contract bindings (per chunk):**

Both domains agree on "what is safe to emit" boundary at `appender.rs` integration site. (reciprocal)

data.head: # Phase 66 Plan — chunk route#69 (Phase B): Drain Rust production implementation + template profiling diagnostics

body: _Generated by /andromeda-phase Phase 4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not edit during /implement run._
- **Phase number:** 66

- **Route chunks covered:**
  - route#69 "Drain Rust implementation + template profiling diagnostics — Drain3 Rust port (depth/similarity/masking); two-phase spike-then-production; diagnostics.template_distribution() panel (capability P-007; detail in pulse-v0_2_0-route §67)" — **Phase B production scope only**
- **Epoch:** Epoch 9 — Foundation v0.2.0 (final chunk in route §2; v0.2.0 Foundation epoch completes with this chunk)

- **Phase A gate:** PROCEED decision committed at `.andromeda/decisions/pre-d2-drain-spike.md` (session 97; 167 LOC algorithm core; 2μs p99 latency = 25× under <50μs target; ~9.7KB memory for 18 templates / 6000 lines; 60% template match rate with clear Apache improvement path via regex-config-driven masker; revised LOC estimate Phase A+B: 900-1100 total).

Implement the production Drain3 Rust port behind the L1c log-template-mining layer (capability P-007), threading template assignment into the OTLP log-record ingestion hot path at `crates/buffer/src/appender.rs` between OTLP decode and DuckDB append with a per-event latency budget of <50μs p99 (Phase A spike measured 2μs in isolation — 25× headroom). The implementation extends the existing `crates/buffer/` crate with a new `drain` module (DrainMiner + DrainTree + DrainConfig + regex-config-driven masker + LRU eviction at `max_clusters=1000`), wires a new `log_templates` table + `log_records.template_id` nullable column into the in-memory DuckDB ring buffer schema (extending RESERVED_TABLES from 7 to 8), persists the template tree to the corpus SQLite substrate (chunk #68) via a NEW `DrainPersistence` trait pattern (trait-in-lower-crate per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-16; `CorpusWriter` trait added to corpus crate to complement the read-only `CorpusReader`), exposes a `diagnostics.template_distribution()` TauRPC procedure following the storage_router.rs precedent (free-function `drain_error_to_app_error` at binary boundary per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-18 orphan-rule pattern), and surfaces a Settings → Diagnostics "Template Distribution" panel (`TemplateDistribution.tsx`) rendering the top-50 templates as a semantic `<table>` with `aria-live="polite"` restart-required notice per P-055. Template content passes through the chunk #68 PII scrubber (`security::scrubber::scrub_attribute`) BEFORE persistence to `log_templates.template_content` per capability P-047 + obs allowlist default-deny posture. Two pre-committed metric signals — `metric.pipeline.l1c.drain_template_count_total` (Counter via heartbeat tick) + `metric.pipeline.l1c.drain_assignment_latency_p99_microseconds` (Distribution via `trace`-level per-event emission) — provide the SLO surface for the <50μs p99 budget enforcement. Phase B is the FINAL chunk in route §2; v0.2.0 Foundation epoch completes with this chunk. Estimated 4-6 sessions of multi-session implementation per route §Risk notes "Largest single chunk in route" with a recommended session split documented in Implementation notes; the plan accommodates either single-session OR multi-session execution at /implement Phase 1 discretion.

1. **Commit to the Phase B persistence design (Open Question Q1 + Q2 resolution)** before writing code. The plan commits to: (a) reuse corpus `pipeline_metrics` table with `metric_name = "drain_template_tree"`, `layer = "l1c"`, `payload = bincode-serialized DrainState` (no corpus schema version bump); (b) introduce NEW `CorpusWriter` trait in `crates/corpus/src/contract.rs` (read-only `CorpusReader` stays unchanged per capability P-051); (c) `DrainPersistence` trait in `crates/buffer/` is the buffer-side abstraction; `Arc<dyn DrainPersistence>` injected into `DrainMiner::new()`; the pulse-app-side adapter (`pulse-app/src/drain_persistence.rs`) wraps `Arc<dyn CorpusWriter>` from the corpus crate. Document the decision in plan/header so /implement Phase 1 doesn't re-explore the design space.

2. **Add new workspace dependencies to root `Cargo.toml`.** Add `lru = "0.12"` to `[workspace.dependencies]` (only NEW workspace dep this chunk — `regex` and `bincode` already present at lines 171 + 136 per Phase A research). Add provenance comment matching chunk #61/#68 precedent. Verify `cargo deny check bans licenses sources` passes with the new dep present.

3. **Create `crates/buffer/src/drain.rs`** (NEW file; ~500-700 LOC including unit tests per Phase A estimate). Contains the Drain3 algorithm core:
   - `pub struct DrainConfig { depth: u32, similarity: f32, max_clusters: usize, masking_patterns: Vec<(Regex, &'static str)> }` with `pub fn default_config() -> Self` providing safe defaults (depth=4, similarity=0.5, max_clusters=1000, masking_patterns = NUM/IP/HEX/PATH categories).
   - `pub struct DrainMiner { config: DrainConfig, persistence: Option<Arc<dyn DrainPersistence>>, tree: Arc<RwLock<DrainTree>>, lru: Arc<RwLock<LruCache<TemplateId, ()>>>, ... }` with `pub fn new(config: DrainConfig, persistence: Option<Arc<dyn DrainPersistence>>) -> Self`.
   - `pub trait DrainPersistence: Send + Sync { fn load(&self) -> Result<Option<DrainState>, buffer::Error>; fn save(&self, state: &DrainState) -> Result<(), buffer::Error>; }` (the trait defined here per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-16 trait-in-lower-crate pattern).
   - `pub type TemplateId = u64;` (sequential IDs starting at 1; 0 reserved for "no template assigned").
   - `pub fn assign(&self, log_body: &str) -> Option<TemplateId>` — core hot-path API; tokenizes, walks fixed-depth tree, computes similarity, returns matching template_id OR creates new cluster + returns new ID. On `max_clusters` overflow: LRU eviction.
   - `pub fn template_distribution(&self, top_n: usize) -> Vec<TemplateDistEntry>` — query API for diagnostics panel.
   - `pub fn tree_state(&self) -> DrainState` — snapshot for persistence.
   - `pub fn load_from_state(&mut self, state: DrainState)` — rehydrate from persistence at boot.
   - `pub struct DrainState { schema_version: u32, templates: Vec<TemplateRecord>, tree_root: SerializableNode }` with `#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]` for bincode round-trip.
   - `#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, Debug)] pub struct TemplateDistEntry { id: TemplateId, content: String, occurrence_count: u64, drift_indicator: DriftIndicator }`.
   - `pub enum DriftIndicator { Healthy, OverGeneralized, UnderClustered }` (per design extract drift indicator column constraint).
   - `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { ... }` — unit tests for tree walk, similarity match, masking, LRU eviction, persistence round-trip, parameter sensitivity (depth/similarity matrix per test extract `#[rstest]` pattern). Co-located per testing convention.
   - **Apply CLAUDE.md 2026-05-14 module-doc colon-list lint trap**: avoid `//!` doc-block colon-list shape that triggers `clippy::doc_lazy_continuation`.

4. **Extend `crates/buffer/src/contract.rs`** — add `Drain { reason: String }` variant to `Error` enum (per existing Init/SchemaCreate/Append precedent); add `drain_template_count: u64` + `drain_lru_evictions_since_tick: u64` fields to `BufferHeartbeat`; extend `heartbeat_payload(...)` signature to accept these from the caller (or to query a state ref).

5. **Extend `crates/buffer/src/schema.rs`** — chunk #69 schema additions:
   - `RESERVED_TABLES: [&str; 7]` → `[&str; 8]` add `"log_templates"`.
   - Add `CREATE_LOG_TEMPLATES` const: `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS log_templates (template_id BIGINT NOT NULL, template_content VARCHAR NOT NULL, occurrence_count BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, first_seen_unix_nano BIGINT NOT NULL, last_seen_unix_nano BIGINT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (template_id))`.
   - Rewrite `CREATE_LOG_RECORDS` const to include nullable `template_id BIGINT` column (Open Question Q4 option (a) — single-DDL approach; DuckDB is in-memory + ephemeral so no real migration concern).
   - Update `SCHEMA_DDL` concat to include `CREATE_LOG_TEMPLATES`.
   - Update `ddl_constants_match_concatenated_schema` spot-check test (add `CREATE_LOG_TEMPLATES` to union).
   - Rename `schema_creates_exactly_seven_reserved_tables` → `..._eight_reserved_tables` + accept 8-element BTreeSet.
   - Extend `each_reserved_table_has_ts_and_ts_unix_nano_columns` rstest cases. **Note**: `log_templates` does NOT have `ts` / `ts_unix_nano` columns; this test asserts presence so either (i) exclude `log_templates` from the rstest cases OR (ii) add a separate test asserting `log_templates` has `first_seen_unix_nano` + `last_seen_unix_nano` instead.

6. **Extend `crates/buffer/src/appender.rs::build_logs_record_batch`** — accept `Option<&DrainMiner>` parameter. When `Some(miner)`, call `miner.assign(&log_record.body)` per log record + accumulate `template_ids: Vec<Option<i64>>` Vec. Add `template_id` field (nullable BIGINT) to the log_records Arrow Schema. Build `Int64Array` (with nulls allowed) for the template_id column. When `None`, write all-NULL template_id column. Extend existing unit tests for both cases.

7. **Extend `crates/buffer/src/consumer.rs::run_consumer`** signature to accept `Option<Arc<DrainMiner>>` param (additive — preserves the existing chunk #62 baseline / chunk #66 fingerprint observer pattern). Extend `dispatch_batch`'s `Batch::Logs(l) =>` arm to thread the miner into `build_logs_record_batch(&l, miner.as_deref())`. **Critical: extend ALL existing `run_consumer(...)` test invocations** to pass `None` (Phase B doesn't require Drain in unit tests covering the baseline + fingerprint paths).

8. **Implement `crates/buffer/src/drain.rs::write_template_to_table`** — after DrainMiner assigns a NEW template (cluster created, not matched), append a row to `log_templates` DuckDB table via prepared statement (NO `format!()`): `conn.prepare("INSERT INTO log_templates (template_id, template_content, occurrence_count, first_seen_unix_nano, last_seen_unix_nano) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)")` + `stmt.execute([&id, &scrubbed_content, &1i64, &now, &now])`. The `scrubbed_content` = `security::scrubber::scrub_attribute(&template_text)` result — store `[REDACTED:{category}]` string when redacted, original text when not. **CRITICAL security constraint** per security extract: PII scrub fires BEFORE the DuckDB write.

9. **Extend `crates/corpus/src/contract.rs`** — add `pub trait CorpusWriter: Send + Sync` with `fn save_pipeline_metric(&self, metric_name: &str, layer: &str, payload: &[u8]) -> Result<(), Error>;` + `fn load_pipeline_metric(&self, metric_name: &str, layer: &str) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>, Error>;`. Implement on the `Corpus` struct (re-using existing `db::insert_pipeline_metric` + encryption pipeline from chunk #68). NOTE: `CorpusReader` stays unchanged (P-051 read-only-by-design is preserved); `CorpusWriter` is a separate trait for the persistence side.

10. **Create `pulse-app/src/drain_persistence.rs`** — `pub struct CorpusDrainPersistence { writer: Arc<dyn corpus::contract::CorpusWriter> }` + `impl buffer::drain::DrainPersistence for CorpusDrainPersistence { fn load(&self) -> ...; fn save(&self, state: &DrainState) -> ... { let bytes = bincode::serialize(state).map_err(...)?; self.writer.save_pipeline_metric("drain_template_tree", "l1c", &bytes).map_err(...) } }`. Adapter at pulse-app binary boundary preserves arch §Module dependency direction (buffer crate stays corpus-free).

11. **Create `pulse-app/src/diagnostics_router.rs`** — TauRPC resolver mirroring `storage_router.rs` shape (~150-200 lines):
   - `pub struct TemplateDistributionPayload { templates: Vec<TemplateDistEntry>, total_template_count: u64, last_updated_unix_nano: i64 }` with `#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq, specta::Type)]`.
   - `#[taurpc::procedures(path = "diagnostics")] pub trait DiagnosticsApi { async fn template_distribution() -> Result<TemplateDistributionPayload, AppError>; }`.
   - `#[derive(Clone)] pub struct DiagnosticsApiImpl { miner: Arc<DrainMiner> }` + `pub fn new(miner: Arc<DrainMiner>) -> Self`.
   - `#[taurpc::resolvers] impl DiagnosticsApi for DiagnosticsApiImpl { async fn template_distribution(self) -> Result<TemplateDistributionPayload, AppError> { ... } }` with `#[tracing::instrument(skip_all, fields(top_n = tracing::field::Empty, result_count = tracing::field::Empty, duration_ms = tracing::field::Empty))]` decorator.
   - Resolver body: invoke `self.miner.template_distribution(50)` → wrap in payload → `span.record(...)` for `top_n` + `result_count` + `duration_ms` → emit `tracing::info!(target: "diagnostics.template_distribution.request", top_n = 50, result_count = N, duration_ms = M, "diagnostics.template_distribution returned")`.
   - `pub fn drain_error_to_app_error(err: buffer::Error) -> AppError` free function at bottom (orphan-rule + arch DAG preservation; sanitized message strings per `storage_router.rs:154-169` precedent — short tokens, no paths, no SQL).
   - `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { ... }` — unit tests covering in-memory miner, sanitized error mapping (no SQL fragments / library versions / paths in AppError::Storage message).
12. **Update `pulse-app/src/lib.rs`** — add `pub mod diagnostics_router;` + `pub mod drain_persistence;`.

13. **Wire Drain at boot in `pulse-app/src/main.rs`** (around line ~370 alongside `corpus_reader` setup):
   - Build `DrainConfig` from `Settings` struct (`drain_depth`, `drain_similarity`, `drain_max_clusters` fields — added to Settings struct in step 14 below).
   - Build `Option<Arc<dyn DrainPersistence>>` from `corpus_writer.as_ref().map(|w| Arc::new(CorpusDrainPersistence { writer: Arc::clone(w) }))`.
   - Construct `let drain_miner = Arc::new(DrainMiner::new(drain_config, drain_persistence));`.
   - On boot, call `drain_miner.load_from_persistence()` if persistence is Some.
   - Pass `Some(Arc::clone(&drain_miner))` into the `run_consumer(...)` invocation (deeper in setup closure).
   - Construct `let diagnostics_impl = DiagnosticsApiImpl::new(Arc::clone(&drain_miner));`.
   - Add `.merge(diagnostics_impl.into_handler())` to the main Router build at line ~1041.

14. **Extend `crates/ui-bridge/src/contract.rs::Settings`** — add `drain_depth: u32` (default 4) + `drain_similarity: f32` (default 0.5) + `drain_max_clusters: usize` (default 1000) fields. Per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-09 lesson: extending Settings struct is the LOWER-COST path for new persistable config; no new TauRPC namespace needed (config flows through existing `get_settings` / `update_settings` envelope). body: _Generated by /andromeda-phase Phase 3 from targeted reads informed by combined.md._

- **Research depth:** moderate-to-deep — codebase is mature (chunks #1-#68 landed). Combined.md signals concrete files to read (appender.rs hot path; storage_router.rs as TauRPC precedent; schema.rs reserved tables; security/scrubber.rs PII primitive; corpus/db.rs persistence backend; observability.rs AllowList).
- **Reads performed:** 14 (full + partial); 8 globs/greps.
- **Parallel batches:** 4.

- `Cargo.toml` (full) — workspace deps already include `regex = "1"` (chunk #68 line 171); **no new workspace dep required for the regex-driven masker**. `bincode = "1.3"` already present (chunk #61 line 136) — usable for template-tree serialization. `rusqlite`, `aes-gcm`, `keyring` already wired through `corpus` crate; no direct buffer access needed for persistence (use `DrainPersistence` trait → `corpus`-backed impl in pulse-app per arch §Module dependency direction).

- `crates/buffer/Cargo.toml` (full) — `[dependencies]` lists `thiserror`, `tokio`, `tracing`, `tracing-error`, `duckdb`, `arrow`, `bytes`, `blake3`, `ingest` (sibling-DAG edge). Adding Drain inside `buffer` requires NO new dep — `regex` and `bincode` will be added via workspace inherit at implement time.

- `crates/buffer/src/lib.rs` (full) — module surface is `appender / broadcast / consumer / contract / fingerprint / retention / schema / state`. New `drain` module slots in as the 9th module (`pub mod drain;`). Public re-exports go through `pub use drain::{DrainMiner, DrainConfig, ...}` at the lib root.

- `crates/buffer/src/schema.rs` (full) — `RESERVED_TABLES: [&str; 7]` array + `SCHEMA_DDL` concat string with `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS log_records (...)` — `body VARCHAR NOT NULL DEFAULT ''` is the Drain input field. Edit shape: extend `RESERVED_TABLES` to length 8 with `"log_templates"` + add a new const `CREATE_LOG_TEMPLATES` block + concat into `SCHEMA_DDL` + add `ALTER TABLE log_records ADD COLUMN template_id BIGINT` (or rewrite `CREATE_LOG_RECORDS` to include `template_id BIGINT` nullable column). **Schema-spot-check test (`ddl_constants_match_concatenated_schema`) will need extension** to include `CREATE_LOG_TEMPLATES`. **Reserved-tables-count assertion (`schema_creates_exactly_seven_reserved_tables`) renames to `..._eight_reserved_tables` + accepts 8-element BTreeSet.**

- `crates/buffer/src/contract.rs` (full) — `pub enum Error` has 8 variants (Init/SchemaCreate/Append/ConnectionLost/InvalidBatch/Retention/BroadcastEncode/BroadcastSizeCapExceeded). Phase B adds `Drain { reason: String }` variant. The `BufferHeartbeat` struct will gain `drain_template_count: u64` + `drain_lru_evictions_since_tick: u64` fields per obs extract heartbeat-tick pattern.

- `crates/buffer/src/consumer.rs` (full) — `dispatch_batch` at line 88 is the hot-path integration site. The `Batch::Logs(l) => { ... let rows = append_table_traced(&guard, "log_records", rb)?; ... }` arm at line 124 is where Drain assignment threads in. The `build_logs_record_batch` call (built BEFORE the append) is where `template_id` enrichment happens. Pattern to follow: extend `build_logs_record_batch` to accept an `Option<&dyn DrainAssigner>` (NEW trait in buffer crate) for `template_id` assignment per-record OR wire post-build mutation pass in `dispatch_batch`. **Trait-in-lower-crate pattern (per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-16 lesson)**: `DrainAssigner` trait defined in `crates/buffer/`, implementation supplied at pulse-app boundary OR — since Drain itself lives in `crates/buffer/`, the DrainMiner directly implements its own assigner protocol and is passed by `Arc` into `run_consumer`. The chunk #62 `BaselineObserverAdapter` + chunk #66 `FingerprintObserver` pattern (composed via `CompositeSpanObserver` per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-17) is the precedent — Drain is the NEXT observer-style hook into `run_consumer`. Buffer's `run_consumer` signature already accepts `Arc<dyn FingerprintObserver>`-style hooks; adding `Option<Arc<DrainMiner>>` (concrete type, not trait) is the simplest extension because DrainMiner lives in the same crate.

- `crates/buffer/src/appender.rs` (lines 1-120 of ~700+) — `build_spans_record_batch` (lines 30-102) + `extract_service_name` (lines 104-117) + `build_metrics_record_batch` (line 119+). `build_logs_record_batch` is the analogous function for log records (need to read full file for exact line range at /implement time; the pattern is the same — accumulate per-field Vec<>, build Arrow Schema, build RecordBatch). The Drain integration site: extend `build_logs_record_batch` to take `Option<&DrainMiner>` and populate a `template_ids: Vec<i64>` column alongside the other fields. Falls back to all-NULL `template_id` column if `DrainMiner` is None (boot-time `drain_enabled = false` mode).

- `crates/buffer/src/fingerprint.rs` (referenced; not fully read) — Precedent for similar per-event observer hook in buffer crate. Chunk #66's `compute_exception_fingerprint` + `FingerprintObserver` trait pattern is the model for `DrainMiner::assign_template_id` + the observer interface.

- `crates/security/src/lib.rs` (full) — single module: `pub mod scrubber;`. Used by `corpus` at ingestion (chunk #68) + `pulse-app/src/observability.rs` subscriber Layer (defense-in-depth). Drain integration: call `security::scrubber::scrub_attribute(template_text)` BEFORE write to `log_templates.template_content` column. The return type is `ScrubbedValue::{Allowed(String) | Redacted { category }}` — store `category` string when redacted, original (matched-against-but-allowed) string when not.

- `crates/security/src/scrubber.rs` (lines 1-100 of ~130+) — `scrub_attribute(value: &str) -> ScrubbedValue` API. Pattern catalog includes 7 categories: jwt / bearer / api_key / secret_kv / email / credit_card / (presumably ssn at lines 100-130). First-match-wins via `OnceLock<Vec<(Regex, &'static str)>>`. Drain calls this per template string before persistence to corpus AND before write to `log_templates.template_content` DuckDB column.

- `crates/corpus/src/lib.rs` (full) — exposes `pub mod contract;` + internal `pub(crate)` modules `db / encryption / error / keychain / schema`. Public surface goes through `corpus::contract::{Corpus, CorpusReader, InspectionMetadata, Error, KeychainBackend, FakeKeychainBackend, OsKeychainBackend}`. Drain persistence reuses this — define `DrainPersistence` trait in `crates/buffer/`, implement in pulse-app via the existing `Corpus` instance. Persistence cell: re-use existing `pipeline_metrics` table (chunk #68 schema) with `metric_name = "drain_template_tree"`, `layer = "l1c"`, `payload = bincode::serialize(&tree_snapshot)`.

- `crates/corpus/src/schema.rs` (full) — `pipeline_metrics` table schema is `(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, metric_name TEXT NOT NULL, layer TEXT NOT NULL, snapshot_unix_nano INTEGER NOT NULL, payload BLOB NOT NULL)` — `payload BLOB` is AES-256-GCM-encrypted (per crate-level discipline at lib.rs). Drain persistence writes `metric_name = "drain_template_tree"` + `layer = "l1c"` + `payload = bincode-serialized DrainState`. Schema migration NOT required — chunk #68 already created this table. SCHEMA_VERSION stays at 1.

- `pulse-app/src/storage_router.rs` (full, 273 lines) — **THE TEMPLATE for `diagnostics_router.rs`**. Identical shape: `#[taurpc::procedures(path = "diagnostics")] pub trait DiagnosticsApi { async fn template_distribution() -> Result<TemplateDistributionPayload, AppError>; }` + `pub struct DiagnosticsApiImpl { miner: Arc<DrainMiner> }` + `#[taurpc::resolvers] impl DiagnosticsApi for DiagnosticsApiImpl { ... }`. Free-function `pub fn drain_error_to_app_error(err: buffer::Error) -> AppError` at the bottom (orphan-rule + arch DAG preservation). `#[tracing::instrument(skip_all, fields(top_n = tracing::field::Empty, result_count = tracing::field::Empty, duration_ms = tracing::field::Empty))]` decorator on `template_distribution`. Test pattern at lines 171-272 covers in-memory + sanitized-message cases.

- `xtask/src/main.rs` (full, 988 lines) — `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES: &[&str]` at lines 655-683 lists 24 current procedures. Add `"diagnostics.template_distribution"` at the end (or after `storage.path`) maintaining alphabetical-by-namespace ordering. `parse_bindings` parses ARGS_MAP from `pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts`. Test `expected_procedures_includes_storage_namespace_at_chunk_68` is the precedent shape; add `expected_procedures_includes_diagnostics_namespace_at_chunk_69` test asserting `"diagnostics.template_distribution"` membership.

- `pulse-app/capabilities/default.json` (full, 12 lines) — Description string lists all router namespaces; **update description to mention `diagnostics.template_distribution` per chunk #68's update precedent** ("Per chunk #69 also covers diagnostics.template_distribution (Drain template profiling diagnostics — read-only-by-design)."). No `permissions` array change needed — `core:default` + `updater:default` cover all TauRPC handlers (per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-03 lesson: TauRPC dispatches all routers through single invoke handler; capability JSON is router-level, not per-procedure).

- `pulse-app/src/main.rs` (excerpts via Grep + Read 340-460 + 1010-1057) — Router build chain at line 1025-1045 (`taurpc::Router::new().export_config(...).merge(introspection_impl.into_handler()).merge(...).merge(storage_impl.into_handler())`). Production setup at line 367-369 builds `storage_impl: Option<StorageApiImpl>` from `corpus_reader.as_ref().map(|r| StorageApiImpl::new(Arc::clone(r)))`. **Diagnostics analog**: `let diagnostics_impl = DiagnosticsApiImpl::new(Arc::clone(&drain_miner))` where `drain_miner: Arc<DrainMiner>` is built at boot from `DrainMiner::new(config_from_settings, persistence_adapter)`. Add `.merge(diagnostics_impl.into_handler())` to the main Router build AND to the `emit_taurpc_bindings` test's Router build (4+1-place binding 4th slot per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-12).

- `pulse-app/src/observability.rs` (Grep matches) — `AllowList::production()` defined at line 104 with `"buffer"` key at line 145. `for_target` at line 1338 implements the resolver: exact-match → strip-suffix `.tick` → `split('.').next()` → `split("::").next()`. Per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-07 lesson: dotted event targets sharing prefix with crate-level entry fall through to crate entry's allowlist. **Diagnostics events target naming**: use `diagnostics.template_distribution.request` (matches storage_router.rs precedent at lines 84-89). Manual edits between runs are fine; do not edit during /implement run._
- **Phase number:** 67

- **Route chunks covered:**
  - route#70 "BaselineState → corpus migration — EwmaTracker / TDigestPair / RollingWindow / ActivityFloor from flat-file baseline-corpus.bin to corpus SQLite via BaselinePersistence trait (capabilities P-009/P-011/P-013/P-051; detail in pulse-v0_2_0-route §70)"
- **Epoch:** Epoch 9 — Foundation v0.2.0

- **Consolidation context:** FIRST chunk of v3 Phase 6 Consolidation (per `docs/v0_2_0/pulse-v0_2_0-route.md` v3 + `docs/v0_2_0/pulse-v0_2_0-consolidation-audit-2026-05-19.md`); closes audit Section 1.A persistence triple-mechanism finding for 3 of 4 flat-file BaselineState components.

Eliminate the flat-file BaselineState persistence mechanism at `<data_dir>/triage/baseline-corpus.bin` (plaintext bincode) by routing all four streaming baseline trackers — `EwmaTracker` (per-service error rate), `TDigestPair` (per-operation latency percentiles), `RollingWindow<u32>` (per-service activity), `ActivityFloor` (288-bucket histogram) — through the corpus SQLite store via a new `trait BaselinePersistence` defined in `crates/triage/src/baseline/`. Implement `CorpusBaselinePersistence` adapter at `pulse-app/src/baseline_persistence.rs` over `Arc<dyn CorpusWriter>`, mirroring chunk #69's `CorpusDrainPersistence` precedent (trait-in-lower-crate + adapter-at-pulse-app-boundary per CLAUDE.md session-learnings 2026-05-16 + 2026-05-19). Schema decision per research recommendation: **reuse `pipeline_metrics` blob slot** with `metric_name="baseline_state"` + `layer="l1b"` (Option A; mirrors chunk #69 exactly). Migration policy: **read-and-migrate-once + delete legacy file + warn-log** (Path A; preserves dogfood continuity across upgrades). Tracing target naming: `triage.baseline.migrate` (mirrors `triage.baseline.persist` verb shape — combined.md rot warning #1 resolution). Inherits the corpus crate's cell-level AES-256-GCM encryption + OS-keychain key custody (chunk #68 substrate) for at-rest defense; PII scrubber single-site coverage extension is OUT of scope (deferred to chunk #72). After landing, `storage.inspect()` TauRPC (Settings → Storage Diagnostics panel from chunk #68) transparently surfaces the populated `baseline_state` row count with zero UI changes. Closes capabilities P-009 + P-013 SHALL-clauses for corpus-backed baseline state persistence and propagates the same trait-adapter pattern that chunk #71 will follow for ServiceRegistry + RetryStormState.

1. **Define `BaselinePersistence` trait** — create `crates/triage/src/baseline/persistence.rs` (NEW submodule, ~30 lines): `pub trait BaselinePersistence: Send + Sync` with methods `fn load(&self) -> Result<Option<BaselineState>, BaselineError>` + `fn save(&self, state: &BaselineState) -> Result<(), BaselineError>`. Send + Sync super-traits required because tokio tasks cross-spawn `Arc<dyn BaselinePersistence>`. Mirror `crates/buffer/src/drain.rs::DrainPersistence` definition shape.

2. **Wire submodule + re-exports** — update `crates/triage/src/baseline/mod.rs`:
   - Add `mod persistence;` declaration near line 16-22 (alongside existing `mod corpus;`)
   - Add `pub use persistence::BaselinePersistence;` to the existing `pub use` block
   - Add tracing target constants near lines 48-55: `pub(crate) const TARGET_BASELINE_MIGRATE: &str = "triage.baseline.migrate";` + `pub(crate) const TARGET_BASELINE_MIGRATE_FAILED: &str = "triage.baseline.migrate.failed";`
   - Update module docstring (lines 1-15) to reflect corpus-backed persistence (replace "persists to a self-versioned bincode corpus file under `<data-dir>/triage/baseline-corpus.bin`" with corpus reference)
   - Remove `resolve_corpus_path` from `pub use corpus::{...}` (line 37-40); keep `bootstrap_from_corpus` + `BootstrapResult` + `PersistStats` (still referenced by signature changes below)

3. **Refactor `crates/triage/src/baseline/corpus.rs`** — convert flat-file ops to trait-based:
   - DELETE `resolve_corpus_path` fn (lines 32-43) entirely — no longer needed
   - DELETE `persist_state` fn (lines 45-73) — replaced by `BaselinePersistence::save` trait method consumed via adapter
   - DELETE `load_state` fn (lines 75-126) — replaced by `BaselinePersistence::load` trait method
   - REFACTOR `bootstrap_from_corpus` (lines 128-158) → `pub fn bootstrap_from_persistence(persistence: &dyn BaselinePersistence, service_cap: usize, now_nanos: i64) -> BootstrapResult` taking the trait reference. Body: call `persistence.load()` → on `Ok(Some(state))` map to `BootstrapResult::Loaded { state, age_nanos }`; on `Ok(None)` map to `BootstrapResult::Fresh { reason_kind: "cold_start" }`; on `Err(BaselineError::SchemaVersionMismatch { .. })` → `Fresh { reason_kind: "schema_mismatch" }`; on `Err(BaselineError::ServiceCountCapExceeded { .. })` → `Fresh { reason_kind: "service_count_cap_exceeded" }`; on other `Err(_)` → `Fresh { reason_kind: "corpus_corrupt_reset" }`. Drop the `SizeCapExceeded` arm (corpus enforces its own size limits via SQLite cell-size — no separate flat-file size cap applies post-migration).
   - UPDATE `run_persist_loop(state, path, interval)` → `run_persist_loop(state: Arc<BaselineState>, persistence: Arc<dyn BaselinePersistence>, interval: Duration)`. Body: replace existing flat-file `persist_state(&path, &state)` call with `persistence.save(&state)`.
   - UPDATE `persist_on_shutdown(state, path)` → `persist_on_shutdown(state: &BaselineState, persistence: &dyn BaselinePersistence)` similarly.
   - UPDATE `bootstrap_state(path, max_size, cap, now)` → `bootstrap_state(persistence: Option<Arc<dyn BaselinePersistence>>, service_cap: usize, now_nanos: i64) -> Arc<BaselineState>`. When `Some(p)` → call `bootstrap_from_persistence(&*p, cap, now)` + map result to Arc. When `None` → return fresh `BaselineState::new()` (cold-start path; covers None-case Q2).
   - DELETE all 8 existing tests (lines 160-318). Replace with 4-5 corpus-aware tests below (see Implementation Step 9).

4. **Create `pulse-app/src/baseline_persistence.rs`** (NEW, ~180-220 lines) mirroring `drain_persistence.rs:1-218`:
   - Module docstring referencing chunk #70 + trait-in-lower-crate + adapter-at-pulse-app-boundary pattern (mirrors drain_persistence.rs:1-24)
   - Constants: `pub const BASELINE_STATE_METRIC_NAME: &str = "baseline_state";` + `pub const BASELINE_PERSISTENCE_LAYER: &str = "l1b";`
   - Adapter struct: `#[derive(Clone)] pub struct CorpusBaselinePersistence { writer: Arc<dyn CorpusWriter> }` + `impl CorpusBaselinePersistence { pub fn new(writer: Arc<dyn CorpusWriter>) -> Self { Self { writer } } }`
   - Trait impl `impl BaselinePersistence for CorpusBaselinePersistence`:
     - `fn load(&self) -> Result<Option<BaselineState>, BaselineError>`: call `self.writer.load_pipeline_metric(BASELINE_STATE_METRIC_NAME, BASELINE_PERSISTENCE_LAYER)` → map `corpus::Error` via `corpus_error_to_baseline_error` → on `Some(bytes)` deserialize via `bincode::deserialize::<BaselineState>(&bytes)` → on bincode error return `BaselineError::Deserialize` → on success Ok(Some(state)); on `None` → `Ok(None)`
     - `fn save(&self, state: &BaselineState) -> Result<(), BaselineError>`: bincode-serialize state → on bincode error return `BaselineError::Serialize` → call `self.writer.save_pipeline_metric(BASELINE_STATE_METRIC_NAME, BASELINE_PERSISTENCE_LAYER, &bytes)` → map `corpus::Error` via `corpus_error_to_baseline_error`
   - Free function `fn corpus_error_to_baseline_error(err: corpus::Error) -> BaselineError`: match arms similar to `drain_persistence.rs:88-103` — `KeyringUnavailable` → `BaselineError::Io { kind: io::ErrorKind::PermissionDenied }`, `MigrationFailed` → ditto, `EncryptionFailed` / `DecryptionFailed` → `Deserialize`, `QueryFailed` → `Io { kind: io::ErrorKind::Other }`, `PathTraversal` → `PathTraversal`, `SizeCapExceeded` → `SizeCapExceeded { actual: 0, max: 0 }` (size info unavailable at adapter boundary — sentinel values), `SchemaVersionMismatch` → `SchemaVersionMismatch { expected: SCHEMA_VERSION, got: 0 }` (sentinel got = 0; corpus error doesn't carry the value), `Io { .. }` → `Io { kind: io::ErrorKind::Other }`. NEVER `impl From<corpus::Error> for BaselineError` (orphan rule + reverses arch DAG).
   - Migration helper: `pub fn migrate_legacy_baseline_if_present(data_dir: &Path, persistence: &dyn BaselinePersistence, service_cap: usize) -> MigrationOutcome`:
     - canonicalize `data_dir.join("triage").join("baseline-corpus.bin")` via `fs::canonicalize` → assert path starts with canonicalized `data_dir` (CWE-22 defense; mirrors security/C1 + C5)
     - if path does NOT exist OR canonicalize fails (not-found) → return `MigrationOutcome::Noop` (no warn-log; cold-start path)
     - else: `fs::metadata(&path)` → if size > 16 MB → return `Failed { error_category: "size_exceeded" }` + emit `triage.baseline.migrate.failed`
     - `fs::read(&path)` → on Io error → `Failed { error_category: "io" }`
     - `bincode::deserialize::<BaselineState>(&bytes)` → on error → `Failed { error_category: "deserialize" }`
     - check `state.service_count() <= service_cap` else `Failed { error_category: "service_count_cap_exceeded" }`
     - `persistence.save(&state)` → on `Err(BaselineError::Io { .. })` → `Failed { error_category: "io" }`; on other Err → `Failed { error_category: "encryption" | "sql" }` (map appropriately)
     - `fs::remove_file(&path)` → on error → `Completed { legacy_file_deleted: false, reason: "remove_failed" }` (data saved; only cleanup failed; warn-log emits with degraded outcome but still success on data side)
     - on full success: emit `tracing::info!(target: TARGET_BASELINE_MIGRATE, legacy_state_size_bytes = bytes.len() as u64, migrated_service_count = state.service_count() as u64, duration_ms = ..., migration_outcome = "completed", "migrated legacy baseline-corpus.bin to corpus")`
     - return enum: `MigrationOutcome::{Noop, Completed { legacy_file_deleted: bool, reason: Option<&'static str> }, Failed { error_category: &'static str }}`

title: Schema decision recommendation (resolves combined.md rot warning #2)

data.head: ## Schema decision recommendation (resolves combined.md rot warning #2)

body: **Option A: Reuse `pipeline_metrics` blob slot** — `metric_name="baseline_state"`, `layer="l1b"`, payload = `bincode::serialize(&BaselineState)`. PROS: (a) mirrors chunk #69 Drain precedent EXACTLY — same code shape, same testing harness, same observability path; (b) no `CorpusWriter` trait extension needed (uses existing `save_pipeline_metric` / `load_pipeline_metric`); (c) no `crates/corpus/src/schema.rs` changes (table exists; reusing existing methods means schema unchanged); (d) preserves the full `BaselineState` shape including DashMap-of-services + DashMap-of-operations + AtomicI64 timestamp; (e) simpler to test (one blob round-trip vs N per-service rows). CONS: (a) no per-service queryability — load fetches the entire serialized state (mitigated: triage already loads all-at-once); (b) the empty `baseline_state` table at corpus/schema.rs:35-42 remains unused at chunk #70 close (could be removed in chunk #74 batch).

**Option B: Populate dedicated `baseline_state` table per-service** — requires extending `CorpusWriter` trait with `save_baseline_state(service_name, operation, payload) -> Result<(), Error>` + `load_baseline_state(...) -> Result<Vec<(String, Vec<u8>)>, Error>`. PROS: (a) per-service queryability (future per-service deletion / inspection); (b) populates the empty pre-allocated table. CONS: (a) substantially more code (~3-4× delta); (b) requires custom load logic к rehydrate the DashMap from N rows + handle partial-load failures; (c) diverges from chunk #69 precedent (one-off pattern); (d) per-row encryption nonces increase storage overhead modestly.

**Recommendation: Option A.** Audit Section 1.A persistence triple-mechanism closure is the primary goal; minimal divergence from chunk #69 precedent reduces review surface + risk. Empty `baseline_state` table cleanup goes to chunk #74 arch registry batch.

title: Migration policy recommendation (resolves combined.md rot warning #3)

data.head: ## Migration policy recommendation (resolves combined.md rot warning #3)

body: **Path A: read-and-migrate-once + delete legacy + warn-log.** PROS: (a) preserves continuity for dogfood users who have accumulated baseline state across sessions; (b) ~30 LOC delta + 2 tests; (c) eliminates dead `<data_dir>/triage/baseline-corpus.bin` files. CONS: requires synchronous corpus write at boot before `health` 10s readiness check; large legacy files (>1 MB; today's cap) could approach the limit but well under it. Migration code: at boot, check `data_dir.join("triage").join("baseline-corpus.bin")` exists; if so, canonicalize via `strict-path` ancestor assertion (mirror existing `resolve_corpus_path` discipline); `fs::read` → `bincode::deserialize::<BaselineState>` → `persistence.save(&state)` → `fs::remove_file` → emit `tracing::info!(target: "triage.baseline.migrate", ...)`. Handle each error category with `migration_outcome = "failed_degraded"` + sanitized `error_category`.

**Path B: cold-start with optional notice log.** PROS: simpler (~10 LOC + 0 migration tests). CONS: dogfood users lose accumulated baselines on upgrade (regrets surface as silent "why are my thresholds reset?" UX bug).
**Recommendation: Path A.** Cost is low; operational benefit is real.

Verb form > noun form by existing precedent.

- **Q1 — adapter Send + Sync bounds**: chunk #69 `CorpusDrainPersistence` is `Send + Sync` by virtue of `Arc<dyn CorpusWriter>` (which has `: Send + Sync` super-trait at corpus/contract.rs:162). Chunk #70's `BaselinePersistence` trait MUST also bound `: Send + Sync` because `bootstrap_state` + `run_persist_loop` cross-spawn `Arc<dyn BaselinePersistence>` into tokio tasks. Path: define the trait as `pub trait BaselinePersistence: Send + Sync` (mirror `crates/buffer/src/drain.rs::DrainPersistence` definition; verify same shape).

- **Q2 — None-case wiring**: if `corpus_writer` is `None` at boot (corpus open failed; keychain unavailable; etc.), should `baseline_persistence` be `None` AND `run_persist_loop` skip spawning? OR should it spawn а no-op persistence task that just keeps the state in-memory + emits periodic `triage.baseline.persist.error` with `error_category = "corpus_unavailable"`? Recommend: skip spawning (no-op task wastes a tokio handle; periodic error emission is noise). Plan.md should specify the skip-on-None branch + emit one boot-time warn at `triage.baseline.persist.error` with `error_category = "corpus_unavailable_at_boot"` to make the degraded state observable.

- **Q3 — BootstrapResult API surface**: existing `bootstrap_from_corpus(path, max_size, service_cap, now_nanos) -> BootstrapResult` takes path; chunk #70's replacement takes `Arc<dyn BaselinePersistence>`. The `BootstrapResult::Fresh { reason_kind: "size_cap_exceeded" | ... }` enum stays valid (corpus returns Some/None; size/cap policies enforced inside the adapter OR via runtime trait method). Adapter can use Corpus's own size_bytes check (already done at chunk #68 `db::file_size_bytes`) OR delegate к the trait's load method to return Error variants that map к BootstrapResult::Fresh kinds. Recommend: adapter returns `Result<Option<BaselineState>, BaselineError>`; bootstrap_state caller maps `Err` к appropriate BootstrapResult::Fresh kind based on BaselineError variant.

But default-features `cargo nextest run -p pulse-app -E 'test(emit_taurpc_bindings)'` (or any default-features nextest invocation hitting that test) transiently overwrites bindings.ts to the no-mcp shape, removing the `mcp` namespace entries.
