body: _Generated by /andromeda-phase Phase 4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not edit during /implement run._
- **Phase number:** 68

- **Route chunks covered:**
  - route#71 "ServiceRegistry + RetryStormState → corpus migration — DashMap → corpus via LifecyclePersistence + StormPersistence traits (capabilities P-017/P-018/P-027; detail in pulse-v0_2_0-route §71)"
- **Epoch:** Foundation v0.2.0 (Epoch 9)

Close the two remaining persistence gaps after chunk #70 BaselineState → corpus by migrating chunk #67's `InMemoryServiceRegistry` (currently `DashMap<String, ServiceRegistryEntry>` lost on every restart) and chunk #66's `RetryStormDetector` (currently `DashMap<[u8; 16], FingerprintState>` whose docstring explicitly defers persistence to chunk #69) onto the corpus SQLite substrate via two new traits — `LifecyclePersistence` in `crates/triage/src/lifecycle/persistence.rs` and `StormPersistence` in `crates/triage/src/pattern/persistence.rs` — with corresponding adapters `CorpusLifecyclePersistence` + `CorpusStormPersistence` at the `pulse-app/` binary boundary, mirroring the chunk #70 trait-in-lower-crate + adapter-at-pulse-app pattern (per combined.md §Patterns to follow + research.md inspection of `pulse-app/src/baseline_persistence.rs`). After landing, capability P-027 verification ("Restart Pulse; verify dot positions match prior session") becomes runtime-true; capability P-018 (retry storm detection) survives process restart so dedup windows are preserved rather than reset; and the broken chunk #66 deferred-persistence promise (storm.rs docstring lines 38-39 + 94-95) is closed.

The implementation also closes the dead-code gap on `TransitionTrigger::CorpusRestore` (state_machine.rs:47 — defined as enum variant and FSM-edge-tested, but unreachable in production) and the missing `set_state_on_corpus_restore` method referenced in `crates/triage/src/lifecycle/registry.rs` docstring lines 7-11 but never defined as code. Both lifecycle + storm follow the chunk #69+#70 N-trait-from-single-Arc pattern: a single `Arc<corpus::contract::Corpus>` at the binary boundary derives `corpus_reader` / `corpus_writer` / `baseline_persistence` / `lifecycle_persistence` / `storm_persistence` views — preserving one rusqlite connection mutex + one OS-keychain encryption key per session, while exposing role-separated trait views to each consumer (per combined.md §Patterns to follow + arch §Cross-cutting Patterns Module dependency direction). No new TauRPC procedures, no new broadcast topics, no new env vars, no new workspace crates — chunk #71 is a pure backend persistence refactor at boot ordering.

Schema reuses pre-allocated corpus tables per chunk #68 design: lifecycle uses the dedicated `service_registry` table (per-row INSERT/UPDATE since its columns — service_name UNIQUE, state TEXT, three timestamp INTEGERs, manual_override TEXT — map directly onto `ServiceRegistryEntry` fields per research.md inspection of `crates/corpus/src/schema.rs:44-53`); storm uses the `pipeline_metrics` blob slot (metric_name="storm_state", layer="l2") mirroring baseline ("baseline_state"/"l1b") and Drain ("drain_template_tree"/"l1c"). PII scrubber call site at lifecycle write path is explicitly deferred to chunk #72 (per route#71 chunk text + combined.md security AC #6); chunk #71 captures the deferral as Acceptance Criteria → Deferred. Storm fingerprints are non-PII by construction (16-byte hashes of normalized exception.type + stack). Migration helpers are NOT introduced (no legacy flat-file source for either RetryStormState or ServiceRegistry — both were always in-memory-only); first boot after chunk #71 lands loads zero rows from corpus → fresh-start path; subsequent boots restore prior state.

1. **Define `LifecyclePersistence` trait** at `crates/triage/src/lifecycle/persistence.rs` (NEW file):
   - `pub trait LifecyclePersistence: Send + Sync` with `load_all() -> Result<Option<Vec<(String, ServiceRegistryEntry)>>, LifecycleError>` (returns `Ok(None)` if no rows exist; `Ok(Some(empty))` is reserved for write-success-but-zero-services, but in practice load_all returns `None` for the empty-table case to mirror BaselinePersistence::load semantics) + `save_all(entries: &[(String, ServiceRegistryEntry)]) -> Result<(), LifecycleError>`. Both methods take/return owned types to avoid lifetime gymnastics on the DashMap snapshot path; the caller (adapter) is responsible for materializing the snapshot from `InMemoryServiceRegistry`.
   - `pub enum LifecycleError` mirroring `BaselineError` shape: `Io { kind: std::io::ErrorKind }`, `Serialize`, `Deserialize`, `PathTraversal`, `SizeCapExceeded { actual: u64, max: u64 }`, `SchemaVersionMismatch { expected: u32, got: u32 }`. (Storm has the same shape — co-located or shared as `crates/triage/src/persistence_error.rs` is an orchestrator-time refinement; default = per-module enums for clarity.)
   - Module-level doc cites schema choice ("per-row INSERT/UPDATE on service_registry table") + trait-in-lower-crate rationale (per session-learnings 2026-05-16) + Send + Sync requirement (spawned into tokio persist task).
   - `pub const TARGET_LIFECYCLE_PERSIST: &str = "triage.lifecycle.persist"` + `pub const TARGET_LIFECYCLE_PERSIST_ERROR: &str = "triage.lifecycle.persist.error"` + `pub const DEFAULT_LIFECYCLE_PERSIST_INTERVAL_SECS: u64 = 60` (mirrors baseline persist cadence). Note: chunk #67 already declared `TARGET_LIFECYCLE_CORPUS_RESTORE = "triage.lifecycle.corpus_restore"` at lifecycle/mod.rs:49 — reuse it; chunk #71 extends its AllowList field set rather than introducing a sibling.

2. **Define `StormPersistence` trait** at `crates/triage/src/pattern/persistence.rs` (NEW file):
   - `pub struct StormStateSnapshot { entries: Vec<(FingerprintBytes, FingerprintState)>, window_seconds: u64, detection_window_seconds: u64, suggested_threshold: u64, autonomous_threshold: u64 }` (Serializable, Deserializable). `FingerprintBytes` is `[u8; 16]`; `FingerprintState` (storm.rs:78-90) requires NEW `#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]` derives — currently has only `Debug` — see Step 5.
   - `pub trait StormPersistence: Send + Sync` with `load() -> Result<Option<StormStateSnapshot>, StormError>` + `save(snapshot: &StormStateSnapshot) -> Result<(), StormError>`. Single load/save pair (no per-fingerprint methods) since storm uses pipeline_metrics blob slot.
   - `pub enum StormError` mirroring `BaselineError` / `LifecycleError` shape.
   - `pub const TARGET_PATTERN_STORM_PERSIST: &str = "triage.pattern.storm.persist"` + `pub const TARGET_PATTERN_STORM_PERSIST_ERROR: &str = "triage.pattern.storm.persist.error"` + `pub const TARGET_PATTERN_STORM_CORPUS_RESTORE: &str = "triage.pattern.storm.corpus_restore"` (NEW target; no existing equivalent in pattern/mod.rs).
   - Module-level doc cites Schema Option A (mirrors baseline_state shape — `pipeline_metrics(metric_name="storm_state", layer="l2")` blob slot) + serialization shape (Vec<...> from DashMap snapshot, NOT DashMap directly because DashMap is not serde-able).

3. **Wire trait modules + re-exports** in `crates/triage/src/`:
   - `lifecycle/mod.rs`: add `mod persistence;` at line ~22 (alongside `mod broadcast; mod registry; mod state_machine;`); add `pub use persistence::{LifecyclePersistence, LifecycleError, TARGET_LIFECYCLE_PERSIST, TARGET_LIFECYCLE_PERSIST_ERROR, DEFAULT_LIFECYCLE_PERSIST_INTERVAL_SECS};` after line ~40.
   - `pattern/mod.rs`: add `mod persistence;` at line ~23 (alongside `mod broadcast; mod detector; mod storm; mod suppression;`); add `pub use persistence::{StormPersistence, StormError, StormStateSnapshot, TARGET_PATTERN_STORM_PERSIST, TARGET_PATTERN_STORM_PERSIST_ERROR, TARGET_PATTERN_STORM_CORPUS_RESTORE};` after line ~36.
   - `crates/triage/src/contract.rs` (or wherever the existing `triage::contract` re-exports live — chunk #70 added `BaselinePersistence` / `BaselineError` / `TARGET_BASELINE_*` here; verify at /implement time): extend with `LifecyclePersistence`, `LifecycleError`, `StormPersistence`, `StormError`, `StormStateSnapshot`, `TARGET_LIFECYCLE_PERSIST`, `TARGET_LIFECYCLE_PERSIST_ERROR`, `TARGET_PATTERN_STORM_PERSIST`, `TARGET_PATTERN_STORM_PERSIST_ERROR`, `TARGET_PATTERN_STORM_CORPUS_RESTORE`, `DEFAULT_LIFECYCLE_PERSIST_INTERVAL_SECS`.

- (obs) Drain template-mining persistence span events (the snapshot_state → bincode → `CorpusWriter::save_pipeline_metric` path being newly wired) MUST follow the §6 DuckDB-query boundary discipline: emit `query_id` + `param_count` + `row_count_returned` + `duration_ms`, never the bincode payload contents or the template body (per obs-plan §6 boundary-call wrappers + §3 Vector 5).

- (obs) The new pre-scrub call sites in `crates/buffer/src/appender.rs:332-356` and the Drain corpus persist path MUST NOT log the scrubber input value (the raw attribute) at any tracing level — if scrubber returns `ScrubbedValue::Redacted`, only emit a counter event with `redacted_field_name` + `category` (per §8 `skip(...)` pattern).

- (obs) `CorpusWriter` trait contract enforcement constitutes a defense-in-depth Layer parallel to obs-plan §8 "At source / At subscriber Layer / At Sentry boundary" three-layer model — the persistence boundary IS the third layer for at-rest data (per §11 PII anti-pattern: "NEVER hardcode scrubbing rules in a single location — rules applied at multiple layers").

- (obs) Heartbeat ticks from `buffer.tick` (15s interval per obs-plan §3 Heartbeat ticks) MUST continue to emit `rows_ingested` / `eviction_count` / `memory_bytes` / `retention_window_seconds` without regression — adding scrubber call sites in the appender hot path MUST NOT widen the field set with raw attribute content (per obs-plan §8 allowlist for `buffer` module).

- (obs) Scrubber call sites in the appender are inside a hot path — per-attribute scrubbing in `appender.rs:332-356` MUST NOT add `info`-level tracing events per record; use `trace`/`debug` gated by `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_LOG_LEVEL` only (per obs-plan §11 Logs "NEVER log in hot path at `info` level").
**Patterns к follow:**

- (security) Boundary validation discipline: scrub at the SAME class of boundary `prost`-decode-then-invariant-checks already establishes — post-decode work at the OTLP `ingest` crate boundary BEFORE handing batches to `buffer::Appender`. Treats `buffer::Appender::insert_*` + `CorpusWriter::save_*` as the same trust-boundary class as `Connection::prepare` + `?` placeholder DuckDB parameter binding (per security plan §Input Validation row 1 "post-decode invariants" + row 5 "reject identifier interpolation entirely" pattern).

- (security) Trait-boundary contract enforcement: closing the `CorpusWriter` "callers SHOULD pre-scrub" docstring gap with a `ScrubbedValue::{Allowed, Redacted}` newtype enum signature mirrors the `AppError::{Validation, NotFound, Internal, Plugin, Storage, Ingest}` `serde`-friendly enum discipline at TauRPC bridge — compile-time-or-runtime-checked enum gate replaces "convention assumed" hope (per security plan §Error Handling TauRPC bridge `AppError` pattern + Conventions Error response schema enum-as-contract discipline).

- (security) Defense-in-depth alongside `tracing` subscriber Layer: this chunk wires scrubber AT persistence; the deferred chunk #70+ pulse-app observability subscriber Layer per CLAUDE.md remains the second layer — this chunk's scope is persistence-boundary closure, NOT subscriber Layer rewrite (per security plan §Logging "Field redaction is applied at the subscriber layer, not at log call sites").

- (security) Idempotent / safe-to-rerun pattern: if a row gets re-persisted (replay / retry / migration), the second scrubber pass over an already-scrubbed value MUST be a no-op (Redacted stays Redacted; the 7-category regex set MUST NOT match `[REDACTED:jwt]` placeholder patterns on the second pass) — mirrors the migration-safety pattern from session-learnings.md 2026-05-20.

- (arch) **Workspace dep already established — extend the existing edge, not introduce new ones**: `crates/buffer/Cargo.toml` already imports `security` (verified via `use security::scrubber::{ScrubbedValue, scrub_attribute}` at `crates/buffer/src/drain.rs:46`). The corpus crate may need to add `security` as a dep IF the CorpusWriter impl invokes scrubber defensively — verify before adding via Cargo.toml inspection.

- (arch) **Persistence-boundary uniformity (chunk #68 → #69 → #72 progression)**: chunk #68 introduced scrubber primitive at single site (drain.rs:600 DuckDB template write); chunk #69 extended Drain bincode→corpus persistence chain; chunk #72 closes the uniformity gap by applying the same pre-write scrubber call at every other persistence-boundary site.

- (arch) **Settings/contract types already extended to support Drain config (chunk #69 precedent)**: chunk #72 does NOT need to extend `Settings` — the scrubber catalog is compile-time constant, no env-var override / settings field appropriate.

- (arch) **CorpusReader + CorpusWriter trait-pair pattern (chunk #69 precedent)** at `crates/corpus/src/contract.rs:142-194`: extend the trait IN-PLACE rather than adding a third trait (per CLAUDE.md user-instructions session learning 2026-05-19 N-trait-from-single-Arc pattern).

- (arch) **NEVER `format!()` SQL composition** (arch §Critical Warnings + obs §PII scrubbing): drain.rs:600 already uses `Connection::prepare` + `?` placeholders; appender.rs:332-356 uses Arrow appender, not raw SQL — scrubbed values flow through these same prepared-statement / Arrow-appender surfaces; no string-interpolation regression introduced.

- (tests) Negative-test pattern from §1 Coverage triggers `security-vector-coverage: DuckDB SQL injection prevention` row: analog for chunk #72 is "assert canary secret `Bearer abc123XYZ...` injected as OTLP attribute value is stored as `[REDACTED]` marker, not as the raw secret". One negative test per P-047 category × per persistence site.
- (tests) Builder factory pattern from §4 / §7 — extend existing `MockTraceSpan::builder()` (and analogous log / metric / span-event builders) with a `.with_attribute_canary(key, raw_secret)` helper.

- (tests) `rstest` parameterized pattern from §4 — `#[rstest] #[case::jwt(...)] #[case::bearer(...)] ...` table-driven across 7 P-047 categories. Same `#[rstest]` table reused at each persistence-site test module.

- (tests) Universal redaction grep-discipline from §3 Log format / §11 Universal — wrap-time gate: `! grep -E '<canary-substring>' ~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/*.log` against the deterministic canary tokens introduced by fixtures.

- (tests) Test-time telemetry injection per arch CLAUDE.md §Cross-cutting Patterns + test-plan §6 — drive end-to-end secret-canary tests by speaking OTLP to the running receiver (no in-process "test ingest" feature flag / mock-channel back-door).

- (obs) Boundary-call wrapper pattern: persistence-boundary scrubber invocations should emit a single aggregate span per OTLP batch append (wrap `appender.rs:332-356` in the existing `duckdb.append` span and add `attributes_count` + `redacted_count` aggregate fields), mirroring the §6 boundary-call table row "DuckDB query" pattern.

- (obs) Default-deny allowlist pattern: register new scrubber-output fields in the `buffer` module allowlist in obs-plan §8 — proposed additions: `attributes_scrubbed_count`, `redacted_category_counts` (per-category histogram with enumerated category labels).

- (obs) Source-at-instrumentation discipline: any new function in the appender or corpus-writer call chain that takes raw attribute strings MUST be annotated `#[tracing::instrument(skip(attr_value, attributes), fields(attr_key, attributes_count))]` — `skip(...)` excludes the secret at the source; `fields(...)` allowlists only safe metadata.

- (obs) Defense-in-depth at multiple layers: chunk #72 makes the `CorpusWriter` contract layer mandatory, matching the obs-plan's "multiple layers" pattern (per obs-plan §8 Integration points + §11 PII Scrubbing).
**Anti-patterns к avoid:**

- (security) NEVER add a NEW `CorpusWriter` / `buffer::Appender` write call site WITHOUT routing through `security::scrub_attribute()` for any field carrying user-controlled OTLP content (per security plan §Logging NEVER-log raw OTLP attribute values).

- (security) NEVER catch-all-bypass the scrubber under a "trusted source" claim — self-observation MUST continue to use `tracing` ecosystem only with NO OTel SDK linked, but if a future event records an OTLP-derived attribute, the scrubber rule applies; no trust-tier exemption (per security plan §Logging & Monitoring NEVER-log list applies universally).

- (security) NEVER widen scrubber coverage by switching to a wildcard "drop everything that looks like a string longer than N chars" — would lose actionable telemetry (service.name, error.type, request_id are NOT secrets); broaden by adding categories, not by switching to deny-by-default-on-length heuristics (per security plan §Data Protection "data classification: user-content").

- (arch) Do NOT introduce a reverse-direction dep edge (e.g., `security` depending on `buffer` or `corpus`) per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns "Module dependency direction".

- (arch) Do NOT introduce a new workspace crate to hold scrub-then-persist plumbing — security + buffer + corpus crates already cover the relevant boundaries.

- (tests) NEVER assert on raw-secret payload bytes in test output even when the assertion is "this got redacted" — assertions must compare to the redaction marker shape, NEVER print the canary substring to test stdout / CI logs / JUnit XML (per §11 Universal "NEVER expose secrets in test output").

- (tests) NEVER mock the scrubber (`crates/security`) at integration tests for appender / drain / corpus boundaries — call the real `scrub_attribute()` (per §8 "use real implementations; mock only traits you own").

- (tests) NEVER skip negative tests for the 7 P-047 categories by claiming "covered by scrubber primitive unit tests" — chunk #72's job is asserting INVOCATION at each new persistence site (per the test-plan 2026-05-08 Decisions Log gap entry).
- (tests) NEVER use `#[ignore]` to skip a failing scrubber-coverage negative test — per §10 zero-flakiness budget + §11 CI.

- (obs) NEVER add per-record `info`-level tracing events inside the new scrubber invocation loop in `appender.rs:332-356` — appender is a hot path; use aggregate per-batch fields on the wrapping `duckdb.append` span (per obs-plan §11 Telemetry Strategy + §11 Logs).

- (obs) NEVER log the raw attribute value being scrubbed at ANY level (not even debug/trace), nor the post-scrub `ScrubbedValue::Redacted` placeholder content (per obs-plan §11 Logs + §11 PII Scrubbing).

- (obs) NEVER emit the Drain template body (the masked log-line string that survives masking) verbatim in scrubber-related tracing events from the corpus persist path — treat the bincode payload as opaque, log `template_id` + `byte_length` + `category` only (per obs-plan §3 Vector 5 query-anonymizer discipline applied to corpus persist path).

data.head: # Phase 69 Plan — chunk route#72: "PII scrubber coverage extension"

body: _Generated by /andromeda-phase Phase 4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not edit during /implement run._
- **Phase number:** 69

- **Route chunks covered:**
  - route#72 "PII scrubber coverage extension — extend scrub_attribute to OTLP appender + Drain corpus persist paths; uniform pre-scrub at persistence boundary (capabilities P-006/P-047/P-048; detail in pulse-v0_2_0-route §72)"
- **Epoch:** 9 — Foundation v0.2.0 (final chunk; closes Consolidation Phase 6 third deliverable per v3 plan)

Extend the PII scrubber from its current single production call site (`crates/buffer/src/drain.rs:600` — DuckDB `log_templates` template-content write) to every other OTLP-attribute persistence path: the OTLP appender's `log_records.body` + `span_events.exception_message` + `span_events.exception_stacktrace` columns (DuckDB ring buffer at-rest), plus the corpus SQLite persistence adapters for Drain template tree (chunk #69) + ServiceRegistry rows (chunk #71) + RetryStormState (chunk #71) + BaselineState (chunk #70). The scrubber primitive (`security::scrubber::scrub_attribute` returning `ScrubbedValue::{Allowed, Redacted{category}}`) already implements the 7 P-047 categories (JWT / bearer / API key / secret KV / email / credit card / SSN) introduced at chunk #68 — chunk #72 is wiring expansion, not algorithm change. Every new scrub site renders `Redacted` matches as the stable `[REDACTED:{category}]` marker (preserving the chunk #68 / #69 convention).

The chunk closes three capability spec gaps surfaced in the consolidation audit (`docs/v0_2_0/pulse-v0_2_0-consolidation-audit-2026-05-19.md` §1.A.6 + §1.A scrubber-coverage rows): P-006 ("exception.message after PII scrubbing per P-047" currently violated by raw `span_events.exception_message` writes at appender.rs:332-356), P-047 ("all content before persistence to corpus or inclusion in Reports" currently satisfied at exactly ONE production site), P-048 ("No raw OTLP attribute values stored beyond what is necessary for hypothesis generation" currently violated by raw OTLP body + exception fields). The `CorpusWriter` trait docstring (`crates/corpus/src/contract.rs:172-176`) shifts from "callers SHOULD pre-scrub" to enforced-by-per-adapter-canary-tests; the trait signature stays unchanged (no breaking change; arch §Occupied Resources receives zero registry additions; no `/andromeda-evolve --allow-arch-registry` needed). Defense-in-depth is preserved alongside the deferred chunk #70+ pulse-app observability subscriber Layer — those layers cover different threat models (at-rest persistence vs in-flight self-observation) per security plan §Logging multi-layer discipline + obs-plan §8 three-layer model.

The Phase 6 user review establishes scope boundaries: this chunk does NOT modify the `security::scrubber` algorithm; does NOT introduce new categories; does NOT add new TauRPC procedures or broadcast topics; does NOT regress the 10k spans/sec ingest budget (scrubber is OnceLock-cached regex set; per-attribute cost is microseconds); does NOT collapse PII-shaped service_names into ambiguous tracker keys without that being a documented + intentional aggregation behavior (security > attribution for misconfigured services).

1. **Wire scrubber into `crates/buffer/src/appender.rs` log + span_event paths.**

body: **Constraints across domains:**

- (arch) Webview source files MUST live under `pulse-app/ui/` (the webview source root) per arch §Infrastructure Patterns "Project directory structure" — Tailwind v4 `@theme` block, font WOFF2 assets, and any CSS files belong under `pulse-app/ui/src/`; MUST NOT introduce a new top-level webview directory or sibling crate.

- (arch) The chunk MUST NOT add a new Cargo workspace member or a new library crate name — workspace crate names LOCKED per arch §Occupied Resources "Cargo workspace crate names" (the 10 reserved names).

- (arch) The chunk MUST NOT introduce a new TauRPC procedure, IPC event name, OTLP route, MCP tool, env var, filesystem path, or network port — design tokens are pure-frontend and build-time per arch §Occupied Resources reserved sets.
- (arch) Dark-mode is the default color scheme per arch §Design Philosophy "Developer-tool surface" — token bundle MUST set dark-mode default and honor "dense, chart-first, low-chrome" framing.

- (arch) The chunk MUST NOT modify any of the 5 reserved Tauri capability identifiers (`pulse:default`, `pulse:tray`, `pulse:notification`, `pulse:updater`, `pulse:plugin-fs`) per arch §Occupied Resources "Tauri capability identifiers".

- (security) The webview CSP literal in `pulse-app/tauri.conf.json` MUST keep `script-src 'self'` (no `'unsafe-inline'` / `'unsafe-eval'` / no remote origin); Tailwind-v4 token output MUST land as a static `'self'`-served stylesheet (no CDN, no inline script generator) per security plan §API Security CSP row.

- (security) Font assets MUST ship locally as bundled WOFF2 next to the `'self'` origin — NEVER add Google Fonts / CDN domains to `connect-src` / `font-src` / `style-src` per security plan §API Security CSP row + Cross-cutting Patterns "no CDN".

- (security) Any new dependency added for token tooling MUST flow through `cargo audit` + `cargo deny check bans licenses sources` clean exit; new transitive duplicates MUST be skip-listed with one-line provenance comments per `.claude/rules/security.md` 2026-05-03 Session Addition.

- (security) WOFF2 / SVG / CSS asset files MUST be original first-party Adobe / JetBrains distributions; SIL OFL 1.1 LICENSE files MUST land in-tree per security plan §Dependency Security `licenses` check.

- (security) `.gitignore` MUST keep covering `*.p12`, `*.pem`, `*.cer`, `.env*`, `*.key`, `~/.tauri/*.key` — gitleaks pre-commit + per-PR gate MUST keep passing per security plan §Bootstrap phases `secret-scanning-ci-gate`.
- (security) Token / theme / font-loading code MUST NOT introduce a `tokio::process::Command` shell-out — token compilation is build-time only per security plan §Code Patterns row 1.

- (design) The `@theme` block MUST contain exactly the CSS custom properties defined in design-system.md §Surface: desktop-webview Tokens — `--color-{primary,secondary,accent,base,raised-1,raised-2,raised-3,inset,text-primary,text-secondary,text-tertiary,text-muted,feedback-success}`, `--spacing-{micro,xs,sm,md,lg,xl}`, `--radius-{sm,md,lg}`, `--font-{display,body,code}`, `--duration-{fast,standard}`, `--easing-{out,in-out}`. Values LOCKED — no substitution, no Tailwind defaults.

- (design) Color values MUST be NASA Deep Space palette literal hex: `#1A1D24` / `#262A33` / `#2D3139` / `#343A45` / `#0F1117` / `#4A90E2` / `#2C3E7F` / `#8B2E3B` / `#E8EEF7` / `#B4BCCB` / `#7D8697` / `#56606E` / `#17B3A3` per design plan §Color Palette.

  - route#10 "Design tokens bundle — Tailwind v4 @theme NASA palette (colors + spacing + radius + motion tokens) + IBM Plex Sans + JetBrains Mono WOFF2 bundled local CSP-safe"
- **Epoch:** Foundation

Materialize the design system's token registry into the empty webview shell at `pulse-app/ui/`. This chunk lands the FIRST `package.json` for the webview (Tailwind v4 CLI toolchain only — no React/Vite yet, those land at chunk #25), the canonical Tailwind v4 `@theme {...}` block carrying all 26 design tokens (22 from design-system.md §Surface: desktop-webview Tokens + 4 a11y-required additions per a11y-plan §6), the four bundled WOFF2 font weights covering the IBM Plex Sans + JetBrains Mono actively-used roles (per design-system.md §Typography table) with their SIL OFL 1.1 license files in-tree, and the `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` override that zeroes motion-token durations (per a11y-plan §6 + design-system.md §Motion).

- (security/obs) NEVER log raw panic payload bytes via the panic hook — payload strings can carry user-content fragments from instrumented OTLP attributes, span names, error messages; raw `PanicInfo::payload()` downcast result is opaque user data (per security plan §Anti-Patterns Logging rows 1 + 4; obs-plan §11 Anti-Patterns; CLAUDE.md project warnings).

- (security) NEVER expose raw `operation_name` strings (sub-task 4) in self-observation tracing events, error messages, or `AppError::Internal { message }` content — use hashed `operation_key` for log fields (per security plan §Anti-Patterns Logging row 1).

- (security) NEVER add `format!()`-built thresholds, panic messages, or operation names into DuckDB / SQLite query construction paths anywhere chunk touches `crates/triage/src/baseline/` or `crates/triage/src/cue/` — prepared-statement-only discipline (per security plan §Anti-Patterns Input row 2 + CLAUDE.md universal invariants). By-construction guardrail; chunk #73 stays in pure-Rust evaluation paths.

- (tests) NEVER use real time via `std::time::Instant::now()` or `chrono::Utc::now()` in P-001/P-014 timing tests — use `tokio::time::pause()` + `advance()` (per test-plan §11 Universal "NEVER use real time without injection"; introduces flakiness incompatible with §10 zero-flakiness budget).

- (tests) NEVER over-mock at integration level for P-003 panic-propagation test — use real panic injection on real spawned task with real broadcast topic; mocking broadcast channel defeats cross-crate verification (per test-plan §11 Test Strategy + §8 Anti-monkey-patching).

- (tests) NEVER expose panic-payload bytes verbatim in tracing-appender output — P-003 test MUST positively assert panic-payload canary is ABSENT from log file content; failing to assert absence regresses logging vector ban (per test-plan §11 Universal + CLAUDE.md §Critical Warnings).
- (tests) NEVER add retry-once policies or `#[ignore]` markers for timing-sensitive P-001/P-003/P-014 tests — quarantine + root-cause per test-plan §10 zero-flakiness budget.

- (obs) NEVER over-instrument the panic hook itself with span creation — panic context is fragile; hook MUST do minimal work; avoid `#[instrument]` wrapper on the hook closure (per obs-plan §11 Telemetry Strategy + §3 init body sketch).

- (obs) NEVER add a separate broadcast topic for panic / ReceiverPanicked transition — existing `pulse://stream/connection-state` carries variant data (per obs-plan §4 + chunk #73 task brief; arch §Occupied Resources).

- (arch) DO NOT add new TauRPC procedure / new broadcast topic / new env var / new workspace crate name — any addition would require `/andromeda-evolve --allow-arch-registry` ahead of implementation (per arch §Occupied Resources + §Architecture Registry Updates lifecycle).
- (arch) DO NOT route panic-hook signal through an OTLP exporter pointed at own ports — infinite recursion (per arch §Established Decisions [Self-Observation] + CLAUDE.md universal invariants).
- (arch) DO NOT introduce reverse dependency edge — must follow trait-in-lower-crate + impl-in-pulse-app pattern to preserve DAG (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns "Module dependency direction").
**Contract bindings:**

- **security ↔ obs** (panic-hook payload sanitization): panic-hook event emitted by sub-task 2 binds to obs-plan tracing-subscriber JSON output discipline — security mandate is absence of raw payload; obs articulates Vector 2 + §11 schema (no `payload` field; `panic_message` is `Display`-string only, `location` from `info.location()`, `spantrace` from `SpanTrace::capture()`). RECIPROCATED. Both sides agree on safe fields. Implementation MUST verify with negative-canary E2E (parallel to chunk #43 PII negative-canary precedent) — trigger panic with secret-shaped string, assert secret absent from `agent-latest.jsonl`.

- **security ↔ obs** (operation_name field surfacing): `operation_name: Arc<str>` field added in sub-task 4 may surface in obs tracing span fields if any new instrumentation site is added — security mandate is tracing uses hashed `operation_key`, not raw name; obs adds field to per-module allowlist (`triage` row) if cue payload includes `scope_id` / `operation` event field. RECIPROCATED. Obs owns whether/where field surfaces; security gates identifier choice (hashed vs raw).

- **security ↔ tests** (no new CI gate surface): no new IPC / capability / dep / capability JSON entries / `cargo deny check` skip-list / advisory-ignore / `gitleaks` exclusion — existing security-CI-gate posture continues unchanged (per security plan §Bootstrap phases `dep-security-ci-gate`). Tests owns regression assertions for panic-hook payload-redaction discipline (greppable). UNILATERAL (security side declares; tests side delivers via Acceptance criteria, doesn't formally acknowledge as "binding" — but tests has the negative-canary criterion which implements the contract).

- **security ↔ arch** (no §Occupied Resources delta): `ReceiverPanicked` variant reachability does not require new §Occupied Resources entry (existing `pulse://stream/connection-state` registered 2026-05-16). No `--allow-arch-registry` evolve needed. RECIPROCATED with arch §Anti-patterns "DO NOT add new TauRPC procedure / new broadcast topic".

- **obs ↔ tests** (heartbeat tick stall-detection): `>45s gap = stall signal` contract (per obs-plan §3 + §10) consumed by tests harness post-test gap analysis script (`xtask/ci/heartbeat-gap-check.sh` per obs-plan §10 CI gates row 3); P-001 threshold shift (5s→10s IDLE / 30s→60s STALLED) MUST NOT collide with 45s heartbeat stall threshold — independent mechanisms per 2026-05-08 obs Decisions Log. Tests harness asserts both invariants separately. RECIPROCATED.

- **obs ↔ tests** (zero-unlogged-panics invariant): tests CI gate enforces `app.panic.fatal` span detection via `jq` aggregation (per obs-plan §10 CI gates row 2 + §10 Error budget); obs-side P-003 panic hook installation provides emission; tests-side CI script asserts presence on synthetic panic injection AND absence on clean runs. RECIPROCATED.

- **tests ↔ harness 5-command discipline**: P-003 integration test relies on `boot` command's `health` TauRPC returning post-boot subsystem state; existing `boot`/`status`/`cleanup` lifecycle covers chunk #73 (per test-plan §3 5-command + Status endpoint shape). No new harness command introduced. UNILATERAL but conventional (harness already implements; tests consumes).

- **arch ↔ all**: arch enforces self-observation channel (tracing only) + module dependency direction + §Occupied Resources discipline — all other domains' constraints flow through arch's architectural commitments. RECIPROCATED across security/obs/tests bindings above.
**Acceptance criteria contributions:**

- (security) Panic hook in `pulse-app/src/main.rs` registered with `std::panic::set_hook`; grep verifies hook implementation does NOT call `tracing::*!(payload = ...)` or `format!("{}", panic_info.payload())` or equivalent that captures raw payload string. Hook emits fixed-shape event with `subsystem` enum field only.

- (security) `cargo deny check` passes all four categories (advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok) — no-regression check against session-108 clean baseline (per security plan §Bootstrap phases `dep-security-ci-gate`).
- (security) `cargo xtask capability-drift` exits 0 — no new TauRPC procedures, no `pulse-app/capabilities/` JSON edits (per security plan §API Security TauRPC capability authorization).
- (security) `gitleaks` (or equivalent secret-scanner) pre-commit + CI step passes — no new `.env*` / `*.key` / `*.pem` files committed (per security plan §Secret Management).

- (security) Negative test: synthetic panic in any receiver task (gRPC or HTTP server) propagates `ReceiverPanicked` as `reason` field on `pulse://stream/connection-state` AND JSON-line emitted to `~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/agent-latest.jsonl` contains neither raw panic message string nor file path / line number / library version (verifiable via grep — per security plan §Anti-Patterns Logging rows 1 + 4).

- (security) `AttentionCue.scope_id` payloads carrying user-controlled `operation_name` strings do NOT appear in any `tracing::info!` / `warn!` / `error!` macro call site introduced by chunk #73 — verifiable via grep for `operation_name` token inside `crates/triage/src/baseline/` + `crates/triage/src/cue/` (per security plan §Anti-Patterns Logging row 1).

- (arch) All chunk #73 code lives in `crates/ingest/`, `crates/triage/`, or `pulse-app/` — no new workspace crate names; `Cargo.toml` workspace member list unchanged (per arch §Occupied Resources + §Inherited Defaults).
- (arch) No new TauRPC procedure, broadcast topic, env var, or §Occupied Resources entry — `cargo xtask capability-drift` clean without amendment; `connection.current_state` return shape unchanged.

- (arch) Module dependency direction preserved: `cargo tree -p ingest` + `cargo tree -p triage` show zero edges back to `pulse-app` or to each other; panic-hook + ReceiverBindStatus signal flows via trait-in-ingest + impl-in-pulse-app (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns).

- (arch) Self-observation discipline preserved: `grep -rE 'opentelemetry::exporter|opentelemetry_otlp' pulse-app/src/main.rs crates/ingest/src/` returns zero hits for panic hook path (per arch §Established Decisions [Self-Observation]).

- (tests) `cargo nextest run -p ingest` passes new P-001 FSM transition tests (Receiving→Idle at 10s+ silence boundary; Idle→Stalled at 60s+ silence boundary) using `tokio::time::pause()` + `advance()` for deterministic timing.

- (tests) `cargo nextest run -p triage` passes new per-capability unit tests for P-010 (baseline-relative spike at 3×/0.5%, 3×/2%, 3×/5% baselines), P-011 (operation_name round-trip + collision-resistance), P-012 (p99 percentile boundary + 3× regression over 60s persistence), P-014 (max-floor: 10s-p95 clamped to 30s, 300s-p95 preserved at 300s).

- (tests) `cargo nextest run -p pulse-app` passes new P-003 panic-hook integration test injecting synthetic panic in receiver task, asserting `ReceiverPanicked` variant emitted on `pulse://stream/connection-state` within 2 seconds.
- (tests) `! grep "<panic-payload-canary>" $LOG_DIR/*.log` confirms P-003 panic hook does NOT leak raw panic payload to tracing-appender output.
- (tests) `cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --lcov` confirms ≥75% line / ≥70% branch / ≥85% function coverage on new code.

- (tests) `cargo fmt --check` + `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` + `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` standard gate baseline passes (per test-plan §12 Decisions Log 2026-05-10).
- (tests) Zero new `#[ignore]` markers and zero quarantined-without-issue tests introduced; zero-flakiness budget honored (per test-plan §10).

- (obs) Panic hook installed in `pulse-app/src/main.rs` boot sequence AFTER `tracing-subscriber` registry init, emits `tracing::error!(target: "app.panic.fatal", ...)` with fields `panic_message` (Display-string only), `location` (from `info.location()`), `spantrace` (`SpanTrace::capture()`) — verified by synthetic panic injection and JSON log line schema assertion (per obs-plan §3 init body sketch + §7).

- (obs) Panic hook negative-canary E2E: panic with secret-shaped string (e.g., `Bearer eyJhbGc...40chars`) in payload — assert grep of `agent-latest.jsonl` for secret pattern returns empty; only `Display`-formatted summary, `Location`, and SpanTrace appear (per obs-plan §8 PII default-deny + chunk #73 task brief).

- (obs) P-001 threshold change preserves heartbeat tick invariant: post-test heartbeat-gap script returns clean (≤45000ms gap between consecutive ticks) across FSM threshold shift; connection-state transition emission cadence unaffected (per obs-plan §10 CI gates row 3 + §3 Heartbeat ticks).

- (obs) P-010/P-011/P-012/P-014 cue evaluator rewrites preserve `metric.triage.*` `tracing::info!` event shape (target prefix + numeric `value` field + bounded label set including new `operation_name` field added to triage module allowlist); negative-cardinality check confirms no per-service-name explosion in tick-cadence emissions (per obs-plan §5 + §8).

Phase 4 plan must enforce both sides — tests' negative-canary criterion is the operational realization of security's "NEVER log raw" rule.

title: Phase 70 Plan — chunk route#73: "Capability spec numeric alignment"

data.head: # Phase 70 Plan — chunk route#73: "Capability spec numeric alignment"

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase Phase 4. Read by /andromeda-implement.
Manual edits between runs are fine; do not edit during /implement run._
- **Phase number:** 70

- **Route chunks covered:**
  - route#73 "Capability spec numeric alignment — fix P-001/P-003 thresholds + failure path, P-010/P-011/P-012/P-014 baseline-relative semantics (capabilities P-001/P-003/P-010/P-011/P-012/P-014; detail in pulse-v0_2_0-route §73)"
- **Epoch:** Foundation v0.2.0 (LAST chunk in epoch and route — closes Consolidation Phase 6 audit Section 1.D capability-PARTIAL HIGH findings)

Close six capability-spec drift findings against the chunks #59 / #61 / #62 / #66 / #70 implementations by aligning their numeric thresholds, identity preservation, and failure-path reachability with `docs/v0_2_0/pulse-capability-spec.md` text. Two of the six sub-tasks (P-001 thresholds + P-014 floor) are straightforward constant bumps; one (P-011 operation identity) is a backend data-shape extension preserving the operation_name `Arc<str>` through the per-operation baseline → snapshot → cue.scope_id path. Two more (P-010 + P-012 baseline-relative semantics) require interpretive choice about what "baseline" means against the current single-EWMA / single-t-digest tracker shape — research.md flags this as an Open Question for /implement Phase 2 to resolve. The sixth (P-003 panic propagation) extends the EXISTING `pulse-app/src/observability.rs::install_panic_hook` to (a) harden the captured-payload form per security plan §Anti-Patterns Logging row 1 + obs-plan §7 + (b) signal a shared atomic that propagates through the chunks #59 / 2026-05-16 `ReceiverBindStatus` trait so `derive_reason` can route to the already-defined-but-unreachable `ReceiverPanicked` variant.

Zero arch-registry delta: chunk introduces zero new TauRPC procedures, zero new broadcast topics, zero new env vars, zero new workspace crates. The `ReceiverPanicked` reason variant is ALREADY defined at `crates/ingest/src/connection.rs:79-83`; the `pulse://stream/connection-state` topic was registered 2026-05-16 (chunk #59). Chunk #73 fills the reachability gap rather than adding new surface area.

Implementation discipline per the 2026-05-16 trait-in-lower-crate + adapter-in-pulse-app + 2026-05-18 free-fn map_err patterns + 2026-05-17 session 84 AllowList aggregate-only convention: panic-signal flows via `ReceiverBindStatus` trait extension (defined in `crates/ingest`, adapter in `pulse-app/src/connection_router.rs`); no reverse-dep edges introduced; operation_name added to baseline/snapshot data shapes does NOT surface in any triage tracing emission (broadcast surface only).

1. **P-001 thresholds** — update connection FSM threshold constants:
   - `crates/ingest/src/connection.rs:39` change `pub const IDLE_THRESHOLD_NANOS: i64 = 5_000_000_000;` → `10_000_000_000;`
   - `crates/ingest/src/connection.rs:44` change `pub const STALLED_THRESHOLD_NANOS: i64 = 30_000_000_000;` → `60_000_000_000;`
   - Update docstrings at lines 38 ("5 seconds" → "10 seconds") and 41-43 (current rationale about being "proactively below the 45s heartbeat-gap CI alarm" becomes false post-bump; new rationale per capability spec P-001 "Stalled (>60s quiet, suspect)"; note independence from 45s heartbeat-gap CI alarm which now fires BEFORE FSM Stalled — the two are orthogonal mechanisms per 2026-05-08 obs Decisions Log)
   - Verify existing FSM tests at lines 386-432 still pass with new boundaries: `compute_state_age_at_idle_threshold_boundary_returns_idle` (uses the const), `compute_state_age_between_idle_and_stalled_returns_idle` (hardcoded 10s lands AT new IDLE_THRESHOLD → returns Idle per `age < STALLED_THRESHOLD`), `compute_state_age_at_stalled_threshold_returns_stalled` (uses the const), `compute_state_age_past_stalled_returns_stalled` (hardcoded 60s = new STALLED_THRESHOLD boundary → returns Stalled per `age >= STALLED_THRESHOLD`).

2. **P-003 panic propagation** — extend EXISTING panic hook + ReceiverBindStatus trait:
   - **Harden existing hook payload capture** at `pulse-app/src/observability.rs:1647-1666`: replace the downcast block (lines 1653-1658) with `panic_message = %info` using PanicInfo's Display impl (per obs-plan §7 + security plan §Anti-Patterns Logging row 1 — Display form is "panicked at 'msg', file:line" without exposing raw downcasted payload). Preserve `location` (file:line per `info.location()`) and `spantrace` (`SpanTrace::capture()`) fields.
   - **Add panic-signal atomic** at module level of `pulse-app/src/observability.rs`: `static PANIC_SIGNAL: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);` + `pub fn panic_signaled() -> bool { PANIC_SIGNAL.load(Ordering::Relaxed) }` accessor + `pub(crate) fn reset_panic_signal_for_tests()` reset method. Modify `install_panic_hook` body to `PANIC_SIGNAL.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);` before the tracing emission. Preserve prior-hook chaining via `let prev = std::panic::take_hook(); std::panic::set_hook(Box::new(move |info| { PANIC_SIGNAL.store(true, ...); /* emit */; prev(info); }));` so any existing tracing-error / Tauri / future hook compositions are preserved (per security plan §Error Handling internal-logging guidance).
   - **Extend ReceiverBindStatus trait** at `crates/ingest/src/connection.rs:160-164` with `fn panic_signaled(&self) -> bool { false }` (default impl provides backward compatibility for any out-of-tree impls).
   - **Update HeartbeatBindStatus adapter** at `pulse-app/src/connection_router.rs:28-43` to implement `panic_signaled` by calling `pulse_app::observability::panic_signaled()`. Update the existing 4 unit tests at lines 130-189 (Stub impls + tests) — Stub gains a `panic` AtomicBool field for parametric panic-signal control.
   - **Update compute_state signature** at `crates/ingest/src/connection.rs:172-191` to accept an additional `receiver_panicked: bool` parameter; precedence ordering: `if any_receiver_failed || receiver_panicked { return ConnectionState::ReceiverFailed; }`. Adjust all 8 existing call sites (mainly in tests + `start_poller`).
   - **Rewrite derive_reason** at `crates/ingest/src/connection.rs:264-282` to accept `receiver_panicked: bool` AND `any_receiver_failed: bool`; precedence: panic → `ReceiverPanicked`; bind failed → `BindFailed`; else `StaleHeartbeat`. Comment block on the unreachable StaleHeartbeat path can be removed (now reachable via stale-heartbeat path that may be added later) or trimmed.
   - **Update start_poller** at `crates/ingest/src/connection.rs:238-262` to read both `bind_status.any_receiver_failed()` AND `bind_status.panic_signaled()` per tick; pass both flags to `compute_state` + `derive_reason`.
   - The `app.panic.fatal` event continues firing via the existing `tracing::error!` call — no AllowList edit required (target already registered).

3. **P-010 baseline-relative error rate (DESIGN-AMBIGUOUS — see Open Questions)** — rewrite `crates/triage/src/cue/evaluate.rs:30-64`:
   - **Recommended Path A' (lighter scope; reuse existing tracker):** read per-service EWMA value via `state.error_rate(snapshot.service_name)` accessor as the "baseline" reference; compare snapshot's currently-observed rate (from a SHORT WINDOW periodic re-capture mechanism added to BaselineState — e.g., a `last_n_observations_rate` field on `ServiceBaseline` populated by a sliding-window observer) against the long-term EWMA. The denominator-zero / nan-safe magnitude formula `(short / long).is_finite()` with explicit `if long > 0.0` guard.
   - **Alternative Path A (full spec implementation; larger scope):** add a second `EwmaTracker` per service with shorter alpha (≈30s effective window). Snapshot exposes BOTH `short_term_error_rate` and `long_term_error_rate`; evaluate.rs compares them with the 3.0× multiplier.
   - For EITHER path: replace `persistence_seconds = snapshot.samples` (sample-count units) at line 45 with wall-clock derivation from `(now_nanos - first_observed_nanos) / NANOS_PER_SEC` — requires plumbing a `first_observed_nanos` field through ServiceBaseline → ServiceMetricSnapshot.
   - For EITHER path: remove the `thresholds.base_error_rate` fixed-denominator semantic; the const becomes obsolete (mark as `#[deprecated]` or remove + update Default impl). `Thresholds` struct's `base_error_rate` field stays for backward compat OR is dropped — design choice deferred to /implement.
   - **/implement Phase 2 must pick A or A' explicitly + surface choice to user at Phase 6.**

4. **P-011 operation identity preservation** — add `operation_name: Arc<str>` field to baseline tracker + snapshot:
   - `crates/triage/src/baseline/mod.rs:113-116` extend `struct OperationBaseline` with `pub(crate) operation_name: Arc<str>`; add `use std::sync::Arc;` import.
   - Modify `observe_span` at line 229+ to seed `operation_name` on first creation via `entry().or_insert_with(|| OperationBaseline { latency_tdigest: TDigestPair::default(), operation_name: Arc::from(operation_name) })`. Use `Arc::from(operation_name)` to share allocation across snapshots.
   - `crates/triage/src/baseline/mod.rs:399-408` extend `struct OperationMetricSnapshot` with `pub operation_name: Arc<str>` field.
   - Modify `iter_operations` at lines 369-385 to clone the Arc into the snapshot: `operation_name: Arc::clone(&entry.operation_name)`.
   - `crates/triage/src/cue/evaluate.rs:91` change `scope_id: Some(snapshot.operation_key)` → `scope_id: Some(snapshot.operation_name.to_string())` so AttentionCue carries human-readable name not hashed key.
   - **CRITICAL** (per 2026-05-17 session 84 observability.md): operation_name MUST NOT be added to any AllowList per-target field set in `pulse-app/src/observability.rs::AllowList::production` — the triage/cue/baseline tracing convention is aggregate-only. AttentionCue is broadcast surface (cross-process to webview); tracing events stay aggregate. Verify by grepping any new `tracing::info!` / `warn!` / `error!` macro call sites in `crates/triage/src/baseline/` + `crates/triage/src/cue/` for the `operation_name` token — should return zero hits.

Known pitfalls discovered in research:

- **Hardening the panic hook FIRST without adding the atomic signal causes a regression** where panics no longer expose the full payload but ReceiverPanicked is still unreachable. The two changes are intentionally bundled in sub-task 2.
- **Don't add `panic_signaled` as a NEW trait method without a default impl** — would break any out-of-tree impls if they exist. The default-impl approach is backward-compatible.
- **Don't add operation_name to AllowList for any triage tracing target** — would silently violate the aggregate-only convention. Verify by grepping new tracing macro call sites after sub-task 4.

- **The static `PANIC_SIGNAL: AtomicBool` is per-process global state** — tests resetting it must use `observability::reset_panic_signal_for_tests()`. Concurrent tests running in the same process could see panic signals from sibling tests; mitigate via nextest's per-process isolation (default) OR by serial-only test grouping if `start_paused` shared state surfaces. Per test-plan §3 cargo-nextest provides per-process isolation by default — should be fine.

- **`%info` field format** captures PanicInfo's Display impl which prints `panicked at 'msg', file:line` — the `'msg'` portion IS the panic message but flows through Display formatting which is the canonical "safe" form per Rust convention (vs raw payload downcast which exposes literal `panic!()` argument).

- **The 45s heartbeat-CI-alarm and 60s STALLED threshold are now in REVERSE precedence vs the pre-bump 45s alarm > 30s STALLED ordering** — after bump, the CI alarm fires BEFORE the FSM transitions to Stalled. This is acceptable because they measure different things (ticks vs OTLP spans); the docstring rewrite at sub-task 1 documents this independence explicitly so future readers don't re-derive the coupling.

1. **Design ambiguity — sub-task 3 (P-010 baseline-relative semantics)**: capability spec P-010 says "short-term (30-second window) error rate exceeds its baseline by factor of 3.0 or more". Current `ServiceMetricSnapshot.error_rate` IS the EWMA baseline (5-min window per chunk #61). There is no separate short-term tracker. To implement the spec correctly requires EITHER (a) add a second EWMA tracker per service with shorter window (e.g., 30s alpha) — non-trivial baseline-state extension; OR (b) interpret the existing snapshot.error_rate as "current" and compare against `BaselineState::error_rate(service_name)` accessor result captured at sample-start (would be self-referential — they're the same value at the same time). Path (a) is the spec-correct path but extends baseline tracker. Path (b) requires "baseline" to mean something different than "current EWMA". /implement Phase 2 must resolve which path; surface to user at Phase 6 review.

2. **Design ambiguity — sub-task 5 (P-012 per-operation t-digest p99 read)**: spec says "current p99 latency for an operation exceeds baseline p99 by factor of 2.5 or more". Current `OperationMetricSnapshot.latency_at_percentile` is the t-digest at the percentile parameter — same value at all sample times for a stable distribution; the "baseline" vs "current" comparison again requires distinguishing short-term vs long-term distributions. Same path A/B dilemma as sub-task 3. Recommend Path (b) for both: reinterpret threshold semantics from "absolute" to "relative against rolling reference window" with the reference window snapshot being captured periodically rather than via a separate tracker.

3. **MIN_QUIET_SECONDS placement**: const in thresholds.rs (hard floor; not user-configurable) vs field on `Thresholds` struct (configurable, hot-reload-able per chunk #86 future scope). Recommend const for chunk #73 (matches "compile-time constants" security extract guidance); upgrade to field if a user-need surfaces.

4. **Panic-atomic placement**: module-level `static AtomicBool` in observability.rs (simplest; tests can reset via `pub(crate) fn reset_panic_signal()`) vs `Arc<AtomicBool>` threaded explicitly through boot wiring (more testable; matches Arc-based dependency injection precedent of `HeartbeatState`). Recommend module-level static + `pub(crate) fn reset_panic_signal()` for tests — minimal API surface change; integration test still works via the public `panic_signaled()` accessor.

5. **`compute_state` signature change for panic signal**: currently takes `any_receiver_failed: bool`. After sub-task 2, derive_reason needs to distinguish bind-failed vs panic. Options: (a) extend signature to `compute_state(last, now, any_receiver_failed: bool, receiver_panicked: bool)` — clean separation; (b) merge into trait read with `compute_state(last, now, bind_status: &dyn ReceiverBindStatus)` — coupling to trait; (c) compute the failure category higher up (start_poller) and pass the reason directly. Recommend (a) — preserves pure-function purity of compute_state for testability; start_poller reads both flags and passes.

6. **Threshold-bump test impact**: chunk #50's `pulse-app/tests/perf_slo_10k_spans.rs` may have implicit timing assumptions about IDLE/STALLED transitions — needs verification. The boundary tests in `crates/ingest/src/connection.rs::tests::compute_state_age_at_idle_threshold_boundary_returns_idle` + `compute_state_age_between_idle_and_stalled_returns_idle` (using hardcoded 10_000_000_000 and 60_000_000_000) should be reviewed after the constant change — the test at line 395 (10s = new IDLE_THRESHOLD boundary) still returns Idle correctly; the test at line 409 (60s past = new STALLED_THRESHOLD boundary) still returns Stalled. No test rewrites needed if hardcoded values happen to land on the right side of new boundaries.

data.head: ### Step 3 — Extend `corpus::CorpusWriter` trait with incident-shaped methods

body: Edit `crates/corpus/src/contract.rs::CorpusWriter` trait to add:
- `fn save_incident(&self, id: &str, workspace: &str, status: &str, created_at: i64, updated_at: i64, resolved_at: Option<i64>, read_at: Option<i64>, payload: &[u8]) -> Result<(), Error>`
- `fn update_incident_status(&self, id: &str, new_status: &str, updated_at: i64, acknowledged_at: Option<i64>, resolved_at: Option<i64>) -> Result<(), Error>`
- `fn mark_incident_read(&self, id: &str, read_at: i64) -> Result<(), Error>`
- `fn load_active_incidents(&self, workspace: &str) -> Result<Vec<IncidentRowRaw>, Error>` — returns raw column data + encrypted payload; adapter at binary boundary decrypts + bincode-deserializes.
- `fn count_active_unread(&self, workspace: &str) -> Result<u64, Error>` — P-045 counter SQL `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incidents WHERE workspace = ?1 AND read_unix_nano IS NULL AND status = 'active'`.
- `fn save_incident_event(&self, incident_id: &str, event_kind: &str, occurred_at: i64, payload: &[u8]) -> Result<(), Error>`.

Add `pub struct IncidentRowRaw { id: String, workspace: String, status: String, created_at: i64, updated_at: i64, resolved_at: Option<i64>, read_at: Option<i64>, payload: Vec<u8> }` (decrypted plaintext payload) parallel to existing `ServiceRegistryRowRaw`.

Impl `CorpusWriter` methods on `Corpus`: each uses prepared statements + `?N` placeholders + `cell_encrypt(self.key(), payload)?` for BLOB writes + `cell_decrypt(self.key(), &encrypted)?` for BLOB reads. Status column is plaintext TEXT (queryable index for the counter SQL); payload BLOB carries serialized `Incident` struct (bincode encoding).
`CorpusIncidentPersistence` struct wrapping `Arc<dyn corpus::CorpusWriter>`. Implements `triage::incident::IncidentPersistence` trait:
- `save_incident(...)` — serialize `Incident` via `bincode::serialize(&incident)?` → call `CorpusWriter::save_incident(...)`.
- `update_incident_status(...)` / `mark_incident_read(...)` — direct trait passthrough.
- `load_active_incidents(workspace)` — call `CorpusWriter::load_active_incidents(...)` → iterate raw rows → `bincode::deserialize::<Incident>(&row.payload)?` per row → return `Vec<Incident>`.
- `count_active_unread(workspace)` — direct trait passthrough.
- `save_incident_event(...)` — serialize event payload via bincode → call `CorpusWriter::save_incident_event(...)`.

Free function `corpus_error_to_incident_error(err: corpus::Error) -> IncidentError` at file scope (orphan rule; mirrors chunk #68 `corpus_error_to_app_error` shape + chunk #70/#71 free-fn map_err pattern).

Plus `run_incident_persist_loop(...)` async function periodically (60s) running `run_incident_persist_cycle` from `triage::incident::persistence`; spawned at boot in `pulse-app/src/main.rs`. Pre-scrub discipline: incident `title` / `detail` / `evidence_refs.fingerprint_hashes` content MUST be pre-scrubbed by the producer (cue emitter / interpretation layer; chunks #62/#83) per chunk #72 uniform PII coverage; this adapter does NOT double-scrub.

`AutoResolveObserver` struct holding `Arc<dyn IncidentRegistry>` + `Arc<IncidentLifecycleBroadcast>` + `Arc<dyn IncidentPersistence>`. Single `run_auto_resolution_loop()` async function with `tokio::time::interval(Duration::from_secs(30))` tick cadence (every 30s evaluates Active incidents for 120s no-reemission window; chunk-decision Q2 from research.md). Per tick:
1. `let now = current_unix_nanos();`
2. `let to_resolve = registry.evaluate_auto_resolution(now);` (returns `Vec<incident_id>`).

3. For each id: `registry.mark_resolved(id, now)?;` then `persistence.update_incident_status(id, IncidentStatus::Resolved, now, None, Some(now))?;` then emit `IncidentLifecycleEvent { from_state: Active, to_state: Resolved, ... }` on broadcast.
4. Emit aggregate tick event: `tracing::info!(target: "triage.incident.auto_resolve.tick", evaluated_count, resolved_count, duration_ms)`.
NEVER hold a `tracing::Span` guard across `.await` in the loop without `.in_current_span()` (per obs-plan §11 Spans/Traces row 4 + CLAUDE.md 2026-05-17 entry).
`IncidentsApi` trait + `IncidentsApiImpl` resolver following exactly the `services_router.rs` shape:

`IncidentsApiImpl::new(registry: Arc<dyn IncidentRegistry>, broadcast: Arc<IncidentLifecycleBroadcast>, persistence: Arc<dyn IncidentPersistence>, workspace_root: String)` constructor (workspace_root is resolved-once at boot from workspace-detector; do NOT re-resolve per-request to avoid CWE-22 surface).
Resolver methods:

- `list_active()` — call `registry.list_active(&self.workspace_root)` (in-memory hot path); fall through to `persistence.load_active_incidents(&self.workspace_root)?` for cold-start / restart recovery. Map to `IncidentsListPayload { items: Vec<IncidentRecord>, total, next_cursor: None }`. Emit `tracing::info!(target: "incidents.list_active.request", item_count, "incidents.list_active returned")`.

- `acknowledge(id)` — `registry.acknowledge(&id, now)?;` → on `IncidentRegistryError::NotFound` map to `AppError::NotFound { resource: "incident" }` (per security plan §Error Handling); on `IncidentRegistryError::CooldownActive { remaining_secs }` emit `tracing::warn!(target: "incidents.acknowledge.cooldown_rejected", cooldown_remaining_ms = remaining_secs * 1000, "ack rejected during cool-down")` + return `AppError::Validation { field: "id", reason: "cool-down active" }` (sanitized; no incident kind/scope leaked in error message). On success: `persistence.update_incident_status(...)?;` + emit `IncidentLifecycleEvent { to_state: Acknowledged, ... }` on broadcast.
- `mark_resolved(id)` — similar shape; `registry.mark_resolved(&id, now)?;` → `persistence.update_incident_status(...)?;` → broadcast emission. NotFound mapping identical к `acknowledge`.

New serde-friendly `IncidentRecord` envelope at file scope (NOT а re-export of `triage::Incident` because the resolver should expose а narrower view; webview consumer doesn't need raw `evidence_refs.trace_id` byte arrays — string-format at emission site). Fields: `id: String, workspace: String, kind: CueKind, scope: CueScope, status: IncidentStatus, severity: Severity, priority_tier: PriorityTier, opened_at_unix_nano: i64, acknowledged_at_unix_nano: Option<i64>, resolved_at_unix_nano: Option<i64>, read_at_unix_nano: Option<i64>, evidence_count: usize` (count NOT raw refs).
Plus `#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq, specta::Type)]` derives for `IncidentRecord` + `IncidentsListPayload`.
All 3 resolver methods wrapped with `#[tracing::instrument(skip_all, fields(... = tracing::field::Empty))]` per obs-plan §4 + chunk #67 services-router precedent.
In the setup closure:

1. Derive incident-write trait view from the existing `Arc<Corpus>` intermediate: `let incident_writer: Arc<dyn CorpusWriter> = Arc::clone(&arc_corpus) as Arc<dyn CorpusWriter>;` (already exists from chunk #69/#71; chunk #78 reuses).
2. Construct `let incident_persistence: Arc<dyn IncidentPersistence> = Arc::new(CorpusIncidentPersistence::new(Arc::clone(&incident_writer)));`.

3. Cold-restore on boot: `let restored_incidents = incident_persistence.load_active_incidents(&workspace_root).unwrap_or_else(|_| Vec::new());` (degraded non-fatal per chunk #70 baseline boot precedent; tracing::warn!(target: "triage.incident.persist.error.boot_restore", error_category, ...)).
4. `let incident_registry: Arc<dyn IncidentRegistry> = Arc::new(InMemoryIncidentRegistry::from_persisted(restored_incidents));` (registry hydrated from corpus).
5. `let incident_broadcast = Arc::new(IncidentLifecycleBroadcast::new());`.
6. Construct `let incidents_impl = IncidentsApiImpl::new(Arc::clone(&incident_registry), Arc::clone(&incident_broadcast), Arc::clone(&incident_persistence), workspace_root.clone());`.
7. Add `.merge(incidents_impl.clone().into_handler())` к the TauRPC Router builder chain.
8. Spawn `tokio::spawn(run_incident_persist_loop(Arc::clone(&incident_registry), Arc::clone(&incident_persistence)));` for 60s cadence.
9. Spawn `tokio::spawn(AutoResolveObserver::new(...).run_auto_resolution_loop());` for 30s cadence.
10. Wire broadcast emission to Tauri Channel via the existing event-emitter pattern at the `pulse://stream/incidents` topic (mirrors chunk #67 service-lifecycle wiring).

**Relevance:** Workspace placement in existing `triage` + `buffer` crates; DuckDB SQL discipline; module dependency direction; no new IPC/broadcast/env-var surface.
**Constraints:**

- L0 ring buffer is DuckDB 1.5.x in-memory via `duckdb` crate 1.10500.x — Q1-Q7 templates execute against the `pulse_buffer` in-memory `:memory:` connection with reserved tables `spans`, `span_events`, `span_links`, `metrics_points`, `log_records`, `resources`, `instrumentation_scopes`, `log_templates` (per arch §Occupied Resources DuckDB database / schema names).

- Code lives in existing workspace crates `crates/triage/` (SQL templates module under `baseline/`) + `crates/buffer/` (query execution helpers if needed) — both reserved workspace member names; no new crate introduced.

- Module dependency direction: `triage` is a leaf crate (consumes `buffer` reads, never the inverse); deps flow TOWARD `pulse-app` binary, never sibling-to-sibling unless declared contract requires it.
- Timestamp columns are `TIMESTAMPTZ` (microsecond, UTC) with sibling `ts_unix_nano BIGINT` where nanosecond precision required; query predicates honor these forms.
- Ring-buffer cutoff is enforced via periodic `DELETE FROM <table> WHERE ts < now() - INTERVAL '<retention> minutes'` task; Q1-Q7 queries MUST tolerate missing/aged-out rows without panic.
- No new arch-level resource: no new TauRPC namespace, no new broadcast topic, no new env var, no new capability identifier, no new filesystem subpath, no new DuckDB table.
**Patterns к follow:**
- Prepared-statement query pattern with `?` placeholders + `Statement::execute([&param])` — established by `viz` crate query routers, reused by corpus reader implementations.
- Library-crate shape: public contract module is only `pub` surface, `pub(crate)` internals, `thiserror`-derived error enum.

- Synchronous query API exposed by helper, async orchestration owned higher up: `crates/buffer/` query execution helpers stay synchronous against DuckDB; the cadence scheduler (chunk #80) wraps invocation in tokio scheduling.
- Feature flag hygiene: any new optional capability gates kebab-case Cargo feature; chunk #79 introduces no new flags.
**Anti-patterns к avoid:**
- NEVER format-string SQL — DuckDB queries MUST use prepared statements with `?` placeholders.
- Do NOT introduce reverse sibling-crate dep edge (e.g., `buffer` depending on `triage`, or `triage` depending on `viz`).
- Do NOT introduce a new DuckDB table or rename a reserved one — new tables require `/andromeda-evolve --allow-arch-registry`.
- Do NOT silently change retention assumptions — Q7's bounds are guards against retention evicting mid-query.
**Acceptance criteria contributions:**
- (arch) SQL templates module + query execution helpers live in existing `crates/triage/` and `crates/buffer/`; no new workspace member added.
- (arch) All Q1-Q7 DuckDB queries use `Connection::prepare` + `?` placeholders + `Statement::execute([&param])`; `grep -rE 'format!\("SELECT' crates/triage crates/buffer` returns zero matches.

- (arch) No new arch-registry surface: zero new TauRPC procedures, zero new `pulse://stream/...` topics, zero new env vars, zero new capability identifiers, zero new DuckDB tables — verified by `cargo xtask capability-drift` clean.

- (obs) NEVER hold `tracing::Span` guards across cadence `tokio::time::interval` `.await` points without `.in_current_span()` — bleeds tick span context into next-tick task (per obs-plan §11 Spans row 4 tokio-context-bleed). Each tick MUST construct a fresh span.

- (arch) Do NOT log raw L1a query payloads / digest contents / inference-prompt bodies / cue evidence strings via `tracing` events from the coordinator — only log structured fields like `tier` / `query_name` / `cadence_mode` / `duration_ms` (per arch §Cross-cutting "Self-observation discipline").

- **security ↔ tests**: chunk #80's tier-coverage tests MUST also verify the SQL parameter-binding contract (no format-string interpolation) and the broadcast payload redaction contract (no raw attribute values in `pulse://stream/cadence-events`).

data.head: # Phase 77 Plan — chunks route#80: "Cadence coordinator + three-tier triggering"

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase Phase 4. Read by /andromeda-implement.
Manual edits between runs are fine; do not edit during /implement run._
- **Phase number:** 77

- **Route chunks covered:**
  - route#80 "Cadence coordinator + three-tier triggering — orchestrate L1a SQL queries per attention cue priority tier (capabilities P-052/P-060; detail in pulse-v0_2_0-route §80)"
- **Epoch:** Epoch 9 — Foundation v0.2.0

Chunk #80 introduces the **Cadence Coordinator** — а new sibling submodule `crates/triage/cadence` that orchestrates L1a SQL query execution + L3 digest assembly + L4 inference invocation per attention cue priority tier (per pulse-distillation-architecture.md §Cadence and Event Triggers). The coordinator runs three independent schedulers (Tier-1 immediate / Tier-2 accelerated 20s / Tier-3 baseline 60s) plus a reflection-mode 1800s deeper-analysis tick. Tier-2 acceleration is conditionally disabled when the hardware profile is `cpu-primary` (a forward-binding hook ready for chunk #82). Cadence values load from a new `[triage.cadence]` config section persisted via Settings; safety floors (baseline ≥ 5s, reflection ≥ 5min) reject out-of-range values per security plan §Input Validation row 6.

A new broadcast topic `pulse://stream/cadence-events` carries L6 visibility events (which tier fired, which query batch ran, when) for future consumer chunks; no TauRPC procedure is introduced this chunk (capability-drift gate stays clean). The coordinator consumes existing chunk #79 `TriageSqlState` (Q1-Q7 SQL templates) via `Arc<dyn Trait>` dep-injection at the binary boundary AND subscribes к both the chunk #62 `CadenceTriggerChannel` (Suggested cues per chunk #62 routing) and the `AttentionCueBroadcast` (filtered for `Autonomous` priority — Tier-1 hard-signal path) per the design decision in §Implementation Steps below. A new metric event `metric.pipeline.l3.digests_assembled_total{mode}` with а bounded 4-value mode label (`tier1|tier2|tier3|reflection`) registers per L3 digest assembly via the obs-plan §5 metric emission convention.

This chunk preserves arch §Cross-cutting Patterns "Module dependency direction" (the `triage` crate stays sibling-dep-free; cross-crate state delivery via trait-in-lower-crate + impl-in-pulse-app per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-16 + 2026-05-19 session learnings), arch §Established Decisions "Self-Observation" (tracing-only, never own-OTLP-dial), and the chunk #62/#63/#64/#67/#78 sibling-submodule precedent (per-leaf observability allowlist + PII-discipline + heartbeat-tick convention). The new broadcast topic registers in arch §Occupied Resources via а follow-on `/andromeda-evolve --allow-arch-registry` amendment after this chunk's implementation lands.
**a.** Create `crates/triage/src/cadence/mod.rs` with:
- Module-level doc header citing capabilities P-052 (Cadence Configuration) + P-060 (Tiered Triggering Priority); reference pulse-v0_2_0-route §80.
- `mod broadcast;`, `mod config;`, `mod coordinator;` private submodule declarations.

- `pub use` re-exports of submodule public surface: `CadenceConfig`, `CadenceConfigError`, `CadenceCoordinator`, `CadenceEvent`, `CadenceEventBroadcast`, `CadenceMode`, `STREAM_NAME_CADENCE_EVENTS`, `start_cadence_coordinator`, `run_one_coordinator_cycle`, `CoordinatorCycleStats`, plus safety-floor const + default-value consts (`CADENCE_BASELINE_SECONDS_MIN`, `CADENCE_REFLECTION_SECONDS_MIN`, `DEFAULT_CADENCE_BASELINE_SECONDS = 60`, `DEFAULT_CADENCE_ACCELERATED_SECONDS = 20`, `DEFAULT_CADENCE_REFLECTION_SECONDS = 1800`).

- `pub(crate) const` declarations for tracing-target constants: `TARGET_CADENCE_TICK = "cadence.tick"`, `TARGET_CADENCE_TRIGGER = "cadence.trigger"`, `TARGET_CADENCE_CONFIG_LOAD = "cadence.config.load"`, `TARGET_CADENCE_CONFIG_SAFETY_FLOOR = "cadence.config.safety_floor"`, `TARGET_METRIC_PIPELINE_L3_DIGESTS_ASSEMBLED_TOTAL = "metric.pipeline.l3.digests_assembled_total"`. Match the chunk #62 cue `mod.rs` shape (per research.md "Conventions to follow").
**b.** Create `crates/triage/src/cadence/broadcast.rs` mirroring `crates/triage/src/cue/broadcast.rs:1-163`:
- `pub const STREAM_NAME_CADENCE_EVENTS: &str = "pulse://stream/cadence-events"`.
- `pub const BROADCAST_CAPACITY: usize = 32` (per cue broadcast precedent).

- `pub struct CadenceEvent` (`serde::Serialize + Clone + PartialEq`) with payload fields per security plan §Logging & Monitoring "What NEVER to log": `mode: CadenceMode`, `mode_label: &'static str` (bounded enum-label), `scheduled_at_unix_nano: i64`, `executed_at_unix_nano: i64`, `cue_kind_label: Option<&'static str>` (bounded; `None` for baseline tick), `cue_priority_label: Option<&'static str>` (bounded), `queries_executed: u32`, `queries_succeeded: u32`. NO `scope_id` / `service` / raw OTLP attribute strings.

- `pub struct CadenceEventBroadcast` thin wrapper over `tokio::sync::broadcast::Sender<CadenceEvent>` mirroring `AttentionCueBroadcast` shape: `new()` / `sender()` / `subscribe()` / `subscriber_count()` + `Default` impl + `Debug + Clone` derives.

- Colocated `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` covering: starts-zero-subscribers, subscribe-increments, round-trip-payload, send-without-subscribers-is-benign, stream-name-matches-pulse-uri-convention, payload-omits-pii-fields negative-canary (assert `CadenceEvent` field-list does NOT contain any `String` field). Mirror the 7-test chunk #62 broadcast tests pattern.
**c.** Create `crates/triage/src/cadence/config.rs`:

- `pub struct CadenceConfig { pub baseline_seconds: u32, pub accelerated_seconds: u32, pub reflection_seconds: u32, pub tier2_acceleration_enabled: bool }` (`serde::Deserialize + serde::Serialize + Debug + Clone + PartialEq + Eq`).

- `pub enum CadenceConfigError` via `thiserror::Error`: `BaselineBelowFloor { requested: u32 }`, `AcceleratedBelowFloor { requested: u32 }`, `ReflectionBelowFloor { requested: u32 }`. Diagnostic messages cite the safety-floor values.
- `pub const CADENCE_BASELINE_SECONDS_MIN: u32 = 5`, `CADENCE_ACCELERATED_SECONDS_MIN: u32 = 1`, `CADENCE_REFLECTION_SECONDS_MIN: u32 = 300` (per arch extract + pulse-v0_2_0-route §80 safety floor).
- `pub const DEFAULT_CADENCE_BASELINE_SECONDS: u32 = 60`, `DEFAULT_CADENCE_ACCELERATED_SECONDS: u32 = 20`, `DEFAULT_CADENCE_REFLECTION_SECONDS: u32 = 1800`.
- `impl CadenceConfig::try_new(baseline, accelerated, reflection, tier2_enabled) -> Result<Self, CadenceConfigError>` enforcing safety floors; reject + return Err for out-of-range.
- `impl Default for CadenceConfig` returning the documented defaults.

- Colocated `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` (use `proptest` 1.10.0 already in dev-dependencies):
  - Property-based safety-floor invariant test (`proptest!` macro): for any random `(u32, u32, u32, bool)` quadruple, `CadenceConfig::try_new(...)` either returns `Ok` with all fields in `[MIN, u32::MAX]` ranges OR returns the appropriate `Err` variant naming the violating field.
  - 3 explicit edge-case tests (boundary at exactly MIN / MIN-1 / MIN+1 per field).
  - 1 default-values-pass-validation test.
**d.** Create `crates/triage/src/cadence/coordinator.rs`:

- `pub enum CadenceMode { Tier1, Tier2, Tier3, Reflection }` (`Debug + Clone + Copy + PartialEq + Eq` + `serde::Serialize`); `pub fn mode_label(mode: CadenceMode) -> &'static str` returning `"tier1"|"tier2"|"tier3"|"reflection"` (4-value bounded set per obs extract reconciliation).

- `pub trait SqlQueryRunner: Send + Sync` declaring async methods `async fn run_q1(&self, window: Duration) -> Result<Vec<Q1RedRow>, SqlAggregationError>` etc. for Q1-Q7 (per arch extract leaf-crate-no-deps invariant — concrete impl over `TriageSqlState` lives at the binary boundary `pulse-app/src/cadence_runner.rs`).

- `pub trait HardwareProfileSource: Send + Sync` forward-binding to chunk #82: `fn current_profile(&self) -> HardwareProfile` + `pub enum HardwareProfile { Unknown, GpuPrimary, GpuFallback, CpuPrimary, CpuFallback }`. Default in-process impl in `coordinator.rs`: `struct UnknownHardwareProfile;` returning `HardwareProfile::Unknown` for boot-before-#82 safety (per security extract "tolerate the chunk #82 profile source being absent by defaulting to the safe posture — Tier-2 enabled").
- `pub struct CoordinatorCycleStats { mode: CadenceMode, queries_executed: u32, queries_succeeded: u32, duration_ms: u32 }` for sync-helper test assertions.

- `pub fn run_one_coordinator_cycle(mode, sql_runner, broadcast_handle, hw_profile, now_nanos) -> CoordinatorCycleStats` deterministic sync helper:
  - If `mode == Tier2 && hw_profile.current_profile() == HardwareProfile::CpuPrimary` → return `CycleStats { queries_executed: 0, ... }` early (Tier-2 disabled per route §80).
  - Per-mode query batch selection per dist-arch v3 §Cadence: Tier-1 + Tier-2 + Tier-3 each invoke a defined subset of Q1-Q7 (the EXACT subset is detailed in dist-arch v3 §Cadence; chunk implementation reads that doc + transcribes; baseline implementation may invoke all of Q1-Q7 every tier if explicit per-tier subsetting is not yet specified in dist-arch v3 — VERIFY at /implement time by reading `docs/v0_2_0/pulse-distillation-architecture.md`).
  - Emit `tracing::info!(target: TARGET_CADENCE_TRIGGER, tier = mode_label(mode), mode = mode_label(mode), cue_kind = cue_kind_label, priority = cue_priority_label, "cadence trigger fired")`.
  - Per-query telemetry: NO raw query result rows in tracing fields (only `query_id` + `result_count` per security plan §Logging vector 5).
  - Emit one `tracing::info!(target: TARGET_METRIC_PIPELINE_L3_DIGESTS_ASSEMBLED_TOTAL, value = 1, mode = mode_label(mode), queries_executed = N, "digest assembled")` per cycle (acts as the L3 digest stub until chunk #81 lands; chunk #80 fires the metric event even before а real digest payload exists per route §80 callout).
  - Send `CadenceEvent` payload to `broadcast_handle.sender()` (best-effort; ignore SendError on zero subscribers).

- `pub async fn start_cadence_coordinator(Arc<dyn SqlQueryRunner>, Arc<CadenceEventBroadcast>, Arc<AttentionCueBroadcast>, Arc<CadenceTriggerChannel>, Arc<dyn HardwareProfileSource>, Arc<CadenceConfig>)` long-running task using `tokio::select!` over:
  - 3 `tokio::time::interval(Duration::from_secs(cfg.baseline_seconds))` ticks (one per tier; skip-first-tick per chunk #62 emitter precedent).
  - 1 `cue_broadcast.subscribe()` filter for `priority_tier == PriorityTier::Autonomous` → Tier-1 path.
  - 1 `cadence_handle.subscribe()` (Suggested cues from chunk #62) → Tier-2 path.
  - Reflection scheduler: separate `interval(Duration::from_secs(cfg.reflection_seconds))` driving Reflection-mode ticks.
  - Heartbeat tick emission every 15s via `TARGET_CADENCE_TICK` per obs extract + obs-plan §3 Heartbeat ticks.

- Colocated `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` covering acceptance criteria below — use the `CapturingSubscriber` + `FieldCollector` pattern (per testing.md 2026-05-11 entry) for PII canary tests. Test list:
  - `run_one_coordinator_cycle_emits_cadence_trigger_event_for_each_tier` (Tier-1 / Tier-2 / Tier-3 / Reflection paths).
  - `run_one_coordinator_cycle_skips_tier2_when_hardware_profile_is_cpu_primary`.
  - `run_one_coordinator_cycle_emits_digest_assembled_metric_per_cycle`.
  - `run_one_coordinator_cycle_emits_event_to_broadcast`.
  - `run_one_coordinator_cycle_does_not_leak_pii_canary_into_tracing_fields_or_broadcast_payload`.
  - `start_cadence_coordinator_spawnable_and_abortable` (mirrors chunk #62 emitter test).
  - `start_cadence_coordinator_emits_heartbeat_tick_every_15s` (use real-time wait per testing.md 2026-05-03 tokio start_paused dev-dep avoidance).
