data.head: ### Chunk route#81: "Digest assembler + LWW queue + active-incident exception"

body: **Constraints across domains:**

- (security) **Pre-write PII scrubbing at corpus persistence boundary** — any OTLP-sourced attribute value rendered into digest body (anomaly samples, exception fingerprints, log template variable bindings, span attributes from L1a Q1-Q7 outputs) MUST pass through `security::scrubber::scrub_attribute()` BEFORE serialization into the digest payload (per security plan §Anti-Patterns §Logging "Uniform scrubber coverage post-#72").

- (security) **Corpus encryption boundary preserved** — digest writes to `digest_archive` MUST go through `Arc<dyn CorpusWriter>`; NEVER bypass cell-level AES-256-GCM by direct rusqlite handle or alternate file artifact (per security plan §Data Protection §At rest + §Secret Management Storage Runtime).

- (security) **Workspace path canonicalization** — workspace-detector filesystem inspection MUST canonicalize via `strict-path` and assert resolved paths live under the user-explicit workspace root before file reads (per security plan §Input Validation row "Configuration values" + §Anti-Patterns §Input bullet 4 CWE-22 ban).

- (security) **Process-spawn ban applies to git activity inspection** — if "recent git activity" inspection uses `tokio::process::Command::new("git").arg(...)`, NEVER pass strings sourced from OTLP attributes or workspace-detector raw output as arg values; prefer in-process git library (e.g., `gix` crate) over subprocess spawn (per security plan §Anti-Patterns §Code Patterns bullet 1 MCP STDIO command-injection cluster).

- (security) **New `tokenizers` workspace dep MUST clear cargo-deny gates** — verify (a) `cargo audit` no advisories; (b) `cargo deny check bans` clean — any new transitive duplicates added to `deny.toml [bans] skip` with provenance comments per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-03 + 2026-05-20 patterns; (c) `licenses` allowlist clean for distribution channels (per security plan §Dependency Security + §Anti-Patterns §Universal bullet 2).

- (security) **Errors crossing broadcast emission boundary MUST sanitize** — if `pulse://stream/digests` payload carries error variants, use `AppError` sanitization shape (no stack traces, file paths, library versions, Rust struct names); full internal chain stays in `tracing` JSON sink only (per security plan §Error Handling).

- (security) **Active-incident exception logic MUST not leak incident-internal state** — digest payload MAY embed `incident_id` / `status` / `severity_tier` (first-party derived classifications) but MUST NOT embed raw span attribute values or unscrubbed evidence_refs payload content without scrubber pass (per security plan §Logging "NEVER log").

- (tests) Unit + integration tests MUST land co-located under `crates/triage/src/digest/` per `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { ... }` flat-function convention (per test-plan §4 conventions / §10 coverage gates).
- (tests) Coverage gate ≥75% line / ≥70% branch / ≥85% function on new `crates/triage/digest` LOC; no exclusion permitted (per test-plan §10 Quality Gates).
- (tests) Fixtures MUST use Rust builder pattern via `rstest` 0.26.1 `#[fixture]` decorators (per test-plan §7 Fixture library + §11 Test Data anti-patterns).

- (tests) Time-sensitive tests (LWW window, active-incident cool-down, cadence timing) MUST use `tokio::time::pause()` + `tokio::time::advance(Duration)` (per test-plan §8 Mocking + §11 E2E anti-pattern "NEVER use `sleep(N)`").

- (tests) Corpus interactions MUST use real `Corpus::open(...)` with in-memory backend + `tempfile::TempDir` per-test isolation; NEVER mock `CorpusReader` / `CorpusWriter` traits at integration level (per test-plan §8 What NOT to mock + chunk #68 precedent).

- (tests) Standard chunk gates runnable: `cargo fmt --check` + `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` + `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` + `cargo xtask capability-drift` (no webview gates — pure backend) + `cargo deny check bans licenses sources advisories` after `tokenizers` dep (per test-plan §12 Decisions Log 2026-05-10 chunk-gate-baseline-coverage + §9 CI cargo-deny).

- (obs) L3 digest module MUST use `tracing` 0.1 + `#[tracing::instrument]` decorators per per-handler instrumentation convention; NO OTel SDK calls (per obs plan §3 Tracing init "NO OTel SDK linked").

- (obs) Token-counting MUST emit `metric.pipeline.l3.digest_token_count_ms` as `tracing::info!(target: "metric.*", value, ...)` event with `token_count_actual` + `token_budget_limit` + `budget_exceeded` fields, mirroring the existing P2 snapshot pattern (per obs plan §5 perf-budget-instruments + §10 SLO budgets snapshot row).

- (obs) LWW drop events MUST emit `metric.pipeline.l3.lww_drop_count_total` as counter increment per drop with bounded label fields only (`cadence_tier`, `drop_reason`); NO unbounded labels like `digest_id` or `service_name` (per obs plan §5 Metric label cardinality + §11 Metrics anti-pattern "NEVER unbounded label cardinality").

- (obs) Active-incident queue depth MUST emit `metric.pipeline.l3.active_incident_queue_depth` as gauge per heartbeat tick or queue-state-change with `severity_tier` bounded label (per obs plan §5 Gauge convention + §3 Heartbeat 15s).

- (obs) Corpus retrieval MUST log `query_id` + `param_count` + `row_count_returned` + `duration_ms` per Vector 5 rule; NEVER raw fingerprint values or workspace path strings (per obs plan §6 boundary-call wrapper row "DuckDB query" + §8 PII table "DuckDB query parameters" High).

- (obs) Workspace path / framework signals / git activity ingested as project context MUST log only basename / vcs_type / boolean markers (NOT full canonicalized paths) per Vector 3 + Vector 6 scrubbing rules (per obs plan §8 PII table rows "Plugin file paths" + "Environment variables (config)").

- (arch) Chunk's L3 digest assembly code MUST live in NEW submodule `crates/triage/src/digest/` per workspace-crate-per-module discipline; do NOT introduce a new top-level crate — digest is a submodule of `triage`, mirroring `triage::baseline` / `triage::pattern` / `triage::cue` / `triage::cadence` precedents (per arch §Inherited Defaults Module boundaries + §Occupied Resources Cargo workspace crate names).

- (arch) New broadcast topic `pulse://stream/digests` MUST be registered via `/andromeda-evolve --allow-arch-registry` amendment to arch §Occupied Resources Tauri IPC events (broadcast channels) — mirrors chunk #80 `pulse://stream/cadence-events` precedent (per arch §Architecture Registry Updates 2026-05-23 entry).

- (arch) New workspace dep `tokenizers` MUST land in `[workspace.dependencies]` block with version pin + provenance comment; transitive duplicates surfaced by `cargo deny check bans` added to `deny.toml [bans] skip` with per-line provenance; NEVER relax `multiple-versions = "deny"` (per CLAUDE.md §Session Learnings 2026-05-03 + 2026-05-20).

body: _Generated by /andromeda-phase Phase 4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not edit during /implement run._
- **Phase number:** 78

- **Route chunks covered:**
  - route#81 "Digest assembler + LWW queue + active-incident exception — compose L3 digest from L1a/L2/corpus; LWW for cadence with active-incident bypass (capabilities P-031/P-032/P-044/P-059; detail in pulse-v0_2_0-route §81)"
- **Epoch:** Foundation v0.2.0

Chunk #81 implements the L3 digest assembler — the composition layer between L1a (DuckDB Q1-Q7 SQL outputs landed at chunk #79), L2 (attention cues + fingerprints from chunks #62/#66/#67), corpus retrieval (top-3 similar past incidents from chunk #68 substrate), and project context (workspace + git activity from chunk #43 workspace-detector + new ProjectContextProvider trait). The assembler produces a structured digest per dist-arch v3 §Appendix C (WINDOW header / PROJECT line / SERVICES table / ATTENTION CUES / TOP EXCEPTIONS / SERVICE GRAPH / CRITICAL PATH SAMPLE / CORPUS MATCHES) bounded to 500-2000 tokens soft / 3000 hard cap via Hugging Face `tokenizers` (new workspace dep). Output flows through two channels in parallel: (a) `pulse://stream/digests` broadcast for L4 LLM consumption (chunks #82-#85, deferred); (b) corpus `digest_archive` append (chunk #68 schema; AES-256-GCM cell-level encryption via `CorpusWriter` extension). LWW queue mechanism is the default for cadence-mode digests; active-incident exception bypasses LWW when L5 has unresolved incident with severity ≥ Suggested per dist-arch v3 §Queue behavior; Tier-1 hard signals never LWW-replaced; all digests written to corpus regardless of queue state.

The chunk introduces 1 new submodule (`crates/triage/src/digest/`) following the chunk #80 cadence submodule precedent, 1 new workspace dep (`tokenizers`), 1 new broadcast topic (`pulse://stream/digests` requiring post-impl `/andromeda-evolve --allow-arch-registry` amendment), 3 new perf-budget metrics (`pipeline.l3.digest_token_count_p99` SLO derived from `metric.pipeline.l3.digest_token_count_ms` raw events; `pipeline.l3.lww_drop_count_total` counter; `pipeline.l3.active_incident_queue_depth` gauge), 4 trait extensions (CorpusReader + CorpusWriter add digest methods; new `DigestAssembler` and `ProjectContextProvider` traits), and 5 binary-boundary adapter wiring points (in pulse-app: `digest_runtime.rs` adapter; `main.rs` boot wire-up; cadence coordinator hook replacement; observability AllowList; PII scrubber closure injection). Implementation discipline per security plan §Anti-Patterns §Logging uniform-coverage framing (post-#72 invariant): every OTLP-attribute-derived field passes through `security::scrubber::scrub_attribute()` BEFORE both broadcast emit AND corpus persistence; per obs plan §3 NO-OTel-SDK self-observation; per arch §Module dependency direction strict-no-reverse-edges + arch §Cross-cutting "Cross-bridge data shape" `serde::Serialize` + `specta::Type`; per CLAUDE.md Session Learnings 2026-05-23 manual `Pin<Box<dyn Future>>` async-trait-without-dep pattern (no `async-trait` workspace dep delta) + 2026-05-19 N-trait-from-single-Arc + 2026-05-16 trait-in-lower-crate + 2026-05-20 cross-crate `scrubbed_clone`.

Tests cover the full surface per dist-arch v3 testability strategy + chunk #77 golden corpus precedent: ≥3 golden-file digest composition tests, LWW behavior with `tokio::time::pause()` clock injection, active-incident exception bypass, Tier-1 never-LWW invariant, corpus append regardless of queue state, token-budget enforcement, PII negative-canary E2E (JWT-pattern → assert absence in both broadcast payload and persisted corpus row), coverage gate ≥75% line / ≥70% branch / ≥85% function on new `crates/triage/digest` LOC.

1. **Workspace dep + Cargo.toml updates.** Add `tokenizers = { version = "0.x", default-features = false, features = ["onig"] }` to root `Cargo.toml [workspace.dependencies]` (verify default-features-disable removes the heavyweight `http` feature; the `onig` feature provides the BPE engine needed for token counting without network deps). Add `tokenizers = { workspace = true }` to `crates/triage/Cargo.toml [dependencies]`. After adding, run `cargo deny check bans licenses sources advisories` and add any new transitive duplicates to `deny.toml [bans] skip` with per-line provenance comments per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-03 pattern; do NOT relax `multiple-versions = "deny"`. body: **Constraints across domains:**

- (arch) LLM runtime pinned to `mistralrs = "=0.8.0"` (exact, no caret); floating constraints cause mid-chunk API churn breakage during L4 implementation window (arch §Established Decisions [LLM Inference Runtime — L4 interpretation layer])

- (arch) `mistralrs` runtime MUST be wrapped behind `pub trait LlmInferenceRunner: Send + Sync` in `crates/triage/src/contract`; async returns as `Pin<Box<dyn Future + Send + 'a>>` (matching 2026-05-23 `SqlQueryRunner` async pattern at `crates/triage/src/cadence/coordinator.rs`); concrete `MistralRsInference` impl at binary boundary in `pulse-app/` (arch §Established Decisions [LLM Inference Runtime] bus factor entry)

- (arch) Step 0 spike requirement — feed representative 100-token L3 digest fixture into mistral.rs strict-schema mode, assert JSON parses round-trip, fail-fast if API surface regressed since v0.8.0 publication (arch §Established Decisions [LLM Inference Runtime] caveat)

- (arch) New workspace crate MUST follow `crates/<module-name>/` pattern with public contract module as sole `pub` surface; cross-crate utilities use `pub(crate)`; no `pub use` re-exports across crate boundaries (arch §Conventions module visibility discipline)

- (arch) New TauRPC procedure `model.current_profile()` MUST conform к §Standard Contracts envelope — returns profile + tier + model identity as `Result<T, AppError>` where `AppError` is serde-friendly (arch §Standard Contracts Tauri IPC introspection)

- (arch) New broadcast topic `pulse://stream/model-status` (load/unload/error events) MUST use existing `tokio::sync::broadcast` pattern (arch §Established Decisions [In-Process Channel Architecture])

- (security) Model file integrity + no auto-download without user consent — load paths MUST validate file signatures or canonicalize paths; no auto-download without explicit user opt-in per Project Intent local-first principle (per security plan §Threat Model Summary §Data classification third-party WASM plugin binaries analog)

- (security) New dependency `mistralrs` 0.8.0 MUST pass `cargo audit` and `cargo deny check bans` gates before merge; resolved version recorded in workspace `Cargo.toml`; Pre-D1 rationale recorded in arch §Established Decisions with decision date + trade-off notes (per security plan §Dependency Security Pinning paragraph)

- (security) New TauRPC procedure `model.current_profile()` requires both router registration AND entry in `pulse-app/capabilities/` JSON — missing entry produces silent runtime rejection (per security plan §API Security TauRPC capability authorization)

- (security) Model load errors MUST collapse to sanitized `AppError` enum variants at TauRPC bridge — no stack traces, model paths, or runtime details exposed (per security plan §Error Handling §External responses TauRPC bridge contract)

- (security) New broadcast topic `pulse://stream/model-status` (load/unload/error events) MUST NOT emit raw model file paths or unredacted error messages — redact paths via `strict-path` canonicalization before any tracing emission (per security plan §Logging & Monitoring NEVER-log list)

- (tests) All hardware profile detection logic must be unit-testable via injected hardware capability flags; no direct CUDA/Metal/CPU feature detection required at test boundary (architecture boundary tested via mistralrs wrapper trait) (per test-plan §4 mocking discipline)
- (tests) Test fixtures for cpu-primary detection must use synthetic hardware config (simulated CPU-only environment); no actual hardware access required (per test-plan §7 fixture bootstrap)

- (tests) Hardware profile detection must trigger cpu-primary one-time notice exactly once per session; subsequent startup must not re-emit (test via corpus state persistence + idempotency assertion per test-plan §3 bootstrap phase 5 "pid-file-commitment-wire")

- (tests) Step 0 spike requirement — chunk #82 plan SHALL include unit test of mistralrs v0.8.0 JSON schema round-trip (100-token L3 digest fixture via strict-schema mode; fail-fast if API surface regressed; recorded in test-run.log as "Step 0 validation: mistralrs JSON schema compatibility") (per arch §Established Decisions caveat)

- (obs) All L4 (interpretation) module code MUST emit self-observation via `tracing` ecosystem only; NO OTel SDK in self-runtime (per obs-plan §3 Established Decisions; tracing-subscriber JSON to `~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/agent-latest.jsonl`)
- (obs) Hardware profile detection spans MUST NOT log raw model file paths or checkpoint paths; use `plugin_path_basename` pattern (canonical path → filename only) (per obs-plan §8 Vector 3 defense)

- (obs) Model status events emitted on `pulse://stream/model-status` broadcast channel MUST include trace_id in Arrow metadata (`_trace_context` field) for end-to-end correlation (per obs-plan §3 trace context propagation)

- (obs) Tokenizer initialization latency MUST be captured in `metric.interpretation.tokenizer_init_latency_ms` events; heartbeat tick `interpretation.tick` MUST emit current model identity + tier (per obs-plan §5 metric coverage pattern)

- (obs) `model.current_profile()` TauRPC procedure response MUST include fields `{profile: gpu-primary|gpu-fallback|cpu-primary|cpu-fallback, tier: primary|fallback, model_identity: string, load_status: loaded|error}` for Settings → Diagnostics surface visibility (per obs-plan §6 log fields binding)
**Patterns к follow:**

- (arch) Async trait surface pattern — `crates/triage/src/cadence/coordinator.rs` defines `SqlQueryRunner` trait with `Pin<Box<dyn Future + Send + 'a>>` returns; replicate for `LlmInferenceRunner` to preserve async composability across chunks #82–#85 without requiring concrete executor knowledge in leaf crates (arch §Inherited Defaults async runtime discipline)

- (arch) Binary-boundary concrete impl placement — `SqlQueryRunner` trait lives in `triage/contract`, `DuckDbQueryRunner` concrete impl lives in `pulse-app/`; replicate for LLM trait + mistral.rs impl to keep leaf crates decoupled from runtime versions (arch §Module dependency direction)

- (arch) Hardware profile enum invariant — follow DuckDB schema pattern; define hardware tier and profile as bounded enum types (not raw strings) with exhaustive match coverage; no `_` catch-all unless explicitly documented (arch §Conventions variable / function naming + Smart enum types validation pattern)

- (arch) Broadcast channel fan-out — `pulse://stream/connection-state` (chunk #59) emits state changes to broadcast; `pulse://stream/model-status` follows identical pattern with Arc<RwLock>-protected or atomic state (arch §Established Decisions [In-Process Channel Architecture])

- (security) Dependency security gate — record `mistralrs` resolved version in workspace `Cargo.toml`; document Pre-D1 decision date + trade-off notes (mirror existing `tonic 0.14 ↔ opentelemetry-otlp 0.31` exemption pattern from `.github/dependabot.yml`) (per security plan §Dependency Security pinning + deny.toml reconciliation)

- (security) Model file path handling — use `strict-path` crate for canonicalization and assertion that paths resolve under plugin/model data directories (per security plan §Input Validation CLI/env var inputs row + CLAUDE.md Critical Warnings path env vars pattern)

- (security) Hardware profile classification errors surface as `AppError::Validation { field, reason }` or `AppError::Internal { message }` at the bridge (per Conventions Error response schema and security plan §Error Handling pattern established at `crates/ui-bridge/src/error.rs`)

- (tests) Builder pattern for test fixtures — `MockHardwareConfig::builder().profile(Profile::CpuPrimary).build()` and `MockModel::builder().checkpoint("model-id").build()` (per test-plan §4 fixture pattern; rstest 0.26.1 composition)

- (obs) Span naming follows `{module}.{operation}` convention — `interpretation.hardware.detect`, `interpretation.model.load`, `interpretation.tokenizer.init` (per obs-plan §4 §Span naming convention)

- (obs) Heartbeat ticks every 15s via `tokio::time::interval(Duration::from_secs(15))` emit `tracing::info!(target: "interpretation.tick", model_profile=, model_tier=, model_status=, "heartbeat")` (per obs-plan §3 Heartbeat ticks; §5 metric coverage)

- (obs) Profile detection metric is `pipeline.l4.hardware_profile_active{profile}`; model tier classification is `pipeline.l4.model_tier_active{tier}` (per obs-plan §5)
- (obs) Error path — model load failure emits `interpretation.model.load.error` span with `error_msg: string, model_identity: string, recovery_action: string` (per route §82 P-053/P-054)
**Anti-patterns к avoid:**

- (arch) Do NOT float `mistralrs` version constraint — `mistralrs = "0.8.0"` OR `mistralrs = "0.8"` are violations; only `mistralrs = "=0.8.0"` (explicit exact pin) is compliant (arch §Established Decisions [LLM Inference Runtime] pin discipline)

- (arch) Do NOT defer the Step 0 strict-schema spike — surfacing API regressions mid-implementation is too late to pivot; spike MUST run BEFORE implementation proper (arch §Established Decisions [LLM Inference Runtime] caveat)

- (arch) Do NOT expose `mistralrs` types in public crate surface — all `mistralrs` imports stay in `pulse-app/`; leaf-crate `triage` surface only exports the trait and error enum (arch §Module boundaries enforcement)

- (arch) Do NOT bind new TauRPC procedure without corresponding `pulse-app/capabilities/` JSON entry — Tauri capabilities are negative-default; missing entry silently rejects bridge calls (arch §Cross-cutting Patterns Webview IPC capability policy)

- (security) NEVER auto-download models without explicit user consent — model download logic MUST require user action (Settings button, explicit Load action, or opt-in environment variable) (per security plan §Data Protection lifecycle + Project Intent local-first framing)

- (security) NEVER hardcode model paths or URLs — all paths resolved from config / env vars and canonicalized via `strict-path` (per security plan §Input Validation CLI/env var inputs row + CLAUDE.md Critical Warnings universal invariant on path env vars)

- (security) NEVER expose mistralrs internal errors (API breakage, format incompatibilities, backend failures) to users via TauRPC without sanitization — catch and convert to `AppError::{Internal, Storage, Ingest}` at bridge (per security plan §Error Handling §External responses)
- (tests) Do NOT test GPU/Metal/CUDA detection directly (hardware-specific, flaky on CI runners); use hardware config injection instead

- (tests) Do NOT validate mistralrs model loading from disk in unit tests (I/O-bound, network-dependent for model downloads); mock model path and assert tokenizer initialization succeeds with known checkpoint identifier
- (tests) Do NOT emit cpu-primary notice more than once per session even across multiple `model.current_profile()` invocations; enforce via idempotency test
- (obs) NEVER log raw OTLP payloads or model checkpoint file paths in any interpretation spans — violates obs-plan §8 Vector 1 + Vector 3; use basename or `model_identity` (semantic name)

- (obs) NEVER emit per-token latency metrics — unbounded cardinality in per-model-tier × per-prompt-length labels; emit aggregate tokenizer batch latency + inference queue depth only (per obs-plan §5 cardinality discipline)
- (obs) NEVER dial own OTLP receivers (`:4317`/`:4318`) from model-generation code — infinite recursion; self-observation is `tracing` file sink only (per obs-plan §1 self-observation discipline)

- (obs) NEVER log inference prompt text or model output JSON to self-observation logs — capture only `{prompt_token_count, output_token_count, latency_ms, result_type}` metadata (per obs-plan §8 Vector 4 MCP response bodies analogy)
**Contract bindings:**

- **arch ↔ tests**: Bus factor trait pattern — `mistralrs` wrapped behind `pub trait LlmInferenceRunner: Send + Sync` returning `Pin<Box<dyn Future + Send>>` enables test doubles without runtime. title: Step 3 — Implement real hardware profile detection

data.head: ### Step 3 — Implement real hardware profile detection

body:
1. Create `crates/interpretation/src/hardware.rs` containing:
   - `pub struct HardwareProfileDetector { /* cached profile */ }`
   - `impl HardwareProfileSource for HardwareProfileDetector` returning `HardwareProfile` based on detected hardware characteristics.
   - Detection logic: GPU presence (Metal on macOS via system_profiler / CUDA on Linux+Windows via nvidia-smi presence / Vulkan probe / Apple Silicon detection); GPU memory (parse from probe output); CPU core count (`num_cpus::get()` if added, OR `std::thread::available_parallelism()`).
   - Classification rules per P-054 + chunk summary: GpuPrimary (Metal/CUDA + ≥6GB VRAM), GpuFallback (Metal/CUDA + <6GB VRAM), CpuPrimary (no GPU OR GPU unavailable), CpuFallback (no GPU + <4 cores OR explicit fallback signal).
2. Detection should be idempotent + cached after first call (boot-time classification; subsequent queries return cached result without re-probing hardware).

3. Tests at `crates/interpretation/tests/hardware_classification.rs` — exercise 4 profiles via config injection (per tests extract MockHardwareConfig builder pattern). Each profile gets a dedicated `#[test]` fn asserting the classification rule.

body: **Constraints across domains:**

- (arch) Webview source root is `pulse-app/ui/`; icon component files MUST land under `pulse-app/ui/src/components/icons/`. The 8 library crates and `pulse-app/src/` Rust source are off-limits for this chunk (per arch §Project directory structure / Infrastructure Patterns).

- (arch) Workspace crate name list is LOCKED at 10; chunk #11 MUST NOT introduce a new crate or rename one. Icon components add ZERO Rust workspace members (per arch §Occupied Resources "Cargo workspace crate names" + Design Philosophy).
- (arch) This chunk introduces NO TauRPC procedures and therefore NO entry in `pulse-app/capabilities/` is required (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns "Webview IPC capability policy").

- (arch) Module dependency direction is locked toward `pulse-app` binary; chunk #11 MUST NOT cause any library crate to depend on the webview / a TS package (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns "Module dependency direction").

- (arch) Tauri build chain consumes `pulse-app/ui/dist/` per chunk #10's `tauri.conf.json build.frontendDist = "ui/dist"`; icon components MUST be reachable through the existing dist pipeline OR a sibling build step that produces output discoverable from `dist/` (per arch §Infrastructure Patterns).
- (arch) Webview source-file naming is delegated to design specialist; arch imposes no naming on `.tsx`/`.ts` icon files beyond React-component convention (per arch §Conventions "File naming").

- (arch) Tray icon glyph is owned by design specialist per Cross-cutting Patterns "Tray icon policy"; the tray monochrome variant referenced in this chunk may be authored at chunk #11 but is materialized into tray-image format at chunk #34.

- (security) New webview-side npm dependencies (React/react-dom/Vite/etc., if introduced) MUST be pinned in `pulse-app/ui/package.json` and committed via `package-lock.json`; existing supply-chain gates apply at the Rust layer (`cargo audit`/`cargo deny`) — npm closure is the project's first webview supply-chain surface (per security plan §Dependency Security CI integration).

- (security) SVG component sources MUST be first-party files committed to the repo; NEVER fetch SVG markup, sprite sheets, or icon-font CSS from a remote CDN at runtime — `tauri.conf.json` CSP `default-src 'self' ipc: http://ipc.localhost; connect-src 'self' ipc: http://ipc.localhost` already forbids it (per security plan §API Security CSP row + Cross-cutting Patterns "no CDN").

- (security) SVGs MUST be inlined as React JSX (not via `` from `data:` URIs assembled from untrusted input, not via `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` of arbitrary strings); NEVER add `'unsafe-inline'` to `script-src` (per security plan §API Security CSP row + §Anti-Patterns API).

- (security) Each new icon component MUST carry only static, hardcoded attribute values (`viewBox`, `fill`, `stroke`, `aria-hidden`, `focusable="false"`); NEVER interpolate user-controlled input into SVG attributes (`href`, `xlink:href`, inline `<script>`, `<foreignObject>`, `on*` handlers) — convention must be set now, before chunks #25/#27 wire data sources (per security plan §Anti-Patterns Code Patterns).

- (security) SVG files MUST NOT contain `<script>`, `on*` event handlers, external `<image href="https://…">`, or `xlink:href="javascript:…"`; manual review at commit time since these are author-controlled glyphs (per security plan §Threat Model webview content vector + §Anti-Patterns Input).

- (security) The chunk MUST NOT touch `pulse-app/capabilities/` JSON, MUST NOT add a TauRPC procedure, MUST NOT introduce any inbound network surface, and MUST NOT modify the existing CSP literal (per security plan §API Security TauRPC capability authorization + Cross-cutting Patterns Webview IPC capability policy).

- (security) Existing CI gates (`cargo audit`, `cargo deny check bans licenses sources`, gitleaks/secret-scanning, `harden-runner`) MUST continue to pass; if React/Vite are introduced, MUST NOT regress the `tonic 0.14 ↔ 0.13` canary or relax `multiple-versions = "deny"` (per security plan §Dependency Security CI integration + Session Additions 2026-05-03).

- (design) Custom glyph set is exactly five: `aperture`, `telescope`, `constellation-grid`, `star`, `circular-pulse` — each carrying specific domain meaning ("view settings" / "investigate" / "service map" / "favorite snapshot" / "compact widget toggle") (per design-system.md §Iconography Primary custom set).
- (design) Glyphs MUST be registered as React components at `pulse-app/ui/src/components/icons/`, addressable as `<Icon glyph="telescope" />` (per design-system.md §Iconography Primary custom set).

- (design) Custom SVGs MUST be monochrome with `#E8EEF7` (Status White-Blue / `--color-text-primary`) as default fill, adaptable per state via design tokens (no hardcoded hex inside the glyph React component) (per design-system.md §Iconography + §Color Palette Text Hierarchy).

- (design) Glyph rendered sizes are constrained to the size grid: 16px (tray icon, inline labels), 20px (buttons, list items, navigation), 24px (card titles, large buttons, hero elements) (per design-system.md §Iconography Size grid).

- (design) Custom set is the PRIMARY visual language; Lucide / Heroicons may only be installed/referenced as fallback for secondary/generic icons; the registry itself ships only the 5 custom glyphs at this chunk (per design-system.md §Iconography Secondary library).

- (design) Each glyph must visibly emerge from the Observatory / Constellation / Mission Control domain; generic stock-library shapes are explicitly rejected (per design-system.md §Anti-Patterns Rejected Defaults item 5).

- (layouts) Aperture glyph is the canonical "settings gear" icon in the custom titlebar of both compact widget and full dashboard; registry naming + default sizing must support titlebar-icon density (per layout-templates §Component — Custom titlebar Components row "Settings button: aperture glyph icon").

- (layouts) Telescope glyph is the canonical "Investigate" trigger icon in the full dashboard header; co-appears with aperture in the dashboard header (per layout-templates §Wireframe — Full dashboard + §Component — Trace data table).

- (layouts) Constellation-grid glyph is one of two valid "App icon" choices for the custom titlebar (aperture or constellation-grid); registry must expose both as titlebar-eligible (per layout-templates §Component — Custom titlebar Components row "App icon").

- (layouts) Star glyph is the canonical tray icon SVG glyph — single monochrome shape, line-based, no fills/gradients/shadows; tray-icon variant has different rendering constraints from webview variants (template-image flag on macOS, OS auto-tinting) (per layout-templates §Component — Tray icon SVG construction).

- (layouts) Circular-pulse glyph does not appear by name in layout-templates.md — orchestrator may need to surface to user/design whether circular-pulse is Halo-State-Pulse-related visual element or unrelated icon. (Halo State Pulse is rendered via WebGPU canvas, not as a static SVG icon — per layout-templates §Component — Halo State Pulse canvas — so circular-pulse cannot be the Halo signature itself.)

- (layouts) Window controls (minimize, maximize, close) are NOT in the chunk's enumerated 5 glyphs; registry scope appears to exclude window controls (per layout-templates §Component — Custom titlebar Components row "Window controls").

- (layouts) Modal close glyph (`✕`) is referenced as a Unicode character in `color-text-secondary`; registry can use Unicode (no SVG asset needed) (per layout-templates §Component — Investigation modal + §Component — Settings modal).

- (tests) Standard tier coverage targets apply (≥75% line / ≥70% branch / ≥85% function per test-plan §10), but pure-presentation SVG components arguably qualify as "view layer with no logic" and may be exempt-by-policy if orchestrator scopes coverage gates to Rust crates only at this Foundation pre-shell stage (per test-plan §10 exclusions for "generated code, test fixtures, mock implementations").

- (tests) Test directory + naming conventions are Rust-centric in the plan (`#[cfg(test)] mod tests`); test-plan is silent on JS/TS test file location and naming — orchestrator must surface this to user (specialist plan §1/§3/§8 silent on this chunk's concern).

- (tests) Agent-driven invariant: every test must produce machine-parseable output; if a frontend test runner is introduced, MUST emit JUnit XML or LCOV/equivalent structured output consumable by the existing CI scaffold from chunk #5 (per test-plan §1 agent-driven-discipline trigger + §9 CI Integration JUnit XML).
- (tests) Self-bootstrapping fixtures only; SVG component output asserted via DOM-shape predicates (e.g., `<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true">`), not via image diff (per test-plan §7).
- (tests) Zero-flakiness budget applies — first-flake = quarantine + root-cause; no retry budget. React rendering tests under jsdom must avoid timer/async-effect flakiness (per test-plan §10).

- (a11y) Custom SVG glyph React components MUST support both decorative (`aria-hidden="true"`) and meaningful (`aria-label` / `role="img"` + label) modes per SC 4.1.2 Name/Role/Value (per a11y-plan §7 Form labels + §11 Screen Reader anti-patterns "redundant labels").

- (a11y) Icons used to supplement state colors MUST be addressable as part of the not-color-alone supplement; registry's API must allow icon adjacent to state-colored text per SC 1.4.1 (per a11y-plan §6 State color tokens not-color-alone + §11 Visual ban).

- (a11y) Icons rendered as `<svg>` MUST NOT redundantly duplicate ARIA roles already inherited from semantic elements (`role="img"` on `<button>` containing only the icon is redundant if `aria-label` is on the button) (per a11y-plan §11 ARIA anti-patterns).

- (a11y) Icon component MUST NOT trap focus or introduce `tabindex > 0` — icons are non-interactive presentation; interactivity comes from the wrapping `<button>` / `<a>` / `<menuitem>` (per a11y-plan §11 Keyboard).

- (a11y) Icon stroke / fill colors MUST resolve to design tokens (default `--color-text-primary`); registry must accept `currentColor` so consumers can compose contrast at usage site to satisfy SC 1.4.11 ≥ 3:1 (per a11y-plan §6 Color contrast pairs SC 1.4.11 + §6 State color tokens).

- (a11y) Icon target-size enforcement happens at the wrapper element (button/control), not the icon itself; registry sizes alone (16/20/24) are NOT sufficient for SC 2.5.8 unless padding brings the wrapper to 24×24 (per a11y-plan §6 Target size tokens + §3 target-size trigger row).

- (a11y) Each icon component's behavior under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` MUST be neutral — no per-icon JS animations introduced at chunk #11; if registry pre-wires Halo State Pulse / circular-pulse motion, the path MUST honor `useReducedMotion` (chunk #15 dependency) and degrade to static glyph (per a11y-plan §6 Motion tokens SC 2.3.3 + §11 Motion).
**Patterns to follow:**

- (arch) Library / crate template pattern: each library crate exposes only its public contract via `pub`; webview-side analogue should mirror this in spirit — single barrel `index.ts(x)` re-export from `pulse-app/ui/src/components/icons/` so consumers import via `@/components/icons` (per arch §Conventions "Module visibility discipline" + §Project Intent "Template patterns").

- (arch) Cargo features are minimal-by-default and `kebab-case`; chunk #11 introduces zero Rust feature flags. If team defers React-runtime introduction to chunk #25, deferral is captured at route/phase level rather than via Cargo feature gate (per arch §Conventions "Feature flags").

- (security) Bundle-in-tree, no remote fetch — chunk #10 already established the precedent (committing WOFF2 + OFL license files under `pulse-app/ui/public/fonts/` + copying via `scripts/build.mjs`); SVG components or any raw `*.svg` design files should follow the same in-tree pattern (per security plan §Anti-Patterns API "no remote content" + Cross-cutting Patterns).

- (security) CSP envelope is `tauri.conf.json` first-party; existing `default-src 'self' ipc: http://ipc.localhost; img-src 'self' data:; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; script-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' ipc: http://ipc.localhost; worker-src 'self' blob:` is the contract (per security plan §API Security CSP row).

- (security) React JSX inlining (e.g., `export const ApertureIcon = (props) => <svg {...props}>…</svg>`) is the safe rendering path because Babel/SWC compiles JSX to `React.createElement` calls — no runtime string parsing, no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, no script injection surface (per security plan §Anti-Patterns Code Patterns + Threat Model webview content vector).

- (security) Pre-existing build-pipeline pattern (chunk #10 `scripts/build.mjs`) on Windows uses `execFileSync(process.execPath, [<path-to-cli/index.mjs>, ...args])` to bypass npm `.cmd` shim CVE-2024-27980 hardening — if this chunk introduces a Vite/Rollup invocation from the same `build.mjs`, follow the same direct-`.mjs` invocation pattern (per `.claude/docs/session-learnings.md` 2026-05-03 entry).

- (design) Token-driven fill: SVG `fill` / `stroke` use `currentColor` (or CSS custom property reference) so callers can re-tint via Tailwind v4 `text-{color}` utilities mapped to the `@theme` tokens shipped in chunk #10 (per design-system.md §Surface: desktop-webview Tokens).

- (design) Component shape `<Icon glyph="telescope" size={20} />` (or per-glyph named exports `<TelescopeIcon />`) — design-system specifies `<Icon glyph="…" />` form; either composition acceptable as long as addressable name matches the registry (per design-system.md §Iconography Primary custom set).

- (design) Size + container padding pairing: 16px glyph → 4px padding, 20px glyph → 6px padding, 24px glyph → 8px padding — these padding values map to design tokens (`--spacing-xs` 4px, ~`--spacing-sm` 8px) (per design-system.md §Iconography Size grid + §Spacing).

- (design) "Icons clarify, not decorate" discipline — every glyph component should be authored to be removable without information loss; no purely-ornamental flourishes inside the SVG paths (per design-system.md §Iconography Rule).

- (design) Mission Control / Observatory contemplative aesthetic — geometric precision, sharp-but-not-cold linework consistent with `--radius-sm` / `--radius-md` chrome (per design-system.md §Brand Identity Design direction + §Border Radius Personality).

- (layouts) Per-surface size + tint variants per glyph — registry should follow a consistent React-component-with-prop pattern (size + color tokens as props) rather than per-variant duplicate components (per layout-templates §Component — Custom titlebar Components row "Settings button" tone references + §Component — Tray icon Color rows).

- (layouts) Line-based simple SVG construction — tray-icon star is "simple line-based design (no complex fills, all strokes) for clarity at small sizes; outer circle (stroke 1px), inner star or aperture cross (4-6 strokes), no gradients, no shadows, no embellishment". Apply this minimal-stroke discipline to the other 4 glyphs since they share brand DNA (per layout-templates §Component — Tray icon SVG construction).

- (layouts) Glyph as React component, not raw `` — chunk title prescribes "registered as React components at src/components/icons/"; inline-SVG-as-JSX pattern is what layout patterns assume (per chunk text + layout-templates §Component — Custom titlebar).

- (layouts) Consumer surfaces are committed but un-implemented — chunk #25 (webview shell) lands the custom titlebar that consumes aperture/constellation-grid/telescope; tray icon implementation lands at chunk #33 (tray icon + native menu, route §2). Registry chunk lands BEFORE both consumers — components should compile + render in isolation, not require fully-wired consumer surfaces.

- (tests) 5-command discipline preserved — if Vitest/jsdom is introduced, hook it under `cargo xtask test:ui` or extend `npm run` scripts in `pulse-app/ui/package.json` so `scripts/agent-run.sh run` (when materialized at chunk #25) can dispatch to it (per test-plan §3 Test Harness Contract).

- (tests) JUnit XML report format — match `cargo nextest --message-format junit` discipline in any frontend test runner (e.g., Vitest's `--reporter=junit` to `target/junit-ui.xml`) (per test-plan §9 CI Integration).

- (tests) Co-location per existing crate convention — if frontend tests land at chunk #11, follow `pulse-app/ui/src/components/icons/<glyph>.test.tsx` adjacent to the source file (per test-plan §4 Unit conventions).

- (tests) Builder factory pattern adapted to React — if test data needed (parameterized icon sizes/colors), use `describe.each(...)` / Vitest `test.each(...)` rather than raw object literals (per test-plan §7 fixture lifecycle).

- (a11y) Decorative-first default with explicit override — `<Icon glyph="telescope" />` should default to `aria-hidden="true"` and accept `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby` prop that, when provided, sets `role="img"` and removes `aria-hidden` (per a11y-plan §4 Per-component pattern catalog).

- (a11y) Semantic HTML first — when an icon is the visual indicator inside an interactive control, the registry's icon stays presentational (`aria-hidden="true"`) and the wrapping `<button>` carries the accessible name (per a11y-plan §2 Agent-runnable invariants + §11 ARIA).

- (a11y) `currentColor` propagation — icon SVG path attributes use `fill="currentColor"` / `stroke="currentColor"` so token-driven color cascades from the wrapper, preserving the contrast verification harness path (chunk #12 + colorjs.io reads `getComputedStyle(wrapperElement).color`) (per a11y-plan §6 Contrast verification harness).

- (a11y) ESLint enforcement — configure `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y` rules `jsx-a11y/img-redundant-alt`, `jsx-a11y/no-redundant-roles`, `jsx-a11y/role-supports-aria-props` against the icon component output. Chunk #13 stack install lands the linter — chunk #11 may pre-author components to be lint-clean against `'plugin:jsx-a11y/recommended'` (per a11y-plan §3 a11y-linting-install bootstrap phase + §11 ARIA).

- (a11y) State-color icon pairing API — registry exports common pairings (e.g., `feedback-success` icon variant, or "icon + label" composition pattern documented in JSDoc) so consumers in P7 settings-modal / P2 investigation-modal can satisfy SC 1.4.1 by composition (per a11y-plan §6 not-color-alone).
**Anti-patterns to avoid:**

- (arch) Do NOT rename or add a workspace crate for icons (e.g., `crates/icons/`) — icons are webview render-time React components, NOT a Rust module-of-growth unit (per arch §Occupied Resources LOCKED crate-name list + §Project Intent "How new functionality is added").

- (arch) Do NOT place icon components under `pulse-app/src/` (the Rust binary crate source) or under any `crates/*` library; `pulse-app/ui/src/components/icons/` is the only correct location (per arch §Infrastructure Patterns project tree).

- (arch) Do NOT introduce a new Tauri capability identifier; LOCKED set is `pulse:default`, `pulse:tray`, `pulse:notification`, `pulse:updater`, `pulse:plugin-fs`. Adding one would inflate the negative-default trust model (per arch §Occupied Resources).

- (arch) Do NOT introduce a frontend dev-server port, env var, or external URL for icon distribution; all glyph assets MUST live in-tree (per §Occupied Resources + Cross-cutting Patterns + chunk #10 in-tree pattern).

- (security) NEVER use `dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: svgString }}` to render SVGs from a string; even with first-party static strings, the convention enables a future data-driven `<DynamicIcon name={spanAttribute} />` regression that becomes a script-injection sink (per security plan §Threat Model webview content + §Anti-Patterns Code Patterns).

- (security) NEVER reference an icon set by external URL (`react-icons` CDN bundle, `lucide-react` remote-fetch variant, `<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/icon...">`); bundle locally only — widening `connect-src` / `default-src` invalidates the CSP envelope (per security plan §API Security CSP + Cross-cutting Patterns).

- (security) NEVER pin npm dependencies (if introduced) by floating semver range alone in `package.json` without committing a corresponding `package-lock.json` to git — reproducible builds depend on lockfile presence, paralleling `Cargo.lock` discipline (per security plan §Dependency Security Pinning).

- (design) NEVER hardcode hex color values inside the SVG `fill` / `stroke` attributes — must reference `currentColor` or one of the `@theme` color tokens; otherwise glyphs cannot retint per state and break the token-purity rule (per design-system.md §Anti-Patterns Universal Bans + Self-Validation Protocol §4 Token Test).

- (design) NEVER substitute a generic stock-library glyph (Lucide / Heroicons / Material) for any of the five custom slots — custom set IS the primary visual language; stock-library equivalents fail the Sameness Test (per design-system.md §Anti-Patterns Rejected Defaults item 5 + Self-Validation Protocol §5).

- (design) NEVER add motion / animation inside the glyph SVG itself — `circular-pulse` is a static glyph that visually parallels the Halo State Pulse rhythm; the actual pulsing motion lives on the WebGPU canvas layer outside the React render tree, not as SVG `<animate>` (per design-system.md §Iconography + §Motion + Surface: desktop-webview Performance notes).

- (design) NEVER ship the glyph components without the path resolved to `pulse-app/ui/src/components/icons/` exactly — design plan specifies this path verbatim (per design-system.md §Iconography Primary custom set).

- (layouts) Do NOT bake the tray-icon star glyph into the same React-component path as the webview star glyph — tray-icon SVG is consumed by Tauri's tray API as a static SVG asset (template-image flag on macOS), not by a React renderer. React component is appropriate for the 4 webview glyphs (aperture/telescope/constellation-grid/circular-pulse); tray-icon star may need a separate static-asset path (per layout-templates §Component — Tray icon implementation context).

- (layouts) Do NOT add gradients, shadows, multi-color fills, or embellishment to any of the 5 glyphs — line-based stroke design is the explicit constraint across all glyphs since brand DNA is shared (per layout-templates §Component — Tray icon SVG construction).

- (layouts) Do NOT introduce a glyph for the `✕` modal close button — layout-templates §Component — Investigation modal + §Component — Settings modal explicitly use the Unicode `✕` character. Adding an SVG close glyph creates inconsistency with the established modal pattern.

- (tests) NEVER include visual regression tests requiring human approval (Percy / Chromatic / Applitools) for SVG glyphs — agent cannot approve screenshots. DOM-attribute assertions only (per test-plan §11 Universal agent-driven).
- (tests) NEVER use `sleep(N)` for synchronization in component tests — wait for explicit render signal via Testing Library `findByRole` / equivalent (per test-plan §11 E2E).
- (tests) NEVER add retry-once policies for component rendering tests — first flake quarantines and root-causes (per test-plan §11 Quality).

- (a11y) NEVER render icons with `aria-label` + `role="img"` AND duplicate the same label on the parent `<button>` / `<a>` — produces double-announcement screen reader noise. One name per accessible target (per a11y-plan §11 SR anti-patterns).
- (a11y) NEVER make an icon focusable (`tabindex="0"` on the `<svg>` or inner `<g>`) — icons are presentational; focusability lives on the interactive wrapper (per a11y-plan §11 Keyboard).

- (a11y) NEVER ship state-indicator icons (success / error / info / warning glyphs) without enforcing the not-color-alone pairing at the registry's documented usage examples (per a11y-plan §11 Visual + §6 State color tokens).

- (a11y) NEVER pre-wire any kinetic SVG animation (e.g., `<animate>` / `<animateTransform>` inside the `circular-pulse` glyph) at chunk #11 — would lock motion ON without honoring `prefers-reduced-motion`. Motion tokens + `useReducedMotion` land at chunk #15 (per a11y-plan §11 Motion + route §2 chunk #15).
**Contract bindings:**

- **security ↔ a11y** (RECIPROCAL): SVG glyphs rendered as React components MUST carry `aria-hidden="true"` for decorative icons or `role="img"` + accessible name for meaningful icons — security cares because untyped SVGs are a content-injection surface; a11y cares because screen readers need correct semantics. Both domains converge on "static, declarative SVG attributes" as the implementation discipline. (security plan §Threat Model webview content + a11y-plan §11 SR anti-patterns + §4 Per-component pattern catalog.)

- **security ↔ design** (RECIPROCAL): SVGs are first-party static authored files, not generated from user input. Flag this gap so the `dep-security-ci-gate` bootstrap phase is updated when chunks #13/#15 (which definitely add npm a11y tooling) land. (security plan §Bootstrap phases `dep-security-ci-gate` + tests §9 CI Integration.)

(design-system.md §Iconography Rule "Icons clarify" + a11y-plan §4 Per-component patterns + §11 Visual.)

- **design ↔ a11y (color contrast)** (RECIPROCAL): glyph default `#E8EEF7` on `#1A1D24` base must satisfy ≥3:1 non-text contrast (WCAG SC 1.4.11) in any chrome surface; design provides token + target; chunk #12 contrast verification harness owns the per-pair JSON emission gate. (design-system.md §Color Palette Text Hierarchy + Downstream Readiness "For a11y specialist" + a11y-plan §6 Color contrast pairs.)

Registry exposes only the static SVG path. (design-system.md §Iconography "circular-pulse" + a11y-plan §11 Motion + §6 Motion tokens SC 2.3.3 + route §2 chunks #15 + #28.)

- **design ↔ tests (anti-pattern lint)** (UNILATERAL FROM design): glyph SVG content must not contain banned-effect markers — gradients, glassmorphic filters, `<animate>` blocks; the upcoming tests-domain motion-and-anti-pattern lint will scan registered components against design-system.md §Anti-Patterns. Tests extract is silent on this specific lint integration. (design-system.md Downstream Readiness "For tests specialist".)

- **layouts ↔ a11y (focus order)** (UNILATERAL FROM layouts → orchestrator note): titlebar settings button (aperture) and Investigate trigger (telescope) are focusable elements participating in surface tab order. Registry components must accept `aria-label` / `aria-hidden` props so consumers (titlebar at chunk #25, Investigate trigger at chunk #34) can wire correct semantics. - **a11y ↔ design (size grid + currentColor)** (RECIPROCAL): icon size grid (16/20/24) binds to a11y-plan §6 Target size tokens — registry sizes alone do NOT satisfy SC 2.5.8 (24×24 minimum); only the wrapping interactive target's computed CSS size does. Registry contract: every icon size variant must be embeddable inside a `--target-button-min` / `--target-input-min` wrapper without overflow. `currentColor` propagation contract: icon SVGs MUST use `currentColor` so the contrast harness measures inherited state color, not a hardcoded `#E8EEF7`. (a11y-plan §6 Target size tokens + §6 Contrast verification harness + design-system.md §Iconography.)

- **arch ↔ design (delegation)** (UNILATERAL FROM arch): webview source-file naming and React-component convention are explicitly delegated to design specialist. Design plan owns the icon-name list (aperture / telescope / constellation-grid / star / circular-pulse), the SVG geometry, the tray monochrome variant. Arch only constrains directory placement (`pulse-app/ui/src/components/icons/`) and workspace-boundary discipline. (arch §Conventions "Webview source files follow the design specialist's convention".)

- **arch ↔ a11y / arch ↔ tests** (UNILATERAL FROM arch): icon components landing here will gain `aria-label` / role / hidden semantics at chunk #13's a11y dev-stack install + per-component a11y review; arch surfaces no constraint beyond "no IPC = no capability ↔ procedure pairing required". When chunk #13's a11y-dev-stack lands (axe-core + Playwright), icon components become subjects of a11y tests run via Webview / browser harness. (arch §Cross-cutting Patterns "Webview IPC capability policy" + arch §Cross-cutting Patterns "Test-time telemetry injection".)

Orchestrator may need to surface to user — does chunk #11 land a JS test runner (Vitest is the Vite-native idiom + already implied by chunk #10's tooling), or defer all React testing to chunk #25 webview shell? Pure-leaf SVG components have minimal logic to test, so a `tsc --noEmit` typecheck gate alone may satisfy Standard tier for these components if orchestrator scopes coverage gates to Rust at this Foundation stage. data.head: ### Open question for Phase 4 / Phase 6 user review

body: The aggregate extracts surface **one major architectural decision** that orchestrator must resolve in plan.md or escalate to user review:
**Q1 — React + Vite tooling at chunk #11 vs defer to chunk #25?**

- **Land at #11 (full path):** introduce React 19 + react-dom 19 + Vite 7 (or chunk #10's @tailwindcss/cli equivalent) + Vitest + jsdom in `pulse-app/ui/package.json`; wire `npm run build` invoking Vite via `scripts/build.mjs` (preserving the chunk #10 `execFileSync(process.execPath, [<cli/index.mjs>, ...])` Windows hardening); dist output continues to land at `pulse-app/ui/dist/`. Chunk #13 a11y dev stack (route §2) and chunk #15 motion library (route §2) both require React tooling, so it lands somewhere in Foundation regardless. Earlier landing means chunk #11 components can be unit-tested + linted in isolation.

- **Defer to #25 (lighter path):** chunk #11 lands the SVG glyph source files as `.tsx` (typescript syntax checked via standalone `tsc --noEmit`) but no React runtime / Vite / test runner; consumers (chunks #13 / #15 / #25) bring their own React tooling when they need it. Lighter chunk; risks "but you can't render these without React" until chunk #25 lands.

Tests + security + arch all flag this question. Design + a11y are agnostic — both paths satisfy their constraints. Recommendation (Phase 4 plan default): **land React + Vite at chunk #11** because (a) chunk #13 (next chunk) already mandates `react-aria-components 1.17` per route §2 chunk text — the runtime is needed within 1 chunk anyway; (b) testability + lintability earned now compounds across chunks #13/#15/#25; (c) the meta-tooling "first React component" decision is best made once, with the registry's discipline as the witness.

- **Phase number:** 8

- **Route chunks covered:**
  - route#11 "Iconography registry — custom SVG glyphs (aperture/telescope/constellation-grid/star/circular-pulse) registered as React components at src/components/icons/"
- **Epoch:** Foundation (Epoch 1)

Land the project's first React components: 5 custom SVG glyph components (`aperture`, `telescope`, `constellation-grid`, `star`, `circular-pulse`) at `pulse-app/ui/src/components/icons/`, addressable both as named per-glyph components AND via the design-system-prescribed `<Icon glyph="..." />` dispatcher. body: **Constraints across domains:**

- (arch) LLM inference runtime MUST be `mistralrs = "=0.8.0"` (pin-exact, no caret) in workspace `Cargo.toml`; never relax к caret or floating constraint (per arch §Established Decisions [LLM Inference Runtime] §Pin discipline).

- (arch) The async inference trait MUST be `pub trait LlmInferenceRunner: Send + Sync` with `Pin<Box<dyn Future + Send + 'a>>` returns, declared in `crates/interpretation/src/contract.rs`; the trait surface MUST NOT import `mistralrs::*` (per arch §Established Decisions [LLM Inference Runtime] §Bus factor mitigation).

- (arch) The concrete `MistralRsInference` impl MUST live at `pulse-app/src/mistralrs_inference.rs` (binary boundary), NOT in the `interpretation` lib crate, к preserve the swap-к-candle path (per arch §Established Decisions [LLM Inference Runtime] §Documented upgrade path).

- (arch) JSON-constrained inference MUST use mistral.rs strict-schema mode (llguidance integration); chunk #83 plan MUST include а Step 0 spike — feed а 100-token L3 digest fixture into strict-schema mode + assert JSON round-trips + fail-fast if API surface regressed since v0.8.0 publication (per arch §Established Decisions [LLM Inference Runtime] §Caveat к verify).

- (arch) L4 inference output schema payload types (the L4 digest report struct with `schema_version` / `prompt_version` / `model_tier` / `hardware_profile` / `is_resolution_summary` fields) MUST implement `serde::Serialize` + `serde::Deserialize` (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns Cross-bridge data shape).

- (arch) Internal-only inference error types MUST be `thiserror` 2.x enums in the `interpretation` crate; conversion к `AppError::Internal { message }` happens at the binary boundary only IF the error reaches а TauRPC procedure (per arch §Conventions Error response schema + §Established Decisions [Error Handling Pattern]). Chunk #83 introduces no new TauRPC, so error sanitization is internal-only к the `incidents` payload flow.

- (arch) No new workspace crate name MAY be introduced. The `interpretation` crate from #82 is reserved per §Occupied Resources Cargo workspace crate names. Code lives in `crates/interpretation/` + `pulse-app/src/mistralrs_inference.rs` only.

- (arch) Cross-crate state delivery into the L4 inference resolver MUST follow the established `Arc<dyn Trait>` injection pattern (per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-16 / 2026-05-19 / 2026-05-23 entries): digest input + incident sink injected at the binary boundary. No reverse dep edges (interpretation MUST NOT depend on triage/corpus directly via Cargo edge).

- (security) L3 digest content + corpus retrieval context feeding the LLM input MUST be treated as user-controlled telemetry content (per §Threat Model Type 5 PII-scrubbed projections). The LLM input assembly path MUST consume the already-scrubbed corpus projection rather than re-reading raw OTLP attribute values from `buffer::` ring buffer tables.

- (security) LLM output MUST go through `serde` deserialization with bounded field shapes (smart enums for `decision` / `severity` / `model_tier` / `hardware_profile`; bounded String lengths for `title` / `symptom` / `timeline` / `justification`) before crossing into corpus persistence or `pulse://stream/incidents` broadcast (per §Input Validation row TauRPC bridge + §Anti-Pattern Code Patterns serde_json+size-cap rule).

- (security) LLM output size MUST be bounded before parse — defense-in-depth size cap on resulting bytes (e.g., 16 KB per inference output) MUST be enforced before `serde_json::from_slice::<L4Output>(buf)?` (per §Anti-Pattern Code Patterns serde_json size-bound rule + §Input Validation row plugin-Arrow-IPC size-cap precedent).

- (security) Errors crossing TauRPC bridge from L4 inference MUST collapse к `serde`-friendly `AppError` variants (`AppError::Internal { message }` sanitized one-liner). NEVER serialize `anyhow::Error` or expose mistralrs internal error chain / model file paths / GPU device strings / tokenizer struct names (per §Error Handling TauRPC bridge bullet).

- (security) mistralrs first concrete `use mistralrs::*` import + transitive deps enter build graph — `cargo deny check bans licenses sources` MUST pass; new duplicates added к `deny.toml [bans] skip` with one-line provenance comments (per §Dependency Security CI integration + 2026-05-03 session learning).

- (security) Chunk #72 `security::scrubber::scrub_attribute` uniform coverage discipline applies к ANY new persistence boundary — if L4 output is archived к corpus `digest_archive`, the archival path MUST route through `scrub_attribute()` for any free-text fields (`title` / `symptom` / `timeline` / `justification`) that may transitively echo PII via the LLM's reasoning (per §Anti-Pattern Logging uniform scrubber coverage paragraph + chunk #72 lesson).

- (tests) Standard tier coverage thresholds apply unconditionally к new code in `crates/interpretation/`: ≥75% line / ≥70% branch / ≥85% function (per test-plan §10 Coverage thresholds + dist-arch v3 §L4 "80%+ coverage of schema parsing and failure paths").

- (tests) L4 schema validation tests MUST be constructed-JSON parse tests (positive valid-shape + negative malformed-JSON / missing-required-field / wrong-enum-value scenarios); LLM output quality assertions are explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for unit tests, deferred к Conductor scenarios per route §83.

- (tests) Tests crossing the binary boundary MUST use trait-based stub injection: stub `LlmInferenceRunner` returning canned JSON strings vs spawning real mistralrs (per test-plan §8 "What TO mock — External services not under test").

- (tests) Parse failure counter tests MUST cover all enumerated failure modes (malformed JSON / schema mismatch / required field absent / enum out-of-range / numeric out-of-bounds) and assert one increment per failure (per dist-arch v3 §L4 + obs binding к `pipeline.l4.inferences_total{result}` metric).

- (tests) Step 0 spike test MUST fail-fast with а clear `expect(...)` message if mistralrs v0.8.0 strict-schema-mode API surface has regressed; feed а representative 100-token L3 digest fixture, assert JSON parses round-trip (per arch caveat + test-plan §11 Unit anti-pattern).
- (tests) Fixture pattern: `rstest` 0.26.1 `#[fixture]` builders for canned L3 digest input + expected JSON output shapes (per test-plan §7 Fixture library).

- (tests) Tests MUST NOT include network calls, file I/O outside `tempfile::TempDir`, or real model file load в the unit/integration test path — model load constructor-injected via stub (per test-plan §11 Universal).

- (obs) Self-observation runtime stays `tracing` 0.1 + `tracing-subscriber` JSON formatter + `tracing-appender` daily file sink only — NO OTel SDK for the new `crates/interpretation/` inference path (per obs-plan §3 Tracing init).

- (obs) New L4 metric events MUST use the canonical `metric.{module}.{measure}` target prefix; chunk #83 specifies exactly three targets: `pipeline.l4.inferences_total` (Counter, labels `result ∈ {success, parse_failure, runtime_error, timeout}`), `pipeline.l4.inference_latency_p99_milliseconds` (Distribution, ms, per inference), `pipeline.l4.inference_queue_depth` (Gauge per heartbeat tick) (per obs-plan §5 + route §83).

- (obs) Inference handler MUST carry `#[tracing::instrument(skip(prompt, digest, raw_output), fields(span.kind = "internal", model_tier, hardware_profile, prompt_version, schema_version, digest_kind))]` discipline — `skip` excludes prompt body / digest payload / raw model output from span fields (per obs-plan §4 Span instrumentation + §8 PII scrubbing-at-source).

- (obs) Metric label cardinality discipline applies: `model_tier ∈ {primary, fallback}`, `hardware_profile ∈ {gpu-primary, gpu-fallback, cpu-primary, cpu-fallback}`, `result ∈ {success, parse_failure, runtime_error, timeout}` — never per-inference-ID or `digest_id` labels (per obs-plan §5 + §Obs Anti-Patterns Metrics).

- (obs) L4 inference is perf-budget-critical path per dist-arch v3 §L4 hardware profile matrix; inference handler MUST emit per-event `value = duration_ms` on `metric.pipeline.l4.inference_latency_p99_milliseconds` so post-test `jq` aggregation can assert p99 against the profile-specific budget (per obs-plan §10 Performance budgets + §5 Distribution convention).

- (obs) Inference handler MUST update `pipeline.l4.inference_queue_depth` gauge from the cadence coordinator's invocation queue every heartbeat tick (15s per obs-plan §3 Heartbeat ticks) — not per-enqueue/dequeue.

- (obs) Zero-unlogged-panics invariant applies: any panic inside model inference / tokenizer / JSON parse MUST be captured by the existing `std::panic::set_hook`; runtime errors at the `LlmInferenceRunner` boundary MUST emit as `tracing::error!(target: "interpretation.inference.error", model_tier, hardware_profile, error_category, ...)` with category enum, never raw `Debug` of the underlying error (per obs-plan §7 Error capture).
**Patterns к follow:**

- (arch) Trait-in-lower-crate + impl-at-binary-boundary (state delivery): construct `Arc<dyn Trait>` views at `pulse-app/src/main.rs` setup closure; inject through constructors (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns Module dependency direction + CLAUDE.md 2026-05-16 entry).

- (arch) Async trait via manual `Pin<Box<dyn Future + Send + 'a>>` (no async-trait macro dep): mirrors the existing `LlmInferenceRunner` from chunk #82 + the 2026-05-23 `SqlQueryRunner` precedent. Type alias keeps signatures readable: `type InferenceFuture<'a, T> = Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<T, InferenceError>> + Send + 'a>>;`.

- (arch) Feature-gate hygiene NOT required for mistralrs runtime: unlike `mcp-server` / `otap-ingest`, the L4 runtime is а Foundation v0.2.0 default-on capability (per arch §Established Decisions [LLM Inference Runtime]). `MistralRsInference` impl lives in pulse-app source directly without `#[cfg(feature = ...)]` gating.

- (arch) Cross-bridge data shape discipline: all types crossing к the webview via `pulse://stream/incidents` or written к corpus `digest_archive` MUST implement `serde::Serialize` + `serde::Deserialize` (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns Cross-bridge data shape).

- (arch) Provenance, not invalidation: the output schema's `schema_version` / `prompt_version` fields support old corpus records remaining queryable with version annotations — а forward-compat pattern.

- (security) PII scrubber at persistence boundary: invoke `security::scrubber::scrub_attribute` returning `ScrubbedValue::{Allowed, Redacted}` BEFORE writing any LLM free-text output к `digest_archive` table or `pulse://stream/incidents` broadcast (per §Anti-Pattern Logging uniform scrubber coverage paragraph; pattern at `crates/buffer/src/appender.rs:332-356`).

- (security) Bounded output deserialize: `let buf = inference_output_bytes; ensure_size_bounded(&buf, MAX_L4_OUTPUT_BYTES)?; let parsed: L4Output = serde_json::from_slice(&buf).map_err(|e| InferenceError::SchemaViolation { reason: sanitize(e.to_string()) })?;` (per §Anti-Pattern Code Patterns serde_json+size-cap rule).

- (security) AppError boundary error conversion: free-function `pub fn inference_error_to_app_error(err: interpretation::InferenceError) -> AppError { ... }` at the binary boundary, mirroring the 2026-05-18 session learning `corpus_error_to_app_error` precedent for Rust orphan-rule resolution.

data.head: ### Chunk route#84: "L4 LLM runtime swap (mistralrs → llama.cpp subprocess D1)"

body: **Constraints across domains:**

- (security) Subprocess invocation of `llama-cli.exe` MUST treat the binary path AND every argument as deeply untrusted with respect to command injection: never construct args by string interpolation of OTLP-derived attribute values, fingerprints, digest fields, or any string field reaching the inference runner from a `pulse://stream/digests` payload. All variable inputs (rendered prompt, schema) MUST flow through stdin (`-st --simple-io`) or file paths (`--json-schema-file <static-path>`), never `Command::arg(user_input)` (per security plan §Security Anti-Patterns §Code Patterns first bullet — MCP STDIO command-injection cluster CVE-2025-49596 / -54994 / -54136 / -22252).

- (security) `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_LLAMA_CUDA_BIN` and `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_LLAMA_CPU_BIN` env vars MUST be canonicalized via `strict-path` and asserted to point at an executable on disk before spawn — same pattern as `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_PLUGIN_DIR` (per security plan §Input Validation row "CLI / env var inputs" + §Security Anti-Patterns §Input env-var canonicalization bullet — CWE-22 path traversal class).

- (security, arch, obs, tests) Subprocess discipline MUST stack FOUR bounds simultaneously: (a) `kill_on_drop(true)` on `tokio::process::Command`; (b) explicit `-n {max_tokens}` argument; (c) `-st` single-turn flag forbidding conversation-mode auto-continue; (d) outer `tokio::time::timeout` wall-clock guard wrapping the entire await chain. Missing ANY one constitutes a regression — defense-in-depth, two runaways during chunk #82/#84 spike track came from missing bounds (per CLAUDE.md Tier 2 session learning 2026-05-25 "Subprocess discipline for long-running external tools" + arch §Established Decisions [LLM Inference Runtime] subprocess invocation discipline paragraph + obs-plan + testing.md §Session Additions 2026-05-25).

- (security, arch, tests) `mistralrs = "=0.8.0"` workspace dep + per-crate `mistralrs.workspace = true` in `pulse-app/Cargo.toml` MUST be REMOVED in the same commit that lands `LlamaCliInference`, not deferred — load-bearing for `cargo deny check bans` posture + arch §Cross-cutting "no sibling crate-graph expansion" + tests `cargo deny check bans licenses sources` clean post-removal (per security plan §Dependency Security + arch §Established Decisions [LLM Inference Runtime] paragraph + test-plan §11 Anti-Patterns Strategy "NEVER skip `cargo deny check bans`").

- (security, obs) L4 inference subprocess stdout (the LLM-generated JSON) is functionally equivalent к an MCP tool response body and MUST NOT be logged verbatim — apply §Logging NEVER-log rule for "MCP tool response bodies" + `llama-cli` writes prompt-echo + token stream which can echo OTLP attribute values surfaced in the digest prompt (transitive PII leakage Vector 1). Log only `result` enum (`success`/`schema_invalid`/`timeout`/`exit_nonzero`/`spawn_failed`), `output_bytes` length, and aggregate latency (per security plan §Logging "What NEVER to log" + obs-plan §11 + arch §Critical Warnings).

- (security, obs) AppError at the TauRPC bridge MUST sanitize subprocess failure modes (binary-not-found, spawn-failed, kill-on-timeout, non-zero exit, schema-validation-failed) into `AppError::Internal { message: <sanitized-one-liner> }` — never expose subprocess command-line strings, binary absolute paths, CUDA driver version strings, or model file paths (per security plan §Error Handling + obs-plan §7 + §8 Vector 2 + arch §Standard Contracts Error response schema).

- (arch) Concrete `LlamaCliInference` impl MUST live at the `pulse-app/` binary boundary, NOT in `crates/interpretation/` — the `LlmInferenceRunner: Send + Sync` trait + `Pin<Box<dyn Future + Send + 'a>>` future-return alias + `ModelTier`/`ModelStatus`/`ModelIdentity`/`ModelLoadEvent`/`InferenceError` contract types stay в `crates/interpretation/src/contract.rs` UNCHANGED; ONLY the concrete `MistralRsInference` → `LlamaCliInference` swap happens (per arch §Established Decisions [LLM Inference Runtime — L4 interpretation layer] Bus factor mitigation paragraph).

- (arch) Hardware-tier routing MUST consume chunk #80 `HardwareProfileSource` trait output: GPU-primary / GPU-fallback → CUDA binary + `-ngl 99`; CPU-primary / CPU-fallback → CPU binary + `-ngl 0` (per arch §Established Decisions [LLM Inference Runtime] Tier routing paragraph + §Stack and Technologies AI/ML serving row).

- (arch) `llama.cpp` build version MUST pin к `b9305` (pin-exact discipline mirroring original `mistralrs = "=0.8.0"`, bumps as deliberate chunk-scoped events only, never via latest-tag drift) — record build tag в workspace Cargo.toml comment block / xtask manifest с provenance comment (per arch §Established Decisions [LLM Inference Runtime] Pin discipline paragraph).
- (arch) `InferenceError` crossing the TauRPC bridge MUST remain serde-friendly (per arch §Standard Contracts Error response schema + §Critical Warnings).

- (obs) Self-observation runtime stays `tracing` 0.1 + `tracing-subscriber` 0.3 JSON formatter only — the new `LlamaCliInference` impl MUST NOT introduce ANY OTel SDK / `opentelemetry-*` crate, even transitively (per obs-plan §3 Tracing init + §11 Universal anti-patterns "NEVER link an OTel SDK into the product's self-observation runtime").

- (obs) NO new high-cardinality fields admitted к AllowList — explicitly NEVER `model_path` / `checkpoint_url` / `binary_path` / `cuda_dll_path` / `llama_cpp_tag` / `pid` / `command_line`. The `_label: String`-from-source-fn pattern applies for any subprocess metadata that needs serialization (per obs-plan §11 Spans anti-patterns + Session Additions 2026-05-17 + CLAUDE.md security.md Session Additions 2026-05-24).

- (obs) `interpretation.{model.load, inference.request, inference.error}` AllowList field sets unchanged at the trait boundary. If new signal dimensions are added (`process.spawn`, `process.exit`, `process.killed`, etc.), they MUST land as new per-target AllowList entries в `pulse-app/src/observability.rs::AllowList::production()` AND get covered by the existing test pattern `allowlist_for_target_resolves_l4_inference_pipeline_targets` shape (per obs-plan §8 default-deny scrubbing + arch §Established Decisions [LLM Inference Runtime] bus-factor mitigation).

- (tests) Standard tier coverage thresholds remain in force on the new `LlamaCliInference` concrete impl: ≥75% line / ≥70% branch / ≥85% function (per test-plan §10 Quality Gates). Spawn-arg construction + tier-routing match + timeout/cap wiring are pure-function shaped and must be unit-tested without invoking the real binary.

- (tests) The L4 runtime + GGUF model file are NOT present in CI. All chunk #84 tests MUST be runnable end-to-end with no network / no GGUF / no llama-cli binary on disk (per test-plan §2 "no human-in-loop verification, no real network except localhost stub, deterministic"). Real-binary tests must be `#[ignore]`-gated.

- (tests) Tests added к `pulse-app/src/llamacli_inference.rs` MUST NOT use the `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` source-level form because `pulse-app/Cargo.toml` has `[lib] test = false` (Windows WebView2 workaround); place them under `pulse-app/tests/unit_llamacli_inference.rs` (per `.claude/rules/testing.md` Session Additions 2026-05-20).

- (tests) `cargo xtask capability-drift` must pass post-chunk; no new TauRPC procedures added, but the `emit_taurpc_bindings` test re-emission discipline applies because `pulse-app/src/main.rs` is touched (per `.claude/rules/testing.md` 2026-05-19 entry — pre-commit `grep -c '"mcp":' pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts ≥1` enforced).
**Patterns к follow:**

- (arch) **Bus-factor sibling-impl swap through unchanged trait surface**: chunk #82 deliberately designed `LlmInferenceRunner` so concrete impl could swap without trait redesign; `LlamaCliInference` joins as the second sibling impl following the established `MistralRsInference` precedent (per arch §Established Decisions [LLM Inference Runtime] bus-factor + three documented swap paths paragraphs).

Preserves "Workspace deps delta: none" discipline (per CLAUDE.md §Session Learnings 2026-05-23 + chunk #82 substrate).

- (arch) **Env-var-driven binary path resolution at boot (lowest-friction dev pattern)**: `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_LLAMA_CUDA_BIN` + `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_LLAMA_CPU_BIN` for v0.2.0 dev cycle; production distribution path (Tauri bundle vs `xtask` download vs user-managed) explicitly deferred (per arch §Established Decisions [LLM Inference Runtime] Caveat-к-verify paragraph).

- (arch) **Background-cadence-driven L4 invocation pattern justifies D1 over D2**: real rate 1-4 invocations/min via `pulse://stream/digests` subscriber (chunk #81); LWW queue absorbs cadence-faster-than-L4 bursts; no user-action L4 trigger; cold-start ~5s happens behind no user-visible spinner (per arch §Established Decisions [LLM Inference Runtime] D1-vs-D2 paragraph + CLAUDE.md §Session Learnings 2026-05-25).

- (security) Strict-path env var canonicalization: pre-existing pattern for `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_PLUGIN_DIR` / `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` / `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_CONFIG_PATH` — apply the same canonicalize-and-assert pattern to the two new llama-cli binary path env vars (per security plan §Bootstrap phases `input-validation-library-install`).

- (security) Tracing instrumentation at all subprocess-spawn call sites uses `#[tracing::instrument(skip(prompt))]` к keep rendered digest prompt out of span fields (per security plan §Secret Management discipline — analogous к `#[tracing::instrument(skip(key))]` pattern).

- (security) `From<X> for AppError` impls at the binary boundary sanitize subprocess errors into stable variants — mirror the `corpus_error_to_app_error` free-fn approach (per session learning 2026-05-18 cross-crate error mapping). Define `pub fn llama_inference_error_to_app_error(err: LlamaCliError) -> AppError` in `pulse-app/src/llamacli_inference.rs`.

- (obs) Chunk #82 AllowList shape at `pulse-app/src/observability.rs:1703-1771` + chunk #83 shape at lines 1773-1846 — extend in place if new subprocess-lifecycle targets are introduced; mirror per-target `[fields].iter().copied().collect()` literal-array shape verbatim.

- (obs) Default-deny `AllowList::for_target()` resolver order: exact-match → strip-suffix `.tick` → `split('.').next()` → `split("::").next()`. For dotted sub-namespaces (e.g. `interpretation.subprocess.spawn`), add EXPLICIT per-leaf entries; otherwise fields silently redact. - (obs) `metric.pipeline.l4.inferences_total` + `metric.pipeline.l4.inference_latency_p99_milliseconds` + `metric.pipeline.l4.inference_queue_depth` continue к be emitted at same call sites; `result` field enum EXTENDED (not replaced) к accommodate subprocess-failure cases (`spawn_failed`, `exit_nonzero`).

- (obs) Heartbeat-tick discipline: L4 inference subscriber is long-running and SHOULD continue emitting `interpretation.tick` (if already wired); subprocess spawn-per-generation does NOT mean per-spawn-process ticks. Aggregate per-tick: `inferences_total_since_last_tick`, `subprocess_spawn_failures_count`, `subprocess_timeouts_count`, `subprocess_exit_nonzero_count`.
