- **Phase number:** 91
- **Route chunks covered:** route#94 "MCP server + tool exposure"
- **Epoch:** Epoch 9 — Foundation v0.2.0 (TERMINAL chunk of the epoch + the 94-chunk route)

- **Group reason:** single-substantial — extends the existing `mcp-server` crate with 4 new tools + 1 new TauRPC procedure + config flag + 1 webview button; multi-crate (mcp-server + pulse-app + ui-bridge + triage/corpus reuse) + multi-domain (backend MCP + IPC + config + UI + tests); terminal chunk so no successor to group with.

**Capabilities:** P-039 (MCP Delivery When Configured), P-040 (MCP Independence — verified by configurable off-by-default).
**Depends on:** #78 (incident records), #87/#88 (Report content + markdown serialization). Both landed.
**Summary:** MCP server exposes four tools — `query_incident_list`, `retrieve_report(id)`, `retrieve_telemetry_slice(id)`, `mark_incident_resolved(id)`. Server enabled via `[mcp.enable]` config (default false). Connected agent identity tracked; "Send to agent" button in the Diagnostic Report toolbar visible only when both configured AND agent connected. MCP delivery markdown content IDENTICAL to clipboard delivery (P-038).
**Constraints across domains:**

- (arch) The `mcp-server` crate is a LOCKED reserved workspace member that ALREADY EXISTS — EXTEND it, do NOT create a new crate nor rename. The 4 new tools join the existing `#[tool]` set alongside `query_traces`/`query_metrics`/`query_logs`/`generate_snapshot` (per arch §Established Decisions [MCP Server Surface] + §Stack MCP server row).

- (arch) MCP surface stays spec-conformant: JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio; new tools via standard `tools/list` + `tools/call`; no custom wire format (per arch §Conventions External wire — MCP server + §Established Decisions [API Style — MCP Server Surface 3]).

- (arch) MCP errors use the standard JSON-RPC 2.0 error object (numeric `code`, `message`, optional `data`) — NOT the AppError enum on the stdio surface (per arch §Conventions Error response schema (MCP)).

- (arch / security) The new `mcp.status()` TauRPC procedure follows `<router>.<verb>` dotted `snake_case` AND requires BOTH router registration AND a `pulse-app/capabilities/` entry (router-level granularity) or it is silently rejected at runtime; `xtask capability-drift` enforces. `mcp.status` already appears in §Occupied Resources as part of `mcp.{status,start,stop}` — verify whether this chunk EXTENDS the existing procedure's return shape (connected-agent identity) vs adds a sibling (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns Webview IPC capability policy + §Conventions Endpoint naming; security plan §API Security TauRPC capability authorization).

- (security / arch) Preserve the MCP double-gate: compile-time `--features mcp-server` AND runtime `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED=true`; the new `[mcp.enable]` config (default `false`, P-040) is an ADDITIONAL enablement layer whose relationship to the env-var gate MUST be resolved at plan time (config precedence: env > config.toml > defaults). Preserve the graceful-degrade `warn` (env/config set against a no-feature build) — do not fail-startup (per security plan §API Security MCP double-gate + §Code Patterns ban 3; arch §Stack MCP server).

- (security) The 4 tools' telemetry/incident reads route through `Connection::prepare` + `?` placeholders (and/or the corpus reader's parameterized path) — NEVER `format!`-interpolated SQL; agent-supplied `id` never names a table/column (per security plan §Input Validation + §Anti-Patterns §Input ban 2).

- (security) `mark_incident_resolved(id)` MUST NOT pass any agent-supplied string into `tokio::process::Command::new(...).arg(...)` — route the mutation through the existing typed `incidents.mark_resolved` resolver / `IncidentPersistence`, not a shell/subprocess (per security plan §Anti-Patterns §Code Patterns ban 1).

- (security / arch) MCP report-markdown content MUST be PII-scrubbed identically to the clipboard delivery path (P-038 parity) — chunk #88's resolver-side `scrub_attribute` discipline produces the same Report payload; single rendering source, not a parallel formatter (per security plan §Logging & Monitoring snapshot/clipboard/MCP hygiene; arch §Cross-cutting Cross-bridge data shape).

- (security / arch) `rmcp` stays at the existing workspace-resolved version (the route note: "verify existing rmcp is sufficient for server-side") — do NOT silently bump/float; the rmcp dependency stays feature-gated so default-features builds don't pull it into the closure (per security plan §Dependency Security Pinning; arch §Cross-cutting Feature-gate hygiene).

- (security / arch) MCP errors + the `mcp.status()` return cross the bridge sanitized: `mcp.status()` returns `Result<T, AppError>` with no stack traces / paths / library versions / Rust struct names; any incident/report types surfaced over TauRPC are `serde::Serialize` (per security plan §Error Handling + arch §Cross-cutting Cross-bridge data shape).

- (obs) mcp-server is boundary-only instrumentation: spans at the stdin/stdout JSON-RPC boundary; tool handlers get `#[tracing::instrument]` but tool RESPONSE BODIES are never logged (per obs-plan §1 instrumentation-scope + §4 P3).

- (obs) When run as the rmcp stdio sidecar, `tracing-subscriber` writer is forced to `std::io::stderr` JSON-only — stdout reserved exclusively for JSON-RPC 2.0 framing (per obs-plan §3 Logging stack + §6 Sink configuration).

- (design) The "Send to agent" button uses only `var(--*)` design tokens (no hardcoded hex/px), the SECONDARY-button token set (`--color-raised-1` bg + `--color-text-primary` + subtle Earth-Blue border + `--radius-sm`) — NOT the primary Earth-Blue fill reserved for the existing "Copy markdown" primary (per design-system.md §Surface desktop-webview Component Patterns > Buttons).

- (design) Hover transition at `--duration-fast` with `motion-reduce:transition-none motion-reduce:duration-0`; send-result feedback conveyed with text (and/or icon), never color alone (per design-system.md §Motion Accessibility + §Anti-Patterns "NEVER use color purely for decoration").

- (layouts) The button lives in the Diagnostic Report toolbar (modal-class surface) co-located with the existing chunk-#88 "Copy markdown" action as a peer toolbar action — NOT a new modal/panel/tab; the optional `[mcp.enable]` control belongs in the existing Settings modal form-section stack as a checkbox+label+helper-text (per layout-templates.md §Component — Investigation modal + §Component — Settings modal).

- (a11y) The button is a native `<button>` with an accessible name + `aria-busy` during async send, activatable by Enter/Space; conditional visibility implemented by conditional DOM render/removal (NOT `aria-hidden` on a focusable element); `:focus-visible` renders `--border-focus`; ≥24×24 CSS px target; label meets SC 1.4.3 4.5:1, connected state not color-alone (per a11y plan §4 Button + §5/§6 + §11 Screen Reader).
**Patterns to follow:**

- (arch) TauRPC-router-per-crate + binding registration: the `mcp.status` extension follows the existing `pulse-app/src/mcp_router.rs` resolver shape at the binary boundary (per arch §Conventions Workspace API style).

- (arch) Shared single-domain-concept: the new `retrieve_report` / `query_incident_list` / `mark_incident_resolved` tools reuse the SAME incident/report primitives the chunk #78/#88 IPC resolvers consume (`incidents.get_report` / `incidents.list_active` / `incidents.mark_resolved`) — not duplicate logic (per arch §Cross-cutting Cross-bridge data shape + §Design Philosophy Token-efficient curation).

- (security) Five-place cfg-gate pattern for the feature-gated MCP namespace: new `mcp.status()` procedure + router wiring in `pulse-app/src/main.rs` + the `emit_taurpc_bindings` test merge all behind `#[cfg(feature = "mcp-server")]` (the `mcp_server_crate` alias only exists when the feature is on) — follow the chunk #49 `mcp.{status,start,stop}` precedent (per CLAUDE.md security rules 2026-05-12).

- (security) Cross-crate state into the resolver via `Arc<dyn Trait>` injection (connected-agent identity / corpus incident reader threaded through the resolver's `::new(...)`), `corpus::Error → AppError` via a free `map_err` fn at the binary boundary (per CLAUDE.md security rules 2026-05-16 + 2026-05-18).

- (security / tests) Bindings.ts regen discipline: any default-features `cargo run`/`cargo nextest`/`cargo tauri dev` rewrites `pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` to the no-mcp shape — run the regen-via-`mcp-server`-feature step as the final pre-commit action; verify `grep -c '"mcp":' bindings/index.ts ≥1` + clean capability-drift (per CLAUDE.md security rules 2026-05-19).

- (obs) Boundary span chain per tool call: parent `mcp.tools.call.request` (fields `method`, `params_count`) → child query/lookup → `mcp.tools.call.response` (fields `result_type`, `result_count`) — mirror the §4 P3 `query_traces` precedent; extend the mcp-server allowlist for any new field, keeping `result_content` excluded (per obs-plan §4 + §8 allowlist).

- (tests) P3 E2E shape: boot `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED=true --features mcp-server` → spawn via piped `tokio::process::Command` → seed buffer/incidents via OTLP → write `tools/call` JSON-RPC frame → parse line-delimited stdout → assert `result` present → cleanup, assert exit 0, no zombie (per test-plan §6 P3).

- (arch / security) Do NOT regress the double-gate to a single gate, and do NOT couple MCP into a non-optional path — pulse MUST be fully functional with MCP disabled (P-040).

- (security) The 4 tools' reads use `Connection::prepare` + `?` placeholders (no `format!` SQL); `cargo deny check bans licenses sources` + `cargo audit` pass with no new banned/unpinned dependency.

title: Phase 91 Plan — chunk route#94: "MCP server + tool exposure"

data.head: # Phase 91 Plan — chunk route#94: "MCP server + tool exposure"

body:
_Generated by /andromeda-phase Phase 4. Read by /andromeda-implement.
Manual edits between runs are fine; do not edit during /implement run._
- **Phase number:** 91

- **Route chunks covered:**
  - route#94 "MCP server + tool exposure"
- **Epoch:** Epoch 9 — Foundation v0.2.0 (TERMINAL chunk of the epoch + the 94-chunk route)

Expose the existing incident/report machinery (chunk #78 incident records + chunk #88 Diagnostic Report markdown) to AI agents over the MCP stdio sidecar as a THIRD output channel, alongside (1) the in-app Diagnostic Report and (2) clipboard markdown. The chunk extends the EXISTING `crates/mcp-server/` (a reserved, locked workspace crate — NOT a new crate) with four `#[tool]` methods (`query_incident_list`, `retrieve_report(id)`, `retrieve_telemetry_slice(id)`, `mark_incident_resolved(id)`), extends the existing `mcp.status()` TauRPC return shape with a connected-agent label, adds a default-off `[mcp.enable]` config flag, and adds one conditionally-visible "Send to agent" button to the Diagnostic Report toolbar. Per arch §Established Decisions [MCP Server Surface] + [API Style — MCP Server Surface 3], the surface stays spec-conformant JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio; per security plan §API Security the double-gate (`--features mcp-server` + `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED`) is preserved and `[mcp.enable]` composes above it; per obs-plan §4 P3 each tool emits boundary spans with `result_type`/`result_count` only (never response bodies, Vector 4); per P-038 the MCP report markdown is byte-identical to the clipboard markdown.

**Architecture decision (Phase 1 user-approved, Option A "Corpus-backed subprocess"):** the MCP sidecar is a SEPARATE process (`andromeda-pulse-mcp`) with its own empty ephemeral DuckDB and no live handle to the main process's `IncidentRegistry` or ring buffer (research.md confirms cross-process buffer sharing was deferred). The four new tools therefore read/write the on-disk `corpus/corpus.db` (cross-process accessible via `CorpusReader`/`CorpusWriter`), which the sidecar already locates via `resolve_data_dir()`. Consequences accepted by the user: `retrieve_telemetry_slice(id)` returns persisted incident context (evidence refs + digest), NOT live telemetry rows; `mark_incident_resolved` is eventually-consistent vs the in-memory registry (durably correct in corpus; re-hydrated at next boot); `mcp.status()` "connected" = sidecar-running. The chunk spec's "MCP = one of three equal-tier output channels" arch.md §Established-Decisions BODY change is STRUCTURAL and OUT OF SCOPE here (registry-only `--allow-arch-registry` cannot apply it) — it stays deferred to a deliberate `/andromeda-arch` touch (record this in the wrap-session handoff). P-038 identity is preserved by moving only the ~135-line `assemble_report` glue from `pulse-app/src/incidents_router.rs:567` into `interpretation::markdown` (where `serialize_report` already lives); the only new Cargo dep edge is `interpretation → security`.

1. Confirm `crates/interpretation/Cargo.toml` does NOT already depend on `security`, and that `security` depends on no in-workspace crate (verify the `interpretation → security` edge introduces no cycle). `cargo tree -p interpretation` / read `crates/security/Cargo.toml`.

2. Confirm the bincode config used by `pulse-app/src/incident_persistence.rs::CorpusIncidentPersistence` for the Incident BLOB encode (research.md Open Question #4). Grep `bincode::` in `incident_persistence.rs`. If a non-default `Options` is used, the sidecar decode MUST use the identical config — extract the encode/decode pair to a shared helper (`triage::contract` or `interpretation::markdown`) so write + read share one definition.
3. Confirm `triage::contract::Incident` + nested types all derive `serde::Deserialize` (needed for the sidecar's bincode decode). (Research confirms; re-verify after any contract churn.)
1. Add `security = { path = "../security" }` to `crates/interpretation/Cargo.toml [dependencies]`.

2. Move `assemble_report(incident: &Incident, l4: Option<&L4Output>) -> Report` + the label helpers (`scrub_string`, `incident_status_label`, `severity_label`, `l4_confidence_label`, `hex_lower`) from `pulse-app/src/incidents_router.rs:567-700` INTO `crates/interpretation/src/markdown.rs` as `pub fn`s. They already operate on `interpretation::markdown::{Report, HypothesisView, InvestigationStepView}` + `interpretation::schema::{L4Output, Confidence}` + `triage::contract::{Incident, IncidentStatus, Severity}` + `security::scrubber::scrub_attribute` — all reachable from `interpretation`.

3. In `pulse-app/src/incidents_router.rs`, DELETE the moved fns; change `get_report` to call `interpretation::markdown::assemble_report(&incident, parsed_l4.as_ref())` (behavior unchanged — same Report, same `serialize_report`, same degraded-mode logic). Keep the `ReportPayload` construction (specta cross-bridge view) in incidents_router.rs.
4. Run `cargo nextest run -p interpretation` + `-p pulse-app --test unit_incident_persistence` (or the get_report-covering integration test) to confirm the move is behavior-preserving.

1. Add `fn load_incident_by_id(&self, id: i64) -> Result<Option<IncidentRowRaw>, Error>` to the `CorpusWriter` trait (`crates/corpus/src/contract.rs`) — `SELECT ... FROM incidents WHERE id = ?1` (prepared statement; decrypt the payload BLOB; return `Ok(None)` when no row). Mirror the `load_active_incidents` decrypt shape.
2. Add the impl on `Corpus`. Add a colocated corpus crate test (`load_incident_by_id` returns the row after `save_incident`, `None` for a missing id).

title: Step 3 — Extend the MCP sidecar context + the 4 new tools

data.head: ### Step 3 — Extend the MCP sidecar context + the 4 new tools

body: 1. Add deps to `crates/mcp-server/Cargo.toml`: `corpus = { path = "../corpus" }`, `triage = { path = "../triage" }`, `interpretation = { path = "../interpretation" }`, `bincode` (for Incident BLOB decode). (security comes transitively via interpretation.)

2. In `crates/mcp-server/src/bin/andromeda-pulse-mcp.rs`: open the corpus via `corpus::contract::Corpus::open(data_dir.join("corpus").join("corpus.db"), OsKeychainBackend::new("com.andromeda.pulse"))` inside the `GateState::Enabled` arm; on open failure, log a structured `mcp.boot.corpus.init` warn + continue with corpus absent (tools that need it return a JSON-RPC error, NOT a crash). Add `corpus: Option<Arc<corpus::contract::Corpus>>` (as both reader + writer trait views) + `workspace_root: String` to `SidecarContext`.

3. In `crates/mcp-server/src/tools.rs`: add 4 dispatch arms + 4 `TOOL_*` consts + extend `ALL_TOOL_NAMES` (→ 8) + `result_type_label` + `result_count_for`. Thread the corpus handle + workspace into `dispatch_tool` (new signature param OR a context struct).
   - `query_incident_list` → `CorpusReader`-style `load_active_incidents(workspace)` (or load-by-id-less list); map each `IncidentRowRaw` → a bounded JSON object (id, status, severity, title, opened_at; bincode-decode payload for severity/kind/title). Paginated envelope shape (`items`/`total`/`next_cursor`) per arch §Standard Contracts.
   - `retrieve_report(id)` → `load_incident_by_id(id)` → bincode-decode `Incident` → parse `resolution_summary_text` → `L4Output` (Some/None) → `interpretation::markdown::assemble_report` → `serialize_report` → return `{ "markdown": <string>, "degraded_mode": <bool> }`. THIS markdown MUST be byte-identical to `incidents.get_report(id).markdown` for the same incident (P-038) — same fns, same inputs.
   - `retrieve_telemetry_slice(id)` → `load_incident_by_id(id)` → return the incident's `evidence_refs` (span_ids hex + fingerprint_hashes) + (if a digest_archive row exists) decoded summary fields; NOT raw telemetry rows. The tool `description` states the persisted-context limitation (research.md Open Question #5).
   - `mark_incident_resolved(id)` → `load_incident_by_id(id)` → set status=resolved + resolved_unix_nano + re-encode payload → `update_incident_status(id, "resolved", now, Some(now), payload)`. Return `{ "resolved": true, "incident_id": id }`. NEVER `Command::arg(id)` — pure corpus write (security ban).

4. In `crates/mcp-server/src/jsonrpc.rs`: rename/extend `tools_list_with_4_tools()` → `tools_list_with_8_tools()` (or generalize to build from `ALL_TOOL_NAMES` + a per-tool schema map); add the 4 new MCP `Tool` schema fragments (name + description + JSON-Schema inputSchema with `additionalProperties: false`; the id-taking tools require an `incident_id` integer property). Update the call site in `andromeda-pulse-mcp.rs:172`.

5. Error sanitization: new tools reuse `short_reason()` for error reasons + map to JSON-RPC codes (`CODE_INVALID_PARAMS` for bad id, `CODE_INTERNAL_ERROR` for corpus failure) in `dispatch_tools_call`.

6. Extend `crates/mcp-server/src/tracing_setup.rs::AllowList::for_mcp_server()` `mcp` entry with any NEW field names the 4 tools emit (e.g., `incident_id`, `incident_count`, `resolved`) — keep `result_content`/response bodies EXCLUDED (obs Vector 4). The `mcp.tools.call.*` targets cascade to the `mcp` key via `split('.').next()`.

1. In `pulse-app/src/mcp_router.rs`: add `connected_agent: Option<String>` to `McpStatusDto` (derive unchanged: Serialize/Deserialize/specta::Type). In `status()`, set it to `Some("stdio-client".into())` when `sidecar_running`, else `None`. This is an EXTENSION of the existing `mcp.status` return shape — no new procedure, no `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` change, no capability-drift delta.
2. Add the `connected_agent` field name to the `mcp` AllowList entry in `pulse-app/src/observability.rs` if `status()` emits it as a tracing field (bounded enum-like value, not high-cardinality).

1. Add `mcp_enable: bool` (default `false`) to `Settings` (`crates/ui-bridge/src/contract.rs`); flows through existing `get_settings`/`update_settings` (no new TauRPC namespace per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-09 Settings-extension). Update `Settings::default()` + any `Settings::load_from_data_dir` defaulting.

2. In `pulse-app/src/main.rs`: read `settings.mcp_enable` at boot; the sidecar spawn-at-boot decision (if any auto-spawn exists) AND/OR the `mcp.start` path gates on `mcp_enable AND double-gate-Enabled`. Default-off means: with `--features mcp-server` built but `mcp_enable=false` + env unset, the sidecar does NOT auto-start (P-040 independence).

- `combined.md §Cross-domain binding reconciliation` — security↔tests↔obs↔arch double-gate / capability-drift / Vector-4 bindings; design↔a11y↔layouts button bindings.
- `combined.md §Cross-domain rot warnings` — Pattern 2 (Command-injection ban by-construction) + Pattern 3 (config-vs-env enablement precedence, resolved as `mcp_enable AND double-gate`).
- `crates/mcp-server/src/bin/andromeda-pulse-mcp.rs` — separate-process sidecar + empty ephemeral buffer (the central architecture finding).
- `crates/mcp-server/src/tools.rs` — existing 4-tool dispatch + `ALL_TOOL_NAMES` + `short_reason` redaction; the extension site.
- `crates/mcp-server/src/jsonrpc.rs` — `tools_list_with_4_tools()` hardcoded schema list; the schema-extension site.
- `crates/mcp-server/src/feature_gate.rs` — complete double-gate; `[mcp.enable]` composes above it.
- `crates/mcp-server/src/tracing_setup.rs` — `AllowList::for_mcp_server` `mcp` entry to extend.
- `pulse-app/src/mcp_router.rs` — `McpStatusDto` to extend with connected-agent label.
- `pulse-app/src/incidents_router.rs` — `assemble_report` (line 567) glue to move; `get_report` resolver call site.
- `crates/corpus/src/contract.rs` — `CorpusReader`/`CorpusWriter` surface; `load_incident_by_id` to add.
- `crates/interpretation/Cargo.toml` + `crates/triage/Cargo.toml` — confirmed `interpretation → triage` edge exists; `interpretation → security` is the only new edge.

- **P-038 single-source discipline is the load-bearing invariant.** Implement Step 1 (move `assemble_report`) FIRST so both `incidents.get_report` and the MCP `retrieve_report` tool call the exact same `interpretation::markdown::assemble_report` + `serialize_report`. The content-identity test then guards against future divergence. Do NOT write a parallel markdown formatter in the mcp-server crate.

- **bincode config parity (Open Question #4) is a silent-failure risk** — verify at Step 0 that the sidecar decode uses the identical config to the pulse-app encode, else `retrieve_report`/`mark_incident_resolved` silently fail to decode the Incident BLOB. If `incident_persistence.rs` uses `bincode::Options`-customized encode, extract a shared `encode_incident`/`decode_incident` pair.

- **Eventual consistency is accepted, not a bug** — `mark_incident_resolved` via the sidecar writes corpus.db; the main process's in-memory `IncidentRegistry` won't reflect it until next boot re-hydration. Document this in the tool description + the chunk's wrap notes. Do NOT attempt a sidecar→main IPC to live-sync the registry (that's the deferred in-process arch).

- **Sidecar corpus-open must be non-fatal** — keychain unavailability or corpus-open failure logs a warn + continues with tools returning JSON-RPC errors; never abort the sidecar (mirrors the existing `mcp.boot.buffer.init` resilience).

- **bindings.ts regen is the classic wrap trap** — run the `--bin pulse-app --features mcp-server` emit_taurpc_bindings regen as the FINAL pre-commit step after all default-features test runs (per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-17/2026-05-25).

- **Windows rlib-race** — if the workspace nextest hits the `libduckdb_sys ... rlib format` error on a cold build, run `cargo build -p pulse-app` first to de-race (per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-31 session 165).

title: Codebase Research — phase-91: chunk route#94 "MCP server + tool exposure"

data.head: # Codebase Research — phase-91: chunk route#94 "MCP server + tool exposure"

body: _Generated by /andromeda-phase Phase 3 from targeted reads informed by combined.md._
- **Research depth:** deep (terminal chunk; combined.md flags a structural arch question + multi-crate touch; the cross-process state-access reality is the central planning input).
- **Reads performed:** 11 full/partial (mcp-server crate × 6, mcp_router.rs, tools.rs, incidents_router.rs, corpus/contract.rs, report.rs, jsonrpc.rs, feature_gate.rs).
- **Globs / Greps:** 6.
- **Parallel batches:** 4.

- `crates/mcp-server/src/bin/andromeda-pulse-mcp.rs` (full) — **CRITICAL FINDING.** The MCP sidecar is a SEPARATE PROCESS. `init_buffer_connection()` opens a FRESH empty `:memory:` DuckDB + `VizState::new()`; `resolve_data_dir()` resolves the data-dir root (so the sidecar CAN locate `corpus/corpus.db` on disk). The stdio loop dispatches `initialize` / `tools/list` / `tools/call` / `ping`. The `SidecarContext { conn, viz_state }` holds ONLY the empty ephemeral buffer — no IncidentRegistry, no corpus, no live ring-buffer handle.

- `crates/mcp-server/src/tools.rs` (full) — existing 4 tools (`query_traces`/`query_metrics`/`query_logs`/`generate_snapshot`) dispatch against the empty ephemeral buffer; `load_recent_spans` comment confirms "live cross-process buffer sharing is deferred." `dispatch_tool(conn, viz_state, name, args)` is the dispatch entry; `ALL_TOOL_NAMES` + `tools_list_with_4_tools()` (in jsonrpc.rs) enumerate the tool set. Prepared-statement discipline already followed (`SELECT_SPANS_RECENT` with `?` placeholders). `short_reason()` redacts paths/versions/`::` from error strings.

- `crates/mcp-server/src/jsonrpc.rs` (full) — JSON-RPC 2.0 framing: `Request`/`SuccessResponse`/`ErrorResponse`/`ErrorObject`; codes (`-32700`..`-32603`); `sanitize_error_data()` redacts; `initialize_result()` advertises `serverInfo.name = "andromeda-pulse-mcp"` + `protocolVersion 2024-11-05`; `tools_list_with_4_tools()` is the hardcoded MCP `Tool` schema list (name + description + JSON-Schema inputSchema + `additionalProperties: false`). **This is where the 4 NEW tools' schemas must be added** (extending to `tools_list_with_8_tools` or generalizing).

- `crates/mcp-server/src/feature_gate.rs` (full) — `validate_double_gate() -> GateState {Enabled, EnvDisabled, FeatureMissing}`; `ENV_MCP_ENABLED = "ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED"`; truthy values `true|1|yes`. The double-gate is fully implemented + tested. There is NO `[mcp.enable]` config-flag layer yet — the chunk's `[mcp.enable]` is NEW.

- `crates/mcp-server/src/contract.rs` (full) — `Error` enum (`FeatureNotEnabled`/`EnvVarDisabled`/`RmcpInit`/`JsonRpcFraming`/`Io`/`TracingInit`/`ToolDispatchFailed`/`ToolArgsInvalid`); MCP errors map to JSON-RPC codes in the sidecar dispatch, NOT AppError.
- `crates/mcp-server/src/tracing_setup.rs` (partial) — stderr-forced JSON; `service.name = "andromeda-pulse-mcp"`; stdout reserved for JSON-RPC framing.

- `crates/mcp-server/Cargo.toml` (full) — deps today: `buffer` + `viz` + `snapshot` + `rmcp` (optional, gated by `mcp-server` feature). `[[bin]] andromeda-pulse-mcp` requires the `mcp-server` feature. To serve incidents/reports the crate needs NEW deps: `corpus` (read corpus.db) + the shared report-serialization surface (see report.rs finding).

- `pulse-app/src/mcp_router.rs` (full) — `mcp.{status,start,stop}` TauRPC resolvers (feature-gated). `McpApiImpl { sidecar_state: Arc<Mutex<Option<Child>>>, sidecar_binary_path }`. `status()` returns `McpStatusDto { state: McpServerState{Enabled,Disabled,Unavailable}, sidecar_running: bool, pid: Option<u32> }`. `start()` spawns the sidecar subprocess with `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_MCP_ENABLED=true` + re-validates the double-gate; `stop()` kills it. **The main process knows "sidecar running" (Child handle) but NOT "an agent has connected to the sidecar's stdio."**

- `pulse-app/src/incidents_router.rs` (partial, lines 1-244+) — `IncidentsApi` trait: `list_active` / `acknowledge` / `mark_resolved` / `mark_all_read` / `get_report` (chunk #88). `IncidentsApiImpl { registry: Arc<dyn IncidentRegistry>, persistence: Arc<dyn IncidentPersistence>, broadcast, corpus_reader: Option<Arc<dyn corpus::CorpusReader>>, workspace_root }`. **corpus_reader is ALREADY wired at the binary boundary.** `get_report` looks up the incident, parses `payload_json` → `L4Output`, calls `assemble_report` + returns `ReportPayload`.

- `crates/corpus/src/contract.rs` (full) — **`corpus/corpus.db` is on-disk SQLite, cross-process accessible.** `CorpusReader` (`list_incidents(status_filter)` / `get_incident(id)` / `list_incident_events(id)` / `inspect` / `digest_archive_count`) + `CorpusWriter` (`save_new_incident` / `update_incident_status` / `mark_incident_read` / `save_digest`). `IncidentRecord { id, scope_id, severity, status, title, detail, created/updated/resolved/read_unix_nano, workspace, payload_json }` — `payload_json` carries the L4Output. So a separate process CAN read all incident data from corpus.db.

- `pulse-app/src/incidents_router.rs` (lines 567-700, the report-assembly internals) — **CORRECTION to an earlier assumption: there is NO `pulse-app/src/report.rs`.** The markdown serializer `serialize_report(&Report) -> String` + the `Report`/`HypothesisView`/`InvestigationStepView` types ALREADY LIVE in the `interpretation` LIBRARY crate (`interpretation::markdown::*`) — mcp-server CAN depend on it. The only binary-trapped glue is the pure fn `assemble_report(incident: &Incident, l4: Option<&L4Output>) -> interpretation::markdown::Report` (incidents_router.rs:567) + its label helpers (`scrub_string`/`incident_status_label`/`severity_label`/`l4_confidence_label`/`hex_lower`). Its deps: `triage::contract::{Incident, IncidentStatus, Severity}` + `interpretation::schema::{L4Output, Confidence}` + `security::scrubber::scrub_attribute`. **`interpretation` ALREADY depends on `triage` (confirmed in interpretation/Cargo.toml) — so `assemble_report` belongs in `interpretation::markdown` alongside `serialize_report`; the only NEW dep edge is `interpretation → security` (security is a leaf crate; no cycle).** This is a ~135-line move, NOT a 600-line crate extraction.

- `pulse-app/src/incident_persistence.rs` (`CorpusIncidentPersistence`) — the Incident-BLOB bincode (de)serialization for corpus rows lives here (binary crate). The sidecar reading `IncidentRowRaw.payload` (encrypted-then-decrypted BLOB) must bincode-decode it into `triage::contract::Incident`. `triage::contract::Incident` IS bincode-(de)serializable (derives Serialize/Deserialize); the sidecar can depend on `triage` + bincode directly and decode the payload itself — OR a shared decode helper moves to a library crate. SUB-QUESTION for /implement Phase 1 (see Open Questions #4).

- **Separate-process MCP sidecar with empty ephemeral state** (`andromeda-pulse-mcp.rs:49-54` + `tools.rs:338-343`): the existing tools query an empty in-memory buffer; the sidecar is spawned but never fed telemetry. Production MCP tools today return empty result sets. This is the deferred-cross-process-sharing reality.

- **Corpus as the cross-process shared substrate** (`corpus/contract.rs` + `andromeda-pulse-mcp.rs:26-47`): `corpus/corpus.db` is on-disk SQLite the sidecar can open via `resolve_data_dir()` + `corpus::Corpus::open`. This is the ONLY live shared state path between main process and sidecar.

- **Report serializer already in a library crate; only the assembly glue is binary-trapped** (`interpretation::markdown::serialize_report` is reachable; `incidents_router.rs:567 assemble_report` is the ~135-line glue to move). `interpretation → triage` edge already exists; only `interpretation → security` is new.

- **Corpus incident-read surface is incomplete for the new tools** (`corpus/contract.rs`): `CorpusWriter` has `load_active_incidents(workspace)` + `count_active_unread(workspace)` + `update_incident_status(id, ...)` + `mark_incident_read(id, ts)`, but NO `get_incident_by_id(id)` and NO list-all-incl-resolved. `query_incident_list` can use `load_active_incidents`; `retrieve_report(id)` + `mark_incident_resolved(id)` NEED a new `load_incident_by_id(id) -> Option<IncidentRowRaw>` corpus method (read-modify-write for the resolve path).

- **mcp.status three-state discriminator** (`mcp_router.rs:29-42`): `McpServerState{Enabled,Disabled,Unavailable}` + `sidecar_running` + `pid`. The chunk's "connected agent identity" extends this (the main process knows sidecar-running, not agent-connected).

- **JSON-RPC tool-list as hardcoded schema array** (`jsonrpc.rs:123-179`): the 4 tool schemas are an inline `json!` array; adding tools = extending this fn + `ALL_TOOL_NAMES` + the `dispatch_tool` match.

- **Five-place cfg-gate for the mcp-server feature** (`mcp_router.rs` + `main.rs:86` `#[cfg(feature = "mcp-server")]`): the `mcp.*` namespace + router wiring + emit_taurpc_bindings test are all feature-gated (chunk #49 precedent).

- **Prepared statements only** for any DuckDB/SQLite read — `tools.rs:51-56` `SELECT_SPANS_RECENT` uses `?` placeholders + `duckdb::params![]`; corpus reads go through `CorpusReader` parameterized methods.

- **Error sanitization at the JSON-RPC boundary** — `tools.rs:290` `short_reason()` + `jsonrpc.rs:72` `sanitize_error_data()` strip paths/versions/`::`; new tools reuse `short_reason` for their error reasons.

- **Tool dispatch span discipline** — `tools.rs:128-178` emits `mcp.tools.call.response` with `result_type` + `result_count` + `duration_ms`, NEVER `result_content`; new tools mirror this (extend `result_type_label` + `result_count_for`).

- **Cross-crate state via trait + map_err free-fn** — `incidents_router.rs:120` injects `Option<Arc<dyn corpus::CorpusReader>>`; corpus errors → tool errors via a local `map_err` (orphan-rule compliant) per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-18.
- **specta::Type derive on cross-bridge types** — `mcp_router.rs:29-53` all DTOs derive `Serialize + Deserialize + specta::Type`; the `mcp.status` extension payload follows suit.
- **`[lib] test = false` + integration tests in `pulse-app/tests/`** — per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-20, any pulse-app test goes in `pulse-app/tests/`, never source-level `mod tests`.

- `pulse-app/ui/src/report/SendToAgentButton.tsx` (+ `.test.tsx`) — the conditionally-visible "Send to agent" button for the Report toolbar (design secondary-button tokens; a11y native `<button>` + conditional DOM render).

- `pulse-app/tests/e2e_p3_mcp_incident_tools.rs` (feature-gated) — P3-style subprocess E2E driving the 4 new tools via JSON-RPC against a seeded corpus.db; content-identity assertion (MCP `retrieve_report` markdown == clipboard markdown, P-038).
- `pulse-app/tests/security_mcp_incident_tools_redaction.rs` (feature-gated) — response-body-never-logged + no-`Command::arg(agent_id)` negative canaries for the new tools.

- (no new shared crate needed) `assemble_report` + helpers move INTO the existing `interpretation::markdown` module (alongside `serialize_report`); only the `interpretation → security` Cargo dep edge is new.

- `crates/mcp-server/src/jsonrpc.rs` — extend `tools_list_with_4_tools()` → the full 8-tool schema list (add `query_incident_list` / `retrieve_report` / `retrieve_telemetry_slice` / `mark_incident_resolved` JSON-Schema fragments).

- `crates/mcp-server/src/tools.rs` — add the 4 new dispatch arms + `ALL_TOOL_NAMES` entries + `result_type_label`/`result_count_for` cases; thread a corpus reader/writer handle into the dispatch context.
- `crates/mcp-server/src/bin/andromeda-pulse-mcp.rs` — open `corpus/corpus.db` via `resolve_data_dir()` + `corpus::Corpus::open`; add corpus reader/writer to `SidecarContext`.
- `crates/mcp-server/Cargo.toml` — add `corpus` dep + the shared report-surface dep (+ `triage`/`interpretation`/`security` transitively via the report crate).

- `pulse-app/src/mcp_router.rs` — extend `McpStatusDto` with connected-agent identity field(s); the `mcp.status` resolver remains (no NEW TauRPC procedure — `mcp.status` already exists; this EXTENDS its return shape, so NO capability-drift delta + NO new `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` entry — confirmed in combined.md arch constraint).

- `crates/interpretation/src/markdown.rs` — ADD `assemble_report(incident, l4) -> Report` + the label helpers moved from incidents_router.rs:567 (alongside existing `serialize_report`); `crates/interpretation/Cargo.toml` gains the `security` dep edge.

- `pulse-app/src/incidents_router.rs` — DELETE the moved `assemble_report` + helpers; call `interpretation::markdown::assemble_report` instead (get_report resolver unchanged in behavior; P-038 single source preserved).
- `crates/corpus/src/contract.rs` — add `load_incident_by_id(id) -> Result<Option<IncidentRowRaw>, Error>` to `CorpusWriter` (read path for retrieve_report + mark_incident_resolved).

- `crates/ui-bridge/src/contract.rs` — add `mcp_enable: bool` (default false) to `Settings` (flows through existing `get_settings`/`update_settings`; no new TauRPC namespace per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-09).
- `pulse-app/ui/src/report/ReportRenderer.tsx` — mount the `SendToAgentButton` in the footer toolbar adjacent to "Copy markdown".
- `pulse-app/ui/src/dashboard/routes/SettingsModalForm.tsx` — add the `[mcp.enable]` toggle (reuses the existing MCP-toggle Switch form-control pattern).

- `pulse-app/src/main.rs` — pass data-dir through to the spawned sidecar (already done — sidecar resolves it itself via `resolve_data_dir()`); wire `mcp_enable` from Settings into the spawn-at-boot decision.
- `crates/mcp-server/src/feature_gate.rs` — the double-gate is complete; the `[mcp.enable]` config layer composes ABOVE it at the spawn decision (main.rs), not inside feature_gate.
- The existing 4 tools' dispatch logic — additive only; do not alter `query_traces`/`query_metrics`/`query_logs`/`generate_snapshot`.

1. **[RESOLVED at /phase via AskUserQuestion — Option A "Corpus-backed subprocess"].** The MCP sidecar stays a separate process; the 4 new tools open `corpus/corpus.db` via `CorpusReader`/`CorpusWriter`. `query_incident_list` + `retrieve_report(id)` + `mark_incident_resolved(id)` become genuinely functional against persisted corpus data. `retrieve_telemetry_slice(id)` returns persisted incident-context (evidence refs / digest from corpus) only — the live ring buffer is unreachable cross-process (same pre-existing limitation as the existing `query_traces` tool). `mark_incident_resolved` writes corpus.db with eventual-consistency vs the main process's in-memory registry (documented divergence; the main process re-hydrates active incidents from corpus at next boot, so the resolved status is durably correct). `mcp.status()` "connected" = sidecar-running. Options B (in-process pivot, arch-gated) + C (defer) were NOT chosen.

No new workspace crate.

Resolution for A: `mcp.status()` extends `McpStatusDto` with a bounded `connected_agent: Option<String>` that at this chunk's scope equals the sidecar-running state surfaced as a label (`Some("stdio-client")` when `sidecar_running`, else `None`); a true sidecar→main agent-handshake round-trip is deferred. Recommended shape: return the incident's `evidence_refs` (span_ids / fingerprint_hashes) + (if present) the most-recent `digest_archive` summary fields — NOT raw telemetry rows. Document the limitation in the tool's MCP `description` ("persisted incident context; live telemetry is served by the separate `query_traces`/`query_logs` tools against the live buffer").

body: _Generated by /andromeda-phase Phase 4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not edit during /implement run._
- **Phase number:** 92

- **Route chunks covered:**
  - route#95 "Export for community training"
- **Epoch:** Epoch 9 — Foundation v0.2.0 (TERMINAL chunk of the 95-chunk route)

Add a privacy-preserving "Export for community training" action to the Settings → Storage surface that produces an anonymized JSONL dump of the incident corpus (one record per incident: trigger context, model interpretation, user feedback, resolution outcome). A pre-write **preview** dialog shows what will be exported (count by status + severity, date range, anonymization-confirmed) BEFORE any file is written; the user explicitly confirms; the file is written locally (default `~/Downloads/pulse-corpus-export-{timestamp}.jsonl`) and **never auto-submitted** — the user manually shares it. This is the L5 export channel (capability P-046), the terminal chunk of the route. Backend = one new TauRPC procedure `storage.export_for_training` in the existing `storage.*` router (`pulse-app/src/storage_router.rs`) reading the corpus via a new `CorpusWriter::load_all_incidents()`, with PII scrubbed at the egress boundary via `security::scrubber::scrub_attribute` (defense-in-depth, per the chunk #88 `incidents.get_report` resolver-scrub precedent). Frontend = a new `ExportForTraining` component mounted in a new Storage section of the chunk #38 Settings modal, reusing the chunk #37 `Modal` primitive for the preview/confirm dialog. Per arch §Occupied Resources (`storage.*` namespace) + security plan §API/§Input/§Logging + obs-plan §6/§8 + design-system §Per-Surface Bans + a11y plan §4/§5/§7 + tests §6/§11. **Workspace deps delta = none; arch registry delta = +1 TauRPC procedure.**

Ordered by dependency: corpus read method → record-assembly module → TauRPC procedure + resolver wiring → boot + bindings + drift → observability → UI → tests. Implement backend through capability-drift-clean before the webview surface.

1. **Corpus read method.** In `crates/corpus/src/contract.rs`, add `fn load_all_incidents(&self) -> Result<Vec<IncidentRowRaw>, Error>` to the `CorpusWriter` trait (where the sibling incident reads `load_active_incidents`/`load_incident_by_id` live) + `impl CorpusWriter for Corpus`. Prepared statement `SELECT id, workspace, status, created_unix_nano, updated_unix_nano, resolved_unix_nano, read_unix_nano, payload FROM incidents ORDER BY id` (NO status/workspace filter — full corpus dump); decrypt each `payload` via `cell_decrypt(self.key(), …)` exactly as `load_active_incidents` does. Add co-located `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` cases (corpus crate has no `[lib] test=false`): empty corpus → `vec![]`; after `save_incident` × N → N rows in insertion order incl. resolved.

2. **Export record-assembly module.** Create `pulse-app/src/training_export.rs`:
   - `ExportRecord` (internal, `Serialize`) — flat shape per incident: `id`, `workspace` (scrubbed), `status`, `kind`, `scope`, `scope_id` (scrubbed), `severity`, `title` (scrubbed), `detail` (scrubbed), `opened_at_unix_nano`, `resolved_at_unix_nano`, `interpretation` (scrubbed `resolution_summary_text`, null for active), `fingerprint_hashes` (scrubbed), `acknowledged`/`read` flags.
   - `fn incident_row_to_export_record(row: &IncidentRowRaw) -> Result<ExportRecord, AppError>` — `bincode::deserialize::<Incident>(&row.payload)` (plain config; cross-process parity) → re-stamp `id`/`workspace`/timestamps from the row columns (mirror `incident_persistence.rs:87-109`) → route every user-facing text field through `scrub_string` (below).
   - `fn scrub_string(value: &str) -> String` — `match security::scrubber::scrub_attribute(value) { Allowed(s) => s, Redacted{category} => format!("[redacted: {category}]") }` (chunk #88 precedent / CLAUDE.md 2026-05-26).

body: _Generated by /andromeda-phase Phase 3 from targeted reads informed by combined.md._

- **Research depth:** moderate-to-deep (mature codebase; reuses chunk #68 `storage.*` router + chunk #78/#94 corpus incident-read path + chunk #38 Settings modal + chunk #37 Modal primitive + chunk #88 incident→report+scrub precedent). Not cold-start.

- **Globs / Greps:** 9.
- **Parallel batches:** 3.

- `pulse-app/src/storage_router.rs` (full) — `#[taurpc::procedures(path = "storage")] trait StorageApi { inspect(); path(); }`; `StorageApiImpl { reader: Arc<dyn CorpusReader> }` + `::new(reader)`; cross-bridge payloads `#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq, specta::Type)]` use `Vec<TableRecordCount>` (not maps); **`corpus_error_to_app_error(err) -> AppError` free fn** (the export reuses this verbatim); resolvers carry `#[tracing::instrument(skip_all, fields(...Empty))]` + `tracing::info!(target: "storage.{verb}.request", ...)` with basename-only path logging. **This is the host file for the new procedure.**

- `crates/corpus/src/contract.rs` (full) — `CorpusReader` exposes ONLY `inspect()` + `path()`. The incident reads (`load_active_incidents(workspace)`, `load_incident_by_id(id)`) live on **`CorpusWriter`** (the "rich corpus operations" trait, despite the name). **No "load ALL incidents (any status, any workspace)" method exists** — must be added. `IncidentRowRaw { id, workspace, status, created/updated/resolved/read_unix_nano, payload: Vec<u8> }` (payload = decrypted bincode `Incident`). All reads use prepared `?` statements; BLOB decrypt via `cell_decrypt(self.key(), …)`. `Error` enum: `KeyringUnavailable / MigrationFailed / Encryption/Decryption / QueryFailed / PathTraversal / SizeCapExceeded / SchemaVersionMismatch / Io{kind}`.

- `crates/security/src/scrubber.rs` (full) — `pub fn scrub_attribute(value: &str) -> ScrubbedValue` where `ScrubbedValue::Allowed(String) | Redacted { category: &'static str }`. 7 P-047 categories (jwt/bearer/api_key/secret_kv/email/credit_card/ssn), first-match-wins, `OnceLock`-cached. `.is_redacted()` + `.category()` helpers. **This is the egress scrub primitive for every exported text field.**

- `pulse-app/src/incident_persistence.rs` (full) — the canonical incident BLOB decode pattern: `bincode::deserialize::<Incident>(&row.payload)` then re-stamp authoritative SQL-column metadata (`id`/`workspace`/timestamps) onto the struct. Plain `bincode` config (no `Options`) — **cross-process parity holds** (CLAUDE.md 2026-06-01). `CorpusIncidentPersistence { writer: Arc<dyn CorpusWriter> }`; `corpus_error_to_incident_error` free fn. The export record-assembly mirrors this decode+re-stamp.

- `pulse-app/src/main.rs` (grep windows) — boot ALREADY derives both views from one `Arc<Corpus>`: `corpus_reader: Option<Arc<dyn CorpusReader>>` (line 314) + `corpus_writer: Option<Arc<dyn CorpusWriter>>` (line 323) via `Arc::clone(c) as Arc<dyn …>` (N-trait-from-single-Arc, CLAUDE.md 2026-05-19). `storage_impl = corpus_reader.as_ref().map(|r| StorageApiImpl::new(Arc::clone(r)))` (line 326); merged at the production Router (lines 860/885 `match storage_impl.as_ref()`) + in the `emit_taurpc_bindings` test (lines 1613–1704, constructs its own in-memory `StorageApiImpl` + `.merge(storage_impl.into_handler())`). **The `corpus_writer` handle already exists at boot** — the export resolver can bind it with zero new boot plumbing.

- `pulse-app/src/incidents_router.rs` (grep window) — chunk #88 `assemble_report` (~line 437) decodes `resolution_summary_text` + maps Incident → rich `ReportPayload`, scrubbing every user-facing text field via a `scrub_string` helper (CLAUDE.md 2026-05-26 defense-in-depth scrubber-at-resolver). `workspace_root` is threaded into the resolver via `::new(…, workspace_root: String)`. **The export record-assembly + scrub mirrors this precedent.**

- `crates/triage/src/contract.rs` (grep window) — `Incident` (line 318): `id`, `workspace`, `title`, `detail`, `kind: CueKind`, `scope: CueScope`, `scope_id: Option<String>`, `severity: Severity`, `resolution_summary_text: Option<String>` (`#[serde(default)]`; attached only on Resolved per chunk #86), + status/opened/updated/resolved/read timestamps. `EvidenceRefs` (line 252) carries `fingerprint_hashes`. **These fields are the export record's source: trigger context (kind/scope/scope_id/title/detail) + model interpretation (resolution_summary_text) + user feedback (read/acknowledge state) + resolution outcome (status/resolved_at).**

- `pulse-app/ui/src/dashboard/routes/SettingsModalForm.tsx` (full) — the Settings form. Sections: Theme / Widget position / Retention / MCP server / Snapshot preset+format / Drain / Diagnostics (with `TemplateDistribution` imported component + a retry-interpretation action button + `role="status" aria-live="polite"` row) / Plugin manager. **NO Storage section** — the export action is net-new UI. Uses `getClient()` cached TauRPC proxy + `__setProxyForTest` seam + react-aria `Button` + inline `var(--...)` token styles. title: Chunk route#96: "Configuration hot reload + prospective threshold application"

data.head: ### Chunk route#96: "Configuration hot reload + prospective threshold application"

body: Capabilities P-055 (Configuration Hot Reload) + P-056 (Prospective Threshold Application). Filesystem watcher on `~/.andromeda-pulse/config.toml` (500ms debounce); hot-reloadable keys (thresholds, cadences, severity rules, suppression, lifecycle boundaries) apply ≤2s; restart-required keys (Drain params, model path, ports, storage path) raise a Diagnostics notice without applying; threshold changes apply **prospectively** (no baseline reset, no retroactive rolling-window re-eval); opt-in `diagnostics.reevaluate_recent_window()` action provides retrospective application; malformed config rejected with previous valid config retained.
**Constraints across domains:**

- (arch) **Config precedence is fixed**: env vars `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_*` > `~/.andromeda-pulse/config.toml` > built-in defaults. Hot-reload MUST reapply file-tier values only and MUST NOT override a key an env var has already set (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns "Config management").

- (arch) **Hot-reload target already lives in `Settings`**: re-load + re-validate through the existing `crates/ui-bridge/src/contract.rs::Settings` (loaded via `Settings::load_from_data_dir`, validated via `Settings::validate()` with `_MIN`/`_MAX` bound constants; cadence keys from chunk #80 are the prime target) rather than a parallel config struct (per arch §Cross-cutting Patterns config management + §Occupied Resources `get_settings`/`update_settings`).

- (arch) **Restart-required vs hot-reloadable partition** maps to arch-locked one-time-init substrate: Drain params, model path, OTLP `:4317`/`:4318` binds, storage/data-dir path are init-time — they raise a Diagnostics notice via the new broadcast topic, never apply live (per arch §Established Decisions [Telemetry Retention] / [Database] / [LLM Inference Runtime]).

- (arch) **`config.<verb>` dotted-namespace `snake_case`** procedure shape; the dedicated `config.*` namespace is justified because reload/status are *operations*, not get/set state (per arch §Conventions "Endpoint naming").

- (security/arch) **The watched config path MUST canonicalize + confine**: if resolved from `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_CONFIG_PATH` / `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR`, `canonicalize()` + assert resolved path under the data dir via `strict-path` BEFORE the `notify` watcher attaches (per security plan §Input Validation "CLI / env var inputs" + §Anti-Patterns §Input; arch §Critical Warnings path-env-var rule; CWE-22). NOTE: `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_CONFIG_PATH` is tagged deferred (no runtime consumer as of chunk #74) — confirm at /implement Step 1 whether this chunk activates it or stays on the fixed `<data_dir>/config.toml`.

- (security) **Validate every reloaded field before applying**: shape via `serde`; port via `TryFrom<u16>`; retention bounded; log level enum; thresholds positive; multipliers in allowed ranges — malformed config rejected with previous valid config retained (per security plan §Input Validation "Configuration values — `config.toml`").

- (security) **`notify` dep pinned** in workspace `Cargo.toml` (no `*`/`latest`); passes `cargo audit` + `cargo deny check bans licenses sources`; new transitive duplicates → `deny.toml [bans] skip` with provenance, never relax `multiple-versions = "deny"` (per security plan §Dependency Security + CLAUDE.md 2026-05-03 deny-skip discipline).

- (security/arch) **+2 TauRPC procedures return `Result<T, AppError>`** AND have a `pulse-app/capabilities/` JSON entry (negative-default; router registration alone is a silent runtime rejection) (per security plan §API Security + arch §Cross-cutting "Webview IPC capability policy" + §Critical Warnings).

- (security) **config-watcher MUST NOT pass any reloaded config string to `tokio::process::Command`** (model-path / Drain-param keys are restart-required NOTICE-only) (per security plan §Anti-Patterns §Code Patterns; command-injection ban).

- (tests) New `crates/config-watcher/` (+ `crates/triage/` hooks) carries co-located `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`; new code meets Standard-tier coverage ≥75% line / ≥70% branch / ≥85% function (per test-plan §10 + §4).
- (tests) Watcher tests self-bootstrap via `tempfile::TempDir` + `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` override (write `config.toml`, then mutate it); NO committed config fixtures (per test-plan §3 + §11).

- (tests) **500ms debounce + ≤2s apply timing tested deterministically with `tokio::time::pause()` + `advance()`** (`#[tokio::test(start_paused = true)]`), NEVER `sleep(N)` / real wall-clock (per test-plan §8 Time + §11 bans).

- (obs) Config load/reload is a boundary that MUST emit structured logs: success → `info` (which keys reloaded, count, last-reload timestamp); validation/path failure → `warn`; use `{module}.{operation}` target naming (per obs-plan §6 Log levels + §2/§4 naming).

- (obs) TauRPC handlers `config.reload`/`config.status` instrumented with `#[tracing::instrument(skip_all, fields(traceparent = %tp))]` extracting the IPC-envelope traceparent (per obs-plan §3 IPC trace-context propagation + §4).

- (obs) **Config keys Low-classification + OK to log structurally, BUT** redact secret-shaped keys (`*_SECRET`/`*_TOKEN`/`*_KEY`) and log file-path values basename-only — never the full canonicalized config/data-dir path (per obs-plan §8 Data classification + Vector 6 CWE-22).

- (design) IF a restart-required notice / reload-status indicator renders, use only design tokens (container = `--color-raised-1` + subtle border + `--spacing-md` + `--radius-md`); no hardcoded hex/px (per design-system §Color Palette + §Border Radius + Component Patterns Cards/Panels).

- (design/a11y) **Not-color-alone**: any restart-required / reload-failed / reload-OK state MUST pair color with a text label and/or icon (per design-system §Anti-Patterns Universal Bans + a11y plan §6 / §11 Visual SC 1.4.1).

- (a11y) IF a dynamic status notice renders in webview, it MUST live in an `aria-live` region (`polite` for confirmations / last-reload timestamp; `assertive`/`role="alert"` for config-rejected errors) and MUST NOT steal keyboard focus on async appearance (per a11y plan §7 Live regions + §11 Status Messages SC 4.1.3 + §4 P4).
**Patterns к follow:**

- (arch) Settings-extension over new namespace where state fits the `Settings` shape (bool flags / enum choices / scaled-integer tuned values flow through `get_settings`/`update_settings`); reserve `config.*` for reload/status operations (per arch §Conventions).

- (arch/security) Cross-crate async state delivery WITHOUT `async-trait` dep: manual `Pin<Box<dyn Future + Send + 'a>>` return types (chunk #80 `SqlQueryRunner` precedent); cross-crate sync state via trait-in-lower-crate + `Arc<dyn Trait>` injection at the binary boundary (per arch §Cross-cutting Module dependency direction).

- (security) Cross-crate error mapping: convert watcher/parse errors → `AppError` via a free `fn …_error_to_app_error(...)` in the pulse-app router file (orphan-rule-safe), not an `impl From` in ui-bridge/watcher (CLAUDE.md 2026-05-18 free-fn map_err precedent).

- (security/arch) Float-shaped tunables stored as scaled integers (`_x100`/`_x1000`) to preserve `Settings`' `Eq` derive (CLAUDE.md 2026-05-19 `drain_similarity_x100` precedent; arch §Established Decisions [Validation Library]).
- (security) Bounded-cardinality `_label: String` for any cross-crate enum referenced in the `config-events` broadcast payload (CLAUDE.md 2026-05-24 precedent).

- (obs) Boundary-call wrapper logging: `method_name` + `argument_digest` (hash, not content) + `result_type` + `latency_ms`, matching the established `ui-bridge` TauRPC allowlist (per obs-plan §6 + §8 whitelist).

- (obs) New broadcast topic follows the real-time-push pattern: emit site span-wrapped (`channel_name`, `payload_size_bytes`), Tauri 2 IPC `Channel`, `pulse://stream/<kebab>` naming (per obs-plan §4 P6 + arch §Standard Contracts real-time push).
- (obs) Self-observation via `tracing` + `tracing-subscriber` JSON + `tracing-appender` file sink ONLY (NO OTel SDK); config-watcher emits into the shared JSON sink (per obs-plan §3).

- (design) Notice container reuses the Cards/Panels primitive (borders-only depth, NO shadow/gradient); error state reuses documented Error state (`--color-accent` border + icon + ≤2-line message); prefer custom `aperture` glyph for config semantics (per design-system §Surface desktop-webview Component Patterns + §Iconography).

- (a11y) Status-message pattern: `role="status"`/`aria-live="polite"` (confirmations) vs `role="alert"`/`aria-live="assertive"` (config-rejected); reduced-motion override via `motion-reduce:` variants (per a11y plan §4 + §6 + §7).
**Anti-patterns к avoid:**

- (security) NEVER read the `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_*_PATH`/`*_DIR` env var resolving the watched location without `canonicalize()` + assert-under-data-dir (TOCTOU / symlink traversal) (per security plan §Anti-Patterns §Input).

- (security) NEVER apply a reloaded value before validation; reject-and-retain-previous is mandatory — never partially-apply or zero out live thresholds (per security plan §Input Validation config row).

- (security/obs) NEVER log raw `config.toml` contents, reloaded values, or full file paths in watcher tracing events / `config-events` payload — emit field names + sanitized reasons / basename only (per security plan §Logging NEVER-log list + obs-plan §11 + Vectors 3/6).

- (obs) NEVER emit a multi-line deserialize/`thiserror` stack trace on malformed-config rejection — one-line sanitized SpanTrace; never serialize `anyhow::Error` across the IPC boundary (per obs-plan §11 + Vector 2).

- (obs) NEVER let a tight `notify` debounce/event loop log at `info` per filesystem event — gate verbose per-event detail behind `debug`/`trace`; only the settled 500ms-debounced outcome warrants `info` (per obs-plan §11 Logs hot-path ban).

- (arch) NEVER bind a new network surface/socket (config-watcher is filesystem-only; OTLP stays loopback `:4317`/`:4318`); NEVER add a new env var beyond the `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_*` namespace without a registry amendment; NEVER let hot-reload mutate locked startup-time decisions live (per arch §Occupied Resources + §Established Decisions).

- (design/a11y) NEVER convey reload state by color alone; NEVER ship a dynamic status surface without an `aria-live` region; NEVER use `alert()`/`confirm()`/native dialogs; NEVER use banned/generic fonts (per design-system §Anti-Patterns + a11y plan §11).
**Contract bindings:**

- **arch/security ↔ tests (capability-drift)**: the +2 TauRPC procedures bind to router registration + `pulse-app/capabilities/` JSON + `xtask EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` + the `emit_taurpc_bindings` test merge; `cargo xtask capability-drift` is the CI gate (per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-12 quadruple-binding + §Critical Warnings). RECIPROCATED (security, arch, tests all acknowledge).

- **obs ↔ tests (log format + status shape)**: `config.status()` JSON shape (last-reload timestamp + errors) + reload/restart-required events bind to the NDJSON log schema (`timestamp`/`level`/`target`/`message`/`fields`) that the tests harness greps via `agent-latest.jsonl`; obs owns the field shape, tests consumes it. RECIPROCATED.

- **obs ↔ security (PII redaction)**: security owns config validation + path safety; obs owns that the WARN/ERROR log on rejection carries basename-only path + redacted secrets + sanitized error category. RECIPROCATED.

- **obs ↔ tests (heartbeat)**: IF the `notify` watcher is a persistent task, its liveness signal binds to the heartbeat/stall check (max tick delta ≤45000ms). Orchestrator must decide tick-emitting (`config.tick` ~15s) vs event-driven-only — see Open question. UNILATERAL-ish (obs raises; tests harness consumes if present).

- **design ↔ a11y (contrast + not-color-alone + reduced-motion)**: state-color contrast (SC 1.4.3), color+label/icon pairing (SC 1.4.1), 200ms fade collapses under `prefers-reduced-motion` (SC 2.3.3) — ALL conditional on a UI surface rendering this chunk. RECIPROCATED.

- **a11y conditional**: IF chunk lands backend-only (no webview component), there are NO active a11y/design/layouts bindings — the consumer Diagnostics surface defers to its own later chunk (v0.2.0-route §95).
**Acceptance criteria contributions:**

- (arch) New code lives in a workspace-reserved crate: either `crates/config-watcher/` legitimized via `/andromeda-evolve --allow-arch-registry` (root `Cargo.toml` members + §Occupied Resources crate-names + §Inherited Defaults) OR extends an existing config module — no unregistered workspace member.
- (arch) `config.reload()` + `config.status()` appear in §Occupied Resources Tauri IPC routes + `pulse-app/capabilities/` JSON + `xtask EXPECTED_PROCEDURES`; `cargo xtask capability-drift` exits 0.
- (arch) `pulse://stream/config-events` registered in §Occupied Resources Tauri IPC events; uses `pulse://stream/<kebab>` Tauri Channel push convention.
- (arch) Config precedence preserved: an `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_*` env-set key is not overwritten by a `config.toml` hot-reload (verifiable by reload-while-env-set check).
- (security) `cargo deny check bans licenses sources` + `cargo audit` pass with the new `notify` dep pinned.

- (security) A malformed/out-of-range `config.toml` write (negative threshold, out-of-range multiplier, invalid port) is rejected, previous valid config remains live, surfaced via `config.status` WITHOUT applying the bad value.

- (security) `config.status` output + `config-events` payload + watcher tracing events contain no raw config contents, no full filesystem paths, no secret-shaped strings (grep/inspection verifies; AppError message is a sanitized one-liner).

- (security) The watched config path resolved from env is canonicalized + asserted under the data dir before the watcher attaches (a `..`-traversal target is rejected; mirrors chunk #95 `training_export.rs` egress validation).
- (tests) `cargo nextest run -p config-watcher` (+ `-p triage` for hooks) passes; new code meets Standard-tier coverage.
- (tests) Debounce/apply timing passes under `#[tokio::test(start_paused = true)]` with `advance` — hot-reloadable key applies within the simulated 2s window; no real `sleep`.
- (tests) Negative test: malformed `config.toml` → previous valid config retained, no panic, error surfaced via `config.status()`/`config-events`.

- (tests) Boot-smoke gate passes (main.rs spawns watcher + registers routers) + the unconditional standard gate set (fmt + clippy --all-features -D warnings + nextest --workspace + capability-drift; webview lint/typecheck/test only if `pulse-app/ui/**` touched).

data.head: # Phase 93 Plan — chunk route#96: "Configuration hot reload + prospective threshold application"

body: _Generated by /andromeda-phase Phase 4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not edit during /implement run._
- **Phase number:** 93

- **Route chunks covered:**
  - route#96 "Configuration hot reload + prospective threshold application"
- **Epoch:** Foundation v0.2.0 (Epoch 9) — TERMINAL chunk of the route

- **Phase-6 scope decisions (user-confirmed before plan write):**
  - **Breadth:** Cadence + lifecycle get genuine live hot-reload; cue-threshold / activity-floor / restart-suppression (#62/#64/#63) are a NAMED follow-up.
  - **Placement:** NEW `crates/config-watcher/` workspace crate (route §94 names it; co-located runnable unit tests).
  - **Reevaluate:** FULL retrospective `diagnostics.reevaluate_recent_window()` — real re-evaluation against new config (scoped to the wired consumers).

Add a cross-cutting configuration hot-reload layer (capabilities P-055 / P-056) so a developer can edit `~/.andromeda-pulse/config.toml` and have tuning keys re-applied to the running process within ~2s without a restart. A new `crates/config-watcher/` crate runs a `notify` filesystem watcher on `<data_dir>/config.toml` with a 500ms debounce; on each settled change it re-loads + re-validates through the existing `ui_bridge::Settings` + `Settings::validate()` surface (malformed/out-of-range config is rejected and the previous valid config is retained), classifies the changed keys into a **hot** set vs a **restart-required** set, publishes the validated `Settings` on a `tokio::sync::watch` channel, and emits aggregate-only events on the new `pulse://stream/config-events` broadcast topic (per arch §Standard Contracts real-time push + obs-plan §6, security-redacted per security plan §Logging) — see `combined.md §Chunk route#96`.

Two live consumers re-read their config from the watch channel this chunk: the **cadence coordinator** (#80 — the only consumer whose source comment explicitly says "hot-reload deferred к chunk #94") rebuilds its tier-3 / reflection intervals on change, and the **service-lifecycle heartbeat** (#67) re-reads its dormant/archived thresholds each tick. Application is **prospective by default** (P-056): a hot threshold edit changes evaluation going forward only — it does NOT reset baselines, replay missed cadence ticks, or retroactively re-classify services. A separate opt-in `diagnostics.reevaluate_recent_window()` TauRPC action performs the explicit FULL retrospective pass — re-classifying every registered service against the new lifecycle boundaries (using each service's existing activity history) and forcing one immediate cadence cycle with the new config. Restart-required keys (Drain params, `mcp_server_enabled`, retention, plus the conceptual model-path / OTLP-ports / storage-path init-time substrate) are NOT applied live; they raise a restart-required notice via `config-events` + `config.status()` rather than mutating arch-locked startup decisions mid-run (per arch §Established Decisions [Database] / [Telemetry Retention] / [LLM Inference Runtime]). Two new `config.*` TauRPC procedures (`config.reload` manual trigger + `config.status` last-reload/errors/pending-restart-keys) round out the surface. Per the breadth decision the only user-visible consumer this chunk is the backend `config-events` topic + `config.status` (a Diagnostics view that renders them is a separate later chunk) — so this is a backend-only chunk: design/layouts/a11y bindings stay dormant (combined.md §Cross-domain binding reconciliation "a11y conditional").

1. **Workspace dep + crate scaffold.** Add `notify` (pin the current stable line, e.g. `notify = "8"`) to root `Cargo.toml` `[workspace.dependencies]`; add `crates/config-watcher` to `[workspace] members`. Create `crates/config-watcher/Cargo.toml` depending on: `tokio` (workspace; needs `sync`/`time` — `full` already provides watch), `serde`, `thiserror`, `tracing`, `toml`, `strict-path`, `notify`, and `ui-bridge` (for `Settings` + `Settings::validate`); dev-deps `tempfile` + `rstest` + `tokio = { workspace = true, features = ["test-util"] }` (paused-clock debounce tests per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-03). NO `build.rs` needed (config-watcher does NOT consume `duckdb` — the rstrtmgr build.rs gotcha per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-23 does not apply). DAG: `config-watcher → ui-bridge` is a forward edge (ui-bridge never depends on config-watcher) — preserves arch §Cross-cutting Module dependency direction.

2. **Watched-path resolution + confinement.** In config-watcher, resolve the watch target as `<data_dir>/config.toml` from the data dir passed by pulse-app (stay on the fixed path per the existing `Settings::load_from_data_dir`; do NOT activate the tag-deferred `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_CONFIG_PATH` env var this chunk — research Open-Q4). Canonicalize the data dir via `strict-path` + assert the resolved `config.toml` lives under it BEFORE attaching the watcher (CWE-22; mirrors chunk #95 `training_export.rs` egress validation) per security plan §Input Validation + arch §Critical Warnings. Reject a `..`-traversal target with a sanitized error.

3. **Debounced reload core.** Implement the watcher loop: `notify` recommended watcher on the config file's parent dir, filtered to the `config.toml` path; coalesce events with a 500ms debounce (a `tokio::time::sleep` reset-on-event window, testable under `tokio::time::pause()`/`advance`). On the settled event, read the file to string + `toml::from_str::<Settings>` + `Settings::validate()`. On parse/validate error: retain the previous valid `Settings`, record the error category in status, emit a `ConfigEvent::ParseRejected` (sanitized — NO raw contents/values), and do NOT publish. On success: continue to step 4.

4. **Hot-vs-restart partition.** Add a pure `partition_changed_keys(old: &Settings, new: &Settings) -> ChangedKeys` classifier returning `{ hot_applied: Vec<&'static str>, restart_required: Vec<&'static str>, silent: Vec<&'static str> }`. Classification table: **hot-applied (live this chunk)** = `cadence_baseline_seconds` / `cadence_accelerated_seconds` / `cadence_reflection_seconds` / `cadence_tier2_acceleration_enabled` / `lifecycle_dormant_after_secs` / `lifecycle_archived_after_secs`; **restart-required (notice)** = `drain_depth` / `drain_similarity_x100` / `drain_max_clusters` / `retention_seconds` / `mcp_server_enabled`; **silent next-read (no notice — UI prefs / per-use)** = `theme` / `widget_position` / `notifications_enabled` / `always_on_top` / `snapshot_preset` / `snapshot_format`. Pure fn → co-located unit tests.

5. **Publish + events.** On a successful reload, `watch::Sender<Settings>::send_replace(new)` (latest-value semantics — prospective; consumers pick up the new value on their next tick/`changed()`). Emit `ConfigEvent::Reloaded { hot_count, restart_required_count, silent_count }` on `ConfigEventBroadcast` (`pulse://stream/config-events`, capacity 32, mirroring `crates/triage/src/cadence/broadcast.rs`). If `restart_required` is non-empty, also emit `ConfigEvent::RestartRequired { pending_count }`. Payload fields are aggregate-only (counts + enum labels) — NO key VALUES, NO paths (PII discipline per security plan §Logging + obs §8; add a PII-negative-canary test mirroring `cadence_event_payload_has_no_string_fields`). Maintain a `ConfigStatus { last_reload_unix_nano, last_error_category: Option<String>, restart_required_pending: u32 }` snapshot behind a mutex for `config.status()`.

6. **`config.*` TauRPC router.** Create `pulse-app/src/config_router.rs`: `#[taurpc::procedures(path = "config")] pub trait ConfigApi { async fn reload() -> Result<ConfigReloadPayload, AppError>; async fn status() -> Result<ConfigStatusPayload, AppError>; }` + `#[derive(Clone)] struct ConfigApiImpl { ... Arc<...watcher handle...> }` + `#[taurpc::resolvers]` with `#[tracing::instrument(skip_all, fields(... = Empty))]` aggregate-only `tracing::info!(target: "config.reload.request" / "config.status.request", ...)`. `config.reload()` forces an immediate synchronous re-read + re-apply (re-uses the step-3/4/5 core) returning `{ applied: bool, hot_count, restart_required_count }`; `config.status()` returns the `ConfigStatus` snapshot. Add a free-fn `config_error_to_app_error(err) -> AppError` (sanitized; orphan-rule-safe per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-18) — multi-line trait doc ABOVE the macro (CLAUDE.md 2026-05-25). Payloads carry no raw values/paths.

7. **Cadence coordinator live re-read (#80).** In `crates/triage/src/cadence/coordinator.rs`, extend `start_cadence_coordinator(...)` with a `mut cfg_rx: watch::Receiver<CadenceConfig>` param and add a `select!` arm `_ = cfg_rx.changed() => { let c = *cfg_rx.borrow_and_update(); tier3_interval = tokio::time::interval(Duration::from_secs(c.baseline_seconds as u64)); reflection_interval = ...; tier3_interval.tick().await; reflection_interval.tick().await; /* skip-first; prospective — no catch-up of missed ticks */ }`. Use the triage-side `CadenceConfig` type (NO ui-bridge dep added to triage). Emit a `cadence.config.reload_applied` aggregate tracing event. Co-located test: a `watch` change rebuilds the interval (assert via `CadenceCoordinator.config` swap + an injected-clock cadence test, or a unit test on the rebuild helper extracted from the arm).

8. **Lifecycle heartbeat live re-read (#67).** In the lifecycle heartbeat (`crates/triage/src/lifecycle/...`, `start_lifecycle_heartbeat`), replace the by-value `dormant_after_secs`/`archived_after_secs` params with `mut thresholds_rx: watch::Receiver<LifecycleThresholds>` (a small triage-side `Copy` struct `{ dormant_after_secs: u64, archived_after_secs: u64 }`) and read `*thresholds_rx.borrow()` at the top of each heartbeat tick (prospective — new thresholds apply from the next tick forward, no retroactive re-classify). Triage-side type → NO ui-bridge dep. Expose a `pub fn reevaluate_now(registry, baseline_state, thresholds, broadcast)` retrospective entry point (step 9 calls it).

9. **Retrospective re-evaluation engine (full).** Create `pulse-app/src/reevaluation.rs`: `pub trait RecentWindowReevaluator: Send + Sync { fn reevaluate(&self) -> ReevaluationSummary; }` (sync trait per arch §Cross-cutting; `Arc<dyn>` injection) + concrete `LiveReevaluator` holding `Arc<dyn ServiceRegistry>` + `Arc<BaselineState>` + the current `watch::Receiver<LifecycleThresholds>` + an immediate-cadence-cycle trigger (`Arc<CadenceConfig source>` + `run_one_coordinator_cycle` handle OR a `watch`-driven nudge). `reevaluate()` performs the FULL retrospective pass against CURRENT config: (a) call `lifecycle::reevaluate_now(...)` to re-classify every registered service against the new dormant/archived boundaries using each service's existing last-activity (emits the lifecycle transitions the new thresholds imply on `pulse://stream/service-lifecycle`); (b) trigger one immediate cadence cycle. Return `ReevaluationSummary { services_reclassified, transitions_emitted, cadence_cycle_triggered }`. (Cue/baseline telemetry-window replay #62/#64 is out of scope per the breadth decision — note in the summary + plan §follow-up; this chunk's retrospective covers the two wired consumers.)

10. **`diagnostics.reevaluate_recent_window()` procedure.** Extend `pulse-app/src/diagnostics_router.rs::DiagnosticsApi` with a 3rd method `async fn reevaluate_recent_window() -> Result<ReevaluateWindowPayload, AppError>`; extend `DiagnosticsApiImpl` with `Arc<dyn RecentWindowReevaluator>`; resolver calls `reevaluate()` + maps the summary to the payload + emits `diagnostics.reevaluate_recent_window.request` aggregate tracing. Keep the existing `template_distribution` + `retry_interpretation` methods intact (extend `DiagnosticsApiImpl::new(...)` arity).

11. **Boot wiring (`pulse-app/src/main.rs`).** In the `.setup(...)` closure: construct the `watch::channel(boot_settings)` Settings channel + `ConfigEventBroadcast`; spawn the config-watcher task (`tauri::async_runtime::spawn`) holding the watch sender + broadcast + data_dir; spawn a small fan-out that maps each new `Settings` → `CadenceConfig` (via `CadenceConfig::try_new`, falling back to previous on the redundant floor check) + `LifecycleThresholds` and pushes to the two per-consumer `watch::Sender`s; pass the per-consumer `watch::Receiver`s into `start_cadence_coordinator` (line ~1138) + `start_lifecycle_heartbeat` (line ~1243); construct `LiveReevaluator` + `ConfigApiImpl`; extend the `DiagnosticsApiImpl::new(...)` call; `.merge(ConfigApiImpl::new(...).into_handler())` in BOTH the production router chain AND the `emit_taurpc_bindings` test router chain (CLAUDE.md 2026-05-12 quadruple-binding).

12. **Observability AllowList.** In `pulse-app/src/observability.rs::AllowList::production()` add aggregate-only entries for: `config.reload.request`, `config.status.request`, `config.load` (watcher reload-applied), `config.load.path_validation` (warn on CWE-22 reject), `config.load.rejected` (parse/validate reject), `config.config_events` (broadcast emit), `diagnostics.reevaluate_recent_window.request`, `cadence.config.reload_applied`, `lifecycle.config.reload_applied` — fields limited to counts + enum/category labels (per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-17 aggregate-only triage discipline; add `for_target` resolver probe tests).

13. **Capability + drift registration.** Append a `config.{reload,status}` + `diagnostics.reevaluate_recent_window` sentence to `pulse-app/capabilities/default.json` `description` (router-level coverage; NO permission-array change). Add the 3 new procedures to `xtask/src/main.rs::EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` + a chunk-#96 drift test. Regenerate `pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` via the mcp-server-feature `emit_taurpc_bindings` run and verify `cargo xtask capability-drift` exits 0 (CLAUDE.md 2026-05-13/2026-05-17 regen discipline; `--bin pulse-app` filter per 2026-05-25).

14. **`notify` supply-chain.** Run `cargo audit` + `cargo deny check bans licenses sources`; add any new `notify` transitive duplicates to `deny.toml [bans] skip` with provenance comments (do NOT relax `multiple-versions = "deny"`) per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-03.

15. **Arch-registry follow-up (wrap-time, NOT /implement code).** A Type-6 `/andromeda-evolve --allow-arch-registry` amendment registers in §Occupied Resources: the `config-watcher` crate, the `config.reload` / `config.status` / `diagnostics.reevaluate_recent_window` TauRPC procedures, the `pulse://stream/config-events` broadcast topic, and the `notify` workspace dep — expected chunk-then-amendment Type 6 per the #67/#68/#82 precedent (D3 will fire at the implementation wrap; close it next session).

data.head: ### Per route#96: "Configuration hot reload + prospective threshold application"

body: - (arch) `crates/config-watcher/` is a registered workspace member (root `Cargo.toml` members) with the forward dep edge `config-watcher → ui-bridge` (no reverse edge); `cargo build --workspace` succeeds (per combined §arch "new workspace crate").

- (arch) `config.reload` + `config.status` + `diagnostics.reevaluate_recent_window` appear in `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` + `pulse-app/capabilities/default.json` description + the `emit_taurpc_bindings` router; `cargo xtask capability-drift` exits 0 (per combined §arch + §tests capability-drift binding).
- (arch) `pulse://stream/config-events` uses the `pulse://stream/<kebab>` Tauri-Channel convention; reload + restart-required events emit on it (per combined §arch broadcast registration).

- (security) A malformed / out-of-range `config.toml` write (negative/garbage value, out-of-range cadence or lifecycle) is rejected, the previous valid config stays live, and the error is surfaced via `config.status` WITHOUT applying the bad value (per combined §security validate-and-retain).

- (security) The watched `config.toml` path is canonicalized + asserted under the data dir before the watcher attaches; a `..`-traversal data-dir override is rejected (per combined §security CWE-22; mirrors chunk #95 egress validation).

- (security/obs) `config.status` output, the `config-events` payload, and the `config.*` tracing events contain no raw config contents, no full filesystem paths, and no secret-shaped strings (PII-negative-canary test passes; grep verifies) (per combined §security §obs PII discipline).
