- `crates/ui-bridge/src/contract.rs` (full, 2387 lines) — `Settings` struct holds EVERY hot-reload-candidate knob: `retention_seconds`, `lifecycle_{dormant,archived}_after_secs`, `drain_{depth,similarity_x100,max_clusters}`, `cadence_{baseline,accelerated,reflection}_seconds`, `cadence_tier2_acceleration_enabled` (+ theme/widget/mcp/notifications/snapshot). `Settings::validate()` (line 286) enforces every `_MIN`/`_MAX` bound + cross-field (`archived >= dormant`) and returns `AppError::Validation { field, reason }`. `Settings::load_from_data_dir(data_dir)` (line 367) reads `<data_dir>/config.toml` via `toml::from_str`, silent fallback to `Settings::default()` on missing/parse error. `#[derive(... PartialEq, Eq)]` → floats stored as `_x100: u32` scaled-int (drain_similarity_x100 precedent). In-code partition markers ALREADY DECLARED: drain_* comment says "changes require restart to apply (P-055 — restart-required notice surface)"; cadence_* comment says "Coordinator reads once at boot per pulse-v0_2_0-route §80; hot-reload deferred к chunk #94."

- `Cargo.toml` (full, workspace root) — `[workspace.dependencies]` has NO `notify` (grep confirmed zero matches) → new dep. `toml = "0.8"`, `strict-path = "0.2"`, `tokio = { features=["full"] }` (so `tokio::sync::watch` is available — no `arc-swap` dep needed), `tempfile`/`rstest`/`assert_fs` dev-deps present. `[workspace] members` = 14 crates + pulse-app + xtask; NO `config-watcher`. (`crates/triage-experimental/` exists on disk but is NOT a workspace member — ignore.)

- `crates/triage/src/cadence/config.rs` (full, 196 lines) — `CadenceConfig { baseline_seconds, accelerated_seconds, reflection_seconds, tier2_acceleration_enabled }` + `CadenceConfig::try_new(...)` safety-floor validator (`CadenceConfigError` variants) + `Default`. This is the value object the coordinator consumes.

- `crates/triage/src/cadence/coordinator.rs` (grep) — **CRITICAL:** `start_cadence_coordinator(..., cadence_config: Arc<CadenceConfig>)` builds `tier3_interval = tokio::time::interval(Duration::from_secs(cadence_config.baseline_seconds))` + `reflection_interval` ONCE before the `loop { select! { ... } }` (lines 275-280); the loop ticks those fixed interval objects and never re-reads the `Arc`. `CadenceCoordinator { config: Arc<CadenceConfig> }` holds an Arc but the running loop captured the durations at spawn → **changing the Arc contents would NOT change the live tick rate.** Hot-reload of cadence requires a loop change (a `watch::Receiver` select-arm that rebuilds the intervals on change).

- `crates/triage/src/cadence/broadcast.rs` (full, 155 lines) — canonical broadcast pattern to mirror for `config-events`: `pub const STREAM_NAME_* : &str = "pulse://stream/cadence-events"`, `BROADCAST_CAPACITY = 32`, thin `XxxBroadcast { sender: broadcast::Sender<Event> }` wrapper with `new/sender/subscribe/subscriber_count` + `Default`; payload is `#[derive(Serialize)]` with aggregate-only fields (enum `mode_label: &'static str` + counts + timestamps; explicit PII-negative-canary test asserting no `service`/`scope_id`/etc.).

- `pulse-app/src/diagnostics_router.rs` (full, 447 lines) — canonical TauRPC router pattern to mirror for `config.*`: `#[taurpc::procedures(path = "diagnostics")] pub trait DiagnosticsApi { async fn ...() -> Result<Payload, AppError>; }` + `#[derive(Clone)] struct DiagnosticsApiImpl { ... Arc<dyn Trait> ... }` + `#[taurpc::resolvers] impl` with `#[tracing::instrument(skip_all, fields(... = tracing::field::Empty))]` + aggregate-only `tracing::info!(target: "diagnostics.<verb>.request", ...)` + free-fn `drain_error_to_app_error(err) -> AppError` sanitizer (no `impl From` at binary boundary — orphan-rule-safe). Multi-line doc moved ABOVE the `#[taurpc::procedures]` macro (per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-25 taurpc doc-comment gotcha). The `diagnostics.*` namespace ALREADY EXISTS here — adding `diagnostics.reevaluate_recent_window()` would extend THIS trait (+3rd method) rather than a new namespace.

- `pulse-app/capabilities/default.json` (full) — single `default` capability; `permissions: ["core:default", "updater:default"]`. New TauRPC procedures need only a DESCRIPTION-block append (router-level coverage; TauRPC dispatches all methods through one invoke handler per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-03) — NO new permission entry, NO new capability file.

- `pulse-app/src/main.rs` (boot regions) — `resolve_data_dir()` (line 177); `boot_settings = Settings::load_from_data_dir(&data_dir)` (line 713) in the early boot sequence; inside the Tauri `.setup(...)` closure a SECOND `settings = Settings::load_from_data_dir(&data_dir)` (line 943) feeds `apply_widget_settings` + the cadence/lifecycle spawns; cadence spawn at 1120-1145 (`CadenceConfig::try_new(settings.cadence_*) → Arc → start_cadence_coordinator(...)`); lifecycle spawn at 1243-1251 (`start_lifecycle_heartbeat(..., settings.lifecycle_dormant_after_secs, settings.lifecycle_archived_after_secs, ...)` — thresholds passed BY VALUE at spawn → read-once); `emit_taurpc_bindings` test at ~1560.

- **`Settings` is the single config surface** (`crates/ui-bridge/src/contract.rs`): all hot-reload candidates already live here + `validate()` already enforces bounds + `load_from_data_dir` already parses `<data_dir>/config.toml`. The watcher re-loads + re-validates through THIS surface — no parallel config struct. (Settings-extension precedent, CLAUDE.md 2026-05-09.)

- **Read-once-at-boot consumers** (main.rs §boot + cadence/coordinator.rs): cadence coordinator, lifecycle heartbeat, and the cue/baseline/storm tick loops all capture config at spawn. There is NO existing live-reconfiguration channel. This is the central implementation gap: hot-reload delivery must be ADDED to each consumer that needs live application.

- **Broadcast topic pattern** (cadence/broadcast.rs): thin `broadcast::Sender` wrapper + `pulse://stream/<kebab>` const + capacity 32 + aggregate-only `#[derive(Serialize)]` payload + PII-negative-canary test. Directly templatable for `ConfigEvent` + `ConfigEventBroadcast`.

- **TauRPC router pattern** (diagnostics_router.rs): trait + `Impl` + resolvers + instrument + free-fn error map. `config.*` is a new dotted namespace; `diagnostics.reevaluate_recent_window` extends the existing `diagnostics` trait.

- **`tokio::sync::watch` is the zero-new-dep delivery mechanism** (Cargo.toml tokio "full"): a `watch::Sender<HotConfig>` published by the watcher + `watch::Receiver` select-arms in consumer loops gives prospective live application without `arc-swap`. The cadence broadcast/cue precedents use `tokio::sync::broadcast`; `watch` (latest-value, no backlog) is the better fit for "current config" semantics.

- **Capability registration = description-block only** (capabilities/default.json): append a `config.{reload,status}` (+ optional `diagnostics.reevaluate_recent_window`) sentence to the `description` string; do NOT add permission array entries. `cargo xtask capability-drift` reads the merged `bindings/index.ts`, not the JSON permissions (per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-03/2026-05-12 quadruple-binding).

- **Quadruple+ binding for new TauRPC namespace** (CLAUDE.md 2026-05-12): router registration in main.rs `.merge(...)` chain + `pulse-app/capabilities/default.json` description + `xtask/src/main.rs::EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` + the `emit_taurpc_bindings` test's `.merge(...)` chain. Multi-line trait doc goes ABOVE the `#[taurpc::procedures]` macro (2026-05-25).

- **Cross-crate state via trait-in-lower-crate + `Arc<dyn Trait>`** / **errors via free-fn `map_err` at the binary boundary** (CLAUDE.md 2026-05-16 / 2026-05-18): if a watcher lives in a lower crate and a consumer in another, deliver via `Arc<dyn Trait>` / `watch::Receiver` injected at the pulse-app boundary; convert watcher errors → `AppError` via a free fn in the router file.
- **Async-trait via manual `Pin<Box<dyn Future + Send + 'a>>`** (CLAUDE.md 2026-05-23) if any async hook crosses the boundary — no `async-trait` dep.

- **Aggregate-only self-observation fields** (CLAUDE.md 2026-05-17 session 84 + observability.rs AllowList): the `config.*` tracing targets + `config-events` payload carry bounded counts + enum labels + sanitized field names ONLY — never raw config values / full paths / secret-shaped strings. New targets need explicit AllowList entries in `pulse-app/src/observability.rs` (default-deny redaction).

- **pulse-app tests live in `pulse-app/tests/`, NOT source-level `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`** (CLAUDE.md 2026-05-20): `[lib] test = false` means source-level pulse-app tests never run. A NEW lower crate (`crates/config-watcher/`) CAN carry co-located `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` that run normally.

- **Time-deterministic tests** (testing.md): `#[tokio::test(start_paused = true)]` + `tokio::time::advance` for debounce/apply-window; NEVER `sleep(N)`. Note `start_paused` requires `current_thread` flavor + `tokio` `test-util` dev-feature (CLAUDE.md 2026-05-03 / 2026-05-06).

- **`notify` dep discipline** (security.md + CLAUDE.md 2026-05-03): pin a version, pass `cargo deny check bans licenses sources`; add new transitive duplicates to `deny.toml [bans] skip` with provenance (do not relax `multiple-versions = "deny"`).
(Final set depends on the Phase-6 placement decision — see Open questions Q2. Both shapes listed.)

- `Cargo.toml` — add `notify = "..."` (pinned) to `[workspace.dependencies]`; add `crates/config-watcher` to `members` IF new-crate path.
- `pulse-app/Cargo.toml` (+ `crates/config-watcher/Cargo.toml` or wherever the watcher lands) — depend on `notify` + `tokio` (watch).

- `pulse-app/src/main.rs` — spawn the watcher in the `.setup(...)` closure; construct `ConfigEventBroadcast` + `watch::Sender`; thread `watch::Receiver` into the consumer(s) chosen by the breadth decision (Q1); register `ConfigApiImpl` in both production + `emit_taurpc_bindings` router `.merge(...)` chains.

- `crates/triage/src/cadence/coordinator.rs` — IF cadence live-reload chosen: add a `watch::Receiver<CadenceConfig>` (or `Settings`) select-arm that rebuilds `tier3_interval`/`reflection_interval` on change (prospective: next tick uses new rate; no retroactive catch-up). Plus `start_cadence_coordinator` signature extension.
- Other consumer loops (`crates/triage/src/...` lifecycle/cue/baseline/storm + their main.rs spawns) — modified ONLY for the categories the breadth decision (Q1) includes.
- `pulse-app/src/observability.rs` — add AllowList entries for new `config.*` + `config-events` tracing targets (aggregate-only).
- `pulse-app/capabilities/default.json` — append `config.{reload,status}` (+ optional `diagnostics.reevaluate_recent_window`) to the description block.
- `xtask/src/main.rs` — add the new procedures to `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` + the chunk #96 drift test.
- `pulse-app/src/diagnostics_router.rs` — IF `reevaluate_recent_window` lands here: extend `DiagnosticsApi` trait + `DiagnosticsApiImpl` (+3rd method/resolver).
- `pulse-app/ui/src/bindings/index.ts` — regenerated (auto) via the mcp-server-feature `emit_taurpc_bindings` run (CLAUDE.md 2026-05-13/2026-05-17 regen discipline).
- `pulse-app/ui/**` — IF a Diagnostics restart-required / reload-status notice surface is included (design/a11y conditional bindings activate); otherwise backend-only.

1. **Hot-reload consumer breadth** (PLAN-SHAPING — surface to user): §94 says thresholds + cadences + severity + suppression + lifecycle boundaries all "apply within 2s", but every consumer reads config once at boot, so each needs a loop modification. Options: (A) full breadth (wire cadence #80 + lifecycle #67 + cue/baseline thresholds #62/#64 + suppression #63 all live) — largest, literal §94; (B) cadence + lifecycle live (the two boot-spawned periodic loops), thresholds/suppression as restart-required-notice + follow-up; (C) cadence-only live (single representative consumer, explicitly the one code-marked "hot-reload deferred to chunk #94") + watcher infra + restart-notice for the rest. DEFAULT: stay on the fixed `<data_dir>/config.toml` per the existing `Settings::load_from_data_dir` — the watcher watches that path; do NOT activate the deferred env var this chunk (avoids an extra arch-registry env-var amendment). - **Phase number:** 94
- **Route chunks covered:** route#97 "Settings → Diagnostics view"
- **Epoch:** Epoch 9 — Foundation v0.2.0
- **Group reason:** single-substantial (multi-domain: +2 TauRPC procedures + corpus metric-history query + NEW 5-section webview surface; terminal registered chunk of the route, capability P-058)

Single read-only L6 self-observability surface bringing together pipeline metrics from prior chunks (#59, #61–#67, #79–#85) into one Settings → Diagnostics view with five sections (Connection / Model / Pipeline / Hardware / Templates), `diagnostics.snapshot()` + `diagnostics.history(metric_name, window)` TauRPC, corpus `pipeline_metrics` reads, 30-day default history retention. All read-only per capability P-051. Capability P-058 (Pipeline Self-Observability — full surface). Workspace deps delta: none. Arch-registry delta: +2 TauRPC procedures.
**Constraints across domains:**

- (arch) Use `<router>.<verb>` dotted-`snake_case` shape; extend the existing `diagnostics` router namespace (`diagnostics.snapshot` + `diagnostics.history` are siblings of `template_distribution` / `retry_interpretation` / `reevaluate_recent_window`) — do NOT invent a new top-level namespace (per arch §Conventions Endpoint naming + §Occupied Resources `diagnostics.*`).

- (arch / security) Both procedures return `Result<T, AppError>` (serde-friendly enum); corpus errors convert at the bridge to `AppError::Storage { message }` with a sanitized one-liner via the free-fn `corpus_error_to_app_error` shape — orphan rule blocks `impl From<corpus::Error> for AppError` (per arch §Conventions Error response schema + security §Error Handling + §Anti-Patterns Code Patterns).

- (arch / security) Both procedures REQUIRE capability registration (negative-default; missing entry = silent runtime rejection); `xtask capability-drift` enforces. Extending the existing `diagnostics.*` router adds NO new per-procedure capability JSON entry (TauRPC capability JSON is router-level), but the procedure names still need to flow through the binding chain (per arch §Cross-cutting Webview IPC capability policy + security §API Security TauRPC authorization).

- (security / arch) `diagnostics.history(metric_name, window)` args deserialize via `serde` and are bounded server-side: `metric_name` validated against a known-enum/allowlist (never interpolated as a SQL identifier), `window` bounded (≤30-day default retention); the corpus query MUST use prepared `?` placeholders, never `format!` SQL (per security §Input Validation DuckDB/query-param row + §Anti-Patterns Input row 2; arch §Critical Warnings prepared-statement rule applied to the corpus rusqlite path).

- (arch) Corpus metric-history read code lives in `crates/corpus/` and extends `CorpusReader`; the `pipeline_metrics` `payload` column is cell-level AES-256-GCM encrypted, so the new history query MUST decrypt via the existing `cell_decrypt(self.key(), …)` path. NOTE: existing `load_pipeline_metric` returns only the single LATEST snapshot (`ORDER BY snapshot_unix_nano DESC LIMIT 1`) — a NEW time-series read method is required (per arch §Critical Warnings + §Occupied Resources Corpus SQLite at-rest posture; verified `crates/corpus/src/contract.rs:432`).

- (arch) Workspace deps delta MUST be zero; arch-registry delta bounded to exactly +2 TauRPC procedures (no new env var / table / path / broadcast topic) (per arch §Occupied Resources; chunk one-liner).

- (security / obs / arch) Aggregate-only logging: `diagnostics.{snapshot,history}` argument values + returned metric payload / decrypted BLOB contents / per-service identifiers MUST NOT be logged verbatim; emit bounded counts / enum tags / numeric values only (per security §Logging NEVER-log list + obs §11 Logs + arch §Critical Warnings).

- (obs) Corpus `pipeline_metrics` history query logs `query_id` + `param_count` + `param_types`, NEVER raw query text or `metric_name`/`window` values — query-anonymizer discipline applies to the SQLite path identically to DuckDB (per obs §6 Boundary-call DuckDB query row + §8 + §11 Logs).

- (obs) `diagnostics.history` time-series MUST NOT log the per-point `value` array or full snapshot subsystem dump at `info`/`error` — log `row_count`/`result_count` only; per-row detail is `debug`/`trace`-gated (per obs §11 Logs hot-path-info ban + §6).

- (obs) READ-ONLY CONSUMER surface — do NOT introduce a new `metric.diagnostics.*` emitter for rendering existing data; reuse existing `metric.*` events / `pipeline_metrics` rows already produced by chunks #59/#61-#67/#79-#85 (per obs §5 single-observability-primitive — avoid double-counting).
- (obs) If a consumer-side `tokio::spawn` drives any live subscription, use `.in_current_span()` to avoid span-context bleed across `.await` (per obs §11 Spans).
- (design) Consume only `@theme` design tokens — no hardcoded hex/px literals (per design §Surface desktop-webview Tokens + §Self-Validation Token Test).

- (design) Data-vs-UI typography split: NUMERIC metric values (success rate %, queue depth, last-span-ago, p50/p95/p99, template counts, backoff countdown) in `--font-code` (JetBrains Mono) + `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`; section headers/labels in `--font-body` (IBM Plex Sans) (per design §Typography + §Anti-Patterns Rejected Default).

- (design) Each section card uses borders-only depth: `--color-raised-1` bg + 1px subtle Earth-Blue border + `--radius-md` + `--spacing-md` padding — NO shadows/gradients/glassmorphism (per design §Depth Strategy + §Surface Component Patterns Cards + §Anti-Patterns Universal Ban).

- (design / a11y) State indicators (connection / model / backoff / inference-success) pair state color with text label and/or icon — never color alone; healthy→`--color-primary`/`--color-feedback-success`, degraded/error/backoff→`--color-accent` (non-text token: border + icon, with `--color-text-primary` for adjacent text) (per design §Anti-Patterns + Decisions Log 2026-05-03 accent-as-non-text-token; a11y SC 1.4.1).

- (design / layouts / a11y) Any sparkline/history-chart or backoff-countdown motion respects `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` and stays within the 0.35 chrome expression budget (≤200ms ease-out; NO entrance/scroll/staggered animation). A live-updating backoff countdown is a data display (tabular-num text), not an animated bar (per design §Motion + layouts §Expression level + a11y SC 2.3.3 AAA).

- (layouts) Diagnostics is reachable from the Settings entry point (gear icon / `/settings` child route) as a routable sub-view per the TanStack Router convention; NOT added to the compact widget or tray menu (per layouts §Component Primary navigation + §IA notes Deep-link convention).

- (layouts) Five sections stacked vertically with consistent rhythm (`gap: space-lg`) reusing the Settings panel layout; metric values render in read-only status-bar/table idiom (no interactive form controls on value cells) (per layouts §Component Settings modal form + §Component Footer read-only status bar). NOTE: the five-section organization is NEW — layout-templates.md is silent on a Diagnostics-specific wireframe (orchestrator surfaces to user).
- (a11y) Tier Standard WCAG 2.1 AA + motion AAA escalation (SC 2.3.3); every claimed criterion has a machine-verifiable path (axe-core / Lighthouse / pa11y / Playwright JSON) (per a11y §1 + §2).

- (a11y) Semantic HTML first: build sections from `<section>` + headings + `<dl>`/`<dt>`/`<dd>` or table; single `h1` ("Diagnostics") + sequential `h2` per section, no skipped levels (per a11y §4 + §7, SC 1.3.1 + SC 2.4.6).

- (a11y) Every metric value perceivable as text; history charts (canvas/sparkline) require a text alternative (table or `aria-label` summarizing the series) since `<canvas>`/WebGPU carries no semantics (per a11y §1 WebGPU canvas + §7, SC 1.1.1 + SC 1.3.1 + SC 4.1.2).
- (a11y) Auto-updating backoff countdown / dynamic updates announce via `aria-live="polite"` (never `assertive` for a recurring tick) (per a11y §7 Live regions, SC 4.1.3).

- (a11y / design) Contrast minimums via tokens: `--color-text-primary/--color-base` ≥ 4.5:1; secondary/tertiary ≥ 3:1 large-text-only (tertiary `#7D8697` NOT for ≤14px body labels) (per a11y §6 + design §Self-Validation Contrast Test, SC 1.4.3).
**Patterns to follow:**

- (arch) Cross-crate read state via `Arc<dyn CorpusReader>` derived from the single `Arc<Corpus>` intermediate (N-trait-from-single-Arc; one rusqlite connection mutex + one key), exactly as `StorageApiImpl` does for `storage.inspect`/`storage.path` (chunk #68) — `pulse-app/src/storage_router.rs` precedent (per arch §Cross-cutting Module dependency direction).

- (arch) Extend the existing `#[taurpc::procedures(path = "diagnostics")]` `DiagnosticsApi` trait + resolver in `pulse-app/src/diagnostics_router.rs` (verified `:100`) — do NOT create a new router file; keeps the namespace single-owner.

- (arch) Corpus error → AppError via free-function `map_err` (e.g. `corpus_error_to_app_error`) at the resolver boundary — `pulse-app/src/storage_router.rs` precedent (per arch §Cross-cutting Module dependency direction).

- (arch) Read-only-first surface: reuse existing read resolvers where they exist (`connection.current_state` #59, `model.current_profile` #82, `diagnostics.template_distribution` #69) rather than duplicating data paths (per arch §Occupied Resources; CLAUDE.md HYBRID-RENDER session-learnings 2026-05-26/2026-06-01).

- (obs) IPC-handler span pattern `#[tracing::instrument(skip_all, fields(traceparent = %tp))]` mirroring the existing `diagnostics.*` handlers (`template_distribution` #69, `retry_interpretation` #86, `reevaluate_recent_window` #96) (per obs §4); span naming `diagnostics.snapshot.request` / `diagnostics.history.request` low-cardinality (per obs §4 + §11).

- (obs) Query-anonymizer pattern for the corpus read (`query_id` + `param_count` + `param_types`); default subscriber fields (`service.name`/`version`/`environment`) ride every line automatically (per obs §5 + §3).

- (obs / design) UI metric values are legitimate UI vocabulary, not PII — PII-grep heuristics distinguish literal secret formats (`Bearer …`/`sk-…`/`ghp_…`/`AKIA…`) from displayed metric/label text (per obs §12 Decisions Log 2026-05-04 UI-vocabulary exemption).

- (design / a11y) Read-only status display with `role="status"` + `aria-live="polite"` + `var(--font-code)` tabular-num values; mirror `pulse-app/ui/src/dashboard/routes/settings/ExportForTraining.tsx` (status region) + `pulse-app/ui/src/dashboard/routes/diagnostics/TemplateDistribution.tsx` (existing diagnostics-namespace surface — directly reusable structural precedent for the Templates section) (per design §Surface Component Patterns; a11y §4 Status pattern).

- (design) Metric label/value row: `display:flex; justify-content:space-between; gap:var(--spacing-sm)`, label `--color-text-secondary` Body + value `--font-code` `--color-text-primary` — exact ExportForTraining category-breakdown pattern (per design §Typography Data role).

- (design) Reuse `pulse-app/ui/src/components/ConnectionDot.tsx` for the Connection section state dimension (color + text, not a re-implementation) (per design §Brand Identity + §Color Palette Semantic Colors).

- (design) Explicit empty/loading/error states per section; prefer registered custom Observatory glyphs (`aperture`/`constellation-grid`/`telescope`) over generic stock icons (per design §Surface Component Patterns + §Iconography).

- (layouts) Tabular metric display (Templates Drain distribution + Pipeline L0-L5) maps to the shadcn `Table` pattern (header `color-base` bg + `font-label` + 1px subtle bottom-border rows + `space-sm` cell padding + monospace tabular numerals) (per layouts §Component Trace data table).

- (layouts) Model section "active tier / success rate / queue depth / backoff countdown" echoes the tray-menu live read-only summary-line idiom (per layouts §Component Tray menu Summary line + Footer read-only status bar).

- (a11y) Wrap each history/sparkline visualization in `<region aria-label="…">` mirroring the established `region[aria-label="Telemetry traces chart"]` pattern (per a11y §7 Landmark roles); reduce-motion via Tailwind `motion-reduce:` / `useReducedMotion`; settings-modal focus discipline (Esc returns to parent Settings, restore focus to trigger) (per a11y §5 + §6 + §9).
**Anti-patterns to avoid:**

- (security / arch) NEVER `format!("…WHERE metric_name = '{}'…", arg)` against the corpus connection — prepared `?` placeholders only; `metric_name` never names a table/column (per security §Anti-Patterns Input row 2; arch §Conventions LOCKED endpoint naming).

- (security / obs / arch) NEVER expose stack traces / file paths / Rust struct names / library versions in `AppError::Internal { message }`; NEVER log returned metric payload, raw `window`/`metric_name` arg values, decrypted BLOB contents, or per-service identifiers in `agent-latest.jsonl` (per security §Anti-Patterns Logging rows 1/3/4; obs §7 + §11; arch §Critical Warnings).

- (arch) Do NOT add a new top-level bare verb / new router namespace, a new env var / fs path / table / broadcast topic, or widen the corpus surface to a write/mutation path (bind `Arc<dyn CorpusReader>`, NOT `CorpusWriter`) (per arch §Occupied Resources + §Conventions; chunk one-liner "+2 TauRPC procedures").

- (design) NEVER use uniform monochrome status icons (green ✓ / red ✗ alone) as sole state encoding; NEVER render shadows/gradients/glassmorphism on the section cards (Halo State Pulse WebGPU layer is the ONLY gradient/blur exception); NEVER use a banned font (Inter/Roboto/Arial/…/Space Grotesk) or Tailwind default palette (purple/sky/zinc) (per design §Anti-Patterns Universal Bans + Rejected Defaults).

- (layouts) Do NOT add Diagnostics to the compact widget or the tray menu (flat fixed hierarchy Open/Snapshot/MCP/Settings/Quit); do NOT introduce a native OS surface element; do NOT render history charts as decorative chrome animation exceeding the 0.35 budget (per layouts §Surface desktop-native + §IA notes).

- (a11y) NEVER render metric values / history series as canvas/visual-only with no text alternative (fails SC 1.1.1/1.3.1); NEVER convey state by color alone; NEVER use `aria-live="assertive"`/`role="alert"` for the recurring countdown tick; NEVER `role="term"`/`role="definition"` on bare `<div>`s instead of `<dl>`/`<dt>`/`<dd>`; NEVER `outline:none` without a `--border-focus` replacement (per a11y §11 + §7, SC 1.1.1/1.3.1/1.4.1/4.1.3/2.4.7).

- (tests) NEVER add `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` to `pulse-app/src/` for the new resolver tests (silently never run under nextest — `pulse-app` has `[lib] test = false`); NEVER include visual-regression / pixel inspection for chart rendering; NEVER assert backoff-countdown / last-span-ago / 30-day-window with real wall-clock (per test-plan §11 + testing.md Session Additions 2026-05-20).
**Contract bindings:**

- **obs ↔ tests** (reciprocal): new `diagnostics.{snapshot,history}` handlers emit `info`-level boundary spans in the binding NDJSON schema; the tests "self-reporting accuracy" check (inject known pipeline behaviors → verify Diagnostics reflects them, source §95) consumes the responses; obs provides the structured-log shape + query-anonymizer fields, tests assert the surface reflects injected state. Orchestrator to reconcile whether self-reporting verifies via corpus `pipeline_metrics` rows (tests-owned) vs log-line grep (obs-owned) (per obs §3 + tests §obs binding).

- **security ↔ tests** (reciprocal): `cargo xtask capability-drift` (+ chunk #77 `capability-widening-check`) is a CI security gate; security owns the pass condition (both new procedures in `EXPECTED_PROCEDURES` + capability JSON; no widening of `pulse:notification`/`pulse:tray`/`pulse:plugin-fs`); an AppError-sanitization + PII negative-canary test fits the `security-vector-coverage` harness (fixtures synthetic only) (per security §Contract bindings + tests §arch capability-drift).

- **design ↔ a11y** (reciprocal): contrast token pairs bind to SC 1.4.3 (colorjs.io harness); state-color tokens bind to SC 1.4.1 not-color-alone; motion tokens bind to SC 2.3.3 reduce-motion; focus ring binds to `--border-focus` SC 2.4.7. Design owns token choices; a11y asserts thresholds (per design §Contract bindings + a11y §Contract bindings).

- **a11y ↔ obs** (reciprocal): a11y violations emit structured violation JSON to obs §6 schema (`wcag_criterion`/`violation_type`/`severity`/`surface`/`selector`/`remediation`) — note this is the SAME `~/.andromeda-pulse/logs/` sink the Diagnostics Pipeline section visualizes; keep the a11y assertion stream conceptually distinct from the product's L0-L5 metrics (per a11y §Contract bindings + obs §a11y binding).

NOTE: research must reconcile actual webview directory layout — `pulse-app/ui/src/dashboard/routes/{settings,diagnostics}/` is the observed existing structure (vs source §95's nominal `pulse-app/ui/settings/`).

data.head: # Phase 94 Plan — chunks route#97: "Settings → Diagnostics view"

body: _Generated by /andromeda-phase Phase 4. Read by /andromeda-implement. Manual edits between runs are fine; do not edit during /implement run._
- **Phase number:** 94

- **Route chunks covered:**
  - route#97 "Settings → Diagnostics view"
- **Epoch:** Epoch 9 — Foundation v0.2.0
- **Capability:** P-058 (Pipeline Self-Observability — full surface)

- **Scope decision (user-confirmed at Phase 3 → AskUserQuestion):** **HYBRID RENDER.** `diagnostics.snapshot()` aggregates only data that already exists/flows; sub-fields with no producer render an explicit "not yet recorded" degraded notice; `diagnostics.history()` lands as a registered stub (validated args → empty series + notice). Both procedures land (+2 TauRPC, matching source §95). Honest about gaps; bounded single-session chunk.

Deliver the read-only L6 self-observability surface — a "Settings → Diagnostics" view bringing the pipeline's own state into one webview surface (capability P-058) — by extending the existing `diagnostics.*` TauRPC router with two procedures and adding a new `Diagnostics.tsx` webview surface with five sections (Connection / Model / Pipeline / Hardware / Templates). Per the Phase-3 producer-check, `pipeline_metrics` is an opaque latest-only state-snapshot store (not numeric metric-history) and no production path records per-metric numeric time-series, so this chunk takes the **hybrid-render** path: `diagnostics.snapshot()` aggregates the live in-memory state that genuinely exists (connection state, model tier/profile/load-status + backoff countdown from the degraded-mode FSM the router already holds, Drain template distribution + count, hardware profile label), and explicitly marks the not-yet-produced sub-fields (inference success rate, queue depth, full L0-L5 per-layer numerics, 30-day history) as "not yet recorded"; `diagnostics.history(metric_name, window_seconds)` lands as a validated stub returning an empty series + a degraded notice. The surface reuses existing read resolvers where they exist (`connection.current_state` #59 for the Connection section; `diagnostics.template_distribution` #69 + the existing `TemplateDistribution.tsx` for the Templates section) per arch §Cross-cutting HYBRID-RENDER discipline, so `snapshot()` carries only the Model/Hardware/Pipeline self-observability data that has no dedicated resolver yet. Per security plan §Error Handling + §Logging, both procedures return `Result<T, AppError>` with aggregate-only tracing; per arch §Occupied Resources the arch-registry delta is exactly +2 TauRPC procedures (no new env var / table / broadcast topic / workspace dep). Scope reconciliation vs source §95: because the hybrid path runs NO corpus time-series query, `crates/corpus/` is NOT touched this chunk (the source-§95 "metric history queries" + the prepared-statement / query-anonymizer constraints are N/A-by-construction); the real-history producer + corpus query path is deferred to a future chunk once a numeric-metric-history producer exists.

1. **Backend — extend the `diagnostics` TauRPC trait + resolvers** (`pulse-app/src/diagnostics_router.rs`):
   - Add to `trait DiagnosticsApi`: `async fn snapshot() -> Result<DiagnosticsSnapshotPayload, AppError>;` + `async fn history(metric_name: String, window_seconds: u64) -> Result<DiagnosticsHistoryPayload, AppError>;`. Place any inner doc as a regular `//` comment ABOVE the `#[taurpc::procedures]` macro (taurpc 0.7 rejects multi-line `///` inside the trait body — session-learnings 2026-05-25).
   - Add payload types (`#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq, specta::Type)]`):
     - `DiagnosticsSnapshotPayload { model: ModelSectionPayload, hardware: HardwareSectionPayload, pipeline: PipelineSectionPayload, captured_unix_nano: i64 }`.
     - `ModelSectionPayload { tier_label: String, profile_label: String, load_status: String, model_identity_name: Option<String>, backoff_state_label: String, backoff_remaining_seconds: u64, consecutive_failures: u32, inference_success_rate_basis_points: Option<u32>, queue_depth: Option<u64> }` — `inference_success_rate_basis_points` + `queue_depth` are `None` this chunk (no producer); basis-points keeps `Eq` (no `f64`, per session-learnings 2026-05-19 scaled-int convention).
     - `HardwareSectionPayload { profile_label: String, detection_detail: Option<String> }` (bounded label from `interpretation::hardware::profile_label`; `detection_detail` `None` unless the profile source exposes a bounded detail string).
     - `PipelineSectionPayload { drain_template_count: u64, per_layer_recorded: bool }` — `per_layer_recorded = false` (L0-L5 numerics not yet produced); `drain_template_count` from the held `DrainMiner`.
     - `DiagnosticsHistoryPayload { metric_name: String, points: Vec<MetricHistoryPoint>, recorded: bool, notice: String }` + `MetricHistoryPoint { snapshot_unix_nano: i64, value_basis_points: u32 }` (empty `points` this chunk; `recorded = false`).
   - Extend `DiagnosticsApiImpl` + `::new(...)`: add `runner: Arc<dyn interpretation::contract::LlmInferenceRunner>` + `profile_source: Arc<dyn triage::contract::HardwareProfileSource>` (it already holds `miner`, `degraded_mode`, `reevaluator`).
   - `snapshot()` resolver: read `runner.tier()/current_status()/identity()` + `profile_source.current_profile()` + `degraded_mode.current_snapshot(now)` (state label + backoff_remaining + consecutive_failures) + `miner.template_count()`; build the payload via the existing `*_label` fns; `inference_success_rate_basis_points`/`queue_depth`/`per_layer_recorded`/`detection_detail` set to None/false. Aggregate-only `#[tracing::instrument(skip_all, fields(...))]` + `info!` at `diagnostics.snapshot.request`.
   - `history()` resolver (STUB): validate `metric_name` against a bounded allowlist const (e.g. `DIAGNOSTICS_HISTORY_METRICS: &[&str]`) → `AppError::Validation { field: "metric_name", reason }` on miss; bound `window_seconds` (≤ 30-day seconds const) clamped; return `DiagnosticsHistoryPayload { metric_name, points: vec![], recorded: false, notice: "metric history recording not yet available" }`. 1. **★ DECISIVE — `diagnostics.history()` / numeric-metric-history has NO data producer (capability-assumed-but-not-implemented).** Source §95 wants `diagnostics.history(metric_name, window)` to return a "time-series" over "30-day metric history from corpus `pipeline_metrics`", and the Model section wants "inference success rate, queue depth". Reality: `pipeline_metrics` stores opaque encrypted STATE-SNAPSHOT blobs (drain/baseline/storm), `load_pipeline_metric` is latest-only, and no production path records per-metric NUMERIC time-series; `LlmInferenceRunner` exposes no success-rate/queue-depth accessor. This is the project's documented HYBRID/DEFER/EXTEND/FORWARD-INFRA fork (session-learnings 2026-05-26 / 2026-05-30 / 2026-05-31) — surfaced to the user via AskUserQuestion BEFORE plan.md is finalized. Options:

Unavailable sub-fields (inference success rate, queue depth, full L0-L5 numeric metrics, 30-day history) render an explicit "not yet recorded" degraded notice. `history()` deferred OR a stub returning empty + notice. Bounded; arch-delta +1 (or +2 w/ stub history). HONEST about gaps; matches the read-only L6 intent + prior-chunk degraded-mode UX precedent.
   - **(B) Snapshot-only, defer history** — implement ONLY `diagnostics.snapshot()` this chunk; do NOT add `history()`. Smallest; arch-delta +1 TauRPC. The "+2 procedures / history" of source §95 becomes a follow-up once a numeric-metric-history producer exists.
   - **(C) Extend backend (full fidelity, larger)** — add a NEW numeric-metric-history producer + persistence path so `history()` has real time-series. ~2x+ scope; needs a producer + likely a new metric-row shape/table (tension with "+2 TauRPC only / no new table"); arguably its own chunk. Full fidelity to source §95.

- **Phase number:** 95

- **Route chunks covered:**
  - route#98 "Background reflection cadence"
- **Epoch:** Epoch 9 — Foundation v0.2.0

- **Scope decision (user, /phase Phase 3 AskUserQuestion):** **EXTEND — full reflection incidents.** Land the reflection L4 prompt variant AND the reflection-incident production path (default Curious unless high-confidence), accepting the `Incident`/`CueKind` contract change + the chunk #91/#92 per-service-severity interaction.

Chunk #98 makes the background reflection cadence (1800s) a first-class interpretation path: a 30-minute-window L3 digest is interpreted by L4 with a **cumulative-trend-emphasis prompt** (not the acute single-event prompt), and a surfacing reflection produces a **workspace-global reflection incident** that defaults to Curious severity unless the model identifies a high-confidence pattern. Per Phase 3 research, chunks #80/#81 already built the bulk of the mechanical surface — the 1800s `reflection_interval` trigger (`coordinator.rs:285-353`), the 30-min window threaded into all 7 L1a SQL queries (`coordinator.rs:172,194-200`) AND into `assembler.assemble(…, window)` (`digest_runtime.rs:104,114`), `DigestKind::Reflection` + `DigestLwwMode::Reflection`, the `push_reflection` LWW absorber (one outstanding reflection digest per workspace = the skip-not-queue cancellation), and the hot-reloadable `Settings.cadence_reflection_seconds`. The genuine net-new is (a) the reflection prompt variant in `crates/interpretation/` + its selection by `digest.kind`, and (b) the reflection-incident producer at the `pulse-app/src/inference_runtime.rs` binary boundary, which today hard-skips non-cue digests (`inference_runtime.rs:634`). Per combined §Chunk route#98, the L4 trait surface stays frozen (arch §Established Decisions [LLM Inference Runtime] bus-factor mitigation), the digest body never reaches logs (security ↔ obs PII scrubbing already at the assembler boundary), and the reflection digest stays distinguishable via `digest_kind` (obs ↔ tests). Zero new TauRPC procedure / broadcast topic / workspace dep / env var / Tauri capability (route §96 deltas NONE) — but this Extend DOES add one `CueKind` enum variant (the one synthetic, non-detector-emitted kind), which is a triage-crate contract change with a bounded exhaustive-match ripple, NOT an arch §Occupied Resources registry item.

1. **Add `PROMPT_VERSION_REFLECTION` const** in `crates/interpretation/src/schema.rs` alongside `PROMPT_VERSION_PRIMARY` / `PROMPT_VERSION_FALLBACK` (value e.g. `"v1.0-reflection"`). Keep `SCHEMA_VERSION` unchanged (the L4 output schema is identical; only the prompt framing differs).

2. **Add the reflection prompt builder** in `crates/interpretation/src/prompt.rs`:
   - Add `ROLE_DEFINITION_REFLECTION` const — a trend-emphasis role: the classifier is reviewing a **30-minute cumulative window** for emergent PATTERNS / drift / recurring signatures, NOT acute single events; default decision is to record-as-curious unless a high-confidence cumulative pattern warrants higher severity.
   - Add `OUTPUT_REMINDER_REFLECTION` const — reinforces: default `severity` to `"curious"` (decision `"watch"` / `"surface"` at curious) UNLESS a high-confidence trend justifies `"suggested"`/`"autonomous"`; same strict-JSON-only contract as primary.
   - Add `pub fn build_reflection_tier_prompt(digest_payload, project_context, corpus_retrieval) -> String` mirroring `build_primary_tier_prompt`'s section structure (Role → Conventions → Schema-with-`PROMPT_VERSION_REFLECTION`-metadata → Project Context markers → Current Digest markers → optional Corpus markers → Output Instructions). Reuse `CONVENTIONS_SNIPPET` + `L4_OUTPUT_JSON_SCHEMA` unchanged. Do NOT set `model_tier="fallback"` (this is a primary-tier-quality prompt).
   - Framing-string discipline: the trend-emphasis discriminators (e.g. "cumulative", "30-minute window", "trend") MUST be schema.json-exclusive — grep `crates/interpretation/src/schema.json` first per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-25.

3. **Add `CueKind::ReflectionTrend` variant** in `crates/triage/src/contract.rs` (the one synthetic, non-detector-emitted `CueKind`; update the enum doc comment to note this single exception to "emitted by triage detectors"). This gives reflection incidents a clean `(kind, scope, workspace)` cool-down identity distinct from the 5 detector cues. Update **all 5 exhaustive `match CueKind` arms** the variant breaks (research-enumerated):
   - `crates/triage/src/cadence/coordinator.rs:248` `cue_kind_label` → add `CueKind::ReflectionTrend => "reflection_trend"`.
   - `crates/triage/src/digest/assembler.rs:497` `cue_kind_label` → add the same arm.
   - `crates/triage/src/cue/classify.rs:69` `cue_kind_label` → add the same arm.
   - `crates/triage/src/cue/classify.rs:55` suppressibility grouping → add `ReflectionTrend` to the `=> false` (not-suppressible) arm (defensive — reflection "cues" are never detector-emitted nor enter the suppression path; document the arm as never-hit-in-practice).
   - `crates/triage/src/pattern/suppression.rs:173` suppressibility grouping → same `=> false` arm + same note.
   - Add a serde round-trip unit test asserting `ReflectionTrend` ↔ `"reflection_trend"` (mirrors the existing CueKind serde tests).

4. **Wire reflection prompt selection** in `pulse-app/src/inference_runtime.rs::handle_digest_outcome` (currently selects by `runner.tier()` at lines 306-315). Extend to a `(tier, digest.kind)` selection:
   - `(ModelTier::Primary, DigestKind::Reflection)` → `build_reflection_tier_prompt(...)` + `PROMPT_VERSION_REFLECTION`.
   - `(ModelTier::Primary, _)` → `build_primary_tier_prompt(...)` + `PROMPT_VERSION_PRIMARY` (unchanged).
   - `(ModelTier::Fallback, _)` → `build_fallback_tier_prompt(...)` + `PROMPT_VERSION_FALLBACK` (unchanged — fallback-tier reflection reuses the fallback acute builder; trend emphasis is a primary-tier enrichment, documented per research Open question 2). The `prompt_version` field already emitted at `TARGET_L4_PROMPT_ASSEMBLE` (line 319) distinguishes reflection in self-observation (no new tracing field needed — obs aggregate-only preserved).

5. **Extend the incident producer** `pulse-app/src/inference_runtime.rs::create_incident_from_l4_output` (lines 617-714) to handle reflection digests:
   - Keep the existing skip predicate (`is_resolution_summary || decision == Dismiss || severity == None`).
   - Replace the unconditional non-cue skip (line 634 `let Some(cue) = digest.attention_cues.first() else { return };`) with a branch: when `digest.kind == DigestKind::Reflection`, derive the synthetic identity `(kind = CueKind::ReflectionTrend, scope = CueScope::Global, scope_id = None)` instead of requiring a cue; for all other digest kinds, keep the existing cue-required path (non-reflection non-cue digests still skip — baseline cadence etc.).
   - Reuse the existing dedup-on-`(kind, scope, scope_id)` re-emission path: `(ReflectionTrend, Global, None)` yields exactly one outstanding reflection incident per workspace (observe_reemission bumps it; no duplicates).
   - Severity is mapped from the L4 output as usual (`map_l4_incident_severity` / `map_l4_priority_tier`); "default Curious" is enforced by the reflection PROMPT (Step 2), consistent with how acute incident severity is entirely model-driven. (Optional defense-in-depth clamp to ≤Curious-unless-high-confidence is deferred — relying on the prompt keeps the producer symmetric with the acute path and avoids depending on the hypotheses-confidence schema shape.)
   - `title`/`detail`/`scope_id`(None) scrubbed via the existing `scrub_text` boundary (chunk #72 invariant) — unchanged.
   - Aggregate-only `emit_incident_outcome` reused unchanged (bounded severity/tier labels; never scope_id/title/detail).

6. **Tests.**
   - `crates/interpretation/src/prompt.rs` `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` (interpretation is NOT `[lib] test=false`; source tests run): add reflection-builder coverage mirroring the primary/fallback shape — embeds schema; embeds `PROMPT_VERSION_REFLECTION`; contains a trend-emphasis marker; trend marker is ABSENT from the primary prompt (distinct-from-acute); section ordering stable; negative-canary (no `span_id`/`trace_id` outside the embedded schema). Use schema.json-exclusive discriminators per CLAUDE.md 2026-05-25.

- **Phase number:** 96

- **Route chunks covered:**
  - route#99 "A11y + perf re-verify + capability coverage check — full a11y/perf SLO re-audit + load profiles; P-001–P-060 verified; v0.2.0 tag gate (detail in pulse-v0_2_0-route §97)"
- **Epoch:** Epoch 9 — Foundation v0.2.0 (terminal chunk — the v0.2.0 tag gate)

Chunk #99 is the final verification pass before the v0.2.0 tag: every capability P-001–P-060 gets at least one named, machine-checkable verification scenario; the four dist-arch v3 load profiles (baseline 1k / high 10k / burst 50k / sustained-extreme 50k spans/s) pass their declared criteria; the full a11y audit re-runs over the redesigned v0.2.0 surfaces at WCAG 2.1 AA + SC 2.3.3 AAA and re-establishes the tuple-regression baseline; and the perf SLO gates (frame p99 ≤33ms, snapshot p99 ≤500ms, buffer ≤512MB, zero panics, no heartbeat stall, per-hardware-profile L4 latency) re-verify green (per combined §Chunk route#99 constraints; source `docs/v0_2_0/pulse-v0_2_0-route.md` §97).

Research shows the verification SUBSTRATE largely exists — chunk #54 built `cargo xtask test:a11y` + `perf:slo-load` + the npm a11y chain with baselines and a regression detector; chunks #55/#56 built the quality/obs gates; `xtask/ci/` carries six paired check scripts including `l4-latency-p99` with the per-hardware-profile budgets already encoded; `capability_widening_check()` already exists at `xtask/src/main.rs:813` (the security extract's "unimplemented gap" flag is stale). The chunk is therefore: (a) BUILD the two genuinely missing pieces — the P-001–P-060 capability verification matrix (data + xtask validator) and the four-profile load suite extending `perf_slo_10k_spans.rs`; (b) EXTEND the a11y harness to the v0.2.0 surfaces it predates (axe specs exist only for v0.1.0 p1–p7; `tests-a11y/keyboard-focus/` matches a playwright glob but does not exist); (c) RE-RUN everything and remediate findings; (d) record the declared specialist-plan touches (test/a11y/obs Decisions Log) via the implement-time amendment protocol.

Hard boundary: this is a ZERO-REGISTRY-DELTA chunk (source §97: TauRPC / broadcast / workspace-deps / arch-registry deltas all none). No new `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_*` env vars, procedures, topics, capabilities, or workspace members — the full-duration load profiles are gated via a nextest profile/filter, not a new env var (per combined §Chunk route#99 arch constraints).

1. **Pre-flight reconciliation (Step-1 inspection discipline).** Verify the "already exists" findings before writing anything: `capability_widening_check()` coverage at `xtask/src/main.rs:813-880` (is it CI-wired? if yes, the `.claude/rules/security.md` gap note is doubly stale); current content of `pulse-app/ui/tests-a11y/axe/p5-compact-widget.spec.ts` (was it already updated for the post-#89/#91 widget? do not assume staleness); `xtask/ci/quarantine-tracking-check.{sh,ps1}` semantics (does it flag ALL `#[ignore]` or only un-issued ones? — informs step 4's gating mechanism); whether `.config/nextest.toml` supports the profile/filter shape needed (nextest `default-filter` per profile). Confirm baseline gates green at HEAD (`cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` + fmt + clippy + capability-drift).

2. **Author the capability verification matrix data** at `docs/v0_2_0/capability-verification-matrix.json`: one entry per P-001–P-060 (60 total; note P-060 sits between P-023 and P-024 in spec document order) with fields `{capability_id, claim_summary, verification_mode, scenarios: [{kind, ref}], notes}`. `verification_mode` ∈ {automated-nextest, automated-a11y, xtask-gate, env-gated-runtime, manual-SR-supplemental, by-construction}. Bind to EXISTING named tests first (E2E files already cite P-ids in doc-comments — e.g. `e2e_pii_scrubber_persistence_coverage.rs`, `e2e_p3_mcp_incident_tools.rs`, `e2e_incidents_lifecycle.rs`, `e2e_storm_detection.rs`); every capability lacking a named scenario gets either a small targeted gap-fill test (preferred when cheap) or an explicit justified classification (`by-construction` / `manual-SR-supplemental`) — never silent omission. The security cluster maps per combined: P-040 → MCP double-gate tests, P-046 → `e2e_p95_export_for_training.rs`, P-041/P-047–P-051 → scrubber/corpus/at-rest/negative-canary suites.

3. **Add xtask `verify:capability-matrix` subcommand** (modify `xtask/src/main.rs`, follow clap + JSON-envelope conventions per research §Conventions): validates the matrix JSON — all 60 P-ids present exactly once, every `scenarios[].ref` resolves (test file exists on disk; a11y spec exists; xtask gate name is a known subcommand), zero capabilities with empty scenarios — and emits a machine-parseable summary (counts per verification_mode + pass/fail). Wire into `ci.yml` per-PR (cheap, file-existence-level) and extend the workflow self-lint (`pulse-app/tests/a11y_perf_workflow.rs` or `quality_gate_workflow.rs` pattern) to assert the new step + preserved SHA-pin/permissions posture in the same commit.

4. **Build the four-profile load suite** at `pulse-app/tests/perf_load_profiles.rs`, extending the `perf_slo_10k_spans.rs` in-process pattern (ephemeral loopback gRPC receiver + real DuckDB + `run_consumer` + tonic client; per research §Patterns). Four tests with dist-arch §Load testing criteria:
   - `baseline_1k_60s` — 1000 spans/s × 60s; zero drops; within perf budget.
   - `high_10k_5min` — 10000 spans/s × 5min; zero drops; `metric.buffer.memory_bytes`-equivalent bound ≤512MB; L1a Q1–Q7 executed DURING load with p99 <500ms.
   - `burst_50k_30s_recovery` — 50000 spans/s × 30s then return to baseline; no crash; recovery to normal operation ≤1min.
   - `sustained_extreme_50k_5min` — 50000 spans/s × 5min; degraded-but-functional; LWW drops acceptable; ZERO L0 data loss within retention window; retention eviction asserted (use deterministic time control where applicable per test-plan §7).
   Gate full-duration runs behind a dedicated nextest profile (e.g. `[profile.load-profiles]` with a `default-filter` selecting only this test binary) so `--profile ci` / default runs exclude them — NO new env var, NO bare `#[ignore]` (respect quarantine-tracking-check semantics verified in step 1). Add xtask `perf:load-profiles` orchestration: runs the nextest profile, then `xtask/ci/perf-slo-check` + `heartbeat-gap-check` + `l4-latency-p99` over the produced log artifacts. Extend `quality_gate_workflow.rs` self-lint for any `nextest.toml` change. Synchronization per test-plan §6: poll readiness, never `sleep(N)`; throughput pacing by batch arithmetic, not wall-clock sleeps where avoidable.

5. **Track a minimal live-load injector example** at `crates/ingest/examples/load_profiles.rs` (cargo example — not a workspace member, zero registry delta; precedent: untracked `inject_demo.rs` which stays untracked): speaks OTLP/gRPC to a RUNNING app at the configured port for the booted-app ACTIVE perf window. Local release-gate evidence flow: `scripts/agent-run.sh boot` → run injector at the four profile rates → `cargo xtask perf:slo-load`-style checks over `agent-latest.jsonl` — this flips `perf-slo-check` (frame p99 ≤33ms, memory) and `l4-latency-p99` from NEUTRAL to ACTIVE (per research §Patterns NEUTRAL-pass discipline). Assert the obs boundary events for the platform (`app.boot.webview.init`, `app.boot.gpu.check`, `app.boot.tray.init`) and heartbeat ticks ≤45s gaps during the window. CI keeps NEUTRAL discipline (webview not booted there).

6. **Extend the a11y harness to v0.2.0 surfaces** (per combined a11y constraints + research gaps):
   - New axe specs continuing the `axe/p{N}-{surface}.spec.ts` scheme: redesigned widget verification in `p5-compact-widget.spec.ts` (update for post-#89/#91 reality: no footer band; connection dot + tooltip; constellation dots; findings counter) + new specs for findings dropdown (Menu pattern), diagnostic report modal (Dialog pattern), Settings → Diagnostics view, constellation canvas `region[aria-label]` semantics, export-preview surface.
   - Create `tests-a11y/keyboard-focus/` specs (the playwright glob already matches): tabbable ground-truth vs actual Tab sequence for widget + dashboard + each modal; Esc closes + focus restores to trigger; `--border-focus` visible on `:focus-visible`.
   - SC 1.4.13 re-evaluation: the chunk-#89 connection-dot TOOLTIP ends the "no hover-hidden content" not-applicable justification — add dismissable/hoverable/persistent assertions (a11y plan §1 staleness flag per combined).
   - SC 1.4.1 not-color-alone custom Playwright assertions for every severity/state hue surface: Halo severity hue, constellation dot hues, findings counter/dropdown severity colors, connection-state dot.
   - Extend `reduced-motion.spec.ts` for the chunk-#90 semantic: static glow + hue STILL updating per cumulative incident severity (never frozen, never blank canvas) — fixtures MUST NOT use the superseded 0.8–2.4 Hz error-rate model (combined rot warning 1).
   - Run the full chain (`cargo xtask test:a11y`); REMEDIATE any violations found (fixes are in-chunk scope unless they would require a registry delta — then halt and route via the amendment path); regenerate `baselines/a11y-violations-summary.json` as the v0.2.0 baseline only after a clean pass.

7. **Tray + window-state verification within agent-driven limits** (pending user decision on research Open question 1; default = option b): extend the P5 IPC surrogate + assert tray/window boundary events during the step-5 booted window; record the SR manual pass spec status (`screen-reader/a11y-sr-*.md` fixtures + `a11y-sr-results.jsonl` schema) for the tray-menu half — manual SR results are supplemental evidence the user can produce; the plan documents the residual tauri-driver headful gap explicitly in the test-plan Decisions Log entry rather than silently claiming coverage.

Also correct the stale `.claude/rules/security.md` "Static analysis test gap (not yet implemented)" note to cite `capability_widening_check()` at `xtask/src/main.rs:813`.

Do NOT push a `v*` tag in this chunk — `release.yml` triggers on tag push and the chunk-#3 DEFERRED signing items (Azure Key Vault EV / Apple notarization / `production-release` environment) are unresolved release blockers; surface to user (research Open question 3).

title: 1. Pre-flight findings (6 points the plan asked us to verify)

data.head: ## 1. Pre-flight findings (6 points the plan asked us to verify)

body: **Location:** `pulse-app/ui/src/halo/HaloCanvas.tsx:124-164` (TS-side uniform computation) + `pulse-app/ui/src/halo/shaders/halo.wgsl:24-64` (WGSL fragment shader applying the breathing envelope).
**Inputs (both React props):**

- `errorRate: f32 ∈ [0, 1]` — drives hue (`lchInterpolate` at `pulse-app/ui/src/halo/lch.ts:20-44` interpolates LCH-space between `--color-primary` Earth Blue and `--color-accent` Alert Burgundy via `colorjs.io`) AND blur envelope (`pulse-app/ui/src/halo/error-rate-to-blur.ts:9-15` linear maps к [4px, 16px])
- `throughputHz` — clamped к [0.8 Hz, 2.4 Hz] (`pulse-app/ui/src/halo/throughput-to-hz.ts:9-17`); phase = `(timestamp / 1000) * 2π * hz` (`HaloCanvas.tsx:164`)

**Source of those props:** **`pulse-app/ui/src/hooks/use-synthetic-widget-metrics.ts:51-52`** — а synthetic simulator producing sine-wave-like values on а 1000ms tick. Comment at line 5 of that file says "real `streams.subscribe_metrics` binding deferred к chunks #34/#35." **Chunks #34 + #35 landed but the widget itself was NOT rewired** — the synthetic simulator survived. This is а major finding (see §5 Hidden complexity).

**WGSL/TS split:** TS computes uniforms (color RGBA + blur_target + pulse_phase as 8-float buffer); shader applies `current_blur = blur_target * (0.5 + 0.5 * sin(pulse_phase))` + smoothstep radial falloff. **No color computation in shader** (per design-tokens.md Session Additions 2026-05-08 audit — colors arrive pre-resolved from design tokens).

**Plan's assumption check:** _"halo formula by error rate"_ — confirmed but oversimplifies. Formula is **two-axis** (errorRate → hue+blur; throughputHz → pulse frequency). The plan's "remove direct error_rate → hue" needs к remove BOTH axes' synthetic source, not just substitute the hue input.

**Component:** `pulse-app/ui/src/widget/CompactWidget.tsx:24-71` (orchestrator) + `pulse-app/ui/src/widget/FooterBand.tsx:50-165` (footer) + `pulse-app/ui/src/components/Titlebar.tsx:36-136` (titlebar) + `pulse-app/ui/src/widget/AggregatedBadgeCanvas.tsx:33-79` (constellation badge area).
**Each footer element's data source** (all surveyed):
| Element | Source path:line | Status |
| `Ingest 200/s` | `widget-types.ts:25-34` → prop wired from `use-synthetic-widget-metrics.ts:51-52` | **Synthetic** — no real metrics subscription |
| `Error 4.2%` | `widget-types.ts:36-42` → prop from same synthetic hook (line 49) | **Synthetic**. Accent border at threshold 0.05 (`FooterBand.tsx:18`) |
| `Retention 3m / 10m` | `widget-types.ts:44-56` → prop from synthetic hook (lines 51-58, ramps 0→600s over 30 ticks then resets) | **Synthetic** — no real config-toml subscription |
| Service constellation aggregated badge | `AggregatedBadgeCanvas.tsx:33-79` | **Synthetic** — `serviceCount` prop, no actual `BaselineKeeper.activity_windows` source |

**Titlebar:** App icon (constellation-grid glyph) + title text + optional Investigate button (telescope glyph, conditional on `onInvestigateClick`) + Settings button (aperture glyph) + platform-specific `WindowControls`. **No connection dot exists yet** — the plan's §5a "header redesign" is greenfield.

**Plan's assumption check:** The plan implicitly assumed the widget is showing **real** Ingest/Error/Retention numbers. **It is not** — they are synthetic. **Phase 5 must add а "wire real broadcast subscriptions" preliminary chunk** before any redesign work.
| Topic (arch §Occupied Resources) | Emit site | Webview subscriber |

| `pulse://stream/spans` | `crates/buffer/src/consumer.rs:79` → broadcast sender at line 106 | `pulse-app/ui/src/App.tsx:13` (comment only, no real consumer). TauRPC `streams.subscribe_spans` at `bindings/index.ts:92` exposed but NOT wired in production code paths |

| `pulse://stream/metrics` | `crates/buffer/src/consumer.rs:87` → line 106 | TauRPC `streams.subscribe_metrics` exposed at `bindings/index.ts:91`. Comment-only reference at `use-synthetic-widget-metrics.ts:5` |
| `pulse://stream/logs` | `crates/buffer/src/consumer.rs:95` → line 106 | TauRPC `streams.subscribe_logs` exposed at `bindings/index.ts:90`. Comment-only reference at `HaloCanvas.tsx:9` |
| `pulse://stream/snapshot-progress` | **NOT IMPLEMENTED** | — |
| `pulse://stream/plugin-events` | **NOT IMPLEMENTED** | — |

**Material finding:** 3 of 5 declared topics are Rust-side emitting, but **zero are wired to actual webview consumers**. The widget reads error/throughput from synthetic; the dashboard reads tracing via `traces.query`/`metrics.query`/`logs.query` TauRPC paginated APIs (NOT live streams). The streams.* namespace is declared infrastructure waiting for consumers.

**Plan's assumption check:** The plan implies adding `pulse://stream/connection-state` / `/anomalies` / `/restart-events` / `/incidents` (= 4 new topics) on top of existing 5. The reality is the existing 5 are 3 declared-and-emitting + 2 declared-and-stubbed. Adding 4 more pushes the namespace к 9 topics, of which **5 will lack webview subscribers** at first. Recommend: bundle Phase 5's incident-card binding chunk to **include the widget's first real `streams.*` subscription** (collapse the chunk #34/#35 deferred wiring into the Phase 5 redesign).

title: 1.4 Snapshot curation pipeline (chunks #39 + #44) — most important finding

data.head: ### 1.4 Snapshot curation pipeline (chunks #39 + #44) — most important finding

body: **ALL anomaly + curation primitives ARE implemented:**
| Primitive | Location | Algorithm |
| Dedupe spans | `crates/snapshot/src/dedupe.rs:30` (`dedupe_spans`) | (service_name, name, 100ms-bucket) HashMap |
| Anomaly: latency outliers | `crates/snapshot/src/anomaly.rs:70` (`detect_latency_outliers`) | **Z-score**; threshold 3.0 (`LATENCY_OUTLIER_Z_THRESHOLD`); severity ∈ [0, 100] |
| Anomaly: error correlation | `crates/snapshot/src/anomaly.rs:113` (`detect_error_correlation`) | `status_code == 2` clustering per service; min cluster 3 errors |
| Anomaly: cardinality spikes | `crates/snapshot/src/anomaly.rs:161` (`detect_cardinality_spikes`) | unique-span-name count per service vs median; 2.0× multiplier |
| Critical-path extraction | `crates/snapshot/src/critical_path.rs:18` (`extract_critical_path`) | DAG longest-path traversal via parent_span_id backlinks |
| p50/p95/p99 aggregation | `crates/snapshot/src/aggregation.rs:21` (`aggregate_metrics`) | nearest-rank percentile over sorted durations; global + per-service |
**Reusability assessment:** **Fully reusable as algorithms — locked by visibility.** All primitives operate on `&[SpanRecord]` (pure data, no DuckDB coupling, no I/O). However:
- All functions are `pub(crate)` — invisible to other workspace crates per Rust module discipline + CLAUDE.md "one crate per module" rule
- Logic operates on **post-query materialized Vec<SpanRecord>**, not on streaming spans from а broadcast subscription
- Coupled к snapshot crate's `SpanRecord` type definition

**STRONG argument для the plan's Phase 2 (BaselineKeeper):** Extract а new `crates/curation/` shared library housing these 6 primitives + their `SpanRecord` type. snapshot depends on it (refactor — chunks #39 + #44 surface unchanged); new `crates/triage/` (or `crates/baseline/`) depends on it for **streaming variants** of the same algorithms.

**The plan completely misses this** — it proposes а greenfield BaselineKeeper using `tdigest` + `dashmap` (neither currently а workspace dep) without acknowledging 6 algorithmic primitives already in the codebase. Even if streaming-vs-batch is а meaningfully different shape, **error-correlation + cardinality-spike + critical-path** are batch-only operations that the BaselineKeeper would benefit from sharing.
**Schema:** `service_name VARCHAR NOT NULL` in `spans` table (`crates/buffer/src/schema.rs:31`).
**Population path:** `crates/buffer/src/appender.rs:101-114` (`extract_service_name`):
1. Reads OTLP `Resource.attributes` (line 105)
2. Matches key `"service.name"` (line 106)
3. Extracts `StringValue` from `AnyValue.value` (lines 107-108)
4. **Fallback when absent:** returns empty string (line 113)
**Edge cases:**
- Span с no `service.name` attribute → stored as `""` (empty string)
- Span с `service.name` = `""` → stored as `""` (same as above; indistinguishable)
- Span с whitespace-only `service.name` → stored verbatim (no trim)
- Multiple service.name attributes — first match wins (HashMap iteration order)

**Plan's Q3 ("what does baseline keeper do when span arrives without `service.name`?"):** Recommend **drop silently in BaselineKeeper** (don't create а phantom "unknown" service that bloats activity windows + UI dots). Reason: empty-string services are typically test fixtures / dev experimentation; promoting them к а constellation dot is high-noise / low-signal. Add а debug-level `tracing::warn!` count of dropped-spans-per-tick для observability.

title: 1.6 What counts as "error" in current halo formula

data.head: ### 1.6 What counts as "error" in current halo formula

body: **Current halo formula (chunk #31 final):** **NONE of the broadcast topics feed the halo's error signal.**
Error rate flows как follows:
1. Webview queries traces via TauRPC `traces.query(args)` → `PaginatedResponse<TraceRow>` (`bindings/index.ts:84`)
2. TraceRow.`error_count` field aggregated client-side (each row contributes 1 if `status_code == 2`, else 0; `crates/viz/src/query.rs:162`)
3. **BUT** — as noted in §1.1 — chunks #31/#32 widget passes а **synthetic** errorRate, not the queried one. The architectural pathway exists; the widget never consumes it.
**Storage shapes:**
- Spans: `status_code: i32` (OTLP enum: 0=Unset, 1=Ok, 2=Error)
- Logs: `severity_number: i32` (raw OTLP scale 1-24; 8=WARN, 9-12=ERROR, 13-16=FATAL)
- Exception events: `span_events` table **exists in schema but is never populated** (chunk #39 stub; deferred к follow-on chunk)

**Plan's Q6 implicit assumption:** the plan's `RetryStorm` detector keys off `exception.type` + `exception.stacktrace` (Phase 3 §3a). **These fields are not currently captured** — exception events ride on spans as `Span.events` (per OTLP spec) but the buffer's `span_events` table population is deferred. The plan needs an explicit dependency: **"Phase 3 requires chunk implementing span events ingestion + storage первой"** — this is а meaningful prerequisite chunk that isn't called out.

title: Phase 1 — Connection state machine: **Feasible с adjustment**

data.head: ### Phase 1 — Connection state machine: **Feasible с adjustment**

body: Realistic given current code. The `LastIngestTracker` (atomic `Instant` updated in ingest hot path) is а natural extension of `crates/ingest/src/mpsc.rs` (where the hot-path receiver already exists).

**Adjustment:** Recommend placing `ConnectionState` machine **inside `crates/ingest/`** as а new module rather than а new top-level crate. `ingest` already owns receiver lifecycle (gRPC + HTTP) and watches mpsc hand-off; bolting Connection state onto its existing instrumentation surface is less workspace churn (skip new crate + new Cargo.toml + new module-boundary discussion). The `pulse://stream/connection-state` broadcast topic is а new topic regardless; can be emitted from inside ingest just like other topics are emitted from buffer.

**Missing dependency:** `ReceiverFailed` state requires а callback path from receiver-task panics back к the state machine. Currently receiver tasks panic-out via `std::panic::set_hook` → `tracing::error!(target: "app.panic.fatal", ...)` (per .claude/rules/observability.md). The state machine needs к either subscribe к panic events OR have an explicit "receiver task health" channel.
**Realistic chunk count:** **1-2 chunks** (1 if module-inside-ingest; 2 if standalone crate).

title: Phase 2 — Baseline keeper: **Feasible but plan misses huge reuse opportunity**

data.head: ### Phase 2 — Baseline keeper: **Feasible but plan misses huge reuse opportunity**

body: See §1.4 finding. Recommended adjustment: **insert "Extract `crates/curation/` shared library" as а prerequisite chunk**. Then BaselineKeeper composes:
- **Streaming variants** of EWMA + t-digest + rolling-window (new — these are streaming, not batch)
- **Batch primitives** reused from `crates/curation/` for restart-suppression / error-correlation / cardinality-spike contextual analysis

**Missing dependency from plan:** `tdigest` crate (or `tdigests`) not in workspace; needs к be added к `Cargo.toml [workspace.dependencies]` + `deny.toml [bans] skip` list. `dashmap` similarly. Both cargo deny / cargo audit clean per current state (no banned advisories для these crates as of 2026-05-14 RustSec DB), but cargo deny `multiple-versions = "deny"` may bite if transitive duplicates exist.

**Restart-awareness coordination:** The plan's "Phase 2 subscribes к Phase 3 RestartEvent" creates а **circular dep risk** — Phase 2 + Phase 3 both subscribe к ingest broadcast, AND Phase 2 subscribes к Phase 3. Either:
- Both subscribe к а shared `pulse://stream/ingest-internal-events` (Phase 2's restart suppression listens for `RestartEvent` from Phase 3 on this channel)
- OR collapse Phase 2 + Phase 3 detection into а single state holder (single crate, no cross-subscription)

I recommend **option 2** — single `triage` crate с modules `baseline` + `pattern`, internal channels. Simpler dep graph; matches workspace discipline (snapshot crate has multiple internal modules — anomaly, dedupe, critical_path — without cross-crate ceremony).
**Realistic chunk count:** **4 chunks** (1 extract curation + 3 for plan's described work; not the plan's 3).

title: Phase 3 — Pattern detector: **Partially feasible — exception events gap**

data.head: ### Phase 3 — Pattern detector: **Partially feasible — exception events gap**

body: Restart-event detector (3b) is feasible immediately — а per-service `last_seen_span_timestamp` tracker против `Instant::now()`-derived gap is straightforward.

**Retry storm detector (3a) blocked on prerequisite:** Exception fingerprinting requires `exception.type` + `exception.stacktrace` fields. Per §1.6, **span_events table exists in schema but is not populated**. Either:
- Pre-requisite chunk: implement OTLP `Span.events` ingestion into `span_events` table
- OR Defer Phase 3a to а post-MVP scope (Phase 4 can ship without retry storm; ErrorRateSpike from Phase 2 covers similar ground at less precision)

**Missing dependency from plan:** Span-events ingestion chunk. Roughly equivalent в complexity к chunk #25 (Query routers) — schema is already defined; the work is in `appender.rs` extending к decode span events from OTLP + new query path.
**Realistic chunk count:** **2-3 chunks** (1 span-events-ingestion prerequisite + 2 for plan's described work; OR defer 3a + 1 chunk для just 3b).

title: Phase 4 — Severity classifier + Incident state: **Feasible as described**

data.head: ### Phase 4 — Severity classifier + Incident state: **Feasible as described**

body: Rule-based engine is а straightforward fit; no new infrastructure beyond existing TauRPC procedure boilerplate.

**Adjustment:** The plan's `Incident.evidence_refs: EvidenceRefs` containing `span_ids: Vec<SpanId>` (8 bytes each) + `trace_ids: Vec<TraceId>` (16 bytes) is а security-touchpoint — these are user-data attribute fragments. Per `.claude/rules/security.md` "NEVER log raw OTLP attribute values, span/log/metric content payloads..." — Incident.detail rendering needs к use anonymized identifiers (e.g., `query_id` / `param_count` style) when emitted to the obs JSON log. **Webview-side display via TauRPC IS the boundary** where the actual IDs cross, gated by the existing `AppError`-style sanitization discipline.

**Missing detail from plan:** `incidents.acknowledge(id)` — what does "acknowledge" do? Plan says "user-driven dismiss". Implication: incidents have а user-state field (`acknowledged_at: Option<SystemTime>`) and the UI hides acknowledged incidents OR sorts them lower. Either way, this needs к be in the `Incident` struct + the dedup logic ("don't re-create acknowledged incidents within а cool-down period").
**Realistic chunk count:** **3 chunks** (matches plan estimate).
Largest scope. The plan's 4-5 chunks is **optimistic by 1-2 chunks** because:

1. **Real-data binding prerequisite** (currently missing). Before redesign, the widget MUST stop using `use-synthetic-widget-metrics.ts` and start using real streams (probably `streams.subscribe_metrics` for throughput + а new `incidents.list_active` poll for cumulative_severity). That's **1 chunk** in itself, not folded into header redesign.

2. **Halo refactor cascades to chunk #34 ConstellationCanvas + dashboard consumers.** The halo's API contract changes from `(errorRate, throughputHz)` к `(connectionState, cumulative_severity, activity_state)`. Chunk #34's per-service Halo dots в the constellation map consume the same `HaloCanvas` component; they need а corresponding refactor OR continue с old props (impossible if HaloCanvas signature changes). Plan should call out the cascade explicitly.

3. **Service constellation aggregated badge replacement:** The existing badge wraps `HaloCanvas` (per §1.2 finding). Replacing с "actual constellation dots" means **removing the HaloCanvas wrap** + adding а NEW per-dot rendering. The plan describes the new behavior but understates the surgery — the existing component is а composite, not а thin display layer.

4. **Chrome cleanup interacts с motion-reduce respect.** The footer removal removes а render path; if the recent-incident-dot-history replacement uses motion (likely), reduced-motion respect needs к propagate. Plan calls out the design touchpoint but not the implementation cost.

**Realistic chunk count:** **5-6 chunks** (1 real-data binding + 5 redesign chunks including connection-dot header + halo refactor + constellation replace + incident card + chrome cleanup; possibly +1 cascade-update chunk for chunk #34's ConstellationCanvas).
| Phase | Plan estimate | Realistic (this review) | Delta |
| 1 — Connection | 2 | 1-2 | -1 to 0 |
| 2 — BaselineKeeper | 3 | 4 (incl. curation extract) | +1 |
| 3 — Pattern | 2 | 2-3 (incl. span-events prereq if 3a kept) | 0 to +1 |
| 5 — Widget | 4-5 | 5-6 (incl. real-data wire-up + chunk #34 cascade) | +1 to +2 |

Plan's estimate **slightly optimistic** but within reasonable margin. Top-of-range total reflects (a) curation extraction + (b) span-events prereq + (c) widget real-data binding — all three are non-negotiable per current code state.

title: 3. Crate organization opinion (answer to plan's Q1)

data.head: ## 3. Crate organization opinion (answer to plan's Q1)

body: **Recommendation: ONE umbrella crate + ONE extracted shared library.**

```
crates/
├── curation/   (NEW; extracted from snapshot)
│   ├── dedupe.rs           (moved from snapshot/src/)
```

- **Connection state inside ingest** (plan §"crate: new connection crate (or а module inside ingest — debatable)"): see §2 Phase 1 — preferred is module-inside-ingest. The triage umbrella above leaves room для it; you could place connection inside ingest AND keep the broadcast topic separate from triage's other topics.

**On the question "agree с plan's sequence (after #52, before #54-56)?"** — Answer: not applicable; chunks #54-56 are done. The plan was written against an earlier state. The new sequencing must append, not insert.

**See §3 above.** TL;DR: 1 umbrella `triage` crate (modules: connection, baseline, pattern, classifier, incident) + 1 extracted `curation` shared lib (refactor from snapshot). Net workspace +2 crates (10 → 12). Plan's 4 separate crates is overkill; matches workspace boundary discipline poorly.

**Strong reuse opportunity. See §1.4 + §3.** Extract `crates/curation/` shared lib housing snapshot's anomaly + dedupe + critical_path + aggregation primitives. Both snapshot AND triage depend on it (snapshot for batch, triage for batch-in-pattern-context after streaming-aware EWMA/t-digest produces candidate windows).

The plan implicitly proposes greenfield duplication via `tdigest`+`dashmap`. This works but **adds maintenance debt** — two implementations of latency-outlier detection will drift over time, and the snapshot version (Z-score) vs triage version (EWMA-baseline-relative) might disagree on edge cases. Better to: extract shared batch primitives + добавь NEW streaming primitives (EWMA + t-digest in а new file).

**Recommend: drop spans с empty `service.name`** в BaselineKeeper (see §1.5 reasoning). Emit а debug-level `tracing::warn!(target: "triage.service_id_missing", count = N)` per tick aggregating dropped count; surface в obs log without per-span verbosity.

Edge case to call out separately: spans с `service.name` = `""` (explicit empty string) AND spans missing the attribute look identical in storage (both empty string). Plan should treat them uniformly (drop). Future: add а sentinel-distinction column в spans schema (`service_name_origin: "explicit" | "absent" | "malformed"`) if granularity becomes important.

**Recommend `tdigest` 0.x** (the crate by `MnO2`; established, permissive Apache-2.0 license, no_std-friendly, ~1.5k downloads/day per crates.io trend, no open RustSec advisories as of 2026-05-14). Alternatives:
- `tdigests` (newer fork, less battle-tested)
- `tdigest-rs` (early-stage; smaller adoption)

Check `cargo deny check bans` posture после addition; expect 1-2 transitive duplicates worth skipping (`num-traits` ecosystem) but nothing к block `multiple-versions = "deny"` posture per chunk #45/#48 pattern.
**Recommend Hybrid (config.toml + read-only display initially):**
- v0.1.0 (or first Epoch 9 ship): config.toml `[triage]` section editable; Settings modal shows current values **read-only** с link к config docs
- post-v0.1.0 backlog: full editable Settings UX

- **Env vars NO** — adding `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_TRIAGE_*` к the reserved namespace requires `/andromeda-evolve --allow-arch-registry` per arch §Occupied Resources discipline. config.toml is а cleaner extension point (the file already exists; modal load handler already plumbed).

Rationale: editable UI = а material amount of webview work (validation messages, dirty-state, save flow per chunk #38 SettingsModalForm precedent); not worth bundling into Epoch 9. Expert-operator escape hatch via config.toml is enough при v0.1.0.

body: Chunk #51 ACTIVE scope landed install-launch-ingest-query smoke harness; tauri-driver headful UI tests for tray + window state P5 were DEFERRED follow-on. The widget redesign в Phase 5 makes those headful tests more valuable (window-state interactions: incident card → opens dashboard → focus restoration). Connection state machine emits к а new broadcast topic AND exposes via TauRPC `connection.current_state()`. Meanwhile, existing `health` IPC (arch §Standard Contracts) already exposes `subsystems.otlp_grpc_receiver.status` / `subsystems.otlp_http_receiver.status` / etc. Cross-domain reconciliation needed:
